130ace7348: An RV resort in the popular Harrison Hot Springs resort village, putting cyclists within easy reach of the famous public hot springs pool and Harrison Lake beach. Likely geared toward RV clients, but the town setting and attractions make it a solid rest stop.
bb35e0ec09: A summer-season provincial park campground set among ponderosa pine and sagebrush directly on Okanagan Lake, with pebbly beach access, swim areas, and panoramic lake and mountain views; the gate is locked off-season and rattlesnakes inhabit the dry hillsides above camp.
18463dde36: A quiet private RV park in Valemount's Robson Valley with 360-degree mountain views and the odd wandering deer; tent/no-services pitches are available at around $35/night, but the park is RV-centric and open only April through October.
1eee7a0f5a: Private RV park on the west shore of Swan Lake with tent sites looking out over calm water; free pedal boats, canoes, and a rowboat make this a laid-back lakeside stop, though the marshy shores mean paddling out for a proper swim. Coin showers, laundry, and Wi-Fi on site.
33fa3ac918: A commercially managed Parkbridge RV resort in Whistler, positioned beside a river in the Sea-to-Sky corridor; the scraped website returned only generic corporate pages with no site-specific details on layout, facilities, or tent camping.
7f09e43a97: A group campsite in old-growth Goldstream Park, 16 km from Victoria, set among 600-year-old Douglas firs beside a chum salmon–spawning river with waterfall and ridge trails nearby; flush washrooms and showers on site, but group-minimum pricing applies.
36255993ee: A frontcountry BC Parks campground managed by the Osoyoos Indian Band, sitting just off Hwy 97 on Green Lake Road at the edge of Okanagan Falls town and near the historic 'little falls' on the Okanagan River; easy highway access but gate-locked off-season and closed one weekend in late September for the Salmon Feast.
f2834693d6: Ruckle Park occupies Salt Spring Island's southeastern shore with seven kilometres of rocky headlands, tidal pools, and grassy meadows overlooking Swanson Channel; ferry access is required and potable water is shut off November 1–March 15.
523dd273f8: A family-oriented commercial campground in cedar groves on the Malahat, 20 minutes from Victoria on the Trans-Canada Highway, with a pool, playground, flush washrooms, showers, and a camp store. Tenting sites run $44–45 CAD/night plus tax — a comfortable highway stopover rather than a wilderness experience.
9489a2a6ef: Walk-in tent sites tucked into old-growth forest on Salt Spring Island, each with its own character and a fire ring, connected directly to Mouat Park trails and a 10-minute walk from downtown Ganges; open year-round with lower winter rates.
936d39bbba: A 1,600-metre sand-and-pebble beach on the Strait of Juan de Fuca with sweeping Olympic Mountain views and gray whale sightings during migration; year-round camping via Highway 14, but facilities are pit toilets only.
5d9d13ef63: Tla-o-qui-aht Nation-owned resort on Pacific Rim Highway 3 km from Tofino, with exclusive access to tinwis Beach and full amenities including showers and laundry; only 5 tent sites among many RV hookups and cabins, so tent spots are scarce and advance reservations are critical.
a32e37b5a0: A private strata resort on Hatzic Lake in Mission, BC, with 395 fully serviced sites, lake swimming, and water sports; sites are primarily privately owned seasonal lots and transient availability for passing cyclists is uncertain.
f4e97ebfe2: A group-only campsite set in a sheltered cove right on the west shore of Harrison Lake, with a sandy beach well-suited for swimming; accessed via 7.9 km of forest service road and available by advance reservation only, with no walk-in option.
dfcb659e41: A fee campground near Chemainus with no confirmed facilities in available sources; the linked webpage describes Dionisio Point Provincial Park on Galiano Island, which does not match this listing's name or community.
1fd333d351: Lakeside Campground is a developed BC Parks site within Sasquatch Provincial Park, set among pocket lakes, birch forest, and mountain ridges six kilometres north of Harrison Hot Springs. Sandy-beach swimming, canoeing, and short hiking trails make it a well-rounded stop; swimmer's itch is possible in the lakes during summer.
c915aa340e: An RV-oriented camp in suburban Surrey near Tynehead Regional Park, convenient for riders navigating Metro Vancouver but offering little in the way of natural setting or cyclist-specific amenities.
55842ac28d: Chivers Point is a small boat-in campsite on Wallace Island Marine Provincial Park in the Gulf Islands, reachable only by kayak or motorboat from Chemainus; a wild island escape with no road access and minimal facilities.
a7c93d976c: A rustic non-profit campground on Squamish's edge near the Mamquam River, serving climbers, cyclists, and paddlers at very affordable rates; no water on site (bring your own — potable water is 600 m away), outhouses only, and strong afternoon winds make it a genuine hazard for tents.
bf3e4e278c: A tidy, flower-lined adult-only RV park on the edge of Creston with large level tent sites and clean heated washrooms; walking distance to grocery stores, pharmacy, and pool, making it a practical town stop with no scenic draw.
d080dd2acd: A resort-style campground sitting directly on Heffley Lake between Kamloops and Sun Peaks, with showers, fire pits, water-activity rentals, and an on-site bistro; the amenities and lake access make it a genuine layover destination, though the seasonal window (mid-May to end of September) and resort pricing apply.
65a319f63d: A well-serviced, family-oriented campground along the Coquihalla River in Hope, with riverfront and forested sites plus showers, laundry, and a playground on site; a bike park and disc golf course sit directly across the street, and the season runs late April through mid-October.
1b4c8f1e46: Boya Lake is celebrated across BC for its vivid turquoise water, making this 44-site developed park on the Cassiar Highway a genuine Stikine Region destination; potable water and washrooms are on-site, but the gate closes on first snowfall so timing is everything.
0c80c2eeb7: A private forested campground beside a small creek on mid-Vancouver Island, with serviced tent sites, hot showers, Wi-Fi, and natural spring water; handy to Nanaimo and BC Ferries but primarily an RV park that also takes tents.
0859d39bbb: A riverside campground in Ponderosa pine and bunchgrass country where the Kettle River meets the historic Kettle Valley Railway corridor; summer tubing, canoeing, and KVR trail cycling are the main draws, with flush toilets and showers on straightforward Highway 33 access.
6a12b5aaa8: Bear Beach is a hike-in backcountry campsite on the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail, a rugged 47 km wilderness route along Vancouver Island's wild southwest coast; trail closures from storm damage are frequent, and there is no vehicle or bike access.
f6ebad567e: A private campground alongside Wilson Creek on the Sunshine Coast Highway between Gibsons and Sechelt, with 14 tent sites, flush washrooms, and showers. Right off Hwy 101 with easy access to Davis Bay Beach, groceries, and coffee shops — functional and convenient rather than scenic.
b95b6432b9: A backcountry campsite at the historic Lindeman City gold-rush townsite along the Chilkoot Trail, reachable only by multi-day hike; entirely inaccessible to loaded touring bikes.
43c8b16d72: A mixed-use RV and tent park on the Trans-Canada in Hope, within a 10-minute walk of Lake of the Woods and easy reach of Fraser Canyon trails; expect a trailer-park atmosphere with showers, laundry, and wifi alongside long-term residents.
b402a18459: Mahood Lake sits at the quiet southwestern corner of Wells Gray Park, a family-friendly lakeshore campground noted for fishing and access to more remote marine campsites; reached via a long gravel road separate from the main park corridor.
9c946f7ebb: Vehicle-accessible campground on the Columbia River flats 7 km south of Trail, with a short riverside grassland walk and fishing for rainbow trout and walleye; note that bicycles are restricted to park roads — trails are off-limits — and the site is flanked by residential land and the Trail Airport.
b4cca5db48: Sulphurous Lake Resort is a year-round lakeside retreat in BC's Cariboo region offering cabins, RV sites, and tent camping with communal shower and washroom facilities. Cabins are fully equipped with cooking appliances, hot and cold running water, and bedding basics, making it a comfortable basecamp for cyclists exploring the Central Interior. The property is pet-friendly and allows campfires subject to seasonal fire regulations.
24d1d35e7a: A tidy 20-site BC Parks campground beside a small sandy beach on Seeley Lake, backed by the Hazelton Mountains, 10 km west of Hazelton on Highway 16; good for a quiet overnight with swimming, trout fishing, canoeing (electric motors only), and a short marsh wildlife-viewing trail. Pit toilets only; highway access is paved and straightforward.
74f47be91d: Tent-only camping stretched along a 2km pebble beach directly on Harrison Lake, with a handful of shaded forested sites; no potable water, no garbage service (pack everything out), and cash only — bring everything you need.
c113f19d9a: An RV park in BC's Cariboo/Chilcotin region; website was unreachable so facilities, fees, and road surface are unknown — confirm details before routing here.
0573551123: A well-appointed national park campground set in cedar-hemlock rainforest at the foot of the Meadows in the Sky Parkway, just 5 km from downtown Revelstoke — and 2 km by bike — with hot showers, flush toilets, and potable water on site. Both a campsite fee and a National Park pass are required for overnight stays.
28b0527f7b: Lucerne Campground sits beside Yellowhead Lake inside Mount Robson Provincial Park along Highway 16, framed by the highest peaks in the Canadian Rockies; an iconic overnight anchor for Yellowhead corridor cyclists with straightforward paved access.
94a56df0f6: Group-only campsite within Metro Vancouver's regional park system, designed for clubs or organized touring parties rather than solo or pair cyclists; fee applies and a group reservation is required.
81a42a228b: A paddle-in wilderness campsite on Widgeon Creek in Pinecone Burke Park, reached by canoe or kayak across Pitt Lake; designated tent pads only, no campfires allowed, no garbage service, and creek water must be treated before use.
ff2010f645: A remote backcountry lake camp in Tweedsmuir Provincial Park (South), reached only by a 20 km trail with 1,000 m of elevation gain through alpine terrain — strictly hike-in and inaccessible to loaded touring bikes.
671bf8024c: A mossy, tree-sheltered village campground at the south end of Sunset Park beside the Yakoun River Estuary on Haida Gwaii; four tent sites with potable water and outhouses, no showers, first come first served.
92fa3123b5: A remote backcountry wilderness camp in the South Chilcotin Mountains, set among alpine meadows, lakes, and mountain peaks; no potable water, no staffed facilities, grizzly bears are common, and the adjacent Spruce Lake Vehicle Closure Area means access is trail-only.
853d05b328: A large commercial resort campground on the Fraser River within Brae Island Regional Park, offering 156 full-service sites with flush bathrooms, laundry, WiFi, and a camp store just minutes from Fort Langley village. Gated and family-resort in feel with organised theme weekends; expect company rather than solitude.
0dc65930b8: One of five campgrounds inside Whiteswan Lake Park, Cave Creek is reached by roughly 25 km of gravel forest service road shared with mine ore and oversized logging trucks; the payoff is two mountain lakes, Lussier Hot Springs, and trophy rainbow trout fishing deep in the Kootenay Rockies with zero cell service.
c64d26ed79: A small 6-site camp in the rolling grasslands and dry open forest of the Kentucky-Alleyne area, near turquoise fishing lakes and cattle-country scenery; drinking water is on site but muddy lake edges limit swimming, and the site is open roughly April through October.
2103d7b929: Forested provincial campground beside Kleanza Creek near Terrace, offering a shaded creekside setting with easy highway access along the Yellowhead corridor; a solid overnight with potable water and washrooms.
21dd2c5216: Hike-in backcountry campsite at an alpine lake deep in E.C. Manning Park's Cascade Mountains; a permit is required ($5/person/night) but no advance reservation, and the site is unreachable by any road or loaded bike.
e123dfef81: A community campground in the remote Nisga'a village of Gingolx, at the end of Highway 113 where the Nass River meets Portland Inlet — simple, locally-run facilities in a place of deep quiet, panoramic mountain views, and rich Indigenous culture, with day trips possible to Hlgu Isgwit Hot Springs and the Nisga'a Lava Bed Park. Tourism infrastructure is basic and the pace is slow, but the setting is genuinely special.
cc44450192: A Mosaic Forest Management lakeside campsite on northern Vancouver Island, reached via active forestry roads; rustic and quiet with a lake as the main draw.
ac6812fdaa: A dry-camping lake site within the fee-based West Harrison recreation system on the west shore of Harrison Lake; family-oriented and pet-friendly, but specific amenities for Wood Lake itself are not detailed in the available page text.
cfca919151: A 4-site walk-in cluster at Green Lake Park's Sunset View area in the Cariboo, beside a warm, shallow 14 km lake with sandy beaches and roped swimming areas; powerboats dominate the main lake, but the carry-in keeps the immediate sites quieter.
ee8f33ca52: A riverside campground in Golden, BC — a cycling hub at the confluence of the Kicking Horse and Columbia Rivers. Amenities and road conditions are unconfirmed as the campground website was unreachable.
816f06fb7b: Big Bar Lake Park sits in the southern Cariboo against a mountain backdrop, offering lakeside camping with a beach, rainbow trout fishing, and a wetland interpretive trail; the 34 km gravel access road is the main hurdle for loaded cyclists.
c8ef16191d: A Mosaic Forest Management campsite beside Macktush Creek in central Vancouver Island's working forest; expect gravel logging-road access and basic or no facilities, with no confirmed drinking water.
9ffe74de82: A remote wilderness campsite at Bare Loon Lake in northern BC or Yukon; no facilities are confirmed and the source page was unavailable, so treat this as a self-sufficient backcountry stop with uncertain access.
e4a18d0796: Remote backcountry camp in central Vancouver Island's rugged Strathcona Park region, reachable only by hike-in or equivalent non-road access — effectively off the table for loaded touring cyclists. Washrooms confirmed on site; no fee, water, or season details available.
7cdc3b7ba2: Witset RV Park and Campground serves the community of Witset (formerly Moricetown), a Wet'suwet'en First Nation community situated along Highway 16 in the Bulkley Valley of northern BC. The campground is a practical stop for cycle tourists riding the Yellowhead corridor between Prince Rupert and Prince George. Its location near the Witset Canyon, a culturally significant salmon fishing site, adds interest for touring cyclists passing through.
459bfb457c: A small 8-site wilderness campground in the remote Chilcotin, associated with Ts'il?os Provincial Park near Chilko Lake; reached via long gravel roads and suited to self-sufficient riders comfortable with limited services.
95448a2006: Shuswap Lake Park's group camp sits beside a one-kilometre sandy beach on Shuswap Lake, with an adventure playground, boat launch, and hiking trail on site; it runs at capacity July through Labour Day, so expect a busy, social atmosphere rather than quiet.
d2a8db985a: A compact 7-site park in riverside cottonwoods just north of Oliver, positioned as a tenter-friendly base for cycling the International Hike and Bike Trail or riding to South Okanagan wineries. The park itself offers little beyond bird watching and a short dike walk; abundant poison ivy keeps you on the paths.
64451d5774: Lakeside BC Parks campground at the north end of Christina Lake — reputed one of Canada's warmest and clearest — with pocket beaches, short trails to the water, and a Monashee Mountains backdrop. Fully reservable with 63 sites, showers, and flush toilets; accessed via paved Hwy 3 and closed by a seasonal gate in fall.
7b90e7e4f6: A boat-in lakeside camp on Alouette Lake within Golden Ears Park's rugged backcountry, offering 16 sites in coastal hemlock forest with pit toilets; reachable only by paddle craft, so inaccessible to touring cyclists but a genuine wilderness retreat.
abfb29888d: A trailhead staging campground deep within Strathcona Park — BC's oldest provincial park and a 250,000-hectare mountain wilderness — suited to hikers and backpackers pushing into the alpine; hard vehicle access and a short snow-free window make it a committed stop, not a casual one.
dad8b7d5b5: Vetter Creek Campground sits inside Nisg̱a'a Memorial Lava Bed Park, where one of BC's youngest lava flows meets old-growth forest and First Nations cultural sites, with guided tours to the volcanic crater; the primary approach via paved Nisg̱a'a Highway is manageable on a loaded bike, though it is 100 km north of Terrace with services only in the adjacent Nisg̱a'a villages. An alternate route uses 86 km of unpaved Nass Forest Service Road — rideable but rough.
fc74675fc5: A small 11-site campground within Skagit Valley Provincial Park, reached via roughly 60 km of loose-surface gravel road through active logging country; potable water on site, but access is seasonal and the gate closes off-season.
a57039bb7c: A premier Vancouver Island park where old-growth forest meets 2 km of warm sandy beach, with all campsites a five-minute walk from the water and tide-warmed swimming at high tide; extremely popular in summer and reservations are required.
acea4d20b0: A busy lakeside park 12 km north of Quesnel on paved Highway 97, offering three sandy beaches, flush toilets, showers, and rainbow trout fishing; campground gates close off-season so access is summer only.
75760599dd: A legendary stop on the Alaska Highway, Liard River Hot Springs gives touring cyclists access to Canada's second-largest hot spring — a geothermal pool in lush boreal forest — though the 53-site campground fills before noon most summer days.
af19b81d96: A remote backcountry wilderness set on Kakwa Lake beneath 3000m peaks and sweeping alpine meadows on the Continental Divide; mountain bikes can ride the final Tote Road section but the first 75km from the staging site requires a 4x4 high-clearance vehicle, and no potable water is available at the park.
79a137b15e: Lakeside provincial campground in Birkenhead Lake Park reached via 17 km of gravel road, set among old-growth forest with mountain views across the lake; bears are very active and the gravel approach is rough for loaded bikes.
89520b1ecc: Buckhorn is a hike-in backcountry campground in E.C. Manning Park, located more than 1 km from any highway within the Cascade Mountains; a $5-per-person nightly permit fee applies, and advance reservations are required during peak summer season. Loaded bikes cannot access it — this is a foot-only wilderness overnight in one of BC's most popular backcountry parks.
33da7dc22e: One of five campgrounds within Whiteswan Lake Park in the Kootenay Rockies, Home Basin offers mountain-lake scenery and access to Lussier Hot Springs; the approach is a gravel forest service road shared with mine ore trucks and logging trucks, with a technically demanding canyon section requiring extreme caution.
7ad33af283: A municipal campground beside Hirsch Creek in Kitimat, offering a basic overnight base in an industrial port town at the end of a paved highway spur off Hwy 16; facilities and amenities are unconfirmed.
47d5bb21f8: Family-run resort campground beside Highway 3 in Erickson, set above the Goat River with flush showers, a playground, general store, and regular live-music events; highway noise carries into the sites.
85773329cf: Spapium "Little Prairie" Farm is a Nlaka'pamux-owned heritage farm located at the historic junction of the Thompson and Fraser Rivers near Lytton, BC, operating on land farmed since 1882. The farm offers ten spacious campsites across five acres alongside cultural farm tours, cedar bark weaving workshops, and heritage produce. Touring cyclists will find a uniquely immersive indigenous cultural experience in the dramatic Fraser Canyon landscape.
ded65316bc: A small community-managed park on a rocky Strait of Georgia shoreline tucked into a quiet Comox neighbourhood, offering mainland views and shade under mature Douglas firs; no designated swim area and no sani-station on site.
1544dd4153: Wigeon Lake sits deep inside Pinecone Burke Provincial Park, reachable only by paddling across Pitt Lake and hiking up Widgeon Creek — firmly out of reach for a loaded touring bike. The wilderness lake is a salmon-country gem with no services: treat all water, pack out all waste, and no campfires are permitted anywhere in the park.
e4cd2ab9a0: A backcountry bivy site within Elk Lakes Park, set amid sub-alpine glaciers, rugged peaks, and productive lakes in the southern Rocky Mountains; no potable water or supplies available, and the approach involves active logging roads with industrial traffic.
a5deb1bbd2: San Josef Recreation Area serves as the trailhead base for San Josef Bay within Cape Scott Park, surrounded by old-growth Sitka Spruce and Western Red Cedar at Vancouver Island's remote northwestern tip; access is via logging road with active truck traffic.
432bacf3af: A 26-site lakeside campground on a quiet 3 km lake east of Greenwood, best known for stocked rainbow trout fly fishing and flat-water paddling; the 12 km approach off Hwy 3 is mostly paved with the final 1.5 km on gravel.
075297d40b: Raven's Nest Resort is a family-run nature retreat nestled in BC's Columbia Valley on ʔAkisq̓nuk First Nation land, offering tent camping, van and RV sites, glamping domes, and log cabins. The campground opened in 2019 and has grown to include an 18-hole disc golf course, a shared bathroom building with flush toilets and showers, and scenic mountain surroundings near Fairmont Hot Springs. Touring cyclists will find a welcoming, pet-friendly base with fire rings, picnic tables, and easy access to the Columbia Valley's riding terrain.
4899474e98: A well-run private campground on Hwy 20 in Hagensborg, set along the Bella Coola River with a river viewing deck and snow-capped mountain backdrops; flush toilets, showers, and Wi-Fi make it one of the best-equipped stops in the valley. Seasonal only — open late May to mid-October.
89b4e2696e: A group campsite attributed to E.C. Manning Park in the Cascade Mountains, accessible from Highway 3; confirmed amenities include showers, potable water, and device charging, but the specific Lone Duck site is absent from available park prose — season is snow-dependent and the park has no cellphone service.
19318dcaef: Full-service RV resort on Osoyoos Lake with a private sandy beach, lake views, flush washrooms, and year-round operation; tent camping is explicitly not permitted, making this a skip for most touring cyclists unless arriving by RV or renting an on-site unit.
29c4462c88: A remote spruce-forest camp run by Tyax Adventures in BC's Cariboo/Chilcotin, likely near Tyaughton Lake in the Gold Bridge area; access involves long gravel roads and amenity details are unconfirmed as the operator website was unavailable.
cc2d5a03fe: An RV park attached to Golden's golf club, likely on the valley floor near the Columbia River with mountain surrounds; facilities and services are unconfirmed as the campground's website returned a 404 error.
00f1c89aae: A 22-site provincial campground on Allison Lake in the Okanagan-Thompson region, offering a calm lakeside stay with potable water and washrooms; gate closes at season's end so plan arrival accordingly.
af77d377c8: Ralph River Campground occupies a forested valley inside Strathcona Provincial Park — BC's oldest park and a 250,000-hectare mountain wilderness — offering a large developed basecamp near Buttle Lake for hiking, fishing, and alpine exploration on a summer operating season.
9cebb21f26: A backcountry wilderness campsite deep in the Purcell Wilderness Conservancy, reached through rugged terrain with unbridged stream crossings, grizzly bear country, no potable water, and no supplies of any kind — strictly for experienced, self-sufficient wilderness travellers.
187af900cc: A municipal campground on Logan Lake with 50 lakeview sites, flush washrooms, hot showers, and potable water — but only two designated tent sites at $28/night plus a $7 resort fee, so availability for cyclists is tight. Walking distance to trails, disc golf, a bike park, and a waterpark makes it an activity-rich overnight in a small Thompson-area town.
5e3a5d8ff7: A tidy highway wayside on the Buckinghorse River at km 278 of the Alaska Highway, offering river swimming, arctic grayling fishing, and reliable moose and bear sightings in the northern Rocky Mountain foothills; cooperatively managed with basic facilities and a gate-controlled season from late May through September.
1661e6d340: Walk-in campground on the scenic narrows of Shuswap Lake, offering 28 sites with potable water and washrooms in a sheltered lakeside setting; loaded touring bikes cannot be ridden directly to the sites from the parking area.
709778c193: A full-service private campground managed by the K'ómoks First Nation, set along the Puntledge River and within a 10-15 minute walk of downtown Courtenay; showers, laundry, and a camp store on site, but note that the lower campground and river access are currently closed for ongoing construction.
9e39c8c05e: Colonel Creek is a remote BC interior forest service-style site reachable only by high-clearance or 4x4 vehicle; expect no confirmed amenities, no drinking water, and a raw backcountry overnight with no frills.
a116603cc7: A large mid-elevation grassland park southwest of Kamloops anchored by two stocked rainbow trout lakes, with 275 campsites across three campgrounds and paved access; curious marmots are abundant and known to chew gear and damage vehicles.
f007f2e8b1: Lakeshore Campground is the Columbia Valley's largest lakefront campground and the only one situated directly on the shores of Lake Windermere, operated by the ʔakisq̓nuk First Nation on Ktunaxa territory with over 10,000 years of Indigenous history. It offers 14 serviced lots with 30-amp electrical, 51 non-serviced lots, and 62 seasonal sites, with mountain views, lake access, showers, walking trails, and a playground. Touring cyclists will find nearby trail networks (Mount Swansea, Old Coach Trail, Westside Legacy Trail) just minutes away, plus easy access to Radium Hot Springs and Invermere.
352de8b2c3: Kwakiutl First Nation–owned riverfront resort where the Cluxewe River meets Broughton Strait, near Port McNeill on northern Vancouver Island, with 123 sites and cabins in a historically significant setting well-suited for fishing, birding, and wildlife watching. Seasonal operation (roughly May–October); washroom type and exact road surface unconfirmed.
8fd3879aa8: An RV park in Tumbler Ridge serving as a functional base for the UNESCO Global Geopark region, with dinosaur trackways, waterfalls, and extensive trail networks nearby; no campground-specific details were available from the retrieved pages.
984be1e431: A backcountry beach campsite on the Juan de Fuca Marine Trail, set on a wild Pacific shore with surf and marine wildlife views; access is hike-in only on a rugged trail prone to storm closures, making it a skip for loaded touring bikes.
f5a4c1e825: A campground in BC's Cariboo, Chilcotin & Central Interior region; no website text was retrieved, so setting, facilities, and access remain unconfirmed from available sources.
e222816307: North Beach Campground is one of three large campgrounds in Golden Ears Park, a major provincial destination about an hour east of Vancouver with Alouette Lake swimming, paddling rentals, and an extensive hiking trail network. It draws big summer crowds and has no cell service on site.
7f9bd52c83: A developed 44-site BC Parks campground on Swan Lake in Northern BC, with potable water, a covered shelter, and washroom facilities; the gate closes when snow falls, so access is limited to the snow-free season.
81faab2615: Boat-access-only campground on Alouette Lake's east shore within Golden Ears Provincial Park; a secluded forested lakeshore setting that is unreachable by loaded bike—watercraft required.
f5010b4d41: Cahill Lake is a backcountry, trail-access campground within Valhalla Provincial Park, set amid the majestic peaks and alpine terrain of the Selkirk Mountains; stocked fishing is a draw, but the hike-in approach rules it out for loaded touring bikes.
8654a5db16: Small BC Parks campground on Upper Arrow Lake in the Kootenays, sitting close to the free Shelter Bay–Galena Bay ferry crossing; washrooms and potable water on site, but no services outside the operating season.
852768ea37: Sikanni River Ranch is a wilderness guest ranch nestled in the Sikanni River Valley of northern BC, surrounded by the Canadian Rocky Mountains, offering a mix of handcrafted log lodges and backcountry cabins. The ranch caters to adventurous travellers with activities including trail rides, ATV rides, snowmobiling, fishing, non-guided hunting, and hiking. A touring cyclist seeking remote northern BC accommodation would find multiple bookable units, on-site meals, and a sauna after a long day in the saddle.
5ce02cdb2e: A backcountry wilderness campsite deep in the Purcell Wilderness Conservancy, reachable only by multi-day hike through rugged glaciated terrain with unbridged stream crossings and active grizzly habitat — wholly impractical for a loaded touring bike.
98efead3ae: Small resort campsite on Moresby Island, Haida Gwaii, with four dry camping spots a short walk from the beach and full access to the on-site restaurant, nordic sauna, golf course, and pickleball courts. Reaching the island requires a BC Ferries connection from Prince Rupert or a flight into Sandspit Airport, making this a true edge-of-the-world stop.
19fbd93b4c: A boutique luxury glamping resort in Tlell on Haida Gwaii, with 10 cedar prospector tents (4 ocean-facing, 6 in the rainforest), each with a private ensuite and deck; complimentary breakfast, cedar spa tub, and geodesic dome kitchen are included, but rates are premium and the site is mid-spring to fall only — reachable by BC Ferries from Prince Rupert.
4ea5bfc9b6: An RV-oriented leisure park near Charlie Lake in Northern BC; with the website unavailable, details on tent sites, facilities, and access are unconfirmed — verify before routing here.
4525b2d1d9: A sunny Kootenay park set in ponderosa pine and Douglas fir forest, built around Surveyors Lake's warm, sandy swimming beach with on-site kayak and paddleboard rentals; paved internal park roads make it an easy roll for loaded touring bikes.
b71152bc30: Loop Brook Campground offers frontcountry trailer and tent sites in Glacier National Park, right at Rogers Pass and accessible from the Trans-Canada Highway; a national park pass plus camping permit are required, and strict bear-safe food storage is mandatory.
b3fb36b2fe: A municipal campground on the banks of the Kicking Horse River in the heart of downtown Golden, BC, with walkable access to restaurants, shops, and a pool across the street; primarily an RV park with some riverside tent spots, open from April, and train noise is a noted drawback at night.
adb5c9cea4: A municipal campground in Kitimat on BC's North Coast; details are unconfirmed as the city parks page returned a 404 error, so expect basic amenities typical of a small-city facility.
ab1baa09ad: Full-amenity frontcountry campground in Mount Robson Park along Highway 16, with the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies overhead; showers, e-bike charging, and potable water on site, but seasonal park gates mean summer-only access.
69b85d0309: A private campground and golf course 3 km outside Valemount, with grassy tent sites beside Swift Creek and the McLennan River under mountain views; flush bathrooms and filtered drinking water are included, tent sites from $34/night plus taxes.
9e7d97bfc2: Commercial resort on Spahats Creek Forest Service Road at the gateway to Wells Gray Provincial Park, directly across from Spahats Falls Day Use Area, with serviced and unserviced sites, showers, laundry, and Wi-Fi; a natural basecamp for the park's waterfalls and Trophy Mountain flower meadows, but the FSR approach means a rough ride in with loaded bags.
012157c6ff: Frontcountry campground on the Alaska Highway in Stone Mountain Park's remote northern Rockies, with dramatic mountain scenery and strong wildlife viewing; cash-only fees, seasonal gate closure (walk-in off-season only), and rapidly changing weather require preparation.
0b78ab5898: A large year-round private RV park on 20 wooded acres just north of Courtenay, with 10 quiet tent-only sites and a direct trail into Seal Bay Nature Park; primarily an RV facility with coin showers and WiFi, so expect a suburban campground feel.
6a8a362a2d: Small user-maintained lakeshore campsite on Kitsumkalum Lake, reached via a short gravel road off the Nisga'a Highway 25 km north of Terrace; sandy beach for swimming and good paddling, but pit toilet only with no potable water — bring your own.
7ef63a20b4: A remote wilderness campsite at Phillip Lake in the Cariboo region, reachable only by non-vehicle means; the hard approach rules it out for loaded tourers, and facilities are minimal despite a fee.
1c7b15394c: A Mosaic Forest Management campsite on northern Vancouver Island, accessed via logging or forest service road; reservations are accepted but site-specific details on setting and amenities are not available from current sources.
d9ec6a6d78: A private resort on 200 feet of sandy beach between Courtenay and Campbell River, offering calm east-coast swimming, full-hookup RV sites, flush showers, and laundry; open year-round but July–August requires minimum weekly bookings.
6345568e40: A flat, full-service campground at the Williams Lake Stampede rodeo grounds in town, with hookups, WiFi, and laundry; tenting is available but the site has no natural appeal — it earns its keep during the annual Stampede rodeo weekend.
cbd3d28c36: A BC Parks campsite whose name suggests a birch-fringed beach in the Cariboo–Chilcotin interior; no scraped page text is available, so details on access, facilities, and fees remain unconfirmed.

f9d0086500: Hike-in backcountry camp at Flora Lake within Sx̱ótsaqel/Chilliwack Lake Park, set amid old-growth forested slopes and spectacular subalpine terrain 150 km east of Vancouver. Advance backcountry registration required, no fires permitted, and no cell service once on park road.

b0f98bc964: A well-serviced BC Parks campground on Highway 97 in the Cariboo, with flush toilets, tap water, and a sani-station; the lake beach, playground, and boat launch are across the highway in a separate day-use area. f6dc30c1a3: Lorna Lake sits inside South Chilcotin Mountains Park, a staffed-facility-free wilderness zone with no potable water, frequent grizzly activity, and rapidly changing alpine weather — every visitor must be fully self-sufficient and filter water from the lake or streams. 53b6bfa254: A 42-site BC Parks beach campground in the Cariboo interior with potable water and washrooms; the gate closes off-season, making this a summer-only stop.

e40a6127b6: A remote wilderness campsite on Fight Lake in the Wells Gray area, reachable only by hard off-road travel; no confirmed amenities or water on record, making it a true backcountry overnight with nothing guaranteed.

4da7474092: A Boston Bar First Nation campground in the Fraser Canyon, set between the Fraser River and Anderson Creek with mountain and water views, full facilities including flush toilets and showers, and a Nlaka'pamux Heritage Village on-site; riverside and creekside sites are closed through late May due to spring runoff, and the season runs April to October.

713586f257: A fee-based lakeside campsite on Mosaic Forest Management timberlands in south Vancouver Island, almost certainly reached via active logging or gravel forest service road; amenities are unconfirmed and the booking page yields minimal detail.

fb8b83595e: Small free Forest Service rec site on Meadow Lake reached via Pelican FSR and the '56' Road; draws anglers after wild rainbow trout and hunters in fall, but the tight FSR approach, swampy shoreline, and minimal amenities make it a niche stop rather than a touring highlight.

fe8ee5fd22: A group-only site on a stocked fishing lake with a boat launch, dock, and 6 km loop trail; the steep, rough Forest Service Road explicitly requires 4x4 and is not suitable for loaded touring bikes. Open March 15–October 31, cash only, gates locked at 11 PM.

0083b2f1fb: True Grain is an organic craft bakery that has been handcrafting sourdough loaves, pastries, and cookies in the seaside village of Cowichan Bay since 2004, using 100% BC-farmed organic grain that the team stone-mills on-site in the Cowichan Valley. The bakery follows a farm-to-mill-to-baker model rooted in European tradition, working with ancient and heritage grains like Einkorn, Emmer, Spelt, and Red Fife with no additives or preservatives. It has grown into a destination for bread lovers exploring Vancouver Island, with in-store pickup, local home delivery, and Canada-wide mail order available.
8ba8d01974: 40 Knots is one of Vancouver Island's largest wineries, farming 24 acres of ocean-cooled vineyards in the Comox Valley. Visitors can explore interpretive trails, stroll gardens, or relax on a terrace with vineyard and ocean views while tasting sustainably produced wines. The winery emphasizes organic and biodynamic farming practices shaped by its proximity to the Salish Sea.
027ccf886c: Peak Cellars is an award-winning, cool-climate winery in Lake Country's Okanagan Valley, producing estate-grown wines recognized internationally — including a Gold Medal Chardonnay at the 2025 Chardonnay du Monde. The property includes a Garden Bistro serving farm-to-table seasonal dishes sourced from an on-site garden, a tasting room with guided premium seated tastings overlooking the vineyard and lake, and on-site accommodations. It is a full-destination stop on the Okanagan wine trail, offering a relaxed, scenic environment well suited to cycling visitors.
91f718a058: Île Sauvage — French for 'Wild Island' — is a Victoria craft brewery specialising exclusively in Belgian-style wild ales and sour beers, using Kveik, Lactobacillus, and Brettanomyces fermentations alongside oak-ageing vessels and local fruit refermentations. The name pays dual homage to the wilderness of Vancouver Island and the wild-fermentation philosophy at the heart of every batch. Cyclists passing through Victoria's inner harbour area can stop at the Bridge Street tasting room for on-site pours or pick up canned releases to take on the road.
f9e76e560b: A full-service restaurant and brewpub situated in View Royal along the Island Highway, housed in what the domain name 'fourmilehouse' suggests is a historic roadhouse building. The on-site brewery produces a rotating lineup of year-round and seasonal beers — from a light lager and West Coast IPA to a non-alcoholic option — all available on draft in the pub. The venue also includes the '4 Below' sports bar, a High Tea program, and weekend brunch, making it an unusually varied stop for cyclists passing through the western edge of Greater Victoria.
013c4d5937: Red Truck Brewery Company is a craft brewery located in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, producing beer on-site. Situated on East 1st Avenue, it occupies a standalone building and is likely a destination-style taproom typical of the neighbourhood's brewery scene. Touring cyclists riding through the area may find it a natural stop for a post-ride pint in one of Vancouver's most bike-friendly districts.
5122aacf55: Divino Estate Winery is a 100% estate winery on a 40-acre Cobble Hill vineyard, tracing its roots to owner-winemaker Joe Busnardo's original Oliver, BC operation in the early 1980s before relocating to the Cowichan Valley in 1996. The winery produces Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Pinot Grigio, Trebbiano, and a rotating cast of limited-release and late-harvest wines entirely from estate-grown fruit, with some rare old vintages only available on-site. Situated just off the Island Highway at the Cowichan Bay Road exit, it sits conveniently between Victoria and Nanaimo for cyclists riding the Vancouver Crossing Loop.
f76ce48247: Electric Bicycle Brewing is a craft brewery and tasting room in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, named with an unmistakable nod to cycling culture. The taproom offers a rotating lineup of house beers spanning pilsners, pale ales, hazy IPAs, sours, and nitro stouts, served in a social space with high tops, booths, and long communal tables. It pitches itself as a lively destination with music and a welcoming atmosphere — a natural stop for cyclists exploring the area.
75fc5bedfd: Kalala Organic Estate Winery is an award-winning, certified-organic estate winery situated on the upper bench of West Kelowna in the Okanagan Valley, producing VQA wines from grapes hand-picked from its own organic vineyards since 2006. It holds one of the largest portfolios of organic Icewines in British Columbia and has garnered gold medals at competitions including Chardonnay du Monde in France. Visitors can book guided vineyard tours and wine tastings at the on-site tasting room.
12ffc7552a: Hester Creek Estate Winery is one of the oldest wine properties in the South Okanagan, with 58 years of history on the Golden Mile Bench wine route just outside Oliver. Cyclists can stop in for a complimentary tasting at the wine shop, enjoy a sit-down meal at the on-site Terrafina Restaurant, or extend their stay at the luxury Villa. Award-winning estate wines and vineyard views make it a standout destination on the Okanagan's wine-country cycling circuit.
01dcc99902: Sage Hayward Vineyards is a family-owned estate winery and bistro on Saturna Island in BC's Southern Gulf Islands, with vines first planted in 1995 in clay soils layered with ancient marine sediment. The property includes a seasonal tasting room and the Feral Goat Bistro, led by Chef Lee Yarrow and focused on locally sourced, seasonal ingredients paired with estate wines. Situated on a dramatic south-facing sea bench between sheer cliffs and ocean currents, it is accessible by BC Ferries, seaplane, or private boat — including via the property's own dock and mooring buoys.
796da14c8f: The View Winery & Vineyard is a family-owned estate winery housed in a restored 1920s apple packing house in East Kelowna, perched above Okanagan Lake with views of Black Knight and Dilworth Mountains. The winery has been on Ward family land for five generations and produces award-winning cool-climate whites, fruit-forward reds, and Wards Cider from its heritage orchards. Walk-in tastings are available seven days a week, and seasonal guided vineyard hikes, Sunday live music sessions, and occasional food trucks make it one of the more animated stops on the Okanagan wine route.
bb84342be5: Howe Sound Inn & Brewing is Squamish's original craft brewery, founded in 1996 with the help of John Mitchell, the 'grandfather of micro-brewing,' and named Canadian Brewery of the Year in 2022. The flagship Squamish location operates as a full-service brewpub with a kitchen serving stone-fired pizzas, burgers, and shareables, alongside an on-site inn with pet-friendly rooms. Situated in the heart of Sea to Sky Country at the midpoint between Vancouver and Whistler, it is a natural gathering spot for cyclists travelling the corridor.
3c1ffc8186: Dirty Laundry Winery is a Summerland destination celebrating 20 years of award-winning BC wines, with Gold medals at national and international competitions across multiple varietals. The property features an on-site Red Iron Grille with self-serve patio kiosks offering pizza and smoked meats alongside the tasting bar and wine shop. It sits on the Bottleneck Drive wine route, making it a natural midday stop for cyclists touring the Okanagan's wine country.
5e9231207f: House of Rose Winery is a craft winery and wine shop located on Garner Road in Kelowna, situated in British Columbia's Okanagan Valley — one of Canada's premier wine regions. The winery is noted as a standout stop on guided wine tours of the Kelowna area. Touring cyclists exploring the region's vineyard routes and the nearby Kettle Valley Rail Trail would find it a natural waypoint.
4d2b756654: Whistler's craft brewery features a taphouse with a full menu of snacks and pizzas alongside their award-winning beers, including BC's first craft gluten-free lager. They also offer brewery tours and growler fills on-site at their Millar Creek Road location south of Whistler Village.
480b95b807: Backcountry Brewing is a craft brewery, tasting room, and kitchen that opened in Squamish in 2017, winning 'Rookie of the Year' at the BC Beer Awards with medals for all three core beers. The 70s ski cabin-inspired tasting room pairs an inventive menu of pizzas, salads, and snacks with more than 50 limited-edition beers released annually, plus a retail store stocked with cans and branded merchandise. A shipping container patio and a 38-seat Barrel Lounge round out a space well-suited to post-ride celebrations.
2f4f727af9: Crown & Thieves is a small-batch winery built inside a striking four-story faux-ruin tucked into the vines of West Kelowna, operated by winemaker Jason Parkes. Part of the Westside Wine Trail, it offers tastings, a rooftop patio with vineyard views, and a speakeasy-style venue called The Broken Hearts Club hosting live music, comedy, and cabaret. It's an eccentric, memorable stop for cyclists touring the Okanagan wine country.
31082b6ecb: Take THE Cake is a bakery business located in Richmond, BC, suggested by its URL domain. Beyond its name and approximate location, no verified details about its offerings, setting, or cyclist-relevant features are available from current evidence.
795ad46125: Wolf Brewing Company is a craft brewery and taproom in Nanaimo, Vancouver Island, serving small-batch beers on 10+ taps including a nitro pour from their on-site brewery. Their kitchen turns spent brewing grain into pizza crust, and local Vancouver Island artists design each beer label. The dog-friendly patio, live music nights, and proximity to the Nanaimo Ferry Terminals and Airport make it a natural gathering point for cyclists arriving on or departing the island.
f05c0183dd: Abandoned Rail Brewing Co. is a family-run estate brewery on the Naramata Bench where the owners farm their own barley to produce European-inspired, award-winning craft beers. The taproom sits alongside the Kettle Valley Rail Trail with sweeping bench views, explicitly positioned as a 20-minute bike ride from downtown Penticton and a natural trail stop. A kitchen serves pizza alongside an extensive tap list that includes a certified gluten-free sorghum-based pale ale, and a Guest House is available for overnight stays.
550dfb6fb1: Bomber Brewing is an East Vancouver craft brewery and taproom situated on Adanac Street, one of the city's most-used cycling routes. The taproom pours a rotating lineup of Czech-style lagers, IPAs, sours, and stouts alongside a food truck (B'SHAKE BURGER), making it a natural rest stop for cyclists passing through East Van. Package sales and delivery via Uber Eats and DoorDash are also available.
71e5f326ff: Volcanic Hills Estate Winery is a three-generation family estate winery perched on the southeast slope of Mt. Boucherie, a 60-million-year-old dormant volcano whose rich volcanic soils inspired the name. The Gidda family has been growing grapes here since 1978, producing a wide range of wines including whites, reds, icewine, and fruit wines, with tastings available by reservation or walk-in. Seasonal events such as yoga-and-bubbles mornings and wedding hosting make it a lively destination on the Okanagan wine route.
a6d4d07bb2: Okanagan Crush Pad is a Summerland-based winery producing organic wines under several labels including Haywire, Garnet Valley Ranch, and Free Form. Haywire's modern tasting lounge overlooks Okanagan Lake and Switchback Organic Vineyard, while Garnet Valley Ranch is a 320-acre working farm with lavender fields, vineyards, and a separate visitor centre open by appointment. Both venues host weddings and music events, making them notable destinations on the Okanagan wine-country cycling circuit.
e9f601c028: Founded in 2019 by the South African Joubert family, Wesbert Winery cultivates over a dozen grape varieties on two Naramata Bench vineyards to produce award-winning wines, including a Double Gold Merlot. The winery sits near the road crossing of the Kettle Valley Rail Trail and describes itself as a favourite among cyclists and hikers. Visitors can book a tasting, enjoy wood-fired pizza on the terrace, or stay overnight in one of three guest suites overlooking the Okanagan hills.
d6b1d6aca5: Salt Spring Vineyards is a craft winery and wine retail shop situated at 151 Lee Road on Salt Spring Island, BC. As one of the Gulf Islands' estate wineries, it draws visitors seeking locally produced wines in a rural island setting. Touring cyclists completing Salt Spring Island's wine route may find it a natural stop along a scenic ride.
2c3c52fa68: Parallel 49 Brewing is a Vancouver craft brewery founded in 2012, recognised as one of BC's early leaders in the craft beer movement. Their on-site Street Kitchen is billed as one of BC's largest craft brewery restaurants, with 40+ beers on tap and a fully stocked indoor food truck concept. An on-site retail beer store carries the full range of releases, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking to resupply with local craft beer.
6a88013b41: A boutique family-run winery in the heart of the Naramata Bench, founded in 2005 by Judy Kingston and now operated with her daughter Katie as head winemaker. The property features a wine shop with tastings, plus an on-site bistro called Terroir Kitchen offering seasonal, locally-sourced food paired with their estate wines. Named BC Winery of the Year and known for small-lot reds including Syrah, Merlot, and Pinot Noir.
5f94987b4a: Neighbourhood Brewing is an independently owned craft brewery in downtown Penticton with a tasting room and a kitchen serving Mexican-inspired food. They offer a wide range of beers from hazy IPAs to sours, and the brewery features a seasonal outdoor patio that's dog-friendly and great for people-watching. Family-friendly and centrally located on Westminster Avenue, it's a natural stop for cyclists exploring Penticton's brewery scene.
d1aebbb7a1: Brassneck Brewery is an independent craft brewery with a walk-in tasting room and growler shop on Vancouver's Main Street, offering a rotating tap list of eclectic styles ranging from tart barrel-aged fruit beers to an 11% Chocolate Banana Imperial Milkshake Stout. The brewery fills growlers from other breweries as well, making it a handy stop for cyclists wanting to stock up. Food is available from their sister restaurant The Magnet, including options to take home.
4ba88865cf: Streetcar Brewing is a craft brewery in North Vancouver producing beer. As a local brewery, it would offer touring cyclists a place to sample locally made beers and take a break from the road. Its North Vancouver location puts it within reach of popular cycling routes on the North Shore.
b053bd2571: Shawnigan House Coffee + Chocolate has been serving the Shawnigan Lake community since 2000, offering globally sourced coffee alongside house-made artisan chocolates crafted with Belgian and organic ingredients. Located on the Shawnigan Lake-Mill Bay Road, it is a natural stop for cyclists riding the Vancouver Crossing Loop through the Cowichan Valley. The shop sells individual truffles and chocolate bars as well as a full espresso menu, making it an easy place to refuel with something sweet.
02d94d264a: Batch 44 is a family-owned craft brewery and full-service kitchen on Sechelt's waterfront, pouring award-winning house beers alongside cocktails, BC wines, and cider. A dog-friendly patio, long communal tables, and a broad menu from poutine to fresh tuna poke make it an inviting gathering spot on the Sunshine Coast. Regular community events — trivia nights, karaoke, and Rock and Roll Bingo — give it a lively local character.
d0bf459b18: Logjam Coffee is Kamloops' original specialty coffee roaster, founded in 2020 in a humble cabin and now running a cafe out of the city's iconic pink building on the North Shore at 437 Tranquille Rd. They roast small-batch, single-origin coffees at their roastery in the hills of Knutsford above the city, with roastery tours available by request. Cyclists on the Lac du Bois Tranquility route will find this an appealing stop for quality espresso and locally roasted beans.
62266327f2: SummerGate Winery is a family-run organic estate winery established in 2009 by the Stohler family, producing 100% BC wine from certified-organic grapes grown on their own Prairie Valley property in Summerland. Located along Summerland's Bottleneck Drive wine route, the property features a family- and pet-friendly licensed patio with picnic area, a weekend kitchen with food service including Sunday waffle breakfasts, and wine tastings of their specialty white, rosé, and frizzante-style wines. It is a natural and convivial rest stop on one of the Okanagan's most popular cycling corridors.

049052d682: Cliffside Cider is a small-batch cidery located in Squamish, BC, producing cider on-site at a unit on Second Avenue. Squamish sits at the gateway to the Sea-to-Sky corridor, making it a natural stop for cyclists riding between Vancouver and Whistler. No current web presence could be confirmed, so the operating status of this taproom is uncertain.
4e143b2326: Granville Island Brewing has been crafting BC beers since 1984 and is one of the province's pioneering craft breweries, with a vibrant public taproom on Granville Island at the heart of Vancouver's seawall cycling network. The taproom pours a rotating small-batch Taproom Series alongside its mainline beers, and serves food on-site with off-sales for those continuing their ride. The patio is dog-friendly and the brewery is wheelchair accessible via a ramp through the side door.
356e855497: The Six Mile Pub & Eatery, established in 1855, is British Columbia's oldest pub, occupying a historic building along Old Island Highway just west of Victoria. The kitchen produces everything in-house — artisan breads raised from named sourdough starters, fresh pasta, and charcuterie — while an on-site apiary supplies honey used throughout the menu and in signature cocktails. A multiple-time Times Colonist Readers' Choice winner, it welcomes patrons of all ages and offers a seasonal riverside patio.
91c5da1eba: Cedar Cafe is a cafe nestled inside the Museum of Anthropology on the UBC campus, on the traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Musqueam people. It offers espresso drinks made from locally roasted beans, sandwiches, bannock, and artisanal pastries in a setting surrounded by one of Canada's premier Indigenous art collections. For cyclists riding the UBC loop or exploring Point Grey, it is a culturally distinctive spot to refuel mid-ride.
ddb344c0f7: The Woods Spirit Co. is a family-owned, female-led craft distillery on North Vancouver's North Shore, producing Italian-inspired liqueurs and spirits using a proprietary vacuum distillation process with 100% BC grain and locally sourced botanicals. Their Barrel-aged Amaro earned Best in Class at the 2026 CASC Awards, and the operation includes a cocktail lounge (Bar in The Woods), regular Friday distillery tours, and cocktail workshops. As a BC Green Business Certified enterprise, they prioritize sustainable production and community engagement.
db9651b276: Mariner Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom in Coquitlam specializing in a rotating lineup of house beers. The taproom includes a full kitchen focused on smash burgers, plus an outdoor patio that welcomes dogs. It hosts community events and actively donates to local causes, giving it a neighbourhood-hub character that touring cyclists passing through the Tri-Cities area may find welcoming.
5a22367e41: The Parkside Brewery is a craft brewery and tasting room on Port Moody's celebrated Brewer's Row, situated directly across from Rocky Point Park at the foot of Eagle Mountain. Beers are brewed on site with a regularly rotating lineup of award-winning ales, lagers, and IPAs, with cans and growler fills available to go. The front patio welcomes dogs, and food trucks are hosted outside on most days, making it a sociable stop at the head of Burrard Inlet.
df3cec3854: Vancouver Island's largest winery, Church and State Wines sits in Brentwood Bay just 15 minutes from downtown Victoria, pouring award-winning BC VQA wines grown exclusively on their own estate vineyards on Vancouver Island and in the Okanagan. The property features a tasting bar and a full bistro menu, plus a covered veranda and event programming that includes yoga in the vineyard and seasonal brunches. Named #1 Small Winery in British Columbia, it is a worthy scenic detour for cyclists riding the Saanich Peninsula near BC Ferries.
0c8f8b1aef: Sheringham Distillery is a small Vancouver Island craft distillery that won the world's largest gin competition and produces a range of award-winning gins, whisky, vodka, akvavit, and liqueurs. Visitors can explore the tasting room and sample spirits made with a chef-inspired, botanical-forward approach. The distillery production is rooted in Sooke using BC grain, with the tasting room located in Langford.
f96bac05b1: Beere Brewing is a family-run craft brewery on North Vancouver's waterfront, founded by a father-and-son duo who put their own name on every can. The tasting room pours a rotating lineup spanning hazy IPAs, West Coast IPAs, fruit sours, Italian-style pilsners, and a non-alcoholic pale ale. Beer is available to take home by the can or by the keg for private events, with a monthly subscription option for home delivery.
e430273bd6: Field House Brewing Co. opened its original tasting room in East Abbotsford in 2016 and is known for a constantly rotating tap list spanning crushable ales, experimental IPAs, and funky barrel-aged sours, with at least one new beer released every week. The Abbotsford location features a laid-back patio and beer lawn alongside a farm-to-table canteen, weekly live music, and a community run club. Non-alcoholic beer options are also on tap, making it a genuinely welcoming stop for cyclists who may not be drinking.
6211dbce8e: A coastal micro-brewery in the historic Townsite district of Powell River, on the shores of the Salish Sea along BC's Sunshine Coast. Known for Belgian-inspired craft beers, the tasting room pours a wide rotating selection including hazy pale ales, IPAs, stouts, and non-alcoholic options like craft soda and Nonny NA beer. The brewery is community-focused and also offers wine, cider, kombucha, and cocktails alongside its house brews.
cbc33f8978: Red Arrow Brewing Company is a craft brewery established in 2015 in the Cowichan Valley, operating a 35-seat taproom and a 65-seat outdoor patio at its Duncan location on Chaster Road. The brewery pours 12 of its own beers on tap alongside craft cocktails, local wines, and non-alcoholic options, all backed by a full-service food menu. The property also features a Sports Court used for concerts, fundraisers, and community events, giving it a strong community-hub character beyond a typical taproom.
5ce1819fa1: Millstone is a small family farm winery and vineyard situated in Nanaimo, crafting wines that reflect the unique character of Vancouver Island's coastal terroir. The estate offers tastings by appointment and regular walk-in hours, making it a relaxed rural stop for cyclists exploring the East Wellington area. As a working farm vineyard, it provides a distinctly local taste of BC wine country outside of the Okanagan.
3f844434d5: Longwood Brewery on Boxwood Road is an 'obsessively local' craft brewery sourcing most of its barley, hops, and other ingredients from Vancouver Island and the BC Mainland — named one of 'the most local of local breweries and beers in BC' by The Tyee Magazine. Its tasting room features a growler bar with 6 core beers and 4 rotating seasonals, plus a seasonal outdoor picnic patio that is pet and family friendly. Visitors are welcome to bring outside food, and the brewery also produces an alcohol-free, gluten-free Hop Soda for non-drinkers.
a8bfcf6ebf: A family-owned craft brewery in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood with two side-by-side tasting rooms on West 8th Avenue. Their core lineup spans amber lagers to Belgian tripels, including a World Beer Cup Silver Award-winning Belgian Tripel. Walk-in only with a casual, spacious atmosphere and seasonal food offerings.
3c8097d1f1: Frind Estate Winery is a large beachfront estate winery on the shores of Okanagan Lake in West Kelowna, self-described as the most-visited winery in Canada with over 10,000 guests weekly. The estate spans 400+ acres of vineyards across the Okanagan Valley, including the largest contiguous vineyard in BC. Touring cyclists can stop for lakeside wine tastings, casual meals at the Takeout Hut with picnic tables, or a full sit-down meal at the patio restaurant with lake views.
5240f3c0f6: Mission Hill Family Estate is a landmark Okanagan winery perched high above the valley with sweeping views of mountains, vineyards, and Okanagan Lake. Named Canada's Winery of the Year a record six times and listed among the World's 50 Best Vineyards in 2025, it offers curated tasting experiences, a fine-dining Terrace Restaurant, and a summer concert series in an outdoor amphitheatre. Access to the estate requires a reservation or membership, though same-day bookings are accommodated when space is available.
bdc1cf1add: La Frenz Winery is a family-owned estate established in 1999 on the celebrated Naramata Bench, farming 62 acres across six vineyards with varieties and clones deliberately matched to each site's soils and climate. It earned recognition as #1 Best Performing Small Winery of the Year and #2 Winery of the Year at the 2021 WineAlign National Wine Awards, making it one of the Okanagan's most decorated boutique producers. Cyclists riding the Naramata Bench wine route can stop at the wine shop for tasting flights and bottle purchases.
fcadd238e4: Seaside Pearl Farmgate Winery is a family-owned boutique farmgate winery set among rolling fields and quiet country roads in the Mount Lehman area of Abbotsford, BC. The winery produces small-lot, cool-climate artisanal wines from both estate-grown and Okanagan grapes, with labels named after local pioneer history. Tastings are held in a copper-spired chapel tasting room with panoramic Fraser Valley views, and a separate Barrel Room is available for events.
4101bf9b0e: Category 12 is a small-batch craft brewery and taproom on Keating Cross Road, brewing just 30 kegs at a time using Canadian-made equipment produced less than 1 km from the brewhouse. The taproom includes a bistro serving scratch-made food with local ingredients, plus a viewing window into the brewing operation so visitors can watch while waiting for growler fills. Regular events — live music, wing nights, and trivia — give it a strong community-gathering character.
13db69d29c: Stoneboat Vineyards is a family-owned estate winery on Oliver's Black Sage benchlands, with vineyards maturing since the late 1970s planted to Pinot Noir, Pinotage, Pinot Gris, and Pinot Blanc. The name references the flat sledge once used to clear the abundant river rocks from the vineyard — those calcium-encrusted rocks are credited with lending the wines a distinct mineral character. Cyclists riding the South Okanagan wine routes can stop at the wine shop for tastings of handcrafted estate, small-lot, and reserve wines.
0a9811a8d6: Kapi Chido Coffee Roasters is an Indigenous-values-rooted roastery and cafe in West Kelowna that roasts all its coffee in-house and serves espresso drinks and vintage-inspired treats on-site. The business is guided by pillars of Care, Culture, and Community, with bean names drawn from Indigenous languages and wildlife. Cyclists passing through the Okanagan can visit the roastery to taste and purchase freshly roasted coffee, or order online for nationwide shipping.
c8cc38b8af: Wild North Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and taproom in Creston, BC, situated just off Canyon St in the heart of the Creston Valley. The brewery emphasises locally sourced ingredients and an authentic approach to craft beer, pouring its own lineup in a taproom with a patio and a lively events calendar that includes trivia nights and community gatherings. It is a natural social hub for cyclists passing through the Kootenays on a longer touring route.
cea1eb62c3: Threefold is a brewery collective on Powell Street in East Vancouver, bringing three independent craft breweries together under one roof alongside Neapolitan pizza. The taproom pours a rotating tap list of craft beers and other drinks, with a food menu that gives cyclists the chance to sample multiple local producers in a single stop. The menu includes a wide range of vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options alongside more conventional fare.
d14f9b531f: Grey Fox Brewing is a dedicated gluten-free brewery located in Lake Country (Winfield), BC, making it a notable stop for cyclists with celiac disease or gluten sensitivities. The brewery has an online shop and a beer-finder page, suggesting both taproom presence and wider distribution. Touring cyclists in the Okanagan wine and orchard corridor will find it a distinctive craft beverage destination.
1836d1e7e0: Ancient Hill Estate Winery is a family-owned boutique estate winery in the Ellison area of North Kelowna, situated on a hillside across from the Kelowna Airport where wine grapes were first grown in the 1940s. The European-style winery building was designed by a noted Penticton architect and produces small-lot wines entirely from grapes grown on-site, including Lemberger, Pinot Noir, Baco Noir, and Pinot Gris. Cyclists can taste wines in the old-world-style shop or enjoy a glass on the patio with panoramic valley views, accompanied by cheeses, crackers, and non-alcoholic beverages.
d2faef107d: White Sails Brewing is an award-winning craft brewery that has been a fixture of downtown Nanaimo since 2015, located across from Maffeo Sutton Park on the waterfront. The open-concept taproom seats over 100 and pours up to 14 beers alongside guest taps, a selection of wines and ciders, a full coffee bar, and a locally-sourced food menu. Their flagship beers have earned gold medals at the BC Beer Awards, Canadian Brewing Awards, and World Beer Awards.
970e77d854: The BX Press Cidery is a craft cider producer rooted in a third-generation transitional organic apple orchard outside Vernon, BC. The operation is currently rebranding to 'Cambium Cider Co' and opening a new farm-to-table restaurant celebrating local purveyors alongside its artisan cider. The 70-year-old Spartan apple trees and generational farming heritage give this destination a distinctive sense of place.
797e8a738b: Little Engine Wines is a boutique winery and tasting room situated on Naramata Road along the Naramata Bench, one of the Okanagan's most celebrated cycling corridors. The tasting room pours across multiple wine series — Elevation, Silver, Gold, and Platinum — and offers a small bites food menu alongside wine club membership. The winery also hosts events and weddings, making it a destination stop rather than just a bottle shop.
098d3dc9e2: Twin Sails Brewing opened in 2015 on Port Moody's 'Brewers Row', founded by identical twin brothers whose name also nods to the sailboats visible on Burrard Inlet right out front. The brewery specialises in progressive American IPAs, stouts, sours, and wild barrel ales, with a taproom, patio, arcade, and a weekend food truck (Mama Said's Pizza) on site. Dogs are welcome on the patio and guests may bring outside food, making it a convivial stop for cyclists riding the Burrard Inlet corridor.
338176f782: BNA Brewing Co. & Eatery is Kelowna's flagship craft brewery, set inside a century-old building that once housed the British North American Tobacco Company — the source of the BNA name. All beer is brewed on-site and spans a wide range of styles from easy-drinking lagers to adventurous sours, served alongside a full kitchen menu in a space that also includes bowling lanes. It is a lively, locally-owned destination in the heart of downtown Kelowna, operating since 2015.
45d6a93102: Terravista Vineyards is a small estate winery on the Naramata Bench — one of BC's most popular cycling corridors — specializing in rare Spanish white varieties such as Albariño and Verdejo alongside a premium small-lot series called En Terre. All three of the winery's Naramata Bench vineyards achieved 100% certified organic status in Fall 2025, reflecting a commitment to sustainable viticulture including solar arrays, electric utility vehicles, and livestock integration. Touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan can book seated tasting experiences and purchase wines directly on site.
4e399966b7: Slackwater Brewing is a craft brewery in Penticton producing BC-brewed craft beer. Located on Martin Street in Penticton's downtown core, it sits within the Okanagan's cycling heartland and offers a taproom destination for touring cyclists. The brewery's active 2025 website references beers, events, and a 'Find Us' section suggesting a welcoming public venue.
90dc022cab: Deep Blue Distilleries is a craft distillery in Richmond, BC, producing small-batch gins and vodkas inspired by the purity of the BC coast using custom-built distillation equipment sourced from Hungary and Spain. The distillery offers guided tours by appointment (typically Wednesday through Friday) covering the full distillation process and concluding with spirit tastings and handcrafted cocktails. Multiple spirit brands are produced on-site — including Nookum Gin and Charm Vodka — and are available for retail purchase directly from the distillery.
330b49d88b: Venturi-Schulze Vineyards is a family farmstead winery established in 1987 on Vancouver Island, practising natural viticulture — no pesticides, herbicides, or irrigation — on a south-facing estate that also produces artisan balsamic vinegar, verjus, and jams. The property includes an outdoor patio tasting area that welcomes leashed dogs, and products can be purchased directly from the wine shop or ordered online with gate pickup available. The winery has earned recognition for its eco-friendly approach and estate-grown, minimally-intervened wines.
5ac0da6868: Tinhouse Brewing is a Port Coquitlam craft brewery and taproom that opened in 2019, with roots going back nearly a decade under the name Sapperton Brewing. The taproom features a 30-seat licensed outdoor patio and welcomes outside food, with local food trucks on weekends and nearby restaurant delivery options. A FAQ note points cyclists toward Dominion Park, just 600m along the trail, where open liquor is permitted and there is a playground.
9f824cc459: A family winery set on 13 acres of pastoral farmland alongside the Serpentine River on the edge of White Rock. They produce a range of wines including Merlot, Cabernet blends, Gewürztraminer, Rosé, and a late harvest red, all available for tasting and purchase on-site. The rural setting and vineyard grounds make it an appealing rest stop for cyclists riding the flat agricultural roads of south Surrey.
05ce6a80f8: Little Straw Vineyards is one of the Okanagan's oldest family estate wineries, with vineyard roots dating to 1969 when the Slamka family first planted in West Kelowna. Now under the stewardship of the Sidhu family, the 12-acre estate is transitioning toward organic certification and hosts TULA Restaurant, offering refined Indian cuisine alongside its VQA wines. Touring cyclists on the Okanagan wine route can combine vineyard tastings and guided tours with a full sit-down meal at this historic property.
8ff1b13eba: Ravens Brewing Company is a family-owned Indigenous brewery and distillery founded in 2014 by Paul and Jocelyn Sweeting, producing a wide range of craft beers from IPAs and Belgian tripels to sours and stouts in the Fraser Valley. The brewery has won a BC Beer Award every year for five consecutive years and took best Gose at the 2018 World Beer Cup. They also offer contract brewing and distribution services, making them a regional hub for craft beverage production.
7025df44cf: Steel & Oak Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and tasting room in New Westminster producing unfiltered, unpasteurized beer using a blend of North American and German brewing traditions, from dry Irish stouts to hazy IPAs. An on-site food truck offers a full menu of burgers, sandwiches, salads, and snacks — a proper sit-down fuel stop rather than just a drink destination. The brewery also hosts events and offers private keg sales, giving it a lively community feel.
ab68eef11c: A family-run boutique winery on Summerland's Bottle Neck Drive, producing small-batch wines from 100% BC VQA grapes grown in the volcanic soils of Giant Head Mountain. The property features a cozy log-cabin tasting room and an outdoor picnic area with a fountain where visitors are encouraged to bring a lunch and relax. A good rest stop for touring cyclists riding the Summerland wine route.
5738818714: Meyer Family Vineyards is an award-winning Okanagan Falls winery recognized as a Top 3 Winery in Canada at the 2025 National Wine Awards, producing about 8,000 cases of Burgundian-style Chardonnay and Pinot Noir from hand-harvested grapes. Operating since 2006, the winery has a tasting room and wine shop where visitors can sample and purchase critically acclaimed small-lot wines. It sits along McLean Creek Road in the heart of BC wine country, making it a natural destination stop on a cycling tour of the Okanagan Valley.
36484a964f: Blackwood Lane Winery is a family-run estate operated by father-and-son team Carlos and Daniel Lee, who use traditional French winemaking methods without chemicals or mechanical pumps to produce award-winning Okanagan wines. Recently relocated from Aldergrove to Penticton, it sits at the very first stop on the Naramata Bench, making it a natural pull-off for cyclists riding that iconic route. The tasting room is open seven days a week and the online shop offers store pickup for those who want to load a bottle into their panniers.
2ae99ed0e0: Tin Whistle is a craft brewery and taproom set inside the historic Cannery Trade Centre, a former fruit cannery turned industrial-chic gathering space in Penticton. It holds the distinction of being the first carbon neutral brewery in British Columbia, a milestone the company announced on Earth Day 2021. The taproom pours a rotating lineup of South Okanagan-inspired beers — including their iconic Peach Cream Ale and experimental seasonal taps — in a setting the brewery describes as always playing records and always pouring something new.
35c83f0a49: Upper Bench Winery and Creamery is a 9.5-acre estate winery on the Naramata Bench sub-GI in the South Okanagan, known for award-winning bold reds, crisp dry whites, and handcrafted artisanal cheeses made on-site from pasteurized cow's milk. The property features a private patio for guided wine-and-cheese tasting experiences and a wood-fired oven wine bar called The Oven. The Naramata Bench is one of BC's premier cycling routes, making this a natural destination stop for touring cyclists exploring the region.
ef08a860b4: 33 Brewing Experiment (33B) is the experimental taproom arm of 33 Acres Brewing Company, occupying a single-storey retail space on West 8th Avenue in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood. It operates on a walk-in basis with bar service alongside a seasonally rotating food menu, and can host private events for up to 60 guests. The location sits steps from the main 33 Acres taproom (33A) at 15 West 8th Avenue.
5695fa31bf: Île Sauvage Brewing is a craft brewery in Victoria specializing in Belgian-style wild ales and sour beers, with a tasting room on Bridge Street. The name translates to 'Wild Island,' referencing both Vancouver Island's wilderness and the brewery's focus on Kveik, Lactobacillus, and Brettanomyces fermentations, oak-ageing, and local fruit refermentations. Cyclists stopping in will find a rotating selection of wild and sour beers available on tap and for takeout.
5060e5151a: Sandhill Wines is an urban winery operating on the historic Calona Wines estate — established in 1932, it holds the distinction of being BC's original and oldest continuing winery. Crafting VQA wines since 1997 from grapes sourced across six vineyards in the Okanagan and Similkameen valleys, it offers guided tastings, curated food pairings, live music, and private events in the heart of downtown Kelowna. A touring cyclist finishing a day's ride into Kelowna will find it a short walk from the waterfront and city centre.
c212d65411: Silkscarf is a family boutique estate winery that has operated under the same founding proprietors and winemakers since 2004, making it one of the longer-running family wineries in the Okanagan. The estate cultivates over 10 varieties across 10-plus acres of class-1 terroir on the Summerland Bench Sub-GI, with a declared commitment to sustainable farming. Touring cyclists on the Naramata–Summerland bench roads can stop for a tasting and browse an extensive library collection of older vintages.
3727ed22e7: Privato is a boutique, family-owned winery nestled along the scenic slopes of the North Thompson River in the Thompson Valley wine region, specializing in small-lot Burgundian-style Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. Their flagship Pinot Noir has earned double gold medals at the All Canadian Wine Awards. Visiting cyclists can enjoy a personalized tasting in the wine garden or linger on the picnic grounds with a glass overlooking the vineyard.
f9553d472c: High Mountain Brewing Co. — widely known as The Brewhouse — has been a Whistler Village anchor since 1997, brewing award-winning ales and lagers on-site and serving a full scratch kitchen of barbecue, pastas, and flatbreads. Part of the Mark James Group, it occupies a large multi-room space with a two-sided fireplace and a generous patio beside the Olympic Rings, making it a natural gathering spot after a day on the bike or the slopes. It is open year-round and capable of handling large groups across its restaurant, bar, and mezzanine levels.
45bbb03b69: Poplar Grove Winery is a family-owned, estate-grown winery near Penticton celebrating its 30th vintage, producing a full range of Okanagan reds, whites, and rosés from its own vineyards. The property features a walk-in tasting room and The Restaurant at Poplar Grove, a full-service dining room with a patio offering vineyard views, open seven days a week for lunch and dinner.
