Cyclists riding through the Penticton bench country will find it a relaxed stop for wine tasting, a sit-down meal, and retail wine purchases including convenient 3-litre bag-in-box formats.
8b1149a375: Foamers' Folly Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and full-service tasting room in Pitt Meadows, BC, pouring 20 taps of house-made beer alongside rotating wine and cider. The tasting room is known for adventurous, boundary-pushing recipes — wild sours, fruit lagers, and hard seltzers sit alongside approachable core styles. A beautiful patio, food menu, and regular events make it a natural gathering point for cyclists passing through the Pitt Meadows flats.
7479877102: A family-owned estate winery in the heart of West Kelowna's wine country, housed in an architecturally award-winning building with a year-round art gallery. The on-site restaurant 31 Charkay serves contemporary Canadian cuisine with vineyard views, making it a rewarding stop along Boucherie Road for touring cyclists exploring the Okanagan wine routes.
46e1c54d09: Millionaires' Row Cider Co. is a family-run cidery on a 100+ year-old apple orchard in Summerland's historic Prairie Valley, named for the wealthy investors who shaped the region's early fruit industry. Visitors taste hand-crafted estate ciders at a stand-up bar in the cellar, then can relax in a picnic area surrounded by the working orchard, with views of Conkle Mountain and Giants Head Mountain. The cidery sells its full range of vegan, gluten-free ciders to take away, making it a natural stop on a cycling tour through the South Okanagan.
218705ec35: Grape Escapes is Penticton's #1-rated wine tour company (TripAdvisor Hall of Fame inductee), operating since 2011 and guiding guests through the South Okanagan's celebrated wine regions including Naramata, Okanagan Falls, Summerland, Oliver/Osoyoos, and the Similkameen Valley. Tours include door-to-door pickup and drop-off from any Penticton address, visits to handpicked wineries, and a catered gourmet picnic lunch with vegan and gluten-free options. For touring cyclists staying in or passing through Penticton, this is a way to explore the wine country without riding the full routes.
f4862f05b7: Family-owned craft brewery on Bridge Street in Victoria, voted Best Brewery seven years running by the Times Colonist Reader's Choice Awards. They produce a wide range of lagers, ales, and seasonal brews, and operate a growler bar and brewery tours on select Saturdays.
c7eaf7cda5: Grape Savvy Wine Tours is an Indigenous-owned hop-on, hop-off trolley and private tour company operating in Penticton and along the Naramata Bench, founded by Métis entrepreneur Savannah 'Savvy' Swaisland. The company offers curated winery tours, corporate charters, wedding transportation, and the unique 'Saddle Up & Sip' experience developed in collaboration with Syilx/Okanagan-owned businesses. For touring cyclists, it represents a way to extend a wine-country visit without pedalling between stops, and the hop-on, hop-off format means bikes could potentially be left at a hub while riders explore by trolley.
d8bd2a9aa2: Ex Nihilo Vineyards is a boutique estate winery in Lake Country whose name—Latin for 'out of nothing'—reflects its artisan philosophy of crafting wines from the ground up in the Okanagan. The property houses a tasting room open seven days a week alongside Chaos Bistro, an evening restaurant that regularly features live music and al fresco dining under the Okanagan sky. Cycling visitors exploring the Okanagan wine country will find it a polished destination stop with walk-in tastings available as well as reservable guided experiences.
305382d30d: White Rock Beach Beer Company is a locally-owned craft microbrewery founded in 2013 by two White Rock secondary school teachers who built the operation from scratch. The brewery operates a tasting room and lounge adjacent to its production space on Russell Avenue, where visitors can sample a range of house-brewed beers from light lagers and pilsners to a Baltic-style porter and a highly-hopped IPA. Its tagline 'Because beaches and beer go better together' reflects its identity as a neighbourhood hangout close to the White Rock waterfront.
f59c9da14d: A family-owned organic winery on a 105-year-old Paynter family farm in West Kelowna, featuring a solar-powered straw bale tasting room and a seasonal food truck. The permaculture property includes farm animals (goats on the roof, sheep, chickens), a local artisan gift shop, and PACS-certified organic wines. A distinctive Okanagan stop where sustainability is baked into everything from the building to the bottle.
a594df4ece: Freddy's Brewing is an in-house craft brewery and full-service brewpub operating inside the McCurdy Bowling Centre, a large entertainment complex in Kelowna. The brewpub pours over 12 in-house craft beers alongside cocktails, wine, and spirits, paired with an elevated pub food menu spanning breakfast through dinner. A touring cyclist stopping here gets a rare combination of serious craft beer and a lively, spacious venue.
cad48baa4a: Intrigue Wines is a boutique, family-owned winery in Lake Country, BC, founded in 2008 by two local families who combined winemaking, business, and community expertise to build an award-winning Okanagan estate. All wines are crafted from 100% BC-grown grapes with sustainability at the core, earning consistent recognition for quality across white, red, rosé, and sparkling styles. Cyclists riding the Okanagan Wine Route can drop in for a bookable tasting experience or pick up bottles at the on-site wine shop in a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere.
d37c1ec5ec: Ace Brewing Company is a family-owned microbrewery and taproom in Courtenay's Comox Valley, themed around the ace fighter pilots of WWI and WWII who flew from nearby CFB Comox. The Landolt family built the brewery around a commitment to quality, producing everything from crisp German-style Pilsners to bold West Coast IPAs. The taproom pours a rotating lineup of craft beers that includes the 2022 Canada Beer Cup Silver Medal-winning Wingman Pale Ale.
58fbf57fa4: Tantalus Vineyards is a boutique estate winery on the eastern slopes of the Okanagan Valley, operating on one of BC's oldest continuously producing vineyards — first planted to grapes in 1927. It holds the distinction of being British Columbia's first LEED-certified winery, and has earned a national and international reputation for its terroir-driven Riesling, Chardonnay, and Pinot Noir. Touring cyclists can book a tasting experience overlooking Lake Okanagan and the City of Kelowna.
447c77154f: Black Kettle Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom that opened in January 2014 just past the rail tracks in North Vancouver, a short ride from the Spirit Trail. The brewpub pours its own lagers, IPAs, and seasonal ales alongside a full kitchen menu of smash burgers, tacos, pizza, and wings. It is pet-friendly on the patio and regularly hosts live music, making it a welcoming destination for cyclists coming off the North Shore mountains or arriving via the Seabus.
95db9c5e35: Laughing Stock Vineyards is a boutique estate winery on the Naramata Bench renowned for its flagship Portfolio Bordeaux-style blend, which has earned 90+ points from WineAlign in 8 of 10 submissions since 2012 and is regarded as one of BC's cult wines. The estate grows all five Bordeaux varieties on-site and offers premium seated tastings with access to limited-production wines sold only at the winery. Cyclists passing by without a reservation can call from the gate to check walk-in availability.
04931d5b73: BNA Brewing Co is a craft brewery and eatery located steps from the beach in Penticton, the third location in a growing Okanagan chain. The venue pairs its own craft beer lineup with a full food menu that spans Filipino-inspired dishes, a raw bar seafood tower, and smash burgers, all inside a lively space with four-lane bowling, shuffleboard, darts, and bocce. It sits in the heart of one of BC's most popular cycling destinations, making it a natural post-ride social stop.
d2c3e415ef: The Parkside Brewery is a craft brewery and tasting room on Port Moody's celebrated 'Brewer's Row,' situated directly across from Rocky Point Park at the eastern end of Burrard Inlet. The brewery produces award-winning beers across a wide range of styles, from easy-drinking lagers to bold hoppy ales, all brewed on-site by head brewer Vern Lambourne. Its location near waterfront trails, forested parklands, and the broader Burrard Inlet cycling network makes it a natural and rewarding stop for touring cyclists.
242ce43bc3: Western Canada's original craft distillery, Okanagan Spirits has been producing award-winning spirits from 100% BC grain and fruit since 2004. The Vernon flagship is a full-service destination featuring a tasting room, cocktail lounge, experience classroom, and drop-in tastings requiring no reservation. In 2025 the distillery earned the World-Class Distillery designation at the World Spirits Awards in Germany, taking home 11 Gold and 5 Silver medals across its whisky, gin, brandy, and liqueur portfolio.
b93104e6fb: Nichol Vineyard is one of the first three pioneering wineries on the Naramata Bench, with vines planted in 1989 at the northernmost tip of Naramata, directly abutting the Kettle Valley Railway trail. The winery is historically notable for planting the first Syrah vines in Canada and takes a rigorous minimal-intervention approach — hand-harvested, unfined, unfiltered, and vegan. A touring cyclist arriving via the KVR will find a relaxed tasting room with Okanagan Lake views, a record player, a covered picnic area for lingering with a brought lunch, and wine available by the glass or bottle.
ed1594dc1e: Dageraad Brewing is a small-batch artisan brewery crafting Belgian-inspired beers from a warehouse tasting room steps from Production Way SkyTrain station in Burnaby, named after the Dageraadplaats neighbourhood square in Antwerp. The 50-seat indoor tasting room is complemented by a 50-seat covered, heated patio — a welcoming stop in any weather. Dageraad was awarded 2018 Brewery of the Year by the Canadian Brewing Awards and offers a rotating lineup of Belgian-style ales including saisons, strong goldens, and mixed-culture fermentations.
4cb53c611d: Beach Fire Brewing Company is Campbell River's own craft brewery, producing award-winning beers including the High Tide Pale Ale (People's Choice at the Mount Washington Tapped Beer Festival) and the Ember Red Ale (Canada Beer Cup Gold in 2023 and 2025). The taproom backs its lineup with a full kitchen menu built entirely around locally sourced, in-house-prepared food — from snacks and shareables to hearty mains and decadent desserts. The brewery markets itself explicitly around community and the active West Coast lifestyle, with a trail-nodding house stout called WheelBender Stout.
8708c91c62: Mission Springs Brewing Company is one of BC's oldest craft brewhouses, opened in 1996 and operating a 10-barrel facility overlooking the Fraser River in Mission. The brewpub pairs its house-crafted beers — available on tap, in growlers, cans, and bottles — with a full pub menu served across three patios and a dining room. It is part of the Springs Group, which also runs an attached liquor store where cyclists can pick up beer to go.
05451f6e21: Play Estate Winery is an estate winery and restaurant perched on Skaha Hills Drive with sweeping, unobstructed views of Skaha Lake and the surrounding mountains, just minutes from downtown Penticton. The property houses both a wine shop carrying estate-grown wines crafted by winemaker Rebecca Ruggeri and The Vista Restaurant, which serves flatbreads, charcuterie, seafood, and other light fare. The winery's arts-inspired identity — its name evoking theatre and the spirit of Shakespeare — lends it a distinctive character among the Okanagan's many wine destinations.
496b040836: Persephone Brewing is a certified B Corp farm brewery on BC's Sunshine Coast, running a working five-acre farm — barley fields, apple orchards, market gardens, and laying hens — alongside its craft brewing operation. The on-site tasting room and kitchen serve multiple award-winning beers, including Canadian Brewing Award winners, made with farm-grown and locally sourced ingredients. Cyclists passing through Gibsons will find a genuinely distinctive farm-to-barrel stop with outdoor picnic areas and a community-rooted ethos.
77d7aedd23: Westholme Tea Company is an 18-year-old organic tea operation on Vancouver Island's Cowichan Peninsula, operating a teashop inside a converted barn alongside a working tea garden with several hundred tea plants — one of Canada's very few commercial tea-growing operations. The shop carries over 150 organic loose-leaf teas, hand-blended tisanes, handbuilt ceramic teaware, and limited-harvest teas grown on the property itself. At least one visiting cyclist reported being greeted with a complimentary tea sample, making this an unusually characterful rest stop on the Vancouver Crossing Loop.
f477b20c95: Deep Cove Winery is a family-owned estate winery nestled between Horth Hill Regional Park and the shores of Deep Cove in North Saanich on the Saanich Peninsula. With three acres of vines planted over 22 years ago, they produce hand-crafted wines including Ortega, Pinot Gris, Marechal Foch, and their signature Alchemy blend. The winery has a lounge with a full food menu and hosts regular events, making it a rewarding stop on a Saanich Peninsula ride.
f45b9166d0: Da Silva Vineyards is a boutique family-owned winery on the Naramata Bench just north of Penticton, rooted in a Portuguese farming heritage brought to the South Okanagan in 1955. The property features an intimate seated tasting room where a winemaker guides small groups through terroir-driven wines drawn from six estate vineyards. An on-site restaurant, The Kitchen, offers unconventional fine dining with Mexican and Portuguese-inspired tapas, making it a potential rest-and-refuel destination for cyclists touring the Naramata Bench.
8b065828b0: A community-focused craft brewery on Dunsmuir Avenue in the village of Cumberland, a renowned mountain biking destination in the Comox Valley. Founded in 2014, it follows a hyper-local model with no distribution outside Cumberland, so the only way to taste their house-brewed beers is to visit in person. The globally inspired food menu and outdoor dog-friendly patio make it a natural gathering spot after a day on the trails.
377ed8e483: Daydreamer Wines is a sustainable, family-run winery on the Naramata Bench founded by Rachel and Marcus Ansems, where Marcus holds the Master of Wine designation. The winery produces limited-batch wines without systemic pesticides, herbicides, or fungicides, earning multiple platinum and gold medals at the National Wine Awards of Canada including Best Red Wine in Canada in 2019. Cyclists on the Naramata Bench can book a tasting at the on-site Wine Shack and purchase bottles to take away.
ff68bc0e85: Pentâge Winery is a family-owned estate on 23 acres overlooking Skaha Lake, producing small-batch, handcrafted wines from their Skaha Bench vineyards since their inaugural 1999 vintage. The property features a striking 5,000-square-foot natural rock wine cellar hand-built by founder Paul Gardner, and a tasting room with panoramic views of the lake and surrounding vineyards. It sits just outside Penticton on Valleyview Road, making it a natural waypoint on the South Okanagan wine route.
78a0286e10: Britannia Brewing Co is a craft brewery with taprooms across the Lower Mainland and Okanagan, producing a nautically themed lineup of ales, lagers, and sours. The Richmond presence is described on the website as a bar and restaurant in Steveston Village, a historic fishing village popular with cyclists riding the Steveston Dyke trail. The brewery's range spans sessionable lagers and blond ales through hoppy IPAs and dark porters.
cbb4e79be1: Hillside Winery has been producing award-winning wines on the Naramata Bench since 1984, making it one of the area's longest-running wineries. The on-site Bistro serves terroir-to-table small plates with locally foraged ingredients in a 65-seat dining room and on two outdoor patios overlooking Okanagan Lake. Located on Naramata Road—a cornerstone of Okanagan cycling—it is a natural refreshment stop for touring cyclists riding the Bench.
4985ea03db: A small-batch craft distillery on the Sidney waterfront, producing award-winning gins including the well-known Empress 1908 Indigo Gin. The retail space offers complimentary tastings and bottle purchases, making it a worthwhile stop for cyclists riding through the Saanich Peninsula. The copper pot stills and waterfront setting give the visit a sense of place beyond a typical liquor store.
5aabfa21ad: Festina Lente is a 5-acre family-run hobby farm in Langley's wine country, specializing in award-winning mead and honey wines crafted by beekeepers-turned-winemakers Bill and Teresa. The farm hosts a covered, heated patio with walk-in tastings, free live music events, and a weekend food truck serving flatbreads, gourmet hot dogs, charcuterie boards, and high tea boxes. Touring cyclists with dogs are explicitly welcomed, and the winery's Renaissance Faire and seasonal events make it a distinctive rural stop on any Langley route.
daafe844f7: Luppolo Brewing is a Vancouver craft brewery and tasting room inspired by the convivial atmosphere of the Italian birrificio, operating for nearly a decade at 1123 Venables St. in the Grandview-Woodland neighbourhood. The brewery produces a wide and rotating range of craft beers — from pilsners and lagers to sours, stouts, and IPAs — and partners with Local Pizzaiolo for hand-stretched authentic Italian pizzas made fresh daily. A seasonal dog-friendly patio and fully wheelchair-accessible space make it a welcoming stop for cyclists exploring Vancouver's east side.
a0b2b5b597: Lightning Rock Winery is an estate winery perched above Okanagan Lake with sweeping views down to Penticton, producing award-winning wines from several distinct Summerland-area vineyards. The tasting room is known for its warm, unpretentious hospitality from hands-on owners, and outdoor tasting options make it a natural rest stop on the Naramata Bench cycling circuit. A wine shop on-site lets cyclists pick up bottles to go.
0993e5716b: Wildeye Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom on the North Shore, a short ride from the Iron Workers Memorial Bridge cycling corridor. The house lineup spans award-winning Czech Pilsner, hazy IPAs, sours, and stouts, alongside an entirely non-alcoholic Easy Series for riders staying dry. The taproom hosts regular live music and trivia nights, offers a full bistro menu, and can accommodate private events for up to 75 guests.
f063d43349: Unsworth Vineyards is a family-owned estate winery founded by the Turyk family in 2009 on a historic early-1900s farmhouse property in the Cowichan Valley, celebrated as 'Canada's Provence.' The estate produces coastal Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, sparkling wines, and expressive whites shaped by a rare rain-shadow microclimate on southern Vancouver Island. Cyclists riding the Cowichan Valley corridor will find a welcoming tasting room only 45 minutes from Victoria, set among rolling vineyards overlooking the Salish Sea.
d8767cce4f: Noble Ridge Vineyards is a family-founded estate winery perched on a ridge above Okanagan Falls in the South Okanagan wine country, offering stunning vineyard views and curated tastings of its award-winning sparkling, white, rosé, and red wines. The tasting room features a five-wine flight experience and a retail wine shop, with tasting fees donated to community causes. The property also hosts seasonal food-and-wine pairing events and offers on-site accommodations, making it a scenic destination for cyclists exploring the South Okanagan wine route.
369ef25e61: Glenora Farm is a biodynamic, life-sharing community near Duncan on Vancouver Island where adults with developmental disabilities live and work alongside caregivers as part of the international Camphill movement. The farm produces organic vegetables, candles, and other workshop goods, some of which are sold at local markets. The website describes the property as people's private homes where visitor access requires advance approval.
905bec9dd8: A family-owned winery on Westminster Highway in Richmond with a retail shop and tasting room. They produce award-winning wines using grapes grown on their own farmland on Lulu Island. A welcoming stop along the flat Richmond cycling corridors, with events like paint nights and bingo alongside regular tastings.
415179b6fa: Songhees Events & Catering is an Indigenous-owned catering and event company operated by the Songhees Nation in Victoria, BC, offering West Coast menus featuring house-made bannock, candied salmon, and locally inspired dishes. The operation includes on-site event space at the Songhees Wellness Centre, off-site catering, and a food truck. A touring cyclist venturing here would encounter a distinctive taste of Coast Salish food culture.
1b1d3fb904: Zanatta Estate Winery holds the distinction of being Vancouver Island's first estate winery, farming 25 acres in the Glenora area of the Cowichan Valley for over half a century. The family-run operation specializes in Champagne-style sparkling wines made entirely from estate-grown fruit across sparkling, white, rosé, and red styles. Cyclists can linger on the verandah with a glass, join wine club events, or pick up bottles to bring home from this heritage stop in a region celebrated for cycle touring.
e68d2793b4: Sons of Vancouver is an independently owned craft distillery on Vancouver's North Shore, founded in 2015 and now centered on a flavour-driven rye whisky program fermented, distilled, and matured entirely on-site. The tasting room offers hand-crafted cocktails made with in-house spirits alongside retail bottle sales, making it a distinctive destination stop rather than a mid-ride refuel. Originally known for its No. 82 Amaretto, the distillery has pivoted to becoming a serious rye whisky producer with limited special releases that often sell out within a day.
8394c97171: Riley's Cidery sits in a remarkable one-of-a-kind heirloom apple orchard on Bowen Island containing nearly a thousand varieties, planted over 30 years by collectors John and Josephine Riley. Visitors can taste craft ciders made from these heritage apples and enjoy a picnic area overlooking the orchard. The cidery is run by Christine and Rob, who took over stewardship of this living museum in 2019 and trained in traditional English cidermaking.
f2ae4bdb69: Gillespie's Fine Spirits is a craft distillery based in Squamish, BC, producing small-batch spirits in one of the Sea-to-Sky corridor's most bike-friendly towns. Touring cyclists passing through Squamish may find it a worthwhile stop to pick up locally made liquor. As a craft producer it likely offers a tasting room or retail counter, though this could not be confirmed from available data.
6dff04bc9a: Blue Mountain Vineyard and Cellars is a family-owned estate winery in Okanagan Falls that has been producing cool-climate wines since 1991, with all grapes grown on a single contiguous site farmed by the Mavety family for nearly 50 years. The winery focuses on minimal-intervention, terroir-driven wines — sparkling, Pinot Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Gris, and reds — with hand-picked, gravity-racked fruit. Tastings are reservation-only and the winery hosts occasional events at the estate and around the broader Okanagan region.
7c7f1d25bc: Britannia Brewing Co. is a nautically-themed craft brewery operating a Brewery & Tap House in Lake Country near Kelowna, one of several BC locations. Their lineup spans West Coast IPAs, farmhouse saisons, Gose-style watermelon sours, oatmeal stouts, and classic lagers — all with ocean-inspired names. The Lake Country tap house sits in the heart of the Okanagan's popular cycling corridor connecting Kelowna-area wineries and trails.
93dbfda0d9: Merridale is a family-owned, woman-led farm cidery and distillery on a 20-acre orchard in the Cowichan Valley, crafting award-winning ciders and spirits for over 30 years. The property functions as a full farm destination with a farmhouse eatery, farm store, guided tastings, distillery tours, yurt accommodations, and seasonal events. Touring cyclists can settle in for a meal or tasting in an orchard setting, with dogs welcome on leash throughout the grounds and patio.
688becb988: Off The Rail Brewing is an East Vancouver craft brewery with a tasting room sitting directly on the Adanac bike path, one of Vancouver's primary cycling corridors. The tasting room pours 10–12 of the brewery's own beers across 15 taps — including 3 nitro taps — and serves light food such as Jamaican patties, potato pea samosas, and grilled cheese sandwiches. The brewery also produces Bine Sparkling Hop Water, a non-alcoholic, hop-infused sparkling water for alcohol-free riders.
980306d664: Copper Spirit Distillery is a family-run boutique craft distillery on Bowen Island, founded by Miguel and Candice Kabantsov, who spent over five years building it from the ground up. Using German copper stills, organic BC grain, and pure West Coast water, they handcraft vodka, gin, rye and wheat whisky, and other spirits. The tasting room serves a seasonal cocktail menu made entirely from fresh organic ingredients, including sugar-free and alcohol-free options.
e9d40c7b03: Deol Family Estate Winery is a family-owned estate operation on an 18-acre vineyard in North Cowichan, growing vines since 1984 and producing wines entirely from estate-grown grapes—Pinot Gris, Pinot Noir, Marechal Foch, and Gamay Noir—with all steps from harvest to bottling done on-site. Touring cyclists can stop at the tasting room and wine shop, and a patio picnic area with tables invites visitors to bring their own lunch and linger over a glass amid vineyard scenery. The winery also sells wines online and at the Cowichan Farmer's Market.
0a69f966b5: Strange Fellows is an East Vancouver craft brewery known for blending old-world tradition with West Coast innovation, with a particular focus on sour, barrel-aged, and vintage limited releases alongside a broad roster of hoppy ales, stouts, pilsners, and Belgians. The tasting room on Clark Drive pours a rotating tap list that also includes cider, wine, and a non-alcoholic IPA, backed by a full snack-and-panini food menu sourced from a local bakery. Cyclists looking to stock up can fill growlers from most taps or shop packaged cans and bottles to carry on the road.
5422961754: Blue Grouse Estate Winery is one of the oldest vineyards on Vancouver Island, a sustainably farmed and award-winning estate situated in the southern Cowichan Valley about 8 kilometres south of Duncan and roughly 1 kilometre west of the Trans-Canada Highway. The winery produces a full range — sparkling, white, rosé, red, and dessert wines — and welcomes visitors for tastings and tours by reservation, with dogs permitted on site. It sits in the heart of a celebrated cycling and wine region, making it a natural destination stop on a Cowichan Valley tour.
63d4fc544a: Cobble Hill Winery is a regenerative-farming estate winery in the heart of the Cowichan Valley, producing cool-climate varietals under the guidance of winemaker Dylan Sheldon alongside proprietors Steve and Tricia. Visitors are welcome to taste wines led by tasting-room staff with views over the vineyard and lavender fields, and are encouraged to bring a picnic to enjoy with a bottle on the garden patio. The winery also participates in the Cowichan Valley Wine Festival and hosts weddings and private events, making it a genuine destination stop rather than a simple tasting counter.
5447b3d9ce: Calona Vineyards is listed as a winery and on-site alcohol retail shop on Richter Street in Kelowna, operating under Andrew Peller Limited, one of Canada's largest premium wine producers with estate properties across the Okanagan. The Richter Street location places it within Kelowna's city core, potentially accessible to cyclists touring the region. Andrew Peller's BC estate properties are recognized within the tourism and hospitality industry for wine and dining experiences.
f3e0bae238: Blind Tiger Vineyards is a family-owned, seasonal winery in Lake Country's Okanagan wine country offering wine tastings by appointment, a lively outdoor patio with lake views, and wood-fired pizza from Marno's. The vineyard leans into a spirit of inclusivity and good vibes, hosting regular live-music events, a drag show series, and welcoming pets and families alike. A Tiger Trunk Gift Shop sells branded merch and canned goods alongside a lineup of naturally grown, chemical-free estate wines.
1b5efe533f: Mount Boucherie Estate Winery is a long-established Okanagan estate winery farming vines since 1968, now anchored by a striking 15,000 sq ft Wine Experience Centre designed by Ciccozzi Architects and opened in 2020. The property combines a daily tasting room, award-winning estate wines across five tiers, and The Modest Butcher Kitchen + Market — a farm-to-table restaurant with full bar service and a rooftop patio overlooking the lake. For a touring cyclist cutting through Okanagan wine country, it offers a full stop with food, wine, and sweeping valley views at the foot of a former volcano.
8bfd058f4e: A small-batch craft distillery in Tofino's industrial area, handcrafting certified organic spirits from BC grain and Meares Island watershed water. The tasting room offers mini-cocktail samplers from a rotating lineup that includes gin, vodka, absinthe, whiskey, and limoncello, plus grab-and-go kombucha and craft tonics.
51829a65b5: Award-winning estate winery on Lakeshore Road overlooking Lake Okanagan, known for cool-climate Pinot Noir and sustainable farming practices including cover crops and Scottish Highland cattle. Features the Home Block Restaurant with a wine-first menu showcasing Okanagan produce, plus guided wine tastings and vineyard tours.
2616f6c6d7: A working vineyard and lavender farm in the Cowichan Valley, producing cool-climate varietals with winemaker Dylan Sheldon and operating under the Cobble Hill Winery brand. Visitors are welcomed for guided tastings in the tasting room and are encouraged to bring a picnic to enjoy on the garden patio overlooking the vineyard and lavender fields. The scenic rural setting and patio make it a memorable stop for cyclists touring the Cowichan Valley.
e26661e401: Red Truck Beer Company is a Vancouver craft brewery and taproom whose name and identity are built around a nostalgic working-truck aesthetic. Located near the Vancouver Crossing Loop route, it is a destination-worthy stop for cyclists seeking local beer and a sit-down break. No further details about the space or experience could be confirmed due to website inaccessibility.
b7f1da0747: Rewind Beer Co is a space-time-travel-themed craft brewery and tasting room housed in an industrial building, pouring its own rotating lineup of lagers, IPAs, sours, and saisons alongside guest taps and cider. The taproom doubles as 'Home of Pizza,' serving wood-fired-style pies made in-house with creative toppings and online ordering available. A touring cyclist would find a full sit-down destination with food, craft beer, and a lively atmosphere in Port Moody's industrial corridor.
f2837f2579: Vivezza Vineyard is a family-owned boutique winery on Salt Spring Island, built on over two decades of research into disease-resistant grape varieties suited to BC's coastal climate. The estate produces two distinct lines: a Traditional Series from old-vine vinifera on Salt Spring and Vancouver Islands, and an innovative Modern Series featuring newly developed disease-resistant varieties grown on the estate itself. The cellar door offers direct wine sales and tastings, making it a genuine destination stop on one of BC's most scenic cycling islands.
cdf461808c: Four Winds Brewing is a BC craft brewery focused on bold West Coast and European-style beers, operating a full taproom in the Tilbury industrial area of Delta. The taproom doubles as a taco shop and casual restaurant, making it a solid mid-ride destination for cyclists looking for a meal alongside a pint. A second Beach House location in Tsawwassen offers another option for cyclists riding the south Delta and Tsawwassen routes.
5622771a49: 8th Generation Vineyard is a family-owned estate winery in Summerland operated by Bernd and Stefanie Schales, who brought eight generations of German winemaking heritage to the Okanagan Valley when they arrived in 2003. The winery produces small-batch, estate-grown wines using sustainable, additive-free methods from vineyards they manage entirely themselves. Cyclists passing along Highway 97 can visit the farmhouse wine shop for tastings and to pick up a bottle.
2c8697826d: Wheelhouse Brewing Company is a craft brewery and full-service restaurant established in 2013, now housed inside Prince Rupert's original train station—a heritage landmark with 270° harbour views and an authentic Italian wood-fired pizza oven burning local red alder. Self-described as 'the wettest brewery in Canada,' it sits at the northern terminus of BC's Yellowhead Highway cycling corridor and serves award-winning craft beers alongside a rotating menu of wood-fired pizzas and coastal-inspired food.
2f091b67c5: Caffe Divano Port Moody is a community-oriented café nestled in the Klahanie neighbourhood, a short walk from Rocky Point Park and connected to St. John's Street via a pedestrian overpass. It was the founding location of the Divano family of cafés, opened in 2008 by Patrick and Lisa Beecroft with a vision of a true neighbourhood gathering spot decorated with local art. All baked goods are sourced from the Beecrofts' sister business, Gabi & Jules Handmade Pies & Baked Goodness, which also employs individuals with autism.
6230de2dc0: North Point Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and tasting room in Lower Lonsdale's Shipyards District in North Vancouver, founded by three North Shore locals inspired by West Coast cabin culture. The taproom pours a rotating roster of house-brewed beers spanning session lagers to high-ABV IPAs, alongside in-house pizza and snacks. An elevated loft with views of the North Shore and Downtown Vancouver is available for private events.
26d5c9888b: Averill Creek Vineyard is an estate winery on the slopes of Mount Prevost in the Cowichan Valley, founded in 2001 and farming 30 acres of vines using organic and biodynamic principles. The winery is known for low-intervention, cool-climate wines made with techniques like wild fermentation, foot-stomping, and whole-bunch fermentation. Touring cyclists can stop at the tasting room for wine flights served on a garden terrace, seasonal snacks including vegan options, and bottles to take away from the wine shop.
147aee881f: Farm Gate Winery is a lovingly restored heritage orcharding homestead perched above Skaha Lake on Highway 97 in Kaleden, roughly ten minutes south of Penticton. The property produces an award-winning portfolio of both traditional Okanagan grape wines and distinctive fruit wines made from estate-grown cherries, peaches, apricots, and plums, all produced and bottled on-site. A rustic tasting room, a back patio with sweeping views of Skaha Lake and surrounding orchards, and an attached fruit stand selling heirloom Okanagan produce make it a genuinely memorable roadside stop for cyclists riding the Skaha Lake corridor.
c1d45dfd74: Backroads Brewing is an award-winning craft brewery founded in 2017 on historic Baker Street in downtown Nelson, BC, producing small-batch ales and lagers with a constantly rotating tap list. The taproom showcases local art and a patio, giving it a character the website describes as 'unique to Nelson.' Food is available on-site through a partnership with The Block Railtown sandwich menu plus bar snacks, and beer can be taken away via growler fill or online order.
1be3ccc40c: Arrowleaf Cellars is an estate winery in Lake Country (Winfield) in the heart of the Okanagan, named after the arrowleaf wildflower native to its vineyards. The property features a tasting room, a picnic and patio area, and rotating food truck days, making it a multi-sensory stop on BC's wine route. Touring cyclists exploring the Okanagan's Camp Road corridor would find it a scenic and well-established destination for local wine and seasonal bites.
a0b788f137: Red Collar Brewing is a craft brewery and distilling operation in downtown Kamloops, running its taproom alongside the in-house Gin Lane Distillery. The space is divided into a main taproom, a dog-friendly fireplace room, and a summer patio with a combined capacity of up to 140 guests. An open BYOF (Bring Your Own Food) policy means cyclists can bring outside food to pair with house-brewed beers and gin cocktails, and growler fills are available for all beers on the menu.
2980b9d3d6: Corcelettes Estate Winery is a 160-acre small-lot estate winery in the Similkameen Valley, consistently ranked in the Top 10 Small Wineries at the National Wine Awards of Canada. Visitors can experience curated wine flights seated on a scenic patio, shop estate wines in the on-site wine shop, or stay overnight at the Sunshot Vineyard Guest House. The winery's portfolio — Bordeaux varietals, Syrah, Pinot Noir, and Chardonnay — is grown entirely in the valley's distinctive stony, mineral-rich soils.
930e6df917: Emandare Vineyard is a boutique, family-run winery perched on a south-sloping hillside in the Cowichan Valley, overlooking Somenos Lake in the rain shadow of Mount Prevost on Vancouver Island. Founded by Mike and Robin Nierychlo, it produces low-intervention, organically dry-farmed, terroir-driven wines from estate and single-vineyard sources using old-world techniques. Visitors can drop into the wine shop for tastings, book a private tour with the winemaker, or take part in a unique wine-and-golf-simulator experience held in the barrel cellar.
e5744edc14: The Shed is an open-air wood-fired pizza and coffee bar perched at Cypress Village, offering panoramic views stretching from Mount Baker to Vancouver Island. It operates year-round as a relaxed pop-up patio with no reservations — cyclists can simply roll up, grab a slice, and take in the mountain air. Come winter, it doubles as an après-ski venue with fire pits and seasonal cocktails.
e5f55a4fe0: Island Brew Byou is a long-running (since 1999) brew-on-premise and homebrew supply shop on Station Avenue in Langford, where customers participate in making their own craft beer, wine, fruit wine, and sparkling cider using stainless steel, gas-fired kettles and 200+ product choices. The shop stocks an extensive range of homebrewing equipment and ingredients and is the only Victoria-area location brewing beer this way. It also sells packaged products — including gluten-free beer — to take home.
6c360d053f: Storm Brewing is Vancouver's longest-running craft brewery, operating since 1994 on the lively Commercial Drive under founder and brewer James Walton. The brewery is celebrated for its ever-changing roster of inventive 'Brainstorm' small-batch beers — over 400 unique brews produced to date — all unfiltered, unpasteurized, and additive-free. Visitors enter through a loading door directly into an active working brewery, an experience that earned a 'Legendary local brewery' nod from Lonely Planet.
cc29abcefa: A-Frame Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom in Squamish, BC, open since December 2016 and built around the nostalgia of BC lake cabin life — each beer is named after a beloved provincial lake. The spacious patio features a fire pit and resident food truck Flipside Burgers, and the BYO-food policy makes it a relaxed, accessible stop for hungry visitors. The brewery has earned multiple Canadian Brewing Awards, including Gold for its Arctic Lake Dark Lager at the 2023 nationals.
604af01160: Macaloney's is Canada's most awarded craft distillery, producing award-winning single malt whiskies using traditional Scottish methods in hand-hammered Forsyth's copper pot stills. The same facility houses TWA Dogs Brewery, with craft beers brewed onsite including rotating seasonals. Touring cyclists can visit the tasting room to enjoy whisky flights, a pint of craft beer, or a behind-the-scenes distillery tour with the option to pour their own personalized whisky.
194efb5609: Rocky Creek Winery is a small family-run winery in Cowichan Bay, currently under new ownership by Jeremy and Susanna East, who took over from founders Mark and Linda (operating since 2005). Jeremy holds a WSET Level 3 award and is completing professional winemaking certification through UC Davis, bringing a craft-focused approach to the operation. The winery sells wines online, with a physical tasting room described as coming soon — making it an emerging destination on the Vancouver Island cycling circuit.
6a2a20173b: Liquidity Wines is an estate winery perched on a hillside in Okanagan Falls, overlooking Vaseux Lake and the iconic McIntyre Bluff, with curated art installations woven throughout the property. Cyclists can stop for wine tastings in the tasting room, share plates in the Tapas Room, or book a night at The Loft on-site accommodation. The winery sits in the heart of the South Okanagan wine country, a region well-travelled by touring cyclists on the Naramata and Okanagan Falls circuits.
a0a8e59d2d: Meadow Vista Honey Wines is a working meadery and artisan farm on a 5.5-acre property nestled among the orchards of East Kelowna, producing award-winning honey wines (meads) from the honey of 150 on-site beehives. The farm offers walk-in tastings, guided bee tours, and a seasonal farm-to-table bistro with outdoor patio and gazebo seating. It is a distinctive stop in Okanagan wine country, offering something genuinely different from the region's many grape wineries.
87284ca32a: The Masthead Restaurant is a waterfront dining destination in Cowichan Bay on Vancouver Island, historically known for seafood and regional cuisine in a harbour-side setting. It sits along the Vancouver Crossing Loop route, making it a potential stop for touring cyclists exploring the Cowichan Valley. Its current operating status is unclear based on prominent closure notices on its website.
7cf323782e: Sea Star Vineyard and Winery is a boutique estate winery on Pender Island in BC's Gulf Islands, recognized by Sip Northwest as one of the '9 Wineries to Visit Before You Die.' The 26-acre terraced vineyard climbs to the summit of Mount Menzies, and the cedar-and-stone tasting room opens onto outdoor seating with views of the surrounding forest and vines. In summer months a local food truck is on site, and the winery produces limited-run coastal whites, rosés, and light reds using minimal-intervention methods.
a8a057ebc0: Fitzpatrick Family Vineyards at Greata Ranch is a historic lakeside winery on Highway 97 between Peachland and Summerland, specializing in Traditional Method sparkling wines made from estate-grown grapes on a site that has grown fruit since 1901. The property features a wine shop patio with panoramic Okanagan Lake views and the 19 Bistro serving lunch. It sits on a quiet bench above the lake, making it a scenic mid-ride stop for cyclists touring the Okanagan Valley.
f7dc2dca30: Fort Berens Estate Winery is Lillooet's first winery, established in 2009 on sagebrush-covered benchland along the Fraser River at the foot of the Coast Mountains — a striking high-desert setting unlike any other BC wine region. The tasting room sits above the vineyard with panoramic views and no reservations required for drop-in visits. The winery sits at the halfway point of the scenic Coast Mountain circle tour via Highways 99, 12, and 1, making it a natural destination stop for cyclists traveling between Whistler and the BC interior.
13b3276de5: Lake Breeze Vineyards is a family-owned estate winery on the Naramata Bench above Lake Okanagan, with vines first planted in 1985 that rank among the oldest on the bench. The property features The Patio Restaurant serving seasonally inspired, locally sourced plates designed to pair with their estate wines, as well as a daily-open wine shop and tasting room. Located just minutes from both Naramata village and Penticton, it sits directly on one of BC's most celebrated cycling corridors.
7f0fb9a9f5: Barn Owl Brewing is a community-focused craft brewery housed in a beautifully restored 1920s Surtees family dairy barn on Kelowna's Lakeshore Road, listed on the BC Ale Trail. The brewery is BC Green Business Certified, uses a water-efficient BREWHA system, and feeds spent grain to a local cattle farm. Touring cyclists will find 20+ small-batch beers alongside rotating food trucks (wood-fired pizza and handmade ramen), plus a lively weekly events calendar featuring live music and a run club.
b8059ee3c6: The 101 Brewhouse + Distillery has been the community gathering spot in Upper Gibsons since 2017, brewing award-winning craft beers — including a 2022 BC Beer Awards first-place lager — and distilling small-batch gin and vodka made from BC-grown ingredients. The kitchen turns out a broad menu of locally-inspired dishes alongside the taps, and the venue runs a steady calendar of live music, trivia nights, and themed events. For a touring cyclist arriving on the Sunshine Coast, it offers a full sit-down meal with vegetarian and gluten-free options plus online ordering for takeaway.
dacfbe0175: The Kitchen Dada is a sushi bar and grill on Alma Street in Vancouver's Point Grey neighbourhood, close to the Vancouver Crossing Loop route. The restaurant posts daily takeout specials and offers online ordering and delivery alongside dine-in service. It is an accessible neighbourhood spot for a quick sushi meal mid-ride.
d2d8845618: Therapy Vineyards is a boutique winery situated on the Naramata Bench, one of British Columbia's most celebrated wine touring routes. Walk-in tastings are welcome for individuals and small groups, making it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the area. The winery operates its own ecommerce platform and tasting room booking system, suggesting a well-established visitor experience.
767de3971a: Ripples Winery & New Wave Distilling is a family-run estate on 12 acres of organic blueberry fields in the Fraser Valley, combining a winery and craft distillery in a lush garden setting with ponds, tropical plants, and shaded patios. The operation produces organic blueberry wines, BC grape wines, and handcrafted small-batch spirits—gins, vodkas, rums, and liqueurs—all from locally grown or sourced ingredients. Touring cyclists can settle into covered or open-air patio seating for a flight, a craft cocktail, or small bites in what the owners describe as a serene garden oasis.
a694de7d9f: Okanagan Spirits is Western Canada's original craft distillery, founded in 2004 and crafting internationally awarded spirits from 100% BC grain and fruit. The Kelowna location on Bernard Avenue features a tasting room, cocktail lounge, and patio open to drop-in visitors without a reservation. In 2025 the distillery swept the podium at the World Spirits Awards in Germany, earning the World-Class Distillery designation alongside 11 Gold and 5 Silver medals.
777c4d90a2: Train Wreck Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom that opened in Port Moody in 2024, producing unfiltered, full-flavoured beers — from hazy IPAs and hefeweizens to Belgian dubbels and dry Irish stouts — using time-honoured techniques and quality local ingredients. The sprawling yet intimate taproom doubles as an event venue with daily food vendors, bar games, and live music, making it a genuine community gathering place. The brewery also offers behind-the-scenes tours, adding an educational dimension for curious visitors.
94543d96af: Tofino Brewing Co. is a locally rooted craft brewery and taproom that has been part of the Tofino community since April 2011, brewing West Coast-inspired beers including a Kelp Stout made with locally harvested kelp and a seasonal Spruce Tree Ale conditioned with fresh spruce tips. The taproom offers an evolving roster of small-batch beers alongside ciders, non-alcoholic options, and wine, with an on-site food truck partner (Picnic at the Brewery) serving grilled sandwiches and local charcuterie on the front patio. Dogs are welcome on the patios and kids are allowed with an adult, making it a relaxed and inclusive destination for visiting cyclists.
42e130bf3a: Dead Frog Brewery is a Fraser Valley craft brewery that has been producing small-batch, unpasteurized beer for over 10 years, brewed just 50 feet from the tasting room taps. Their Langley tasting room pairs a rotating lineup of creative craft beers — from habanero hazy IPAs to peanut butter stouts — with a full food menu and a dog-friendly patio. Regular events including live music, themed brew competitions, and family-friendly afternoons make it a lively community stop in Langley's industrial corridor.
59a68bd4cb: Rewind Beer Co is a Port Moody brewery tasting room with a time-travel theme, pouring a rotating lineup of house-brewed craft beers alongside guest taps and ciders. The tasting room doubles as a pizza kitchen, serving creative wood-fired pies available for dine-in. It's a lively neighbourhood spot with a full non-alcoholic beverage selection and regular food features.
3a13677668: Bad Dog Brewing Company is a craft micro-brewery tucked into the rural back roads of Sooke, BC, pouring 12 taps of house-brewed ales, IPAs, stouts, and seasonal specialties in an indoor tasting room, on a heated patio, or at outdoor picnic tables. An on-site Hot Diggity Dog food trailer rounds out the experience with hot food. Now celebrating its 8th year, the brewery hosts live music events and community fundraisers, making it a lively destination on the quieter roads west of Victoria.
b8b73d3bd3: Arbutus Distillery is a BC-classified craft distillery in Nanaimo that brews, ferments, distils, and bottles all its spirits on-site using 100% BC-grown fermentables and many botanicals grown on the property. Its award-winning lineup includes Canadian Single Malt Whisky, Canadian Rye Whisky, brandy, absinthe, and gin. Visiting cyclists can sample and purchase bottles directly at the on-site Tasting Lounge, which also offers weekend cocktail service.
25c13a816d: Salt Spring Brewing Co. is a craft brewery tucked into the woods of Salt Spring Island, offering a tasting room and outdoor patio where visitors can sample core and seasonal beers. The brewery bills itself as 'a gem hidden in the woods' and hosts events including an annual Oktoberfest celebration. For cyclists touring the island, it serves as a scenic off-the-beaten-path destination to rest and enjoy locally made beer.
a9c8d5cd04: The Waddling Dog is an award-winning neighbourhood pub attached to the Quality Inn Waddling Dog hotel in Saanichton, serving classic pub dishes with a west coast twist alongside a full bar. An onsite beer, wine, and spirits shop rounds out the offering, making it a convenient stop near the BC Ferries Swartz Bay terminal and Butchart Gardens. It sits just off Highway 17 (Patricia Bay Hwy), a key artery for cyclists on the Saanich Peninsula.
5feb0e4703: Enrico Winery is a 100% local, family-owned BC winery set on a working vineyard in Mill Bay, offering drop-in tastings in their tasting room and across two outdoor patios. Dogs are welcome on the outdoor patio and the facilities are confirmed accessible. Wine is available to purchase and take away, and light snack items are available for on-site purchase.
df078d8d05: Kutatás Wines is a small artisan winery with an open cellar door in Chemainus on Vancouver Island, where visitors can taste and purchase wines produced on-site. The food program is seasonal, but the winery actively encourages guests to bring a picnic to enjoy with their wines. Bottles can be purchased to take away or shipped within BC for those stocking up for the road.
31d3bbabab: Summerhill Pyramid Winery is Canada's only Demeter-certified biodynamic vineyard, founded by the Cipes family in 1986 on 17 hectares above Okanagan Lake in Kelowna. The property is anchored by a replica Egyptian pyramid cellar built to sacred geometry proportions, used to age the winery's 100% organic wines. Cyclists can browse the retail wine shop, dine in the bistro with panoramic lake views, or arrange a tour of the pyramid — a genuinely singular stop in the Okanagan wine country.
72c8dad31a: Truck 59 Cider House is a craft cider tasting room perched along the West Kelowna wine trail with panoramic Okanagan Lake views, wide-open lawn space, and a laid-back family-friendly atmosphere. Part of the Jason Parkes Customs family of producers, it pours its own handcrafted ciders alongside beer from The Hatching Post, JPC wines, and cocktails in the newer adults-only Truck Yard section. A regular calendar of live music, food-truck pop-ups, and seasonal events makes it a lively stop on a West Kelowna ride.
a2e56a1105: Twin Island Cider is an artisan cidery on North and South Pender Islands that harvests fruit from dozens of century-old settler orchards, fermenting exclusively with native yeasts to produce terroir-driven natural ciders and perries. Visitors are welcomed to an outdoor picnic area for drop-in tastings and cider by the glass, with current bottled releases available for purchase on-site. The cidery has been featured in Wine Enthusiast, Montecristo Magazine, and Cider Craft Magazine for its distinctive place-based approach to craft fermentation.
f89dc5f1cf: R&B Brewing is one of Vancouver's original craft microbreweries, operating in the historic Brewery Creek district of East Vancouver since 1997. Their Ale & Pizza House taproom pairs house-brewed artisan ales and lagers — including award-winning staples like Raven Cream Ale and Stolen Bike Lager — with a full menu of pizzas, sandwiches, and salads crafted by an in-house chef. The space is dog-friendly on the patio, kids-welcome indoors, and driven by a strong community ethos with a live code of conduct and growler fills available for take-home beer.
5bda262149: Bridge Brewing Company is a North Vancouver craft brewery operating a taproom and tasting room at its original Charlotte Road location, one of three Bridge Brewing venues across the North Shore. The taproom pours a rotating lineup of core and seasonal house beers, and the site also hosts a playful 'Bridge Arcade' experience. A keg rental program and private event space at a sister location round out the brewery's community presence.
6c562ccbb4: Garry Oaks is a boutique, award-winning estate winery on Salt Spring Island where every grape is grown on-site across seven acres of vineyard. Current owner Nalini Samuel has expanded the program to include sparkling and dessert wines, and the winery operates with certified organic practices under the BC Environmental Farm Plan Program. Visitors can drop in for tastings, join a guided vineyard tour, and browse the on-site shop stocked with estate-bottled wines and locally sourced food and beverages.
037765b96b: Kettle River Brewing Company is a small-batch craft brewpub in downtown Kelowna's North End, running a 5-barrel in-house brewhouse with ten rotating draught taps since 2016. The kitchen is helmed by Food Network Canada Top Chef veteran Brock Bowes, producing a monthly-changing premium pub food menu crafted with the brewery's own beers in mind. The taproom is a self-described BIPOC and LGBTQ2S+ inclusive safe space with regular live music, trivia nights, and Sunday brunch.
bc103e7d14: Luppolo Brewing Company is a neighbourhood craft brewery and tasting room in Vancouver's East Side, inspired by the relaxed social culture of the Italian birrificio, pairing an extensive rotating tap list with hand-stretched authentic Italian pizzas made fresh daily in partnership with Local Pizzaiolo. The brewery has been a community gathering spot for nearly a decade, owned and shaped by two couples whose warmth sets the tone for the space. Touring cyclists will find dedicated bike parking, a full food menu, and a wide range of non-alcoholic and gluten-free drink options.
7122fc0d58: Quails' Gate Estate Winery has been growing and crafting award-winning wines on Boucherie Road since 1989, when the Stewart family planted their first vines on this Okanagan Lake-side estate. The property combines a daily-open wine shop and guided tasting experiences with the acclaimed Old Vines Restaurant, offering farm-to-table cuisine alongside sweeping lake and vineyard views. On-site accommodations at The Lake House and The Nest make this a natural overnight destination for touring cyclists exploring the West Kelowna wine-route corridor.
b46dcc58ea: Hainle Vineyards Estate Winery is BC's 8th estate winery, founded in 1972, and holds the distinction of being both the birthplace of North American Icewine and Canada's first certified organic winery (1988). The estate produces naturally handcrafted, chemical-free wines from its own Peachland vineyard using winemaking traditions dating to the mid-1800s. Touring cyclists can visit the wine shop for tastings and in-store purchases, and the property also offers a Bed & Breakfast for those looking to extend their stay in the Okanagan.
a5e25625e2: Gray Monk Estate Winery is one of British Columbia's pioneering wineries, established in 1972 when founders George and Trudy Heiss planted Canada's first Pinot Gris vines. The estate overlooks Okanagan Lake in Lake Country and features The Lookout Restaurant with lake views, wine tastings, and a shop. Touring cyclists on the Okanagan rail trail or lake loop will find it a scenic and rewarding stop for award-winning cool-climate wines and a sit-down meal.
8acc7988b2: Superflux Beer Company is a craft brewery and taproom nestled between Strathcona and East Vancouver, specializing in IPA alongside a broader range of styles including lagers and pale ales. The brewery offers a full food menu with seating both indoors and on a covered patio, and operates an on-site beer store selling cans to go. The /home page title also identifies it as a dog-friendly brewery, which may appeal to cyclists travelling with pets.
bb9ce8ee21: Angel Estate Winery sits on Westham Island Road in the agricultural flatlands of the Fraser River delta, a scenic rural cycling area accessible from the Ladner area of Delta, BC. Tagged in OSM as both a craft winery and an alcohol shop, it appears to operate as an estate winery with on-site sales. The pastoral delta setting — dyke roads, farmland, and river views — makes it a natural waypoint for cyclists exploring the South Delta cycling network.
aef63bab43: Spinnakers Gastro Brewpub is Canada's first purpose-built gastro brewpub, crafting beer on the Victoria waterfront since 1984 with views of the Inner Harbour. The site combines a pub-style restaurant, taproom, a covered and heated outdoor patio, and heritage guesthouses, all supported by house-brewed ales, ciders, and sours made with local ingredients. Touring cyclists can fuel up on locally-sourced seasonal fare and pick up growler fills from the on-site provisions store.
4159540e39: Slow Hand Beer Company is a small BC-licensed craft brewery that brews a constantly rotating selection of small-batch beers skewing toward lighter, crisper, and sessionable styles with creative twists on world beer traditions. Their retail store and tasting lounge are hosted within Threefold Brewery at 1507 Powell St in Vancouver's Strathcona neighbourhood. The two-person operation — one owner focused on sales, one on brewing — keeps things intimate and craft-forward.
7dbb8f9e7e: A community-focused craft brewpub on the Sunshine Coast, brewing award-winning beers inspired by the coastal lifestyle since 2017. The patio overlooks Howe Sound and has been voted best patio by the Sunshine Coast People's Choice Awards. The on-site Burger Shack serves food seven days a week, making it a reliable refuelling stop for touring cyclists on the Sunshine Coast.
47502bffd4: Sternwheeler Craft Distillery is an award-winning small-batch operation in downtown Creston producing spirits exclusively from locally grown fruit — saskatoons, apples, and other Creston Valley produce — with no grains, nuts, or artificial additives. Founded in 2017 as Wynndel Craft Distilleries, it relocated to a converted heritage building on Canyon Street in 2024 and opened a Lounge Bar in early 2025 stocked entirely with local beers, wines, ciders, and its own spirits. The distillery has accumulated multiple Canadian Artisan Spirit Competition honours including several Best in Class and Gold medals, making it a notable destination in the Kootenays.
5905b3a641: Cherry Point Estate Wines is one of Vancouver Island's pioneering wineries, established in 1990 on 34 acres of a former mink ranch in the Cowichan Valley, and among the first licensed wineries on the island. Positioned along the Vancouver Island Wine Route about 50 km north of Victoria, it offers daily guided tastings of award-winning whites and reds — including notable dessert wines — with suggested pairings from knowledgeable staff. A seasonal bistro on a brick patio amid the vines serves West Coast-inspired lunches, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists on a multi-day tour.
e38e28bf0a: Lang Vineyards holds the distinction of being British Columbia's first farm-gate winery, founded by Guenther Lang in 1990 and home to the oldest vines on the Naramata Bench. Now in its 35th year, this boutique family estate produces a wide range from crisp whites and rosés to dessert wines, with tastings available by reservation. The Naramata Bench is one of the Okanagan's premier cycling corridors, and this historic winery sits directly along that route.
145a72663b: Painted Rock Estate Winery is a family-owned operation perched on the eastern bench of Skaha Lake, producing ultra-premium terroir-driven wines from a 56-acre single-estate vineyard in the Okanagan Valley. The Skinner family has spent over 20 years crafting award-winning Bordeaux blends and single-varietal wines with the stated goal of raising the profile of Canadian wine internationally. A touring cyclist stopping here can visit the daily-open tasting room and take in sweeping views of Skaha Lake alongside tastings of some of Canada's most acclaimed estate wines.
d7e272fc11: Black Swift Vineyards is a single-vineyard winery perched in the hills of West Kelowna, part of the Jason Parkes Customs family of wineries and tasting rooms on the Westside. The tasting room is open daily with a casual, no-reservations-needed atmosphere, offering guided tastings and vineyard tours by golf cart. Named after the elusive Black Swift bird that lays just one egg per season, the winery emphasizes restraint and terroir-driven winemaking.
3eccd17c70: Niche Wine Co. is a small-batch family winery and working farm perched 620 metres above the Okanagan Valley floor in West Kelowna, offering tastings at the Hilltop Bar & Patio and a rotating lineup of food pop-ups on Sundays. The property includes The Outside Inn, a collection of luxury vineyard cabins that make it one of the few true agritourism stays in the Okanagan — a compelling stop or overnight for cyclists riding the Westside Wine Trail. The winery is explicitly welcoming to 2SLGBTQIA+ guests and families, and prides itself on an inclusive, relaxed farm atmosphere.
b5289cf21d: Vancouver Urban Winery is a working urban winery and atmospheric event venue in Railtown, housed in a 1923 building featuring exposed Douglas fir beams and floor-to-ceiling barrels. Established in 2011, it produces its own label wines and pours a rotating selection of over 30 BC wines on tap. Casual visitors are welcome for wine flights and tastings alongside the private-event bookings that anchor the business.
cd6c44a9d7: Beaumont Family Estate Winery is a family-run boutique winery at the foot of Boucherie Mountain in West Kelowna, producing 100% certified-organic estate wines since 1995 across 36 acres of vineyards. The Lubchynski family crafts small-batch wines including Pinot Noir, Gamay Noir, skin-contact Pinot Gris, and icewine, with daughter Alana serving as winemaker after working vintages in Australia, New Zealand, and Europe. Cyclists on the Okanagan wine route can stop in for a tasting, pick up bottles to go, and take in 360-degree views of the surrounding mountain valley and lake.
411362b731: Yellow Dog Brewing is a craft brewery that opened in Port Moody in 2014 and sits on Murray Street, the heart of the city's well-known Brewers Row. The tasting room serves daily snacks sourced from local bakeries and butchers alongside rotating food trucks throughout the week. In 2024 the brewery expanded with a second tasting room in Penticton.
8f08a23358: Ramification Cellars is an estate winery on the shores of Vaseux Lake near Penticton, producing wines exclusively from grapes grown on their own property with a focus on ecological stewardship of the Okanagan Valley. The winery offers tastings, a wine club, and event hosting in a scenic lakeside setting, making it a natural stop on the Okanagan wine route. Cyclists riding the area will find a tasting room with on-site washrooms and parking.
df31f4f816: Left Field Cider Co. is a family-owned artisanal cidery making handcrafted English-style cider from blends of English, French, and BC dessert apples. Founded in 2011 by sisters Theresa and Kate on their family ranch at Mamette Lake, they converted a hayfield into an orchard and a barn into a ciderhouse. The tasting room is located on Hwy 97C between Merritt and Logan Lake, offering a seasonal stop for passing cyclists in BC's Interior.
5a31b3f867: Twin City Brewing Company is an award-winning craft brewery and full-service taproom in Port Alberni, crafting a rotating roster of beers—from West Coast IPAs and German pilsners to fruit sours—entirely on-site. The kitchen turns out scratch-made food including hand-stretched pizza, smoked meat sandwiches, tacos, and rice bowls, making it a genuine meal stop rather than just a tasting room. Positioned in the Alberni Valley as part of Port Alberni's emerging tourism and recreation identity, it serves as a lively community hub for both locals and visitors exploring Vancouver Island.
d248777e90: Rust Wine Co. is a small-lot winery on the Golden Mile Bench — BC's first designated sub-appellation — sourcing from old-vine vineyards planted as far back as 1968. The tasting room offers sweeping views over the Black Sage Bench toward Osoyoos, and a restored 19th-century bunkhouse relocated from a silver mine serves as a unique vacation rental on the property. Weekly live music events through the season make it an animated stop along the South Okanagan winery route.
643f8b1aad: Whitetooth Brewing Company is a craft brewery and tasting room established in 2016 in Golden, BC, nestled between the Purcell and Rocky Mountain ranges near the confluence of the Kicking Horse and Columbia Rivers. They specialize in award-winning Belgian-inspired and West Coast-influenced small-batch beers, with names like 'Speed Metal Foreign Extra Stout' and 'Blower Pow IPA' directly celebrating mountain biking and powder skiing culture. The tasting room has no in-house kitchen but has delivery partnerships with three local restaurants, positioning it as a welcoming post-ride stop in one of BC's premier adventure-sport hubs.
da46f6538c: Red Barn Winery is a boutique winery situated on Black Sage Road in Oliver, squarely in the heart of South Okanagan wine country and along one of BC's most popular cycling corridors. Wines are sourced from Jagged Rock Vineyard and lean into bold fruit expression under an intentionally rebellious brand identity. The property hosts seasonal events including Tramonto Music Nights with live music on the patio, making it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the region.
3ea808a971: Alberni Brewing Company is a craft brewery and full-service brewpub in the heart of Port Alberni, producing its own house beers alongside rotating guest taps, wine, and cider. The kitchen menu is extensive — drawing on local suppliers for specialty bakery and meat products — and intentionally complements the brewery side of the operation. Dog-friendly patios, varied indoor seating, and a welcoming atmosphere make it a practical rest stop for cyclists riding the Alberni Valley corridor toward the Pacific Rim.
ad3fbc34d9: Mt. Begbie Brewery is an award-winning craft brewery that has been operating in Revelstoke, BC since 1996, making it one of the longest-running independent craft breweries in the province. The brewery features a tasting room and a retail store where cyclists can pick up packaged beer to go, alongside a food menu. Revelstoke's position as a gateway to mountain recreation makes this a natural stop for touring cyclists passing through town.
2a619e58f3: Celista Estate Winery is an 80-acre farm and vineyard on the north shore of Shuswap Lake in BC's interior, producing award-winning wines that have accumulated 115 medals over 14 years at national and international competitions. Visitors can take guided vineyard and winery tours, sample wines in the tasting room, dine at the on-site restaurant, rent one of four lakeside cabins, or attend a summer concert. The property is kid- and pet-friendly and wheelchair accessible, and the vineyard-and-lake panorama makes it a memorable destination stop.
0b9819fadf: Celista Estate Winery is an 80-acre vineyard estate on the north shore of Shuswap Lake in BC's interior, with vines first planted in 2002 and over 115 medals accumulated in national and international competitions across its first 14 years. Beyond wine tasting, the property offers guided vineyard tours, fine dining, four lakeside cabin rentals, weddings, and a busy summer concert series — making it an unusually multi-faceted destination. Cyclists exploring the Shuswap's quieter north shore will find it a welcoming, pet- and family-friendly stop with sweeping vineyard and lake views.
6f7af080c8: Dolly's Reach is a family-run wood-fired pizza restaurant in Quesnel, BC, operating since 2017 with two generations of family expertise in horticulture and food craft. The menu leans heavily on produce from their own farm and local growers, featuring house-made doughs, sauces, and seasonal cheesecakes. Cyclists will find a welcoming outdoor patio surrounded by the garden that supplies the kitchen, offering cocktails, mocktails, and hearty farm-to-table meals.
b6573d7191: Mythology is a boutique winery and distillery near Osoyoos in BC's South Okanagan, producing a range of reds, whites, rosés, and craft spirits including brandy, vodka, and gin. Visitors can book a guided tasting in the vineyard-side tasting room or linger in the pet-friendly picnic grounds over wine and charcuterie. The property also includes the Sonora Desert Inn, offering overnight accommodation surrounded by vineyard-lined hills and Okanagan valley views.
2da1d7c486: The Osprey Nest is a restaurant and social house situated on the shores of Williams Lake, on the traditional territory of the Williams Lake First Nation (T'exelcemc). Its menu blends brunch classics, hearty burgers, and bowls with inspiration drawn from Indigenous culinary traditions, featuring bannock, Three Sisters Scramble, and locally sourced seasonal ingredients. A virtual tour sponsored by Spinal Cord Injury BC highlights the venue's commitment to accessibility and welcoming all visitors.
2c6f3d1bdc: Gladstone Brewing Co. is a BC Brewery of the Year award-winner set inside a converted mechanic's garage in the heart of downtown Courtenay, in the Comox Valley. It serves a full scratch-made menu from brunch through dinner alongside its European lagers, Pacific Northwest pale ales, and experimental small-batch beers. Two distinct indoor spaces — the lively Brewers Bar and the intimate Engine Room — plus a large outdoor patio make it a natural gathering spot for locals and travellers alike.
87025b5822: Swiws Spirit Tours is an Osoyoos-based tour operator offering guided wine tours through the Oliver-Osoyoos wine region and Indigenous cultural tours led by members of the Osoyoos Indian Band (syilx nation). Their Spotted Lake tour departs from the Nk'Mip Desert Cultural Centre and includes a guided walk and a snakes-alive show. For a touring cyclist looking to explore the South Okanagan's wineries without pedalling, this company offers pick-up and drop-off at local accommodations.
2ac357b104: Chaberton Estate Winery is the Fraser Valley's oldest winery, founded in 1981 and set on a 55-acre vineyard in South Langley roughly 45 minutes from Vancouver. Visitors can take guided tours through the crush pad, tank room, and barrel cellar before tasting award-winning 100% BC VQA wines in the boutique tasting room or at outdoor picnic tables overlooking the vines. The on-site Bacchus Bistro serves authentic French-inspired cuisine made with local ingredients, making this a genuine wine-and-dine destination for touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.
f715046e71: A small boutique winery on the northern edge of the Great Basin Desert near Oliver, producing about 18,000 bottles per year. Wines are aged in a unique underground cellar overlooked by the namesake hidden chapel, and the tasting room is set among pines and gardens. Located only 5 km outside Oliver and 3 km from the District Wine Village, making it a feasible side trip for cyclists touring the South Okanagan wine country.
49d7f0d87b: Bordertown Cider & Winery is a family-owned estate winery and cidery in the heart of Osoyoos, operated by the Gill family whose fifth-generation farming roots go deep in the South Okanagan. The winery produces 14 VQA-certified varietals from 100 acres of estate vineyards, including award-winning Cabernet Franc and Viognier, plus a craft hard apple cider pressed from their own orchard fruit. Visitors are welcomed into a Mission-style tasting room with no reservation required, making it an accessible stop on a wine-country cycling route.
61a1fec8cb: Angry Hen Brewing is a craft brewery and lounge in the heart of historic Kaslo, BC, operating a 7-barrel brewhouse — one of the last built by Newlands — that produces a rotating lineup of lagers, ales, and a signature dry Irish stout on nitro. Originally founded in 2017 by brewer Shirley Warne, it is now owned by Cassie and Rogan, who continue the tradition of pairing quality craft beer with live music on a covered patio year-round. A welcoming stop for cyclists passing through the Kootenays, it positions itself as Kaslo's community living room with snacks, non-alcoholic drinks, and frequent local music events.
887e16e62b: Roots and Wings Distillery is Langley's first craft distillery, a family-owned farm operation near Fort Langley producing seed-to-sip spirits — including vodka, whiskey, gin, absinthe, and liqueurs — from ingredients grown on their own land. Visitors can sample craft cocktails, enjoy an in-house menu, and browse a bar gift shop stocked with artisan bottles to take away. The rural Fraser Valley setting and farm-to-glass story make it a distinctive destination on cycling routes through the Langley countryside.
96c334feae: Land & Sea Brewing Co. is a community-focused craft brewery and taproom in Comox, opened in December 2018 as the third craft brewery in the Comox Valley. The bright tasting room seats 70 guests with an open kitchen, and a sunny patio adds room for 40 more. The brewery actively encourages guests to arrive by bike or transit, noting its location steps from two BC Transit Route #1 bus stops.
3dcc714623: Robin Ridge Winery is a small, family-operated organic estate winery on the Similkameen Bench near the junction of Hwy 3 and Hwy 3A in Keremeos, with 18 acres of vines farmed without synthetic chemicals or pesticides. Founded by Tim and Caroline Cottrill, the winery is best known for its award-winning Gamay and produces a broad range of varietals including Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meritage, and a traditional Sparkling Finch. Cyclists exploring the Similkameen wine country will find a tasting room offering wines that aim to express the distinctive terroir of the valley.
49c71a1555: Beaufort Vineyard and Estate Winery is Vancouver Island's first certified organic winery, established in 2007 and situated on a 20-acre estate in the Comox Valley near Courtenay. The winery produces cool-climate varietals including Ortega, Gewürztraminer, and Pinot Noir under Ecocert organic certification using regenerative farming practices. Visiting cyclists can book guided tastings in a gazebo overlooking the vines, linger at the picnic area with a wine flight, and pick up locally sourced charcuterie boards on site.
9ca5f8b881: Black Hills Estate Winery is a premier South Okanagan estate on the Black Sage Bench near Oliver, founded in 1999 and renowned for its flagship Nota Bene red blend, which quickly developed a cult following. The winery has practiced organic and regenerative viticulture since 2020 and features a Wine Experience Centre with panoramic views of Mount Kobau, weekend dining at The Vineyard Kitchen in partnership with acclaimed Chef Jeff Van Geest, and the Vineyard Lodge for overnight stays. Black Sage Road is one of the most popular cycling routes through the South Okanagan wine region, placing this winery directly on many touring cyclists' routes.
69dde7ba77: Teníye Local Market is a community-driven grocery and vendor market proudly owned by the Simpcw First Nation and operated by Simpcw Resources Group in Barrière, BC. The site features a food truck serving bison burgers, sausages, and traditional Bannock as a nod to Simpcw heritage, plus a walk-up coffee and ice cream window. A dog-friendly fenced park and large-vehicle parking at the back make it a practical and welcoming rest stop for touring cyclists passing through the Thompson region.
0e934c3107: Quinta Ferreira is a family-owned Portuguese-heritage estate winery on the Black Sage Bench near Oliver, BC, established as an orchard in 1979 and converted to a vineyard beginning in 1999. The winery produces an extensive range of reds, whites, rosé, and dessert wines from varietals including Merlot, Syrah, Viognier, and Zinfandel, and is internationally recognized for award-winning wines. It hosts seasonal food-and-wine events on a licensed patio — including a Pig Roast and Paella Party with live music — making it a destination stop on one of the Okanagan's premier cycling roads.
b043faec85: Fox Mountain Brewing Co. is Williams Lake's hometown craft brewery, pouring a rotating lineup of house-brewed beers — from a Hillbilly Blonde to a hazy IPA named Pumptrack — alongside a full kitchen menu in a taproom with patio views of Williams Lake. The brewery operates with a no-reservations walk-in policy and welcomes dogs on the patio, making it an approachable stop for travellers passing through the Cariboo. Growler fills and 4-pack takeout are available for cyclists who want to carry their haul down the road.
0c8d950c4d: Smithers Brewing Co. is a timber-framed craft brewery in northern BC, crowned Brewery of the Year at the 2025 Canadian Brewing Awards. Their taproom runs 12 taps with four mainstay beers and five rotating seasonals alongside house-brewed kombucha, nitro cold brew, and BC wines for non-beer drinkers. It is a walk-in-friendly, first-come-first-served space with an outdoor patio that welcomes pets.
c985972ec4: A family-owned estate winery nestled in the Creston Valley of the Kootenays, Baillie-Grohman grows cool-climate varieties including Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris, and Gewürztraminer on its own vineyard.
