d2df8eef15: Kinara Indian Cuisine is an authentic Indian restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, specializing in tandoor-cooked dishes such as Butter Chicken, Fish Tikka, and Tandoori Prawn prepared by master chefs using traditional spices and clay tandoor techniques. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the heart of Vancouver. Vegetarian options including Palak Paneer and Crispy Pakora round out a diverse menu celebrating regional Indian culinary heritage.
864de805e4: Rudi is a Victoria restaurant that channels the owner's west coast upbringing and international travels into an evolving, craft-driven menu — described as discovering a personal culinary identity rather than replicating tradition. The restaurant operates both a daytime express concept and evening dinner service, and can host group events for up to 70 guests.
1812db3ecc: Thai Corner is a well-established Thai restaurant on Sidney's main commercial strip, blending central and northeastern (I-San) Thai culinary traditions under a chef with over two decades of experience cooking in Thailand and abroad. The restaurant offers a broad menu of curries, spicy salads, stir-fries, and noodles with customizable spice levels, and serves both buffet-style lunch and à la carte dinner. Cyclists passing through Sidney-by-the-sea will find a sit-down meal, takeout, and even free delivery within downtown Sidney.
235408b5e6: Spicy Pro Hot Pot is a hot pot restaurant located in Richmond, BC, a city known for its diverse and high-quality Asian dining scene. Hot pot dining is a communal, table-cooked experience where diners simmer fresh ingredients in a shared broth — a filling option for cyclists refuelling after a ride. The restaurant is located in a multi-unit commercial address on Capstan Way.
302988c647: Papa John's is a well-known international pizza chain with a location in North Vancouver offering takeout and delivery. The brand emphasizes fresh dough and quality ingredients under its 'Better Ingredients, Better Pizza' promise. Cyclists looking for a quick, hot meal can order for carryout without a drive-through queue.
8a2cf8e1db: Perry's Pizza and Grill is a long-established Cranbrook restaurant that started in Kimberley's Platzl in 1988 and relocated to Cranbrook in 2004. The menu centres on fresh daily-made dough pizzas, house-made burgers on Kaiser buns, pasta, and salads, with catering and online ordering available. A convenient stop for touring cyclists needing a filling sit-down or takeout meal in central Cranbrook.
4bf9d72abb: This Subway franchise sits on Columbia Avenue in Castlegar and offers the full lineup of Footlong and 6" sandwiches, wraps, and salads alongside breakfast options. It features a drive-through lane and supports multiple ordering modes including in-restaurant dining, curbside pickup, and delivery. A convenient calorie stop for cyclists passing through the Castlegar corridor on a long touring day.
237474a824: Tripke Bakery is a neighborhood bakery in Kelowna serving baked goods and related food items. As a bakery stop, it offers a place for cyclists to rest and purchase food.
25dbd721ea: Café salade de fruits is a French bistro tucked into Vancouver's Fairview neighbourhood at the corner of Fir Street and West 7th Avenue. It offers dine-in lunch and dinner service in a neighbourhood-bistro setting. Cyclists riding the nearby Seaside Greenway or the Arbutus Corridor will find it a convenient midday or evening stop for French-inspired cuisine.
ee91971427: Manchu Wok is a Canadian Chinese fast food chain that has operated for over 45 years, founded in 1980 and now present in over 80 locations across three countries. This location sits in the food court at Metropolis at Metrotown, one of Metro Vancouver's largest shopping malls. Cyclists can expect quick counter-service combos with choices of rice or noodle base and a variety of wok-fired entrées including vegetable options.
f769a56a99: Pidgin is an Asian-French fusion restaurant situated in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, blending the culinary traditions of two distinct food cultures into a single dining experience. It occupies a prominent spot on Carrall Street, a key corridor connecting downtown Vancouver to the seawall cycling network. The restaurant has garnered enough acclaim to announce a future location at Time Out Market Vancouver.
53959fcc0f: Best Bite Pizza is a Chilliwack pizzeria that has been serving the community since 1995. The menu spans an extensive range of specialty pizzas — from a Tandoori Masala to a HOT-HONEY — alongside pasta, cheesy fingers, and desserts, making it a substantial food stop for hungry cyclists. Gluten-free crust is available across the menu.
2562b88ae7: Brexit Pub is a pub located in Penticton, BC. Its original standalone website appears to be defunct, and discovery notes suggest a possible rebrand may have occurred. No further details about the venue's character or offerings could be confirmed from available sources.
27d55aa76c: Crêpe & Café is a French cuisine spot on West 41st Avenue in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, offering both dine-in and takeaway. Its accessible entrance (wheelchair=yes per OSM) and takeout option make it a plausible quick stop for a cyclist passing through the area. No outdoor seating is noted, so riders would be eating indoors or taking food to go.
1240a73a99: Mr. Dumpling (包好吃) is a Chinese fast food counter in Richmond, BC serving dumplings from a unit inside a larger commercial complex on Westminster Highway. Richmond is one of Canada's premier destinations for authentic Chinese cuisine, and this spot sits within that rich culinary corridor. A touring cyclist looking for a quick, filling bite after riding the flat dyke trails of the Fraser delta would find it a practical and flavourful stop.
5f1a9e061b: The Fish Man is a restaurant in Richmond offering both indoor and outdoor seating in a smoke-free environment. It provides a casual dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.
056b3e17da: Copa Cafe is a Hong Kong-style cafe restaurant that has been serving classic Cantonese-Western fusion dishes since 2006. Signature items include baked pork chop on rice, sizzling hot plates, and a coconut-milk curry beef brisket rooted in traditional Hong Kong cafe (cha chaan teng) cooking. The restaurant operates a VIP membership program and rotating seasonal specials, suggesting a loyal local following.
434a98fd66: Marina Bay Cafe is a Deaf-owned and operated specialty cafe perched on the scenic Esquimalt waterfront in Victoria, offering a creative menu of espresso drinks, tea lattes, smoothies, and toasties sourced from local suppliers including Fernwood Coffee. The cafe was featured on CHEK News for its community story, and staff are encouraged to learn American Sign Language, making it a notably inclusive stop on Victoria's waterfront cycling routes.
87e6f31799: Brunch is a Mexican-inspired brunch restaurant in Downtown Vancouver's Granville Street corridor, specializing in dishes like chilaquiles, enchiladas suizas, and eggs Benedict made with Mexican-sourced flavors and techniques. The restaurant offers a warm dine-in experience alongside takeout and delivery, making it a flexible stop for those exploring the downtown core. Vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free accommodations are available on request from staff.
bfddd69d4a: Belgard Kitchen is a full-service restaurant in Vancouver's Railtown Design District, just east of Gastown, highlighting Canadian ingredients from coast to coast with globally influenced techniques and a drink menu centred on BC wines and craft beer. It operates lunch on weekdays, brunch on weekends, happy hour, and dinner seven nights a week, with private dining spaces available in the Mezzanine and Cellar venues. The same hospitality group runs sister restaurants Havana Vancouver, The Flamingo Room, and Violeté.
843e74d7f0: Jita's Cafe is a coffee shop in downtown Golden on 11th Avenue North. It offers internet access and serves as a stopping point for cyclists and visitors to the area.
cf3656d208: TAKO is a Korean-fusion fast food shop specializing in tacos, burritos, quesadillas, bibimbap bowls, and poutine built around Korean BBQ fillings like bulgogi, spicy pork belly, and BBQ short rib. It sits directly across from Rogers Arena at the Stadium/Chinatown SkyTrain stop, putting it squarely on Vancouver's inner-harbour cycling corridor. The outdoor patio makes it a natural drop-in stop for cyclists exploring the nearby seawall.
9c57da5445: Smile Chicken is a Korean fast-casual restaurant in downtown Victoria specializing in Korean-style fried chicken and corndogs alongside sides like kimchi and pickled radish. Located in a unit at 1001 Douglas St, it offers online ordering with a 15-minute pickup window, making it a quick stop for cyclists passing through the city centre. With 53 customer reviews, it has established a following for its corndog and seasoned chicken offerings.
297819aa4d: Pizza Rubato Napoletana is a Neo-Neapolitan pizzeria on West Broadway that takes its name from the musical concept of 'tempo rubato' — staying rooted in 300-year-old Neapolitan tradition while freely riffing on ingredients and flavour combinations. The kitchen uses imported Italian '00' flour, a 48-hour fermentation process, and an AVPN-approved Valoriani oven that replicates a wood-fired experience, producing a crispy, charred crust. Cyclists heading along the Broadway corridor will find an extensive creative menu alongside catering and events services.
1430c56f3d: Charqui is a gastropub and resto-bar that has anchored the Kitsilano neighbourhood since 2007, known for its wings, craft beer selection, and lively entertainment programming including live music and karaoke. It sits on Cornwall Avenue, close to the popular Kitsilano Beach cycling corridor along the Vancouver waterfront. Indoor and outdoor seating are both available.
9fcde2f653: Fol Épi is an organic bakery and cafe established in 2009 in Victoria, BC, whose name means 'crazy wheat head' — an homage to French baking tradition and wild yeast cultures. Operating out of Dockside Green, they stone-grind their own flour on-site and produce artisan breads, all-butter viennoiserie, seasonal pastries, and daily sandwiches using local, small-scale producers. It is a well-established community fixture that also supplies other local businesses.
7f7ab29f99: Fuego Old Town Eatery is a lively, rustic Mexican-style brunch spot established in 2015 in Victoria's historic Old Town neighbourhood. It serves a creative all-day breakfast and lunch menu featuring chorizo, pulled pork, eggs benedict, chilaquiles, and house-made cornbread on a first-come, first-served basis. Its location on Store Street puts it squarely in the heart of Victoria's waterfront cycling corridor.
56b4bc5154: The WISE Hall is a storied East Vancouver institution founded in 1957 as a social club for Welsh, Irish, Scottish, and English immigrants, now a 250-capacity concert venue with a rich history of Canadian performers gracing its stage. The downstairs Lounge is a classic cash-only neighborhood pub with pool table and darts, operating as a members-and-guests club open to anyone 19+ with valid ID. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a genuinely local hangout steeped in community history, steps from the Adanac cycling corridor.
f14316346a: Shelter Waterfront is a long-running Tofino dining institution first opened in 2003, relocated in 2022 to a scenic waterfront home at the Tofino Resort and Marina after a fire destroyed the original location. The restaurant celebrates locally sourced West Coast ingredients — including fresh-shucked Vancouver Island oysters and locally caught salmon — served in an open-concept space with natural wood finishes and a patio overlooking the Tofino Inlet and Clayoquot Sound. It operates as a full-service café through dinner service and is a well-known gathering place for both locals and visitors passing through Tofino.
6ea10f963a: ZUBU is a Japanese ramen restaurant with four Lower Mainland locations, with this downtown Vancouver outpost opening in January 2023. The menu, helmed by Executive Chef William Cao (a graduate of Kitchen Hyodo Ramen School in Oyama, Japan), centres on ramen made with locally sourced and Japanese-imported ingredients, alongside temaki, hand-made gyoza, and rice bowls. A full cocktail program rounds out the experience.
3197f6af08: Blooming Spice Fish House is a Sichuan-style restaurant specialising in its signature 'boiling fish' — black fish slices doused tableside in two pounds of scorching hot oil loaded with chili and Sichuan peppercorns sourced directly from China. The dish follows a 30-year-old recipe, and the menu extends to cold jelly noodles, spicy frog, and dry-pot dishes. This is the chain's sole BC location, situated in a commercial complex in central Richmond.
c45eb2889b: Bel Café is a patisserie café located within the Rosewood Hotel Georgia, a beautifully restored 1927 heritage landmark in downtown Vancouver. Operated by the Hawksworth Restaurant group, it serves handcrafted drinks, fresh pastries, and light fare including soups, sandwiches, and salads. The refined lobby-café setting provides a distinctive midday stop for cyclists passing through Vancouver's downtown core.
cf460cf302: Social is a full-service restaurant and bar on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most bicycle-friendly streets and a hub of the local cycling community. The venue features a street-level dining room and a rooftop patio, making it a lively spot for a sit-down meal after a ride. Reservations are accepted downstairs while the rooftop operates on a first-come, first-served basis.
7945419a81: Boston Pizza Big Bend is a full-service Canadian casual dining chain restaurant and sports bar located in the Big Bend area of Burnaby. Founded by a Greek immigrant in Edmonton in 1964, it is now Canada's largest casual dining brand with hundreds of locally owned franchise locations. The Big Bend location offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery with a broad menu spanning pizzas, pastas, wings, burgers, and more.
3a9aa60bba: Cilantro & Jalapeño is a multi-award-winning authentic Mexican takeout restaurant inside Lonsdale Quay Market on North Vancouver's waterfront, voted Best Mexican Restaurant on the North Shore six consecutive years (2010–2015). The kitchen produces scratch-made tacos, tamales, enchiladas, burritos, and house sauces using traditional recipes, alongside a retail selection of hard-to-find Latin American specialty ingredients. The market location sits steps from the SeaBus terminal, making it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists travelling between downtown Vancouver and the North Shore.
f02c824bfe: Simply Pho is a family-owned Vietnamese restaurant in Tsawwassen offering an extensive menu of authentic pho varieties alongside classic appetizers like spring rolls, salad rolls, and calamari. The restaurant is located in the Canoe Pass Way retail complex near the Tsawwassen Mills area, making it a convenient sit-down meal stop for cyclists riding the South Delta region. It is one of the few Vietnamese dining options in this part of the Lower Mainland.
a789a09d1e: Uptown Pizza is a sit-down pizza and Italian restaurant offering an unusually broad menu spanning classic and specialty pizzas, stuffed pastas, seafood dishes, wings, burgers, and more. The restaurant has both indoor and outdoor seating and accepts online orders for pickup and delivery. Its extensive menu makes it a substantial refuelling stop for cyclists seeking a full meal rather than a quick snack.
985d28de63: Kami Pizza is a pizza fast food establishment in Kamloops on Tranquille Road. It provides a casual food option for cyclists passing through the area.
966fb30f39: Nemesis Coffee is a specialty coffee roaster and multi-location café group based in Metro Vancouver, with this Surrey 'Pavilion' branch serving espresso and filter coffee sourced from named farms and individual producers. Pastries from their in-house Dope Bakehouse label — including croissants and pain au chocolat — round out the menu. The company roasts its own beans and is a proud supporter of World Coffee Research, signalling a genuine craft-roaster ethos rather than a commodity café.
450b149d55: La Cantina (branded online as Tacos La Cantina) is an authentic Mexican taqueria founded by Pepe Barajas, inspired by the street-food culture of Mexico. The Nesters Plaza location operates as a takeout and delivery outlet, offering tacos, burritos, quesadillas, and margaritas with a strong emphasis on dietary inclusivity. It has built a local reputation as Whistler's best taqueria, with delivery available through Skip the Dishes, DoorDash, and Uber Eats.
008e8febcb: Yu Xiang Yuan Restaurant is a Chinese cuisine spot on Fraser Street in Vancouver, specializing in regional dishes spanning Szechuan, Northern Chinese, and Xinjiang traditions. The menu features hand-pulled and dragging noodles, steamed dumplings, cumin lamb kabobs, and classic stir-fries like Ginger Beef and Kung Pao Chicken. Online ordering is available through their website, offering a convenient stop option for cyclists fueling up on a long urban route.
842550b39f: Foodies on Board is a chef-driven dine-in and takeout restaurant in Burnaby's Production Way corridor, built around an ever-changing weekly menu sourced directly from local BC farmers and cooperatives. Chef Ken's all-day brunch program features house-baked pastries, organic eggs from Rabbit River Farm, and nitrate-free smoked bacon, paired with Lavazza espresso drinks. Beyond the restaurant, the business also runs a catering service and a weekend meal prep program offering a wide range of dietary options.
9bac00bb1a: A family-owned German restaurant established in 1975, The Black Forest sits on the Esplanade in Harrison Hot Springs overlooking Harrison Lake, about 10 km off Highway 1. It specialises in authentic schnitzel, pork hock, bratwurst, and housemade spaetzle, and is widely regarded as one of the area's standout dining destinations. A heated patio with lake views makes it a rewarding stop after a day on the bike.
5cb6d37c60: Peqish is a walk-in fast food restaurant on Seymour Street in downtown Vancouver. The business does not operate a drive-through service. It provides quick-service dining for area visitors and locals.
a943274f2a: Drip Coffee Social is a community-focused café established in 2018 on the Departure Bay waterfront in Nanaimo, offering indoor seating, a patio, and a sandy beach directly across the street. The menu spans specialty espresso drinks, grain bowls, sandwiches, and baked goods alongside beer, wine, and seasonal cocktails. A second location operates on Dufferin Crescent, but the Departure Bay outpost is the standout cycling stop given its beachside setting.
b87a59998b: Browns Socialhouse is a restaurant in the North Vancouver town centre. It offers a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.
0338a09bcc: Woo Korean BBQ is a table-grill Korean BBQ restaurant in South Surrey emphasizing fresh premium Canadian meats alongside seafood and traditional Korean dishes. It bills itself as Greater Vancouver's best Korean BBQ spot and offers a broad menu ranging from beef BBQ courses to dolsot bibimbap and stews. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a sit-down, full-service meal suited to refuelling after a long ride.
877f14711b: Cream Pony is a casual counter-service spot on Main Street in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood specializing in fried chicken and donuts, with a second location in North Vancouver's Shipyard District. The shop has built a loyal following for its glazed donuts and juicy chicken sandwiches. It also offers catering and is available through major delivery platforms.
2457e8ba6d: Pacific Poke is a chef-driven, quick-serve poke restaurant chain founded in Vancouver by two food-passionate entrepreneurs who discovered Hawaiian poke in California and brought a fresh West Coast spin to it. The menu features build-your-own poke bowls with locally-sourced ingredients alongside chef-inspired signature bowls, emphasizing responsible sourcing and sustainability. The brand has expanded to multiple BC and Alberta locations, making it a recognizable stop for cyclists passing through Vancouver's West Broadway corridor.
46fc7b14f1: The Keg Steakhouse + Bar is a well-known Canadian steakhouse chain with a recently renovated Abbotsford location situated just off Highway 1 at Sumas Way. The restaurant features a full lounge and bar with televisions, a semi-private dining room, and patio seating, making it a comfortable stop for a sit-down meal after a long day in the saddle. Free parking and wheelchair accessibility round out the practical amenities at this location.
4045bf3e3d: Landmark Hot Pot House is a restaurant specializing in hot pot cuisine on Cambie Street in Vancouver. It features indoor seating and operates daily for dinner service, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking a meal. The restaurant offers a communal dining experience where diners cook ingredients in a shared broth at their table.
485100381e: The Old Spaghetti Factory is a 100% Canadian-owned chain Italian restaurant with a New Westminster location on Eighth Street, offering multi-course pasta meals made with locally-sourced ingredients where possible. The restaurant is a full-service sit-down establishment with indoor seating and no outdoor patio. It is one of 15 locations across Canada and can accommodate a range of dietary needs including gluten-free, vegan, and allergen requests.
1e24d47180: La Ruota Pizzeria is a Neapolitan-inspired pizza franchise with four Metro Vancouver locations, cooking its pies in a 900°F oven using authentic Caputo '00' flour and fresh ingredients sourced from Italy and BC. The West Broadway location sits on one of Vancouver's primary east-west cycling corridors and offers a broad menu spanning meat and veggie pizzas, sandwiches, pastas, and antipasti. The restaurant operates a franchise model with online ordering, delivery, and a loyalty rewards program.
639662c334: A street food vendor specializing in waffles operating in Kelowna. Offers quick takeaway meals ideal for cyclists seeking a casual roadside stop.
ed5500579b: C Market Coffee takes its name from the global commodity exchange where Arabica coffee is traded, and the Port Coquitlam location is part of a growing BC chain that roasts micro-lot beans in-house and pairs them with fresh, thoughtfully crafted food in a design-forward space. Beyond espresso drinks, the café offers matcha, loose-leaf tea, coffee classes, pop-up markets, and room rental, functioning as a genuine community hub rather than just a quick-stop café. Cyclists will find a full food menu with published nutrition and allergen guides, and a mobile app for ordering ahead.
893d54dd05: A two-storey McDonald's location in Delta, BC offering drive-through, takeaway, and outdoor seating. As a full-service fast food restaurant on 56 Street, it serves as a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. The national rewards app offers app-exclusive deals that can be useful on longer rides.
58c1382d28: The Salty Caramel Kitchen is a fully plant-based bakery and cafe just off Okanagan Lake in Lake Country, serving breakfast, lunch, baked goods, and specialty coffees. Started in 2016 as a home-based vegan cake business, it opened its brick-and-mortar shop in 2018 and has built a loyal following for plant-based food that appeals well beyond the vegan crowd. The cafe's relaxed beach vibe and proximity to Pebble Beach make it a natural stop for cyclists on the Okanagan Centre road.
66ff7b704b: Waterfront Wines Restaurant is a multiple-award-winning fine dining destination on Kelowna's Okanagan Lake waterfront, recognized as the 'Best Okanagan Restaurant' by Vancouver Magazine twelve consecutive years running. Chef-Sommelier Mark Filatow builds seasonal menus around a curated network of Okanagan producers — Ocean Wise seafood, heritage proteins, foraged mushrooms, and organic produce — paired with a cellar of over 300 local and international wines. A touring cyclist looking for a celebratory dinner will find inventive, ingredient-driven plates in an approachable waterfront setting.
3b922112a5: A Starbucks Coffee location in Langley, BC, offering the full range of espresso drinks, cold refreshers, and grab-and-go food items. With outdoor seating and free Wi-Fi, it serves as a comfortable mid-ride rest stop in the city. As a corporate chain location, cyclists can expect consistent service and indoor facilities.
a344719eb2: Viva Mexicana is an authentic Mexican restaurant founded by Carmen Ruiz, who set out to bring traditional flavours from scratch-made dishes to the Okanagan, opening in Lake Country during the pandemic and later adding a second Vernon location. The restaurant serves a broad menu of tacos, burritos, enchiladas, tamales, and seasonal specials like Sunday pozole, alongside a Mexican grocery section where cyclists can pick up authentic ingredients to go. It sits on Highway 97, a primary cycling corridor through the central Okanagan.
6d5bac23c2: Founded in 1995 by Belgian-trained pastry chef Olivier Lebeau, this patisserie specializes in authentic Liège and Bruxelles waffles, rice pies, craquelins, and speculoos made fresh daily from natural ingredients. Located on West 2nd Avenue near the Arbutus Greenway, it sits along a popular Vancouver cycling corridor. The shop has been a proud multi-year waffle sponsor of Ride to Conquer Cancer and a supplier for Tour de Cure, giving it a genuine footprint in the local cycling community.
e4b397d33a: Big Way Hot Pot Olympic Village is part of a rapidly expanding BC-based self-serve hot pot chain offering over 100 fresh ingredients and more than 18 broths and dry mixes, including signature Mala and slow-simmered Collagen Bone Broth options. Located in the Olympic Village neighbourhood near Vancouver's seawall cycling routes, it offers a customizable, hearty sit-down meal format where each diner cooks ingredients in their own individual pot. The chain has grown to include locations across Metro Vancouver, Ontario, and the United States.
795e892c17: Score on Davie is a long-running sports bar and pub that has operated in Vancouver's West End since 2007, earning multiple 'Best of Vancouver' awards. Known for its Caesar cocktails and a comfort-food menu of wings, burgers, and deep-fried snacks, it draws a lively crowd from the surrounding neighbourhood. The bar has both indoor and outdoor seating and a no-smoking policy.
81608799f7: Taco Nori is a fast-casual fusion concept inside downtown Vancouver's Bentall Centre, serving nori tacos made with deep-fried seaweed shells filled with fresh sushi-style ingredients like Atlantic salmon, ahi tuna, and avocado. The concept originated at the Richmond Night Market in 2018 under the name Nori Express and expanded to a fleet of three food trucks and a trailer before opening its first permanent storefront. It sits along the busy Burrard Street corridor, making it a quick and inventive lunch stop for cyclists moving through the financial district.
1629c7fbd4: Halibut House is a family-owned and operated Cantonese restaurant in Victoria, BC, well regarded locally for its warm, kid-friendly atmosphere in a small but comfortable dining room. The kitchen cooks with no MSG added and is happy to accommodate allergies, dietary restrictions, and gluten-free or wheat-free needs. Both dine-in (reservation recommended) and takeout/pickup are available, making it a practical stop for a touring cyclist looking for a hot meal.
4af370a2a4: Sailor Hägar's is a neighbourhood brew pub in North Vancouver offering views of Vancouver Harbour and the city skyline, with a rotating selection of craft beers on tap alongside a full pub menu of burgers, wings, fish and chips, and more. The pub is known as one of the only spots on the North Shore staying open until 2am on weekends, and hosts regular karaoke nights, themed parties, live music, and sports viewing. An attached liquor store adds convenience for cyclists stocking up before a ride.
e649a1f362: Indian Essence Bistro is an authentic Indian restaurant in Fort St. John, BC, where a chef with experience in India's 5-star hotels serves an extensive menu of meat and vegetarian dishes in an elegant dining room suited to intimate dinners or group events. The menu spans tandoori grills, biryanis, curries, and a full vegetarian selection. Online ordering and local food delivery are also available.
5d0a6fbc7b: Cantonese BBQ Seafood Restaurant is an authentic Cantonese eatery on Kingsway in east Vancouver, specializing in BBQ meats alongside an extensive menu of noodle dishes, fried rice, and seafood. It is part of a small two-location chain (Vancouver and Richmond) and offers online ordering with in-store pickup. Touring cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor will find a wide-ranging lunch and dinner menu covering everything from quick single-item BBQ-over-rice plates to large combination banquet sets.
7c1a82c252: Monzo Burger is a smashburger restaurant located in Vancouver House on Granville Street, inspired by the 1980s Milanese youth movement known as the 'Paninari.' The menu centres on house-ground Canadian beef smash patties, hand-made chicken cutlets, beef-tallow fries, and soft serve gelato, alongside a custom Italian-style pilsner brewed in collaboration with Ravens Brewing. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a full sit-down meal with online ordering and a vegetarian burger option.
6a304cba92: Japanese Village is a long-established teppanyaki restaurant in downtown Victoria where personal chefs cook steak and seafood on a searing iron grill right at the table — part culinary performance, part dinner. Voted Best Japanese Restaurant in Victoria since 1994 by Black Press Media readers, the restaurant features an extensive sake and cocktail bar alongside its signature teppan dinners. Takeout is available by phone, and a dedicated children's menu makes it a flexible option for touring groups stopping in the city.
67eb282df1: Lennox Pub is a neighbourhood pub at 800 Granville Street in the heart of Vancouver's entertainment district. It offers both indoor and outdoor seating in a smoke-free space and is wheelchair accessible, making it a welcoming mid-ride stop for cyclists moving through downtown. Card payments are accepted.
abbd552b29: Aling Ening is a Filipino restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver. The venue serves as a meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.
9b4a51381f: Rosemary Rocksalt is a Montreal-style bagel shop on Vancouver's cycling-friendly Commercial Drive, hand-rolling and stone-baking honey-boiled bagels fresh each day in an open-flame hearth oven. The menu spans breakfast sandwiches, deli-style bagel sandwiches using wild BC sockeye salmon and Montreal smoked meat, and take-home dozens — making it a practical fuelling or stocking-up stop mid-ride. The shop operates three Metro Vancouver locations, with the Commercial Drive outpost sitting at the heart of one of the city's busiest cycling corridors.
7427d92c45: 5th Street is a neighbourhood pub and full-service restaurant in Victoria's Quadra Village, built around a wood-fired rotisserie and stone-oven pizza program alongside a broad scratch kitchen menu. The pub side hosts regular community events including Monday trivia nights and Thursday music bingo, giving it a genuinely local feel beyond the tourist circuit. Cyclists will find dine-in, takeout, and weekend brunch all available under one roof.
efd457f428: Freshii is a Canadian-founded fast-casual chain specializing in salads, wraps, bowls, and burritos aimed at health-conscious diners. This unit is located at 2325 Ottawa Street in Port Coquitlam. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a quick, customizable meal option in a suburban retail setting.
7983c74aed: Le Coq Frit is a Vancouver fried chicken eatery that opened on West Broadway in 2021, offering hand-battered chicken in Korean-inspired preparations (Nashville Hot, Black Soy, Sweet & Spicy) alongside signature brioche bun burgers and croissant waffles. The restaurant has a sustainability focus, using recyclable non-woven bags in place of plastic. It has a second location in North Vancouver's Lonsdale Quay.
c5b2a8f413: Akihana Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Vancouver's Davie Street offering both dine-in and online takeout service. It provides a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists in an urban neighborhood, with the option to order ahead. The restaurant features indoor seating.
b841d840a8: Kuroki Kaiseki Omakase Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant in Richmond's Chatham Street area specializing in kaiseki-style omakase dining, a multi-course format curated entirely by the chef. Omakase restaurants typically offer an intimate, counter-style experience that can be a memorable stop for a touring cyclist seeking a distinctive meal in Metro Vancouver's food-rich Richmond district.
91c725d12d: In Er G Plant Alchemy is a Victoria-based raw, plant-based wellness shop specializing in cold-pressed juices, smoothies, health shots, cleanses, nut milks, and raw food. All products are 100% vegan, gluten-free, and made without artificial colours, flavours, or preservatives. The business operates as a pick-up and delivery service, making it a convenient stop for cyclists seeking nutrient-dense, whole-food refreshments in the downtown Victoria area.
aca6a0212e: CRAFT Beer Market English Bay is a multi-level restaurant and bar perched directly on the seawall, with a heated rooftop patio overlooking English Bay beach and floor-to-ceiling windows throughout. Part of a Canadian chain rooted in the craft beer movement, it pours a broad selection of craft beers alongside a menu of fresh, locally sourced food. Its beachside location on Beach Avenue puts it squarely on one of Vancouver's busiest recreational cycling corridors.

9a4a212c48: Vadapav Mirchi is a strictly vegetarian Indian restaurant specializing in Maharashtrian street food, with the signature dish being vada pav — a deep-fried spiced potato dumpling served in a bread bun with garlic chutney and fried green chillies. def04e52da: Raven's Nest is an on-mountain restaurant operated by Whistler Blackcomb, located in the Alder Creek area of Whistler Mountain and accessible via gondola. 5ba4dec903: Rhino Coffee House is an award-winning multi-location coffee shop serving specialty espresso drinks, craft cocktails and beers, and a full all-day food menu including breakfast wraps, sandwiches, bowls, and housemade donuts. f6e910fabd: Rocko's has been a Mission landmark since opening as the Hi-Lite Burger Bar in 1956, transitioning to its current identity in the 1980s and becoming the city's first 24-hour restaurant. Touring cyclists on the Lougheed Highway can count on round-the-clock home-style diner food — burgers, milkshakes, and hot dogs — in a classic roadside setting. 5ad04da9ec: House of Dawn Steakhouse + Bar is a fine-dining steakhouse in Richmond offering premium cuts including Prime, Wagyu, and house dry-aged selections alongside a curated wine list and craft cocktail program. Private dining rooms accommodate intimate groups up to 12 and semi-private events up to 60 guests.
2d326361e4: Diner on Six is a no-frills homestyle breakfast-and-lunch diner on Highway 6 in Vernon, part of a small family of three Norman's Diner locations across the Okanagan. For a touring cyclist riding Highway 6 through the Shuswap–Okanagan corridor, it is a well-positioned, filling fuel stop in a standalone building.
359e505bc3: Delicia Cafe & Bakery is a specialty coffee shop and scratch bakery on Columbia Street in downtown New Westminster, founded by owners with 15 years of cafe experience in Australia. Pets are welcome on the patio and the space doubles as an event venue for personal and corporate gatherings.
d552531fe0: Poké Bar is a fast-casual Hawaiian-style poke bowl chain with roots in Japanese sushi dating back to 1989, offering fully customizable bowls built from fresh-daily fish, multiple bases (rice, noodles, or greens), and a wide array of toppings and sauces. Online ordering, in-store pickup, and multiple third-party delivery services are available.
3942bd9c71: Artusi is a contemporary rustic Italian restaurant in New Westminster named after Pellegrino Artusi, the 19th-century author considered the father of modern Italian cuisine. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the restaurant offers a takeout option for cyclists looking to eat on the move.
9695989a81: Leisure Tea & Coffee (儷舍咖啡) is a café in Richmond, BC offering tea and coffee beverages in an indoor-only setting. Its bilingual Chinese-English name reflects Richmond's multicultural character and suggests a menu likely rooted in Asian tea and coffee traditions. The lack of an address in OSM and a Facebook-only web presence make it difficult to assess its broader hospitality offerings for touring cyclists.
a3d5012ab1: Greek Islands III is the South Fraser Way Abbotsford location of a three-restaurant family-owned chain founded by twin brothers George and Gus Sahamis, who emigrated from Sparta, Greece in 1974 and have been serving Greek and international cuisine in the Fraser Valley since 1982. 6c6ab9495e: A bakery on Mainland Street in Vancouver offering freshly baked goods and provisions for customers. The business lists regular operating hours, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists seeking food.
dab78d6809: A Starbucks Coffee location in Vancouver, BC, part of the global coffeehouse chain that originated in Seattle in 1971. Starbucks offers a wide range of espresso drinks, refreshers, teas, and food items including sandwiches. Touring cyclists will find it a familiar rest stop, though specific in-store amenities vary by location.
c8cd0d9e79: Black Kettle Brewing Company is a North Shore craft brewery and taproom that has been pouring house-crafted ales and lagers since opening in January 2014, founded by Bryan Lockhart and Phil Vanderborre in a no-frills industrial unit just past the rail tracks. The about page describes it as 'minutes down the Spirit Trail' and 'a casual & pet-friendly oasis,' making it a natural pit-stop for cyclists finishing a ride on the North Shore trail network. The kitchen turns out burgers, tacos, salads, and wings, and the pet-friendly patio hosts live music on Saturdays.
0859f1688f: Humboldt Bar is an intimate cocktail bar in downtown Victoria inspired by the life and work of Alexander von Humboldt, the 19th-century German naturalist. Located on the Arcade Level of the DoubleTree Victoria hotel, it offers an immersive nature-themed environment with a creative cocktail program drawing on Humboldt's travels and discoveries. Small plates from the kitchen are also available on most evenings.
4bf31b5c3f: Motonobu Udon is Vancouver's first authentic Japanese udon restaurant, opened in August 2020 during the pandemic and earning Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand recognition consecutively in 2023, 2024, and 2025. Chef Shin Iwamoto follows his grandmother's Sanuki-style family recipe, using locally sourced Canadian flour to produce handmade noodles freshly cut and boiled to order. Located on East Hastings Street near PNE Playland, it operates as a walk-in-only spot with takeout and Uber Eats delivery available.
8a3b1fad89: Ramie's Greek Restaurant is a family-owned Greek restaurant on Burnaby's Kingsway corridor, celebrating 25 years in business. It has been voted Best Greek Restaurant in Burnaby, winning the Quality Business Award for both 2023 and 2024 based on satisfaction, quality, service, and reputation. The restaurant is operated by owner Ramie and his two sons, with a stated commitment to authenticity and quality in their cooking.
16c0898351: Little June is a neighbourhood café nestled in the heritage building at the heart of Fernwood Square, one of Victoria's most distinctive communities. The cosy spot draws on its 110-year-old building's history while offering everything from grab-and-go baked goods to lingering egg dishes and locally sourced beer and wine.
a6f53114e9: Iron Road Brewing is an award-winning craft brewery in Kamloops, BC, founded by two geologists who teamed up with an award-winning brewer to produce a rotating lineup of balanced, flavourful beers. The 60-person, family-friendly taproom is steps from Thompson Rivers University and serves food alongside the house-brewed lineup. Cyclists may catch a live band or watch the brewing process up close.
62fa9c7876: Tavola is a neighbourhood Italian restaurant on Robson Street in Vancouver's West End, celebrated for house-made pastas, fresh burrata, and family-style sharing plates sourced from local farmers. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down meal or a quick takeout order available nightly, with weekend brunch service as well.
9f551dc2e0: Tutto Belle Il Gelato is a gelateria on the popular West 4th Avenue cycling corridor in Kitsilano, blending Canadian seasonal ingredients with authentic Italian gelato-making traditions. 7bc128e692: Lao Shan Dong Homemade Noodle House is a long-established Chinese noodle restaurant (est. 1949) located in Richmond's busy Number 3 Road corridor, serving handmade Taiwanese and northern Chinese noodle soups, dry noodles, dumplings, and rice dishes. A touring cyclist can expect a hearty, carb-rich meal well-suited to refueling mid-ride.
df9c8e2e85: Driftwood Great Chinese Buffet is the Nanaimo outpost of a Vancouver Island–owned chain celebrated for its all-you-can-eat lunch and dinner buffets alongside a full à la carte Chinese menu. The chain prides itself on fresh, hand-crafted dishes made with 100% vegetable oil and no added MSG, and each location features a full bar with local beers. Cycling through Nanaimo's south end, riders will find both dine-in and take-out options readily available.
d3e93f5559: COFU is a fully plant-based Japanese restaurant in Vancouver's Chinatown, founded by Akiko Gulkison, a Japanese immigrant and single mother who built Canada's first fully plant-based omakase experience. The intimate 18-course tasting menu is served at an 8-seat counter handcrafted by Japanese carpenters, blending traditional technique with seasonal vegetables sourced locally and from Japan. d489274ce9: Alta Bistro is a modern seasonal alpine cuisine restaurant in Whistler, established in 2010, built around locally sourced ingredients from suppliers such as North Arm Farm and Pemberton Valley producers. The restaurant operates a transparent Employee Health Benefit program, collecting 2% of net sales before tax to support year-round staff wellness.
bd339a4aa6: Cafe Lu Quan is a cafe located on Kingsway in Vancouver. Its Instagram account carries the display name 'The World Famous Cafe Lu,' hinting at a degree of local notoriety. Beyond its presence on a well-travelled arterial corridor, little detail is publicly verifiable without access to its social media content.
46299320f0: Victoria's first and only Italian bakery, established in 1978 and now operated across three generations of the Pozzolo family. The shop produces organic sourdough breads, Northern Italian pastries, cakes, gelato, and frozen meals, and offers both eat-in table service and take-away. 613b222f37: Ole Chicken is a Korean pub situated on the second floor at 1256 Robson Street in downtown Vancouver, specializing in Korean fried chicken served in a variety of sauces alongside traditional anju share plates and soups. It sits on one of Vancouver's busiest pedestrian corridors, making it a convenient urban stop for cyclists coming in off the Robson Street corridor.
62e2899673: Pizza Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 1967 with over 750 locations coast to coast, including this Delta outpost. Cyclists can grab a quick hot meal with a wide range of pizza styles, sides, and specialty items. The location is open late into the night, making it a convenient stop on longer evening rides.
1e7cda507c: JOEY is a well-established Canadian casual-dining chain with locations across North America, known for its globally inspired menu developed by a team of Executive Chefs. The Coquitlam location sits on Lougheed Highway and offers a full-service dining room, lounge, bar, and patio. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find a reliable stop for a sit-down meal with a broad menu.
e294d8fec3: Provence Marinaside is an award-winning French seafood restaurant and bar on Marinaside Crescent in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, situated steps from the False Creek seawall — one of the city's most popular cycling routes. It offers group and private dining bookings and participates in seasonal dining events such as Dine Out Vancouver.
1e6ae0e206: Lucky Hong Kong Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant in Richmond offering dine-in service. Located on Westminster Highway, it provides a full-service sit-down dining option for touring cyclists seeking a more substantial meal. Wi-Fi access is available for customers.
8e1a957aac: Ogopogo Burgers & Shakes is a casual diner on Osoyoos's main commercial strip, named after the legendary Okanagan lake monster. Takeout and delivery are both available via Clover online ordering.
7c0f26c09f: Arriva Ristorante is a 42-year landmark on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, the city's historic 'Little Italy' district, where owner Paolo Frau serves entirely house-made Italian cuisine including scratch-made gnocchi, sausages, pancetta, breads, and desserts. It has become a destination restaurant drawing diners from across the region with an extensive Italian and international wine list. Commercial Drive itself is a major cycling corridor through east Vancouver, putting this long-established sit-down restaurant directly on common touring routes.
c76fde2fd0: Mello is an artisan donut shop in Vancouver's Chinatown specializing in fresh brioche donuts made entirely from scratch each day, with fillings ranging from Madagascar vanilla custard and tiramisu to an Everything Bagel cream cheese option. The shop rotates seasonal and specialty flavours regularly and also serves coffee using a custom blend from Agro Roasters. Donuts can be pre-ordered online or purchased in-store while supplies last — the handmade process means sell-outs are common.
41166ff9a6: The Shameful Tiki Room is a dimly lit, immersive vintage tiki bar on Vancouver's Main Street corridor, serving expertly crafted classic exotic cocktails like the Zombie, Jet Pilot, and Mai Tai alongside share plates. The decor is sourced from around the world — tapa cloth from Tonga and Fiji, custom California-carved tikis, and puffer fish lamps — evoking a genuine mid-century escape. Live surf bands and ukulele players appear regularly, and the venue welcomes all ages.
d7a1420775: CoCo Fresh Tea & Juice is a bubble tea cafe serving specialty tea drinks and refreshments. The location provides indoor seating in Burnaby, convenient for touring cyclists looking for a quick rest stop.
a871245552: Tealips Cafe is a bubble tea and dessert café serving Burnaby's Highgate neighbourhood with a broad menu of milk teas, fruit slushes, coffee drinks, Korean-style bingsoo, Belgian waffles, and fresh focaccia sandwiches. Cyclists will find a wide range of cold and hot drinks, light meals, and vegetarian-friendly options.
ff684ddd55: Hainan Kitchen is a Chinese restaurant in Richmond's Garden City area specializing in authentic Hainanese chicken rice and Southeast Asian comfort food. Both dine-in and takeout options are available, making it a practical meal stop for cyclists passing through the Blundell Road corridor.
3a64a3a9fb: HellCrust Pizza is a pizza chain operating on Vancouver's busy Main Street corridor, offering online and app-based ordering. 08603d777e: Spice of Punjab is an Indian restaurant located in Tsawwassen, BC. It would offer a warm sit-down meal option for touring cyclists passing through the South Delta area. No further detail about the menu, facilities, or current operation could be confirmed.
31acd1b1fb: Blenz Coffee is a BC-based specialty coffee chain with a location inside Library Square, a busy commercial and office complex in the heart of downtown Vancouver. It sits on Robson Street, a key cycling corridor connecting the West End to downtown, making it a convenient stop for urban touring cyclists.
80d6795298: Mittz Kitchen is a downtown Kamloops upscale casual restaurant founded by brothers Jeff and Steve Mitton, who bring a combined 54 years of hospitality experience to the table. 747c664318: The Lion's Den Cafe is a restaurant located on East 15th Avenue in Vancouver. The casual name suggests a welcoming neighborhood atmosphere. It serves as a dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.
4990d67f21: Camp Lifestyle & Coffee Co. is a mountain espresso bar and lifestyle store in Whistler, BC, serving third-wave coffee using 49th Parallel beans in a space that celebrates West Coast outdoor culture. For touring cyclists rolling through Whistler, it offers quality coffee and a relaxed outdoor spot to sit and decompress.
2ebc7c1634: The Wizard Grill is a dining venue within the Whistler Blackcomb resort complex, operated as part of the Vail Resorts mountain dining portfolio. c50466f913: The Commodore Grand Cafe & Lounge is a tapas bar and lounge on Victoria Street in downtown Kamloops, offering drinks, small plates, and occasional events. 9456341dd0: Stonesedge Kitchen is a modern sports bar in Whistler Village operated by the Gibbons Hospitality Group, blending elevated comfort food — centred on high-quality burgers — with craft cocktails, frozen drinks, and boozy milkshakes, plus an unexpected caviar offering. For a touring cyclist rolling into Whistler, it offers a full sit-down meal and cocktail experience steps from the village centre.
293da1aa63: Lucky Bar is a storied live-music and DJ venue in downtown Victoria, programming an eclectic range of genres — punk, metal, hip-hop, house, reggae, folk, jazz, and more — alongside variety shows and film screenings under the motto 'Everything happens at Lucky Bar.' For touring cyclists, it offers an accessible evening entertainment option right in the heart of the city.
0664aa98c7: Pho Stanley is a family-owned Vietnamese restaurant in North Delta serving steaming bowls of pho, vermicelli, and rice plates made with fresh ingredients and time-honoured recipes. The casual dining room is described as comfy and welcoming, suited to a relaxed post-ride meal.
473b52aa8b: Yummy Donair & Kebab is a fast-casual restaurant in North Vancouver specializing in Middle Eastern and Persian-inspired cuisine, including donairs, kebabs, and falafel. Online ordering and catering services are available, making it a practical stop for a quick hot meal.
80fedd9925: Wok Box is a Canadian fast-casual franchise founded in Edmonton in 2004 and now operating over 60 locations coast to coast, drawing its menu from more than 10 Asian culinary traditions — rice boxes, noodle boxes, wings, poutines, and more. The chain emphasizes freshness and offers diet-accommodating options including vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-friendly dishes.
db892d03c5: RE-UP BBQ is a barbecue restaurant situated on Quayside Drive in New Westminster, with a capacity of 50 and both indoor and outdoor seating. ef49078427: Fuji Market is a Japanese grocery store and casual deli eatery at the heart of Whistler Resort, serving locals and visitors for several decades with an authentic taste of Japan. cfa8e05633: Sushi Time Express is a fast-casual sushi counter in Victoria's St. Andrew's Square, serving an extensive menu of rolls, rice bowls, bento boxes, nigiri and sashimi, noodles, and breakfast items alongside healthy smoothies. The Express concept centers on fresh ingredients prepared quickly at counter service, making it a practical downtown stop for cyclists passing through the Yates Street corridor. Bento boxes and a broad roll menu — including several vegetarian and potentially vegan options — give touring cyclists flexible, portable meal choices.
d7914b7475: Modus is a Vancouver-based specialty coffee micro-roaster operating an intimate cafe at 112 West Broadway, known for a hyper-seasonal menu of single-origin light roasts built around close producer relationships. The Broadway shop doubles as a retail space for beans, brewing gear, and apparel, and is available for private events seating up to 30 people. Coffee education is offered through The Coffee Division, the workshop arm of the business, running public tastings and private corporate sessions.
6738112028: IKEA Bistro is a Swedish-style fast food counter on level 1 of the IKEA Richmond store, serving classic IKEA fare in a large retail environment. The Richmond location is undergoing a planned expansion and is conveniently accessible from the Canada Line via several bus routes. For cyclists navigating Richmond's flat terrain, it sits just off Sweden Way near Jacombs Road.
0d1a0765a0: Kwan Kee Noodle House is a Chinese fast-food noodle restaurant in North Vancouver. It offers quick dining service typical of casual Asian cuisine establishments, providing a convenient meal option for cyclists passing through the area.
bacc1ffe48: KJ Enjoy Garden Restaurant is a Chinese cuisine restaurant in Pitt Meadows serving a broad Cantonese and Szechuan menu spanning beef, chicken, pork, seafood, tofu, noodle, and rice dishes. Located on Harris Road, it sits near cycling corridors connecting Pitt Meadows to the Golden Ears and Pitt River recreational areas.
c9b5b5ea6b: Tobiko Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant inside Fleetwood Plaza on Fraser Highway in Surrey, operating as 'Tobiko Sushi 1' — the first of what appears to be a multi-location operation. The menu spans classic rolls, nigiri, sashimi, and an extensive lineup of party trays in sizes from 33 to 104 pieces. Both dine-in and online takeout ordering are available, making it a functional meal stop for cyclists moving along the Fraser Highway corridor.
2d3b8d55e3: Sakuya Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in South Surrey offering a broad menu of rolls, sashimi, nigiri, tempura, donburi, and teriyaki. The kitchen features dozens of specialty and signature rolls alongside bento lunches and party trays. It sits near the Tsawwassen boundary, making it a convenient meal stop for cyclists on the South Surrey–Delta corridor.
15713bf8ac: Clover Sushi is a Japanese-focused restaurant in a commercial unit on Admirals Road in the Esquimalt/View Royal area of Greater Victoria, blending traditional sushi techniques with creative rolls, premium sashimi, and a few Korean-inspired dishes like bibimbap. The restaurant offers both a dine-in experience in what it describes as an elegant yet comfortable setting, and a pickup option through their mobile ordering service.
4886cd8db2: A cafe and gift shop on 5th Avenue in Valemount serving food and beverages to locals and travelers. Located in a small mountain community on the Yellowhead corridor, it provides a convenient stopping point for cycling tours.
e3841cf10d: Copper Beach Bar + Kitchen is a full-service restaurant and bar perched on the Sea to Sky Highway in the historic copper-mining village of Britannia Beach, roughly halfway between Vancouver and Squamish. The venue seats up to 120 guests, serves burgers, American classics, and brunch, and is dog-friendly on the patio.
d16613c5d6: Fernwood Pizza Company is a neighbourhood pizzeria in Victoria's Fernwood district, billing itself as 'The People's Pie' for its community-minded, inclusive ethos. The menu spans creative vegetarian combinations to classic meat pies, with gluten-free crust and vegan cheese substitutions available. Rotating craft beer, wine, and cider complement the pizza selection, making it a solid refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the area.
2147aa2fba: Gringo is a casual Mexi-Cali cantina in North Vancouver's Lonsdale neighbourhood, one of three Vancouver-area locations that trace their roots to a Gastown opening in 2013. It is a full-service, sit-down establishment with a takeout option, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists passing through the area.
0f88005e90: Ignite Pizzeria's South Surrey location sits in the Morgan Crossing open-air mall, offering 60 indoor seats and a 24-seat south-facing patio in a contemporary minimal space. Crescent Beach is roughly 15 minutes away, making this a practical refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the South Surrey waterfront.
2e05fab561: A Thai restaurant in Chilliwack operating since 2021 that also offers catering services. A dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.
2c2fee7bcf: Waves Coffee House is a Canadian coffee chain with a location on Columbia Street in North Vancouver. It provides both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a practical stop for cyclists on tours in the area.
13bfddca6c: Trees Organic Coffee is a Vancouver-area cafe chain established in 1996, known for its in-house roasted organic coffee and award-winning homemade New York-style cheesecakes. With 14 locations across greater Vancouver, Trees also hosts live music events and offers online ordering with in-store pickup and delivery.
04ecbbfa2f: Caffè Cittadella is an espresso bar and bistro housed in a heritage building dating to 1894, complete with a scenic outdoor patio that makes it a welcoming rest stop. A curated thrift boutique operates on the second floor, giving the stop an unusually eclectic character.
8f3d115ccc: Orrange Kitchen + Bar is an independently owned neighbourhood restaurant and bar in Port Coquitlam, founded in 2013 by local resident Brian Orrange as a community gathering place inspired by family recipes and travel. c1c8449fd5: Caveman Cafe bills itself as the 'King of Keto' — a health-focused restaurant and bakery serving globally-inspired whole-food meals that are fully customizable for keto, paleo, vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free diets. The operation also does large-scale off-site catering and has a community record of supplying healthy meals to social-service organizations across Vancouver.
3e354715da: A casual bistro café in Nanaimo offering both dine-in and takeout service. Located on McCullough Road, it provides a convenient food stop for touring cyclists needing a meal break.
9de0afb2a5: The Buvette is a cozy lunch spot in Squamish serving gourmet homemade sandwiches alongside coffee, natural wine, and beer. Outdoor seating and a take-away option make it easy for cyclists to refuel without lingering.
d50d2a9601: Bayview Brewing Company is a microbrewery and pub in Ladysmith that brews its own beer on-site. It offers outdoor seating and accepts multiple payment methods. Touring cyclists will find a casual spot to enjoy locally-crafted beverages.
778c6e0590: Steve's Poke Bar is an authentic Hawaiian poke chain founded by Steve Huynh, whose recipes draw on family traditions from Oahu and years spent between Vancouver and Honolulu.
