Cyclists can order customizable poke bowls for pickup with vegetarian options including a tofu bowl.
b0837fc2d9: Dusty's Bar & BBQ is one of the oldest bars in the Whistler valley, established in 1965 and anchored in Whistler Creekside with a lively mythology involving a stuffed horse that allegedly galloped into the night. The venue serves slow-smoked BBQ alongside a creative cocktail menu, with live music three times a week and a daily après scene that draws locals and visitors alike. A 'Bike 'n' Grab' section on the menu signals a deliberate nod to the cycling crowd passing through Creekside.
a2b0c9143f: Lakeside Beach Club is a full-service restaurant and patio in Cultus Lake, roughly 10 km south of Chilliwack and a five-minute walk from the main beach. Owned by chef Chris Ovens and his wife Christy since 2015, the kitchen draws on locally sourced ingredients from Columbia Valley farms and pairs them with creative cocktails and an innovative menu. Cyclists can settle hearthside in winter or cool off on the patio in summer, making it a year-round destination on the Cultus Lake circuit.
e4c5c15a72: Cockney Kings is a family-owned fish and chips institution that has been serving classic English-style fish and chips in Metro Vancouver since 1965, growing from a single East Hastings shop to four locations across the Lower Mainland. The New Westminster location is a full-service dine-in restaurant offering traditional battered fish — cod, haddock, snapper, salmon, and halibut — fried in beef tallow alongside hand-cut chips, seafood starters, and comfort sides. It remains a multi-generational family operation with a loyal local following built over six decades.
a20441403a: Fable Diner is an East Vancouver original established in 2016 inside the historic Lee Building at the busy Main & Broadway intersection in Mount Pleasant. Featured on Food Network's Diners Drive-Ins and Dives (Season 29, Episode 17), the diner is celebrated for creative comfort food built on locally sourced ingredients, with signature dishes like the Duck Pancake with kimchi. It is a well-rooted neighbourhood institution offering full table service, weekend brunch, and online ordering.
732416e3cb: The Greek Kouzina Express is a family-run Greek restaurant and food truck in Kamloops's Westsyde neighbourhood, operated by third-generation restauranteur Andreas Mougholias whose family has run Greek and Italian eateries in the area since 1975. The menu centres on souvlaki wraps, traditional Greek plates, and shareable sides made from house recipes and fresh ingredients. In addition to the brick-and-mortar dine-in location, they operate a mobile food truck that appears at various community events around the region.
5aa685e964: Big Feast Bistro is a locally-celebrated small-town bistro with an urban atmosphere that opened in Maple Ridge in 2010 and was featured on the Food Network's 'You Gotta Eat Here.' The kitchen sources from over 50 local suppliers and hand-crafts its menu daily with a strong emphasis on gluten-free, vegetarian, vegan, and Ocean Wise seafood options. The bistro also operates a retail line of artisan small-batch products available in-house, making it a useful resupply stop for cyclists wanting to take local goods on the road.
320b4ac025: Manvirros Indian Grill is a family-owned restaurant in Nanaimo serving authentic East Indian cuisine using recipes passed down through generations, with a menu spanning tandoori, biryani, curries, and regional specialties. The dining room is described by customers as cozy and warmly decorated, and the kitchen is helmed by a chef trained in Chandigarh with experience cooking North Indian and Mughalai cuisine. Catering for events and parties is also available.
6805fb2843: Rosemary Rocksalt is a Vancouver-area bagel chain specializing in authentic Montreal-style bagels that are hand-rolled, honey-boiled, and baked fresh daily in a traditional open-flame stone-hearth oven. The Richmond location on Steveston Highway offers bagel sandwiches, house-made cream cheeses, soups, and take-home grocery items sourced from local suppliers. It sits along the Steveston cycling corridor and markets itself as a community gathering place, making it a welcoming and substantive food stop on a coastal or delta touring route.
e5c8a60b51: Pine House Bread & Cake Shop is a local bakery situated on Kingsway in Vancouver's east side. It specializes in bread and cakes, making it a convenient stop for cyclists looking to pick up freshly baked goods along a busy arterial route. The OSM record notes wheelchair accessibility at the premises.
dc4e8ebe06: Wings West Kelowna is part of the WINGS restaurant chain, a BC franchise known for award-winning chicken wings in 28 globally-inspired flavours. This 'food primary, all ages welcome' location offers a full sit-down menu including wings, burgers, salads, and pastas alongside weekly dine-in specials. Cyclists in the West Kelowna area will find a casual, family-friendly stop with online ordering available.
fa8cc06e79: The Black Clover is a downtown Prince George Irish pub offering authentic Irish-inspired cuisine alongside an extensive selection of spirits, a 10-tap 'Brass Cascade' draught system featuring Irish and domestic craft brews, and a revolving wine list. It bills itself as Prince George's newest downtown gathering spot with a traditional Public House atmosphere — quiet corners, live entertainment, and an unpretentious service ethos.
900b39da5e: Cavo Bar+Kitchen is a modern Mediterranean restaurant and bar on Granville Street in Vancouver's entertainment district, serving mezze plates, handmade pastas, flame-grilled skewers, and craft cocktails with a coastal-inspired flair. The venue features both indoor seating and a back patio with a laid-back island atmosphere, and sits just steps from a SkyTrain station. Private event bookings are also available for groups and corporate gatherings.
f356f15fbf: The Borscht Bowl is a regional restaurant in Grand Forks specializing in Eastern European cuisine and traditional borscht soup. Located on downtown Market Avenue, it offers a distinctive dining experience for touring cyclists and travelers passing through the area. The restaurant contributes a unique cultural flavor to Grand Forks' food scene.
262b53aeb2: Jolly Mac's is a family-owned neighborhood pub and liquor store in Surrey serving American-style comfort food including burgers, wings, ribs, and fish and chips. The venue features a 200-person seating capacity, a 1,000 sq ft outdoor patio, and a large HD screen for sports viewing. It also hosts events such as birthday parties, fundraisers, and has run an annual car and bike show.
f4764a9076: Pho 68 is an authentic Vietnamese restaurant in Surrey, BC, with over two decades of community presence. It specializes in traditional noodle soups — including the signature Pho Dac Biet and spicy Bun Bo Hue — alongside desserts like the Everything Coconut. Cyclists can dine in or order online for pickup.
c06c29c40d: Ryuu Japanese Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant serving authentic home-style Japanese cuisine with a UBC campus location on University Boulevard. It is one of three Ryuu locations in Vancouver and offers online ordering with a loyalty rewards program. Cyclists navigating the UBC area will find it a convenient dine-in or takeout option.
6901962e9f: Hynes' is an Irish-owned and Irish-run pub in the Kitsilano neighbourhood, dedicated to the Hynes family of Galway and built around good Guinness, draught beers, and comfort-food cooking. It hosts traditional Irish music sessions and live musicians multiple nights a week, and offers a hireable private lounge for groups of up to 60. Weekend brunch is served Saturday and Sunday, making it a viable stop at multiple points in a cycling day.
aed777af48: Kent's Kitchen is a long-established Cantonese takeout restaurant on Victoria Drive that relocated from Vancouver's Chinatown and has retained a devoted local following. The menu spans classic dishes — fried rice, chow mein, spareribs, and fresh seafood — with online ordering available for fast pickup. Cyclists will find it a convenient, affordable stop for a filling hot meal on a busy arterial corridor in south Vancouver.
1dbd914c8d: Loriz - Our Daily Bread is a Filipino specialty bakery offering traditional breads including pandesal, ensaymada, Spanish bread, monay, and pan de coco. The bakery emphasizes authentic island baking traditions rooted in Philippine culinary heritage, with a product line spanning sweet buns, savoury buns, empanadas, and hopia pastries. Cyclists stopping in would find a distinctive selection of Filipino baked goods not commonly found at mainstream grocery stops.
7445e1efaa: House of James is a well-established Christian bookstore and coffeeshop in Abbotsford, BC, carrying an extensive selection of books, music, church supplies, and gifts across a two-storey retail building. The store features rotating art installations by local artists, including fluid art canvases displayed on the grand staircase. The in-house coffeeshop makes it a practical rest point for cyclists moving through the Abbotsford commercial corridor.
568ec63970: An Indian restaurant and sweets shop in Surrey's Newton neighbourhood, now operating under the name New Parmar Sweets & Catering, with a second South Surrey location recently added. The kitchen prepares a broad range of authentic subcontinental dishes daily — from street-food chaats and tandoori items to curries and Indo-Chinese fusion — alongside house-made fresh sweets. The dining hall seats up to 50 guests and the business offers online ordering and full event catering.
dc466b44b1: A ramen restaurant located in Port Coquitlam. No details about amenities, services, or current operational status are available due to website unavailability.
b1908cf9c6: Cozen Japanese Cuisine is a full-service Japanese restaurant on Vancouver's busy Commercial Drive, formerly known as Tatsu Japanese Bistro. The menu centres on sushi, sashimi, and Japanese mains prepared from fresh, globally sourced ingredients, including creative specialty rolls the restaurant considers exclusive to its kitchen. The business also provides online ordering, catering packages, and private event hosting.
e824b28b7d: A Japanese sushi restaurant situated in a strip mall on King George Boulevard in Surrey, BC. The restaurant offers dine-in service and online ordering, making it a convenient stop for a hot meal on a long King George corridor ride. The OSM record lists it as wheelchair accessible.
51a1acf0d9: A pub located in Lake Country (Winfield). Serves as a gathering place for locals and visitors seeking food and beverage.
4c53507d03: Zalas Restaurant is a Revelstoke institution since 1976, serving charbroiled steaks, classic Italian pastas and pizzas, and seafood in a warm dining room with a fireplace and full bar. The restaurant explicitly welcomes guests arriving after outdoor adventures in the Monashees and Selkirk Mountains, making it a natural stop for touring cyclists finishing a big day. Private event hosting and a curated wine list round out the experience.
5c58dbf391: Umé is a family-owned Japanese restaurant tucked into Burtch Plaza on Highway 97 (Harvey Avenue) in Kelowna, serving sushi, sashimi, bento boxes, donburi, and more—all prepared MSG-free with fresh ingredients. It has earned a strong local reputation, landing in TripAdvisor's Top 10 best sushi in Kelowna and holding a 4.7-star Google rating from 360+ reviews. Cyclists riding the Highway 97 corridor have the option to dine in or grab takeout via Skip the Dishes or DoorDash.
48c7afd63f: Mott 32 is a globally acclaimed Chinese restaurant brand with locations across Asia, the Middle East, and North America, known for its 42-day applewood-roasted Peking Duck, handcrafted dim sum, and award-winning interior design blending New York industrial style with traditional Chinese culture. The Vancouver location sits at the base of the Arthur Erickson-designed tower in Coal Harbour, featuring an expansive main dining room, four private dining rooms, and an outdoor terrace with views over downtown Vancouver. It is one of the more celebrated upscale Chinese dining destinations in the city.
ca529bee01: Cantina di Luigi is a dimly lit Italian wine bar nestled in the back of Mercato di Luigi in Vancouver's Chinatown, offering a curated all-Italian wine list by the glass, half litre, or bottle alongside pasta, cheeses, and cured meats. It is part of the Kitchen Table Restaurants group and shares its style of service with the well-regarded Ask for Luigi next door. The space is designed for slow, convivial dining with an emphasis on small-producer and indigenous Italian grape varieties.
9334e7f842: Kekuli Cafe is an Indigenous-owned fast-casual cafe founded by Sharon Bond-Hogg of the Nooaitch First Nation, celebrating Indigenous culinary traditions through bannock-based sandwiches, tipi tacos, Mother Earth Bowls, and organic fair-trade espresso drinks. The menu draws on locally sourced ingredients and highlights traditional ingredients like venison, wild salmon, and saskatoon berries. It is part of a small BC franchise with locations in West Kelowna, Kelowna, Merritt, and Kamloops.
81bd8b6502: Fomi's Bakery is a bakery on Highway 6 in Winlaw, BC. Bakeries provide fresh baked goods and are a convenient food stop for touring cyclists. Website content is unavailable, so specific services and amenities cannot be confirmed.
b33a6fa96d: This Subway franchise, branded 'Subway Metropolis At Metrotown', is located inside the large Metropolis at Metrotown shopping mall on the busy Kingsway corridor in Burnaby. It offers the full Subway lineup of customizable sandwiches, wraps, and salads with multiple ordering options including pickup, delivery, and in-restaurant dining. As a mall-level food court unit, it gives cyclists access to a quick, customizable meal near a major transit hub.
88dcc5e0bb: The Templeton is a nostalgic American-style diner in the heart of Vancouver's Granville entertainment district, dishing up all-day breakfast made with free-run eggs and naturally smoked bacon alongside gourmet burgers and authentic milkshakes. The retro atmosphere features a jukebox and a no-reservations, first-come first-served policy that keeps things lively. Fully licensed and indoors-only, it is a locally loved comfort-food destination in a central, high-traffic part of downtown Vancouver.
13000269a4: A McDonald's fast-food restaurant in the Lynn Valley area of North Vancouver, offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, McCafé beverages, and desserts. The location has a drive-through and takeaway service, making it a quick stop for cyclists passing through this suburban corridor. As part of a large national chain, the range of hot and cold food and drink options is broadly consistent across locations.
5a502b7ed2: EATology is a bright, quick-service diner in downtown Vernon, established in 2015, serving breakfast and lunch with 90% of dishes made in-house using fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The menu changes regularly and always includes vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options, with coffee from Vernon-roasted Multiply Coffee. Touring cyclists will find it a convenient downtown stop for a real meal, with takeout available for those hitting the road.
c0d1a48065: This McDonald's, branded internally as the 'TV Towers' branch, sits on Robson Street in central Vancouver near the entertainment and shopping district. It is a dine-in location with both indoor and outdoor seating and no drive-through. As a 24/7 urban fast-food stop it offers a reliable resupply point for cyclists passing through the city core.
5a9b23b136: A sit-down Nepalese and Indian restaurant on East Broadway in Vancouver offering traditional South Asian cuisine with vegan and vegetarian options. The restaurant supports online ordering and serves as a dining option for touring cyclists in the area.
f0f3479725: Yellow Deli is a chain of rustic, handcrafted delis founded in Chattanooga, Tennessee in 1973 and operated by an intentional religious community. Locations are known for their distinctive décor of barn beams, macramé, leatherwork, and custom booth seating, often spread across multiple floors of converted spaces. The menu centres on sandwiches on fresh-baked bread, made-from-scratch soups, garden salads, and homemade desserts.
ac3c31d941: The Italians is a small, intimate Italian restaurant in Vancouver's West End where all pasta is made in-house daily and the menu stays unapologetically rooted in regional Italian tradition—dishes like Spaghetti alla Carbonara and Bucatini all'Amatriciana are prepared the authentic Roman and central-Italian way. The room has a cozy date-night atmosphere with table service, but the kitchen also handles takeout orders and full-scale catering for private events. Reviewers consistently single out the freshness of ingredients and the attentiveness of staff.
4fcb7c09ea: Grouse Grind Coffee Bar is a café within the Grouse Mountain resort in North Vancouver, named after the famous Grouse Grind hiking trail that draws thousands of visitors to the area. The resort also hosts the Grouse Bike Park — a lift-accessed mountain bike park — making this a natural stop for cyclists in the area. It sits within a busy outdoor recreation hub that includes gondola access, wildlife habitats, and multiple dining venues.
37a0ad5d36: Legends Pub & Restaurant is a well-established Richmond sports bar with roots going back to 1994, now settled in a two-storey building near Vancouver International Airport. The venue boasts over 30 TVs including three large screens, making it Richmond's self-described prime sports destination. It offers a full kitchen with daily house-made soups, a wide selection of vegetarian dishes, and off-sales beer to go.
ddc5a39f18: A neighbourhood sports pub and casual eatery in Mission that has been serving the community since 1977. The pub features a broad selection of Pacific Northwest craft beers, daily food and drink specials, multiple big-screen TVs for sports, and an attached liquor store open 365 days a year. Live bands perform every second Saturday and karaoke runs every Friday, making it a lively stop for an evening meal.
21b9f13a66: Beacon Pub & Eatery is a craft beer and comfort food pub located in the heart of Whistler Village Square, with what the venue describes as the best patio and après vibe in town. The menu leans into hearty fare — Canadian beef and bison burgers, poutine, wings, and loaded tacos — designed to refuel after a full day on the trails or slopes. The venue operates on a first-come, first-served basis with a 90-minute dining limit, so arriving early is advisable during peak periods.
d4a67d7c3c: Mexican restaurant on Keefer Street in Vancouver's Chinatown neighborhood. Offers casual dining in the heart of the historic district. Active on social media but maintains a minimal online presence.
37f4cccc88: A fast-food location on Harvey Avenue, one of Kelowna's main commercial strips, positioned conveniently for cyclists passing through the city core. The OSM record identifies it as KFC, but the linked website is a Taco Bell location page with the same address and phone — it is likely a co-branded KFC/Taco Bell restaurant. Either brand offers quick, affordable hot food and takeout options well-suited to a mid-ride stop.
1a020e4a84: Rice Bowl Rose Garden is a fast food establishment located on Columbia Street West in Kamloops, BC. Beyond its OSM address record, no further details about the restaurant's cuisine, format, or cyclist amenities could be verified due to its website domain resolving to an unrelated third-party delivery platform.
5c90079125: COBS Bread is a Canadian franchise arm of the Australian Bakers Delight chain, with 190 locations across Canada. Everything is baked from scratch on-site daily, and any unsold goods are donated to local charities at closing time. A touring cyclist stopping here can pick up fresh bread, rolls, bagels, scones, and savory baked items including mini pizzas and croissant-based pastries.
b5c929e490: Plaisir Sucré is a traditional French bakery and cafe in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, established in December 2009 by Fabrice, a Paris-born baker who brings daily fresh-baked croissants, artisan breads, and classic pastries to the counter. The family-run shop has been voted Best in Vancouver for its almond tartes and is known for its authentic atmosphere and kid-friendly environment with a dedicated play corner. Touring cyclists will find a full lunch menu of soups, quiches, and sandwiches alongside a complete espresso bar.
e92c1a2fc1: Rusted Rake Brewing is a farm-to-tap craft brewery and gourmet eatery on a working farm in Nanoose Bay, where the barley for its beers is grown on-site alongside honey, berries, garlic, and herbs used in the kitchen. The brewery has been voted Best Brewery Food Program in BC two years running by Growler Readers' Choice Awards, and its seasonal tap list reflects whatever is growing on the farm at any given time. Set between the sea and fields of barley, the grass patio and farmhouse setting make it a standout experiential stop on Vancouver Island's craft beer trail.
50d559f1c2: Naked Sprout is a cafe in Whistler, BC offering online food ordering. Cyclists can conveniently order and pick up meals while visiting the area.
1992414239: La Casa Gelato is a Vancouver institution housed in an iconic pink building on Venables Street, holding the Guinness World Record for 'Most Commercially Available Flavours' with 238 gelato flavours available at any one time. Family-owned and operated for three generations, the shop also offers gelato cakes, Italian pastries, and handmade chocolates. A well-known destination in East Vancouver and a natural stop for cyclists exploring the area — though note they accept only Canadian cash, Canadian debit, or U.S. cash; no credit cards.
33c23288e5: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen is a national fast-food chain specializing in Louisiana-style fried chicken, operating out of a ground-floor unit at 700 Hamilton Street in downtown Vancouver. This location has no drive-through and offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a sit-down quick-service option in a dense urban area. For touring cyclists passing through the downtown core, it provides a convenient calorie stop with takeout available.
997fc9c6d1: 24 Train Express Noodle House is a Vietnamese noodle restaurant located on Nelson Street in downtown Vancouver, offering both indoor dining and a street-facing patio. Its express-style concept and train-themed branding set it apart from the neighbourhood's broader dining scene. Cyclists passing through the downtown core will find it a convenient stop for a hot bowl mid-ride.
48d0b95974: Fountain Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant situated in Blanshard Square in central Victoria, BC. The establishment offers dine-in, takeout, and online ordering, with delivery also available for those staying nearby. Its location in a commercial plaza in a busy part of the city makes it a convenient stop for cyclists moving through the area.
ba05868a00: Silvano's Restaurant is a dining establishment located in the Fraser Valley region of British Columbia. Beyond its classification as a restaurant, no further details about cuisine style, setting, or cyclist-specific offerings could be verified from available sources.
c5b3ee5299: Jack's Spot is a small, independently operated cafe on Kingsway in East Vancouver, offering coffee, matcha, sandwiches, bread, and pastries. Its Instagram-only web presence gives it a distinctly local, community-facing character on this busy commercial corridor. Cyclists passing through the Kingsway strip will find it a compact neighbourhood spot for a quick coffee and bite.
61f66177e1: Milano Coffee is a Vancouver-rooted specialty coffee roaster with over 30 years of history and an Italian-heritage blending tradition, earning 15 gold medals from the International Institute of Coffee Tasters. The West 8th Avenue location is both the head office and working roastery, where Master Roaster Brian Turko crafts blends of up to 20 Arabica bean varietals on-site. It is also one of the only places in Vancouver offering an espresso tasting bar where visitors can sample up to eight different espressos.
d1d0b614e1: Rice 'N Spice is a family-run food court restaurant that has been a downtown Vancouver institution since 1992, blending Sri-Lankan curries with Mediterranean and Southeast Asian flavours. Located on the lower level of Harbour Centre near the edge of historic Gastown, it is known for freshly ground spices, overnight-marinated shawarma, and a commitment to no MSG and no preservatives. Touring cyclists stopping in the core will find a wide range of hearty rice-bowl dishes, including a fully vegan and gluten-free vegetarian line-up.
c816612391: LR Pizza & Curry is a Burnaby fast-food restaurant that fuses classic Canadian-style pizza with a full South Asian kitchen covering tandoori, curry, and Indo-Chinese dishes — an unusually broad menu under one roof. Unique offerings like Desi Style pizzas (Tandoori Chicken, Palak Paneer, Shahi Paneer) sit alongside extensive beef, lamb, and seafood curries, giving cyclists a substantial and varied refuelling option. Indoor seating is confirmed via OSM.
394c79b26c: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain franchise with a location in Coquitlam's Clarke Road corridor, known for using 100% Canadian wheat dough made fresh in-house and organic tomato sauce. The menu leans into plant-based and meat-free options alongside conventional pizzas, salads, and sides. A touring cyclist passing through Coquitlam could stop here for a quick hot meal or a takeout order.
8acf4b241a: Vegan Fried Chick'un is a fully plant-based fast-food restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver specializing in vegan fried chicken alternatives, Asian-inspired comfort food, burgers, wraps, poutines, and desserts. Every item on the menu is vegan, making it a reliable stop for plant-based cyclists who might otherwise struggle to find cruelty-free options in the fast-food landscape. The restaurant offers takeout, online ordering, and dine-in seating in a casual setting, and can also host group events.
263bcd05de: Mr. Pretzels is a global soft-pretzel franchise founded in Puerto Rico in 1994, operating kiosk-style in shopping centres worldwide. The Victoria location on Douglas Street offers freshly hand-rolled pretzels baked on the spot in sweet and savoury flavours including cinnamon sugar, chocolate, salted, sesame seed, and pretzel dogs. It is a quick, portable snack stop well placed in downtown Victoria for cyclists passing through.
7cc660a48d: Waffle House Diner is a retro-style breakfast and brunch spot in Surrey, BC, that recently relocated from New Westminster and brought with it an updated menu and a modern twist on the classic diner atmosphere. The kitchen leans into elevated comfort food — think Chicken and Waffles with chili-infused maple syrup, Turkish Eggs on garlic yogurt, and a rotating lineup of creative waffle and French toast builds. Pickup and delivery are both available, making it a practical stop for cyclists wanting a substantial meal without a long sit-down commitment.
27c1461caf: Faculty Brewing Co. is a 7-barrel craft microbrewery and 30-seat tasting room in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, occupying the former space of the Pedal Bike Depot bicycle shop on the Ontario Street cycling corridor. The brewery operates as an 'open-source' brewery, publishing all recipes publicly and numbering beers by flavour complexity using a university course system. Cyclists can enjoy rotating taps of house-brewed beer and Oddity Kombucha alongside snacks, or fill a growler to take on the road.
fcbce3c851: MeiWei Chinese Cuisine is a fully licensed Chinese restaurant on Highway 97 in Kelowna serving a broad menu of traditional Cantonese and Szechuan dishes, group share dinners, and combination plates. The kitchen prides itself on fresh, quality ingredients — their ginger beef uses real red pepper flakes, honey, and freshly ground ginger with no MSG. Online ordering, takeout, delivery, and catering options make it a flexible meal stop for solo cyclists and touring groups alike.
89f8027dbd: Back and Forth Bar is a games-and-drinks venue in Vancouver offering six rentable ping-pong tables, two basketball pop-a-shot machines, air hockey, and buck hunter alongside a rotating selection of BC craft beers and cocktails. The space bills itself as a one-of-a-kind atmosphere in Vancouver and welcomes outside food, making it a flexible social stop. Entry is restricted to ages 19 and up with valid ID.
eb06389ff9: Pho Pasteur Restaurant is a Vietnamese noodle house on Hastings Street in Burnaby serving a broad menu of pho, wonton noodle soups, and vermicelli dishes made with traditional flavors and fresh ingredients. The restaurant describes itself as a cozy, modern space offering dine-in alongside online ordering for pickup. Touring cyclists heading along the Hastings corridor will find it a solid stop for a filling hot meal.
5b7686724a: Ukee Scoops is an ice cream shop in Ucluelet, BC — 'Ukee' being the affectionate local shorthand for the town. The shop offers outdoor seating, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists passing through this gateway community to Pacific Rim National Park Reserve. It sits at the tip of the Ucluelet Peninsula, where touring routes converge after the scenic Highway 4 approach.
22e1edd467: Established in 2013, Formosa Tea Café is a locally owned Taiwanese bubble tea shop in Kelowna serving authentic milk teas, iced teas, cream drinks, fresh fruit smoothies, and specialty coffee — most teas sourced from USDA-certified organic beans and leaves tracing back to Tai-Chung, Taiwan. The café partners with local Kelowna businesses to feature regional products and artworks. Cyclists on Harvey Avenue will find a wide drinks menu including hot, iced, and blended options, plus delivery service for the surrounding area.
f416fe285d: Gojo Little Africa Cafe specializes in Ethiopian and international cuisine on Vancouver's Commercial Drive. It's a sit-down restaurant with no outdoor seating, so cyclists must secure bikes inside before dining. The restaurant serves traditional Ethiopian fare in a casual neighborhood setting.
b55814af43: Sky Space Indian Cuisine is a full-service Indian restaurant in Abbotsford offering a broad menu of traditional and Indo-Chinese dishes made with fresh, seasonally sourced ingredients. The kitchen emphasizes authenticity alongside international standards, with a lunch buffet, daily house-made bread, and a specialized catering program for events. A tiffin service is also available, allowing customers to order prepared meals packed to go.
b9778b09f5: Mike's Place Pub is a classic multi-level pub inside the historic Hume Hotel in downtown Nelson, drawing a colourful mix of locals, artists, and ski-bums. The pub is well known for its broad lineup of local and BC craft beers and a menu anchored by the 100 Mile Burger, made with hormone-free grass-fed beef from a neighbouring Creston farm. Pool tables, darts, and foosball make it a natural stop for a post-ride pint in one of BC's most celebrated cycling towns.
62e9a3d3c1: The Bombay Restaurant is an established Indian fine-dining restaurant on Lougheed Highway in Port Coquitlam, offering a broad menu spanning tandoori, curries, biryani, and both meat and vegetarian dishes. The kitchen draws on chefs with experience across India, Malaysia, the UK, and North America. A daily lunch buffet and online ordering for takeout make it a practical stop for riders looking for a substantial Indian meal.
c0bdb1fc31: Olove Greek Kitchen is a family-run Greek restaurant on East Hastings Street in Burnaby, serving traditional dishes like moussaka, grilled octopus, housemade spanakopita, and souvlaki wraps stuffed with house-cut chips in the Greek street-food style. The kitchen carries a warm, playful brand voice rooted in home-cooking, and the menu caters to a range of dietary needs including a dedicated vegan option. Takeout is available alongside full dine-in service.
f43209d693: MOD Pizza is a fast-casual pizza chain where customers build their own individual pizza or salad from over 40 fresh ingredients and eight finishing sauces, cooked in a high-temperature gas-fired oven in minutes. This Country Club Centre location is MOD's second-ever Canadian outpost, opened in 2022 inside a large shopping centre conveniently near a Save-On-Foods grocery store. Touring cyclists will find a quick, filling, fully customizable meal available for carryout.
6daad93135: Triple O's is a BC-based premium quick-service burger chain known for its secret 'Triple O' sauce, hand-scooped milkshakes, and fresh Canadian beef patties. This outlet is tucked inside SFU's AQ Building at the Mackenzie Café on Burnaby Mountain, making it a potential refuelling stop for cyclists who make the climb to the university. It is a counter-service, takeout-only operation with no dine-in seating.
494ea8afcb: A neighbourhood pub and full-service restaurant in Port Coquitlam, The Arms Pub offers a broad daily menu of steak dinners, seafood, flatbreads, and weekend breakfast, alongside an attached liquor store stocked with cold beer, wine, and spirits. Regular entertainment nights — Tuesday trivia, Wednesday music bingo, and Saturday live bands — make it a lively community hub. Touring cyclists passing through on Coast Meridian Road would find a hearty sit-down meal and a convenient stop for cold drinks.
0ef107c4fd: Pepino's Spaghetti House is a neighbourhood Italian restaurant on Commercial Drive in East Vancouver, formerly operating as Nick's Spaghetti House and now reborn as a lively spot for pasta, pizza, and Italian mains. Situated on one of Vancouver's most walkable and cyclist-friendly thoroughfares, it offers both dine-in service and a full takeout menu. A sister wine bar, La Tana, operates next door at 635 Commercial Drive.
9422a1ea9a: COBS Bread is a Canadian franchise bakery that bakes all products fresh on-site every day with no frozen or refrigerated products used. The Fort St. John location offers a broad range of breads, loaves, buns, rolls, bagels, scones, croissants, and savoury items including pizzas and buffins. As part of a community-focused brand, any leftover baked goods are donated to local charities at the end of each day.
d71b40deea: Ladner Pho Saigon is a Vietnamese restaurant in the Ladner neighbourhood of Delta, BC, specializing in house-simmered bone broth pho and a broad menu of noodle soups, rice dishes, vermicelli bowls, and fresh salad rolls. 310b4c9c09: Sushiwa is a Japanese sushi restaurant located in the Promontory neighbourhood of Chilliwack, offering both à la carte and all-you-can-eat menus. Its suburban Promontory Road location sits away from the main cycling corridors through central Chilliwack.
10f9c9a725: Yummy Slice Pizza is a Canadian-owned fast-food pizza chain specializing in pizza by the slice, with a broad menu of classic and signature pies spanning meat, vegetarian, and South Asian-inspired options. Cyclists can order online for pickup or delivery, making it a convenient and quick refuelling stop.
cf30b54e8c: Oliver Twist Pub & Grill is a neighbourhood pub and grill operated by Daebak Tavern Ltd on Edmonds Street. It maintains a no-smoking environment throughout. A touring cyclist passing through the area would find a sit-down pub setting with food service.
a9100d3263: Dalina is a Vancouver café and catering business founded in 2016, with this location in the Chinatown/Mount Pleasant neighbourhood serving daily from-scratch brunch and specialty coffee roasted by nearby Pallet Coffee Roasters. A rewards and loyalty program is available across all ordering channels.
55b58106ad: Gyu-Kaku is a Japanese BBQ chain where diners grill their own meats and vegetables at table-mounted charcoal grills. 074482e381: A restaurant located on Victoria Drive in Vancouver. Website access failed, preventing verification of menu type or cyclist-specific amenities.
d0a6feeb6b: Round Table Pizza Garden City is a family-owned Richmond franchise operating exclusively as a delivery and takeout business for over 20 years, with no dine-in seating. 504beefbb4: Eggspectation is a breakfast-and-brunch café chain with a Richmond, BC location offering an all-day menu spanning Eggs Benedict variations, Belgian waffles, French crepes, pancakes, pasta, and burgers. Touring cyclists will find it a solid refueling stop with a broad menu and full table service.
218f2410c7: The Old Spaghetti Factory is a long-running Canadian Italian restaurant chain with a full sit-down location in Abbotsford, positioned beside the Coast Hotel just off Highway 1 on Sumas Way — a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley. Large-group inquiries are available for parties of seven or more, making it a practical option for group rides.
ea0148b63a: Mary Brown's is a 100% Canadian-owned fast food chain founded in St. John's, Newfoundland in 1969, now operating nearly 300 locations coast-to-coast. The chain specialises in hand-cut, hand-breaded fried chicken using fresh Canada Grade A chicken, hand-cut 'Taters' from whole Canadian-grown potatoes, and handmade coleslaw prepared daily in each store. The Abbotsford location on McCallum Road is a takeout-oriented stop in a strip-mall unit.
2a483155e6: A fast food restaurant specializing in kebab and shawarma in Richmond. Quick takeaway meals for touring cyclists passing through.
6650481bde: Four Winds Beach House & Brewery is the Tsawwassen outpost of Four Winds Brewing Co., a well-regarded BC craft brewery celebrated for bold West Coast and European-style beers. The beach house setting features outdoor seating and a full food menu alongside the on-site brewing operation. It is a natural stop for cyclists exploring the Tsawwassen area, offering craft beer, a kitchen, and a relaxed waterfront atmosphere.
e3b872be13: A restaurant offering regional cuisine in Sidney. Limited details available due to website access issues, but appears to be a local establishment in this Vancouver Island community.
edf08e95d0: Caffè Artigiano is a pioneering Vancouver-born specialty coffee chain with over 25 years of history, known for award-winning latte art, 100% ethically sourced Arabica beans roasted locally in Burnaby, and artisanal in-house baked goods. 45a5289eab: A Filipino restaurant in Vancouver providing indoor dining with a no-smoking policy. Recent OSM verification (April 2025) indicates it is currently operating.
d5b9fc0ecf: Momo Sushi on Bidwell Street is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Vancouver's West End, steps from Stanley Park and the seawall cycling corridor. The restaurant accepts debit or cash only and offers online ordering for takeout.
7e8410b28a: Bendick's Ice Cream Factory is a locally owned small-batch ice cream producer that has been manufacturing premium Canadian dairy ice cream from the same Vancouver location since 1986. Best known as the maker of Sara's Old Fashioned Ice Cream, Bendick's also runs a public-facing Cash & Carry outlet where cyclists can purchase their full product line — including cakes, tubs, and cups — as well as clearance items from major ice cream brands. A hidden-gem factory stop for anyone riding through the Marpole/Oakridge area.
c51079a109: Sushi Asakusa is a casual Japanese sushi restaurant in Langley offering sit-down dining with authentic Japanese cuisine. Located in a commercial area on Walnut Grove Drive, it provides touring cyclists with a proper meal break option.
11765de7e8: Big Way Hot Pot is a growing BC-based hot pot chain offering a self-serve individual hot pot format with over 100 fresh ingredients and more than 18 broths and dry mixes. The Richmond location is part of a network spanning multiple Lower Mainland cities. Diners choose their broth — including a vegan tomato option — and cook premium meats, seafood, and vegetables tableside.
ad4755a48e: Restaurant Yugo is a Japanese-French fusion dining destination located on the first floor of The Amazing Brentwood mall in Burnaby, with a sister location in Vancouver. Dine-in, takeout, catering, and to-go menus are all offered.
edd86a9aa1: Mega Sushi is an award-winning Japanese restaurant located near Steveston Harbour in Richmond, voted best sushi restaurant by Richmond Review readers and top-rated on TripAdvisor. Part of the Mega Group's 14-location BC chain, this independently run outpost is known for using fresh local ingredients and a distinctive roasted-salt technique that enhances the flavour of its fish. Cyclists exploring the Steveston waterfront will find it a short ride from the pier, with a full dine-in menu as well as Korean dishes and desserts.
e56a46f594: Chaibaba is a community-focused loose leaf tea shop in downtown Kelowna, operated by Crystal Russell for over a decade. The shop blends and sells globally sourced organic teas and offers an in-store drink menu with hot and cold beverages. It is a calm, intentional stop with sidewalk seating — a nice contrast to the typical cyclist pit stop.
badf4c5e50: Blaze Café is a Vancouver coffee shop built around ethically sourced Indonesian beans — a Sumatra-Java blend that produces an earthy, chocolate-and-hazelnut cup. The Mount Pleasant flagship is co-located with Blaze Gourmet Burgers and runs a weekend brunch menu with hearty egg and meat dishes; a second express kiosk operates inside City Square Mall. The business also offers a mobile coffee catering service for events around the city.
0022386744: This McDonald's occupies a two-level building on Lougheed Highway in Burnaby's Brentwood corridor, a major east-west arterial connecting communities across the lower mainland. It offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a practical rest stop for cyclists passing through. Vegetarian menu items are available, and the location supports delivery via multiple third-party platforms.
f932f1be78: Dragon Garden is a Chinese restaurant in Langley on Fraser Highway. It serves as a sit-down dining option for touring cyclists seeking a meal break during their journey. The restaurant provides indoor shelter where cyclists can rest and refuel.
4d7e0679c8: A Chinese restaurant located in North Vancouver. Specific details about dining options and cyclist amenities could not be verified due to website access issues.
53d8dd0e98: The Bent Mast is a casual pub and comfort-food restaurant in Victoria's historic James Bay neighbourhood, housed in a character building dating to 1884 and featured on Victoria's Ghost Walks. Located less than a 10-minute walk from the Inner Harbour, it serves a wide selection of local craft beers alongside its kitchen menu, with a spacious patio and upstairs event rooms. Touring cyclists finishing a ride along the waterfront will find a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere right in the heart of the neighbourhood.
e9f1601bb3: Jake's at the Lake is a year-round waterfront restaurant on the shores of Lake Cowichan, housed in a classic woody cabin with high ceilings and large windows framing open lake views. The waterfront patio explicitly welcomes boaters, hikers, and families, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring the Cowichan Valley.
e2b54d5bc3: One20 Public House is a neighbourhood pub in North Delta that bills itself as 'Going Urban in the Burbs,' offering a full food menu spanning tapas, brunch, and desserts alongside draft beer and wine. 3bd3f748b3: A wood-fired bakery located in Kelowna, BC. Specializes in baked goods prepared in a wood-fire oven. Website information could not be accessed during verification.
a97da3c60a: Longwood Brewery's Boxwood Road tasting room is a production brewery and growler bar named one of "the most local of local breweries and beers in BC" by The Tyee Magazine, sourcing the majority of its hops and barley from Vancouver Island and BC mainland farms. A seasonal uncovered picnic patio is pet- and family-friendly, with no onsite kitchen.
072f0c2c9f: Small Gods Brewing Co. is a family-owned microbrewery and taproom in Sidney, BC, situated minutes from the Swartz Bay Ferry Terminal and about 25 minutes north of Victoria. The brewery draws deep inspiration from literature, hosting monthly author readings, book swaps, and a book club, making it a notably community-rooted gathering space. Cyclists stopping in will find a rotating lineup of house-brewed ales and lagers alongside a counter-service deli of house-baked sandwiches and snacks, with a dog-friendly patio.
1e839dc79e: Gasthaus on the Lake is a long-established Bavarian pub and restaurant perched on the shore of Okanagan Lake in Peachland, serving authentic German cuisine — schnitzels, bratwurst, spätzle, and more — since 1991. The lakeside setting and hearty menu make it a natural stop for cyclists riding the Okanagan Valley routes.
a42d1c3ec5: OEB Breakfast Co. is a chef-driven Canadian breakfast and brunch chain founded in 2009 by classically trained chef Mauro Martina, built around farm-to-table sourcing from local Canadian suppliers. The North Vancouver outpost is one of several BC locations offering an inventive menu of Benedicts, breakfast poutines, scramblettes, and bold blue plate specials. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a solid refuelling stop for cyclists on the North Shore.
bed96033fb: Pink Elephant Cafe is a Thai restaurant located on Dunbar Street in Vancouver's Dunbar neighbourhood. Dunbar Street is a local commercial strip serving a residential area, making this a neighbourhood dining spot for locals and passing cyclists alike. The cafe's Instagram handle suggests an active social media presence, though no further details about the dining experience could be verified from publicly accessible content.
611e9d8d76: Krob Krua Thai is a sit-down Thai restaurant in downtown Kamloops serving a broad menu of classic dishes including soups, stir-fries, and noodle dishes. The restaurant prominently highlights Halal food service and offers gluten-free, vegetarian, and vegan adaptations across much of the menu. Located on 3rd Avenue, it sits within easy reach of Kamloops' city centre for cyclists passing through.
ad4d003607: Barley Station Brew Pub is a craft microbrewery and full-service pub in the heart of Salmon Arm's Shuswap region, named after a replica of the town's historic train station. The brewery crafts its own rotating lineup of ales, lagers, pilsners, and seasonal beers using locally sourced ingredients, paired with an elevated pub menu featuring everything from fish and chips to Korean fusion tacos. A pet-friendly patio makes it a welcoming stop for cyclists touring the Shuswap corridor.
8e4fac63ef: Third Beach Concession is the food service kiosk serving Third Beach in Stanley Park, one of Vancouver's most scenic and popular waterfront destinations. It sits along the Seawall route, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists touring the park. The concession offers beach-goers and passing cyclists a convenient place to grab food without leaving the park.
d18a63fa33: Metro Coffee Bar & Billiards is a Portuguese-cuisine bar with billiards tables located on Vancouver's Kingsway. It serves as a social venue offering food, drinks, and gaming facilities. A casual gathering spot for dining and recreation.
395dbb0259: A sushi restaurant in Richmond offering quick counter-service dining. Indoor seating provides weather-sheltered meal breaks for touring cyclists.
3d02846498: Doner Kebab is a fast-food spot on West 4th Avenue in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, a popular cycling corridor connecting downtown to UBC. It serves doner kebab, a Turkish-style dish of seasoned rotisserie meat sliced into flatbread or wraps — a filling, portable option for cyclists passing through. The business was field-verified in OSM as recently as August 2024.
e4594000bc: Perched above the waters of Horseshoe Bay, Olive & Anchor is a casual West Coast dining spot serving scratch-made lunches and dinners in a relaxed, friendly atmosphere. Chef Lisa Kim brings a fine-dining background to a menu of elevated comfort food, complemented by a curated wine list and a selection of local craft and imported beers. Situated 30 minutes from downtown Vancouver in Horseshoe Bay, it makes a natural mid-route stop for cyclists exploring the North Shore.
02d36a9943: Chachi's is a Canadian fast-casual sandwich chain founded in Calgary in 2006, now operating over 20 locations across BC, Alberta, and Manitoba. Pick-up and delivery through multiple apps are available at this location.
37b5fdcadd: Rodney's Oyster House is a celebrated seafood destination in Vancouver's Yaletown, set in a restored heritage building with nautical décor and rustic wood accents. The restaurant is known for its oysters shucked to order from a curated selection sourced from both coasts, alongside broader seafood offerings featuring fresh, locally sourced ingredients. It draws both locals and visitors seeking a lively West Coast dining experience in a vibrant neighbourhood.
4d42c40dfe: Seymour's Pub is a community neighbourhood pub on North Vancouver's Old Lillooet Road, known for homemade food made from scratch daily — including all sauces and dressings — alongside 22 beers on draught spanning local craft, domestic, and international selections. Fifteen TV screens make it a reliable spot to catch major sporting events, while live music on select Fridays and a DJ every Saturday night give it an energetic evening atmosphere. A twice-daily happy hour and rotating daily food specials make it a well-established local gathering point on the North Shore.
9283f23e53: BenGong's Tea is a bubble tea and specialty drink kiosk tucked inside SFU Burnaby's MBC Food Court, serving bubble tea, milk tea, slushes, and their signature bubble waffle. It operates as a takeout-only counter catering to the campus community. Cyclists riding through the SFU area can stop here for a cold drink refuel on a hot day.
e6b0b3b860: Old Towne Inne is a Wild West-themed licensed restaurant and inne in Boston Bar, at the heart of the Fraser Canyon, serving an expansive menu of pizzas, pastas, steaks, Fish & Chips, and over 21 burger varieties. The property also offers self-contained cabins and rooms, making it a potential overnight stop for cyclists tackling the Fraser Canyon corridor.
41bb620242: Agra Sweets & Restaurant is a takeaway-only food business in North Vancouver. Touring cyclists can purchase ready-made meals to take with them. The venue offers no dine-in or outdoor seating for rest stops.
a3c2250df6: Red Bird Brewing is a cozy craft brewery in downtown Kelowna offering over fifteen beers on tap alongside wood-fired sourdough pizzas made with locally sourced ingredients. 38d74fefe7: Homestead Cider is a family-run farm cidery nestled between Mount Cheam and Bear Mountain in Agassiz, crafting cider from estate-grown apples and local BC ingredients. It is dog and kid friendly, and products can also be purchased for pickup or local delivery through the online store.
ab0bb807dd: White Heather Tea Room is a Victoria institution with over 25 years of service in the Oak Bay neighbourhood, dedicated entirely to the art of traditional British afternoon tea. Cyclists can settle in for an elaborate multi-course experience featuring handmade scones, seasonal finger sandwiches, and rotating desserts, or pick up takeout teaboxes and patisserie items to go. Seasonal themed menus — Valentine's, Easter, Mother's Day — make it a notable destination stop on longer tours of the Saanich Peninsula.
3475eb043b: Balkan Bakery is a small East Vancouver artisan bakery specializing in traditional Balkan phyllo pastries — hand-stretched pita and flaky burek filled with meat, cheese, spinach, or potato — alongside handcrafted empanadas and a full organic espresso bar. The shop prides itself on freshly made products using high-quality ingredients and traditional techniques rooted in Balkan home-baking culture. It sits in a residential-commercial neighbourhood with street-level access and car parking front and rear, making it a practical savory-snack stop for cyclists passing through the area.
bf75640aad: Winter Bear Dessert & Teahouse is a dessert-focused cafe and teahouse on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, steps from the Stanley Park Seawall cycling route. The venue offers indoor seating in a no-smoking environment and accepts both credit and debit cards. Its Denman Street location makes it a natural stop for cyclists completing the seawall loop.
788e6d5198: Blenz Coffee is a BC-born specialty coffee chain founded in Vancouver in 1992, with this location inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre on Harvey Avenue in Kelowna. The café offers handcrafted espresso drinks, nitro coffee, whole-leaf teas, protein shakes, and a broad food menu including breakfast sandwiches, wraps, and baked goods. It is a locally owned and operated franchise in a busy mall setting on Kelowna's main commercial strip.
473df15443: The Vic Downtown is an independent coffee roaster and cafe on the corner of 4th Avenue and Victoria Street in the heart of Kamloops, roasting small batches of globally sourced fair-trade and organic beans — including from a women's cooperative in Peru — in-house throughout the week. Beyond coffee, the shop offers a broad food menu spanning breakfast through afternoon snacks, plus over 65 varieties of loose-leaf tea available by the cup or to take home. A sunny street-corner patio makes it a natural gathering spot in the middle of downtown Kamloops.
0b9bd5a59e: Cactus Club Cafe is a well-established Canadian chain serving an upscale casual menu of international dishes — steaks, sushi, pasta, and inventive cocktails — in a stylish, high-energy setting. The West Broadway location sits at a busy urban intersection and is part of a large multi-city network, offering full sit-down dining as well as takeout and delivery. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a broad menu with something for most tastes and the convenience of curbside pickup.
6d7eb2bf49: Murmur is an intimate Mount Pleasant restaurant that began as a daytime café and evolved into an evening tasting experience, led by head chef Abbie Gluvic whose rotating menus draw on modern Vietnamese flavours and seasonal ingredients. It offers multi-course dinners with inventive cocktails in a cozy room that also hosts private gatherings and a recurring Tuesday accordion jam. The space sits quietly on East Broadway, positioned as a neighbourhood destination with a personal, community-minded feel.
2a94b80f27: Uma Sushi is a traditional Japanese eatery in Vancouver's Cambie and Broadway neighbourhood, helmed by Chef Ma, who trained at Le Crocodile and the Art Institute of Vancouver. The restaurant focuses on authentic sushi and donburi bowls, with farm-to-table ingredients and carefully sourced fresh fish — including seasonal highlights like spot prawns and sanma. It operates as a casual, family-friendly spot with both dine-in and takeout available.
b6a5f166bf: Big Daddy's Fish Fry has been a Tofino institution since 2001, built on a commitment to locally sourced, fresh Pacific seafood. The casual counter-style spot offers scratch-made chowder, seafood burgers featuring locally caught halibut and lingcod, fish fry classics, and poutine. For a touring cyclist arriving hungry on the Pacific coast, it represents a hearty, community-rooted meal a short distance from the waterfront.
71706051cf: Blenz Coffee is a BC-born specialty coffee chain operating since 1992, with this location inside Kelowna's Innovation Centre. The café serves handcrafted espresso drinks, nitro coffee, whole-leaf teas, protein shakes, and a broad food menu ranging from breakfast wraps to baked goods and desserts. As a locally franchised outlet in a downtown business hub, it makes a convenient mid-ride stop for cyclists passing through central Kelowna.
d032731e03: Main Street Brewing is a craft microbrewery and taproom in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, pouring an eclectic lineup of pilsners, IPAs, lagers, sours, and small-batch 'Garage Series' specialties brewed on-site. The taproom doubles as a retail store where cyclists can pick up canned beer to take on the road, and an in-house kitchen serves food most days. The brewery's Main Street Premium Pilsner earned a gold medal at the 2024 Canadian Brewing Awards, and an ongoing 'Tunnerman's True Cask Ale' program offers traditional cask-conditioned pours.
48a8949d84: Puerto Vallarta Amigos is a Mexican food operation whose flagship location occupies a colourful floating houseboat in the vibrant community of Fisherman's Wharf in Victoria. The business also runs kiosks at Uptown Mall and the Royal BC Museum courtyard, and operates mobile food trucks for catering. Cyclists exploring the Victoria waterfront can stop here for wraps, burgers, and Mexican street food right at the harbour's edge.
315ceb44dc: Chuihong is a Korean-Chinese fusion restaurant in Surrey's Fraser Heights neighbourhood, specializing in classics like Jjajangmyeon (black bean noodles), TangSooYuk (sweet-and-sour fried pork), and Jjambong (spicy seafood noodle soup). It has built a loyal local following and manages demand through a virtual waitlist system. The restaurant also offers meal kits for customers who want to recreate the dishes at home.
b64904be9d: Scott's Inn & Suites is a long-established downtown Kamloops hotel that has operated for over 60 years, offering studio to three-bedroom suites with kitchenettes and amenities including a rooftop sundeck with BBQ and free parking. On-site food is now provided by 'Scott's On The Go Eats,' a grab-and-go counter offering fresh snacks, coffee, cold beverages, and ice cream after the original restaurant closed due to fire. Its central location and ample parking make it a practical overnight stop for touring cyclists passing through Kamloops.
fcbb98c355: Bean Around The World is a Vancouver-area specialty coffee roaster with over 30 years in the business, roasting small batches daily and sourcing beans from around the world. The brand operates multiple retail café locations across the region alongside a robust online subscription service. A touring cyclist stopping in can expect freshly roasted espresso and drip coffee in a well-established local coffee culture setting.
a6d1d0cf3c: Bean Scene is a pioneer of third wave coffee in the Okanagan, roasting small-batch, hand-crafted espresso since 2002 using a vintage 12 kg Probat roaster retrofitted with an emission control system. The company operates multiple locations across Kelowna and runs its own wholesale bakery, producing fresh scratch-baked goods daily with local ingredients. Touring cyclists will find a serious, independent coffee culture with baristas trained to international competition standards.
c026632c03: The Burrow is a Mexican-inspired vegetarian and vegan restaurant that has anchored Commercial Drive in East Vancouver since 2009. It is known for creative weekend brunch served on morning-baked cornbread, handmade tacos on locally sourced corn tortillas, and cult-favourite baked burritos and nachos — all made entirely without meat. The casual, community-driven atmosphere and entirely plant-based menu make it a compelling stop for cyclists riding one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors.
bf92c2e5d1: Lynx Cafe is a food truck located on the Sea to Sky Highway in Pemberton, offering a convenient stop for cyclists passing through this mountain community. Operating in the fast food tradition with fish and chips and coffee, it provides quick service for travelers. The truck represents a casual, mobile dining option along the highway corridor.
adb8269947: Archr Coffee + Bakery is a community-focused specialty cafe in Langley, BC, offering espresso drinks and a rotating menu of baked goods, sandwiches, and burritos sourced from local BC producers including Elysian Coffee Roasters and To Live For Bakery. Located in unit A150 behind the building at 20161 86 Ave, the shop is tucked away from the street but serves as a neighbourhood gathering spot with catering available for larger events.
e0683e41d6: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, founded in 1928 and still serving its legendary burgers made from 100% fresh Canadian beef alongside a broad family menu at this Kerrisdale location. The West Boulevard spot sits in a walkable, bikeable neighbourhood and offers a patio as well as full dine-in service. Touring cyclists will find familiar comfort food, takeout and delivery options, and a well-known brand with dozens of locations across BC for route planning.
a6d67bd7cd: Rumi Rose Tea is a Sufi-inspired tea and coffee café at 3660 East Hastings, offering over 49 custom-blended healing teas alongside signature espresso and Turkish coffee, and voted Vancouver's Best Sufi Coffee & Espresso. The 6,000-square-foot space doubles as a Middle Eastern market stocking halal meats, Turkish and Iranian sweets, spices, and over 400 grocery items — making it an unusually well-stocked stop for a touring cyclist needing more than just a drink. Local pickup and delivery are available, and the shop operates six days a week.
6d4509900a: Got Pho? is a Vietnamese restaurant located on Nanaimo Street in Vancouver. The name and OSM cuisine tag indicate a focus on pho and other Vietnamese dishes. It provides a casual dining option for tourists and local cyclists.
739387a11f: Kakai Sushi is a Japanese restaurant with two Greater Vancouver locations, offering dine-in and online ordering at its East Broadway location near Commercial Drive. The restaurant focuses on authentic Japanese cuisine with contemporary atmosphere and table reservations available. Cyclists on the Broadway corridor will find it a convenient stop for a sit-down meal or takeout.
7b68fca8ff: Kootenay Tamil Kitchen is a South Indian restaurant on Nelson's main commercial street, run by Tamil immigrants who cook authentic, family-heirloom recipes — heart-healthy dishes free of butter and cream. The operation has expanded to include an Indian grocery store across the street at 639 Baker St and a neighbourhood cafe (KTK Rosemont) at 1516 Crease Avenue. Chef Ciraj's background includes eight years on US cruise lines feeding thousands of guests, making this a genuinely accomplished kitchen in a small-town setting.
5b2b5d13fc: Donair Dude is a Mediterranean-style fast food chain that opened its first location on Davie Street during the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics and has since grown into a multi-location franchise. The restaurant serves freshly prepared donairs, pita wraps, and platters made with premium BC-sourced meats slowly roasted in-house, alongside a dedicated vegan menu featuring falafel. The Davie Street location sits in Vancouver's walkable West End and offers both indoor and outdoor seating.
eb9e55a6d0: Drip Coffee Social is a community-minded independent café established in 2018, operating two Nanaimo locations with a stated focus on inclusivity and local gathering. The Dufferin Crescent location offers a full espresso and tea menu alongside food bowls, sandwiches, baked goods, and even beer, wine, and seasonal cocktails. Mobile ordering is available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists moving through the south Nanaimo corridor.
1e0281f46a: The Green is a modern Korean-fusion breakfast and brunch restaurant on East Hastings Street in Vancouver, specializing in vibrant, plant-forward dishes like bibim tofu bowls, smoked duck with brown rice, and signature multigrain cloud-foam beverages. The cafe operates under a 'Eat Green, Stay Green' philosophy and also offers catering with individual lunch boxes and buffet-style options. Touring cyclists heading through Vancouver's east side will find a health-conscious, vegan-friendly stop with a distinctive Korean-Canadian menu.
abd93be08f: The Chopped Leaf is a Canadian chain founded in 2009, specializing in fresh salads, wraps, bowls, and sandwiches with a focus on making greens feel like comfort food. This location is on Willowbrook Drive in Langley, convenient for cyclists passing through the Township. The menu emphasizes customizable, produce-forward meals that could appeal to riders looking for a lighter, nutritious stop.
e01a740ad9: Grand Noodle Emporium is an AMS-owned and operated pan-Asian restaurant located in the Lower Level of the Nest at UBC Vancouver, seating up to 60 guests. It serves made-to-order comfort dishes spanning Chinese, Thai, and Southeast Asian cuisines — think Pad Thai and Thai curry alongside classic Chinese take-out from a concourse window. It also offers catering and online ordering for pickup, making it a practical stop for cyclists passing through the UBC campus.
26bbe4bb11: Royal Garden Seafood Restaurant occupies a prominent spot inside the Empire Centre shopping mall on Number 3 Road in Richmond, serving authentic Chinese cuisine including traditional Dim Sum, lunch, and dinner. The kitchen team is selected for skill in sourcing fresh, seasonal ingredients, and the restaurant is well regarded in the Lower Mainland for its quality. 590d32bed9: Zaaki Cuisine is a fast-food doner and donair restaurant in New Westminster offering quick, casual meals. The menu includes vegetarian options, providing choices for cyclists with diverse dietary needs.

Touring cyclists passing through the Coquitlam area would find a full sit-down or takeout Japanese meal option here.
bfa2ea7b12: Cafe Overflow is a North Vancouver café blending Korean cuisine with brunch and coffee-shop offerings — an unusual combination that could make it a compelling stop for touring cyclists looking for something beyond standard cafe fare. b55232d4d8: Brassneck Brewery is a well-established craft brewery and tasting room on Main Street in Vancouver, known for a rotating roster of adventurous beers ranging from tart barrel-aged fruit ales to imperial milkshake stouts. d36961f91d: Yaletown Gelato is a neighbourhood ice cream and gelato shop on Homer Street in Vancouver's Yaletown district. 4c0eaa7a5e: Osaka Sushi is a Japanese restaurant on Burrard Street in Vancouver offering sushi, sashimi, donburi, noodles, hot pot, and more. 538ec21b0d: Pallet Coffee Roasters is a locally owned Vancouver specialty coffee roastery established in East Vancouver in 2014, now operating eight café locations across Metro Vancouver. 092926008a: Horin Ramen + Sake is a Japanese ramen restaurant on Robson Street in Vancouver whose heritage traces back 59 years to a pioneering tonkotsu ramen shop in Ogori, Fukuoka Prefecture — the first in Japan to use chili peppers in pork-bone broth. 7777f23642: The Jolly Miller Pub is a traditional pub in Chilliwack offering food and beverages. It serves as a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking for a meal or refreshment while traveling through the area.
36954586eb: Churchill Draughthouse is a cozy Victoria pub occupying a historic Government Street building whose roots trace back to the Garrick's Head Saloon of 1867, with its most colourful chapter being the rough-and-tumble Churchill Hotel of the 1940s–70s. fac213fc8f: Alley 16 is an upscale Japanese BBQ restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver where guests grill premium cuts tableside, with the menu centred on A5 wagyu beef — the highest possible rating — alongside uni sashimi, seafood, and handcrafted sides. b34ced3bb0: The Farmer's Daughter is a fromagerie, bistro, and wine bar on Sidney's main Beacon Avenue, specializing in over 150 artisan and farmhouse cheeses cut to order alongside a curated wine selection. 07a2697d93: JAPADOG is an award-winning, iconic Vancouver hot dog concept founded in 2005 that blends Japanese flavours and ingredients with the classic North American hot dog. 6cb0b83443: Mek's Delight is a Malaysian restaurant located on 104 Avenue in Surrey, BC. Malaysian cuisine — with its rice dishes, noodles, and hearty curries — can be a satisfying refuel for long-distance riders.
b5fe4af30b: Haidilao Hot Pot is a globally recognized Chinese hot pot chain whose first Canadian location opened in Richmond in December 2018. The brand is widely known for elaborate tableside service and a broad menu spanning dozens of proteins, vegetables, and custom dipping sauces.
44f6e7412b: Sushi Farm is a fast food sushi restaurant on Princess Street in North Vancouver with indoor seating. It provides a quick dining option for touring cyclists in the area.
ac99a87eb2: Ichiro Japanese Restaurant is a Japanese-owned and operated full-service restaurant in Steveston Fisherman Village, serving authentic washoku cuisine since 2006. cd82940691: 49th Parallel Cafe is a cafe located in Ladysmith on the east coast of Vancouver Island, British Columbia. c93dd4bb4d: Sushi Sei is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Kingsway in Vancouver, offering both dine-in and online ordering options. Touring cyclists can stop in for a fresh sushi meal and Japanese cuisine in a casual dining environment. The restaurant's central location makes it accessible to cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor.
b158bb5592: Tekkaba is a Japanese restaurant on East Cordova Street in Vancouver, specializing in Kaiseki-style Omakase and traditional Izakaya cuisine, established by Pacific Dream Group. 58be8cfd16: Golden Inn Seafood Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant in Nanaimo serving authentic dishes including Peking duck, Peking ginger beef, lobster, and crab, with lunch and dinner buffets. Delivery, pick-up, and catering are all available, making it a flexible dining option for cyclists passing through Nanaimo.
51713df242: Bella Nonna's is an Italian-inspired artisan bakery, deli, and grocer located in downtown Maple Ridge, BC, handcrafting a wide array of specialty baked goods — breads, cookies, cakes, and pastries — alongside charcuterie boards and gourmet platters. A touring cyclist stopping here can pick up artisan breads, pastries, and specialty deli items to fuel the road ahead.
b3d52e9250: Garrick's Head Pub has occupied Bastion Square since 1867, making it one of the oldest English pubs in Canada and a genuine Victorian-era institution. ed510efd26: Plum Garden is a Japanese restaurant situated on Cornerstone Mews in what appears to be the UniverCity neighbourhood near Simon Fraser University on Burnaby Mountain. Cyclists ascending or descending the SFU corridor would find it a convenient stop for Japanese food in an otherwise limited dining area.
9052e9d43c: Good Choice Restaurant has been a neighborhood fixture on Fraser Street since 1990, specializing in Cantonese cuisine and freshly made dim sum prepared daily from scratch. aa13e17e8a: A Japanese ramen and bubble tea restaurant in Surrey. Limited details available due to website access failure.
009111ae47: Prince Chinese Seafood Restaurant (王子海鮮酒家) is a full-service Chinese seafood restaurant on Grandview Highway in East Vancouver, offering dim sum, dinner service, and banquet facilities. d46e0c729c: Taco Luis is a Mexican-style fast-food counter celebrating 25 years at Lansdowne Shopping Centre in Richmond, serving crispy tacos, burritos, taco salads, and loaded nacho dishes. 5e9997d93e: Yayu is a 100% plant-based cafe tucked into Ucluelet's downtown, serving consciously crafted specialty coffee drinks, smoothies, and nourishing bowls and wraps on the traditional territory of the Yuułuʔiłʔatḥ Nation. 95e4952f89: Grist and Mash Brewery is a craft microbrewery tucked into Kimberley, BC, offering an ever-rotating selection of draft beers on-site and for off-sales in crowler cans or growler bottles. For cyclists passing through the Kimberley area, it offers a relaxed stop for a locally brewed pint in a no-smoking environment.
f8eb9b7b74: Crystal Hut is an on-mountain dining destination operated by Whistler Blackcomb, situated on Blackcomb Mountain and reachable via gondola or the Whistler Mountain Bike Park lift system. c7e8a48b19: Essence of India is a long-established Indian restaurant in the Garibaldi Highlands neighbourhood of Squamish, founded and helmed by Chef Don, who honed his craft across Greek, Italian, French, and Punjabi cuisines before opening this spot. It sits in a suburban commercial area and would serve as a warm sit-down meal stop for cyclists tackling the Sea-to-Sky corridor.
278b292152: Nobi Nobi Obanzai is a Japanese comfort food restaurant in Richmond inspired by the Obanzai cooking tradition of Kyoto, which centres on small seasonal dishes. Online ordering is available, making it a practical stop for a quick meal.
ccc866521e: Earnest Ice Cream is a values-driven Vancouver artisan ice cream company founded in 2012, operating four scoop shops with this Frances Street location also housing their East Van production kitchen. Event catering and self-scoop tub pickups are available exclusively from this Frances Street shop.
8b5cf00c40: Gratia is a community-focused cafe and bakery that evolved from its original Maple Ridge home (formerly Breads & Buns, est. 2016) and opened this Langley outpost in May 2021 in the Walnut Grove neighbourhood. 05c8363b95: Storm City Coffee is a scratch-made, health-conscious neighbourhood café that has anchored Kitsilano since 2017, run by owners Sara and Assad with a philosophy of organic ingredients, 100% extra-virgin olive oil, and locally roasted espresso. The café doubles as a genuine community hub—hosting art workshops, silent book clubs, and free community gatherings, with wall space consigned to local artists.
86fbf26c05: A smoothie and juice cafe on West Vancouver's Marine Drive offering quick refreshment for cyclists and locals. The business operates on a pickup model with indoor seating, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists in a hurry.
ed99fca2e4: Fortitude Wine Bar is a curated wine bar and upscale restaurant anchored in Chilliwack's new District 1881 development on Thunderbird Lane, offering 60+ wine labels hand-selected by an Abbotsford sommelier with a focus on sustainable producers, small wineries, and women in wine. 2577899a1b: Bon Sushi is a neighbourhood sushi restaurant in Oak Bay, Victoria, serving a broad menu of Japanese fare including specialty rolls, sashimi, rice bowls, bento boxes, and party platters. a941e4cd08: Chicken World is a Canadian fast-food chain with a Victoria location on Pandora Avenue, specializing in fried and peri peri chicken with South Asian-inspired spice blends. Cyclists stopping here will find a broad, filling menu with quick-service options in a central Victoria location.
91e3353464: Valley Bakery has been a Burnaby institution since 1957, producing European-style baked goods including artisanal breads, buttercream pastries, wedding cakes, and savoury meat pies. A touring cyclist could stop here for fresh-baked bread and savoury meat pies as a food resupply.
d06234c1c9: Corner House Cafe is a neighbourhood restaurant and cafe situated on Jubilee Street in Duncan, on southern Vancouver Island. 604a9be2e7: Chamnamoo is a Korean restaurant operating out of a unit in a Langley commercial complex on 88 Avenue. A touring cyclist passing through the Langley area would find it a sit-down dining option in an otherwise suburban commercial corridor.
2e45a472ca: Earnest Ice Cream is a Vancouver-area institution founded in 2012, crafting small-batch ice cream from local and seasonal ingredients across four scoop shops — including this North Vancouver location on West 1st Street. 4f3f8ea686: Rise and Shine Coffee House is listed in OSM as a café in Penticton, BC. No independent website or contact information has been confirmed for the Penticton location, as the discovered URL resolves to a same-named but unrelated business in Cornell, Wisconsin.
b035eba0ad: A McDonald's fast-food restaurant on Powell Street in East Vancouver offering drive-through, curbside pickup, and delivery alongside dine-in service. 580a633779: Hungry Eats is a family-owned American diner in Surrey serving a broad comfort-food menu of burgers, fish & chips, salads, wraps, and starters. Touring cyclists will find a filling, varied menu including several vegetarian options.
1b6f34566e: Paco's Tacos is a restaurant listed in OSM at 111 Rainbow Road in Duncan, BC. Details about the business's offerings, setting, or cyclist-relevant features could not be confirmed, as the only discovered website resolves to a different establishment on Salt Spring Island.
757a2d15e3: Sushi Flamingo is a Japanese restaurant located on Burrard Street in Vancouver's South Granville area, a corridor popular with cyclists commuting between downtown and the southern neighbourhoods. a61f25bcc7: Mariner Pizza is a family-owned and operated pizzeria that has been serving the Sidney and North Saanich communities for over 20 years. 1820f9f5fc: Sabra is a Glatt Kosher and Halal restaurant and bakery in Vancouver, founded in 1992 by the Kahlon family and supervised by the Orthodox Rabbinical Council of British Columbia. dc7ed894cf: Mandarin Hong Kong Cafe is a Chinese restaurant on West King Edward Avenue in Vancouver. It serves Mandarin-style cuisine and is easily accessible to touring cyclists passing through the area.
e1822179e0: Kinton Ramen Sunwood Coquitlam is a Japanese ramen restaurant located inside Sunwood Square, part of one of North America's largest ramen chains with 50+ locations founded in Canada in 2012. The menu centres on customizable bowls with pork, beef, chicken, or vegetarian broth bases paired with a choice of thin, thick, or shirataki noodles. Touring cyclists will find a warm, filling meal with substantial carbohydrate options in a sit-down dine-in setting.
2eef402fa2: Browns Social House is a casual full-service restaurant and bar chain with dozens of locations across BC and Alberta, operated by the Browns Restaurant Group. It sits in a commercial plaza on King George Boulevard, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Surrey city centre corridor.
648fc82404: Patina Brewing Co. is a multi-award-winning craft brewery and BBQ taproom in Port Coquitlam, recognized as the only brewery in the city to receive a BC Beer Award. Touring cyclists can refuel with BBQ food and a flight of locally crafted beer in a welcoming community gathering spot.
0bd09208e6: The Aroma Bistro & Bar is an Indian restaurant in Abbotsford serving a wide-ranging menu of South Asian dishes — from tandoori specialties and butter chicken to Indo-Chinese fusion and daily thali specials. Online ordering and a reservations system make it accessible for both quick stops and longer meals.
9900463ef0: Mary Brown's is a 100% Canadian-owned fast food chain specializing in fresh, hand-cut and hand-breaded chicken, with nearly 300 locations across Canada including this Chilliwack stop on South Fraser Way. The chain prides itself on whole, Canada Grade A chicken marinated and cooked fresh in-store rather than pressure-fried, making it a recognizable comfort-food option for cyclists passing through. c46bc6432a: Osaka Teppanyaki is a Japanese teppanyaki restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver where chefs cook at your table with dazzling cutlery skills on an iron griddle. The restaurant welcomes birthday parties and groups, making it a convivial stop for cycling groups riding through the Kitsilano corridor.
3877ebb134: Cosy Inn Cafe is a long-standing neighbourhood diner on Dunbar Street in Vancouver serving a broad menu of Chinese dishes, all-day breakfast, burgers, and sandwiches.
