Its central Dunbar location makes it a practical mid-ride or post-ride meal stop for cyclists in the area.
72b16d9543: LA Sushi Fusion Restaurant is a sushi-focused fusion dining establishment in the Fraser Valley. Touring cyclists passing through the region would find it a sit-down option for a fuller meal. Limited publicly available details exist beyond its cuisine type and street address.
76e1d21f91: Diamond Sweets & Restaurant is a multi-location Indian food chain operating across Surrey and Delta, BC, rooted in traditional South Asian recipes, house-made spice blends, and scratch-prepared Indian sweets. e60132b9ae: Blaze Gourmet Burgers is a BC-born gourmet burger brand that grew from a COVID-era ghost kitchen into a multi-location operation. 0321621326: Thelma & Marcella's Sips Cafe is a single-storey retail cafe located on 100 Avenue in Fort St. John, a hub city for cyclists travelling the Alaska Highway corridor in northeastern BC. 6d538ca53e: Grizzly Flatbread is a Neapolitan-style pizza and flatbread restaurant in Ladner, BC, known for hand-tossed dough made with imported Italian 00 flour cooked in an open-flame stone hearth oven. The menu features meat and vegetarian/vegan pizzas, flatbreads, salads, and sides, with both in-house dining and online ordering for pickup or delivery. A welcoming neighbourhood spot with a casual atmosphere, it sits along Ladner Trunk Road in the Tsawwassen/Ladner area of Metro Vancouver.
7579e166f9: Steamworks Northshore is the newest location of Steamworks Brewing Co., a well-established British Columbia craft beer brand, operating as a taphouse and full-service restaurant on the North Shore. The space pours signature Steamworks brews alongside rotating guest taps celebrating the local craft scene, served in a group-friendly dining room with an expansive patio. The kitchen offers pub favourites, fusion creations, plant-based dishes, and weekend brunch — a solid refuelling stop for cyclists coming off the North Shore trails.
9172219f80: Granville Island Brewing, BC's first craft brewery established in 1984, operates a taproom and retail store on Granville Island, one of Vancouver's most popular cycling destinations. 5023c9eb17: Living Tree Foods is a plant-based food producer with a retail storefront in New Westminster, BC, founded in 2020 by two UBC Law graduates. ba2dffeea8: The Workshop Vegetarian Café is a Japanese-inspired plant-based café in North Vancouver, established in 2016, specializing in handcrafted ramen and udon noodle bowls made with housemade organic noodles and locally sourced ingredients where possible. The team describes itself as including outdoor enthusiasts, and the café also offers catering, frozen products, and ramen kits to go.
0249b0e0de: Vista 18 is a full-service restaurant and lounge on the 18th floor of the Chateau Victoria hotel in downtown Victoria, offering sweeping panoramic views of the Inner Harbour, Juan de Fuca Strait, and the Olympic Mountains. Touring cyclists arriving in Victoria's downtown core will find a distinctly elevated dining experience anchored by an extensive B.C. and Vancouver Island wine program.
4996a2b143: Yummy Slice Pizza is a Canadian-owned pizza-by-the-slice chain with locations across Metro Vancouver, offering pickup and delivery seven days a week. The chain also runs school and corporate catering programs, making it a practical fuel stop in a busy urban corridor.
0bfec294d6: Cafe Talia is a cafe in Duncan, BC, listed in OpenStreetMap with minimal metadata. The Instagram handle associated with this listing could not be verified due to Instagram's login wall, and discovery notes suggest the business may have rebranded as Switchboard Cafe.
192d3b57f5: Torake is a contemporary Japanese restaurant in Richmond that blends modern Japanese and French culinary techniques, emphasizing locally-sourced and seasonal ingredients. 18577b6a26: Burger Factory is a franchised Canadian smash-burger chain emphasising fresh, halal, and locally-sourced ingredients, now with over 40 locations across North America. Cyclists can order ahead via the chain's mobile app for a quick fuel stop.
3a9ae1a54b: Established in 2021, Pizzeria La Stella is an upscale Italian pizzeria in Nanaimo serving artisanal thin-crust and Sicilian-style pizzas made entirely from scratch — dough, dips, and house-cured pepperoni included. Cyclists can dine in for a full three-course meal, grab a coffee and tiramisu at the counter, or call ahead for a pick-up order.
92540b3c3e: Genji is a Japanese restaurant located in the Parkgate shopping area of North Vancouver, steps from the Mount Seymour Parkway corridor that serves as a gateway to North Shore trails. Its proximity to Mount Seymour Provincial Park and regional cycling routes makes it a natural rest stop for cyclists coming off the mountain.
9602a18dd1: Brix & Mortar is a locally family-owned Canadian cuisine restaurant operating since 1999 inside a 1912 heritage brick building in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood. Touring cyclists passing through Yaletown will find a full dinner menu of locally sourced Canadian fare, creative cocktails, and a take-out option for meals on the go.
98ee2a330f: Chez Céline is a French-Canadian bistro occupying a corner spot in Vancouver's Fraserhood neighbourhood, channelling the culinary spirit of Montréal and Québec through dishes like escargots, beef tartare, poutine, and Crêpes Suzette made with local, seasonal ingredients. It offers both a dinner menu and a weekend brunch, making it a viable mid-ride or end-of-ride dining destination for cyclists exploring the Fraser Street corridor.
fdb4be2c2b: Cafe Ricotta is a cafe located in a unit at 20349 88 Avenue in Langley, BC. Beyond this, details about its offerings and atmosphere remain unverified due to limited accessible web presence.
9891fc39f4: Maurya's Fine Indian Cuisine is an Indian restaurant offering sit-down dining in Kamloops. The restaurant serves Indian cuisine, making it a convenient full-meal dining option for cyclists traveling through the area.
cbad390da9: Mandarin House is a Chinese restaurant located at 201 Fourth Street in downtown Nanaimo, offering dine-in, takeout pickup, and local delivery. ae0239ccf4: Fujiya is a Japanese grocery and deli chain celebrating over 50 years in BC, with the Victoria location on Shelbourne Street open since 1991. 456521bdb6: The Keg Scott Road is a full-service steakhouse and bar in Surrey, part of the long-established Canadian chain founded in the 1970s. a6cb7743ed: Shawnigan House Coffee and Chocolate is a specialty coffee and artisan chocolate shop that has been serving the Shawnigan Lake area since 2000. 73bc2b438b: Wild Flour Pizza Co is a sourdough-focused pizza restaurant building each 12-inch pie on a naturally leavened crust with creative topping combinations. 3c1f8fa147: A Subway franchise located on Terminal Avenue North in Nanaimo, offering sandwiches, wraps, salads, and breakfast items. 0af444fc68: Koto Sushi is a high-end Japanese restaurant in downtown Victoria serving sushi and broader Japanese cuisine in a signature red-and-black dining room. 783b53446a: Hestia Kitchen + Bar is a casual full-service restaurant and bar in Richmond's commercial core, built around the concept of "premium ingredients + casual space." 55fa6f4874: Vis-à-Vis is a wine bar and French-inspired bistro in the heart of Oak Bay Village, offering wine selected by an in-house sommelier alongside locally sourced lunch, dinner, and late-night menus. 945ce0429f: The Taphouse is a modern neighbourhood tavern in Coquitlam offering a full food menu alongside local craft taps and a broad drinks list. fda2b01b55: Yuki Cafe is a neighbourhood sushi restaurant on Kingsway in East Vancouver, run by Japanese Master Chef Yuki who brings over 20 years of culinary expertise to the menu. f26c431eaf: The Red Wagon Cafe is a brunch and diner-style cafe on East Hastings Street in Vancouver's east side, offering indoor seating in a neighbourhood restaurant setting. 2e070ef745: The Parlour is a stylish yet unpretentious restaurant anchored in Vancouver's historic Yaletown neighbourhood, blending East Coast edge with West Coast hospitality. 8b35043509: Baoguette Vietnamese Bistro is a sit-down restaurant in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood serving authentic Vietnamese dishes including pho, bánh mì, spring rolls, and vermicelli bowls. 08a87a073c: Siegel's Bagels is an authentic Montreal-style bagel shop with a location inside Granville Island Public Market, one of Vancouver's most-visited culinary destinations. 609e4e3fe4: Bavaria Restaurant is a family-run European fine dining institution that has anchored Abbotsford's dining scene since 1975, founded by Czech immigrants whose heritage shaped a menu of schnitzels, bratwurst, goulash soup, and tableside specialties like Steak Flambé and Flamed Escargot. d4cab51db4: Ethical Bean Coffee is a Vancouver-based coffee roaster founded in 2003, certified 100% fair trade and organic from day one, sourcing Arabica beans seasonally from Central and South America with full crop-to-cup traceability. e9b3c63f80: The business at this address appears to operate as Singapore Hawker Restaurant, an authentic Singaporean and Malaysian hawker-style eatery whose chef brings over 25 years of dedicated experience in these cuisines. e66ca7ef08: Ono Poké is a Victoria-based Hawaiian poke bowl chain with four shopping-centre locations across the city and Saanich. 0c2c3d87a5: Uno Gelato is a Vancouver artisan gelateria making small-batch, farm-to-cone gelato and sorbetto fresh daily from natural local ingredients including Vancouver Island sea salt and Avalon Dairy milk. 49705bdaf7: Torafuku is a contemporary pan-Asian restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street, helmed by Taiwanese-born chef Steve Kuan, who first made his mark with the acclaimed Le Tigre food truck before opening this brick-and-mortar location. 90428ca1dd: Fishboat — also known as Fishboat Fish & Chippery — is a fish and chips eatery on White Rock's Marine Drive waterfront that has been operating since 2009. 4f700a3765: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain franchise offering delivery and takeout only, with no dine-in seating at this downtown Vancouver location. 821b837081: Melriches Coffee House is an independent cafe that has served Vancouver's West End neighbourhood since 1997, deliberately positioning itself as a community alternative to chain coffee shops with mismatched furniture and a weekly neighbour meet-up table by the window. ff9e6bacee: Sweet Leaf Bakery & Cafe is a locally-owned bakery and espresso bar tucked inside Piccadilly Mall in the heart of Salmon Arm, serving creative seasonal desserts including cupcakes, macarons, and custom cakes alongside freshly roasted local coffee. 6b11f50094: Amsterdam Restaurant is a cozy, locally owned breakfast and lunch eatery that has been introducing Kamloops to Dutch pannenkoeken (crepes) for over 20 years. 60e40da2b9: The Fox & Hounds is a long-established neighbourhood pub in Aldergrove, BC, whose fanciful origin story claims its heavy timber frame was shipped from England by a fox-hunting publican and reassembled in the alder grove that gave the town its name. 45b7d07c83: Goldie's Donuts & Bakery is a gourmet brioche donut shop that uses a 24-hour slow fermentation process imported from Korean baking tradition to produce exceptionally light and flavourful donuts. e818617df8: Kwao Thai Restaurant is a family-run authentic Thai restaurant in Esquimalt, just outside Victoria. 770dbc9740: Blind Rabbit is a neighbourhood bar and charcuterie restaurant on East Hastings Street in Vancouver's Hastings-Sunrise area, specializing in an extensive lineup of BC craft gins and spirits alongside boards, paninis, and fondue. 1acfc97206: The Blue Ox Pub is a classic, cozy community pub in Lumby, BC, serving pub food and drinks seven days a week. c97b506204: White Lotus Cafe is an authentic Vietnamese restaurant in North Burnaby serving pho, Bún Bò Huế, bánh mì made with daily-baked bread, and fresh salad rolls. 2d0962f0b9: Caffè Artigiano is a pioneering Vancouver specialty coffee brand with over 25 years of history and international barista competition recognition, known for award-winning latte art and its own Burnaby roastery producing 100% Arabica blends. 16098e4746: Kaide Sushi Bar is a Japanese restaurant on Richards Street in downtown Vancouver, operating for over 20 years. 207ea0f1a7: Avalon Restaurant is a brunch-focused restaurant on Victoria's Fort Street. Details about cyclist amenities are currently unavailable as the website is under maintenance.

908942a731: Chef Tony Seafood Restaurant is an award-winning upscale Cantonese dining destination in Richmond's Imperial Centre, recognized with multiple Gold wins for Best Chinese and Best Dim Sum by local dining guides. ab0d6a418d: The Cordova Room is an intimate whiskey and cocktail bar tucked into the heart of Gastown, featuring dark green walls, warm wood, and golden accents. 2c265c9737: Lin Chinese Cuisine is an award-winning Shanghainese restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver, known for dishes like Xiao Long Bao (Shanghai juicy pork dumplings), Tea Smoked Duck, and Honey Prawns. 7e5b5faa65: A tiny, family-run Japanese restaurant that has been serving authentic food in White Rock for over 40 years, founded by Yoshi and Michiko in 1982. fd34f61bc2: Anna's Cake House is a family-owned Hong Kong-style bakery founded in 1974 by Anna, Ronald, and Kathleen Cheung, now celebrating 50 years as a community institution in Greater Vancouver. c5ef399cf1: Vegan Shoku is a fully plant-based Japanese restaurant on West 41st Avenue in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, offering an extensive menu of sushi rolls, ramen, udon, donburi, and creative vegan interpretations of Japanese seafood dishes. d228f3cdbd: Chez Christophe is a Swiss-inspired chocolaterie and patisserie founded in 2013 by Swiss-trained pastry chef Christophe Bonzon, operating its original flagship in Burnaby Heights on Hastings Street. efb8d47b8e: Stinky's on the Stroll is a legendary neighborhood pub on Whistler's Village Stroll, conceived by long-time local Jeremy 'Stinky' Peterson as a community gathering place and love letter to the town. 36db673303: Notti Biscotti is a South Surrey artisan bakery and café founded by Shelley Quesnel, specializing in over twenty flavours of thick, chocolate-based Italian biscotti made with all-natural, preservative-free ingredients. d82ff62174: Pho 37 is a multi-location Vietnamese restaurant chain that started in Steveston and expanded to Robson Street in Vancouver, serving freshly made pho, vermicelli bowls, and traditional Vietnamese appetizers. 987960326f: Desi Indian Lounge is a modern fine-dining Indian restaurant on Hornby Street in downtown Vancouver, blending traditional regional recipes with elegant lounge-style presentation and a full cocktail bar featuring Indian-inspired drinks. e331c145dc: Benanna Bakery is a quaint, artisanal European-inspired bakery in Chilliwack that has been baking from scratch since 2012. 31bee9782d: Chicha San Chen is a bubble tea cafe chain location. It offers indoor seating and takeaway service, providing cyclists with a spot to grab a beverage during a ride.
05a32e7805: The Sunflower Café is a beloved Crescent Beach institution serving wholesome breakfast and lunch for over 20 years, with everything made in-house from whole ingredients including freshly baked multigrain sourdough. 9623c04970: Deadbeetz Burgers is a locally focused fast-food burger spot on Oak Bay Avenue in Victoria, built around house-made ingredients like pickled beets, dill pickles, and a signature Vancouver Island sauce. fe1e4c05b0: Sushi California is a Japanese cuisine restaurant in Vancouver with two locations. Cyclists in the area can stop for sushi takeout via online ordering.
4e77b768f0: Nook is a Vancouver-born Italian restaurant group that opened its first location in the West End in 2009, built around housemade pasta, wood-fired pizza, and locally sourced ingredients supplemented by imported Italian products. 06fc4c4300: Hashi Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Richmond, BC, a city celebrated for one of Canada's most diverse Asian dining scenes. 1f3827a90e: Dae Bak Bon Ga is a long-running Korean BBQ restaurant on Vancouver's busy Robson Street, serving both à la carte and all-you-can-eat BBQ menus with over 140 seats for small and large groups. 460b6ea326: Paris Baguette is a Korean-origin international bakery café chain known for freshly baked pastries, custom celebration cakes, and café beverages. 6d02870aef: The Golden Horn is a halal-certified Turkish bakery and cafe on Vancouver's Cambie corridor, specializing in handcrafted pastries including baklava made in-house from over 40 layers of homemade yufka dough, plus boreks, pide flatbreads, and traditional Turkish coffee. 6320c6414a: Blackfish Pub is a neighbourhood pub in Gibsons on British Columbia's Sunshine Coast, positioned as a casual local gathering spot with a seasonal menu of food and drink. afd691c5b5: Burger Crush is a BC-born fast-casual chain reviving the classic burger shop with smashed Canadian Angus beef burgers, vegan and veggie alternatives, hand-dipped shakes, and loaded fries. eb8d6b1a2e: BBQ King Delight is a Cantonese-style roasted meat shop in Surrey specializing in Hong Kong BBQ classics: roasted duck, honey BBQ pork, soy sauce chicken, and crispy roasted pork, sold by weight or as rice bento boxes. 49eac00a0b: Domino's is a national pizza chain franchise located on Highway 97 N in Lake Country, sitting directly on the main Okanagan cycling corridor between Kelowna and Vernon. eebbc1a150: Mazaj Best Donair is a Middle Eastern restaurant in Langley specializing in donairs, a beloved street-food staple in BC. c3998ed067: Bellaggio Café is an owner-operated Italian restaurant in the heart of downtown Vancouver, steps from the Vancouver Art Gallery and Pacific Centre. It is a predictable, accessible stop for cyclists travelling through the Royal Oak area.
0700fcc3a5: GRNHSE at the Refinery is a second-floor cocktail lounge and private event venue situated in Vancouver's Granville Entertainment District, featuring an 18-foot full-service bar, elegant decor, and both indoor and covered outdoor heated patio spaces for groups of 20 to 75. The bar menu spans hand-crafted cocktails, beer, wine, and a food menu with vegetarian and gluten-free options including nachos and salads. While the space is primarily available for private bookings, it also opens to the general public on weekend evenings.
1a67b26715: Cafe & Life Co. is a community-minded cafe that opened during the COVID-19 pandemic with a mission to reconnect the local neighbourhood over quality coffee. The Richmond location serves a full brunch menu alongside specialty coffee, pastries, and catering, with delivery available through Uber Eats and Fantuan. It has since expanded to a second Vancouver location, reflecting a growing loyal following.
85bab6d95e: The Pie Shoppe is a small-batch, artisan pie and coffee shop founded by sisters Stephanie and Andrea French, also home to Panoramic Coffee Roasters. The shop is built around handcrafted seasonal pies using local BC fruit from the Fraser Valley, Okanagan, and nearby islands, served with hand-drip pour-over or Aeropress coffee. Seating is extremely limited, making it a grab-and-go stop for cyclists riding the nearby Adanac Bike Path.
b7f1dd73fc: McDonald's at 7295 Knight Street is a no-drive-through fast-food outlet in Vancouver's Knight Street corridor, offering the full Canadian McDonald's menu including McCafé beverages. The indoor and outdoor seating areas make it a sit-down-friendly stop rather than a drive-past convenience. It is one of the more accessible rest points in this stretch, with wheelchair access and on-site washrooms confirmed in OSM.
7daa5ae10d: Lucia Gelato is a Whistler-based artisan maker of dense, milk-based gelato and sorbetto crafted from fresh, natural ingredients using traditional Italian techniques. The business operates as a mobile food truck and rotating seasonal outdoor stands at public locations including Lost Lake Park, Whistler Olympic Plaza, and Blackcomb base, putting it squarely on the route of cyclists exploring the Sea-to-Sky corridor. Gelato is also stocked in 475 mL retail packs at grocery stores across Whistler, Squamish, and Pemberton.
9eff61fc17: Pier Bistro Restaurant sits at the end of Beacon Avenue on Sidney's pier, beside the Fish Market, offering panoramic harbour views from a casual waterfront setting. The menu is built around BC coastal seafood staples — fish and chips in three species, house crab cakes, clam chowder, and local mussels — alongside burgers, sandwiches, and salads. For a touring cyclist finishing a ride through the Saanich Peninsula, it is a classic end-of-the-road lunch or dinner spot with the ocean right outside.
4d18efd7e7: Sharetea is a Taiwanese bubble tea franchise founded in 1992, serving premium boba tea made with high-quality tea leaves imported directly from Taiwan. With over 400 stores worldwide, this Vancouver location offers a wide variety of milk teas, fruit teas, ice-blended drinks, and customizable toppings such as tapioca pearls, pudding, and lychee jelly. A convenient refreshment stop for cyclists passing through the area.
d5d8556c84: The Summit Lodge is a 9,000 square-foot facility perched at the summit of the Sea to Sky Gondola above Squamish, featuring a West Coast-inspired restaurant and café with local food and beverage options beneath dramatic floor-to-ceiling windows and Douglas fir beams. The lodge includes the Sky Pilot Restaurant, Co-Pilot Café, a viewing deck, and access to the Sky Pilot Suspension Bridge. Cyclists on the Sea to Sky corridor can reach it as a destination excursion from the gondola base station off Highway 99.
de67a05cc3: Jade Dynasty Restaurant is a traditional Chinese dim sum destination in the heart of Vancouver's Chinatown, in continuous operation since 2005 and winner of the Chinatown Best Traditional Restaurant award for 2023. Newly renovated in 2019, it offers classic dim sum alongside a full regular menu, takeout menu, and chef's specials. Cyclists riding through Chinatown will find both dine-in and pickup options at this well-established neighbourhood institution.
f53e50d30f: Dockside Restaurant sits on the waterfront of Granville Island inside the Granville Island Hotel, offering panoramic views of False Creek, the Vancouver skyline, and the North Shore Mountains through floor-to-ceiling windows. The award-winning patio spans over 200 seats and is one of the city's most celebrated outdoor dining spaces. A seasonal menu of fresh, locally sourced ingredients with international influences is served across breakfast, lunch, dinner, and weekend brunch.
9598958356: Blue Coast is a Japanese seafood restaurant in Vancouver offering both dine-in and online ordering. Located on Vanness Avenue, it provides a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists in the neighborhood. The restaurant serves prepared Japanese seafood cuisine whether customers choose to eat on-site or take food with them.
a7e2d85dd1: James Street Cafe is a small cafe located in a unit off the Trans-Canada Highway in Duncan, BC, serving sandwiches, soups, tea, and coffee. The space is described as cozy and community-oriented, with local art on the walls and a welcoming atmosphere suited to a quick stop or a longer work session. It is wheelchair accessible and situated in a commercial unit, making it a practical refuelling option for cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley.
862c3083b6: Morning Tide Eatery is a modern brunch spot in Coquitlam, owned by a local Tri-Cities couple who wanted to bring quality, creative brunch to the suburbs without the long city drives and waits. The menu blends classic brunch staples with Asian-inspired touches, including a house-made longanisa (sweet Filipino pork patty) sandwich with atchara, alongside eggs benedict, loaded bowls, and fried chicken. The restaurant is located within a bowling alley complex, lending it an unexpected and memorable setting.
358908486c: Cafe Duello is an espresso bar and board game lounge tucked inside Academie Duello, Vancouver's world-renowned Historical European Martial Arts academy—the largest such centre globally. Cyclists can refuel with Italian espresso, smoothies, fresh pastries, grilled cheese, and avocado toast while choosing from 80+ board games including Catan, Root, and Ticket to Ride. The cafe is open to anyone, no sword training required.
e2b6ac3e45: The Fish Store is a floating seafood restaurant and licensed fish processing plant moored at Fisherman's Wharf in Victoria, where fishing boats tie up directly at the store to deliver their catch. By purchasing fish and shellfish straight from the fishermen and processing on-site, it cuts out the supply chain entirely to offer some of the freshest local seafood on the coast, including salmon, halibut, albacore tuna, Dungeness crab, and spot prawns. The entire menu is 100% Ocean Wise certified, and menus are available in five languages, reflecting its prominence as a destination for visitors to the Inner Harbour waterfront.
779f0af818: Mega Donair is a Port Moody fast-food restaurant established in 2011, specializing in donairs with freshly baked pita and an expanded topping selection including cucumber, spicy carrots, parsley, and feta cheese. It serves halal chicken and beef alongside lamb and falafel, and claims to offer the largest donair size in British Columbia. Catering and limited-radius delivery are available for larger orders.
3e944ab9b6: Stage is a wine bar and restaurant in Victoria's Fernwood neighbourhood, known for a seasonally rotating menu built around ingredients sourced directly from local farmers and purveyors. The room accommodates private and semi-private events up to 90 guests, and Sunday evenings feature a family-style three-course dinner. A touring cyclist stopping in Fernwood will find a relaxed neighbourhood spot with a full evening menu and happy hour service.
b88fb52191: Trees Cheesecake & Organic Coffee has been a Vancouver institution since 1996, roasting small-batch organic beans in-house and pairing them with award-winning homemade cheesecakes made fresh daily in rotating flavours. The Burrard Street location is one of roughly 13–14 Vancouver cafes operated as a mix of corporate and franchised outlets. Cyclists stopping here can expect a full cafe menu of sandwiches, baked goods, teas, and cold drinks alongside the signature coffee and cheesecake.
bbc7a87082: Real Food Café is a weekday lunch spot in downtown Nanaimo built around the philosophy of using only natural, unprocessed ingredients. The kitchen turns out four house-made soups daily alongside fresh sandwiches, salads, and artisan cakes baked in-house. It's a solid midday refueling stop for cyclists seeking a wholesome, made-from-scratch meal.
4e60f68749: An organic bakery and cafe on Salt Spring Island offering organic baked goods and confirmed vegan options. A casual stopping point for touring cyclists seeking refreshment. Serves walk-in customers with an organic-focused menu.
e014d32480: Kafka's Coffee is a Vancouver-based specialty coffee roaster with multiple locations; the Great Northern Way outpost doubles as the company's bakery hub, serving house-made breads, pastries, and a full breakfast and lunch menu from a sun-soaked patio on the Emily Carr University and Centre for Digital Media campus. Espresso is pulled on a custom-modified Synesso machine using beans sourced directly from farmers and roasted weekly in Vancouver. The space also functions as a community arts venue, hosting rotating solo and group exhibitions by local artists.
4e3e7d82b2: Sergio's Pizza is a neighbourhood pizza takeout counter tucked into a strip-mall unit in Port Moody, offering a broad menu of house specialty pies, build-your-own options, pastas, wings, and family packs. The shop caters primarily to call-in and walk-in orders, making it a straightforward fuel stop for cyclists passing through the Tri-Cities corridor. With over twenty specialty pizza choices and a full sides list, it can accommodate a hungry group after a long day on the saddle.
f3e9ab2bd3: Burger & Cafe Joy is a Japanese-inspired burger cafe that has been operating inside Sahali Mall in Kamloops since 2011, where owners Ben and Peiting make every burger from scratch using locally sourced meats, house-made sauces, and fresh vegetables. The menu blends North American comfort food with Japanese flavours — think teriyaki beef, pork katsu, oyster burgers, and yakisoba sides — alongside bubble tea and homemade Asian desserts. A touring cyclist can call ahead for takeout and head straight to pickup, or have the meal delivered to a nearby stop.
8e6780a025: AFURI is a Tokyo-origin ramen chain serving light, yuzu-accented broths alongside sushi and small plates at its Vancouver location on Main Street. The kitchen avoids artificial ingredients and preservatives, emphasising naturally derived umami from fresh, high-quality ingredients. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down meal with vegan and gluten-free options, as well as online ordering for convenience.
56a7ebf39b: A Mexican restaurant in downtown Vancouver on Hornby Street. A centrally located food option for cyclists exploring the city.
5089a195a0: Hyderabad Haveli is a South Indian restaurant on Vancouver's Kingsway corridor specializing in Hyderabadi cuisine, with dum biriyani, regional curries, and tandoori dishes rooted in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh culinary traditions. The menu spans non-vegetarian and vegetarian mains, starters, breads, and desserts, making it a substantive meal stop for cyclists riding through the Kingsway area.
14f330ff1b: Nemesis Coffee is a Vancouver-based specialty coffee roaster with five Lower Mainland café locations; the GNW branch sits at 555 Great Northern Way in the arts-and-innovation corridor between Mount Pleasant and East Vancouver. The café serves espresso and everyday filter coffees sourced from named farms alongside freshly baked pastries from their in-house Dope Bakehouse. The brand actively supports World Coffee Research and acknowledges operating on the unceded territories of the Musqueam, Squamish, and Tsleil-Waututh Nations.
8a887515b2: Sprouted Oven is a 100% plant-based, non-GMO bakery, kitchen, and grocery space offering everything from sourdough and custom cakes to pizzas, burgers, lattes, and smoothies under one roof. The bakery maintains a dedicated enclosed gluten-free area with its own ovens, utensils, and air-pressure system — a rare setup that makes it genuinely accessible to celiac cyclists. It's a full-service food stop for riders with dietary restrictions who would otherwise struggle to find satisfying plant-based options along this corridor.
4684f093f2: Salt & Brick is a restaurant in Kelowna, BC. Website content could not be retrieved, so specific details about cuisine, amenities, and services are unavailable.
41a6936de1: Neighbour's Restaurant & Pizza House is a second-generation, family-owned Greek-Italian establishment on Victoria Drive that has been serving Vancouver since 1982. The menu spans souvlaki, spanakopita, wood-style pizza, and a full cocktail bar, reflecting its Italian-with-a-Greek-touch identity. The restaurant regularly accommodates large groups and private parties and offers online ordering with delivery through major platforms.
d59faffde6: Creekbread is a wood-fired pizza restaurant in Whistler Creekside that opened just before the 2010 Winter Olympics, situated directly across from the Olympic downhill finish line. The kitchen bakes flatbreads in a wood-burning oven using locally sourced ingredients including Pemberton potatoes and house-made fennel sausage. Its lively après atmosphere and strong community ties make it a natural stopping point for cyclists rolling into Creekside.
7a6ae97996: Hamaei Japanese Menu is a Japanese restaurant located in North Vancouver. It offers indoor dining in a smoke-free environment, making it a sit-down option for cyclists passing through the area. The Facebook-based web presence suggests a small, independently operated establishment.
f9ab4a7321: Big Bad John's is a world-famous hillbilly bar that traces its roots to BC's first-ever licensed cocktail lounge, opened in 1954 at the Strathcona Hotel. Originally a temporary transformation for the 1962 Seattle World's Fair, the bar proved so popular with patrons that it never reverted — peanut shells still litter the floor and guests are invited to add their own mementos to the walls. It operates as one of several distinct venues within the large Strathcona Hotel entertainment complex in the heart of downtown Victoria.
69949cb255: Yum Yum Tree is a casual Chinese-Canadian restaurant in Kelowna that has built a strong local reputation (4.6 stars from nearly 400 Google reviews) for its MSG-free cooking, fresh ingredients, and generous portions. The menu spans appetizers, soups, fried rice, chop suey, chow mein, and a range of chicken, pork, beef, and seafood dishes. It operates primarily as a takeout and pick-up counter, making it a practical quick-stop for hungry cyclists passing through the Gordon Drive corridor.
5913d102ca: Regard Coffee Roasters is a specialty coffee roaster with a physical retail location in north Nanaimo at Metral Drive. The business sells whole-bean coffee, subscriptions, and merchandise both in-store and through its Shopify online store, and also offers wholesale supply. For touring cyclists passing through Nanaimo, it's a dedicated coffee stop with roaster-direct beans.
26994e5eea: Spitfire Grill is a family restaurant perched beside Victoria International Airport on the Saanich Peninsula, offering breakfast, lunch, and dinner with views of aircraft arriving and departing. The menu spans classic breakfasts, eggs benedicts, omelettes, salads, sandwiches, burgers, pasta, and curries, all freshly prepared. The website also promotes catering services, suggesting the kitchen handles volume orders beyond standard sit-down service.
a643f60fac: Hot House Pizza is a multi-location BC pizza chain with a Gordon Head outpost on Shelbourne Street in Victoria. The menu covers specialty, chicken, veggie, and classic pizzas in three sizes, with crust choices that include gluten-free and dairy-free options. Online ordering with cart checkout is available, making advance pickup straightforward for cyclists passing through the area.
56633bb6b6: Dachi is a refined farm-to-table neighbourhood restaurant on East Hastings Street, earning Platinum recognition at the Vancouver International Wine Festival for its curated selection of natural wines and craft sake. The menu rotates seasonally around local and organic ingredients, served in a warm dining room and a spacious outdoor patio that can accommodate groups up to 50 in summer. Cyclists finishing a ride through East Vancouver would find an upscale yet relaxed setting well suited to a celebratory dinner.
46511752ad: The Bread Quarter is a neighbourhood artisan bakery in North Vancouver with over 40 years of continuous operation, now in its fourth ownership by a local family committed to preserving its traditions. The bakery specialises in naturally fermented sourdough using a wild starter said to be over 50 years old, alongside Persian Barbari flatbread, rye breads, and scratch-made buns produced fresh daily without preservatives. Touring cyclists passing through the Lower Lonsdale area can stock up on dense, calorie-rich breads and pastries well-suited to long days in the saddle.
ff36e43626: Dad's Homemade Soups & Sangy's is a long-established Langford institution, open since 2003 and a two-time winner of the Times Colonist 'Best of the Island' Award for Best Fast Food Restaurant (2022 and 2023). The menu rotates daily homemade soups made from scratch using fresh, MSG-free and preservative-free ingredients, paired with made-to-order sandwiches on house-baked breads. The shop has a notable community ethos, providing hot lunches to over 15 schools across Greater Victoria.
558bee3e37: Islands Cafe is a Hawaiian surf-culture-inspired coffee roaster and café chain that started as a surfboard company before pivoting to espresso drinks and sandwiches. The company roasts its own green-bean coffee on-site and operates multiple lower-mainland locations, with this node corresponding to the Grandview Corners (Mauka) branch. Touring cyclists will find outdoor seating and a laid-back island atmosphere well-suited to a rest stop on routes through the South Surrey–Tsawwassen corridor.
17a27c4eb9: Tian Shi Fu (田师傅湘菜) is a Chinese restaurant on Richmond's busy Number 3 Road corridor, specializing in Hunan cuisine. The business is set up for online ordering and takeout, as reflected in the 'togo' domain and prominent 'Order Online' prompts on its website. Its current operating status is uncertain based on available evidence.
7a5e7a13e4: Charisma Social Club House is a long-standing family-run cafe in Vancouver's Chinatown, celebrated for housemade soups, award-winning cheesecakes, and boutique bubble teas served late into the evening. The spacious venue doubles as a vibrant community hub, hosting regular language exchanges, creative workshops, paint-and-sip nights, and chef-led pop-ups throughout the week. Its central Chinatown location makes it a lively and welcoming stop for cyclists exploring the downtown core.
c4447fb01b: Discovery Coffee is a locally owned specialty coffee roaster and cafe headquartered in Victoria, BC, roasting all of its beans in-house and offering house blends alongside single-origin lots from Peru and Rwanda. The brand has grown to operate multiple cafe locations in the city and partners with Yonni's Doughnuts for baked goods. Cyclists stopping in will find a craft-focused espresso bar with an accompanying online retail operation for beans and brewing gear.
b931176128: Fatburger is a Canadian-owned fast food burger chain founded in 1947 by Lovie Yancey in Los Angeles, with its first Canadian location opening in Vancouver in 2005. The Kelowna outlet on Harvey Avenue serves made-to-order burgers using fresh, never-frozen Alberta Angus beef alongside chicken sandwiches, wings, milkshakes, and plant-based options. It is a convenient quick-stop for cyclists travelling along Harvey Avenue (Highway 97).
17837840e9: The New Frontier Bar & Grill is a bar and grill in central Fort St. John. It serves as a casual dining stop for touring cyclists seeking food and refreshment during their travels through northern British Columbia.
19820d526a: Jejudo is a Korean and seafood restaurant located on the second level of a commercial building in North Vancouver, named after Jeju Island, the South Korean island renowned for its seafood. The restaurant's OSM record indicates a dine-in establishment, but no further detail about the dining experience, menu, or atmosphere is verifiable from available sources.
6e7eae0042: Caffè Soccavo is an Italian-style neighbourhood café on Vancouver's vibrant Commercial Drive, serving espresso, wood-fired paninos, and Neapolitan-style pizzas in a casual, soccer-watching atmosphere. The café leans into its 'Little Italy' identity with charcuterie, antipasto, and an aperitivo-hour tradition, making it a social stop rather than a grab-and-go. For touring cyclists on the Commercial Drive corridor, it offers a full sit-down meal or a quick takeout option.
ad74a0ce21: Mumu Kitchen is a Korean restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver offering indoor seating in a smoke-free environment. No outdoor seating is available.
287d895cab: Jade Valley is an established Cantonese-style Chinese restaurant located inside Impact Plaza in Surrey, serving a broad menu of seafood, hot pot, and classic Chinese-Canadian dishes. The restaurant's Hot & Sour Soup earned first place at the 2007 Soup-Off competition. It operates as a full sit-down restaurant with delivery available for nearby orders.
f03db3429e: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, founded in 1928, and a beloved regional institution known for fresh locally-sourced ingredients including Canadian beef and BC chicken. The Mission location offers dine-in with a patio, takeout, and delivery options, making it a reliable full-service meal stop in the Fraser Valley. Touring cyclists passing through Mission will find a familiar, sit-down dining option with a broad menu and a well-established brand presence.
7d8ba33fc6: Irori Sushi is a dedicated sushi restaurant on Vancouver's West 4th Avenue. It provides a sit-down dining option for touring cyclists looking for a prepared meal in the area. No cyclist-specific amenities could be verified from available information.
d370cd9d88: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, founded in 1928, serving family-style breakfast, lunch, and dinner with a menu built around locally sourced ingredients including Canadian beef and BC chicken. The Abbotsford location on South Fraser Way is a standalone dine-in restaurant with curbside pickup and multiple delivery options. Touring cyclists will find a reliably accessible full-service meal stop with wheelchair-accessible entry on a major arterial route through the Fraser Valley.
419d2a10db: Babylon Cafe is a long-established Middle Eastern restaurant on Denman Street serving shawerma, falafel, wraps, and combination plates made with fresh daily-prepped vegetables, house-made sauces, and marinated meats. The restaurant traces its roots to a beloved hole-in-the-wall on Robson Street that opened in 2004 and built a loyal following entirely by word of mouth. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the menu carries strong vegetarian options across both Vancouver locations.
63806dea4f: Nook is an Italian restaurant on Yew Street in Vancouver offering dine-in service. The establishment has no outdoor seating.
4ea2e214d7: The Bao Place is a Chinese restaurant on Edmonds Street specializing in bao, the pillowy steamed or baked buns popular across Chinese cuisine. Situated in the Edmonds neighbourhood, it offers indoor seating for cyclists looking to rest and refuel after a ride. Its cuisine focus makes it a distinctive stop among the more generic dining options along this corridor.
35dc705666: Cake It Easy is a family-owned boutique specializing in Filipino-inspired desserts, particularly ube-flavored cakes, sans rival, and bubble teas. The New Westminster location sits inside the Shops at New West mall at SkyTrain concourse level, making it a convenient stop for cyclists arriving by transit or passing through downtown New Westminster. Signature offerings include the Ube Flan Cake and Ube Rival Cake, with several gluten-free options available.
4bea02121e: 350 Bakehouse and Cafe is a scratch bakery and espresso café in Kelowna founded in 2017 by a fifth-generation Dutch baker. Everything on the menu is made fresh daily in-house, from classic glazed donuts and croissants to savoury cruffins and sausage rolls. Cyclists will find a full espresso bar, grab-and-go deli sandwiches, and daily hot lunch specials — plus catering available for larger groups.
273c74a19d: Alexander's Coffee (also listed as Alexander's Coffee Bar) is a compact café on Beacon Avenue in Sidney's town centre. Customer reviews highlight a surprisingly substantial menu for its size, with specialty drinks like a Mexican Mocha made with almond, chocolate, and cinnamon. Reviewers describe it as a cozy, local atmosphere with generous portions.
797ebc67a3: Uli's Restaurant has anchored the White Rock waterfront strip for over 30 years, founded by Ulrich (Uli) Blume and now run by his son Tyson. The kitchen follows genuine farm-to-table principles, sourcing seasonally from neighbouring BC farms and vendors and rotating the menu accordingly. Its location on Marine Drive — a popular coastal cycling corridor through South Surrey and White Rock — puts it directly on many touring riders' routes.
3e77d3227c: Tokyo Joe's Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Richmond offering an extensive menu spanning sushi rolls, sashimi, nigiri, udon, teriyaki, and donburi. The restaurant supports online ordering with quick pickup, making it a practical food stop for cyclists passing through the Richmond area. A dedicated vegetarian rolls section and party tray options round out a menu broad enough to suit most touring appetites.
f79985c27e: Mon Paris Patisserie is an artisan French bakery and café founded by Chef Elena Krasnova, who trained at the Ferrandie Ecole de Gastronomie in Paris. The Burnaby location in the Metrotown area offers handcrafted croissants, macarons, chocolates, custom cakes, and a café menu of espresso drinks. Cyclists can stop in for freshly made pastries, croissant sandwiches, and quality coffee in a small café setting.
d4ae98b758: Slim's BBQ operates as a barbecue restaurant on Main Street in Vancouver. Details about its offerings and cyclist facilities are not available through accessible sources.
c31a8062c5: Cafe Loyal is a restaurant located in Richmond on Bridgeport Road. Limited details are available due to website access limitations.
f48749eba3: Fusion Express is an Indian cuisine restaurant operated by the Students' Union Okanagan on the first floor of the University Centre Building at UBC Okanagan. It is one of several campus eateries run by the SUO, making it a convenient food stop for cyclists passing through or arriving at the university campus. The restaurant sits within the UNC building, a central hub of the UBCO campus in Kelowna.
7d96f83013: C|Prime is an upscale Italian restaurant and steakhouse situated just below the Century Plaza Hotel in downtown Vancouver, offering handmade pastas, prime-cut steaks, fresh seafood, and an extensive wine program spanning B.C. and international labels. Executive Chef Behshad Zolnasr trained at Michelin-starred kitchens in Rome, London, and New York before bringing that experience to Vancouver. The restaurant serves from breakfast through a late-night bar, making it a full-day dining option for cyclists passing through the Burrard Street corridor.
449f28218c: Hi Dozo Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in New Westminster offering a wide menu of sushi rolls, nigiri, sashimi, udon, teriyaki, and appetizers. The restaurant has indoor seating and caters to groups with party tray options. Online ordering is temporarily suspended, but in-store and phone orders are accepted.
62fa6aa61c: Van Bahn Mi & Yoghurt is a Vietnamese fast-food spot in Vancouver's Pacific Street area specializing in bánh mì sandwiches across a wide range of fillings — from lemongrass grilled chicken to a fully vegan tofu-and-avocado option — alongside house-made yogurt cups and smoothies. The menu is compact and takeout-oriented, making it a quick, affordable refuelling stop. Online ordering is available through multiple delivery platforms for those who want food ready on arrival.
b411d95219: DQ Grill & Chill is a full-service Dairy Queen location on Hillside Avenue in Victoria, offering burgers, chicken, and ice cream alongside the classic soft-serve treats the brand is known for. As a sit-down fast-food restaurant rather than a kiosk, it provides a reliable stop for a hot meal or cold treat mid-ride. It sits in a busy commercial corridor making it easy to find on a cycling route through the city.
52ebfedafc: A single-location Nanaimo pizza and pasta restaurant in business since 1997, situated on Metral Drive in the north end of the city. The kitchen describes itself as doing 'more than just Pizza & Pasta' and offers citywide delivery alongside in-store pickup. A reliable sit-down or takeout option for touring cyclists passing through Nanaimo's north side.
4a696b6b4c: Subway is a fast-food sandwich franchise offering quick meals and takeaway service. Located on Island Highway in the Victoria area, it provides a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists in the region.
e835c0e171: Bright Jenny Coffee is a Kelowna specialty coffee roaster that runs a café alongside its online bean-subscription business, sourcing single-origin coffees from Brazil, Ethiopia, Colombia, and Guatemala. The café has a food menu in addition to espresso drinks, and mobile ordering lets customers order ahead and have their drink ready on arrival. It is an independent local roaster with a wholesale program and a distinctly hands-on, small-team character.
363512972e: Happy Hong Kong Cafe is a nostalgic Hong Kong-style Cha Chaan Teng located inside the Abercorn Inn in Richmond, BC, evoking the bustling retro cafe culture of 1990s Hong Kong with vintage-inspired decor. The menu spans classic Cantonese comfort dishes — from Baked Pork Chop with Tomato Sauce on Rice and Hainanese Chicken Laksa to congee and Hong Kong French Toast — blending East-meets-West techniques across a broad, eclectic offering. Touring cyclists stopping near Richmond's Bridgeport corridor will find a full sit-down meal with both dine-in and pickup options in a hotel-hosted setting.
71c50c2f00: Barbara is a small, intimate reservation-only restaurant on East Pender Street in Vancouver, serving a creative tasting menu in a space limited to parties of four. The kitchen highlights Pacific Northwest ingredients — spot prawns, arctic char, duck hearts, seasonal vegetables — in a multi-course format. Walk-ins are welcomed at two standing tables for cocktails or wine, and the restaurant offers an inventive zero-proof drinks programme alongside its full bar.
b923867786: A Mexican restaurant in Stewart, BC, operated under the name El Tostador (formerly Toastworks). The restaurant offers outdoor seating and accommodates large vehicles. Washroom facilities are available on site.
e56a45a6f1: Hello Nori is a Japanese hand roll bar specializing in Temaki made to order with crispy premium nori, warm seasoned rice, and Ocean Wise-certified sustainable seafood sourced from local Vancouver suppliers. The Robson Street location features a Japanese-inspired interior with sake served in cedar 'Masu' boxes beneath cascading wooden wave ceiling installations. A dedicated to-go menu and delivery partnerships via Uber Eats and DoorDash make it a practical quick-stop for cyclists who want quality Japanese cuisine without a long sit-down.
fb2ed6b0ea: Penguin Ice Cream is a lively dessert and quick-service food shop on Wellington Avenue in Chilliwack, serving premium slow-churned ice cream and Italian-style gelato in an extensive lineup of flavours. Beyond frozen treats, the menu spans hand-spun shakes, smoothies, burgers, poutine, and Indian-inspired sides like samosa, spring rolls, and gulab jamun with ice cream. It makes for a satisfying and eclectic mid-ride stop for cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley.
6e40c1f7b3: Adriana's The Whole Enchilada is a Mexican deli and restaurant in Saanichton with over 25 years of history, run by Adriana Ramírez and Wayne Adams. It is described as Vancouver Island's sole large-scale producer of corn tortillas, supplying numerous Victoria-area restaurants and retail stores. Cyclists stopping by can order takeout from a rotating weekly lunch menu of tacos, burritos, enchiladas, and taquitos, with both corn (gluten-free) and wheat menus available.
23d505ee1b: Di Reggae Cafe is a Jamaican restaurant in Surrey serving traditional dishes like curry goat, jerk chicken, jerk pork, and flaky Jamaican beef patties using recipes passed down through generations. The kitchen emphasizes authentic preparation — meats are marinated for 24 hours in traditional spices and curries are slow-cooked with Caribbean seasonings. A welcoming community-focused spot on King George Boulevard, it offers both dine-in and online ordering for pickup or delivery.
e58c09c005: Glorious Bao & Fried Rice is a food-court Taiwanese restaurant founded in 2019 by alumni of a Michelin-starred kitchen, specializing in handmade soup dumplings, gua bao, and wok-fried rice dishes made to order. Located on the second floor of a Burnaby mall, it has earned a loyal following for delivering restaurant-quality food at food-court prices. A touring cyclist looking for a quick, substantial hot meal will find generous portions and a frequently praised egg fried rice.
5e6cb84637: Cedarbrook Bakery & Deli is a neighbourhood bakery and deli in Langley, BC, baking fresh bread, cheese buns, donuts, and other goods in-store daily. The deli counter carries a wide selection of cured meats and cheeses, and the shop also offers gluten-free baked goods for cyclists with dietary restrictions. Customer reviews highlight friendly staff and high-quality food, making it a welcoming stop on a ride through the Langley area.
3168301696: McDonald's is a globally recognized fast food chain serving burgers, chicken sandwiches, fries, breakfast items, and McCafé beverages. This North Vancouver location includes a drive-through and takeout service. It is a reliable stop for touring cyclists needing a quick, widely available meal in an urban area.
518bbb04c0: Blenz Coffee is a BC-born specialty coffee chain founded in 1992, serving hand-crafted espresso drinks, organic whole-leaf teas, protein shakes, and a food menu of sandwiches, wraps, baked goods, and more at this Fort St. John location. The brand emphasizes premium ingredients — 100% Arabica beans, single-origin chocolate, and ceremonial-grade matcha — and offers takeout and mobile ordering through its app. For cyclists heading through Fort St. John, it is a convenient in-town stop for hot or cold beverages and a snack.
6632a8faac: MAD Chicken is a takeout stall in Simon Fraser University's MBC Food Court on the Burnaby campus, serving an American-Asian fusion menu of crispy fried chicken, ramen, beef noodle soup, and dumplings. As part of SFU's campus food program, it sits within a large university building with full campus amenities nearby. A touring cyclist ascending Burnaby Mountain would find it a convenient hot-meal stop during the week.
dafb3bd7fc: Apna Chaat House specialises in Indian street food, offering dishes like Golgappas, Vada Pav, Bhel Puri, Samosa Chaat, Pav Bhaji, and Kathi Rolls under one roof. Founded by Komal Shaikh, whose past ventures include Cafe Bombay and Bombay Se, it bills itself as Surrey's go-to spot for authentic regional Indian street cuisine. A touring cyclist looking for a quick, flavourful, and affordable meal in the Surrey area would find a wide variety of street-food classics here.
7f8a8554cb: Red Wasabi is a quick-service sushi spot on Davie Street in Vancouver, specializing in 100% gluten-free inari, fresh rolls, and rice bowls prepared daily from locally sourced ingredients. The restaurant emphasizes plant-based options and sustainable sourcing, making it a health-conscious stop for cyclists. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and online ordering for pickup and delivery is offered.
97a89610b9: Founded in 1974 by Spanish-born Valentine Aguirre, Old Surrey Restaurant is a long-established French fine dining landmark in Surrey's Fraser Valley, sourcing lamb and veal from the family's own Chilliwack farm. The restaurant is known for tableside theatrical service including flambéed desserts and Caesar salads prepared at the table. It also partners with Surrey Civic Theatres, making it a destination for an evening cultural outing that a touring cyclist might plan ahead for.
be088a81c9: Pizazz Pizza is a family-owned Victoria institution that has been serving the community since 1998, offering a broad menu of pizzas, pasta, wings, and salads. The restaurant actively accommodates dietary restrictions with gluten-free crust, whole wheat options, and vegan alternatives. Both takeout and delivery are available, making it a practical refueling stop for cyclists in the Wilkinson Road area of Saanich.
c41a44898d: La Pache Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain serving authentic Neapolitan-style pies with fresh dough made from scratch daily at their Commercial Drive location. The menu spans meat, vegetable, and vegan options, with online ordering available. Commercial Drive is one of Vancouver's most-used cycling corridors, placing this spot directly on route for cyclists crossing through East Vancouver.
70d20d3f1c: Tony's Fish & Oyster Café has been a fixture at the entrance of Granville Island since 2002, earning recognition as one of Vancouver's Top 20 Seafood Restaurants and multiple TripAdvisor Certificates of Excellence. The restaurant specializes in battered fish and chips made with wild sockeye salmon, Pacific cod, and Atlantic haddock, alongside house-made clam chowder and a signature banana flambé. It's a walk-in, first-come-first-served spot well-positioned on the cycling routes that converge at Granville Island.
d951b87aba: Ridge Garden is a Chinese restaurant in Vancouver's Arbutus Ridge neighbourhood, situated near the ICBC office on Macdonald Street. The restaurant offers dine-in service and has recently reopened its dining room, making it a sit-down meal option for cyclists moving through this quieter residential corridor of the city.
bfefc156de: Washington Avenue Grill is a long-standing White Rock landmark with over 28 years of operation, serving upscale casual Pacific-Northwest cuisine from a dining room overlooking Semiahmoo Bay at the east end of White Rock Beach. The restaurant features an award-winning wine list, weekly live music, and has been recognized as one of Canada's top 100 scenic restaurants. Its location on Marine Drive places it directly on a popular waterfront cycling corridor.
272968a94b: Otreat is a Korean-influenced brunch cafe tucked into a commercial complex in Langley, serving a creative menu of coffee drinks, mimosa flights, mocktails, and hearty brunch plates alongside dishes like Gochujang Bulgogi wings and chicken benny. The menu is updated regularly and the waitlist feature on the site signals a popular local destination. A touring cyclist stopping here can expect a full sit-down brunch experience with both alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverage options.
8f8ef18034: Butchers Block BBQ is a family-owned backyard-style barbecue restaurant in Burnaby Heights, slow-smoking beef brisket, pulled pork, ribs, pork belly, and sausages daily with house-made rubs and sauces. Operating since 2005, it has earned recognition including Vancouver Magazine's 'Best Barbecue' award and multiple 'Best of Burnaby' honours. Cyclists on the Hastings Street corridor can fuel up with generous platters or grab takeout via phone or online order.
95d6d6b2ba: Mogiana Coffee is a family-heritage specialty coffee roaster founded in 2008 by Cristina Dias, sourcing beans directly from her family's farm in the Mogiana region of Brazil — a tradition spanning five generations since the 1890s. The Burnaby roastery sells small-batch, roasted-to-order beans direct to the public and operates a regular circuit of Vancouver-area farmers markets. Cyclists can purchase whole-bean coffee on-site at the roastery, though calling ahead is recommended to ensure staff are available.
ea2c45b262: Sunday Cider is a craft cidery and cider bar on a 20-acre property along the Sunshine Coast Highway near Gibsons, producing small-batch ciders from 100% fresh-pressed BC apples with no added yeast, filtration, or additives. Cyclists can settle into the outdoor picnic area with cider flights, resident food trucks (Sea Monkey Coffee and Casa Beto Tacos), and regular live music on the grass. Dogs and kids on leashes are explicitly welcome, making it a relaxed stop on the Sunshine Coast route.
3e797ff642: Bow & Stern is a family-owned, ocean-inspired seafood restaurant founded in 2014 by the Smith family, rooted in a fish-and-chips recipe the founders have been perfecting since 1988. The Abbotsford location on Montrose Ave is the original of three Fraser Valley and Lower Mainland outposts, offering a full sit-down menu of fish, chips, oysters, and ale alongside brunch, happy hour, and dessert menus. Cyclists passing through the Abbotsford area will find online pickup ordering available as well as table reservations.
2df214435c: Aiyaohno Cafe is a Japanese-inspired cafe in Vancouver's Chinatown, run by a husband and wife team who draw from countryside café experiences gathered during travels through Japan. The kitchen focuses on vegetable-forward cuisine with many vegan options and some local wild seafood, paired with matcha imported directly from Kyoto. The space doubles as a small retail hub for pottery, merch, and curated fashion, making it a distinctive neighbourhood stop.
0904ea29c9: Canada's first purpose-built gastro brewpub, Spinnakers has been crafting its own ales and pairing them with farm-to-table cuisine since 1984, drawing on partnerships with over 35 local Vancouver Island producers. Perched on Victoria's Vic West waterfront with views of the Inner Harbour, the site combines a full-service restaurant, taproom, provisions store with growler fills, and heritage guesthouses in a single destination. Cyclists can linger over a range of house-brewed craft beers and seasonal pub fare on a covered heated patio.
88043431df: Granville Kebab & Poutine is a Middle Eastern and Mediterranean restaurant on Vancouver's busy Granville Street, blending classic Canadian poutine with grilled beef and chicken kebabs in platters, wraps, and loaded poutine bowls. The fusion concept is a notable curiosity — baklava and kebab skewers share a menu with fries and gravy. Online ordering with a quick pickup window makes it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists moving through the downtown entertainment district.
7f3c211038: Kojima Sushi is a sushi restaurant on Commercial Drive in Vancouver, serving a broad menu of rolls, sashimi, nigiri, oshi sushi, bento combos, and Japanese appetizers. The restaurant is noted for its Salmon Oshi Sushi and creative specialty rolls, and handles a high volume of online orders. Both dine-in and pickup are available through the Zomi platform.
969a735281: A standard Taco Bell franchise location in Delta, BC serving Tex-Mex fast food including tacos, burritos, and the Crunchwrap Supreme. The restaurant offers both dine-in and drive-thru service, as well as online ordering and delivery. It is one of several Taco Bell locations in the Metro Vancouver area.
b9e7fff706: Nyonya House is a Malaysian restaurant in Richmond's Steveston area serving a broad menu of Southeast Asian classics including Hainanese Chicken Rice, Curry Laksa, Rendang Beef, Roti Canai, and Satay. The restaurant operates an online ordering system with over 56 menu items spanning appetizers, noodles, rice dishes, and desserts. It is a sit-down restaurant that also supports takeout orders, making it a convenient stop for cyclists exploring the Steveston waterfront area.
ab3bb50a65: LURE Restaurant & Bar occupies a prime position on Victoria's Inner Harbour, serving a West Coast seasonal menu built around local seafood, Vancouver Island produce, and craft cocktails made with local spirits. The venue offers both indoor dining and an outdoor waterfront patio with panoramic harbour views, and hosts live music on Friday evenings. It draws a broad mix of locals and visitors, making it a natural destination for touring cyclists arriving at or departing from Victoria's waterfront.
caa037985f: Cuckoo Trattoria & Pizzeria is a full-service Italian restaurant in the small Vancouver Island town of Coombs, led by Italian-born Head Chef Fausto Bellicini who blends traditional Italian technique with local west coast ingredients such as wild-caught salmon, locally sourced mussels, and foraged mushrooms. Wood-fired oven pizza is a centrepiece of the menu, and a forest-facing patio is open through the summer season. Situated on the Alberni Highway, it also functions as an events venue for weddings and larger gatherings.
886389cfb3: Pizza Garden is a BC-based Neapolitan pizza chain with over 25 years in the industry, serving wood-fired pizzas with authentic charred crusts, san marzano-style tomatoes, and creamy mozzarella. The Abbotsford location at Trethewey Street is one of more than a dozen locations across British Columbia. Cyclists can order ahead via the Pizza Garden app and choose pickup or delivery.
1ccd2cb17b: Shipyards Coffee is an independent coffee bar tucked into the Shipyards District at Lonsdale Quay in North Vancouver, proudly serving the waterfront community for over 15 years. The café offers a full espresso bar, freshly baked croissants and pastries, smoothies, and a rotating selection of specialty single-origin and blended coffee beans. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a welcoming stop along the North Shore waterfront cycling corridor.
6cf8c512ad: King Kabob is a halal Persian grill restaurant on South Fraser Way in Abbotsford, billing itself as the first dedicated kabob house in the Fraser Valley. The menu centres on flame-broiled kebabs marinated with saffron, dried limes, and traditional Middle Eastern spices, served with basmati rice. The restaurant holds BCMA halal certification and offers both dine-in and online pickup/delivery ordering.
a98e79cd35: Domino's is a national pizza chain franchise offering delivery and carryout from its Nanaimo location on Norwell Drive. The menu covers pizza, wings, pasta, cheesy bread, and desserts, with a gluten-free crust option available. As a takeout-and-delivery-focused operation, it provides no dine-in seating or dedicated cyclist facilities.
668350c2b9: A full-service lakefront resort and Italian restaurant on Highway 24 (The Fishing Highway) near Lone Butte, BC, open year-round and set on 47 acres beside one of British Columbia's most photographed lakes. The Italian restaurant features northern Italian chefs preparing fresh entrees daily, offering a distinctive sit-down dining option along this rural cycling corridor. The resort is widely known among anglers for trophy Gerrard Rainbow trout fishing, and the surrounding area provides access to over 100 lakes within an hour's drive.
451d1a31e5: Bella Gelateria is an internationally award-winning artisan gelato maker founded in Vancouver in 2010, recognized at competitions in Italy, Chicago, and Austin, and ranked No. 1 in the Gelato World rankings. The Metrotown Mall location is one of five Greater Vancouver outposts serving handcrafted small-batch gelato made from 100% natural ingredients using Italian Effi machines. Cyclists looking for a sweet mid-ride treat will find a broad menu including dairy-free, gluten-free, and vegan sorbetto options.
d26cd5d941: An Indian restaurant specializing in dosas in Richmond. Offers vegetarian and vegan menu options. A casual dining stop for touring cyclists seeking quality Indian cuisine.
f020b31459: New Mandarin Seafood Restaurant (時代文華海鮮酒家) is a Cantonese seafood and dim sum restaurant located in East Vancouver's Gladstone neighbourhood. The kitchen leans heavily on traditional Hong Kong-style preparations — roasted and hotpot squab, fresh BC crab, whole lobster combos, and a daily dim sum service — earning a local reputation cited on the restaurant's own site. Online ordering and pickup are available, making it a practical meal stop as well as a sit-down destination.
cfe41fcb74: Master Rice Roll (腸粉大王) is a Chinese specialty restaurant in Richmond focused on cheung fun (rice rolls) and congee, offering more than 20 varieties of rice roll alone. Located in a retail unit on Number 3 Road, it also serves a range of snacks and drinks. Cyclists passing through Richmond's busy commercial corridor will find it a practical stop for a quick, filling Cantonese meal.
97e5e2cc82: Orange Julius is a juice beverage chain with a Vancouver location offering fresh juices and casual refreshment. Located in a mall basement, it provides indoor seating and takeout service. A convenient stop for cyclists seeking a quick drink while touring the area.
74095fc354: Cioffi's Cucina is the scratch-made kitchen arm of Cioffi's Italian Meat Market & Deli, a family-run Burnaby institution operating for over 25 years. Award-winning chef Jason Symington turns out daily hot specials, housemade panini, fresh pasta, and baked goods drawing directly from the adjacent deli and meat counter. A touring cyclist can grab anything from a quick Lavazza espresso to a full cold-pack of lasagna, arancini, or roasted chicken to go.
bcce5d5931: Ajuker Fried Chicken is a Korean and fried chicken restaurant in North Vancouver with indoor seating. It offers casual dining as a meal option for touring cyclists passing through the area.
b70d532180: Mayuri Indian Cuisine is a family-run, fully vegetarian restaurant in Surrey specializing in South Indian cooking, with dosas as its centrepiece alongside pakoras, rice dishes, and vegetable entrees made from scratch using traditional spice blends. The restaurant has a family-focused dining room atmosphere and also offers off-site catering for parties and functions. It has received recognition on Restaurant Guru and draws a loyal local following for its authentic regional Indian flavours.
5b802efaca: The Break is a scratch-kitchen café and bakery in the heart of Ucluelet, known for house-smoked meats, fermented vegetables, fresh-baked sourdough and bagels, and made-to-order brunch sandwiches. Everything from pastry fillings to sandwich sauces is prepared in-house using fresh, seasonal, and locally sourced ingredients. Touring cyclists stopping in Ucluelet will find a quality sit-down food stop with a strong local reputation.
59153dcc8b: Cook & Pan is a Polish delicatessen and cafe established in 1996, now operating out of a restored heritage house in downtown Victoria. It combines an imported-goods deli, a fresh-sausage and cold-cuts counter, an espresso bar, and a kitchen turning out traditional dishes like pierogi, cabbage rolls, and bigos. A dedicated frozen take-home menu and an upstairs event space make it a distinctive stop for cyclists wanting a substantial, home-style Polish meal.
d0566576d3: Food Folk Eatery is a food court venue inside McArthurGlen Designer Outlet Vancouver, a large open-air outlet mall directly across from the SkyTrain Canada Line's Templeton Station in Richmond. The centre sits only two stops from Vancouver International Airport and about 20 minutes from downtown Vancouver, placing it on a heavily trafficked cycling corridor near the Sea Island routes. Outdoor seating is available at the eatery, and the surrounding centre offers a variety of quick-service food vendors including Cha House, JAPADOG, and A&W.
f70b7be200: Bulalohan Sa Ilocos is a Filipino restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver serving authentic cuisine from the Ilocos region. It offers a casual dining stop for cyclists seeking local flavors while touring the area.
1f0f710bfd: Obanhmi is a BC-grown Vietnamese sandwich chain specializing in bánh mì, fresh spring rolls, and iced coffee, now serving nine locations across the Lower Mainland. The menu spans classic French-influenced cold-cut sandwiches to halal chicken and fully vegan options, all built on freshly toasted baguettes with house-made ingredients. Cyclists passing through Coquitlam's North Road corridor will find quick, customizable, and filling meals available for in-store pickup or delivery.
a3dd97340f: Peaceful Restaurant is an award-winning Northern Chinese restaurant that has been serving Metro Vancouver since 1998, recognized by Food Network and USA Today for its hand-pulled noodles, beef rolls, and dumplings. Executive chef and owner Charlie Huang draws on the spice-laden culinary traditions of Xi'an and the Silk Road, offering a menu spanning artisanal dim sum to noodle creations. A touring cyclist would find a full sit-down meal with vegetarian options available.
6c35449678: The Yoga Chef is a chef-led artisan catering company based in Port Coquitlam, serving corporate, wedding, private, and film productions across Metro Vancouver and the Sea to Sky corridor. The business emphasizes seasonal, locally sourced ingredients and visually considered menus. With over 300 Google reviews, it is an established presence in the Lower Mainland catering scene.
bedc617881: Mucho Burrito is a Canadian fast-casual chain serving Mexican-inspired food with what the brand calls a 'Modern Mexicana' twist, located in the Tuscany Village shopping centre on McKenzie Avenue in Saanich. The menu centres on burritos, bowls, quesadillas, and tacos, with online ordering and a punch-card loyalty program available. It is a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the McKenzie corridor in Victoria's eastern suburbs.
1aee6a776f: The Spud Shack Fry Co. is a Belgian-inspired frite and poutine counter tucked into the New Westminster SkyTrain station above Safeway, making it one of the more transit-accessible food stops in the Lower Mainland. The menu leans into creative poutines — from smoked meat to butter chicken to a full vegetarian chili version — alongside handmade burgers and a rotating selection of craft beers and sodas. It's a no-fuss, satisfying refuel spot with a distinctly local character.
50d7822c8c: Milk Jam Donuts is a small-batch artisan donut shop in downtown Nanaimo specializing in 24-hour-raised brioche donuts, filled cronuts, and house-made flavoured milks. Their glazes and fillings are crafted from real ingredients — fresh fruit, vanilla bean, organic cocoa — and coffee is brewed from locally roasted Drumroaster beans. Stock is limited and sells out regularly, so cyclists stopping by should check their @milkjamdonuts social feed before making a detour.
81eafdd9bf: Frankie's Modern Diner is a family-friendly sit-down restaurant on Victoria's Government Street serving breakfast through dinner daily, with a broad menu of house-made dishes built around fresh local ingredients including locally caught wild cod and salmon, craft beers from Hoyne, Phillips, and Driftwood, and breads from Irene's Bakery. The kitchen leans on from-scratch preparation — stuffed meatballs, house desserts, fresh-squeezed mimosas — and the diverse menu is designed so everyone at the table can find something. It has been voted Victoria's best for brunch, burgers, and value by Open Choice Diners.
24a64cd418: Flamez Chicken is a fried and flame-grilled chicken restaurant in the heart of Downtown Nanaimo, located at the corner of Wallace and Fitzwilliam streets. The menu spans signature fried chicken, grilled options, poutines, seafood, wraps, rice bowls, and house-made sauces, with catering available for groups. Positioned near the Harbourfront Walkway and ferry terminal, it sits in a convenient spot for cyclists exploring downtown Nanaimo.
8fef208ee9: Kelly's Kitchen Café is a breakfast-and-lunch spot in Nanaimo serving homemade all-day breakfast with a locally-flavoured menu — dishes are named after Nanaimo landmarks like Newcastle, Duke Point, Millstone, and Mount Benson. The menu leans heavily on classic egg preparations: bennys with fresh Hollandaise, omelettes, hashes, and griddle favourites, all served with homestyle hash browns. It's a filling sit-down stop for cyclists looking for a substantial meal before or after a ride.
2eabb67c64: Masala India Bistro is an Indian restaurant in Langley, BC. Status and specific details could not be verified due to website unavailability.
1e1ec234c3: Lee's Donuts is an iconic Vancouver-born donut chain founded in 1979 at the Granville Island Public Market, now with multiple Metro Vancouver locations including this Brentwood outpost. The shop is known for handmade, small-batch classic donuts using original recipes, with rotating seasonal flavours made fresh daily. A quick and reliable sugar stop for touring cyclists passing through Burnaby, with indoor seating and no drive-through.
f76318f5da: The Coffee Pitt is an independent community cafe in Pitt Meadows specializing in specialty espresso drinks, freshly baked goods, and made-to-order sandwiches using locally roasted beans. Beyond the daytime cafe menu, the shop offers a cocktail program featuring espresso martinis and aperol spritzes, and rents its venue for private events after closing. Cyclists riding the Pitt Meadows area trails and dyke routes will find vegan and gluten-free options alongside the signature cinnamon buns.
720b082837: Jordan Sushi is listed in OSM as a sushi restaurant, but its website now presents an entirely Korean menu — including Padak Chicken, Cheese Kimchi Rice, and Sweet Pig Trotters — under the tagline 'Enjoy the Authentic Taste of Korea in a Relaxed and Cozy Environment.' Online ordering is available through the site. The significant mismatch between the OSM address and the website address raises questions about whether the original business still operates at the listed location.
ee58ae2f56: Just Matcha is a specialty matcha tea shop founded in 2013 by Tiffanie and Kip Home, now operating from its second Victoria home on Pandora Avenue after its original Oak Bay Avenue location closed during the pandemic. The shop sources a curated range of premium Japanese matcha powders, traditional bowls, and accessories, built on years of hands-on sourcing expertise. Cyclists passing through downtown Victoria will find a focused specialist with deep matcha knowledge and an authentic product selection.
1193f50869: Hanwoori has been serving authentic Korean cuisine since 1997, earning 8 Gold Awards from Vancouver Magazine and three 'Best Korean Restaurant' titles from Burnaby Now — a remarkable record of sustained excellence. The menu spans Korean staples like shabu shabu, seafood pancake, and beef combos alongside cocktails such as their signature Pink Blossom. Its longevity and award history make it a well-known dining destination in the Burnaby area.
2a5a2d8036: Koffi is a neighbourhood coffee house that opened in 2007 in a converted laundromat at Haultain Corners, founded on a philosophy of serving only the highest-quality espresso in just two sizes. The café partners with local Victoria bakeries and makes paninis in-house, and features a rotating 22-by-12-foot art wall showcasing local artists. It also hosts events and provides catering, making it a genuine community hub in a quiet residential corner of Victoria.
8b18ace2db: Sushi Street is a Japanese takeout restaurant inside King George Hub at the King George SkyTrain Station in Surrey, offering a broad menu of sashimi, nigiri, rolls, bento boxes, tempura, teriyaki, and ready-to-eat foods. The transit-adjacent location and emphasis on quick, convenient service make it a practical stop for cyclists passing through the area. Online ordering and delivery through Skip the Dishes and Uber Eats are available, and catering services are offered for larger groups.
5c39fa814f: Cafe Log is a coffee and desserts café occupying a second-floor unit in North Vancouver, previously operating under the name Snowy Village. It offers indoor seating in a no-smoking environment and is noted as wheelchair accessible. Cyclists looking for a sweet stop in North Vancouver may find it a quiet, sheltered retreat for coffee and desserts.
93c6d74265: A Local Public Eatery in Vancouver.
841d8ce780: Villages Pizza is a regional pizza chain with deep roots in Victoria's neighbourhoods, operating under Sanderson & Louis Holdings. The Oak Bay Avenue location sits in a walkable, bikeable commercial strip and offers both delivery and in-store pickup. The chain supports school lunch programs and community catering, making it a practical stop for groups or solo touring cyclists passing through Oak Bay.
a9119bf23f: Osmanthus is a fine-dining Chinese restaurant on Level 2 of Aberdeen Centre in Richmond, specializing in Jiangnan cuisine with roots in the Song Dynasty. The restaurant has hosted a Michelin Chef's Night event and offers an extensive menu of crafted beverages alongside its food menu.
