Touring cyclists looking for an upscale sit-down meal in Richmond's busy Aberdeen Centre area will find this a distinctive cultural dining experience.
080d532705: House of Dosas on Davie Street is a South Indian restaurant specializing in dosas, biryanis, and spiced chicken dishes rooted in Chef Ganesh's authentic southern Indian recipes. It operates around the clock every day of the week, making it a rare all-hours dining option in Vancouver's West End. Cyclists passing through the Davie Village corridor will find a warm sit-down meal available at any hour.
951ecd43c4: Proud Up is a sit-down Canadian comfort food restaurant serving breakfast and dinner, formerly operating as The Taco Factory. The menu leans hearty — eggs Benedict variations, skillets, chicken and waffles — with a selection of vegetarian-friendly dishes. Located on East Columbia Street in New Westminster, it offers a relaxed neighbourhood dining experience for cyclists passing through.
cf0d9e2152: Blanshard St. Winery is a locally owned, family-operated craft winery that has been producing wines in Victoria since 1996, making it the longest-running winery in the city under its original owners. Spread across a 4,000 sq ft facility with state-of-the-art bottling equipment, it offers an extensive lineup spanning premium reds and whites, dessert wines, wine coolers, and ciders sourced from vineyards around the world. A touring cyclist interested in BC's craft beverage scene could visit to browse or purchase bottles, with wedding and custom-label wine services also available.
ac1a611234: Matteo's Gelato is a neighborhood Italian gelato shop on Mary Hill Road in Port Coquitlam, run by a passionate gelato maker who prepares small daily batches from traditional recipes using imported Italian ingredients. Beyond its signature gelato, the shop serves authentic espresso, specialty coffee drinks, fresh sandwiches, and artisanal chocolates, making it a full Italian cafe stop. The shop has earned strong local acclaim for flavor authenticity from reviewers with firsthand travel experience in Italy.
b523dcedd3: Newton Pizza is a local pizza chain with several locations across the Surrey and North Delta area of British Columbia, built on a reputation for fresh ingredients and house-perfected recipes. The Surrey/North Delta outlet on 128 Street serves the surrounding community with dine-in and online ordering. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find it a straightforward stop for a quick hot meal.
e56a22a8e8: Cocobay is a bubble tea café on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver specializing in bubble tea and vegetarian-friendly drinks. Located at street level in a busy urban corridor, it offers air-conditioned indoor seating — a welcome refuge on a hot ride. The downtown location puts it within easy reach of the Vancouver Seawall and other popular cycling routes.
eb86431673: Saigon Ivy is a Vietnamese restaurant in downtown New Westminster, an area well-suited to cycling stop-offs on the Central Valley Greenway and nearby routes. OSM records place its founding before 1948, making it one of the older eateries in the community. Indoor seating is noted in OSM tags, offering a sit-down meal option for cyclists passing through New Westminster.
cda29f4c91: Original Udder Guys is a scratch-made artisan ice cream parlour and retro candy shop on the Cowichan Bay waterfront, scooping from recipes perfected since 1999 and operating year-round under new ownership since 2023. The 24-flavour cabinet spans classics to inventive combinations alongside in-store fudge, imported British crisps and sweets, espresso drinks, milkshakes, and Slush Puppies. Cyclists can sit outside at picnic tables with a view of the bay or settle into indoor booths after a ride through the Cowichan Valley.
1ddc87652f: A pizza restaurant in Christina Lake serving the local community and passing travelers.
e40d9379da: Sushi 2 Go is a fast-food sushi spot located on or near Salt Spring Island, BC, suggested by the Instagram handle 'sushi2go_ssi'. It offers a quick sushi option for cyclists exploring the Gulf Islands. The recent OSM check date of March 2026 indicates the business was active as of that visit.
b77b83e070: Caffe Motivo is a downtown Kamloops café situated on Victoria Street in the city core, specializing in fresh-baked goods and coffee sourced from JJ Bean roasters. It also offers light lunches and breakfasts prepared in-house daily, making it a solid resupply stop for cyclists rolling through the Thompson Valley. Catering is available for groups with advance notice.
13ea620238: Pho Goodness is a Vietnamese comfort food restaurant established in 2011 in Vancouver's West End, serving pho, banh mi, rice dishes, and vermicelli bowls with a focus on home-style cooking. The Davie Street location has been a neighbourhood staple for over a decade, earning Westender Magazine's Best Vietnamese and Best Pho awards in 2012, 2016, and 2017. Online ordering with pickup is available, making it a quick and convenient stop for cyclists passing through the West End.
7f81a2386d: Neptune Wonton Noodle is a fast-casual Chinese noodle restaurant in Richmond operated by the Neptune Restaurant Group, a Greater Vancouver hospitality company established in 1997. The group's sister brand, Neptune Seafood Restaurant, holds membership in the Commanderie des Cordons Bleu de France and has won Vancouver's Top Ten Chinese Restaurant Award, reflecting the culinary pedigree behind the brand. For touring cyclists, it offers a quick, filling Chinese noodle meal with convenient takeout and delivery options in the heart of Richmond.
77ba4a937f: Miku pioneered Aburi (flame-seared) sushi in Canada when it opened in Vancouver in 2008 and has earned Michelin Guide recognition and the Wine Spectator Award of Excellence. The waterfront location at Granville Square features a full bar and lounge, a patio overlooking the harbour, a private dining room, and a full-service sushi bar showcasing Ocean Wise seafood and regional west coast ingredients. A touring cyclist arriving along the seawall would find a distinctive upscale dining experience blending traditional Japanese technique with local flavours.
ac5c63ca01: Smitty's is a Canadian-owned casual dining chain operating since 1960, with this Parksville location sitting on the East Island Highway — a key corridor for cyclists touring Vancouver Island. The menu centres on all-day breakfast, pancakes, and burgers, positioning it as a substantial meal stop for riders needing to refuel. As part of a well-established national chain, the restaurant offers a predictable, family-friendly dining experience.
a0e86c87ce: Yook Korean Grilled BBQ and Bistro is a sit-down Korean BBQ restaurant on Nanaimo Street in East Vancouver, where guests grill premium meats at the table alongside traditional Korean dishes. The head chef brings over 30 years of experience from home-style Korean restaurants in both South Korea and Canada, and the kitchen produces all banchan in-house. It offers a substantial, warm meal stop well-suited to hungry cyclists finishing a longer urban or cross-town ride.
9e51558e8e: El Dorado Pie & Treats is a family-run bakery operating since 2002, run by a mother, daughter, and son team, offering an extensive menu of sweet and savory baked goods with a Latin American influence. The shop is best known for its handcrafted empanadas in over a dozen varieties — from traditional beef to vegan — alongside fruit pies, tarts, quiches, and hand-decorated cookies. Located at Lonsdale Quay in North Vancouver, it is a convenient stop for cyclists riding the North Shore waterfront.
e5239ed4f3: Quayside Tiki Bar is a tropical-themed bar and restaurant located steps from the Fraser River in New Westminster, serving handcrafted cocktails — including Mai Tais, Blue Lagoon, and Quay Breeze Punch — alongside a wide-ranging menu of sushi, seafood, pizzas, and grilled meats. The venue features a spacious waterfront patio with river views and a lively atmosphere, making it a colourful option for cyclists riding the riverfront. The business appears to have opened recently, with a grand opening event listed on its website.
466433f8fb: Purebread is a well-regarded artisan bakery chain with roots in Whistler that has expanded to multiple BC locations including this Mount Pleasant shop. It specialises in freshly baked breads, pastries, pies, and cakes, and has been featured by the New York Times, Lonely Planet, and Vogue. The Mount Pleasant location offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a pleasant urban rest stop for cyclists.
2bbb41167b: McDonald's is a globally recognised fast food chain offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, fries, and McCafé beverages. This North Vancouver location includes a drive-through and takeaway service. It is a reliable, familiar stop for touring cyclists in need of a quick and filling meal along a busy corridor.
bd442e7d6a: Crazy Cows Ice-Cream is a small ice cream shop on Marine Drive in White Rock serving visitors and locals with cold treats and refreshments.
dd16fc6139: Subway is a fast-food sandwich chain with takeaway service located in Chilliwack. It provides quick meal options for touring cyclists passing through the community. Specific cyclist amenities such as bike parking and water refill are not documented.
8b1f1ee7cd: AM Cafe is a 100% plant-based, order-at-the-counter café in the heart of Mount Pleasant, founded by chef Lindsay Loudon whose background spans yacht kitchens and high-end corporate events. The menu leans into plant-based comfort food built to surprise — dishes like the Rogue Waffle and the Faux-Let O' Fish Burger regularly prompt the reaction 'This isn't chicken?' It is a community-focused neighbourhood spot with a relaxed, settle-in atmosphere built around the philosophy of a few ingredients done extremely well.
cbd446bfcf: Gawon Express is a quick-service Korean restaurant near SFU's University High Street, specializing in rice bowls, noodle dishes, soups, and Korean dumplings. The restaurant encourages online pre-ordering for pickup to reduce wait times, making it a practical stop for cyclists passing through the Burnaby Mountain area. A substantial dedicated vegetarian menu — including bibimbap, kimchi fried rice, and soft tofu soup — gives plant-based riders plenty of fueling options.
b82d9c6b22: Rain or Shine Ice Cream is a Kitsilano institution making small-batch, scratch ice cream from BC dairy sourced exclusively from Birchwood Dairy Farm in Abbotsford, with flavours built around locally and organically sourced ingredients like Okanagan honey, Surrey blueberries, and Vancouver-roasted espresso. Founded by a couple inspired by artisan ice cream encountered while travelling, the shop now operates three Vancouver locations, with this one sitting directly on West 4th Avenue—one of the city's busiest cycling corridors. The entirely egg-free base, rotating seasonal menu, and dedicated vegan options make it a distinctive treat stop rather than a generic chain.
830ab6572b: A Starbucks Coffee location in Sardis, part of the well-known international coffee chain. This outlet includes a drive-through lane, making it convenient for quick stops along Luckakuck Way. Touring cyclists passing through Chilliwack's commercial corridor will find it a familiar and reliable refuelling spot.
d6eddf7c3e: Prado Coffee is a Vancouver specialty coffee brand founded by Sammy Piccolo, a four-time Canadian Barista Champion who has represented Canada at the World Barista Championships. What began as a single shop on Commercial Drive has grown into a network of neighbourhood cafes across Vancouver, Burnaby, and Surrey, each focused on craft espresso and fresh baked goods. The Dunbar Street location brings that same community-first ethos to a residential cycling corridor on the west side of Vancouver.
254dcc7a8b: Established in 1992, Murrayville Town Pub is a long-standing Langley neighbourhood pub known for its warm, community-oriented atmosphere. It boasts over 200 seats, pool tables, and 20 screens for sports, plus an adjoining private banquet room called Manhattans. The pub has raised over $100,000 for Big Brothers & Sisters and is deeply embedded in the local Murrayville community.
427ed8e2cf: Cold Shoulder Cafe is a small family-run cafe and bakery in Jordan River on the south end of Vancouver Island, founded in 2014 and now operated by one of the original founders and his family. Situated on West Coast Road near surf breaks and provincial parks, it serves soups, sandwiches, and pastries and also sells branded merchandise online and in-store. It sits on the challenging but scenic cycling route between Sooke and Port Renfrew, making it a natural rest stop for touring cyclists on this stretch of coast.
833267517f: Jim's Pizza Walnut Grove is a locally run pizza restaurant in Langley's Walnut Grove neighbourhood, serving a broad menu of specialty and build-your-own pizzas alongside pasta, ribs, and chicken wings. The shop operates its own delivery fleet and also accepts online orders, making it a practical stop for a takeout meal. Gluten-free crust and vegetarian options are available on request.
fcd92ccae3: Britannia Brewing Lake Country is a craft brewery restaurant and bar set on a 10,000 sq ft facility in the Okanagan, near the popular Okanagan Rail Trail cycling corridor. Established in 2014 and expanded from its Steveston and Ladner origins, it offers a full menu of house ales alongside locally inspired dishes featuring Okanagan ingredients like peaches and BC mushrooms. The 200-seat restaurant with outdoor picnic area makes it a substantial stop for cyclists exploring the Okanagan Valley.
da3d0cbe87: Pappa Leo's Pizza is a locally owned and operated chain founded in 2003 by two brothers in Pitt Meadows, now expanded to 7 Metro Vancouver locations. The Port Coquitlam shop makes pizza dough fresh daily and sources quality ingredients, earning multiple best-pizza awards. Gluten-free crust is available, and the location offers both pickup and delivery.
78b282aae8: Kinkura Sushi + Sake is a Japanese restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, blending traditional sushi culture with a modern dining experience. The menu is extensive, covering salads, tempura, udon, teriyaki, sashimi, and a wide range of classic and specialty rolls including aburi (flame-seared) preparations. Online ordering is available, offering touring cyclists a convenient option for a quick Japanese meal in a dense, walkable neighbourhood.
e2c8761033: Craft Bierhaus is a bar and restaurant billing itself as being 'in the heart of Revelstoke,' with a kitchen centred on slow-smoked meats — brisket, beef ribs, whole chicken, and pork — alongside rotating craft beers and local BC wines. The OSM record notes outdoor seating, making it a sociable place to unwind after a long day in the saddle. Its central downtown location in Revelstoke positions it as a natural end-of-day stop on popular cycling routes through the Columbia Mountains.
f562ef8ef4: Red Arrow Brewing Company is a craft brewery established in 2015 in the Cowichan Valley, operating out of a distinctive red-brick building that was originally an Arrow Custom Motorcycles showroom built in 1990. The taproom pours 12 beers on tap alongside craft cocktails and a full food menu, with a spacious family- and pet-friendly patio that features a Coast Salish totem carved by artist Tom Lafortune. It functions as a community hub in Duncan and welcomes reservations and brewery tours by arrangement.
338583fe40: Wok Box is a fast-casual Chinese restaurant chain offering takeaway service to customers. Located in a commercial shopping area, it provides quick meals for those seeking Asian cuisine. Touring cyclists can grab food without waiting for full table service.
8ad71be306: The Golden Boot is a family-owned Northern Italian trattoria that has been serving handmade pasta, pizza, and sauces in Coquitlam since 1997. Chef-owner David Azzi trained in Modena, Italy and has maintained a strict 'quality over quantity' philosophy, with everything from the bread to the desserts made in-house. The restaurant has earned Restaurant Guru's 2019 Best Italian Restaurant Award and OpenTable's Diners' Choice 2022, and also offers U-Bake take-home items and full event catering.
5a2a8563e4: Rossland Beer Company is an award-winning craft brewery and tasting room in Rossland, BC, producing small-batch beers including the Canadian Brewing Award gold-medal-winning Seven Summits Milk Stout and the BC Beer Award-winning Paydirt Pale Ale. The tasting room overlooks the brewing operation and opens onto a sunny patio, drawing outdoor enthusiasts directly from Rossland's world-class mountain bike trails and ski slopes. The brewery actively sponsors local mountain biking athletes and is deeply embedded in the town's adventure-sports culture, making it a natural gathering point for touring cyclists.
b5c2eb1e3a: Operating for over 30 years, this artisan bakery on Vancouver's Davie Street produces traditional-style breads, pastries, muffins, and gluten-free baked goods using no preservatives or artificial ingredients. It is notably the premier film-industry catering provider in Vancouver, supplying on-location production sets across Metro Vancouver. The Davie Street shop offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a comfortable stop in the heart of the West End.
8d9048b6dc: McDonald's at 1055 West Georgia Street is a fast food restaurant in downtown Vancouver, situated inside a mixed-use building near the West End and steps from the central business district. The restaurant offers a broad menu spanning burgers, chicken, breakfast items, and McCafé beverages, with indoor seating and vegetarian options available. Its downtown core location makes it a practical food and beverage stop for cyclists transiting through Vancouver.
ee62b1f0cf: Hunnybee Bruncheonette is a counter-service cafe and brunch spot in Vancouver's Strathcona neighbourhood, sitting on the corner of Gore Avenue and Union Street. It serves brunch classics — shakshuka, ricotta pancakes, eggs benny variations, and fresh-pressed juice — alongside espresso drinks and cocktails. The same address hosts a sibling evening restaurant, Thank You Pizza, making it a versatile stop on a city ride.
c2ae4ac241: Ali & Baba is listed in OpenStreetMap as a Turkish restaurant in North Vancouver. Beyond the cuisine tag, no verified web presence for this specific business could be confirmed, leaving its character and offerings largely unknown to potential visitors.
ac415e7ca1: Two Stones Grill is a casual grill-house restaurant inside the Tsawwassen Commons shopping centre in Delta, BC, serving a broad menu of handcrafted burgers, charcoal-broiled steaks, grilled salmon, pasta, and Mediterranean-influenced dishes alongside a full cocktail and BC wine list. The restaurant covers all three dayparts—breakfast, lunch, and dinner—making it a versatile refuelling stop for cyclists riding the Tsawwassen waterfront corridor. Catering with delivery or pickup is also available for events in the Tsawwassen/Delta region.
e617a42137: Mandarin Garden Buffet has been a Chilliwack-area institution since 1998, serving a wide-ranging Chinese smorgasbord buffet alongside a full take-out menu six days a week. It has earned the Chilliwack Times Reader's Choice award for Favourite Buffet, drawing diners from Chilliwack, Abbotsford, and Agassiz. A large private banquet room rounds out the offering for groups and special occasions.
cceb9cc57c: The Acorn is a Michelin-recommended, award-winning vegetable-forward locavore restaurant and bar on Vancouver's Main Street, operating a zero-waste kitchen that sources 99% of its ingredients from BC and Western Canada. Cyclists can choose between a multi-course blind tasting menu served family-style or an à la carte menu featuring inventive dishes built around seasonal foraged and farmed produce. The restaurant is also noted by Michelin for its weekend brunch program.
4df8c8e30a: Andreas Restaurant is a family-owned North Vancouver institution open since 1984, run by father-and-son duo Andreas and Dimitrios, with a scratch kitchen that hand-makes an extensive menu of over 130 items — from Greek specialties to pizza, pasta, steaks, and seafood — every morning. The restaurant explicitly welcomes tour groups with specially crafted group menus and offers free delivery across North Vancouver, West Vancouver, and Deep Cove. A long-standing local favourite, it sends guests home with complimentary fresh-baked bread as a nod to the founder's original tradition.
34a83e8e79: Sushi Tengoku is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Surrey offering online ordering for takeout and dine-in service. It provides a convenient casual dining option for touring cyclists seeking Japanese cuisine along their route.
c99369119f: This McDonald's sits on the second floor (level 1) of a building on the busy Broadway-Cambie corridor in Vancouver, without a drive-through. It offers both indoor and outdoor seating alongside takeaway and delivery options, making it a quick resupply stop for cyclists travelling along the Broadway corridor. The location is a standard urban franchise outlet with no cycling-specific features confirmed.
e6f22438a9: Mai's Vietnamese Restaurant is a family-owned establishment that has been serving authentic Vietnamese cuisine to the Langley community since 2008. The menu spans phở, vermicelli bowls, bánh mì, salad rolls, and family-style hot pot, with Western and Asian-inspired options available for catering. Cyclists can order for pickup or dine in at a full-service restaurant that prides itself on fresh ingredients and consistent quality.
838ec7a146: Delicious Pho is a Vietnamese restaurant on downtown Vancouver's Robson Street, one of two Lower Mainland locations (the other in Coquitlam). The menu centres on signature satay pho with aromatic broth, alongside fresh salad rolls, banh mi, and a deluxe combo pho loaded with mixed proteins. The restaurant emphasises traditional recipes and is wheelchair accessible, making it a practical sit-down stop in a busy urban cycling corridor.
707338b6fb: Ton Khao Thai Cuisine is a family-run restaurant in Historic Downtown Abbotsford, owned by Suthin and Ya, offering an extensive menu of Thai street-food classics spanning curries, noodles, stir-fries, and grills. Dishes are built around the five traditional Thai flavour pillars — sweet, sour, salty, spicy, and creamy — with adjustable spice levels from none to Thai hot. Cyclists passing through downtown Abbotsford will find both dine-in and call-ahead takeout service.
81cea2e3da: Bagheera is a hidden speakeasy cocktail bar in Vancouver's Chinatown, concealed behind the fictional storefront of the Happy Valley Turf Club — a betting parlour facade that masks the entrance. Inside, the theme shifts to Victorian India and Jungle Book imagery, with expertly crafted cocktails and small Indian-inspired dishes. The elaborate concept extends to the bar's own website, which is disguised as a horse-racing racecard.
537712ffa3: Thai Basil is a Thai restaurant established in 2008 with four Vancouver locations, including this one on Commercial Drive — a popular cycling corridor in the city's east side. The menu spans curries, noodle soups, salads, and rice dishes with a range of protein choices including tofu. Cyclists can dine in or order takeout for a convenient mid-ride meal.
5afa077184: Bonnie Bread Bakery is a bakery located in Vancouver, BC. For touring cyclists passing through the area, it offers a potential stop for freshly baked goods and bread. The business was recently verified in OSM in May 2026, suggesting it is actively operating.
19c7f8e58c: Sago To Go is a café in Vancouver. As a food service business, it can serve as a convenient stop for cycling tourists moving through the neighborhood.
844eb49c30: The Ramen Butcher is an authentic Hakata-style tonkotsu ramen restaurant operated by Menya Kouji Enterprises, with noodles, gyozas, and rice bowls made in-house daily by chefs trained in Japan. The Burnaby location on Hastings Street offers a broad menu spanning classic tonkotsu, tsukemen, miso, and coconut curry ramens alongside donburi rice bowls and gyoza. It is one of two BC locations, with a second shop in Vancouver's Chinatown.
69b10ecb68: Grand Crystal is a Chinese seafood restaurant and wedding banquet venue located in Burnaby's Kingsway corridor. It serves dim sum and dinner, and also functions as an event space for large gatherings. Touring cyclists riding through the Burnaby stretch of Kingsway would find it a substantial stop for a full sit-down meal.
1cc0a8a2b4: Dana Pani Indian Cuisine is a North Indian restaurant in the Queensborough neighbourhood of New Westminster, offering a broad menu of tandoori specialities, biryanis, curries, and freshly baked breads. The kitchen is notable for its range of both meat and vegetarian dishes, from classic Butter Chicken to Paneer Stuffed Chana Bhatura, with wraps and rice bowls also available for quick meals. Touring cyclists can order pickup directly through the restaurant's own website.
aa8c6c4c85: Kamei on Broadway is a long-established Japanese restaurant tucked behind Broadway Plaza in Vancouver, celebrated as a local hidden gem since 1988. It offers distinctive Japanese Tatami rooms and private booths with sweeping panoramic views of downtown Vancouver. The menu focuses on innovative Japanese cuisine with an emphasis on fresh, high-quality seafood prepared by specially trained Japanese chefs.
0db293c017: Established in 2004, 21 Steps Kitchen & Bar is a locally owned and operated second-storey restaurant in the heart of Whistler Village, offering views of the village and surrounding mountains. It serves modern comfort food with generous portions in a warm, casual atmosphere with a full bar. The restaurant has earned recognition for Best Casual Dining and Best Customer Service in Pique News Magazine's 'Best Of Whistler' awards.
e28d7d5645: Caffe Artigiano (now branded as Artigiano) is a Vancouver-founded specialty coffee chain with over 25 locations across BC and Alberta, built on a reputation for latte art and internationally award-winning barista craft. The Main Street location offers indoor and outdoor seating, accepts credit and debit cards, and is wheelchair accessible. The chain roasts its own 100% Arabica beans at a Burnaby roastery and emphasizes organic, locally sourced ingredients in its house-made baked goods.
f7da4b6d69: Hoi An Cafe is a Vietnamese cafe on Victoria Drive in Vancouver with indoor seating. It provides a casual stop for cyclists to rest and refresh during tours in the area.
e10684e631: Pudgie's Pizza & Pasta is a long-established neighbourhood restaurant at Horseshoe Bay, serving pizza and pasta with fresh, locally sourced ingredients since the late 1980s. Its location steps from the BC Ferries terminal makes it a natural stop for cyclists riding to or from the Sunshine Coast. The restaurant is also known for stocking what it bills as Vancouver's largest selection of rare and specialty sodas.
afaa943f7e: Mr. India Restaurant & Bar is an Indian restaurant in Abbotsford serving cuisine inspired by regions across the subcontinent, from street snacks like golgappa and vada paav to full curry entrées and cocktails. The restaurant offers both a dine-in bar experience and a robust takeout and catering operation, including tiffin service and large-group party packs. With over 600 Google reviews and more than 30 vegetarian and non-vegetarian entrées, it is a well-established local dining destination.
e6b6ac798e: St. Lawrence is a Michelin-starred restaurant on Powell Street in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood, blending classic French technique with the culinary traditions of Québec under Chef/Owner Jean-Christophe Poirier. Opened in 2017, it has earned placement on Canada's 100 Best Restaurants list multiple years running and was named to the World's 50 Best Discovery List. The experience centres on a four-course table d'hôte menu with a rotating seasonal focus, currently drawing inspiration from Provence.
1822846021: Board with Friends Cafe is a board game cafe on Victoria's Johnson Street where visitors can drop in and play from an extensive in-house library for as long as they like, with no time limit. The cafe also retails what it describes as Victoria's largest selection of board games, available in-store and online, along with a loyalty rewards program and a private room that seats up to 12 for group occasions. As of the most recent website check, the business is actively relocating to an undisclosed address, so cyclists should verify the current location before visiting.
03deadc415: Bubble Waffle Cafe is a Hong Kong-style street food cafe specializing in egg waffles (雞蛋仔), fish soup noodle combos, curry fish balls, and rice noodle rolls — popular street snacks brought from Hong Kong to Metro Vancouver. Located inside a mall food court, it offers an extensive menu with dozens of soup base, noodle, and topping combinations alongside a full range of bubble teas and fruit drinks. The cafe operates multiple locations including Aberdeen Centre, Public Market, and Park Royal.
df129acc15: D² Tea Lab is a specialty craft tea café in Burnaby built around the '3/7' ratio — three parts milk to seven parts tea — developed through what the owners describe as years of scientific research and sensory analysis. The menu centers on craft milk teas, pure teas, and snowy lattes, sourced from premium leaves chosen for quality and sustainability. The lab-themed branding and data-driven flavour philosophy give it a distinctive character among BC's bubble tea scene.
09b3b8d0b4: Hydra Estiatorio is a high-end Greek seafood restaurant occupying the soaring 60-foot atrium of Vancouver's EXchange Tower, named after the Aegean island renowned for its culinary traditions. The restaurant operates a Raw Bar with daily fresh seafood flown in from Greece, New Zealand, and Hawaii alongside locally sourced BC salmon and oysters, with fish deboned and plated tableside. The venue is located within Vancouver's first LEED Platinum heritage conversion hotel and uses geo-exchange thermal regulators, solar thermal panels, and storm water retention systems as part of its sustainability program.
671a899f57: Outer Clove is a locally owned European comfort-food restaurant in downtown Nelson specializing in Balkan and Hungarian cuisine — think schnitzel, chicken paprikash, halusky, and Hungarian cabbage rolls. The restaurant stands out for its curated selection of Czech draft beers poured from Lukr faucets and rare Central European craft wines. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery are all available, making it a flexible stop for cyclists passing through Nelson.
947f4c84ce: Machi Sushi is a compact neighbourhood Japanese restaurant on Cadboro Bay Road in Oak Bay, serving an extensive menu of creative specialty rolls, sashimi, nigiri, and donburi bowls with a focus on fresh and locally sourced ingredients. The chef's signature rolls — including the Vancouver Roll and Caterpillar Roll — have earned consistent praise from local diners. Dine-in, takeout, and online ordering are all available.
012a6e5c90: West B Pizza is a Vancouver pizzeria on West Broadway serving a creative lineup of pies including fusion options like Paneer Masala and Vietnamese Chilli Chicken alongside classics and pasta dishes. The shop offers indoor seating and online ordering, making it a convenient stop for cyclists along the busy Broadway corridor. A range of vegetarian options and sides like peri peri wings and fries round out the menu.
0aa904f145: The Bund Shanghai Cuisine & Bar is a Chinese restaurant and bar on White Rock's scenic Marine Drive, specializing in Shanghai-style dishes alongside Sichuan and Cantonese favourites. The menu spans dim sum staples like soup dumplings and a full Peking duck service alongside a broad selection of wok dishes. Situated on one of the Lower Mainland's most popular waterfront cycling corridors, it offers a full sit-down meal or online pickup for cyclists on the move.
ca5689331e: Buckhorn & Main Mountain Eatery is the full-service restaurant and lounge inside Trickle Creek Lodge, a ski-in/ski-out resort at Kimberley Alpine Resort. The menu spans burgers, seafood, steaks, salads, and desserts, with a kids' menu and a lounge offering cocktails and draft beer on tap. Its location at the base of the alpine resort and near the Peak to Plaza trail network makes it a natural refuelling stop for cyclists exploring the Kimberley area.
2f43747568: Wild Ginger is an Asian fusion restaurant on Main Street in downtown Penticton, serving a broad menu spanning Vietnamese, Thai, and Chinese cuisines including Beef Pho, Pad Thai, Chow Mein, and signature stir-fries. The kitchen caters to dietary needs with gluten-free and vegan adaptations available across most dishes and free tofu substitutions on request. Online ordering and local delivery make it a convenient refuelling option for cyclists passing through the Okanagan.
57530a0054: Molly's Reach by Black Bean occupies one of British Columbia's most storied cafe buildings — a Gibsons landmark that served as the primary filming location for the CBC series 'The Beachcombers' from 1972 to 1990. Since December 2024, the Black Bean Cafe has brought its locally roasted Sunshine Coast coffee and daily house-baked goods to this iconic waterfront address. It's a walk-in, no-reservations spot with outdoor seating and a relaxed coastal atmosphere — an easy diversion for cyclists arriving via the Langdale ferry.
dd8b09aee9: The Royal Grill is a restaurant located on Baker Street in Nelson, BC, a cycling-friendly downtown corridor. Beyond its OSM listing as a restaurant, no current details about cuisine, atmosphere, or cyclist-specific features can be confirmed, as the business's registered domain has been taken over by unrelated gambling content. A visit or direct call would be needed to assess its suitability for touring cyclists.
b102182306: Roy's Towne Pub is a well-established neighbourhood pub sitting right on the South Island Highway in Royston, in the heart of the Comox Valley between Courtenay and Union Bay. Under current ownership since 2021, it serves classic pub meals, cold drinks, and hosts regular live music featuring local artists across rock, folk, Celtic, jazz, country, and blues. It's a genuine community hub with ample on-site parking and a welcoming, family-friendly atmosphere.
32f3bafe55: Pho Canada is a Vietnamese restaurant in Surrey serving an extensive menu of pho noodle soups, stews, fried plates, and appetizers including salad rolls and spring rolls. The menu spans dozens of pho variations — beef, chicken, seafood, and vegetarian — making it a substantial stop for a hungry touring cyclist. The restaurant is located in a unit at a Surrey strip-style address on 100 Avenue.
4f75295cc0: L'OTUS Cake Boutique is an artisan cake shop specializing in handcrafted crepe cakes, chiffon layer cakes, cheesecakes, and gelato with Asian-inspired flavour profiles such as matcha yuzu and mango sticky rice. It operates on a pre-order pickup model, so cyclists planning a stop should order in advance. The boutique offers a distinctive selection of visually elaborate celebration cakes that would make an unusual but memorable mid-tour treat.
df8b834d33: White Sails is an award-winning craft brewery and taproom that has been a fixture of downtown Nanaimo since 2015, located across from Maffeo Sutton Park. The large, open-concept west-coast-inspired space seats over 100 guests and offers up to 14 beers on tap alongside wines, ciders, a full coffee bar, and a hyper-local food menu sourced from neighbourhood butchers, bakers, and cheese-makers. Its medal-winning flagship beers and rotating small-batch releases make it a genuine destination stop on any Vancouver Island cycling route.
e3c1a7221a: A McDonald's fast food restaurant situated on the busy Kingsway corridor in Vancouver, serving burgers, chicken, breakfast items, and McCafé beverages. The location includes both indoor and outdoor seating areas and a drive-through lane. It sits on a well-travelled urban cycling route connecting Burnaby and Vancouver.
cf2630ce4e: Tonics Pub is a downtown Kelowna institution on Ellis Street, offering an extensive tap selection of 11 domestic and imported beers alongside premium spirits and wines in a casual setting. The venue features two of the largest screens in Kelowna, drawing crowds for games and events. Its menu reaches well beyond standard pub fare, with an emphasis on home-style quality — a solid option for a meal stop in the heart of the city.
eab6233a34: The Farmhouse is an intimate Italian restaurant housed in a restored heritage home in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, featuring a backyard patio and a short service bar overlooking the open kitchen. Its kitchen is stocked by local BC growers and foragers — notably Campagna Farm in Abbotsford — weaving West Coast seasonality into classic Italian antipasti, mains, and desserts. The restaurant is part of the Viaggio Hospitality group and offers brunch through late dinner service alongside a curated list of biodynamic and organic wines from BC and Italy.
8aa5222fe9: The Locavore Bar & Grill grew from a humble food truck into a vibrant hybrid indoor/outdoor venue set inside former greenhouses on the edge of Squamish, sharing a property with the Cloudburst Cafe. The kitchen focuses on local BC flavours for lunch and dinner, with a bar program built around regional cocktails, beer, and wine. The venue explicitly positions itself as a destination for unwinding after mountain biking or hiking, making it a natural stop on the Sea-to-Sky corridor.
93cff43cc7: Founded in 1998, New Amsterdam Cafe bills itself as North America's first 420-friendly cafe and one of the oldest cannabis companies in the world, operating as an inclusive cannabis-inspired lounge in Vancouver's Gastown neighbourhood. The venue combines a relaxed lounge atmosphere with food, drinks, catering, and event bookings, and hosts the annual Cannabis Hospitality Summit. Patrons must be 19 or older to enter.
c41bb04a4e: Mucho Burrito is a Canadian fast-casual Mexican chain serving burritos, bowls, quesadillas, and tacos with a 'Modern Mexicana' approach emphasising fresh ingredients. This Tsawwassen location sits at 4949 Canoe Pass Way — close to the Tsawwassen ferry terminal, making it a plausible quick-fuel stop for cyclists arriving or departing on BC Ferries routes. Vegan and vegetarian options are available across the menu.
312b9b36d5: Black Frog Eatery is a sports bar, restaurant, and live entertainment venue perched on the edge of Gastown with waterfront views of Vancouver harbour. A long-standing local institution, it draws locals, tourists, and sports fans with multiple big screens, rotating BC craft beers, and a packed event calendar of live music, stand-up comedy, and trivia nights. Its all-season patio and hearty pub menu make it a lively food-and-drink anchor in one of Vancouver's most visited neighbourhoods.
2bd425ac70: Sagewood Winery is a small estate winery on the outskirts of Kamloops producing a broad range of whites, reds, rosé, and sparkling wines from their own vineyard. The operation emphasizes sustainable practices including biodiversity, drip irrigation, and organic methods in the vineyard. The property is dog-friendly and welcomes visitors for tastings, making it an appealing rural stop for touring cyclists exploring Thompson Valley wine country.
fce8116988: Thai Cook is an authentic Thai restaurant on Victoria Crescent in downtown Nanaimo, serving dine-in, takeout, and delivery. The menu spans curries, noodles, stir-fries, and appetizers with spice levels ranging from mild to Thai hot. Many dishes are gluten-free, and multiple tofu and vegetable protein options appear throughout both the lunch and dinner menus.
fb506c0fa9: Mi Casa Mexicana is a family-owned Mexican restaurant that opened in December 2019 on Burrard Street in Vancouver, rooted in a culinary tradition dating back to their grandmother's cooking in 1970s Mexico. The menu focuses on handmade pozole, birria, tacos, and tamales built from family recipes and daily-fresh ingredients. Touring cyclists will find a warm sit-down spot with takeout available and gluten-free options on the menu.
b55eca43a7: An adult entertainment bar and lounge on Whalley Boulevard in Surrey operating as an exotic show lounge with a rotating weekly lineup of performers. The venue offers VIP experiences and special events nights. It is a late-night destination operating into the early morning hours.

c2b442f2f6: Steveston Built Local Taphouse is a neighbourhood pub situated near the historic Steveston waterfront in Richmond, an area well-travelled by cyclists on the dike trails and coastal routes. The taphouse bills itself as locally focused, with its menu available as a PDF download from the website. It occupies a unit in a mixed-use development at the edge of the Steveston community.
1f54c7d218: Thai by Thai is a sit-down and pickup Thai restaurant on Scott Road (120 St) in Surrey, offering an extensive menu of curries, noodle dishes, and stir-fries alongside lunch specials. The restaurant has earned 209 customer reviews and operates a fully functional online ordering system for pickup. Cyclists riding the Surrey/Delta corridor will find it a convenient stop for a hot meal or a quick takeout order.
9b92399e19: India Delight Bistro & Bar is a North Indian and Mughlai restaurant on Sooke Road serving authentic curries, tandoori dishes, and Indo-Chinese appetizers for dine-in or takeout. Chef Data Ram Bhaat brings experience from kitchens in India, Singapore, and Germany, with a focus on freshly prepared sauces and handpicked herbs and spices. The restaurant also offers catering for events of 50 or more people, making it a notable stop in an otherwise limited dining corridor west of Victoria.
bc39c6fa07: Slo Coffee is a specialty coffee shop that originated in Vancouver's Fraserhood neighbourhood and expanded to a second downtown location at Pacific Centre in December 2025. The shop is built around a philosophy of mindful, unhurried coffee culture—emphasizing community, connection, and quality pour-overs and espresso drinks. Food offerings include vegan-friendly spreads, toasts, and overnight oats alongside sandwiches and seasonal signature beverages.
f095f50d8e: Founded in Kitsilano in 1968, The Naam is Vancouver's oldest natural foods restaurant and a long-standing neighbourhood institution on West 4th Avenue. It is a fully vegetarian, family-run restaurant that uses organic, locally-sourced ingredients including house-made tofu and tempeh, and locally-sourced vegan beer and wine. The relaxed, homey atmosphere and central Kitsilano location make it a welcoming stop for cyclists passing through the area.
682c2be8aa: Nana Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant situated on Victoria Crescent in downtown Nanaimo, marketing itself as the 'Best Sushi in Nanaimo.' The menu spans traditional appetizers, miso soups, salads, and a range of sushi in a relaxed dine-in setting. Online ordering for pickup is available, which can be convenient for cyclists wanting a quick meal on the go.
ef27c9c00d: Sleeping Giant Fruit Winery is a BC fruit winery near Summerland offering 19 table wines, 12 late-harvest dessert wines, and four sparkling wines, all made from BC-grown fruit using classic winemaking techniques. The tasting room is operated alongside its parent company Summerland Sweets, and sits just 210 steps from the historic Summerland Steam Train trestle bridge — a natural stop on that scenic rail-trail corridor. Tastings are offered by reservation or walk-in, and wines can be purchased in-store or through the online Shopify shop.
5c55b9cf4c: Obanhmi is a Vietnamese bánh mì restaurant located in Burnaby's Newton Street area. The name suggests a specialty in the classic Vietnamese baguette sandwich, a popular quick and filling meal for cyclists on the move. The OSM record lists daily hours, indicating consistent availability throughout the week.
40a6a44cec: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain with a location in Fort St. John offering delivery and takeout. The brand distinguishes itself with a commitment to Canadian-grown wheat, organic tomato sauce, and a broad selection of plant-based, dairy-free, and gluten-free options. For a touring cyclist passing through Fort St. John, it is a convenient stop for a hot meal with customizable dietary accommodations.
ef8372e396: Breaking Bean is a coffee shop at 551 Cardero Street in Vancouver. The establishment serves coffee and beverages to the local community.
f69ffcc6ec: CinCin Ristorante + Bar is a long-established Italian restaurant on Robson Street, accessed by a winding stone stairway above street level. The kitchen is anchored by a Grillworks Infierno, a two-metre wood-fired grill and rotisserie where fish and prime meats are cooked over fruitwood charcoal alongside housemade pastas. With over 25 years of operation and a nationally recognized wine program, it is considered one of Vancouver's premier fine-dining Italian destinations.
a4299a2b67: Patisserie Le Pont is a premium French-Japanese artisan pastry shop in West Vancouver, founded by Makoto Yamaguchi, a classically trained pâtissière who graduated from Le Cordon Bleu in Paris and previously ran her own shop in Tokyo for 15 years. The patisserie specializes in handcrafted eclairs — both sweet and savoury — alongside cakes, tarts, and baked goods made fresh daily without preservatives or pre-mixes. OSM records both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a pleasant stop for a cyclist looking for a quality sweet treat.
3aa646e54b: MGM is a family-run community institution in Nanaimo that has been serving home-cooked all-day breakfast, lunch, and dinner since 1984. The restaurant doubles as a neighbourhood gathering place, hosting chess nights, live music with dancing, game nights, and other community events in a space that includes a dance floor, stage area, and large banquet section. A seniors menu and kids menu round out its broad, welcoming appeal.
3b150637f6: Milano Coffee is a Vancouver institution founded in 1984 by Italian Master Roaster Francesco Curatolo, bringing three generations of artisan espresso tradition to the West Coast. The Denman Street espresso bar sits at the gateway to Stanley Park and the seawall — one of the most heavily cycled corridors in Metro Vancouver. The roaster has earned 15 gold medals from the International Institute of Coffee Tasters and is known for blending up to 20 origin coffees into its signature espressos, with outdoor seating available.
69884c9d60: Fable Café is the brick-and-mortar café of Fable, a Certified B Corp best known for its premium tableware and homewares brand. Situated in Vancouver's South Granville neighbourhood, it serves espresso drinks, rotating pour overs, matcha, hojicha, and seasonal beverages alongside sweet bites. The café runs a no-tipping model with living wages for staff and charges nothing extra for alternative milks.
367e819e24: Family Thai Restaurant is a family-owned eatery that has brought authentic Thai cuisine to Cranbrook's East Kootenay community since 2017. The menu spans a wide range of Thai classics — curries, stir-fries, noodle dishes, and soups — with a house spice scale from 1 (mild) to 5 (Thai-nationals-only). The kitchen cooks each dish fresh to order without MSG, and can accommodate vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free diners on selected items.
b0f2bc47c8: Thai Green Elephant is a family-run Thai restaurant established in September 2014, drawing on over 30 years of culinary experience to serve authentic Thai cuisine in Esquimalt near Victoria. The extensive all-day menu caters to a wide range of dietary needs, with clearly labelled vegan, vegetarian, and allergen-tagged dishes. Online ordering and takeout are available, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists looking for a full sit-down or take-away meal.
f0ac27ae6d: The Ruby on Johnson is a locally owned breakfast and brunch restaurant open since 2015, located inside the Best Western Carlton Plaza Hotel on Johnson Street in Victoria. It offers a refined take on brunch blending eclectic southern-inspired fare with scratch cooking and locally sourced ingredients. The restaurant is part of a small Victoria-based group with two additional locations and is known for its vinyl record collection and emphasis on staff wellbeing.
5869482bd2: Freshslice Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain offering by-the-slice and whole-pizza options with a wide variety of customizable toppings, including vegetarian choices and a gluten-free cauliflower crust. This Tsawwassen location on Ladner Trunk Road sits in a commercial strip in Delta and offers both dine-in and takeout service. It is a practical calorie stop for cyclists passing through the area en route to or from the Tsawwassen ferry terminal.
abfdd74361: Tofino Licks is an artisanal soft-serve ice cream shop in Tofino that collaborates with local restaurants and bakeries — Tacofino, Sobo, Common Loaf, and the Tofino Ucluelet Culinary Guild — to create uniquely topped sundaes using ingredients from the town's culinary scene. Their Italian-imported soft serve and sorbets are prepared in-house, with both creamy vanilla gelato and a vegan chocolate sorbet as bases. It's a well-known local stop for a sweet treat after a ride on Vancouver Island's west coast.
61935796e9: The Bubble Tea Shop is a local small business with locations in Richmond and Vancouver's Olympic Village, specializing in bubble tea and DIY milk tea kits. The Richmond storefront offers in-store pickup of ready-made drinks and retail supplies including loose leaf teas, flavoured powders, and toppings. It is a community-oriented café-style shop that also ships its DIY kits across Canada.
9e44eaaf64: Tim Hortons is a Canadian quick-service chain institution on Northfield Road in Nanaimo, offering coffee, baked goods, soups, and breakfast wraps with both dine-in and drive-thru options. For a touring cyclist, it provides a reliable, familiar stop for a hot drink and a quick meal at the northern edge of the city. The location supports mobile ordering and a loyalty rewards program.
a70a96ec64: Floyd's Diner is a Victoria, BC institution established in 2004, celebrated for its signature challenge dish 'The Mahoney' and generous breakfast and brunch portions. The family-oriented diner has grown to four locations across the greater Victoria area, including James Bay, Langford, Royal Oak, and the Gorge. Touring cyclists will find it a reliable all-day breakfast stop open seven days a week.
34cc3a85e2: Cooks Restaurant is a gourmet smash burger joint on Cumberland's historic former mining town main street, operated by chefs Jake Galbraith and Christopher Matthews. It was called a 'worth-the-detour' destination by the Vancouver Sun, serving freshly ground local chuck burgers, fried chicken sandwiches, hand-spun milkshakes made with Island Farms dairy, and local draft beer. Cumberland itself is a well-known cycling hub, making this a natural post-ride stop.
b13bb5d1a8: BeaverTails is an iconic Canadian pastry chain, famous for hand-stretched whole-wheat pastries fried to order and topped with a wide range of sweet or savory options. The Victoria location on Broughton Street sits close to the Inner Harbour, one of the city's busiest cycling and tourist corridors. Beyond pastries, the menu includes poutines, BeaverDogs, lemonades, and hot chocolate — a solid quick-fuel stop on a ride through downtown Victoria.
51625dd126: Il Covo Trattoria is a family-run authentic Italian restaurant located in Victoria's historic James Bay neighbourhood, housed in a 112-year-old heritage building steps from the Inner Harbour. The restaurant holds the Ospitalità Italiana seal from the Italian Chamber of Commerce, certifying its authenticity, with an owner originally from Genova who has been bringing Italian flavours to Victoria since 1999. Cyclists can dine on northern Italian classics and family recipes, with the option of eating al fresco in the garden patio.
9dd5d514e5: PappaRoti is a Malaysian-origin café chain famous for its signature roti buns: a soft, pillowy interior wrapped in a crisp coffee-caramel crust with a salted butter centre, baked fresh throughout the day. The Coquitlam location is one of several BC outposts of a brand with over 400 locations worldwide, serving buns alongside hot and cold drinks, pastries, sandwiches, salads, and soups. It makes a convenient stop on Pinetree Way for a quick, filling snack.
b59c6c57d4: The Longhorn Saloon is one of Whistler's most iconic après-ski and après-bike bars, situated at the base of Whistler Mountain just steps from the gondolas and operated by the Gibbons Hospitality Group. It features an expansive slopeside patio known for high-energy atmosphere, live music, and weekly themed events. The venue explicitly caters to mountain bikers finishing their day on the mountain alongside skiers and snowboarders.
44d8660434: The Firehouse Grill is a casual full-service restaurant in downtown Nanaimo on Front Street, offering an eclectic fusion of house sushi rolls, grill items, and craft beer. The menu blends West Coast ingredients — sockeye salmon, local prawns, and albacore tuna — with Japanese technique, making it a distinctive dining stop near the Nanaimo waterfront. Cyclists finishing a coastal or inland route into Nanaimo will find a broad menu suited to refuelling.
3768c32f96: Pamir Diner is an Afghan restaurant in Delta, BC, serving traditional dishes including handcrafted mantu dumplings, slow-cooked lamb, and mixed kebab platters using family recipes. The menu draws on generations of Afghan culinary tradition with an emphasis on fresh, daily-prepared ingredients. Online ordering is available for pickup and delivery, making it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists riding through the area.
43e8ca5571: An Indian restaurant situated on 43 Avenue in Vernon, BC, with a dining capacity of 78. It offers both takeout and delivery in addition to dine-in service, making it a potential stop for cyclists looking for a hearty meal in the Okanagan. The outdoor area permits smoking.
8de2480cd8: Sachi Sushi has been a Whistler institution since 2003, earning the Best Sushi award in the Pique Newspaper's Best of Whistler competition and a glowing mention in Lonely Planet. Owner and head chef Toshiyuki Kobayashi brings over 30 years of sushi experience, with a focus on the freshest ingredients in creative rolls and sashimi. Located in the Summit Lodge on Main Street, it's a popular walk-in-only spot that draws visitors from around the world.
da5e3b7833: Village Books & Coffee House is an independent bookstore and coffee shop tucked into a Richmond retail unit, offering a curated selection of fiction, young adult, and new-release titles alongside café service. It is a community-oriented stop where browsing a book shelf and a coffee order go hand in hand. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's southwest corner would find it a welcoming place to rest and recharge mentally, if not mechanically.
64df110ecb: Standard Pizza is a small, independently owned neighbourhood pizzeria on Cook Street in Victoria, serving wood-fired pizzas in two sizes (12" and 16") for dine-in or takeout. The menu centres on classic and creative combinations using quality ingredients, with a flexible build-your-own approach and a strong selection of vegetarian options. Cook Street Village is a lively, walkable strip and a natural waypoint for cyclists moving through the city.
c3640b5bc8: Charlie Don't Surf has been a fixture on the White Rock waterfront strip since 1985, serving fresh wild seafood alongside local organic vegetables and a broad selection of craft beers. Situated on Marine Drive directly adjacent to White Rock Beach, it draws both locals and visitors looking for a casual seaside meal. The restaurant also operates a bar and offers outdoor seating, making it a natural rest point for cyclists riding the waterfront.
3626b42bc9: Banter Ice Cream is a Fraser Valley-founded handmade ice cream shop located in Abbotsford's Jubilee Park, housed in the old library building with adjacent outdoor green space. Founded by Laura and Zach after a trip to the Gulf Islands, the shop rotates four new seasonal flavours each month using locally sourced ingredients from Fraser Valley farmers and artisans. The park setting with outdoor space makes it a natural rest stop, and the shop encourages visitors to bring picnics and lawn games.
4b3311392f: So Hyang Korean Cuisine is a Korean restaurant on Fraser Street in Vancouver's Sunset neighbourhood, open seven days a week. The restaurant operates on a walk-in basis with no reservations accepted, and offers online order-ahead for pickup. It sits on a busy arterial cycling corridor connecting south Vancouver to the city centre.
b498e99be0: Crab Hot Lau is Vancouver's original Hải Phòng rice field crab hotpot restaurant, specializing in authentic Northern Vietnamese cuisine with signature hand-filtered crab broths and traditional regional dishes. The restaurant has earned the Vancouver Magazine Gold Award for Best Vietnamese Restaurant three consecutive years (2024–2026), drawing a loyal local following and consistent media coverage. The Kingsway location sits on a major east–west arterial in East Vancouver, making it a convenient sit-down dining option for cyclists in that corridor.
5b766e27fb: The Vault Cafe is a cafe and bar on Wallace Street in Nanaimo offering indoor and sidewalk seating. The cafe serves vegan and vegetarian options and features free Wi-Fi for customers.
0a006b2583: A casual cafe located on Becher Bay Road in Sooke. Positioned on a scenic coastal cycling route, it offers a convenient refueling stop for cyclists exploring the region.
daf47f253a: D-Plus Pizza is a locally-owned and operated pizza and Indian food chain with five locations across Surrey and Delta, BC. Originally founded as D Hut Pizza in the Fraser Valley, it grew by blending classic pizza with Indian-influenced dishes like butter chicken pizza, paneer pizza, samosas, and channa bathura. Cyclists stopping here can expect a varied menu available for walk-in pickup or online pre-order.
73256fc238: ZUBU Ramen is a Japanese ramen chain with four Lower Mainland locations, including a Park Royal outpost in West Vancouver. Executive Chef William Cao trained at the Kitchen Hyodo Ramen School in Oyama, Japan, and sources ingredients both locally from Pacific West Coast farms and directly from Japan. Beyond ramen, the menu spans fresh temaki, handmade gyoza, rice bowls, and Japanese-inspired cocktails.
294430629a: The Watson is a neighbourhood cocktail bar in the heart of Mount Pleasant on Main Street, created by the team behind Bartholomew bar in Yaletown. It features inventive, expertly crafted cocktails alongside elevated bar food and hearty comfort dishes. There is a sun-drenched patio and a mezzanine lounge, making it a welcoming stop along one of Vancouver's main north-south cycling corridors.
ace3033c8f: The Meat Up BBQ is a modern all-you-can-eat restaurant specialising in Asian charcoal-grill BBQ and customisable hotpot, with multiple tiered menu options and a lively, communal atmosphere. It is part of a small chain with locations in both Richmond and Burnaby. The Richmond location sits on busy Number 3 Road, making it a convenient stop for cyclists exploring Richmond's main commercial corridor.
03e2579e1e: A Chinese restaurant in Chilliwack operating since 2011. Provides a meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.
2068f9c595: Elysian Coffee Roasters is a Vancouver specialty coffee roaster that sources and roasts its own single-origin beans from Ethiopia, Rwanda, Guatemala, and Colombia, with four neighbourhood cafes across the city. The Kitsilano location at 5th & Burrard sits on West 5th Avenue, a well-known cycling corridor connecting the waterfront to the broader metro network. The brand built its identity around consistent, high-quality espresso and filter coffee, with a stated emphasis on a positive in-cafe work environment.
ab426b918f: Red Burrito is a Vancouver-born Mexican restaurant chain that has been making fresh, house-made burritos, tacos, and tamales since 2006. The Cambie Street location sits along one of Vancouver's primary cycling corridors and offers both indoor and outdoor seating. Handmade tamales, tortilla soup, and a catering programme round out a menu built around daily-fresh ingredients.
1b446fd705: Restaurant 62 is a farm-to-table restaurant in Abbotsford billing itself as the Fraser Valley's top farm-to-table destination, with a menu built around locally sourced ingredients including Fraser Valley meats, Mt. Lehman cheese, and seasonal produce. The kitchen offers lunch, dinner, and happy hour alongside private dining and catering. Touring cyclists would find a full sit-down dining experience with a regionally rooted menu and a catering operation that speaks to the restaurant's scale.
4578ebcb84: Vietnamese pho restaurant located at 1469 Marine Drive in North Vancouver. The business website was not accessible for verification of amenities or current operational details.
8c8238fa0f: McCulloch Station Pub is Kelowna's original neighbourhood pub, opened in 1985 in East Kelowna and named in honour of Andrew McCulloch, the engineer who built the Kettle Valley Railway — the very rail corridor that touring cyclists now ride as the KVR trail. Situated near historic East Kelowna landmarks, the family-owned pub features a celebrated patio, a full food menu, an on-tap draught selection, and an attached liquor store. It is an adult-only (19+) establishment.
b016a8c63f: Yalla is a family-owned Middle Eastern street-eats restaurant in Victoria serving halal shawarma, falafel, and Persian-inspired dishes across pita and bowl formats. The kitchen draws on culinary traditions from multiple Middle Eastern countries, with standout items like the Persian shawarma and lamb shank with baghali polo. The team is openly accommodating of food allergies including gluten and nuts, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.
f1fe72cac2: The Gelateria is a walk-up gelato and sorbetto counter situated inside The Butchart Gardens' Italian Garden, one of BC's most celebrated horticultural destinations near Sidney. The culinary team travelled to Italy specifically to learn authentic gelato-making, and seasonal flavours feature locally-sourced ingredients. Cyclists visiting Butchart Gardens will find this a fitting sweet stop mid-garden-tour, though paid garden admission is required to reach it.
63966f82d1: Corner Cafe is a casual breakfast and lunch spot serving the Cloverdale area of Surrey, blending Korean-inspired dishes (Cupbop, wonton soup) with classic cafe fare like club sandwiches and wraps. The owners emphasize simple, quality ingredients cooked well over elaborate presentation, creating a warm and unpretentious atmosphere. The cafe also offers online ordering and catering for group inquiries.
d7432ad4cb: Beeryani Indian Cuisine is a full-service Indian restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street, known for its signature 'Beeryani' — a fusion dish blending traditional slow-cooked biryani with locally brewed Canadian craft beer. The menu spans tandoor-grilled proteins, rich curries, and vegetarian staples like Dal Makhani, rounded out by curated craft beer pairings suggested by staff. The restaurant also offers catering for events of all sizes.
2973828c52: Anatolia's Gate is a Turkish restaurant located on Kingsway in Vancouver, offering halal-certified cuisine. It provides sit-down dining suitable for a touring cyclist's meal break. A specialized ethnic cuisine option in the local area.
c65431768c: The Alley is a bubble tea and specialty coffee franchise cafe on Hornby Street in downtown Vancouver, operating under a 'Hub' concept that blends a drinks counter with individual working pods, a collaborative multi-purpose room for up to ten people, and a lounge area. The menu centres on hand-crafted drinks alongside grab-and-go food including pastries, salads, and fried snacks, with house-made sugar cane syrup and freshly hand-rolled tapioca prepared on-site each day. The multilingual branding (English, French, Traditional Chinese) reflects the cafe's origins as a Taiwanese-rooted international franchise.
88920f47a6: Penang Szechuan Cuisine Restaurant is a Szechuan Chinese restaurant in White Rock praised by reviewers for bold, authentic flavors including kung pao chicken, mapo tofu, dan dan noodles, and spicy fish fillet. It offers dine-in with a cozy atmosphere as well as online ordering and takeout, making it a practical meal stop for cyclists exploring the South Surrey and White Rock waterfront area.
e5957ac4fe: Bar Asra is a South Granville cocktail lounge and share plates restaurant led by Executive Chefs Kanwardeep Ahluwalia and Baldeep Singh, whose backgrounds span 16 Taj properties, the 2010 Commonwealth Games, and Fairmont hotels in Vancouver and Lake Louise. The menu draws on global travel and memory — paneer tarts, crab satay, chargrilled steak — paired with a craft cocktail program featuring fat-washed gins, milk-clarified cachaca drinks, and zero-proof options. Free live acoustic music on select evenings makes it a distinctive neighbourhood spot steps from Downtown Vancouver and Kitsilano.
e79eb8863b: A cozy 25-seat natural wine and cocktail bar tucked beside its sister restaurant Farmer's Apprentice in Vancouver's South Granville neighbourhood. The kitchen and bar emphasize low-intervention wines, seasonal ingredients, and a zero-waste ethos, turning leftover herbs and citrus peels into syrups and infusions. Walk-ins are welcome, making it an easy stop for cyclists exploring the area.
08b157f76a: Village Pizzeria is a family-owned takeout restaurant that has been baking artisan pizza in Harrison Hot Springs since 1994, using 48-hour aged handmade dough pressed thin and cooked in a traditional deck oven. Situated right behind Harrison Lake and a short walk from Harrison Spa Resort, it sits in the heart of a popular resort town. The menu rounds out with Greek salad, pasta, and chicken wings — a solid refuelling option after a ride into the Hot Springs.
1098cfb679: Cazba is a Persian grill on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, part of a multi-location Lower Mainland chain rooted in the traditions of Persian hospitality. The menu centres on slow-cooked, heritage recipes — kebabs, Ghormeh Sabzi, and lamb shank dishes prepared from fresh ingredients. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the restaurant is wheelchair accessible.
16036bcf6e: Zambri's has been serving honest, authentic Italian food in downtown Victoria since 1999, earning a loyal following and critical recognition over more than two decades. Founded by Peter Zambri and now co-led by Executive Chef Julia McInnis, the restaurant occupies the Atrium building and draws on seasonal, local ingredients for its ever-changing feature menus. Private dining rooms accommodating up to 55 guests make it a popular destination for celebrations, and delivery via Uber Eats extends its reach beyond dine-in.
2fa2437f32: Cafe Malabar is a Kerala cuisine restaurant in downtown Victoria, founded by chefs Kiran Kolathodan and Karma Tenpa, both raised in Southern India with over 30 years of combined experience in luxury kitchens across Canada and India. The menu centres on Malabar seafood—prawns, curries—alongside vegetarian and meat dishes layered with spices reflecting Portuguese, Dutch, and French culinary influences. A seasonal patio is available, and the restaurant takes reservations as well as take-out orders.
a9d53b9363: This Tim Hortons occupies the Library building at UBC Okanagan campus, offering the familiar Canadian staples of coffee, tea, baked goods, and sandwiches to the campus community and any visitors passing through. The website notes that line-ups are very common, reflecting its high traffic volume. As one of several food outlets managed by UBCO Food Services, it sits within a larger campus dining ecosystem.
673e3b425a: Polish Bistro is a Polish cuisine restaurant in Penticton, British Columbia, operating from a compact single-storey retail building. Penticton is a hub on the Okanagan cycling circuit and near the Kettle Valley Rail Trail, making it a natural resupply point for touring riders. A Polish menu typically offers hearty, filling dishes — a welcome prospect after a long day in the saddle.
634beb95d8: Sabà Bistro is a woman and family-owned Mediterranean-inspired restaurant nestled in historic Fort Langley. The ingredient-forward menu features a crafted balance of local and seasonal flavours, with dishes designed to be shared family style. It operates alongside a sister café and an upcoming pizzeria, both within walking distance on Mavis Avenue.
171f143fef: Stuffies Pastries is a North Vancouver café bringing a South Korean animal-shaped waffle pastry concept to Vancouver, with custard- and jam-filled treats as their signature item. The cafe also serves coffee and beverages, soft-serve ice cream, and sandwiches, salads, and soups, making it a reasonable stop for a sweet or savoury refuel. It is part of a small multi-location chain with stores in Burnaby and Surrey as well.
674e1a266c: Established in 1998, Locus is a long-standing fixture on Vancouver's Main Street — a funky, gothic-decored neighbourhood restaurant and lounge offering an eclectic fusion of globally inspired dishes built around seasonal, locally sourced ingredients. The kitchen rotates through daily brunch, lunch, happy hour, and dinner specials, with local wines and craft beers on offer throughout. Walk-ins are welcome, making it an easy drop-in along one of Vancouver's most active cycling corridors.
ca0146dd84: The Rose and Crown bills itself as Tsawwassen's only neighbourhood pub, a lively sports bar with 12 large-screen TVs, a games room with pool table and dartboard, and a separate quieter lounge called Metro's Lounge for a more relaxed visit. The kitchen runs seven days a week with a full pub menu and a weekend brunch, while the pub calendar includes live music nights, themed DJ nights, monthly karaoke, and a last-Wednesday trivia night. It is a well-established local institution — the head chef has been on staff for over 23 years — and a natural stop for cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen ferry and border corridor.
1f342f3af4: The Sportsbar is a 14,000-square-foot, 420-seat sports bar and full-service restaurant on the 3rd level of Rogers Arena, home of the Vancouver Canucks. It is accessible directly from outside the arena without a game ticket via the Georgia Viaduct entrance, making it a standalone dining destination in downtown Vancouver. The venue features over 100 4K HDTVs, a 90-foot illuminated bar, 60+ draft taps, and a menu from Executive Chef Robert Bartley built on fresh and local ingredients.
16c1d3ab00: Ninja Bubble Tea is a handcrafted bubble tea and Asian fusion café founded in 2013, now operating three locations across BC's Lower Mainland. The menu spans classic tapioca milk teas, artisanal designer teas, fresh poke bowls, Filipino halo-halo shaved ice, and comfort food items like mac and cheese. The New Westminster location sits inside the Rivermarket complex on Quayside Drive.
a8d3eb2031: A Japanese sushi restaurant in Tsawwassen offering online ordering and dine-in service. The recently redesigned website indicates an active, well-maintained business. Useful to touring cyclists needing a meal stop in the area.
3de9868da4: The Shed is a low-and-slow BBQ smokehouse and bar in downtown Kimberley, leaning into the Kootenay ethos of 'dirt-baggery' — a celebration of adventure and free time over busy-ness. The menu is a deep roster of smoked meats, tacos, loaded nachos, and sandwiches built for sharing, alongside local draught beer and cocktails. It operates entirely first-come-first-served with no reservations, making it a laid-back stop after a day on the trails.
6e6090bdcc: Wela is a fast-casual health restaurant in downtown Vancouver specializing in globally-inspired bowls, wraps, and superfood smoothies built around a Thai-rooted 'find your balance' philosophy. Founded in 2019, it offers a wide spectrum of customizable options spanning vegan, gluten-free, and omnivore diets, making it a practical and satisfying stop for touring cyclists seeking a quick nutritious meal. The restaurant also partners with Too Good To Go to reduce food waste, reflecting its sustainability-minded ethos.
a2be4468a0: The Parsonage Cafe in Victoria's Fernwood neighbourhood is the founding location of Fernwood Coffee Company, where a 1936 Barth roaster once sat in the back and sparked a craft roasting business that went on to win the Canadian Barista Championship. The cafe has outdoor seating and serves as a neighbourhood anchor for Fernwood Coffee's specialty coffee culture. Cyclists riding through Victoria's residential streets will find it a welcoming spot for quality coffee with a genuine local history.
ea26616ba4: Cookie's Ice Cream is a family-owned shop in the Tsawwassen Southlands development offering premium small-batch, barrel-churned ice cream and sorbet in over 90 rotating flavours served in a cookie, cup, or cone. Beyond scoops, the shop carries custom ice cream cakes, mini donuts, artisan soda floats, specialty candy, and hot chocolate bombs, making it a well-stocked sweet-stop on a ride through the Delta farmlands. Cookie's also runs a mobile fleet — trailer, truck, and cargo bike — for events across the Lower Mainland.
551c87af1c: Regard Coffee Roasters is a Nanaimo-based coffee roaster with an e-commerce presence offering coffee subscriptions, merchandise, and wholesale supply. OSM identifies a physical location on Bowen Road tagged as a cafe, which may serve as a retail counter or tasting space alongside the roasting operation. The nature and scale of walk-in service are unclear from available evidence.
c67dc0acca: Skinny Duke's Glorious Emporium is a retro-inspired dinner restaurant and cocktail bar on Kelowna's waterfront Water Street, blending nostalgic aesthetics with a forward-thinking, eclectic menu of creative dishes. The venue leans into a lively atmosphere with curated music, private event space, and a late-night dim sum program on weekends. Takeout is available directly through DoorDash for cyclists who prefer to eat on the go.
06589278ab: Hope Mountain Cafe is a breakfast and lunch destination in Hope, BC, founded in 2018 with a menu inspired by global flavors and fresh, sustainable ingredients. The cafe serves specialty coffee, all-day breakfast, sandwiches, and desserts, positioning itself as a solid full-meal stop for cyclists moving through the Fraser Canyon corridor. Online ordering and takeout are available for those who need to eat on the move.
