The outdoor-recreation-friendly vibe, reinforced by the hashtag #getmuckedup, makes it a natural gathering spot for cyclists finishing a day on the trails.
7aca9f65ec: Domino's is a franchise pizza chain location in Victoria's Fairfield/Gonzales neighbourhood on Foul Bay Road. It offers both delivery and carryout, making it a quick calorie stop for cyclists passing through the area. The menu includes pizza, chicken wings, cheesy bread, pasta, and desserts.
d2113e211c: Side Project Coffee is a campus coffee shop operated by the University of Victoria Graduate Students' Society (GSS), located on the UVic Ring Road campus in Victoria. It shares an organizational home with the Grad House Restaurant, both run as student-facing food and beverage services by the GSS. Touring cyclists on the Galloping Goose or Lochside trails — which connect directly to the UVic area — would find it a convenient on-campus stop for coffee and a rest.
03bd646c15: Phở 37 is an award-winning Vietnamese restaurant chain that began in the Steveston neighbourhood of Richmond and has since grown to five BC locations. The Steveston Highway location has earned the Canadian Choice Award for Vietnamese Restaurant in Richmond and recognition from Richmond Business Excellence Awards. Cyclists will find a full sit-down menu of pho, vermicelli bowls, rice plates, and appetizers, with vegetarian and tofu substitutions throughout.
a0cdae5161: Deer Garden Signatures is a well-known Richmond noodle restaurant group celebrated for their signature fish soup rice noodles (魚湯米線) made without MSG. The Alexandra Road flagship sits in Richmond's busy 'food street' corridor, a popular dining destination in the city's heart. Cyclists will find a substantial sit-down meal with online pre-ordering available.
9283640b81: Cannon Estate Winery is a family-owned estate winery opened in 2022 on 20 acres in the Mt. Lehman area of Abbotsford, producing French-style terroir-focused wines under the Cannon and The Wick labels. The property includes Calibre by Cannon, a lounge offering sit-down dining, weekend brunch, and regular live music, making it a destination rather than a simple bottle shop. Located 10 minutes north of Highway 1, it sits in the heart of the Fraser Valley wine country and is a natural stop on rural cycling routes through the region.
9ae1082cf0: Pulp Fiction Coffee House is a one-of-a-kind café in downtown Kelowna where freshly roasted espresso drinks share space with rare pulp fiction books, Art Deco antiques, and vivid jacket-cover art, all curated by owner Max Sloan over a 45-year career of global collecting. Situated on the corner of Pandosy and Lawrence, the groovy retro interior spills into back rooms filled with glowing Art Deco globes, old clocks, and collectible book cover prints. Touring cyclists will find a genuinely distinctive and unhurried rest stop that doubles as a small museum of mid-century popular culture.
946221b067: PETPLS is a pet food and supply store in Richmond's Number 3 Road commercial corridor, offering a curated selection of high-quality pet foods and supplies for cats and dogs sourced from Canada, Korea, Germany, Italy, and New Zealand. The store features a bookable cat room where visitors can interact with adoptable rescue cats, and also offers cat boarding services. Located beside a SkyTrain station, it is an accessible stop for cyclists traveling with animal companions.
a67bd55f1c: Frank's Honeybun Café is a Yates Street diner that bridges all-day North American breakfast with a full Chinese cuisine menu — wonton soups, udon noodles, stir-fry lunch combos, and more. The broad, eclectic menu makes it a practical refueling stop for cyclists at any time of day. Real fruit smoothies and bubble teas are also on offer alongside the full food menu.
5968bca2ff: A 24-hour McDonald's drive-through and dine-in location on Main Street in Vancouver, offering the full Canadian McDonald's menu including breakfast, McCafé beverages, and vegetarian options. Situated in a standalone retail building, this location is convenient for cyclists passing through the Main Street corridor. Indoor seating is available.
099c0419ce: Blenz Coffee is a BC-born specialty coffee chain founded in Vancouver in 1992, now operating locally owned and operated franchise locations across Canada. The Davie Street location serves handcrafted espresso drinks, organic teas, protein shakes, and a full food menu ranging from croissants and breakfast sandwiches to samosas. Outdoor seating and a central West End location make it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists riding the Seawall or nearby routes.
58df64a00c: A Nanaimo seafood restaurant with fish and chips as its signature item, complemented by burgers, salads, and soups. Offers a meal option for the community and visitors to the area.
f4153e48ca: Seoul Grill House is a Korean restaurant situated in a commercial unit along 101 Avenue in Surrey, BC. Specializing in Korean cuisine, it offers a sit-down dining experience that could serve as a satisfying meal stop for cyclists exploring the Surrey area. The restaurant's location along a commercial strip makes it reasonably accessible to riders passing through.
49df339aba: Mr. Red Cafe is a Vietnamese restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver. It offers casual dine-in service.
d1a75ee35e: Sushi Yoi is a casual Japanese restaurant in Burnaby specializing in fresh sushi, sashimi, and aburi-style nigiri alongside classics like tempura and donburi. The restaurant emphasizes high-quality, locally sourced ingredients and offers both dine-in and takeout, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Rosser Avenue corridor. Outdoor seating is noted in OSM, which may allow cyclists to keep an eye on their bikes.
12533f49dd: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, founded in 1928, known for burgers made with 100% fresh Canadian beef and locally sourced ingredients including BC chicken and BC-grown potatoes. The New Westminster location on Sixth Street offers full table-service dining as well as a patio, curbside pickup, and third-party delivery. Touring cyclists will find a familiar, family-friendly stop with a broad menu and vegetarian options.
56dd5a73ab: Happy Family Restaurant has been serving Cantonese-style Chinese cuisine on Vancouver's Kingsway corridor since 2010, with a menu that leans into traditional Hong Kong-style cooking — think whole braised chicken, lobster in lotus leaves, and house-made BBQ pork cheek, all available in limited daily quantities. The air-conditioned dining room offers a full sit-down table-service experience in a neighbourhood-focused setting. Cyclists looking for a substantial hot meal mid-tour will find a wide-ranging menu with both familiar and adventurous options.
35ca5bed9e: Bonta is an authentically Italian restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, run by an owner with over 20 years of multiregional Italian cuisine experience. The kitchen leans on generational recipes and locally sourced artisanal ingredients, spanning antipasti, house-made pasta, pizza, and mains such as saffron lamb shank with house gnocchi. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and online ordering is supported.
3f15d02042: Soi Ram is a Thai restaurant located in Tsawwassen, BC, serving the Delta Street corridor. As a sit-down Thai restaurant, it would offer a warm meal stop for cyclists exploring the South Delta area near the Tsawwassen ferry terminal and the surrounding flat farmland cycling routes.
766116ef2f: Kobe Japanese Steakhouse is a long-running teppanyaki-style restaurant in Vancouver's West End, billing itself as 'a party at every table' — a nod to the theatrical tableside cooking style. Located on Alberni Street near the Coal Harbour waterfront, it occupies a standalone building and draws both locals and visitors for Japanese cuisine in a lively setting. A touring cyclist finishing a ride in downtown Vancouver would find a sit-down dinner destination within easy reach of the seawall.
91c0b6336a: El Santo is a contemporary Mexican restaurant in the heart of New Westminster, named after El Santo — the legendary masked luchador and childhood hero of founder Alejandro Diaz. Since opening in 2015, Executive Chef Sam Fabbro has built a menu around Pacific Northwest ingredients with a Mexican twist, including house-made corn tortillas and regional specialties not found elsewhere on the Canadian coast. The restaurant also runs el Santo CAN, a community fundraising initiative that has raised over $120,000 for the Canucks Autism Network.
8e6e7f0567: Mèreon is a French-inspired bistro in West Vancouver offering brunch, happy hour, and dinner menus that blend classic French technique with fresh West Coast ingredients. The restaurant was founded by Ophelia Arida and features menu development by Chef Emmanuel Joinville, who trained at a Michelin 3-starred restaurant in Dijon before becoming known in Vancouver for the long-running Jules Bistro in Gastown. The bistro seats up to 50 guests and is committed to locally sourced produce and house-made preparations throughout.
4678d82a73: A family-friendly breakfast and lunch cafe in Nelson specializing in homemade fare and sandwiches. Offering indoor seating on Kootenay Street, it provides a casual dining stop for cyclists passing through downtown Nelson.
7fc5091683: Kitchen on the Ridge is a family-owned restaurant that has been serving Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows since 2005, offering a full dine-in menu alongside weekend Dim Sum service. Situated on the Lougheed Highway, it is a convenient meal stop for cyclists traveling through the Fraser Valley corridor.
9b1ad53755: Thai Town Restaurant is an authentic Thai eatery on Vancouver's busy Granville Street, serving dishes like Traditional Pad Thai with tamarind, Red and Green Curries, Spicy Drunken Noodle, and Som-Tum. The kitchen emphasizes the classic Thai balance of sweet, umami, sour, and spicy. Online ordering with pickup is available, making it convenient for cyclists passing through central Vancouver.
2e7cc2e022: Cofee Loft is a neighbourhood cafe in Burnaby's Metrotown area serving coffee alongside a varied menu of salads, soups, sandwiches, cakes, and ice cream. It offers indoor seating in a smoke-free environment, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking for a sit-down meal or snack near the Metrotown corridor.
b66bcf9816: Rusticana Coffee is a café located in Sidney, BC, a compact waterfront town on the Saanich Peninsula that serves as a gateway to the Gulf Islands ferry network and is popular with touring cyclists. The 'Ltd' in its Facebook name suggests an established local business rather than a pop-up or chain outlet. Sidney's walkable downtown core and proximity to the Lochside Regional Trail make cafés here natural rest stops for cyclists arriving or departing via the nearby ferry terminal.
44f84e2805: Trees Organic Coffee is a Vancouver-area cafe chain that has been operating since 1996, known for its in-house roasted organic coffee and award-winning homemade cheesecakes voted best in Vancouver. The Gilmore location in Burnaby is one of 13–14 locations across the region. The menu extends beyond coffee to include sandwiches, baked goods, and a lunch selection, making it a practical stop for a mid-ride meal.
7cb742987b: Tacofino is a BC-born West Coast beach food chain with roots in Tofino, now operating multiple Lower Mainland locations including this White Rock outpost on Johnston Road. The restaurant serves Mexican-inspired fare with a casual, coastal vibe well suited to a post-ride meal. Pickup and third-party delivery options make it easy to grab food quickly and get back on the road.
2bc78f96bc: Uptown Pizza & Sports Bar is Nelson's self-described only dedicated sports bar, housed within the Adventure Hotel on Vernon Street in the heart of downtown. The venue features wall-to-wall flat screens, a rotating lineup of BC craft beers on tap from breweries like Mt. Begbie, Four Winds, and Fernie Brewing, and a full pub menu of hand-made pizzas, burgers, and wings prepared by an in-house chef. Touring cyclists can also take advantage of takeout and delivery service if they prefer to eat elsewhere.
bd9d28fda6: The Eatery has been Kitsilano's home for creative sushi and Japanese fusion since 1983, earning a devoted local following over four decades on West Broadway. Billed as 'The Funkiest Place for Japanese Food,' it combines inventive rolls and Japanese dishes with a lively, music-filled atmosphere. A touring cyclist finishing a ride on the Arbutus Greenway or along the Vancouver waterfront would find it a well-placed stop for a sit-down meal or a takeout order.
eaba37182a: Subcity Donair is a multi-location Okanagan chain specializing in beef and chicken donairs made with a proprietary blend of 23 herbs and spices, served with a choice of seven sauces. The downtown Kelowna location sits on Bernard Avenue, the city's main commercial street, making it a convenient mid-ride stop. A dedicated vegetarian menu featuring falafel and veggie subs broadens its appeal to cyclists with varied dietary needs.
baaaf62a56: CRAFT Beer Market sits right on Victoria Harbour, offering waterfront views from its surf lounge and an all-year patio. A full-service restaurant and bar with over 100 beers on tap, craft cocktails, and a sharing-style food menu, it is a lively chain destination known for its extensive draft selection and group-friendly spaces. Cyclists arriving at the Inner Harbour area will find it a substantial stop for a meal or post-ride drinks.
db12f47cbb: Siam Le Bien is an authentic Thai restaurant and bar established in 2023 on Burnaby's Hastings Street, named for Siam (the former name of Thailand) and the French word for 'good.' The kitchen emphasizes fresh, high-quality ingredients and a defining balance of sweetness, sourness, saltiness, spiciness, and umami across a wide menu of classic Thai dishes. Touring cyclists can dine in or order takeout via Uber Eats and DoorDash.
656980f611: Hoang Gia is a Vietnamese restaurant in Kelowna near Costco on Highway 97 N, specializing in pho, sushi, and noodles. The restaurant distinguishes itself by using Brant Lake Wagyu Beef — naturally raised, hormone-free Alberta beef — in all beef dishes. Online reservations are available and the dining room is described as having a distinct atmosphere.
4c5578ec57: Wendy's on Grandview Highway is a full-service fast food restaurant offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, salads, breakfast, and Frosty desserts. The location features a drive-through and supports mobile ordering and mobile payment. It is one of five Vancouver Wendy's locations and sits along a major east-west arterial road.
b89608836e: A French-inspired café perched on a small hill above the Snug Cove ferry landing on Bowen Island, with sweeping views of ocean, mountains, and forest. In operation since 2009, it draws both locals and visitors with fresh-baked breads, viennoiserie, rich lattes, and grilled paninis. For touring cyclists arriving by ferry, it offers a welcoming first stop with outdoor seating, Wi-Fi, and vegetarian and vegan options.
c57e95afbc: Boston Pizza is a well-established Canadian casual dining chain and sports bar serving gourmet pizzas, pasta, wings, and more, with roots going back to Edmonton in 1964. The Fort St. John location on Alaska Road North serves as a full sit-down restaurant with dine-in and delivery options. For touring cyclists passing through this northern BC hub on the Alaska Highway corridor, it offers a reliable, high-capacity meal stop with a broad menu.
aa61b91138: Poké Aye is a Hawaiian-cuisine restaurant in Langford (Greater Victoria), specializing in poke bowls. Located in a unit-numbered commercial space (Unit 103), it sits in the western suburban corridor popular with cyclists commuting or touring between Langford and Victoria. The restaurant's name and Facebook branding are consistent with a contemporary, counter-service poke concept.
80f21bdefd: Ministère of Seafood is a French-inspired seafood bistro in East Abbotsford, founded by Executive Red Seal Chef Gaya and General Manager Ishara, whose combined decades of experience span renowned hotels and restaurants worldwide. The menu centres on fresh BC seafood — spot prawns, halibut, Dungeness crab, and lobster — prepared with French and Italian technique, alongside a broad cocktail and wine program. It won a Community Votes Abbotsford 2025 award and offers family-sized take-home meals as well as a three-course dinner experience.
e4c546eefd: Bozzini's is a restaurant in North Vancouver with established operating hours and local service. A dining option for the community with both weekday and weekend availability.
81fd5b3941: Snackshot is a Chinese and dessert-focused cafe on Kingsway in Vancouver. It offers a casual environment for customers seeking light meals and Asian sweets.
b8591c3fc4: Simonholt is a locally operated full-service restaurant in Nanaimo's north end, featuring a mainly from-scratch kitchen with a focus on fresh local seafood, an extensive wine selection, and a fully stocked bar. The restaurant offers three patios including a rooftop deck with ocean and mountain views, and can accommodate groups of up to 150 for corporate and club events. It regularly hosts live music from local and touring artists, giving it a lively community atmosphere well beyond a typical dinner stop.
d62c5028d2: A Wendy's fast food location on Hawthorne Avenue in Abbotsford offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, salads, and breakfast. The restaurant operates a drive-thru as well as dine-in seating and supports mobile ordering and payment. For a touring cyclist passing through the Abbotsford area, it offers a reliable late-night food option with free Wi-Fi.
172aa0c320: Aroy Thai Kitchen is a family-owned Thai restaurant situated in Rocky Point Centre in Port Moody, where 'aroy' means 'delicious' in Thai. The kitchen prides itself on fresh, locally sourced vegetables picked daily and house-made sauces, dressings, and hand-rolled spring rolls prepared from scratch each day. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down restaurant offering both dine-in and takeout, with delivery available through Skip The Dishes and DoorDash.
c2ddaaeb57: Bean to Cup is a specialty coffee house in Vernon that has been roasting its own beans since 1998 — notably, it claims to be the only specialty coffee bar in the North Okanagan doing so in-house. The cafe offers gourmet espresso drinks alongside a full breakfast and lunch menu of wraps, paninis, soups, and fresh-baked pastries, set in a space that includes a garden patio. It has earned three consecutive TripAdvisor Certificates of Excellence (2017–2019) and accepts Bitcoin Lightning payments.
a8419fa15b: Sushi-Q is a Canadian chain founded in 1997 and one of the country's early pioneers of grab-and-go sushi, serving sushi rolls, sashimi, nigiri, and Japanese ramen. The Burnaby outlet is located inside Lougheed Town Centre mall. The chain emphasises fresh daily preparation and chef-inspired presentation as its main differentiators.
acffbd5cb3: Van 168 Coffee is a family-run Vietnamese cafe and restaurant on Kingsway founded by Lynda, who brought her mother's Northern Vietnamese recipes to Vancouver nearly 40 years after immigrating. The menu centres on authentic pho, bun noodle soups (including regional specialties like Bun Bo Hue and freshwater snail vermicelli), rice plates, and Vietnamese iced coffee. It opened in 2023 and occupies a storefront unit in a mixed-use building on one of Vancouver's main east-side corridors.
69fd29cc37: Established in 1998, Quality Coffee Systems is the official JURA Hospitality and Service Centre for Western Canada, operating a public showroom in Burnaby where visitors can see live espresso machine demonstrations and receive expert guidance on commercial and residential equipment. The company carries premium European brands including JURA, Profitec, Olympia Express, and Rocket, alongside coffee beans, grinders, and accessories. A touring cyclist could stop in to purchase coffee beans or small accessories, though this is fundamentally a specialty equipment retailer and repair shop rather than a place to get a drink.
861debb372: The Dining Commons is Capilano University's main on-campus cafeteria in North Vancouver, housed in a two-storey building serving the university community. It is listed under CapU's student services as the primary food and dining destination on campus. Cyclists in the North Shore area may find it a convenient stop given its location on an established university campus.
0caed3e852: Moore's Bakery of Kerrisdale is one of Vancouver's oldest storefronts, operating since the 1930s with Dutch and British baking traditions passed down through a family-owned business. The bakery produces handmade breads, buns, pastries, cakes, cookies, and savoury items fresh daily on site. A touring cyclist passing through Kerrisdale will find a genuine neighbourhood institution offering hearty baked goods well suited for fuelling a ride.
83a2e29e73: Oretachi Curry is the Canadian outpost of an Osaka, Japan original, serving authentic Japanese curry rice and a signature curry ramen built on a house-made shrimp oil and ebi miso broth. Every order gets a freshly panko-fried katsu made in-house, and the curry blend draws on over 20 spices with locally sourced BC ingredients. The restaurant sits in the Riley Park stretch of Main Street, one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors, and offers online ordering and takeout for riders on the move.
b549698923: N.S.C.S. Discovery Café is a burger and American food restaurant in Vancouver staffed by culinary school students. It offers a casual dining experience with outdoor seating and is licensed with beer on tap, making it a welcoming stop for touring cyclists.
bb72b22105: Pacifico Pizzeria & Ristorante is a downtown Vancouver Italian restaurant that combines Pacific Northwest ingredients with traditional Italian recipes and has earned recognition as Vancouver's Best Pizzeria. The Smithe Street location offers dine-in and online takeout or delivery, with a second outpost near English Bay on Davie Street. It sits in the heart of the city core, making it a practical meal stop for cyclists on urban routes.
7c0230cd8c: Shio Japanese Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant that opened on The High Street in Coquitlam in May 2018, serving a mix of traditional sushi and original dishes like the Katsu Burger. It sits in a busy commercial hub near Douglas College, Lafarge Lake, and Coquitlam Centre, with free underground parking accessible off Atlantic Ave. Dine-in and takeout are both available, with Uber Eats delivery as well.
e046f20ee7: A pizza restaurant in Ucluelet on the west coast of Vancouver Island. Situated along the route to the Pacific Rim region, it could be a convenient dinner stop for cyclists touring the area.
2eddd8556a: A Vietnamese sandwich shop specializing in bánh mì (traditional Vietnamese sandwiches) in Chilliwack. Operates as a fast-food takeout establishment serving fresh sandwich fare to locals and travelers.
0111e18cef: Shanghai Dumpling King is an authentic Shanghai pot sticker restaurant in Richmond specializing in Huaiyang-style dumplings with thin wrappers, crisp bottoms, and abundant juices. The owner hand-grinds the meat and hand-rolls the wrappers, blending traditional Shanghai pot sticker technique with northeastern Chinese dumpling influences. Cyclists passing through Richmond's Westminster Highway corridor can order online for quick pick-up.
9458926a8e: Diplomat Bakery is a family-owned European-style dessert bakery operating since 1996, specializing in luxury cakes, cheesecakes, and espresso-based drinks. Located on London Road in Richmond near the Dyke Road entrance, it sits close to popular cycling routes along the Richmond dyke trail system. Cyclists can stop in for a range of coffee drinks, cakes by the slice, or pre-order whole cakes for pickup.
0577164b7e: Freddy's Brewpub is a pub located in Kelowna on McCurdy Road. The name and amenity tags suggest it operates as both a craft brewery and public house. Limited verifiable information is available due to website access issues.
74b8ce650e: Cibo & Vine Ristorante is an Italian restaurant on Beach Avenue in Peachland, serving housemade pasta, artisan pizza, and an extensive drinks list anchored by Okanagan wines. The restaurant operates two outdoor patios overlooking Lake Okanagan and the boutiques along Beach Ave, making it a scenic lakeshore stop on the Okanagan cycling corridor. It was formerly known as The Waterfront Grill & Pizzeria.
955ca6ae40: Cookie's Ice Cream Co. is a family-owned, small-batch ice cream shop in the historic Ladner Village neighbourhood of Delta, offering premium barrel-churned ice cream, sorbet, and sherbet across 90+ rotating flavours served in cups, cones, or house-made cookies. Beyond the scoop shop, they operate a mobile fleet — trailer, truck, and tricycle — serving events across the Lower Mainland. Specialty items include made-in-house ice cream sandwiches and cakes, hot chocolate bombs, and custom decorated sugar cookies.
4c3e60539e: Le Marché St. George is a home-based café and general store in Vancouver that also serves as an occasional event space. The business blends residential and commercial functions in a community-oriented model. Touring cyclists can visit for refreshments, food, and locally-sourced supplies.
68c02a535c: Kulinarya is an authentic Filipino restaurant established in 2009 on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, cooking family recipes anchored in fresh local ingredients. It is known for dishes like kare-kare and sinigang, as well as a communal Kamayan feast served directly on banana leaves. The restaurant offers both dine-in and takeout, making it a viable stop for cyclists riding one of Vancouver's most active commercial corridors.
570bb869f4: Sushi Garden is a Japanese restaurant chain with three Burnaby locations, offering a broad sushi menu in a casual sit-down setting. The Brentwood branch is located on Lougheed Highway near Brentwood Town Centre, on a major arterial route through Burnaby. Online ordering and takeout are available at all branches.
104c10cf00: Oliver's Tearoom is the High Tea section of Dickens Sweets and British Museum, an immersive British-themed complex in downtown Chilliwack that also houses a Victorian-era museum, a replica Tally Ho pub, Pickwick's Pie Shop, and a British sweet and grocery shop. The multi-storey museum takes visitors through Royal history, a vintage office, Fred's Toyshop, and a Titanic exhibit. Cycling visitors can pick up takeout savories — sausage rolls, steak pies, and baked goods — from Pickwick's, making it an unusual and memorable detour.
ab250ffba7: Fern Cafe and Bakery is a 100% vegan bakery cafe tucked into the Fernwood neighbourhood of Victoria, established in 2018 and owner-operated by a couple with over a decade of plant-based cooking experience. The menu leans into vegan comfort food — burgers, poutine, mac and cheese, fried chickun, all-day breakfast — alongside specialty pastries and espresso drinks made entirely in-house from scratch. Their famously oversized cinnamon buns and fresh-daily doughnuts have earned a strong local following, making it a worthwhile stop for plant-based touring cyclists passing through central Victoria.
9b6832ed8f: A Whistler institution since 2003, the Southside Diner serves hearty homestyle breakfasts and burgers in an old-school diner atmosphere at Whistler's Creekside neighbourhood. The building also houses Southside Suds, described as Creekside's only coin-operated laundromat, making it an unusually practical stop for multi-day touring cyclists who need to refresh their kit. The diner has cultivated a loyal following among both locals and visitors over more than two decades.
98f59889df: Big Star Sandwich Co. is a Lower Mainland sandwich chain founded in 2013, now operating six locations including this Langley outpost. Sandwiches are built on fresh-baked filone bread with meats cooked in-house — beef slow-roasted overnight for 13 hours, hand-pulled turkey breast, and authentically prepared corned beef. Catering is available for groups, and a loyalty rewards program makes it a worthwhile repeat stop on a multi-day tour through the Fraser Valley.
31216e790e: Brass Monkey Taproom is a craft microbrewery and taproom on Bay Street in Victoria, brewing its own beer on-site and serving a food menu that includes burgers and wings. The venue runs a packed weekly events calendar — trivia leagues, specialty cask tappings, bingo nights, and live DJ sets — giving it a lively neighbourhood pub atmosphere. It sits a short ride from Victoria's inner harbour in a mixed residential-commercial area, making it a natural end-of-ride destination for cyclists exploring the city.
9d02bb3746: Basalt Wine & Salumeria is a dine-in restaurant and wine bar located in the heart of Whistler Village, describing itself as 'Authentic. Lively. Local.' The salumeria focus suggests a menu centred on cured meats, charcuterie, and wine. Outdoor seating makes it a pleasant stop after a ride through the Sea-to-Sky corridor.
ddcb1c72c7: McClennan Car/Truck Stop is a casual family dining restaurant and truck stop located on McLennan Road on the outskirts of Valemount, BC. Positioned along a route through the Robson Valley, it serves travellers — including those passing through on Highway 5 — looking for a sit-down meal. The 'Where You're Part Of the Family' tagline suggests a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere typical of rural BC roadside stops.
334246169f: Secret Zone Bar & Grill is a neighbourhood sports bar near the Burquitlam SkyTrain station serving wings, burgers, pasta, and cocktails. It screens major sporting events including UFC, Champions League, NHL, NBA, and the World Cup. Online ordering and pickup make it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Burquitlam corridor.
01ef79f311: Bodega on Main is an updated take on a long-standing Vancouver Spanish tapas institution, serving authentic tapas made with locally sourced and specialty imported ingredients, including OceanWise certified seafood. The 75-seat lounge and dining area features custom leather seating, hand-carved bar stools, and a blend of vintage artwork and antique accents. Touring cyclists will find a full-service sit-down restaurant with a well-stocked bar, takeout options, and delivery partnerships.
ad56d4ab97: The Corner Stone Bistro is a casual coffee shop and cafe in North Vancouver that welcomes the cycling community. It offers a comfortable outdoor seating area and complimentary Wi-Fi—practical amenities for touring cyclists looking for a break.
b35ab5865f: Tamam is a fine-dining Palestinian restaurant on East Hastings Street in Vancouver, serving scratch-made dishes such as freekeh with lamb shanks, fried Mediterranean sea bass, kibbeh, and kunafah alongside Lebanese arak and BC VQA wines. The restaurant operates as a cultural gathering space and regularly runs community fundraisers with proceeds directed to Gaza. A touring cyclist will find a thoughtful menu with clearly labelled vegan and gluten-free options, catering available, and online ordering.
cea1a6aab2: Café de Gourmet is an award-winning neighbourhood sandwich café in Ladner, BC, operated by the same owners since they purchased it years ago. Everything is made fresh daily in-house, from handcrafted sandwiches and home-style soups to baked goods from their own bakery. Located in the heart of Ladner near South Delta cycling routes, it offers a full espresso bar and call-ahead takeout for cyclists in a hurry.
26cfaaeb5c: Donair Affair is a BC-based fast-food chain approaching 25 years in operation, specializing in donair kebabs that blend Middle Eastern and Canadian flavors using beef, lamb, chicken, or falafel. The Maple Ridge location on Dewdney Trunk Road is one of more than 20 outlets across the Lower Mainland and Fraser Valley. It offers a casual sit-down atmosphere alongside takeout and online ordering, making it a convenient stop for a filling wrap or platter mid-ride.
e7f7d4fee2: A family restaurant in Coldstream offering regional cuisine with outdoor seating and takeaway service. The venue is wheelchair-accessible with customer washrooms and welcomes both dine-in and take-away customers.
dd9ebcaac8: Rocky Point Ice Cream started as a small scoop shack at Rocky Point Park in Port Moody in 1997 and has grown into a beloved multi-location artisan ice cream brand — operating BC's first licensed dairy plant dedicated exclusively to craft ice cream production. The original Port Moody location sits right in Rocky Point Park, making it a natural and satisfying stop for cyclists on the area's waterfront trails. All ice cream is handcrafted from scratch, with rotating seasonal flavours and a permanent selection that includes plant-based options.
2360d426bf: Dining Wok Shanghai Restaurant is a casual dine-in Chinese restaurant in White Rock specializing in Sichuan, Peking, and Shanghai cuisine. The relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere makes it a comfortable stop for a sit-down meal. Online ordering is available for those who prefer takeout.
217c654422: Papa John's is an international pizza chain with over 5,000 locations in 44 countries, emphasizing fresh dough and quality ingredients under the 'Better Ingredients. Better Pizza.' brand promise. This Chilliwack location at McCallum Road offers carryout and delivery pizza. It is a familiar, predictable refuelling option for touring cyclists moving through the Fraser Valley corridor.
46d6d64a65: Scratch Kitchen is a North Shore artisan pizza restaurant that started in Deep Cove in 2018 and expanded to Central Lonsdale in 2024, built around made-from-scratch food using fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The menu spans creative 12-inch pizzas, sharing plates, salads, and rice bowls, with a carefully curated list of local craft beer and BC wine. Both locations offer strong plant-based and gluten-free options throughout the menu, making it a flexible stop for cyclists with dietary needs.
088776d687: The Copper Room is the signature evening dining venue at Harrison Hot Springs Resort & Spa, situated on the shores of Harrison Lake beneath the Coastal Mountains. It offers a multi-format dinner menu (à la carte, table d'hôte, children's menu, and a drink menu) alongside nightly live music and an open dance floor, making it one of the more theatrical dining experiences in the Fraser Valley. 72ad5d97dc: A Mexican restaurant located on Highway 97 in Oliver, BC. Serves as a dining option for local residents and traveling cyclists passing through the area.

This North Vancouver location sits on the second floor and is an indoor-only dining environment.
2f7d3fdf47: Lamb Hot Pot is a casual Chinese hotpot restaurant in a Richmond strip mall specializing in lamb-based pots served with bones, marrow, and cumin lamb skewers. The restaurant features a DIY dipping sauce cart and offers plastic gloves for hands-on eating — a fun, communal experience well suited to groups. Reviewers highlight generous portions and a welcoming atmosphere despite the no-frills setting.
f44c3cb626: Tenen Restaurant is a Serbian and Eastern European diner in Burnaby, founded in 2015 by two childhood friends from Knin — a Roman-era town whose ancient name, Tenen, the restaurant carries. The menu features hearty Balkan staples like chevapi, karadjordjeva schnitzel, cabbage rolls, and traditional meze, served in a kitschy, homey atmosphere that reviewers describe as feeling like coming home. A loyalty program and catering service round out the offering.
541bf9b0c4: La Cuisson Cafe is a family-owned artisan coffee shop and in-house roaster in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, founded in 2004 by owner Jason Hsu after 30 years of coffee expertise. The café is known for rare and specialty brewing methods including syphon-style, pour-over, and Italian-style coffees using single-origin beans sourced globally and roasted weekly on-site. It also offers an extensive menu of fresh in-house baked pastries, toasts, sandwiches, waffles, and desserts, making it a well-rounded café stop.
2021679456: Old Town Ice Cream is an ice cream shop located in the historic downtown core of Ladysmith on Vancouver Island. Ladysmith's First Avenue is a heritage commercial strip popular with cyclists riding the E&N corridor or touring the island, making a sweet stop here a natural fit for a long ride.
4425bbda7e: The Peri Peri Shack is a North Vancouver restaurant specializing in flame-grilled chicken marinated for 24 hours in a peri peri spice blend, available in seven heat levels from Mild to Peri Nero. The concept draws on the culinary tradition of the African bird's eye chili, carried to the Iberian Peninsula by Portuguese explorers and now reimagined as a cornerstone of the local community. Cyclists can fuel up on generous sharing packs, a range of sides, and a vegetarian paneer option, with online ordering also available.
c6a591b739: La Meza Grill is a family-owned Filipino restaurant that has been serving traditional regional cuisine in North Delta since June 2014. The extensive menu draws on culinary traditions from across the Philippine archipelago — from grilled chicken inasal and pork sisig to breakfast silog plates — offering a hungry cyclist a substantial and flavourful sit-down meal. DoorDash delivery is also available for those who prefer to eat on the go.
444bf39eee: Mink is an artisan chocolate café in downtown Vancouver specializing in handcrafted ganache chocolate bars and bonbons made with Cacao Barry chocolate. The signature experience is a personal fondue where guests roast marshmallows at their table and dip them in their choice of milk, dark, or dairy-free dark chocolate ganache. A touring cyclist would find it a memorable indulgence stop right in the city centre, across from a park at the Hornby cross street.
d6dd3ca4cf: A Persian bakery located on Marine Drive in North Vancouver with indoor and outdoor seating. Offers fresh-baked goods in a smoke-free environment.
4481b7ec6d: Oystercatcher is a waterfront seafood and cocktail bar on Salt Spring Island, opened in 2002 and part of the locally-owned Salt Spring Group. Cyclists can dine casually by the river-rock fireplace or on the waterfront deck, with a menu highlighting local seafood, Salt Spring lamb, and regional craft beverages. Its Ganges harbour location makes it a natural stop on a Salt Spring Island cycling loop.
f3b0b72be9: The Ruby is a locally owned scratch brunch restaurant with three Victoria locations, open since 2015 and built around relationships with local suppliers. It offers a refined take on eclectic southern brunch fare paired with the city's best vinyl collection and warmly attentive service. A touring cyclist arriving hungry would find generous, hearty dishes with strong vegan and gluten-free options well-suited to refuelling.
142d425f4d: Szechuan Chili Restaurant has been serving bold, spice-forward Szechuan cuisine on Vancouver's West 6th Avenue since 2001. Signature dishes include Dry Szechuan Chili Ginger Beef, General Tso's Chicken, and a wide range of dumplings and noodle dishes. The restaurant offers both dine-in and online ordering with pickup, and also provides catering services.
b1c9ba1179: Big Bite Donair has been a fixture of the Lynn Valley community since 2016, serving authentic Middle Eastern and Mediterranean fare — kababs over open flame, homemade sauces, shawarma, falafel, and rich Afghan rice dishes. It is primarily a takeout operation with very limited seating, and the owner is widely praised by customers for personal attention and food quality. The restaurant also accepts Bitcoin Lightning payments, an unusual feature for a small neighbourhood eatery.
77ff799213: Sal y Limon is a family-founded Mexican restaurant inspired by traditional recipes from Manzanillo, Mexico, serving tacos, tortas, burritos, and other street food-style dishes. The South Surrey location is part of a small Vancouver-area chain created by four food enthusiasts who wanted to bring authentic Mexican flavour to BC. The restaurant emphasizes a welcoming, family-friendly atmosphere and offers both pick-up and delivery ordering.
34c8ca7ef3: Monarch Burger is a Vancouver cult-favourite burger spot born out of the legendary 'Dirty Burger' served at Campagnolo Upstairs, where a nightly limit of 35 burgers created a ravenous following. The kitchen uses dry-aged, freshly ground BC beef, hand-shaped buns baked at a local East Van bakery, and housemade pickles and sauces. In addition to its fixed Main Street location, Monarch runs seasonal pop-ups across the Lower Mainland.
a1e8395e7c: Yuan Soy Food (人和豆腐) is a Chinese fast food spot on East 1st Avenue in Vancouver's East Side, with a name suggesting a focus on soy and tofu-based dishes. Located on the ground floor of a commercial building, it offers a quick stop for cyclists riding through this neighbourhood. Its Instagram presence hints at an active local following, though the content is only accessible to logged-in users.
37eab427fa: Captain's Oven Pizza is an authentic Neapolitan-style pizzeria founded by siblings who trained in Naples and Istanbul before bringing their craft to Vancouver. Pizzas are hand-stretched daily using San Marzano tomatoes and fresh mozzarella, then baked in a 3-ton stone-brick oven imported from Tuscany. The North Vancouver location is one of five Lower Mainland outposts and offers dine-in, takeout, and local delivery.
7c271fde61: Lighthouse is a fast-food fish and chips spot in Richmond, BC. Fish and chips is a classic refuelling meal for touring cyclists, offering a hearty, portable option. The Richmond area is popular with cyclists on the Dyke Trail network, making local quick-service spots like this potentially convenient pit stops.
19c6a3112a: Kirin Seafood Restaurant is a long-established fine Cantonese seafood and dim sum restaurant that has been a fixture of Richmond's culinary scene since 1987, operating under world-class chefs with roots in Hong Kong's celebrated 'New Era' cuisine movement. The Richmond location sits in Three West Centre at Westminster Highway and No. 3 Road, offering elaborate menus featuring whole abalone, lobster, and dim sum alongside banquet and wedding services. For touring cyclists exploring Richmond, it represents a notable opportunity to experience high-end Cantonese cooking in one of Canada's most acclaimed Chinese-food destinations.
e2ef7cd340: Manoush'eh is a halal Lebanese and Levantine restaurant on Vancouver's Davie Street specializing in freshly baked manousheh — a traditional Middle Eastern flatbread topped with everything from za'atar and cheese to kafta, falafel, and soujouk. The menu also features plates, wraps, soups, and desserts such as knafeh, with many items clearly marked vegan or vegetarian. Reviewers consistently praise the handmade dough quality and the warm, community-oriented atmosphere.
23dd75f084: Amble Coffee is a specialty coffee shop and mobile truck tucked near the Vedder River, built around the philosophy of slowing down and connecting with nature. The 'Amble' name is intentional — it invites customers to linger over coffee or tea rather than rush. For touring cyclists finishing a ride along the Vedder, it offers a nature-adjacent café stop in Chilliwack.
964672c584: Kumare Express is the Vancouver outpost of the Kumare family of Filipino restaurants, which also operates a Richmond location and a roving street food truck serving the Lower Mainland. The kitchen leans into the full breadth of Filipino regional cooking — silog breakfast combos, slow-cooked soups like bulalo and sinigang, and fried appetizers like lumpiang Shanghai — alongside a bakery offering authentic Filipino pastries available for provincial shipping. The restaurant embraces both dry and saucy versions of classic dishes, reflecting the rich regional diversity of Filipino cuisine.
6bba9e3065: Breka Bakery & Café is a locally rooted, family-owned Vancouver institution open around the clock every day of the year, with roots in a German bakery founded in the Sunset neighbourhood in 2006. The Bute Street location is one of eight spread across the city, each carrying a wide range of baked goods, sandwiches, soups, snacks, and hot beverages alongside dedicated vegan and gluten-friendly items. It has become a neighbourhood anchor regularly voted among Vancouver's best cafés, and its 24/7 availability makes it an unusually reliable resupply stop for touring cyclists at any hour.
a4faef3b2b: Peaceful Restaurant has served Northern Chinese cuisine in Vancouver since 1998, led by owner-chef Charlie Huang whose hand-pulled noodles, dumplings, and beef rolls have earned recognition from Food Network, USA Today, and local food media. The menu centres on Xi'an-inspired flavours — aromatic spices, bold sauces, and house-made dim sum — drawing on the culinary crossroads of the ancient Silk Road. Situated on West 4th Avenue, a key cycling corridor connecting Kitsilano to downtown Vancouver, it is a convenient mid-ride dining stop.
47acb37420: Hoshi is a Japanese cuisine restaurant tucked beneath the Burrard Bridge on Beach Avenue, steps from the Vancouver Harbour seawall—one of the city's busiest cycling routes. The kitchen spans everyday sushi, teishoku lunch sets, and traditional kaiseki multi-course dinners available by pre-order, offering a broad range of dining experiences in one spot. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the restaurant provides free validated parking in the adjacent building for those arriving by car or with a loaded touring bike.
2fa1b29c1d: 3 Dogs Brewing is a craft microbrewery and pub located in a commercial unit in Tsawwassen, BC. OSM tags it as both a brewery and a retail alcohol shop, suggesting it may operate a taproom alongside production. Tsawwassen is near the BC Ferries terminal and the US border crossing, making it a potential stop for cycle tourists on the Salish Sea corridor.
888e1498c1: Everest Indian & Nepalese Restaurant is a family-owned, licensed fine dining establishment in West Kelowna, BC, run by owner Ram Sapkota who immigrated from Nepal in 2007 and trained as a chef across Europe. The restaurant serves an extensive menu of authentic Indian and Nepalese cuisine—from tandoori specialties and Nepalese meals to fusion dishes—and has accumulated over 200 five-star Google reviews. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery with an online ordering option make it a flexible stop for touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan.
4e49628bc9: Bubble World is a Chinese restaurant located at 10090 152 Street in Surrey, BC. Beyond its OSM classification as a Chinese cuisine restaurant, no operational details are available as the business website is currently a placeholder.
c03945705d: Faubourg is a family-owned French boulangerie-pâtisserie founded in Vancouver in 2010, with three city locations including this Kerrisdale outpost. The bakery produces croissants, artisanal breads baked five times daily in a French deck oven, and a full range of pastries and macarons alongside a specialty coffee program. Touring cyclists will find a solid stop for quality food and espresso drinks in Vancouver's west side, with both dine-in and takeout available.
1ce6ecfb10: Wendy's is a major North American fast food chain specialising in fresh, never-frozen beef burgers, chicken sandwiches, and sides. This Chilliwack location offers drive-through and takeout service, making it a quick calorie stop for cyclists passing through the area. As a well-known chain it provides predictable food options including salads and chili alongside its signature burgers.
e57ed737bf: Langfords Fountain Diner is a restaurant in the Langford area west of Victoria, situated along Bryn Maur Road. The diner-style name suggests a casual, approachable eatery that could be a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists travelling through the western communities of Greater Victoria.
cba88466af: Gateway to India is an authentic Indian restaurant in Nanaimo serving dishes prepared with imported spices from both northern and southern India. The restaurant offers full dine-in service as well as takeout, with a menu spanning appetizers, curries, tandoor-baked breads, and desserts. Their spice blends and sauces are also sold at grocery stores across Vancouver Island and the Lower Mainland, reflecting the depth of their culinary operation.
a26613b76a: Pokérrito is a proudly Canadian fast-casual chain serving customizable poke bowls, sushi burritos, and warm bowls at its Marine Way Market location in Burnaby. Cyclists can build their own bowl choosing from a wide range of proteins, bases, and toppings, with many vegan and gluten-free options clearly marked on the menu. The location features indoor seating and air conditioning, making it a comfortable stop after a ride.
a57620ef4f: Saint Germain Bakery is an award-winning chain founded in 1984 that has trained under pastry chefs from France, Japan, Hong Kong, and Australia, earning multiple Culinary Olympics gold medals. The Kerrisdale location is a standalone street-front shop in a quiet residential neighbourhood, offering cakes, pastries, and baked goods. It is part of a broad BC and Ontario chain, with wholesale supply to major hotels and airlines.
d016dad643: Varsha Indian Kitchen is a modern Indian restaurant on Government Street in downtown Victoria, billing itself as Victoria's finest Indian restaurant. The menu blends traditional tandoor cooking — fish, prawns, paneer tikka, seekh kebab — with Indo-Chinese fusion dishes and a strong vegetarian lineup. Catering is also available, and online ordering and takeout make it convenient for cyclists passing through the inner harbour area.
dd0df3afaf: Tendon Kohaku is a downtown Vancouver outpost of an international Japanese tempura rice bowl (tendon) chain, born from a collaboration between Nadai Fujisoba — Japan's largest soba chain — and the Kings Know Group. The restaurant distinguishes itself with specially selected Hokkaido rice varieties, a proprietary vegetable-sesame oil blend, and a secret sauce slow-boiled for over 12 hours with more than 15 ingredients. The menu spans prawn, chicken, vegetable, eel, and sashimi tendon bowls alongside udon noodles, offering a hearty and distinctive meal stop in the heart of downtown Vancouver.
9295057e4f: Cha House is a bubble tea cafe located inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre, one of Kelowna's main retail hubs along Harvey Avenue. It specializes in milk tea, fruit tea, slushies, and a wide range of specialty drinks. For a touring cyclist, it offers a cool indoor respite from the Okanagan heat in a large, well-serviced mall environment.
9d8f3e3f03: Speed's Neighbourhood Pub has been a Ladner fixture since 1995, recently renovated under new ownership with a refreshed ambiance and river views over the historic Mitchell Bay waterway. The pub's patio overlooks a moored WWII-era vessel that inspired its logo, lending a uniquely local character. The menu spans classic pub fare through elevated dishes, with craft beers, wines, and cocktails alongside a kids menu and daily specials.
0a6b373fe0: A Vietnamese sandwich restaurant on the Trans-Canada Highway in Duncan. The menu features Vietnamese-style subs and sandwiches. Situated along a primary transportation corridor for Vancouver Island travelers.
3f106022ee: Vina Vietnamese Restaurant is a sit-down Vietnamese restaurant on Marine Drive in West Vancouver, offering both indoor and outdoor seating. It sits along a busy cycling corridor on the north shore, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists exploring the area. The restaurant maintains a smoke-free environment.
efda73d40f: Newton Pizza is a local pizza chain with a White Rock/South Surrey location on King George Boulevard, offering 36 specialty pizzas across multiple crust styles and sauces, plus wings, sides, and salads. The air-conditioned dine-in space and online ordering make it a practical meal stop along the King George corridor. It is one of three Surrey-area locations operated by the same brand.
7713929d44: Mongo Bongo is a Mongolian grill in New Westminster where diners build their own stir-fry bowl by selecting proteins, noodles, fresh vegetables, and sauces before watching chefs cook it on a large grill. The interactive concept — taglined 'a self-inspired creation' — makes it a filling, customizable stop with both lunch and dinner seatings. A full bar including beer, wine, and signature martinis rounds out the menu for cyclists looking for a proper sit-down meal.
9dd9885098: Steamship Grill & Bar occupies the historic 1924 Heritage Steamship Terminal building on Victoria's inner harbour, designed by Francis Rattenbury in the Beaux-Arts style and now a landmark directly across from the BC Legislature. The restaurant specializes in fresh local seafood — halibut, salmon, oysters, mussels — paired with BC wines and Victoria craft beers, served on a heated and covered harborfront patio voted one of Canada's Top 100. It can accommodate groups from 10 to 200, making it a practical stop for cycling tour groups passing through downtown Victoria.
f0c24a001d: B House is an Asian fusion eatery on Vancouver's lively Commercial Drive, blending Eastern and Western culinary traditions across an all-day menu that spans brunch, lunch, dinner, and happy hour snacks. The restaurant emphasizes fresh local ingredients, contemporary presentation, and a guest-first philosophy, with reservations available and walk-ins welcome. Its location on one of Vancouver's most walkable and cyclist-friendly strips makes it a natural rest stop on a Commercial Drive touring route.
a3fc7772ca: Okanagan Estate Wine Cellars is a Kitsilano neighbourhood wine shop devoted exclusively to British Columbia wines, sourced from regional winemakers and sold at winery prices with no obligations to hotels or restaurants. The 3669 West 4th Avenue location is one of two Vancouver stores and offers in-store wine flights and tastings alongside online ordering with in-store pickup. Staff are trained specifically in BC wine and food pairing, making it a useful stop for cyclists looking to bring home a bottle from their tour.
db19de4412: Kita no Donburi is a fast-food Japanese restaurant specializing in donburi rice bowls with seafood and sushi options. Located on Seymour Street in downtown Vancouver, it offers online ordering for quick, convenient meals. The restaurant provides indoor seating and wheelchair accessibility.
2b25c0e916: Pot Empire is a Chinese hotpot restaurant on Kingsway in Burnaby, offering the communal hot-pot dining style popular in Chinese cuisine. Located on a busy arterial road with transit and commercial amenities nearby, it sits along a corridor cycling tourists may pass through when travelling east-west across Burnaby. Hotpot restaurants typically offer a sit-down, customizable meal experience where diners cook ingredients in a simmering broth at the table.
7cd0bbf462: Ladurée is the iconic Parisian macaron brand operating a boutique and tea salon on downtown Vancouver's Robson Street shopping corridor. The space features Parisian-style tea rooms offering classic French dishes and an Afternoon Tea service, alongside a retail selection of macarons, pastries, jams, and specialty teas. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, making it a scenic urban rest stop, though it is a specialty destination rather than a practical resupply point for touring cyclists.
52c92b15ed: The Dime is a budget-friendly pub and late-night dining spot on Commercial Drive, one of 17 locations in the Warehouse Group chain that blends casual restaurant comfort with a bar and nightlife atmosphere. It sits in the heart of the eclectic 'Drive' neighbourhood, within easy cycling distance of Trout Lake, and the kitchen keeps turning out wings, burgers, and comfort food well into the night. The chain's value-oriented pricing and all-day service make it a practical stop for cyclists exploring East Vancouver.
42f542d958: The Junction is an LGBTQ-primary pub situated on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, the heart of the city's queer village. It operates as a full-service bar with a food menu, lounge drinks, and a regular events program including a guestlist system for special occasions. The venue is smoke-free, wheelchair accessible, and offers both indoor and outdoor seating.
774d6c5f27: Grace of India is a small, intimate Indian restaurant on Kingsway in Vancouver, founded in 2018 and helmed by a chef with over 25 years of experience drawing inspiration from across the Indian subcontinent. The menu spans tandoori specialties, karahi dishes, lamb, seafood, and a range of vegetarian options, with rotating weekday specials. Online ordering with pickup, delivery, and dine-in is available.
9ebda15105: Doe Coffee Roasters is a community-focused Vancouver café that small-batch roasts its own beans on-site and bakes all pastries fresh in-house overnight. The shop has removed tipping at checkout as a deliberate policy, and its Doe Pass subscription model reflects an unusually loyal neighbourhood following. A reviewer notes at least two locations — the original East Hastings spot and a newer Clarke Street outpost — suggesting growing local presence.
e2ed35ac3a: Fatburger Nanaimo is a casual burger restaurant on Rutherford Road offering cooked-to-order burgers made with fresh, never-frozen Alberta Angus beef. A Canadian-owned franchise of the iconic chain founded in 1952, it offers a broad menu including plant-based burgers, chicken, milkshakes, and poutine. Takeout and delivery are available, making it a convenient fuelling stop for cyclists in the south Nanaimo area.
969811bd7e: New Amsterdam Bakery is a family-run Surrey bakery with over 25 years of experience producing handmade specialty breads, custom cakes, and pastries with no chemicals or preservatives. The shop offers vegetarian (egg-free), vegan, sugar-free, and salt-free options alongside classics like cinnamon buns, danishes, and Black Forest cake. For a touring cyclist, it is a practical stop to pick up fresh bread or baked goods in a residential Surrey neighbourhood next to a TD Bank.
a5b51587d4: 101 Canada Boba is a Metro Vancouver bubble tea chain founded in 2020, specializing in grab-and-go fruit teas, milk teas, and seasonal specialty drinks made with premium ingredients sourced predominantly from Taiwan. The Cambie Street location is one of six BC stores in a rapidly expanding Canadian brand built around a streamlined, fast-service model. Cyclists passing through the Cambie corridor will find a quick refreshment stop with indoor seating but a strictly beverage-focused menu.
15f087fb93: The Thirsty Vintner is a winemaking kit shop that has operated at the same Shelbourne Street location in Victoria for over 25 years, offering customers the choice of making wine on-site with staff guidance or purchasing Winexpert kits to craft at home. The shop carries an extensive range spanning reds, whites, rosés, fruit wines, and oak-barrel aged varieties from wine regions around the world. Staff speak English, Cantonese, Mandarin, French, and Tagalog, making it an unusually welcoming stop for a diverse range of visitors.
5a0fdc030a: A Portuguese bakery specializing in nata (custard tarts). Business operational status and amenities are unclear from the 'Coming Soon' website.
e386ba8245: Gooi-Ga Korean BBQ is a Korean barbecue restaurant located in North Vancouver, offering the interactive tabletop grill experience typical of the genre. Korean BBQ restaurants are popular refuelling stops for touring cyclists seeking high-protein, communal meals with generous portions. The restaurant was verified as open in late December 2024 via OSM.
0301cefc4d: The Captain's Boil is a seafood boil franchise restaurant on Vancouver's busy Robson Street in the West End, serving fresh seafood feasts where diners choose their catch, flavour sauce, and heat level. The hands-on, bag-style dining format is designed for group feasting. The Robson Street location is wheelchair accessible and sits on a major pedestrian and cycling corridor.
85edbf484e: Le Coq Frit is a Korean-influenced fried chicken eatery with a North Vancouver outpost at Lonsdale Quay, serving hand-battered chicken in several styles—honey garlic soy, Nashville hot, sweet & spicy, and a double-fried 'real crispy' version—alongside chicken burgers on French brioche buns. The restaurant sources ingredients locally from Canadian farms and has committed to zero-waste, eco-friendly non-woven bag packaging. It is one of two Greater Vancouver locations, with menus available in multiple languages including Korean, French, and Chinese.
00a2d6ae1e: Kam Tou Seafood Restaurant serves authentic Chinese cuisine in Richmond's Sexsmith Road area, specializing in dim sum and seafood dishes such as steamed scallop dumplings and traditional dry-fried beef ho fun. The restaurant offers online ordering through its own website for those wanting takeout. It operates within a commercial unit, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through Richmond's busy Brighouse area.
b5b197dfb9: Chaiiwala of London is a South Asian-inspired chai cafe serving globally popular drinks like Karak Chaii and Pink Chaii alongside street food such as samosas, Aloo Paratha, and Butter Chicken Poutine. Located at King George Hub just one to two minutes' walk from the King George SkyTrain station, it's a convenient urban rest stop for cyclists connecting to the transit network. The cafe has outdoor seating, accepts cash and cards, and is wheelchair accessible.
e88ff2ef32: Sushi Mori has been a Coquitlam institution since 2008, serving Japanese fusion cuisine that blends fresh local ingredients with traditional techniques across an extensive menu of rolls, sashimi, and specialty dishes. The restaurant is known for its warm vintage interior with cozy booths, cherry blossom décor, and attentive service. It sits along the Barnet Highway corridor, making it a solid stop for cyclists travelling through Port Moody and Coquitlam.
b1763a0411: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain with a location in Chilliwack, notable for its commitment to quality ingredients: dough made fresh in-house from 100% Canadian wheat, organic tomato sauce, and meats raised without antibiotics. The menu spans pizzas, salads, sides, dips, and beverages, with a strong emphasis on plant-based and meat-free choices. Touring cyclists can call ahead or order online for pickup.
57a21a5255: Old Yale Brewing Co. is an award-winning craft brewery and kitchen that has been brewing since 1999, now running three taprooms across BC and Alberta. The Abbotsford location pours 15+ craft beers on tap and serves a full Campfire Kitchen menu in a family- and dog-friendly space with outdoor patio seating. Touring cyclists will find a well-rounded stop with a broad food and drink menu, including non-alcoholic options, in a comfortable sit-down setting.
e960c2cd08: A cafe and bakery on Galiano Island serving coffee and baked goods to visitors. Listed in the local dining directory as a community gathering spot. Offers casual refreshments to touring cyclists exploring the island.
f0d48afdc5: Beaucoup Bakery & Café is an award-winning French pastry destination in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, celebrated for delicate viennoiseries and East-West fusion creations such as the Peking Duck Croissant and Golden Mochi Croissant. Opened in 2012 and now co-owned by pastry chef Betty Hung and her brother Jacky, it has earned recognition from Lonely Planet, Forbes Travel Guide, and USA Today. Cyclists stopping here can expect espresso-based beverages, savoury seasonal sandwiches, and a rotating menu of baked goods.
13e23b358b: Meat & Bread is a well-established Vancouver sandwich chain with multiple locations, known for its house-roasted porchetta and craft sandwiches served on artisan bread. The Robson Street outpost sits in the heart of downtown Vancouver and offers breakfast sandwiches in the morning alongside a full lunch lineup. Cyclists passing through the city centre will find a compact, efficient spot for a hearty midday meal with online pickup ordering available.
3c2166e1da: Chipotle Mexican Grill is a fast-casual chain located near Douglas and Fort Streets in downtown Victoria, offering customizable burritos, bowls, quesadillas, tacos, and salads. The chain emphasizes its 'Food with Integrity' sourcing philosophy, using only 53 real ingredients from farms adhering to humane and sustainable practices. It's a reliable downtown stop for a quick, filling meal with in-store pickup and delivery options.
27f4a038ca: Momo Chen Cakes is a custom cake design studio specializing in elaborate wedding cakes, celebration cakes, and sweet treats such as cupcakes, cookies, cake pops, and macarons. The studio operates primarily on a consultation-and-order model, with an online shop offering a wide range of pre-designed cake options. It delivers to the Greater Vancouver area, making it a potential stop for cyclists seeking a sweet treat or special-order cake in the Richmond area.
7a7ca61862: Cilantro Indian Cuisine is a full-service Indian restaurant on West Broadway serving a broad menu of North and South Indian dishes alongside Indo-Chinese fusion items, with freshly ground spices and house-made chutneys. The kitchen has over 20 years of experience spanning India, Malaysia, the UK, and North America, and the Vancouver location is a second outpost of an original White Rock restaurant. Touring cyclists will find a wide range of dietary accommodations including vegan, gluten-free, and Jain dishes, plus online ordering for convenient takeout.
7832a4aad7: Cheese Slap is a Halal fusion restaurant on Vancouver's Granville Strip blending North American comfort food with South Asian flavors through dishes like Tandoori Chicken Cheesesteak, Butter Chicken Pizza, and Double Slap Smash Burgers. Set in a modern, renovated space at the heart of the downtown entertainment district, it caters to both lunchtime and late-night crowds. Free pickup ordering via the ZOMI platform makes it a practical and flavorful stop for cyclists passing through downtown Vancouver.
a5f69fedae: Big Way Hot Pot is a growing BC-based chain offering a self-serve individual hot pot experience with over 100 fresh ingredients and more than 18 broths and dry mixes. The Kerrisdale location sits on West 41st Avenue and is part of a network that spans Metro Vancouver and beyond. Diners cook their own selection of premium meats, seafood, and vegetables in flavourful broths ranging from Signature Mala to vegan-friendly Tomato.
7e9a2f09c1: Pür & Simple is a Canadian breakfast and brunch franchise with over 65 locations nationwide, with this Burnaby outpost anchored inside Station Square Metro Town. The restaurant specialises in creative comfort-food twists on classics — think Eggs Benedict, French toast, pancakes, and crepes — served in an upscale indoor setting with dedicated vegan and vegetarian menu sections. Cyclists coming off the Burnaby routes can order online for takeout or join a same-day waitlist on weekends.
ae8e4d9a2c: McDonald's on Ladner Trunk Road is a fast food restaurant in Tsawwassen offering burgers, breakfast, McCafé coffee, and snacks with a drive-through and outdoor patio seating. OSM records it as open 24/7, making it a reliable any-hour stop for touring cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen area. An on-site PlayPlace adds to its appeal as a rest and refuel point for families on tour.
9dcea82268: Obanhmi is a BC-based Vietnamese street food chain specializing in bánh mì sandwiches, fresh rolls, and iced coffee, now operating 9 locations across Metro Vancouver. The menu ranges from French-influenced cold cuts to fully vegan and halal options, all built on house-made ingredients and freshly baked baguettes. Cyclists passing through the West Broadway corridor can place an online order for fast in-store pickup.
4580039f37: Mykonos Pizza and Spaghetti House is a sit-down restaurant in Penticton, BC, offering pizza and pasta in a retail-building setting. It sits near the heart of Penticton, a popular hub on the Kettle Valley Rail Trail and Okanagan cycling routes, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through town.
9109b526b7: Rivers Restaurant is a casual diner in Chilliwack. It provides a convenient stop for touring cyclists looking for a sit-down meal. Limited details about specific amenities are currently available due to website access limitations.
6d9ab1e74f: The Dining Room Restaurant is set inside the historic Butchart family residence at The Butchart Gardens, one of Vancouver Island's most celebrated horticultural destinations. It serves a seasonally inspired Afternoon Tea and summer dinners using locally sourced ingredients, with menus that include gluten-free, vegetarian, and vegan options. Cyclists should be aware that paid admission to The Butchart Gardens is required to access the restaurant.
afc9ea3948: Breka Bakery & Café is a Vancouver-born, local family bakery operating continuously since 2006 across 8 locations, including this East Hastings outpost. It is one of the rare cafes open around the clock every day of the year, making it a reliable stop for cyclists at any hour. The menu spans artisan breads, pastries, sandwiches, soups, cakes, and hot beverages, with dedicated gluten-free and vegan selections.
2006c844a1: Prado Coffee is a Vancouver-born specialty coffee roaster that grew from a single bar into a multi-neighbourhood chain, with its Commercial Drive location anchoring the brand on one of the city's most cycling-friendly streets. Founded by Sammy with a stated goal of making great coffee and making people feel welcome, the company now roasts its own beans and ships subscriptions across the region. Cyclists riding the Drive will find a familiar neighbourhood café atmosphere at a location well-placed for an East Side route.
8a69a586b4: Esquimalt Roasting Company is a small-batch specialty coffee roastery that roasts its beans on-site in the Esquimalt neighbourhood of Victoria, British Columbia. The ERC Gateway café at 854 Esquimalt Road is one of two physical locations where customers can enjoy freshly roasted single-origin and blended coffees. Beans are also available for online purchase with delivery across BC and Canada, reflecting the roastery's community-focused, locally rooted ethos.
921d6da66d: The Cambie is one of Vancouver's oldest continuously operating bars, established in 1897 in the aftermath of the Great Vancouver Fire and a fixture in downtown Vancouver ever since. The venue runs as a full bar and grill with a patio, regular live music nights, karaoke, and a wide rotating selection of BC craft beer on tap. An associated Cambie Hostel operates on the same property, making it a natural waypoint for budget-conscious touring cyclists passing through the city.
fa59d1c098: Banchan Korean Bistro is a Korean restaurant in the Willoughby Town Centre mall in Langley, specializing in Korean, Korean Fried Chicken, and Asian cuisine. The restaurant operates primarily as a takeout destination with online ordering and real-time pickup notifications. It is a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the Willoughby commercial corridor.
9a76fdd862: Vietnamese restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End specializing in vegan and vegetarian dishes. Features both indoor and outdoor seating. A convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking quality Vietnamese food with dietary flexibility.
c0e0482722: Butter Lane Bake Shop is a North Vancouver bakery founded in 2014 and specializing in custom cakes for weddings, birthdays, and celebrations, alongside savoury catering and dessert bars. The shop operates from two locations: a dedicated bakery at 175 W 3rd St and a stall inside the Lonsdale Quay Market. Cyclists passing through the Lonsdale area or the Lower Lonsdale neighbourhood can stop in for freshly baked pastries and sweets.
c0ead186ea: Hoxton Gastown is a comedy-focused bar and restaurant in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, offering a chef-driven food menu alongside stand-up shows, weekly trivia nights, and a full bar. The venue doubles as a rentable creative space for film shoots, music videos, private parties, and brand activations. A touring cyclist stopping in Gastown would find a lively, food-forward spot with a distinct comedy-club atmosphere.
8f2dfecf96: Shawarma 2 Go Grill is an authentic Mediterranean fast-food restaurant in Richmond's Brighouse neighbourhood with over 30 years of shawarma expertise. The menu spans classic chicken and beef shawarma wraps, made-to-order falafels, lamb shank plates, and fusion items like shawarma poutine. It is one of two Richmond locations and offers online ordering with free in-store pickup.
9be991267a: Crust Bakery is an award-winning, female-owned French-inspired bakery and pastry shop that has been a downtown Victoria institution since 2013. Made-from-scratch breads, tarts, pastries, savoury snacks, and fresh Caffe Umbria espresso draw long lines of locals and visitors alike. A second location also operates at the Uptown Mall; the Fort Street shop is the original and sits within easy reach of Victoria's inner harbour cycling routes.
941d646069: Flourist is a bakery located on Commercial Street in Vancouver's vibrant Commercial Drive neighbourhood, a corridor well-known to local cyclists. The shop offers both indoor and outdoor seating and is wheelchair accessible.
9b040c66f5: Mount Pleasant Vintage & Provisions is a cocktail bar and Argentinian-style wood-fired grill tucked into Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, described on its own site as 'an unassuming cocktail bar disguised as a postmodern thrift shop.' The bar runs an ever-rotating cocktail list with an emphasis on forward-thinking techniques alongside elevated classic bar food cooked over wood and charcoal. It has earned recognition from The Pinnacle Guide (one pin, 'Excellent') and hosted the North America's 50 Best 2025 gala, signalling a destination-worthy stop for cyclists wanting a full sit-down meal and craft drinks.
b3101a0fb4: Home Restaurant is a long-established homestyle diner on the Lougheed Highway in Maple Ridge's West Central neighbourhood, part of a small BC chain with four locations. It has served the community for over 20 years, with a menu centred on all-day breakfast, comfort classics, and house-made pies. Pickup and third-party delivery are both available, making it a flexible stop for cyclists on the Lougheed corridor.
5a6112e623: A Starbucks coffee shop location on Douglas Street in Victoria offering drive-through and takeaway service. Convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking quick beverages and snacks.
536357a2fb: Rocky Point Ice Cream is a family-owned artisan ice cream brand that started as a seasonal scoop shack at Rocky Point Park in 1997 and now operates four Lower Mainland storefronts, including this one set within Coquitlam's Town Centre Park. All ice cream is made from scratch in BC's first licensed dairy plant dedicated exclusively to craft production, and the Coquitlam outpost offers outdoor seating in a park environment that suits a mid-ride stop well. The menu regularly features plant-based and lactose-free options alongside rotating seasonal flavours.
7a215de8c3: Bernie's is a supper club and cinema experience on Kelowna's main downtown strip, pairing a full-service restaurant with an in-house movie theatre. The menu leans heavily on Okanagan-region ingredients and a dedicated raw bar featuring oysters, seafood towers, and caviar. Touring cyclists looking for an upscale downtown Kelowna dinner stop will find local craft beers, creative cocktails, and a distinctive dine-in-film atmosphere.
56882de1f8: Moo-Lix Ice Cream is a local ice cream destination on Kelowna's main downtown commercial strip, Bernard Avenue. Situated in the heart of the city's walkable core, it offers a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring the Okanagan. The late evening hours make it a popular warm-weather treat stop after a day on the trail.
5f30c5418b: Grand Chinese Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant on Lougheed Highway in Burnaby, one of two locations operated by the same brand. The menu centres on Sichuan cuisine, Northern Chinese-style dim sum, Shanghai-style xiao long bao made fresh daily, and handcrafted Lanzhou noodles. The restaurant also caters private group events for parties of 10 to 200.
326796259c: A Greek restaurant in Surrey offering dine-in, takeout, and delivery service, with online ordering available. Catering services are offered for events of any size.
2bf5811594: The Bubble Tea Shop is a local café specializing in freshly made bubble teas, with a Vancouver location in the cycling-adjacent Olympic Village neighbourhood and a second location in Richmond. Beyond in-store drinks, the shop sells DIY bubble tea kits, loose-leaf teas, syrups, and toppings for home brewing. The Olympic Village location sits near the seawall cycling corridor, making it a plausible refreshment stop for cyclists on popular Vancouver routes.
280d190ca4: Jimmy's Lunch Box is a brunch cafe in Port Coquitlam offering online ordering and breakfast and brunch service. It provides a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking a substantial meal without a long wait.
12e77f3f4e: Trees Organic Coffee is a Vancouver cafe chain founded in 1996, celebrated for small-batch organic coffee roasting and award-winning homemade New York-style cheesecakes. The Joyce-Collingwood location is one of 13–14 stores across Greater Vancouver, offering a full menu of sandwiches, baked goods, teas, and cold drinks alongside the signature cheesecake. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available.
c4b514e024: Gary's is a small, farm-to-table dinner restaurant in Vancouver's Fairview neighbourhood, sourcing from over a dozen named BC farms and producers including suppliers from the Fraser Valley, Bowen Island, and the Gulf Islands. The intimate space seats up to 26 at a long communal table or 36 standing, making it well-suited for a group meal at the end of a day's ride. Walk-ins are welcome, though space is limited on busy evenings.
5928f3d6a0: Autostrada Oyster Bar and Grill is a seafood-forward restaurant perched in the small coastal community of Britannia Beach along the Sea-to-Sky corridor, operated by the same hospitality group behind a Vancouver Italian osteria. The menu leans into local Pacific ingredients — fresh-shucked oysters, BC albacore tuna, Salt Spring mussels, sockeye salmon — alongside pastas, burgers, and Italian-inspired starters. For a touring cyclist riding between Vancouver and Squamish, it is one of the few full-service dining options in this stretch of highway.
1ef87fe5c2: Hot House Pizza is a pizza restaurant in Victoria's Cook Street Village offering a broad menu of specialty, chicken, veggie, and classic pizzas alongside calzones, wings, and beverages. Multiple crust options are available including original, gourmet thin, whole wheat thin, and gluten free. It's a filling and convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through one of Victoria's busiest neighbourhood commercial strips.
1d7934940d: Tasty Indian Bistro is a contemporary Indian restaurant in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, one of three Lower Mainland locations alongside Delta and Abbotsford. The menu blends traditional subcontinental dishes—tandoori, curries, biryanis—with inventive fusion plates like Blue Cheese Naan and Tasty Bao Buns, plus a full cocktail bar.
