The Yaletown location offers a lounge, patio, private dining, and delivery, making it a versatile stop in a walkable, transit-friendly urban corridor.
2e0ee386e9: The 4 Mile Restaurant & Brewpub is a full-service pub and craft brewery located in View Royal on the Island Highway, one of Victoria's main cycling corridors. The venue houses a restaurant, an in-house brewery with a rotating lineup of craft beers, a sports bar called 4 Below, and a High Tea service — an unusually broad range for a single stop. Online ordering is available, and weekend brunch is offered, making it a viable option for cyclists at multiple points in the day.
fab779355d: The American is a bar on Main Street in central Vancouver. It offers a rest stop for food and drink during cycling tours through the city.
9beb01ebd7: Camy's Pizza has operated in Surrey since 1985 and claims to be the originator of the butter chicken pizza. Located in Townline Plaza (Cedar Hill), it offers an unusually broad menu spanning specialty pizzas, Indian cuisine, Greek dishes, pasta, calzones, and wings, all made to order. Both pickup and delivery are available, making it a practical food stop for cyclists passing through the area.
4a8c9cb197: Fiamo is an Italian kitchen, pizza, and wine bar in downtown Victoria occupying a warm, European-bistro-style space with exposed brick walls adorned with authentic Italian racing bikes and a centrepiece chandelier. The menu leans traditional Italian with Mediterranean, French, and Spanish influences, featuring wood-fired pizzas, house-made pasta, and a broad international wine list. A heated patio, a mezzanine for private gatherings of up to 18, and a late-night pizza service make it a versatile stop on the Yates Street corridor.
124fa056ba: Mr. Mike's is a Canadian casual steakhouse franchise with roots going back to 1960, serving premium steaks, burgers, pastas, salads, and shareable appetizers in a relaxed, unpretentious setting. The Fort St. John location sits on Alaska Road North along the Alaska Highway corridor, a natural waypoint for cyclists travelling through northeastern BC. The restaurant welcomes walk-ins and also offers takeout and delivery.
f5c1216ff3: Picnic K-Street Food is a compact Korean street food counter on the second floor of a New Westminster building, specialising in kimbap rolls, bibimbap, deopbap (rice bowl) dishes, and ddeokbokki. The menu is tightly focused on traditional Korean staples with both meat and tofu-based options, and online ordering enables quick pickup. Recent reviews consistently praise the food quality and the friendly owner.
9adae1ff9c: Hitoe Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant situated on West 4th Avenue in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, a well-travelled cycling corridor connecting downtown to the city's western districts. The restaurant distinguishes itself with an explicit gluten-free focus, prominently featured across its web presence. Touring cyclists passing through Kitsilano will find it a compact dining option on a route that sees heavy bicycle traffic year-round.
1c75939540: Papi's Seafood and Oyster Bar is a casual seafood restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, situated steps from the English Bay Seawall with a heated outdoor patio offering panoramic water views. The interior draws on Greek mythology, anchored by a full-wall mural of the sea goddess Amphitrite painted by local artists Arden Marow Ross and Peter Ricq. Part of the award-winning Viaggio Hospitality group, the restaurant focuses on fresh Pacific Northwest catches paired with sea-inspired cocktails.
ec9ca3c059: Tulip Donair is a Mediterranean and pizza restaurant in Chilliwack specializing in donairs — lamb, beef, chicken, and vegetarian falafel — alongside pizzas, salads, and poutines. The restaurant operates a streamlined online pickup ordering system, making it a practical quick-stop option for cyclists moving through the area. A kids' menu and a range of vegetarian items round out the offering for mixed groups.
5a3b04bcb9: Romeo's is a multi-location Vancouver Island pizza and Italian restaurant chain that has operated in this Westshore Town Centre location since 1982. The Langford restaurant offers dine-in with a patio, plus delivery and takeout across a broad menu of pizzas, pastas, burgers, and mains. It is part of a four-location family operation serving Vancouver Island since 1974, making it a reliable and familiar stop for cyclists riding through the Westshore corridor.
1a3dab70b8: Sushi Mura is a Japanese sushi chain that has operated in Vancouver since 2012, with the Main Street location one of several across the Lower Mainland. The restaurant emphasises daily-delivered fresh fish and a broad menu spanning rolls, sashimi, nigiri, noodle bowls, and hot appetisers. Dine-in, takeout, and third-party delivery are all offered, making it a convenient stop on a busy urban cycling corridor.
4883908ea7: Focacciaza is Vancouver's only focacceria on wheels, run by 'Focaccia Joe' — a Red Seal chef who studied sustainable food development and draws on Italian heritage to serve pizza al taglio (Roman-style focaccia) cut to order. The all-electric cart runs on zero emissions and is solar-panel assisted, using biodegradable paper-sleeve packaging throughout. Cyclists will appreciate the quick street-food format and the eco-conscious ethos of this one-of-a-kind mobile vendor.
ba15f6ecc1: Scratch Kitchen is a North Shore artisan pizza restaurant that started in Deep Cove in 2018 and expanded to Central Lonsdale in 2024; this record covers the Lonsdale location. Everything is made from scratch using fresh, locally sourced ingredients, with artisan pizzas, sharing plates, and salads paired alongside local craft beer and BC wine. The kitchen caters broadly to dietary needs, with gluten-free, dairy-free, and fully plant-based options available across the menu.
64ad0c648f: Sweethoney Dessert is a Hong Kong dessert chain with a Burnaby franchise offering handcrafted traditional desserts made fresh in-store, including mango pomelo sago, tofu pudding, and housemade grass jelly. The chain was founded to bring authentic Hong Kong dessert culture to North America using premium, natural ingredients. It is one of several BC locations and markets itself as a relaxed gathering spot.
a2c88e6314: GoodSide Pastry House is a Victoria neighbourhood pastry shop founded in 2020 by pastry chefs Haley Landa and Curtis Helm, each with over a decade of professional kitchen experience. The shop specializes in Euro-style cakes, croissants, and pastries crafted with traditional French techniques and West Coast-inspired flavours and ingredients. A rotating monthly menu and pre-order custom cakes make it a distinctive artisan food stop on Fort Street.
710dc173ce: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, operating since 1928 and known for its classic burgers made with fresh Canadian beef and locally sourced ingredients. This Surrey location is a full-service family restaurant offering breakfast, lunch, and dinner in a sit-down setting. Touring cyclists will find a familiar, accessible stop with takeout options available.
f1a8689732: Street Hawker is a halal-certified smashed burger and fried chicken fast-food joint in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, known for creative fusion riffs like Filipino adobo chicken sandos, kimchi burgers, and palabok poutine. All beef is 100% Canadian and chicken is hormone-free farm-fed, with an explicit commitment to plant-based options. Online ordering and pickup are available, making it a quick and filling stop for cyclists passing through the Main Street corridor.
d04dde0601: Blenz Coffee is a BC-born specialty coffee chain founded in Vancouver in 1992, now operating locally owned and franchised cafés across Canada. The menu spans handcrafted espresso drinks, nitro coffee and tea, whole-leaf organic teas, protein shakes, and a broad food selection including croissants, sandwiches, samosas, and baked goods. A touring cyclist stopping in can expect a community-focused café atmosphere with a diverse range of beverages and snacks.
a7f1562ba8: Lala Ji's Pizzeria is a family-run Indian-pizza fusion restaurant in downtown Penticton, owned and operated by a father-and-son chef team with decades of combined experience in Germany, India, and Canada. The kitchen specializes in authentic Indian-style pizzas alongside traditional Indian dishes, making it a genuinely distinctive stop on the Okanagan touring circuit. Dine-in, takeout, and delivery are all available, and the online ordering system supports scheduled pickup.
d3a3665ecb: Awesome Bagel & More is a downtown Vancouver café located steps from Canada Place, serving handcrafted bagels baked fresh daily, gourmet sandwiches, artisan pastries, Italian-style gelato, and espresso drinks. It positions itself as a gathering spot for locals, tourists, and professionals and operates with indoor seating only. The online menu spans over 57 items across categories including breakfast bagels, paninis, soups, and a full espresso bar.
4580fefffc: The Heatley is a community pub on East Hastings Street in East Vancouver, self-described as the neighbourhood homebase since 2015 and known for an inclusive, diversity-celebrating atmosphere. It hosts a regular live events calendar and has earned press coverage from The Daily Hive and The Globe and Mail. The pub serves a casual shareable-food menu alongside a full bar, making it a solid stop for a post-ride pint in a genuinely local venue.
11915ee098: Tandoori Fusion is an Indian cuisine restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver. As a full-service restaurant, it offers meal service to customers and would provide a dining and rest stop for touring cyclists.
7d0ef85e48: Little Caesars is a national pizza chain franchise offering carryout and delivery pizza at this Burnaby location. The store operates on a takeout-only model with no indoor or outdoor seating, making it a quick-stop option for cyclists needing a hot, filling meal without lingering. The menu includes pizzas, Crazy Bread, and wings, with vegetarian options available.
0a117b46c3: Woking Dragon is a family-owned Chinese restaurant operating since 2003, known for western-style Chinese cuisine with a modern twist on tradition. The brand has been voted favourite Chinese food in Coquitlam and offers online ordering across its locations. Touring cyclists would find familiar comfort-food options with some vegan and gluten-free adaptations available.
8ff9b97edb: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen is a large international fast food chain known for its Southern-style fried chicken, located on 96 Avenue in Langley. The location offers both dine-in and drive-through service, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through the area. It sits in a commercial corridor with easy road access.
372105c1f3: The Crabapple Cafe is a popular all-day breakfast and brunch spot in Brackendale, a community within Squamish, well-positioned on the corridor between Vancouver and Whistler. Formerly known as the Red Bench, it draws a loyal crowd with creative West Coast dishes like a Cajun BBQ Salmon Hash made with wild barbecued salmon and house-made hollandaise. A heated patio and a warm local atmosphere make it a comfortable stop year-round.
80d61151a0: Domino's Pizza is a national pizza chain franchise located in a unit at 19265 Airport Way in Pitt Meadows, offering delivery and carryout orders. The location serves the Pitt Meadows area and is one of the few late-night food options along this corridor. Touring cyclists can grab a hot meal to go without needing to sit down.
3aff9fba8b: The Modern Pantry is a bakery, cafe, and retail shop in Ambleside, West Vancouver, known for seasonally inspired pastries, organic sourdough breads, and made-from-scratch soups and sandwiches. The space doubles as an event venue and stocks a freezer of freshly prepared take-home meals alongside artisan retail goods. Owner Kendall Parslow brings an international food background — including a Masters in Food Culture and time at Borough Market in London — to this locally beloved North Shore spot.
d0cc67c2c8: Noodlebox is a Canadian fast-casual chain specializing in wok-fired noodle and rice bowls inspired by Asian cuisines — from Pad Thai and Kung Pao to Butter Chicken and Cambodian Jungle Curry. This Port Place location in Nanaimo lets cyclists fuel up with a customizable hot meal made fresh to order. The chain's broad menu and quick-service format make it a practical stop for touring cyclists moving through downtown Nanaimo.
752f92dc57: Dolly's Fish Market Restaurant is a licensed seafood restaurant and working fish market on the waterfront Cow Bay strip in Prince Rupert, one of the northernmost communities on BC's coast. It is part of a multi-location Northern BC operation that combines a sit-down restaurant with fresh seafood retail, custom and commercial fish processing, and wholesale sales. Cow Bay is a well-known visitor destination, making this a natural meal stop for cyclists arriving by ferry or touring the Yellowhead corridor.
42c42ca236: Riddim & Spice is a Caribbean restaurant on Vancouver's lively Commercial Drive, specializing in Jamaican and Caribbean cuisine including slow-cooked oxtail, jerk chicken, and golden flaky patties filled with spiced beef, chicken, or vegetables. Situated on one of the city's most cycling-friendly corridors, it offers both in-person pickup and online delivery ordering. Its hearty, flavour-forward dishes make it a distinctive cultural stop for cyclists rolling through East Vancouver.
39831cadb3: Yanaki Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Vancouver with both dine-in and online ordering options. Located on West 6th Avenue, it serves as a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists and other visitors passing through the area.
69b8fc25dd: Stages Bistro & Lounge is a full-service restaurant and lounge situated on the lobby floor of the Holiday Inn Vancouver-Centre on West Broadway. It offers an extensive menu spanning breakfast, lunch, and dinner, plus a Friday seafood lunch buffet and a daily happy hour with discounted cocktails and appetizers. The Broadway location makes it a convenient stop for cyclists moving through central Vancouver.
40cb33a06c: Taco Time is a fast-food Mexican restaurant in Courtenay. As a branch of a national Canadian chain, it provides reliable casual dining for travelers passing through the community. Touring cyclists can grab a quick meal without lengthy wait times typical of sit-down restaurants.
3e3601e964: Blenz Coffee is a BC-born specialty coffee chain that has been hand-crafting beverages since 1992, opening its first store on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. The 550 Burrard Street location sits in the heart of Vancouver's financial district, offering espresso drinks, nitro coffee, whole-leaf teas, protein shakes, and a broad range of baked goods and lunch items. As a locally founded chain with franchised community-oriented stores, it provides a familiar and comfortable stop for cyclists passing through downtown.
e194e9d7f7: Funky Winker Beans is a self-described 'hardcore' dive bar in Vancouver's Downtown East Side, known for its low-lit, utilitarian atmosphere that welcomes everyone. The bar features pool tables, pinball machines, and art from local artists for sale on the walls. Regular karaoke and open mic comedy events make it a lively destination in the heart of downtown.
7c388ba3e3: Pizza Factory Vancouver is a franchise location of a BC pizza chain originally founded in Coquitlam in 1984 by Sam Sanghera, now with multiple locations across British Columbia. The shop makes artisan dough and sauce fresh daily in small batches, earning strong local reviews for crust quality and friendly service. It offers both walk-in and online ordering for takeout, making it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists on Fraser Street.
f9d7e02041: Bastion Pizza Company is a pizza restaurant in Nanaimo offering indoor seating and online ordering. The business advertises dietary options including vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free meals.
c1099e4254: Okanagan Estate Wine Cellar is a specialty wine shop on Marine Drive in West Vancouver dedicated to bringing Okanagan Valley wines to Vancouver's North Shore, stocking labels from over 20 BC wineries including Mission Hill, Quails' Gate, and NK'MIP Cellars. The shop is staffed by knowledgeable wine professionals who can advise visitors across all experience levels. Cyclists passing through could pick up a bottle of BC wine to enjoy at camp or as a take-home gift.
4882a06fc9: Master Donair is a Mediterranean restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver's West End, serving donair wraps, shawarma platters, pita wraps, tabbouleh, and poutine. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, curbside pickup, and delivery, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through one of Vancouver's busiest urban cycling corridors. Reservations are available online alongside walk-in service.
90d9b3fefb: Bean Around The World Coffees is a BC-based independent coffee chain with over 35 years of history, roasting its own beans from a North Vancouver roastery. The Ambleside location sits on Marine Drive in West Vancouver, making it a natural stop for cyclists riding the coastal route between West Vancouver and North Vancouver. The brand sells coffee drinks, retail beans, brewing gear, and apparel alongside its in-store café experience.
304e48cf84: A Shanghainese restaurant in Burnaby with full indoor seating and no outdoor patio. The sit-down format provides a sheltered meal option for touring cyclists. The restaurant specializes in regional Chinese cuisine from Shanghai.
efa4b0d539: Pizza Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 1967 with over 750 locations coast to coast, making it a familiar and reliable stop for hungry travellers. The Mission location sits along the Lougheed Highway and offers pizza, panzerottis, poutine, sandwiches, and sides for takeout or dine-in. Touring cyclists passing through Mission on Highway 7 will find it a straightforward refuelling option in a commercial strip.
b8b07b0022: Sun Sushi is a sushi restaurant on West 10th Avenue in Vancouver. It serves sit-down diners in a neighborhood setting, offering a convenient place for touring cyclists to stop for a meal.
a39468a9bc: Pita Land is a Canadian Middle Eastern restaurant chain that has been serving shawarma, pita wraps, and traditional Mideast cuisine since 2003, drawing on generations of family recipes. The Nanaimo location sits in a strip mall on Terminal Avenue North and offers a broad menu of wraps, rice bowls, plates, burgers, salads, and desserts. Touring cyclists will find it a convenient stop for a filling, flavour-forward meal with both dine-in and online ordering options.
16a83627c1: Macu Tea is a Taiwanese bubble tea chain founded in 2008 in Kaohsiung, known for fresh fruit teas made with real seasonal ingredients. The Kerrisdale branch is one of several Metro Vancouver locations offering a creative menu including fruit pulp teas, cheese teas, and indulgent 'drinking desserts' like Mango Pomelo Sago. Everything is freshly made to order, making it a quick refreshment stop in a quiet residential-commercial strip of West Vancouver.
bad7be4046: Little Bird Dim Sum + Craft Beer is a three-generation family restaurant on Kitsilano's West 4th Avenue, pairing traditional Cantonese dim sum with a curated lineup of BC craft beers and wines. The restaurant earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand recognition, tracing its roots to the family's earlier Flamingo Chinese Restaurant. Touring cyclists passing through Kitsilano will find a full sit-down dim sum experience alongside takeout pickup.
b7d0d36b7e: Stickleback is a waterfront West Coast eatery perched on Cooper's Cove just outside downtown Sooke, featuring a natural cedar bar, a life-sized mural of Sombrio Beach, and a patio with wildlife and ocean views. The menu leans toward house-made burgers, wraps, pastas, Baby Back Ribs, and local halibut, with gluten-free options throughout. Situated right beside Rush Kayak Adventures, it's a natural stop for cyclists exploring the Sooke waterfront corridor.
24a5562377: The Starbucks at Dilworth Plaza sits on Highway 97 North, one of Kelowna's main commercial arterials, making it a natural rest stop for cyclists traveling through the Okanagan corridor. The location is drive-through enabled and offers the full Starbucks menu of espresso drinks, teas, Refreshers, and packaged food items. OSM records outdoor seating, giving road-weary riders a place to sit and refuel off the busy highway.
be7d09f032: SURA Korean BBQ is a full-service Korean restaurant located inside Aberdeen Centre mall in Richmond, offering tableside Korean BBQ alongside traditional dishes including soups, stews, and hot pots. The restaurant emphasizes premium ingredients and authentic flavours prepared by seasoned chefs. It has earned recognition from the Vancouver Magazine Restaurant Awards, Georgia Straight Golden Plates, and WE Vancouver's Best of the City Dining.
e17fb6557c: A vegetarian bakery in Chilliwack offering plant-based baked goods. It serves as a convenient stop for touring cyclists to source fresh food provisions while passing through the area.
3c5e361f57: Victoria Sushi is a Japanese restaurant situated on Wilson Street in the Esquimalt area of greater Victoria, serving sushi and Japanese cuisine. The restaurant supports online ordering, offering touring cyclists a convenient way to have a meal ready on arrival. It is a straightforward sit-down dining stop in a neighbourhood accessible from Victoria's network of urban cycling routes.
a4040b62d7: Toro's Liquor Store is a well-established Vernon bottle shop with over 45 years of experience, carrying more than 450 beers, 800+ spirits, and 1,100+ wines with an emphasis on Okanagan regional producers. It offers personalized staff guidance and a curated focus on local craft breweries, artisanal cideries, and regional vineyards. Touring cyclists could use it as a resupply stop for locally sourced beverages to enjoy at camp or a destination accommodation.
48e3afc9e0: A non-profit social club dedicated to fundraising for local charities. The club features live music performances, pool tables, shuffleboard, and darts, creating a community gathering space for locals and visitors. Touring cyclists will find a casual venue for food, drink, and social connection.
3316fa8b7f: Portobello is an elevated casual dining cafe situated inside the Fairmont Chateau Whistler in Whistler's Upper Village, a locals' favourite known for its animated open kitchen. The restaurant features the only kitchen of its kind in Whistler — a Rotisol rotisserie, Alto-Shaam smoker, and antique European Miwe Wenz 1919 ovens — producing rotisserie chicken, smoked brisket, pork ribs, gourmet sandwiches, and fresh pastries. A full-service bar with local craft beers, a market-style retail space, and a summer outdoor patio with Adirondack chairs and a fire pit complete the rustic alpine setting.
572f6ccf70: Topinoy is a takeout-only pizza and bubble tea spot in Tofino, launched in 2024 and quickly earning strong local reviews for its handcrafted pizzas made with fresh ingredients. It operates as a counter-service window — no dine-in, no delivery — making it a fast and convenient stop for cyclists passing through town. Bubble tea in multiple flavors rounds out the menu, offering a refreshing option after a long ride.
05ae4a465a: Sushi Town is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Marine Drive in North Vancouver serving authentic Japanese cuisine with indoor seating. It sits on a busy commercial corridor convenient to cyclists on the North Shore. Online ordering and takeout are available for riders who prefer to grab a meal on the go.
0d0c1dbfa0: Lynn Canyon Café sits inside Lynn Canyon Park, a cherished North Vancouver natural area anchored by a 50-metre suspension bridge that has welcomed visitors since 1912. The café serves fresh, locally sourced meals and beverages — from bakery items to light lunches — and markets itself as an energy stop before or after exploring the park's trails, pools, and falls. Its emphasis on sustainability and community connection makes it a natural rest point for cyclists riding through the Lynn Valley area.
a87e013f67: Earl of Sandwich is a quick-service sandwich chain with a Langley location inside Willoughby Town Centre. The chain is known for hot, freshly baked sandwiches and has earned repeated recognition on TripAdvisor's Top 10 Best Quick Bite list. Online ordering for pick-up or delivery is available, making it a convenient fuel stop for cyclists passing through the area.
30e404e482: Plateau Pizza is a family-owned gourmet pizzeria that has served the Westwood Plateau neighbourhood in Coquitlam since 1999. Known for handcrafted pizzas with slow-fermented dough, house-made sauce, and 100% mozzarella, the menu spans classic and specialty pies alongside calzones, pasta, and salads. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery, with gluten-free crust and vegan cheese options available.
81917b0134: Paisanos Slice Shop is a neighbourhood pizzeria in downtown Nanaimo specializing in hand-stretched Neapolitan and New York-inspired slices and whole pies, available for pickup only. The creative menu includes offerings like miso bechamel mushroom, hot garlic honey pepperoni, and potato with rosemary and arugula. A straightforward quick-refuel stop for cyclists moving through central Nanaimo.
0c37625fb9: Gami Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Richmond offering takeout service. The restaurant features online ordering for customer convenience.
9090d7be96: Saint Germain Bakery is an award-winning Canadian bakery chain founded in the 1980s, with gold medals from the 2004 and 2008 Culinary Olympics in Germany and a reputation built on techniques drawn from French, Japanese, Hong Kong, and Australian pastry traditions. The Burnaby outlet is a counter-service unit inside Metropolis at Metrotown, offering takeaway-only baked goods including cakes, pastries, and breads made without artificial essences. The chain supplies desserts to nine airlines and major hotel brands across North America, giving it an unusually high culinary pedigree for a mall bakery stop.
c5a16a3a3f: Reddy Made Cakes is a bakery café in downtown Abbotsford run by Crystal Reddy, who trained at culinary school and worked alongside a French pastry chef before building her business around entirely scratch-made cakes, cupcakes, wedding cakes, and other baked goods. Every component — ganache, fondant, buttercream, preserves — is made in-house using what the business describes as only the best quality ingredients. Cyclists can stop in for walk-in cupcakes and treats, including gluten-free options, or arrange custom pickup orders.
0dc9d026f1: Milton Street Public House is a gastropub occupying a heritage home built in 1892 in Nanaimo's old city quarter, open since 2015. The kitchen emphasizes scratch cooking with local produce, offering an elevated casual menu spanning creative small plates, fresh seafood, flatbreads, and craft cocktails. Touring cyclists passing through Nanaimo's historic downtown will find a polished sit-down dining experience in a characterful Victorian setting.
fc1e041b69: The Taco Hole is a Mexican-Canadian fusion eatery tucked inside the Cowichan Community Centre in Duncan, serving creative takes on tacos, burritos, and sides like Birria Poutine and Quesabirria. The menu spans classic beef and chicken preparations through to vegan chorizo-spiced tofu, making it accessible to a wide range of cyclists. It is a compact, community-centre-style counter that offers a satisfying and filling stop on the Cowichan Valley corridor.
db953a00de: Domino's Pizza at 770 Bay Street is a large national pizza chain offering carryout and delivery in downtown Victoria. It serves a broad menu of pizzas in multiple styles alongside sides and desserts, with frequent combo coupons available. Its central location on Bay Street makes it a convenient calorie stop for cyclists moving through the city core.
72c15fb767: Nanda Chicken is a restaurant in Nanaimo, BC specializing in chicken dishes. Located in unit A of its building, it appears to be a neighbourhood eatery that would offer a hot meal stop for cyclists passing through the area. No further detail is available from accessible sources.
5c2e8c19fe: Baby Dhal Roti Shop is a Trinidadian restaurant on Vancouver's Commercial Drive serving handcrafted recipes passed down through generations — doubles, pholourie, aloo pie, and curries made with locally sourced meats and fresh ingredients. Situated on one of the city's most beloved cycling corridors just south of Broadway, it offers quick phone-order takeout and DoorDash delivery for cyclists looking for a hearty, flavourful refuel. The menu spans vegetarian curries to oxtail, with house-made roti shells also available fresh or frozen.
97c6393230: Basecamp Burger Joint is a casual sit-down burger and breakfast restaurant perched on Esplanade Avenue in Harrison Hot Springs, a well-known cycling destination in the Fraser Valley. The kitchen builds burgers from 100% Premium Alberta beef patties made in-house, and the menu ranges from classic egg benedicts and buttermilk pancakes through to a grilled wild salmon burger and a fully vegan Beyond Burger. Its lakeside village location makes it a natural mid-ride or end-of-day refuelling stop for cyclists coming off the Harrison or Vedder corridor routes.
6186a8f91d: A cafe located in Marysville, BC. Limited details are available; website access was unsuccessful.
58d2311f7b: Tim's Fish & Chips is a takeout-only fish and chip shop located on Northwest Boulevard in Creston, BC. For touring cyclists passing through the Creston Valley, it offers a classic fast-food stop in a town that sits at the junction of several regional cycling routes. The takeout-only format makes it a practical grab-and-go option rather than a sit-down rest.
d25ead2fc1: My Greek Taverna is a family-style Greek restaurant in Coquitlam's Brunette Avenue corridor, serving traditional Mediterranean dishes including souvlaki, moussaka, rack of lamb, and fresh seafood prepared with time-honored recipes. The cozy, rustic dining room is designed to evoke an authentic Greek atmosphere. Touring cyclists will find satisfying, protein-rich plated meals with generous accompaniments of Greek salad, rice, roast potato, and pita bread.
903bfcf545: Brewhall is a two-floor social hall and pub from the Tap & Barrel group, situated in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood within easy reach of the city's cycling network. The main level offers a spacious bar, outdoor patio, and arcade games, while the upstairs DRINKLAB serves as a private event and trivia venue. The kitchen focuses on scratch-made, locally sourced food paired with 22 taps of craft beer and cider, and the walls display a museum-grade collection of BC and Canadian artwork.
21cd433fc7: A-FRAME Brewing Co. is an award-winning craft brewery and tasting room in Squamish, BC, celebrated for its relaxed 'cabin vibes' atmosphere—an outdoor patio with a fire pit, mountain backdrop, and an inclusive, welcoming community ethos. The brewery names its beers after BC lakes and earned Gold and Silver at the 2023 Canadian Brewing Awards. Cyclists will find a natural post-ride stop with growler fills, cold packaged cans to go, and regular on-site food truck service.
64073dfc84: The original 49th Parallel café, opened in Kitsilano in 2007, now pairs specialty coffee roasted in-house with Lucky's Doughnuts made on site—a combination that has made it a neighbourhood institution. The spot sits steps from the beach and the Seaside Greenway, making it a natural pitstop for cyclists riding along Vancouver's waterfront corridor. An enclosed patio and ample bike racks round out the appeal for anyone arriving on two wheels.
a7abe8177e: Prado Cafe, now trading as Prado Coffee, is a specialty coffee brand founded by Sammy Piccolo, a four-time Canadian Barista Champion who has represented Canada at the World Barista Championships. Starting as a single shop on Commercial Drive focused on quality espresso and neighbourhood hospitality, the brand has grown to multiple locations across Vancouver and Burnaby. The company roasts its own blends, ranging from approachable everyday espresso to seasonal single-origin offerings.
bc7a212824: Analog Coffee is a specialty coffee chain founded in Calgary in 2011 with a strong emphasis on sourcing and carefully crafting single-origin coffees. The brand built its identity around an obsessive attention to every detail of the guest experience, from equipment to décor. A touring cyclist stopping in can expect a serious, community-oriented café with a full espresso program and a range of brewing methods.
52044fbcfc: Original Joe's is a bar and grill restaurant with a location on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. The venue features indoor and outdoor seating in a no-smoking environment. It offers vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free menu options.
99e7e0ceff: The Keg Morgan Creek is a full-service steakhouse and bar located in South Surrey's Morgan Creek neighbourhood, about 10 minutes from White Rock Beach. The location features a heated and covered patio, a lounge with bar and TVs, and free parking. It is a well-established chain destination offering a sit-down dining experience as well as takeout and DoorDash delivery.
053ed93980: Reggiano's Pizza is an authentic Neapolitan-style pizzeria with multiple Lower Mainland locations, baking pies in a traditional Marra Forni wood-fired oven using Caputo '00' flour and mozzarella di bufala for a characteristic charred, leopard-spotted crust. The Port Coquitlam location offers both dine-in and takeout, including pizza by the slice for a quick stop on the go. Beer and wine are served on premises.
08773fc176: Pallet Coffee Roasters is a locally owned Vancouver specialty coffee company established in East Vancouver in 2014, and this location serves as the company's flagship HQ and working roastery. With eight café locations across Metro Vancouver, Pallet is also a wholesale partner and barista training provider, making the HQ a hub where cyclists can experience freshly roasted coffee alongside food and baked goods. The company emphasizes ethical sourcing and long-term relationships with farmers from origin countries such as Peru, Colombia, and Brazil.
b765bd9db1: Presotea is a Taiwanese bubble tea franchise established in 2006, now operating multiple Lower Mainland locations including this Metrotown branch on Kingsway. The shop specialises in freshly brewed teas made using a high-pressure espresso-style machine, offering an extensive menu of milk teas, fruit teas, and slushes. It is a takeout-only counter with no indoor or outdoor seating.
ef5de5bc96: The Blind Angler is a full-service lakeside restaurant on Beach Avenue in Peachland, named after a legendary local figure who continued fishing on Lake Okanagan after losing his sight in WWI. The restaurant sits overlooking the marina with views described as among the best in the Okanagan, and serves everything from eggs benedict at breakfast to seafood and steaks at dinner. It is a notable stop for cyclists riding the Okanagan lakefront corridor.
7edd40e905: Afghan Kitchen is a family-run restaurant in South Surrey built around the owner's personal journey from Kabul to Canada, serving traditional Afghan dishes made entirely from his mother's recipes. The restaurant earned the South Surrey & White Rock Chamber of Commerce Business of the Year (Medium) award for 2023 and was featured on the Food Network in March 2021. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a welcoming sit-down dining experience with catering available for group events.
b696c15845: Sisto's Pub has anchored the Hatzic neighbourhood of Mission since 1978, earning a reputation as a hidden gem and home-away-from-home for locals. Part of the Springs Group chain, it serves classic, large-portioned pub food with in-house dining, patio seating, and a seasonal back lawn with lawn games. Weekly events include Music Bingo, Karaoke, Family Feud, and Trivia nights, making it a lively stop for cyclists looking for a full meal and evening entertainment.
7a68ab7003: On the Rocks is a pub and grill that bills itself as Kamloops' local favourite, serving an extensive menu that spans Maple-Glazed Salmon, AAA Prime Sterling Silver Sirloin, and hearty pub fare alongside a wide selection of draft and bottled beers from around the world. The venue doubles as an entertainment hub, with big-screen TVs for major sporting events and regular live music performances. Touring cyclists arriving in Kamloops would find a full sit-down meal option with a varied menu and a lively atmosphere.
7a76d02411: BarBurrito is Canada's largest Mexican-inspired burrito chain, proudly Canadian since 2005 and now operating 385+ locations nationwide. This Langley location serves fully customizable burritos, bowls, tacos, and quesadillas assembled from fresh, in-house ingredients with a wide range of proteins. Cyclists looking for a quick, filling meal will find substantial options including vegetarian and gluten-free choices.
1e118d5ccb: Stick In The Mud Roastorium is a specialty coffee roastery located in Sooke, BC, offering freshly roasted coffee beans, brewing equipment, and coffee education classes. The business operates both a physical roasting facility and an online shop selling single-origin coffees, grinders, brewers, and accessories. A touring cyclist rolling into Sooke's outskirts will find a craft-roaster destination rather than a typical café counter.
87821208e0: Axum Ethiopian Restaurant serves traditional Ethiopian cuisine — spiced stews, injera-based communal plates, and a robust vegetarian selection — from its East Hastings Street location in Vancouver. The restaurant offers full sit-down dining alongside online ordering, private event hosting, and catering packages for all occasions. It is a lively neighborhood destination known for both hearty meat dishes and a wide range of entirely plant-based options.
b6424b6512: Woodstone Pizza is a Neapolitan-style pizzeria in Chilliwack making wood-fired pies on a sourdough crust from a family recipe passed down for generations. The kitchen uses premium ingredients including fior di latte, hand-stretched dough, and prosciutto cotto, with a menu spanning classic Italian specialties and local-style combinations. The restaurant is currently open and operating normally while a full rebrand is in progress.
9795b27f8b: Thunderbird is a Korean Fried Chicken restaurant tucked into Cook Street Village, one of Victoria's most bike-friendly neighbourhood strips. Founded by Korean-Canadians who moved to Victoria in 2009 and found no KFC restaurants in the city, it specialises in double deep-fried chicken with sauces like Yang-nyeom (sweet & spicy) and Megan Burger (spicy soy). The menu also features bao, chicken katsu curry, cro-waffles, and rice bowls, making it a solid stop for a calorie-rich refuel after a coastal ride.
99051a2cfe: JiangNan Wok is a Chinese restaurant in Richmond's Capstan Way commercial district, drawing its name from the Jiangnan region along China's lower Yangtze River, known for refined home-style cooking. The restaurant offers indoor seating only, making it a sit-down dining option for cyclists passing through the area. It is located in a multi-unit commercial building, typical of Richmond's dense mixed-use developments.
9ff0187aff: L'aromas Coffee Southlands is one of four locations of a Delta-based coffee brand that grew from a backyard roasting project and community market presence into a local café chain, officially opening its first location in July 2015. Founded by three friends with a mission to create a 'home away from home,' the brand is community-rooted and independently owned. The Southlands location offers a full café experience with outdoor seating and on-site washrooms.
d56625f9a1: Kiyo Sushi is a sushi restaurant located in Richmond, BC. Additional details about the business and its facilities are unavailable due to website fetch failure.
09bf251e15: La Ruelle Bakery is a small-batch French Canadian artisan bakery tucked into a charming back alley in downtown Nelson, BC, specializing in organic sourdough breads, handmade pastries, and fresh sandwiches to go. The open-concept bakehouse lets customers watch bakers at work, using organic flours and seasonal locally sourced ingredients — continuing a tradition inherited from the predecessor bakery Au Soleil Levant. All sales are takeaway-only, making it a straightforward stop for a freshly baked loaf or a quick lunch on the road.
6783eb9de6: O Sushi is a sushi restaurant on Granville Street in central Vancouver with both indoor and outdoor seating. The restaurant serves vegetarian menu options and provides wireless internet access to customers.
bc87732215: Red Umbrella Cafe is a locally-owned breakfast and lunch spot in Vancouver's West End, serving the neighbourhood since 2007 and rebranded under current owner Mitra Ameri in 2014. The cafe is known for homemade and handcrafted food — including all-day breakfast, creative lunch sandwiches, specialty coffee, and slow-roasted meats — using fresh, premium ingredients. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and takeout is offered for those who prefer to eat on the move.
d52525face: Maple Palace Restaurant is a Chinese restaurant in Sidney, BC, run under new management and helmed by a chef born and raised in China with over 20 years of experience. The dining room is decorated with hand-painted murals and offers a unique view of aircraft taking off from nearby Victoria International Airport. The menu spans classic Cantonese staples through Szechuan and Mongolian dishes, with both dine-in and takeout available.
d6e4f8b54a: Superbaba is an award-winning Middle Eastern restaurant located in the Atrium building in downtown Victoria, serving made-from-scratch wraps and bowls with pita baked in-house daily. It is a second outpost of the celebrated Vancouver original, recognized multiple times as Best Casual Restaurant by Vancouver Magazine and featured on Food Network's Big Food Bucket List for its falafel sandwich and eggplant bowl. Dine-in, takeout, and DoorDash delivery are all available.
7ac193c13f: Koon Bo Seafood Restaurant is a long-established Cantonese eatery tucked into a strip mall near Fraser and 41st Avenue in Vancouver, serving traditional Guangdong-style cuisine since 1998. Known locally as a quiet 'hidden gem,' it draws a loyal following with standout dishes like house special shredded chicken, roast squab, Peking duck (advance order required), and a broad dim sum selection. Online ordering is available directly through the restaurant's site as well as through Uber Eats and DoorDash.
3e348774fa: Troll's is a long-standing fish and chip restaurant in North Vancouver that bills itself as 'World Famous.' It offers dine-in seating and online ordering for pick-up, making it a practical stop for cyclists seeking a classic BC coastal meal. The restaurant hosts events and accepts reservations, suggesting a community-rooted operation rather than a simple fast-food outlet.
46a6f2af5a: Cardero's is a full-service waterfront restaurant operated by the Sequoia Company of Restaurants (est. 1978), perched at Coal Harbour Marina on the east side of the Westin Bayshore Hotel. It offers an eclectic Pacific Northwest menu heavy on local seafood, with live music daily and panoramic marina views that make it a landmark dining stop on Vancouver's scenic Coal Harbour seawall. The heated enclosed patio and spacious main dining room can accommodate large groups, and the marina-side setting is a natural reward for cyclists finishing a loop around the seawall.
a196edac3e: Nat's New York Pizzeria is a Vancouver institution over 30 years in operation, serving hand-tossed thin-crust New York-style pizza rooted in 100-year-old Calabrian family recipes. The West End location on Denman Street opened in January 2000 and sits close to the Stanley Park seawall — one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors. The restaurant is celebrated for deep community ties, a warm neighbourhood atmosphere, and a loyal following that has included celebrities Ryan Reynolds and Joshua Jackson.
33b4872e27: Lee's Donuts is a beloved BC institution founded in 1979, famous for handmade classic donuts crafted fresh daily from scratch using original recipes. The Steveston location is one of a growing network of shops carrying on the legacy started at Vancouver's Granville Island Public Market. A fast, friendly stop for a cycling snack in the historic Steveston village area of Richmond.
f0bd7ee03f: Bimini's Since 1975 is a Kitsilano institution recognized as British Columbia's first neighbourhood pub, operating since 1974 at 2010 West 4th Avenue. Recently renovated under new ownership, the three-floor, 294-capacity venue blends heritage elements — reclaimed wood from a historic Vancouver mill, imported tiles — with a modern sports bar boasting 16 screens and 24 craft beers on tap. It serves as the official pub partner of Vancouver Whitecaps FC and hosts live music, DJ nights, trivia, and special events, making it a lively stop on the West 4th corridor.
52ba19f393: Macau Cafe (澳門街) is a Chinese fast food cafe situated in the busy Number 3 Road retail corridor of Richmond, BC. It serves the large local Cantonese community and is a convenient stop for cyclists navigating Richmond's flat, bike-friendly grid streets through the city's commercial heart.
29097c8770: Bubble Waffle Cafe is a Hong Kong-style street food cafe specializing in egg waffles (雞蛋仔), fish soup noodle combos, curry fish balls, and a broad selection of Taiwanese-style bubble teas. Operating across multiple Lower Mainland locations including Aberdeen Centre, a Public Market, and Park Royal, it brings authentic Hong Kong street snack culture to the Vancouver area. Cyclists will find a wide range of quick, customizable snacks and noodle bowls served in a casual takeout format.
121f70c7a2: Rivers Restaurant is a sit-down dining spot located in Yarrow, a small rural community southwest of Chilliwack in the Fraser Valley. The Yarrow area sits along quiet agricultural back-roads that attract recreational and touring cyclists, making a local restaurant a welcome find. Its Facebook presence suggests active community engagement, though details about the menu and atmosphere are not publicly accessible without a Facebook account.
b02f4e00c8: Lee Gar Nei (이가네) is a Korean restaurant located in a Surrey strip-mall plaza, formerly operating as BJS Korean Restaurant. The menu spans Korean appetizers, soups, hot pots, and set meals, with a student lunch option that suggests it serves a local residential and campus crowd. Online ordering is available, making it a practical stop for a cyclist wanting to pre-order a hot Korean meal.
c1559b84ee: Mongolie Grill is an independently owned stir-fry restaurant that has operated in the heart of Whistler Village since 1996. Diners select their own combination of meats, seafood, vegetables, and sauces, then watch the chefs cook the meal theatrically on a large open grill. The restaurant caters to a wide range of dietary needs and is consistently cited as one of Whistler's top dining experiences.
0cb0904555: Bouchons Bistro is an authentic French bistro operating in Kelowna's cultural district since 2004, helmed by Parisian chef Stephane Facon and offering classic regional dishes from escargots de Bourgogne and duck confit to bouillabaisse. The restaurant maintains a temperature-controlled Burgundy-style cellar stocked with over 750 bottles spanning Okanagan Valley producers and French appellations. Situated within walking distance of the Delta Grand Hotel, Kelowna Community Theatre, and Prospera Place, it serves as a polished evening dining destination for cyclists exploring the central Okanagan.
5a3b336c66: Homeland Cafe & Bar sits on Marine Drive in White Rock, a popular waterfront cycling corridor, and blends South Asian and Western cuisine — from VADA PAV and paneer bhurji paratha to Cajun chicken sandwiches and ceremonial-grade matcha drinks. The cafe operates with a full bar and outdoor seating, making it a potential stop for cyclists riding the White Rock promenade route. The menu spans breakfast, brunch, and evening service with a notable range of plant-based and vegetarian options.
d477672b8b: Formerly known as Arigato Sushi, this Japanese restaurant rebranded as Miso Sushi in March 2026, while retaining the same menu and staff. It sits directly on the Trans-Canada Highway in the Valleyview area of Kamloops, making it a convenient stop for cyclists traveling that corridor. Online ordering is available.
f4d7e48b8a: Zorba's Bakery & Foods is a family-operated Greek and Mediterranean food manufacturer that has been producing pita bread, phyllo pies, dips, and falafel for the North American market since 1985, with roots tracing back to a village bakery on the Greek island of Evia. Products use locally sourced BC ingredients including Okanagan yogurt and Fraser Valley vegetables, and include vegan, gluten-free, and lactose-free options. OSM tags the location as a takeaway-only bakery shop, though the business also distributes wholesale to grocery retailers across the region.
b12635d93b: Seh-mi Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Port Alberni offering casual dining along the main highway. A convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking Asian cuisine in the region.
f3f787e35a: PumpJack Pub has anchored Vancouver's Davie Village as a queer community bar since December 2000, serving as both a daytime sports bar with two large projection screens and nine TVs and a weekend nightclub with live entertainment. It operates as an explicitly inclusive safe space under the BarWatch program and welcomes all queer lifestyles, hosting themed weekly and monthly events. A touring cyclist passing through the West End would find a lively neighbourhood pub atmosphere in one of Vancouver's most walkable and bikeable urban corridors.
e86a53993f: Adam's Crepes is a small French-style crêpe café established in 2017 on Rumble Street in south Burnaby, with seating for around 24 guests. It offers outdoor seating, giving cyclists a comfortable place to rest along this residential corridor. The café also offers delivery, suggesting a takeout-friendly model.
ed4f7aabee: The Canadian Brewhouse is a large western-Canadian chain sports bar and restaurant with dozens of locations, known for a broad food menu, extensive beer selection, and wall-to-wall screens for live sports. The Prince George location features a licensed patio, table reservations, a kids menu, and online ordering, making it a full-service dine-in destination near the Recplace recreation complex. Touring cyclists passing through Prince George will find a reliable, high-capacity food stop with takeout available.
2aff2c9db7: Nine Bar Coffee is a specialty café in Yaletown, Vancouver, built around carefully sourced local beans and skilled preparation, with a strong emphasis on community gathering in a relaxed neighbourhood setting. The café offers both indoor and outdoor seating and also operates a mobile battery-powered espresso bar for weddings, corporate events, and private gatherings across Metro Vancouver.
b091a1853e: Adriana's is a compact sandwich and pizza shop in Tofino serving Italian-inspired subs, focaccia sandwiches, and wood-style artisan pizzas. The shop runs rotating specials — including a Friday meatball sub and a weekly feature pizza announced via Instagram — and supports online pre-ordering with in-store pickup. Its varied menu and quick-service format make it a practical mid-ride refuel stop in the heart of Tofino.
528a84a3e3: Humpty's Big Plate Diner is the Fort St. John franchise of a Western Canadian family restaurant chain founded in 1977 and best known for its all-day breakfast and 'Famous Pan Scrambler.' Located on Alaska Road North, the full-service diner offers breakfast, burgers, and comfort-food classics with cash and card payment. It is one of only a handful of Humpty's locations in British Columbia, making it a notable sit-down option for cyclists travelling the Alaska Highway corridor.
cf7b3e9b27: Big Star Sandwich Co. is a Lower Mainland sandwich chain founded in 2013, known for hearty, made-from-scratch sandwiches built on a fresh rustic Filone loaf with slow-roasted meats, house-made sauces, and vintage cane-sugar sodas. The Maple Ridge location is one of six across the region, offering dine-in, takeout, and delivery with vegetarian and vegan options confirmed. The About page notes the chain pays living wages and offers staff benefits — a community-minded operation that's been a local fixture for over a decade.
bc6cf43d09: Via Tevere is an award-winning Vera Pizza Napoletana-certified restaurant in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, recognized by Vancouver Magazine and Georgia Straight for best pizza on the East Side. Authentic wood-fired Neapolitan pizzas are the centrepiece, alongside antipasti, pasta, and house-made gnocchi. The restaurant also operates a second brick-and-mortar location on Victoria Drive and a food truck, making it a well-established local institution on a popular urban cycling corridor.
7cc995090e: Shagun Sweets is an Indian restaurant located in Surrey, BC. The establishment features vegetarian options, making it accessible to plant-based touring cyclists. It operates as a dine-in restaurant serving the local community.
e3ad327cf0: Ignite Pizzeria Express is the Gastown outpost of a Vancouver stone-fired pizza chain founded in 2017, and the only Express-format location in the group where pizza by the slice is sold. Hand-tossed pies are fired at 800° with a low-sodium dough rested for three days, and the menu spans carnivore, vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-friendly options. It sits on West Cordova Street in the heart of historic Gastown, making it a convenient refuelling stop for cyclists cutting through downtown Vancouver.
1feef81c45: Ga Hyang Ru is a Korean and Chinese restaurant located on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver, providing both indoor and outdoor seating. The establishment maintains a non-smoking dining environment. It is positioned on a main commercial corridor in North Vancouver's local business district.
89c6679c6f: Dragon Bowl is a modern Chinese restaurant chain founded in 2022, with a Burnaby outpost on Kingsway specializing in rice bowls, noodle dishes, and bento-style meals made with natural, seasonal ingredients. The restaurant blends traditional Chinese flavours with a health-focused approach, including vegetarian choices and customizable meal combinations. Online ordering and corporate catering round out an offering aimed at quick, satisfying meals.
5c8c87f466: Lionsgate Pizza is a North Vancouver institution that has been serving gourmet pizza since 1989, evolving from the original Raven Pizza tradition dating back to 1979. The kitchen makes dough and slow-simmered sauce from scratch daily, using local BC cheese, fresh vegetables, and artisan meats sourced from a North Shore supplier. Specialty pizzas, Italian pastas, and gluten-free crusts are all on the menu.
d9552e29ed: Naruto Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Commercial Drive in Vancouver offering dine-in and takeout service with online ordering. A straightforward meal option for cycling tourists passing through the area.
f5344ea045: Alcatraz Chicken is a fried chicken restaurant established in 2023 in Kelowna's Rutland Centre, built around a proprietary 13-spice blend and 24-hour marination process applied to every piece of chicken. The menu spans whole pieces, tenders, wings, family combos, sandwiches, and kids meals, making it a practical high-calorie refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the Rutland corridor. Orders can be placed online for pickup or through UberEats, DoorDash, and SkipTheDishes for delivery.
8a7d78d6d1: Provisions is an all-day neighbourhood café in the heart of Whistler Village, backed by the Toptable Group and open since 2023. It offers a full espresso bar with custom-roasted coffee, daily fresh-baked pastries, made-to-order breakfast and lunch dishes, and slow-roasted rotisserie chicken — serving both dine-in and takeout. A natural refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the village, with online ordering available for both its Whistler and Kitsilano locations.
c8cf5375ad: Papa John's is a pizza fast-food restaurant, part of the national franchise. It is notable to touring cyclists for its brand familiarity and quick-service model. The Kingsway location provides accessible meal service without requiring reservation or seated time.
26e18d2221: Steel & Oak Brewing Co. is a New Westminster craft brewery that blends North American and German brewing traditions to produce unfiltered, unpasteurized beers — from a crisp Cold Lager to an Imperial Hefeweizen — all poured in their own tasting room. The venue has both indoor and outdoor seating, and an on-site food truck rounds out the experience with a full menu of burgers, sandwiches, and sides. Community events, live music, and private keg sales make it a genuine neighbourhood destination rather than just a stop for a pint.
f3532c3838: Ricky's All Day Grill is a Canadian family restaurant chain with over 60 years of history, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner all day from a sit-down dining room. The Nanaimo location sits along Island Highway North, a primary cycling corridor on Vancouver Island. The menu spans all-day breakfast classics and Eggs Benedict through to Alberta Angus beef burgers, comfort mains, and Fish & Chips.
48e8c72f53: Marble House Eatery is a Chinese restaurant on the second floor of Crystal Mall in Burnaby, described on its own site as one of the city's most iconic Chinese restaurants. It offers three distinct culinary formats under one roof: traditional dim sum at lunch, all-you-can-eat mini hotpot at dinner, and BBQ available throughout the day. A touring cyclist looking for a hearty, varied Chinese meal along the Kingsway corridor will find a full-service restaurant with a lively neighbourhood atmosphere.
b062e3373f: Turtle Bay Pub is a family-friendly waterfront pub on Wood Lake in Lake Country, open year-round and welcoming dogs on its lakeside patio. The venue pairs theatrical cocktails with a compact menu of dumplings drawn from regional Chinese cuisines — Sichuan, Tibetan, Xinjiang, and more. It's a genuinely hidden-gem bar experience in one of Vancouver's most historically dense and walkable neighbourhoods.
23dcbae7ef: New Fuji is a Japanese restaurant located on West 1st Avenue in Vancouver, near the False Creek seawall — a popular cycling corridor. 3a0031bdf1: Joe Pesto's is a locally owned and operated wood-fired pizzeria in downtown Squamish, voted best pizza in the city. Cyclists finishing a ride in the Sea-to-Sky corridor will find a full dine-in experience with local beer and wine on tap, or a quick takeout option to fuel the next leg.
a93ddc2039: SpearHead Winery is an award-winning Kelowna estate winery specializing in single-vineyard Pinot Noir from the Central Okanagan Valley, led by winemaker Grant Stanley who brings experience from New Zealand, Oregon, and BC. Situated on Spiers Road in the heart of Okanagan wine country, it makes a natural destination stop on a cycling wine tour through the Kelowna region.
8869ab1640: White Spot is BC's longest-running restaurant chain, operating since 1928 and known for burgers made with 100% fresh Canadian beef and locally sourced BC ingredients including BC chicken and BC-grown potato fries. The Fort Street Victoria location is a full sit-down family restaurant offering breakfast, lunch, and dinner, with dine-in, takeout, curbside pickup, and third-party delivery options. It's a reliable, familiar stop for a touring cyclist wanting a full hot meal in a comfortable setting.
42935039be: Noah's Cafe is a Japanese fusion bistro and cocktail bar on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, a short ride from the Stanley Park seawall. The kitchen offers creative tapas-style sharing plates — from aburi tuna tataki to wagyu beef tartare — alongside an omakase course experience. The bar program leans on Japanese spirits and techniques, making this an atmospheric evening stop for cyclists exploring the neighbourhood.
f33e4fa074: The Sandbar is a full-service seafood restaurant on Granville Island, situated on the water between the Arts Club Theatre and Ocean Cement, directly under the Granville Street Bridge with views over False Creek. Cycling tourists on the Vancouver Seawall will find it a natural stopping point, as it sits steps from False Creek Water Ferries and the Seawall itself.
32c43cbf0f: Acquafarina is a Michelin Guide-recommended Italian fine dining restaurant in the heart of downtown Vancouver, operated by the Perse Hospitality Group. The kitchen specializes in modern Italian cuisine made from scratch with locally sourced ingredients, spanning handmade pasta, fresh seafood, Wagyu beef, and a curated caviar program. A polished bar program, weekend brunch, private event spaces, and a unique Liquor Locker membership add to its reputation as one of Vancouver's most refined dining destinations.
e164d80170: Di Muzio Ristorante is an Italian restaurant located in Kamloops, BC. It appears to be a dinner-focused establishment, suggesting a sit-down dining experience suited to cyclists looking for an evening meal after a day on the road.
4da4e1b476: Selkirk Cafe is a neighbourhood cafe situated on Jutland Road in Victoria, BC, a corridor that sees steady commuter and recreational cycling traffic near the Gorge waterway. The cafe operates weekday mornings and lunchtimes, making it a potential mid-ride stop for cyclists exploring the west side of the city. Beyond its OSM listing and Facebook presence, little additional detail is publicly verifiable.
8d3f362a26: Little Sprout Café is a social enterprise café operated by Communitas Supportive Care Society, a BC charity supporting people living with disabilities, with all profits reinvested into that mission. The menu centres on microgreens grown in-house and Fraser Valley sourced ingredients, prepared in a fully visible open-kitchen concept by an inclusively hired team. It is a community-rooted, values-driven spot that offers a genuinely local and nutritious food stop in the Abbotsford area.
6000f010d3: Bori Korean Restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue serves home-style Korean meals inspired by the nourishing qualities of barley ('Bori'), with a menu spanning traditional pancakes, deep-fried dishes, and hearty mains. The restaurant operates as both a sit-down dining room and a takeout spot, with online pick-up ordering available. It sits on a busy commercial corridor in North Vancouver that cyclists commonly travel when exploring the North Shore.
90874d7e2a: The Tartan Toque is a Victoria neighbourhood taphouse and wing restaurant that has won 'Victoria's Best Wings' multiple times since opening in 2012. Known for double-cooked crispy wings with dozens of house-made sauces, scratch-made burgers, and a rotating selection of local craft beers on tap, it offers casual comfort food in a relaxed setting. Dietary-friendly options including gluten-free, lactose-free, and vegetarian items are available throughout the menu.
2d3eccd7ac: Green Waves Salads is a salad-focused fast food establishment located in Tofino, BC. As a quick-service spot in a popular surf and cycling destination, it would cater to health-conscious visitors seeking fresh food options. Current operational status is uncertain.
11e7776681: A Cantonese restaurant on Kingsway in Vancouver offering indoor seating. Touring cyclists can stop for sit-down meals of traditional Cantonese cuisine.
20ca5eb861: Samz is a neighbourhood pub in Surrey offering food, drinks, and live sports viewing, with an attached liquor store on the same premises. The liquor store next door stocks beer, wine, and spirits at competitive prices, making this a convenient stop for cyclists looking to resupply.
48eb798563: Burnt Orange Cafe + Bistro is a brunch and lunch spot on Hastings Street in Burnaby, known for its specialty fluffy pancakes and 49th Parallel coffee. It operates seven days a week and offers table reservations, suggesting a sit-down dining experience. A touring cyclist rolling along the Hastings corridor would find it a solid mid-morning or midday refuelling stop.
3ba6eda693: Two Horns is an upscale Korean and Japanese BBQ steakhouse in Richmond specializing in premium cuts including dry-aged beef and Canadian Prime Beef. A touring cyclist visiting the Richmond cycling network would find a full sit-down dining experience with lunch specials and delivery/online ordering available.
acb1e64291: Epic Grill Silogs is a small restaurant serving Chinese and Filipino cuisine, including the Filipino staple silog dishes (garlic rice with protein). It operates as a takeout-friendly spot and maintains a no-smoking environment. Touring cyclists passing through the New Westminster area may find it a quick stop for hearty, inexpensive Filipino comfort food.
861554946b: A family-run neighbourhood café that has been caffeinating East Vancouver since 2003, The Laughing Bean is known for locally roasted coffee, fresh-baked pastries, and a dog-friendly patio on East Hastings Street. 676a3e5db0: The Roost is a working 10-acre farm in North Saanich that grows and mills its own wheat for daily fresh bread, tends a 2-acre vineyard producing estate wines, and raises free-range hens and sheep — making the food genuinely farm-to-table rather than a marketing claim. A short ride from the Victoria International Airport ferry corridor, it offers cyclists a genuinely pastoral stop with regional cuisine and local wine.
0ac192dc72: Kalvas The Loghouse Restaurant is an upscale fine-dining destination in Parksville housed in a distinctive log building, specializing in prime-grade steaks and fresh Pacific Northwest seafood including wild sockeye salmon, halibut, and Dungeness crab. The restaurant also offers phone-ahead pickup for those wanting a quality meal on the go.
7eaa53310e: Bella Roma Pizzeria & Ristorante is a locally owned Italian restaurant in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, helmed by chef Jimmy Khinda who trained for three years in Italy before bringing his craft home to BC. d7fc31e256: Chez Christophe is a Swiss-inspired chocolaterie and patisserie founded by Swiss-trained pastry chef Christophe Bonzon, with this White Rock location opening in 2019. A rewarding stop for touring cyclists seeking quality coffee or an indulgent chocolate treat along the Johnston Road corridor.
aa865f69fc: Smokehouse 93 is a slow-smoked BBQ restaurant located at the Crossroads in downtown Invermere, serving Canadian meats hand-rubbed with a signature spice blend and smoked for 12–20 hours until fall-off-the-bone tender. a4d2bd3371: Gmen@NanChuu Ramen Shop is a ramen restaurant located in Richmond's Alexandra Road dining corridor, a dense stretch of East Asian eateries popular with locals and visitors alike. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's flat, bikeable streets will find it a convenient stop for a hot bowl after riding the dyke trails or nearby greenways.
d2a902768b: Bao is an Asian fusion restaurant situated in Victoria's historic Chinatown, specializing in Taiwanese steam buns (Gua Bao) with a rotating cast of fillings alongside ramen, bibimbap, and Korean fried chicken. The compact, focused menu reflects a blend of East and Southeast Asian flavours, with most dishes available in vegetarian, vegan, or gluten-free adaptations on request. It makes a solid mid-ride meal stop given its Chinatown location and dine-in or takeout flexibility.
5d3b17e946: Junior's Pub & Grill is a neighbourhood pub on the corner of Commercial Drive and Graveley in Vancouver's East Side, positioning itself as a welcoming community gathering spot. The pub also hosts regular events such as Friday live entertainment, Sunday karaoke, and fundraiser nights for local sports teams and charities.
72db7895a1: Namiya is a sushi restaurant on Vancouver's West Broadway offering Japanese cuisine. The business offers online ordering for convenient takeout. Located on a busy urban street, it provides a casual dining option for cyclists in the neighborhood.
8e72b242f5: Kyuzo is a Japanese restaurant on Granville Street specializing in omakase dining, where the chef curates a personalized meal based on guest preferences and allergies using fresh, seasonal ingredients. 32c5ea4864: A breakfast and coffee cafe on Bowen Island with outdoor seating. Located on Dorman Road in the island community. No additional details confirmed due to website unavailability.
15deba6703: Little Thai Place has served authentic Thai cuisine in Victoria since 2003, operated by a Bangkok family with a strong local reputation for fresh ingredients, house-made sauces, and consistent quality. a294473c71: The Irish Times is a Victoria institution on Government Street, voted best pub in North America in 2017 and best Irish Entertainment Venue in 2018. Located on one of Victoria's main cycling corridors, it serves as a natural stopping point for touring cyclists exploring the city.
786fe290f8: Crust n Crunch is a BC-based pizza and donair chain with over 11 years in the industry, known for bold flavour combinations including South Asian-inspired options like Shahi Paneer and Butter Chicken pizzas alongside classic donairs. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a fast, filling meal with strong vegetarian options and online ordering.
3cf0c6c138: Sakura Sushi & Grocery is a beloved Victoria institution that opened in 1997 and has grown into one of the city's most popular Japanese takeout destinations, offering handmade sushi rolls, hot kitchen dishes like udon, donburi, curry, and bento, as well as Japanese grocery items. 80f77869f8: The Corner Hotpot is a hotpot restaurant located on West Broadway in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood. dc58ec7374: GAON Korean Cuisine is a Korean restaurant on Kingsway in Burnaby, offering indoor seating in a no-smoking environment. 4d20586994: Pho Ten is a Vietnamese restaurant in Richmond specializing in traditional dishes including phở, rice plates, vermicelli bowls, bánh mì, and spring rolls, all prepared with fresh ingredients and traditional recipes. 81b780e306: Mama Said Pizza Co. is a Brooklyn-style pizza restaurant in Port Moody, BC, serving scratch-made deck-oven pies with premium toppings. 6c6d4500cd: Gateway to India is an Indian restaurant in Nanaimo serving authentic dishes made with exotic spices imported from the northern and southern regions of the Indian subcontinent. 017f8cc980: Jacks On The Water is a waterfront restaurant and bar that opened in 2024 on Sidney's Seaport Place, offering panoramic views of the Saanich Peninsula shoreline in a casual, inviting setting. edb46859d7: The Cabin is an upscale-casual restaurant in the seaside community of Crescent Beach, serving Pacific Northwest cuisine centred on fresh local seafood, AAA steaks, and gourmet pasta alongside a full bar with craft beers and signature cocktails. 38afd3df09: The apron is a contemporary Canadian farm-to-table restaurant inside the Westin Wall Centre, steps from Vancouver International Airport, serving Pacific Northwest cuisine sourced from local farmers, growers, and fishers. 37476c60d2: Fiore Famiglia is a neighbourhood Italian restaurant in Vancouver's west side, focused on 'simple Italian done right' with a full menu spanning lunch, dinner, happy hour, and takeout. 377e0e2603: The Thunderbird Café occupies the admission-free lower level of the Squamish Lil'wat Cultural Centre in Whistler's Upper Village, serving Indigenous-inspired dishes such as bannock tacos, venison chili, and cedar plank salmon chowder prepared with fresh local ingredients. 4173e1171f: Nubo Kitchen + Bar is a Japanese fusion restaurant in the historic Janion building near the Johnson Street Bridge in downtown Victoria, serving fresh sushi, sashimi, ramen, tapas-style sharing plates, and modern cocktails since 2019. 21a65b1eee: O'Hare's Gastropub is a full-service pub and liquor store in Richmond's Steveston neighbourhood, a popular destination for cyclists exploring the flat dyke trails and waterfront. c042ac5fba: Pizza Pizza is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 1967 with over 750 locations coast to coast, operating here as a counter-service restaurant in a Burnaby strip unit along the busy Lougheed Highway corridor. e774311110: Sushi Aji is a neighbourhood Japanese restaurant on Kingsway in East Vancouver offering a broad menu of sushi rolls, nigiri, sashimi, oshi sushi, bento boxes, and hot dishes. 0a57ce4e0a: The Ivanhoe Pub is a no-frills East Vancouver neighbourhood bar established in 1907, serving locals on Main Street for over a century. da69f796b1: Sushi Tendo is a Japanese sushi restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver's Cambie Village neighbourhood, offering indoor-only seating with no outdoor patio. 3d9203b42c: Triple O's is a BC-born quick-service burger chain and sibling brand to White Spot, known for its signature Triple 'O' sauce, hand-scooped milkshakes, and Kennebec fries. b70c659410: Numero Uno Pizza is a family-run thin-crust gourmet pizza shop on Davie Street in downtown Vancouver, baking with house-made dough and sauce and offering a broad menu of meaty and vegetarian pies available by the slice or whole. fd72138097: Take Five Cafe is a Metro Vancouver coffee franchise that has been operating since 2003, serving specialty Arabica espresso drinks alongside Italian-inspired savouries such as panini and wraps, freshly baked pastries, and seasonal specialty drinks. aa68f35855: Bless'd Sips & Slices is a family-owned artisan pizza-by-the-slice restaurant located near Gyro Beach in Kelowna, cooking pizzas in a gas-fired brick oven using slow-fermented Italian flour and no canola oil. 9e5449cd48: The Brownstone has been a downtown Kamloops landmark since 2004, housed in the beautifully restored 1904 Canadian Bank of Commerce building — once the workplace of poet Robert Service. dd197826e2: Dublin Crossing is a full-service Irish pub on SW Marine Drive in South Vancouver, offering a broad menu of pub classics alongside a robust bar program featuring Irish whiskeys, draught beers, and creative cocktails. 11c9237fc0: Popeyes Louisiana Kitchen is a well-known fast food chain specializing in Southern-style fried chicken with Louisiana-inspired seasoning. e1149e80fe: Big Chicken Town is a Korean fried chicken restaurant in Surrey, BC, specializing in double-fried chicken with traditional Korean recipes and signature sauces such as Honey Garlic, Black Yummy, and Green Mountain. 7c29bfd442: Pizza Camp is a fast-food restaurant offering pizza and Indian cuisine with both indoor and outdoor seating. It operates via an online ordering platform, providing convenient takeout options for touring cyclists in need of a quick meal.
962d305b44: Canada Cafe is a restaurant in Merritt, BC offering dining for local patrons and travelers. Limited amenity details are available, but the business is confirmed to be operating and accessible by phone for inquiries.
59f7e51e9e: Lido Restaurant (麗都餐廳) is a Cantonese restaurant located in Richmond's Aberdeen area, a neighbourhood known for its concentration of authentic Hong Kong-style dining. The restaurant offers a traditional dim-sum and Cantonese menu in a community-oriented setting.
a442789b8a: Quesada Burritos & Tacos is a Canadian fast-casual Mexican chain with locations across BC and the rest of Canada. It is a takeout-friendly stop well positioned along the Lonsdale corridor for cyclists passing through North Vancouver.
4a39f79ad0: Chalo Momo is a quick-casual Nepali kitchen serving traditional momos, Indo-Chinese noodles, tandoori dishes, and fusion items made fresh to order. d6cb2be53b: Noma Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in the Willoughby Town Centre shopping complex in Langley. The restaurant offers online ordering and takeout options, providing a convenient food stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.
19715f0979: PappaRoti is a Vancouver outpost of a Malaysian-origin cafe chain celebrated for its signature coffee-caramel buns — a soft, buttery roti with a crisp coffee crust born from a family recipe in Malaysia around 2000. aff940d057: Angel Cake Cafe is a restaurant located on Fraser Street in Vancouver. It accepts cash payments only. Additional business details are unavailable due to website connectivity issues.
a14b79fd73: Part and Parcel is a neighbourhood restaurant in Victoria's Quadra Village that has been cooking for its community since 2013, known for seasonal small plates, creative cocktails, and low-intervention wines sourced from small producers. 5f5959b140: Mercado Mexican Market & Taqueria is a Coquitlam outpost of the Restco restaurant group, combining a Mexican grocery market stocked with salsas and ready-to-cook essentials with a quick-service counter. f5676166b2: A small neighbourhood café and scratch bakery on the Vancouver seawall at Leg In Boot Square, a few minutes west of the Cambie Street Bridge. 1ad3253046: The Fernwood Inn is a community gathering place anchoring Fernwood Square in one of Victoria's oldest and most colourful neighbourhoods, serving artisan pub fare, locally-sourced organic ingredients, wild seafood, and Island microbrews. 5c59c8bd01: The Crow & Gate holds the distinction of being BC's first neighbourhood pub, having opened in 1972 in rural Yellow Point south of Nanaimo. 420e9a8c31: Tong Fei is a Chinese restaurant in Chilliwack serving the local community. It provides a sit-down dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area. Contact the restaurant directly for current menu and operational details.
37509442eb: Second Slice Pizza is a late-night pizza counter on Douglas Street in downtown Victoria, built around fresh multigrain dough made daily and an extensive by-the-slice menu. 0f279836fc: Villa Rosa Ristorante is one of Penticton's most established Italian restaurants, open at the same Westminster Avenue location since 1996 and under current owners Tyler and Nicole Gable since 2007. 6680a32c42: Masala Junction is a family-owned Indian restaurant founded in 2013, drawing on over 25 years of culinary experience across India and Europe. fb7989c54e: A 24/7 McDonald's fast food location in Chilliwack on DeLair Road, offering burgers, chicken, McCafé beverages, and a full drive-through. 46c27ab6ae: A McDonald's fast food restaurant in North Vancouver offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, fries, and McCafé beverages.
