7082aa1aa4: Parkhill Seafood Restaurant (陶源金閣海鮮酒家) serves fusion-style Hong Kong cuisine in Richmond, with a menu spanning dim sum, seafood, set menus, and banquet dining. Led by Head Chef Lung Chow, the kitchen blends traditional Cantonese flavors with innovative twists. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down dining experience with takeout pickup also available.
7bb0c3584e: Continuum Coffee Roasters is a specialty small-batch coffee roaster founded in 2012, now operating out of a roastery in Burnaby where visitors are welcome to stop in. They source fair trade, organic, and single-origin coffees from producers around the world, roasting in batches of 1–10 kg for maximum freshness. Cyclists passing through can explore a range of espresso blends, single-origin offerings, and limited special-release lots from notable producers.
3b883dd678: Innocent Ice Cream is a family-run, gluten-free ice cream sandwich shop in Vancouver's Hastings-Sunrise neighbourhood, founded in 2014 after the owner spent years perfecting celiac-safe cookie recipes. The shop crafts hand-made ice cream sandwiches, milkshakes, cones, and soda floats entirely in-store year-round, with plant-based and non-dairy options available. Beyond the storefront, Innocent also operates a solar-powered ice cream truck and a pink tricycle for catering events across the city.
73b7a6d0d7: The Orca Inn is a historic pub and hotel in Alert Bay, built in the 1930s in what was formerly the town's 'Chinatown' district, combining two original commercial buildings into the social heart of this remote island community. It offers oceanview rooms, suites with kitchenettes, a restaurant, and a pub with live music overlooking Johnstone Strait. Alert Bay is a compelling destination for First Nations culture and orca whale watching, making this inn a natural base for cyclists exploring British Columbia's remote north coast.
86106e10e2: El Caracol Mexican Cafe is a sit-down Mexican restaurant located on Victoria Drive in Vancouver's Sunset neighbourhood. The Victoria Drive corridor is a well-travelled cycling route connecting south Vancouver to the city centre, making this cafe a convenient stop for riders coming from or heading toward Fraserview and Champlain Heights. As a neighbourhood cafe with regular hours, it offers a full-service dining experience in an area with relatively few comparable options.
73851e822a: Amogha Indian Kitchen & Bar is a full-service Indian restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street built around twelve distinct regional cuisines — from Hyderabadi dum biryani to Malabar moilee — developed after two years of research across the subcontinent. The kitchen pairs regionally-specific cooking with a craft cocktail bar built on Indian aromatics like tamarind, cardamom, and saffron. With 80 seats and a menu extensively marked for dietary preferences, it is a substantial dining stop for cyclists riding the Main Street corridor.
a6e5fac7c4: J&J Wonton Noodle House is a long-running Cantonese and Szechuan restaurant on Fort Street in Victoria, a multi-time 'Best of the City' honoree that emphasizes local ingredients and freshness. A distinctive glassed-in kitchen lets diners watch chefs at work, and the extensive menu ranges from wonton noodle soups to Sichuan specialties. Vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options are well-represented, making it a practical and satisfying stop for cyclists with varied dietary needs.
0d135eb3e1: Ancora Ambleside is a multi-award-winning waterfront restaurant on the Ambleside shore of West Vancouver, serving Nikkei fusion cuisine that blends Peruvian and Japanese traditions with Pacific Northwest sustainable seafood. The dining room features high ceilings, sweeping panoramic views, a theatre-style open kitchen, and coastal-inspired décor by Vancouver's SmartDesign Group. It has appeared on Canada's 100 Best Restaurants list and earned repeated Wine Spectator Awards of Excellence.
f0fd7d38b1: A Japanese sushi restaurant with two locations in Vancouver (Fraser and Davie Streets), specializing in authentic Japanese food. A convenient dining option for touring cyclists exploring the city.
70c330482c: Okome is a Japanese restaurant in Richmond whose name means 'rice' — the grain that anchors its menu and culinary identity. The brand draws on Japanese folklore, with a Kitsune fox logo representing the deity of rice and prosperity. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's south end will find a sit-down or takeout meal option with online ordering available.
596179ad3a: Viet Flavour Restaurant is a Vietnamese eatery on West Broadway serving pho, vermicelli bowls, bánh mì, and fresh salad rolls. With 81 customer reviews and a dedicated vegetarian section on the menu, it caters to a range of dietary needs. Online ordering with quick pickup makes it a practical stop for cyclists passing through the Kitsilano–South Granville corridor.
9ee0f5b50f: SAKU is a Japanese katsu restaurant chain that introduced traditional breaded-and-fried cutlets to Vancouver when it opened its first Robson Street location in early 2018. The Richmond branch is one of several Lower Mainland outposts operated under the LLH Eatery parent company, specialising in premium-quality meats served in the katsu style. Walk-ins join a digital waitlist rather than booking a table in advance.
b925de79a7: Mr Pickwick's Fish & Chips is a fish and chips restaurant on 96 Avenue in Surrey, BC. It is listed in OSM as an active restaurant with a Facebook presence. Cyclists passing through Surrey's 96 Avenue corridor could find it a convenient stop, though amenity details remain unverified.
b0bd4effc5: Country Vines Winery is a family-owned, small-batch estate winery on Steveston Highway in Richmond, producing award-winning wines from grapes grown in its on-site vineyard — an unexpected terroir for the Lower Mainland. Visitors can join guided vineyard and barrel room tours, enjoy charcuterie pairings in a covered outdoor lounge, or relax in the picnic area alongside resident animals. The winery hosts live music throughout the summer season and is proudly pet- and family-friendly.
181e3fc4a7: T-Bay Bistro is a noodle restaurant situated on Granville Street near the Marpole neighbourhood of Vancouver. OSM records it as an active restaurant as of mid-2024. Cyclists riding the Granville corridor would find it a convenient stop for a hot noodle meal.
faa8100524: Ross Bay Pub is a cozy neighborhood pub on Fairfield Road in Victoria, tucked close to the Dallas Road waterfront and the Fairfield and Oak Bay neighborhoods. It offers food, drinks, daily specials, and community events, positioning itself as a local gathering spot. The location makes it a convenient stop for cyclists exploring the scenic coastal routes of Victoria's south shore.
5bd1df1ab4: Delicado's is a funky, high-energy southwestern cafe and deli known for freshly made wraps, burritos, enchiladas, and homemade soups prepared daily on the premises. The Nanaimo North location is one of several BC franchises offering both dine-in and takeout, with a mini-market stocked with specialty hot sauces, salsas, and oil-free hummus. It's a solid stop for cyclists wanting a filling, colourful meal with plenty of vegetarian-friendly options.
0d07dba603: John's Place is a beloved Victoria institution that has been serving scratch-made breakfast and lunch for over 40 years from its downtown Pandora Avenue location. The kitchen makes everything from scratch — including herb bread, cornbread, and all salad dressings — and gained national attention when Food Network Canada featured it on 'You Gotta Eat Here,' showcasing dishes like Eggs Benedict with real-butter hollandaise and Belgian Waffles. A touring cyclist rolling into Victoria will find a relaxed, diner-style room and hearty Canadian comfort fare to fuel the next leg.
785f841fec: Paragon Pizza is a locally owned and operated fast-food pizza shop on Victoria Drive in Vancouver, serving handcrafted pizzas made with fresh ingredients across a range of veggie, chicken, and meat toppings. The shop offers a simple, welcoming dine-in space alongside pickup and delivery options. It sits on a busy commercial corridor that touring cyclists traveling the east side of Vancouver may pass through.
88b036b9bb: Little Beetle (also known as Little Beetle Bistro) is a regional cuisine restaurant that opened in August 2024, tucked into a unit on Vedder Road in Chilliwack. It is a no-reservation, sit-down spot with air conditioning and full wheelchair accessibility. Cyclists travelling the Vedder Road corridor will find it a convenient stop for a meal in a comfortable indoor setting.
2a5adbd162: Bond Bond's Bakery is a bakery located on Blanshard Street in central Victoria. The business appears to be open and operational based on OSM records, though website maintenance prevented verification of specific amenities or services.
01cb33e826: Well Tea is a full-service Taiwanese restaurant in Richmond's Hazelbridge commercial district, specializing in individual hotpots, wok stir-fries, and traditional bubble teas. The menu spans over a dozen hotpot broth options alongside classics like five-spice pig intestine, teppanyaki beef, and scallion pancakes with beef. Reservations accommodate groups up to 24, and online pickup and delivery orders can be placed through third-party platforms.
a563b7af18: Otaru Japanese Kitchen is a Japanese restaurant in Richmond, BC serving authentic dishes including sushi, rolls, udon, and tempura. The restaurant positions itself as striving to be the best in Richmond and offers both dine-in and pickup ordering. A touring cyclist passing through Richmond's No. 2 Road corridor would find it a convenient stop for a full Japanese meal.
80735dcdcf: Kinton Ramen UBC is a location of one of North America's largest ramen chains, situated on the University of British Columbia campus just west of the University Boulevard and Westbrook Mall intersection. The restaurant offers a broad range of soup bases — pork, beef, chicken, and vegetarian — with multiple flavour and noodle options, and a patio for outdoor seating. It is part of a Canadian chain founded in 2012 with over 50 locations across five provinces and two countries.
e7eacda980: POW Pizza serves Detroit-style pizza in Windermere, BC, with a sourdough crust naturally leavened with local spring water and baked in square steel pans with a signature cheese crown. The restaurant operates year-round and offers dine-out seating on an outdoor deck by the fire, a short walk from the lake. Notably, the business accepts cash and cryptocurrency only — no credit or debit cards.
3f90d614de: Big Way Hot Pot is a self-serve hot pot chain with a location on North Vancouver's West Esplanade, offering individually served pots with over 100 fresh ingredients and more than 18 broth and dry-mix options. Diners customize their meal from premium meats, seafood, and fresh vegetables cooked tableside in broths ranging from Signature Mala to collagen pork bone. The restaurant is part of a rapidly expanding BC-based chain with a rewards program and app-based ordering.
56ad863b2d: El Guapo is a lively Yaletown restaurant serving SoCal and BC West Coast-inspired cuisine, with a menu spanning brunch, lunch, dinner, and happy hour anchored by their signature margaritas. The space is designed to feel welcoming to all comers, with live music every weekend and big-screen sports coverage including FIFA matches near BC Place. Dishes range from Huevos Rancheros at brunch to Carnitas Tacos at happy hour, with delivery available through Uber Eats and DoorDash.
0785a9cbc6: A cafe in Kimberley, British Columbia. Operating details and amenities are unverifiable due to website access limitations.
7401eb9166: Provisions Italiana is an Italian restaurant operated by Executive Table Group, located inside the boutique Seaside Hotel in North Vancouver's vibrant Shipyards District at Lower Lonsdale. The kitchen focuses on Roman-style pizzas, northern Italian pastas, and a celebrated vegetable program inspired by Italian countryside cooking, served in a warm room anchored by an open kitchen and flickering fireplace. It's a sit-down destination for cyclists finishing a ride along the North Shore waterfront.
603fcf2db1: Noodle Road is a Korean and Japanese restaurant in Abbotsford serving a broad menu of Asian noodles, sushi, sashimi, teriyaki, tempura, and udon-style dishes. The casual sit-down spot also accommodates phone-in pickup orders, making it a flexible stop for cyclists moving along the South Fraser Way corridor. The menu spans both meat and tofu-based preparations across multiple Asian culinary traditions.
b51174db41: Coast & Country Diner and Caterers has been serving the Fraser Valley of British Columbia since 1997, offering dine-in breakfasts and a full catering operation for weddings, corporate events, and celebrations. Located in the Cloverdale neighbourhood of Surrey, the diner is known for fresh, made-to-order food and strong repeat clientele. Private event bookings are also available for groups.
9e28fea0dd: Papa John's is a national pizza chain franchise located on Sooke Road in the western Victoria area, serving pizza, breadsticks, and wings. The location offers both delivery and carryout ordering. It sits in a strip-mall unit convenient for cyclists passing through the Colwood corridor.
0aeeb0ca58: Nonna's Cucina Pop-up is an intimate Italian restaurant on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, relocated from its original Hastings Street home and helmed by Joe Fazio. The menu centres on handmade pasta with chef-selected sauces, appetizers, cocktails, and Italian wines served in a lively neighbourhood setting. The restaurant positions itself as an ongoing pop-up experience celebrating classic Italian home cooking.
4e33aad1f0: The Barking Parrot Bar is a waterfront bar and restaurant situated within the Penticton Lakeside Resort, just steps from Okanagan Lake. It serves food, cocktails, and draft beer, and bills itself as Penticton's most popular bar. Regular events include wing nights, smash burger specials on weekends, and a daily Flappy Hour promotion.
ad9679aea1: Freshslice Pizza is a Vancouver-founded pizza chain known for by-the-slice and whole-pizza service at accessible prices, with both indoor and outdoor seating. The Robson Street location sits in one of the city's busiest pedestrian and cycling corridors, making it a convenient fuel stop for cyclists passing through the West End. A gluten-free cauliflower crust and a broad range of vegetarian toppings give riders with dietary restrictions solid options.
5e41be6fae: East Side Craft House is a family-owned neighbourhood pub in East Vancouver, operating since 2012 in the former Elephant Walk Pub space. It pours 16 taps of local Vancouver craft draft beer alongside fresh-grilled burgers, never-frozen chicken wings, and a rotating pub menu. The pub has a dog-friendly patio and hosts weekly community events including Wing Wednesdays, Trivia Saturdays, and NFL Sunday Ticket screenings.
16548fd269: U Town Hot Pot Malatang is a hot pot and mala tang restaurant in Coquitlam where diners choose fresh ingredients, have them weighed, and cook them in rich, made-from-scratch broths — from classic spicy mala to tomato dry mix. The menu features unusual finds like frog legs and razor clams alongside premium meats and a broad condiment bar for customizing heat and flavour. The space is described as open, bright, and spacious with attentive service, making it a viable stop for a hungry touring cyclist needing a substantial sit-down meal.
df645cae7f: Japanese Bistro Kamome is a small Japanese bistro and lounge bar in Vancouver's Joyce-Collingwood neighbourhood serving classic and modern Japanese cuisine. The restaurant's signature creation is the 'Ja-Panini,' a grilled rice sandwich with a choice of meat, seafood, or vegetables wrapped in seaweed and pressed on a panini press. The lounge side of the menu features cocktails including a range of martinis and mojitos.
970f301f59: Habitat Café sits on the second floor of the Grant Building within the historic 565-acre Hatley Park estate at Royal Roads University, a National Historic Site featuring Edwardian Hatley Castle and renowned Italian, Japanese, and rose gardens. The café is committed to social responsibility and locally sourced BC ingredients, serving seasonal menus that are globally inspired. Touring cyclists can combine a meal stop here with a stroll through some of the most spectacular gardens in the Victoria region.
04938d831d: Dosa Crepe Cafe is a South Indian fusion restaurant that blends traditional fermented-rice dosa with French crepe techniques, serving an extensive menu of dosas, curries, biriyani, bubble tea, and alcoholic beverages. The Rutland location is one of four BC outposts, and the restaurant takes reservations for groups of 4–12 while remaining walk-in friendly for solo cyclists. The menu is notably inclusive, with gluten-free and vegan options throughout.
9ea091dc14: Rock Salt Restaurant & Café sits at the Fulford Harbour ferry terminal on Salt Spring Island, making it a natural first or last stop for cyclists crossing by ferry. The restaurant features a 180-degree ocean view dining room with a scratch kitchen that emphasises local ingredients, while the café side offers baked goods, wraps, and sandwiches for riders who need to eat on the run. The menu is deliberately broad, covering meat-eaters, vegetarians, kids, and gluten-free diners.
96513a7d02: A locally-established Indian restaurant in Nanaimo offering traditional curries and regional dishes. A convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking a substantial meal.
247d736547: Smitty's is a Canadian pancake restaurant chain with a location in Nanaimo on Island Highway North. It serves casual breakfast and lunch dining to traveling customers and locals.
e247e784d6: A McDonald's fast food restaurant on Rutherford Road in Nanaimo, serving burgers, McCafé beverages, and breakfast items. The location offers drive-thru, curbside pickup, and delivery via multiple third-party partners. For touring cyclists passing through north Nanaimo, it is a familiar and accessible stop for a quick meal or snack.
dbc9bc0004: Cannery Café is a casual diner situated in the historic Steveston Village waterfront district of Richmond, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner. The café is locally notable for having served as the filming location of Granny's Diner for ABC's Once Upon a Time and Once Upon a Time in Wonderland. Outdoor seating is available, positioning it as a natural rest stop along the scenic Steveston waterfront cycling corridor.
4f801163fc: Shanzee's Biscuit Café is a Victoria brunch spot run by chef and owner Shannon Stead, celebrated for homemade biscuits and gravy and inventive flavour combinations developed at the Carnarvon concession. Voted one of Canada's top 100 places to eat on Yelp, it offers both hearty comfort dishes and vegan-friendly options. Located in Victoria's Old Town area on Pandora Avenue, the café features outdoor seating.
aafb2e8b05: Unique Green is a bubble tea cafe in Richmond, BC, serving specialty tea drinks in an indoor setting. The OSM record notes no outdoor seating, suggesting a fully indoor experience. For cyclists passing through Richmond, it offers a spot to rest and rehydrate with a cold drink.
4a580d7b81: Tino's Pizza is a family-style Italian-Canadian pizzeria that has been a Richmond staple for over 25 years, located inside the Richlea (Broadmoor) Mall between Starbucks and FreshCo. The kitchen produces fresh dough daily, hand-crafts small-batch sauces, and sources vegetables locally when available. Cyclists can eat in or grab a carry-out order from a full menu of pizzas, pastas, and salads.
73b8431036: The Oxy Pub is a pub in downtown Nanaimo. It serves as a community gathering place for food and drink.
ebe99bd852: A Starbucks Coffee location on Main Street in Osoyoos, sitting at the southern tip of the Okanagan wine country and a natural stop on cycling routes along Highway 3. The shop offers the full Starbucks espresso and seasonal beverage menu with outdoor seating, making it a convenient rest point for riders crossing the Similkameen corridor. As a recognized chain, it provides predictable food and drink options in a town that serves as a gateway to several long-distance touring routes.
3f21115319: Kernels Popcorn is a Canadian popcorn chain franchise operating since 1983, offering a wide range of sweet, salty, spicy, and cheesy popcorn flavours. This location sits inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre, Kelowna's largest regional mall with over 170 stores. A touring cyclist stopping here can grab a quick snack to go while the mall's broader services are also accessible.
bd038fc1a7: Freshslice Pizza is a BC-based pizza chain with a location on Pacific Boulevard near the False Creek waterfront and Vancouver Seawall cycling corridor. The restaurant offers pizza by the slice or whole pie with any toppings, including a gluten-free cauliflower crust option, making it a quick and flexible stop for hungry cyclists. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available.
e73080184c: Vij's is a landmark Indian restaurant on Vancouver's Cambie Street, a three-time recipient of the Michelin Bib Gourmand Award (2023–2025) recognized for exceptional cuisine and genuine hospitality. The menu spans vegetarian snacks, curries, seafood, and meat dishes alongside a curated beverage program with sommelier-guided wine pairings. Walk-in guests are always welcome, and seasonal patio seating makes it a viable stop for cyclists riding the Cambie corridor.
954f144922: Lee's Donuts is a Vancouver institution founded in 1979, originally at Granville Island and now expanded to multiple locations including this Gastown outpost on Water Street. The shop is known for handmade, scratch-made classic donuts — honey dips, jelly-filled, and rotating seasonal flavours — all made fresh daily. Featured on Netflix and beloved by generations of Vancouverites, it's a reliable quick stop for a sweet treat in one of the city's most walkable and bikeable neighbourhoods.
b42287fc08: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain that prides itself on fresh-made dough from Canadian wheat, organic tomato sauce, and meats raised without antibiotics. The Creston location offers takeout and delivery of pizza, salads, sides, and desserts. Cyclists passing through Creston can fuel up with a hot meal including a range of plant-based and meat-free options.
edb52bdb14: Mr. Shawarma claims to be the first Middle Eastern and shawarma food truck in Canada, serving downtown Vancouver since 2009 from multiple street-level locations including Robson Square and two SkyTrain station entrances. All food is prepared fresh daily from scratch using halal-certified, locally sourced BC ingredients out of their own 8,000 sq ft commercial kitchen.
029219d5a2: Zenya Japanese Kitchen is a fast-casual Japanese restaurant tucked into the second-floor food court of International Village in downtown Vancouver, specializing in handmade onigiri with 19 fillings alongside udon, curry rice, donburi, and sandwiches. Opened in July 2023, it emphasizes traditional Japanese seasonings combined with locally sourced Vancouver ingredients. Delivery is available through Fantan and Uber Eats for cyclists who prefer off-bike pickup.
31d7be20ad: Hanaya Japanese Restaurant is a Japanese sushi and dining restaurant in Surrey, BC, in operation since at least 2004. It offers dine-in, online ordering, and delivery, making it a practical stop for cyclists looking for a full sit-down Japanese meal. The restaurant is wheelchair accessible and accepts credit and debit cards.
b16bca173d: King's Kitchen is a restaurant located in Maple Ridge. The business website is currently under development and does not yet provide information about the establishment.
22f50028fd: Donnellan's Irish Pub is an authentic Irish-themed bar in Vancouver's Granville Entertainment District, known for live music and DJs every weekend and a hearty Irish menu anchored by what the pub bills as the best pint of Guinness in the city. The venue includes a second-floor Balcony event space with its own private bar for up to 60 guests, as well as a large open-plan main bar with a stage, pool table, and dart boards. Part of the IRL Group, Donnellan's also hosts a monthly newcomer networking event and has been featured in several local media outlets as a community hub.
4ca975f955: The Coconut is a South Indian restaurant in downtown Kamloops helmed by Chef Lalichan Joseph, whose background cooking aboard cruise lines shapes his commitment to quality and technique. The menu spans the regional breadth of South India — dosas, coconut curries, tandoori dishes, and street-food favourites — made with locally sourced west coast ingredients. Touring cyclists get a warm reception, with a customer-praised bike parking spot right out front and an extensive vegetarian menu.
0f375c9678: BarBurrito is a Canadian fast-casual burrito chain founded in 2005 and now operating 385+ locations across the country. The Abbotsford West Oak location serves customizable burritos, bowls, tacos, and quesadillas made with fresh, in-house ingredients and a wide range of proteins. A touring cyclist looking for a quick, filling, customizable meal on South Fraser Way would find this a reliable stop.
723fd2901f: Me Coffee&Tea (覓Me) is a bubble tea café situated in the busy Number 3 Road retail corridor in Richmond, a hub of the city's vibrant Chinese-Canadian food scene. The shop offers takeaway service, positioning it as a quick hydration stop for cyclists moving through Richmond's commercial centre. Its Chinese-language name and bubble tea focus reflect the cultural character of the surrounding neighbourhood.
992f765665: Umi Sushi Express is a quick-service Japanese cuisine franchise operating over 30 locations across Canada, offering fresh sushi and related dishes for customers on the go. The Burnaby outlet on Kingsway is a takeout-only counter with no on-site seating, making it a grab-and-go stop for cyclists passing through the corridor. It is one of three banner formats in the Umi family, focused on fresh, healthy Japanese food made with care.
5d0ae0116a: Omni Kitchen + Bar is a lively full-service restaurant and bar in historic Fort Langley serving smashed burgers, Neapolitan-style pizzas, brunch, and creative cocktails. The venue is deeply community-oriented, hosting weekly Open Mic nights, ticketed Mixology Showcases, and watch parties for major sporting events. It also operates a food truck and catering service, making it a versatile stop for group rides or events passing through the Fraser Valley.
17f774f48c: Aroma Indian Restaurant is an award-winning fine-dining Indian restaurant in Port Moody, operated by chef CM Bhatt whose recipes were developed in India's 5-star hotels and refined over 26 years. The restaurant has been recognized with multiple Yelp business excellence awards and was repeatedly voted a favourite for Indian food in the Tri-City News A-List contest. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down dining experience with an extensive menu of both meat and vegetarian dishes, plus live music on weekends.
f59e51d3db: Freshslice Pizza is a BC-based pizza chain known for by-the-slice and whole-pie sales with any toppings, available for in-store pickup or delivery. The Vancouver location sits at level 0 with indoor seating and no drive-through. The chain also offers a gluten-free cauliflower crust, making it a flexible quick-stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.
4fac5317e2: A Japanese restaurant located in downtown Vancouver with both indoor and outdoor seating options. Offers casual dining for touring cyclists seeking a substantial meal break.
64530e7ade: Threefold is a brewery collective that brings together three craft breweries — Temporal Artisanal Ales, Boombox, and Slow Hand — under one roof on Powell Street in East Vancouver. The tasting lounge pairs rotating craft beers on tap with a full Neapolitan-style pizza menu plus snacks and desserts. It offers a relaxed, food-forward taproom experience with a strong selection of vegetarian and vegan options.
974612b0c7: Great Dane Coffee is a family-run cafe on the UBC campus, founded in 2012 by mother-and-son team Toni and Andrew, built around house-made food and locally sourced ingredients including Brightside Beans espresso. The shop bakes its own focaccia bread for a range of sandwiches and produces daily pastries such as scones, cinnamon buns, and croissants. Set beside Gage Towers with a patio and large windows, it offers an off-the-beaten-track feel along with online ordering for quick pickup.
02c39c3993: Fufú Café is a Japanese-inspired dessert café on West Broadway in Vancouver, known for its signature soufflé pancakes in both sweet and savory varieties. The menu also features Japanese-style sandos (sandwiches), espresso drinks, matcha beverages, and seasonal specialty sodas. It's a sit-down café that also offers online ordering for pickup and delivery.
8c92af67c9: Coffee Central Roasting bills itself as Vancouver's first coffee roasting commissary — a fully permitted, shared roastery where clients book time to roast their own batches and train with industry experts on machines, Cropster software, and coffee science. It also offers access to small-lot specialty green coffees imported seasonally, and a fully equipped coffee bar for cupping and team training sessions. Access is by appointment, making it a destination for coffee professionals and enthusiasts rather than a drop-in café.
60097a79aa: Megabite is a Vancouver-based pizza franchise with several Lower Mainland locations, including this one on Granville Street in the heart of the city's entertainment district. The menu spans pizza, wings, poutine, and sides, with online ordering, delivery, and a catering service. Vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options are available, making it a practical food stop for groups with mixed dietary needs.
95fe4fa320: JJ Bean is a Vancouver-based independent specialty coffee roaster with cafés across Metro Vancouver, founded in 1996 by the Neate family and repeatedly voted Vancouver's best. This location at Big Bend in Richmond serves freshly roasted espresso and drip coffee alongside house-made baked goods and an all-day breakfast and lunch menu. JJ Bean sources high-quality single-origin and blended coffees roasted daily in small batches at their Powell Street roastery.
bea2585849: Tera V Burger is an all-vegan fast-casual restaurant on West Broadway in Vancouver, specializing in plant-based burgers, loaded bowls, fries, and shakes — with every menu item fully vegan rather than just vegan-optional. It offers dine-in with reservations, takeaway, and home delivery, making it a flexible stop for cyclists passing through the Kitsilano–Point Grey corridor. Reviewers consistently praise the bold flavors and welcoming atmosphere, noting the food impresses even committed meat-eaters.
dd24948acb: Macchiato Caffe is a locally owned Italian-inspired café that has been a downtown Victoria fixture for nearly two decades, operating at the Johnson Street address as 'Macchiato @ The Juliet'. The café serves artisan espresso from Caffe Umbria — a third-generation family roaster based in Vancouver — alongside freshly made panini, salads, soups, and baked goods prepared on-site daily. Both downtown locations offer comfortable indoor seating and an outdoor patio, making them a natural mid-ride stop in the heart of Victoria's Old Town.
040922bc6e: JOEY is a family-owned upscale casual dining chain operating since 1992, with locations across Canada and the US. Each restaurant is custom-built with a distinct design and serves a globally inspired menu of handcrafted dishes and cocktails developed by a team of Executive Chefs. The Kelowna outpost sits along Highway 97, making it a recognizable stop on one of the Okanagan's main cycling corridors.
9bdb338b48: A McDonald's fast food location on Kingsway in Vancouver, offering burgers, chicken, McCafé beverages, and a full breakfast menu. It is an indoor-seating location with no drive-through, positioned on a major arterial road that cycling routes frequently cross. As a 24/7 operation per OSM, it could serve as an around-the-clock food stop for touring cyclists passing through Burnaby/Vancouver.
5c21aa2ab8: The Ramen Butcher serves authentic Hakata-style tonkotsu ramen in Vancouver's Chinatown, with chefs trained in Japan through the parent Menya Kouji Group. Everything — noodles, gyoza, and rice bowls — is handmade daily, and the menu spans classic tonkotsu, tsukemen, miso, and vegetarian broths. The Chinatown location is a takeout-friendly stop in a dense, walkable neighbourhood.
1f2996bc8f: A pub and liquor store in Langley, BC. Limited information is available due to the business website being non-functional.
92cbb858f5: Bar Luna is a Mexican cantina housed in a beautifully restored 1890s fire hall in downtown Nanaimo, offering bold-flavoured tacos, quesabirria, ceviche, and handcrafted mezcal cocktails with a West Coast twist. The heritage building gives the restaurant a distinctive character, though its original front steps make wheelchair access challenging. It can accommodate groups up to 18 in its loft and up to 96 for private events, with catering available.
84adea7512: Jerusalem Shawarma is a Palestinian-rooted family business serving shawarma, donair, falafel, hummus, and kababs on busy Robson Street in downtown Vancouver. The restaurant offers dine-in seating indoors alongside takeout and online ordering for pickup. It is part of a multi-location chain with roots in its founder's grandfather's village restaurant in Palestine, emphasizing fresh Mediterranean cuisine.
801808d06d: The Firewood Café is a family-owned Mount Pleasant institution that has been crafting hand-tossed, thin-crust pizzas in a firewood brick oven since 1989. Located at the corner of 14th and Cambie, it offers a broad menu of classic and creative pizzas alongside made-to-order pasta dishes. Cyclists can grab a quick pickup order or settle in at one of the small number of dine-in tables.
7d9ecf5b73: Med Grill occupies a 100-year-old heritage building — the former Saanich Municipal Hall — in Royal Oak, just minutes from Downtown Victoria. Head chef Andrew Johnson crafts seasonal Mediterranean-inspired menus with west coast flair, served in a candlelit interior with a cozy fireplace or on a spacious wrap-around patio. The restaurant has been a local Victoria favourite since 1997 and features a rotating Tuscan Table three-course dinner alongside a rotating monthly menu.
afc3612d3f: Joe Fortes Seafood & Chop House is a celebrated Vancouver institution operating for over 35 years, named after Seraphim 'Joe Fortes,' the city's first official lifeguard. The restaurant spans multiple distinctive spaces — a horseshoe oyster bar grand room, mezzanine with live music, mahogany-walled wine room, and a rooftop garden with a living green wall and outdoor fireplace. It is known for its daily-sourced Pacific Northwest seafood, 300-bottle award-winning wine list, and loyal following of locals, tourists, and celebrities.
0fe08b3866: Yummy Slice Pizza is a Canadian-owned pizza-by-the-slice chain with a Richmond location on Number 1 Road, offering pickup and delivery seven days a week. The menu spans classic and signature pies including a broad range of vegetarian and South Asian-inspired options such as Tandoori Paneer and Yummy Potato. With multiple Lower Mainland locations and a catering program, it is a reliable quick-stop for a hot meal on a Richmond cycling route.
3d4b4cd2e3: Hungry Guys Kitchen is a downtown Vancouver fast food restaurant with two Granville Street locations, serving hand-crafted gourmet burgers, fries, shakes, salads, and build-your-own bowls made from locally sourced, fresh ingredients. Founded by entrepreneur Aldo Velaj, the concept emphasizes allergen-friendly customization and sustainable sourcing. The 988 Granville location has indoor seating and is wheelchair accessible, making it a comfortable urban refuelling stop for cyclists.
634e419415: Kam Wai Dim Sum is a family-run dim sum shop that has been a fixture of Vancouver's Chinatown since 1991, specializing in both frozen take-home dim sum classics and ready-to-eat takeaway items. The menu spans pork siu mai, wonton soup, BBQ pork bao, and vegan mushroom dumplings, with staff serving customers in English, Mandarin, and Cantonese. A second location (Kam Wai Legacy) now operates in the Hastings-Sunrise neighbourhood at 2285 E Hastings St.
547cffff0a: Boba Boy is a bubble tea chain with locations across BC, Ontario, and the US, operated by Tea Shop 168 Group Inc. The South Surrey location sits in a strip unit on Highway 10 and distinguishes itself by producing tapioca in-store from fresh ingredients rather than using pre-manufactured pearls. Cyclists on the Highway 10 corridor can stop in for made-to-order boba drinks and place orders online for pickup.
2c08a1f4f9: Swad Indian Kitchen is a family-owned North Indian restaurant on Marine Drive in West Vancouver, founded by Kamal Mroke who arrived from Punjab in the early 1980s and worked his way from dishwasher to restaurateur over 35 years. The menu spans aromatic curries, tandoori dishes, and street food classics, with strong vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free coverage. A private dining room with ocean views is available for groups, and free parking is provided at the rear of the building.
521cfb147d: Jane's Tea Garden is a specialty tea shop in Richmond offering premium loose-leaf teas sourced from traditional Chinese tea-growing regions, alongside hand-crafted ceramic teaware. The shop operates both as an online retailer and a physical location where visitors can taste teas and explore Chinese tea culture in person. It is a niche destination for tea enthusiasts rather than a full-service café.
fbee301ff9: Whitby's Coffee House is a cafe and ice cream shop in Tsawwassen located on Marine Drive. It offers outdoor seating for patrons. The establishment serves local cyclists and travelers passing through the community.
f83d5d3839: The Madras Diaries is a South Indian and Indo-Chinese restaurant on Kingsway in Vancouver, drawing on the cuisines of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh with dishes like Chettinadu chicken, Mandhi biryani, and an extensive dosa menu. Clay pot preparations and regional specialties such as Kozhi Kuzambu and Gongura Lamb distinguish it from generic Indian restaurants. Online ordering with a quick pickup window makes it a practical fueling stop for cyclists passing through East Vancouver.
e9774edacc: AVIK is a tech-driven franchise specialty coffee shop on West Broadway offering espresso drinks crafted with beans from Moving Coffee Roastery, locally sourced high-grade teas, and artisanal pastries baked in-house daily. The brand blends a digital-first experience — including a mobile app with an order-ahead and rewards system — with a self-described fun, vibrant atmosphere. It sits in a busy urban neighbourhood convenient to cyclists travelling the Broadway corridor.
8695227343: Tsukiji Kitchen is a grab-and-go seafood kitchen and community hub on lower Lonsdale in North Vancouver, opened December 2025 and run by Takuya Hikita, a former Tsukiji Market auctioneer with a marine biology background and a mandate to promote sustainable BC seafood. The Ocean Wellness Bowls pair Japanese-sourced seaweed and salmon roe with locally sourced BC proteins such as salmon, shrimp, and scallop. The space also includes a coffee corner and a second-floor event room used for cultural programming and community gatherings.
2a457ea1e6: A fast-food pizzeria in Burnaby offering pizza with Indian-fusion options. Convenient for cyclists seeking quick meals on Canada Way.
427a8623eb: Phở Fresh is a family-owned Northern Vietnamese restaurant in Tsawwassen, Delta, founded in 2018 by a Vietnamese-Canadian engineer who spent 15+ hours daily simmering scratch-made bone broth in the Hanoi tradition. The clean, modern dining room is designed for a comfortable sit-down meal, and the restaurant also caters events and offers delivery through major apps. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a restorative, allergen-conscious bowl of phở made entirely from local BC ingredients where practical.
afce0fae27: A pub serving the Cowichan Bay community on Vancouver Island's south coast. Offers casual food and drink service to locals and travelers. Website is currently under redesign but remains accessible via phone and social media.
e5613badb5: Il Greco is a Greek and pizza restaurant located in Victoria's Gorge neighbourhood, operating as a takeout and delivery focused spot. With a gmail contact address and a compact unit-suite location, it has the feel of a neighbourhood quick-service restaurant rather than a sit-down destination. Cyclists passing through the Gorge Road corridor could use it as a pickup stop, though amenity details beyond takeout are unverified.
cfc444c1f6: Kiku Sushi is a Japanese restaurant at Metrotown in Burnaby, one of two Lower Mainland locations, serving sushi, rolls, grilled entrees, noodles, and kitchen appetizers. The restaurant describes a large dining hall with a cozy interior and a broad menu designed to suit varied tastes. A touring cyclist riding the Kingsway corridor would find a full sit-down meal option here with online ordering also available.
8e13c6e2e3: Social 242 Lounge & Grill is a full-service lounge and restaurant in downtown Kelowna offering wings in 26 flavours, AAA steaks, and a creative cocktail program with signature and seasonal drinks. The venue also features a dedicated vegan menu and gluten-free options throughout, catering to a wide range of dietary needs. Its central Lawrence Avenue location makes it a convenient food-and-drink stop for cyclists exploring the Okanagan.
c00ce66171: D Spot Dessert Café is a Canadian dessert franchise established in 2014, specializing in homemade ice cream, fresh waffles and crepes, Belgian chocolate creations, and savoury items. The Delta location is part of a growing national chain known for inventive, social-media-worthy desserts made with high-quality ingredients. All products are halal-certified and kosher, making this a broadly inclusive stop for cyclists seeking a sweet break.
16b4cc5b07: Papa John's is a national pizza chain franchise located in a strip-mall unit in Langley, BC, offering takeout pizza. Touring cyclists passing through the area can pick up a ready-made or custom pizza order by phone or in person. No drive-through is available, making it a walk-in or call-ahead stop.
e221494bef: Taku Japanese Kitchen is a neighbourhood Japanese restaurant on Royal Oak Avenue in Burnaby, serving a sit-down menu in a no-smoking indoor dining room. With no outdoor seating, it offers a quieter indoor respite for cyclists passing through the Royal Oak corridor. It accepts Visa and Mastercard, making it a convenient cashless stop mid-ride.
429f92ea76: Mucho Burrito is a Mexican fast-casual chain offering burritos, bowls, quesadillas, and tacos with what the brand calls a 'Modern Mexicana' twist. Located on Lansdowne Street in downtown Kamloops, it is a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the city's commercial core. Takeout and online ordering are available, making it a quick resupply option.
39b75aa660: Mishmish (مشمش, meaning 'apricot' in Arabic) is a third-culture Middle Eastern bakery and café on Fraser Street in Vancouver, founded in 2024 and named Vancouver Magazine's Best Bakery 2026. Chef/owners Abdallah El Chami and Leah Christ blend Lebanese, Iranian, German, and Canadian traditions into creations like the Baklava Cream Top and Mishmish Bar. The café features covered outdoor seating where dogs are welcome, and serves coffee from Modus Coffee and tea from Tea Sparrow.
8222c05bc7: Baiyulan Shanghai Cuisine is a sit-down Shanghainese restaurant in a Richmond strip mall, specializing in authentic dishes like Jelly Pork, Ham & Taro Soup, and Crispy Ginger Beef alongside a broad menu of specialty noodles, dim sum, and cold appetizers. The restaurant has built a loyal local following with 84 online reviews and caters to vegetarian diners. Cyclists can order online for pickup or delivery as well as dine in.
1b12911900: The Dutch Bakery & Diner is a beloved Victoria institution on Fort Street, now celebrating 70 years of operation under three generations of the Dutch-immigrant Schaddelee family. The diner serves all-day breakfast and lunch including Dutch specialties like croquettes, burgers, omelettes, and salads, alongside an extensive selection of house-made pastries, cakes, cookies, and chocolates from the bakery counter. It's a characterful, old-fashioned stop in the heart of downtown Victoria with a loyal following and a long-tenured staff.
f5af7b2727: Chen's Garden (operating as Chan's Garden) is a Chinese restaurant in New Westminster serving an extensive menu of Cantonese and Szechuan-inspired dishes, from Ginger Beef and Wonton Noodle Soup to stir-fried lamb and whole-category seafood selections. The restaurant offers indoor dine-in seating alongside a full online ordering system for pickup and delivery. With nearly 500 customer reviews, it is a well-established neighbourhood stop suited to refuelling a hungry touring cyclist.
759923975f: Pagliacci's is a Victoria institution that has been serving Italian-influenced comfort food since 1979, with housemade focaccia, pasta, fresh local seafood, and AAA Angus steaks. The restaurant claims the longest-running free live music program of any restaurant in Canada, with nightly performances spanning jazz, klezmer, and more. It operates on a no-reservations basis with a famously fast-moving queue, and is located in the heart of downtown Victoria.
fbf805a677: Ocean Palace is a long-established Chinese restaurant in the heart of Tsawwassen, serving authentic dishes for over 28 years with an emphasis on fresh ingredients and high standards. The extensive menu spans seafood, pork, poultry, beef, and vegetarian options, with popular items including special fried rice, chicken chow mein, and ginger beef. No-MSG preparation is available on request, and dinner combo packages cater to groups of varying sizes.
4b944a1bba: Gramma's Marine Pub is a waterfront sports pub established in 1989 on the Lower Sunshine Coast, with an enclosed patio overlooking Shoal Channel, Keat's Island, and Gibsons Harbour. Originally BC's first licensed 'Marine Pub', the building has a colourful history stretching back to the early 1900s and still includes an attached cold beer and wine store. Cyclists will find a full scratch kitchen, a rotating selection of 10–12 draught taps featuring local Sunshine Coast breweries, and accessible street-level and waterfront seawall entrances.
d2f36c6671: Perfecto Cafe is a Vancouver artisan cafe chain where every pastry, cake, sandwich, and gelato is made entirely from scratch in-house, with bakers starting at 5am daily and gelato crafted using techniques from the Carpigiani Gelato University in Italy. The Davie Street location is one of four, pairing a custom coffee blend developed exclusively with Agro Roasters alongside an ever-changing seasonal baked goods menu. Outdoor seating and a community-hub ethos make it a quality mid-ride refueling stop in the West End.
5f59a9874c: The Hanoi Corner is a cafe on Commercial Drive in Vancouver's East Side, a lively, cyclist-friendly strip lined with independent restaurants and cafes. Its name evokes Hanoi, Vietnam's capital, making it a likely Vietnamese or fusion spot, though OSM tags it as Korean — the actual cuisine is unverifiable from available sources. Commercial Drive is a well-traveled urban cycling corridor and a natural stop for riders crossing East Vancouver.
d041b30a58: Gary's Kitchen is a sit-down restaurant in Tofino serving a Chinese-American fusion menu. It offers takeout as well as dine-in, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists who need a hot meal to go. Tofino's remote location on the west coast of Vancouver Island means options are limited, and a full-service restaurant covering two cuisines is a useful find after a long day on the road.
1ed16f4b7a: A bar and grill restaurant in Tsawwassen, British Columbia. Website access failed during initial research, preventing verification of specific amenities and services useful to touring cyclists.
cdc62881c6: Strathcona North is the North Shore waterfront outpost of Strathcona Beer Company, situated at Lonsdale Quay with an interior blending natural wood, marble, brass, and a large indoor tree for an indoor-outdoor feel. It offers a full food program spanning lunch, dinner, and weekend brunch alongside house-brewed craft beers and cocktails. An on-site bottle shop lets cyclists pick up takeaway Strathcona and LOLO products to go.
9241c42e81: Tim Hortons is a Canadian quick-service chain at a prominent Central Avenue location in Grand Forks, serving coffee, baked goods, soups, and breakfast items with both dine-in and drive-through options. For touring cyclists passing through the Boundary Country, it offers a reliable, familiar stop with indoor seating, Wi-Fi, and a full menu from early morning.
7f5a74afca: Oak Bay Seafood is a family-run fresh fish market and eat-in restaurant on Oak Bay Avenue, drawing on over four decades of hands-on fishing experience by owners Gregg and Anne Best. The kitchen serves made-from-scratch seafood including fish and chips, chowder, seasonal spot prawns, and steamed Dungeness crab, all sourced from local BC waters under Oceanwise sustainability guidelines. With outdoor seating and a combined deli and restaurant format, it makes a distinctive stop for cyclists touring the Oak Bay neighbourhood.
14ec4969c3: Red Tomato Pies is a BC-born pizza chain founded in Williams Lake by Jason and Amber Akeson, now operating 11 locations across Western Canada including two in Kamloops. The North Shore location on Tranquille Road serves handcrafted pizzas in four sizes alongside wings, chicken dippers, salads, pasta, and desserts. The chain has grown entirely through word-of-mouth and touts an award-winning approach to fresh ingredients and creative specialty pies.
ffd96715d8: Pak Tak Chiu Chow Restaurant has been serving authentic Chiu Chow and Cantonese homestyle cuisine from inside Yaohan Centre in Richmond since 2000. The restaurant is particularly known for its Soy Sauce Duck, Cold Crab, and Braised Pork Belly with Preserved Vegetables. Its mall location gives cycling visitors access to a full food court environment with takeout and catering options.
1f19a63576: The Galley Lakeside Cafe sits on the Okanagan Lake waterfront at the Kelowna Yacht Club, a community fixture dating back to 1945. It serves handcrafted coffee drinks, salads, sandwiches, smoothies, beer, wine, and house-made gelato from a heated, dog-friendly patio with unobstructed lake views. A retail shop on-site carries local products and KYC merchandise, making it a natural stop for cyclists riding the downtown Kelowna waterfront.
258a18210d: Red Star Seafood Restaurant is a well-established Cantonese dining destination in Richmond, offering hundreds of classical dim sum dishes alongside live seafood, hot pot, and full banquet service for celebrations. One of two BC locations (the other on Granville Street in Vancouver), the Richmond branch seats diners in an elegant atmosphere and is a popular choice for family reunions and wedding banquets. Takeout and self-pickup orders are available from both locations.
943e2fc836: The Cascade Room is a gastrolounge in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, named after the historic Brewery Creek area that once housed the original Vancouver Brewery and its Cascade label. Opened in 2007, it has built a reputation as a destination for BC craft beer on tap, signature cocktails, and an elevated pub menu driven by locally sourced ingredients. Head Chef Darrel Ahenakew draws on BC farms, fields, and ocean to produce a rotating, seasonally inspired menu.
f4c2ef4aa3: Subway Ambleside Centre is a franchise sandwich shop on Marine Drive in West Vancouver's Ambleside neighbourhood, a popular coastal cycling corridor. It offers made-to-order Footlongs, wraps, and salads with in-restaurant dining, takeout, and delivery. As a recognised chain stop near the Ambleside waterfront, it could serve as a quick resupply point for cyclists on the North Shore.
3fcaa4e89f: Syros Pizza & Spaghetti is one of Kamloops' oldest restaurants, operating since the 1960s and beloved by locals for its halal pizza and Greek food. It offers both pickup and delivery, making it a convenient stop for touring cyclists moving through the North Kamloops area. The menu spans freshly baked pizza to Greek fare, with an emphasis on quality ingredients.
45aa3f53be: Kermode Wild Berry Winery is a premium alpine winery established in 2005 in Dewdney, BC, specializing in 100% wild organic berry and fruit wines — including what it claims is the only Pure Alpine Wild Blueberry Wine produced anywhere in the world. The winery sources wild blueberries by hand from the forests of Northern BC each summer and produces over 600,000 bottles annually across a broad range of styles from dry table wines to ports and ice wines. Named after the rare Kermode 'Spirit Bear' of Northern BC, it has earned international awards and is considered one of Canada's largest fruit wine producers.
be96ec9e0e: Clough Club is a compact cocktail bar in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, named after the area's old-timey one-armed lamp lighter. The intimate 1,600 sq. ft. space seats 33 and accommodates 50 standing, with an experienced bar team serving strong custom cocktails and small plates. Live music runs on weekends and a private back room is available for group bookings.
c227e68fb3: A Japanese restaurant located on Dunbar Street in Vancouver.
ce41e7a4e1: Tickleberry's at Skaha Park is a seasonal ice cream and sweets kiosk at Skaha Beach in Penticton, part of a beloved Okanagan chain operating since 1990. The shop scoops over 150 flavors of hand-crafted ice cream alongside house-made fudge produced in an on-site Fudge Factory, chocolate-covered dried fruits, and local gifts. For touring cyclists on the Skaha Lake corridor, it's a quintessential lakeside sweet stop with quick takeout service geared toward people ready to roll.
d5783f0e9e: Subway North Nanaimotown Center is a franchise sandwich restaurant in north Nanaimo offering Footlongs, 6" sandwiches, wraps, salads, and breakfast with customizable fresh ingredients. The location supports in-restaurant dining, curbside pickup, and delivery. It sits in a strip-mall context on Rutherford Road, a main arterial corridor in the north end of Nanaimo.
2cad24e26d: Zab Zaab Thai Cuisine is an authentic central Thai restaurant in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, recipient of the Thai Select award granted by Thailand's Ministry of Commerce to certify genuine Thai taste. The menu spans traditional dishes including Tom Yum, papaya salad, curries, and noodles, with monthly specials that rotate through street-food classics. It sits one block from the Yaletown-Roundhouse SkyTrain Station, making it a convenient downtown stop for cyclists moving through the city core.
d7f8e50630: Paul's Kitchen is a Chinese fast-food restaurant in Richmond. As a quick-service establishment, it offers counter-service meals convenient for cyclists seeking a brief stop.
90f5abf232: Maar's Burger Bar is a craft burger joint at Cultus Lake founded by two brothers who grew up on the lake and set out to bring quality food to an area they felt was underserved. The menu features locally sourced ingredients from BC suppliers including Old Yale Brewing, Anita's Organics buns, and an award-winning butcher. For a touring cyclist, it offers a fast, filling stop with burgers, craft beer, wine, and a focused menu of sides.
f27a758140: Pho Century Fine Vietnamese Cuisine is a sit-down Vietnamese restaurant located on Kingsway in Burnaby, a busy commercial corridor that connects several cycling routes across the municipality. The restaurant offers indoor-only seating in a no-smoking environment. Its pho and Vietnamese menu would offer a warm, hearty meal option for cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor.
77ff3786e9: JJ Bean Coffee Roasters is a Vancouver-born independent specialty coffee brand established in 1996, roasting high-quality single-origin and blended coffees in small batches daily across multiple Metro Vancouver cafés. The Cambie Street location is a full-service café offering all-day breakfast and lunch made fresh in-house alongside its renowned coffee program, with outdoor seating for customers.
8cd80221d0: The Squarerigger Pub is a recently renovated English-style pub on Marine Drive in West Vancouver's Ambleside neighbourhood, situated directly across from Ambleside Beach and steps from the North Shore seawall cycling corridor. It blends a traditionally rustic atmosphere with a modern sports bar setup featuring large HD screens, and draws a loyal local crowd with live music every Friday and karaoke every Saturday. The kitchen serves pub fare daily through Mani's Food Services, making it a plausible refuelling stop for cyclists on the seawall route.
d71973a1a0: Las Shilas Mexican Street Food brings authentic Mexico City street food culture to New Westminster's Quayside Drive, serving handcrafted tacos with fillings like beef tongue, birria, and pastor alongside Mexican-style burgers and hot dogs. The kitchen leans into traditional Chilango flavors, with drinks including horchata, jamaica, and Mexican Coke rounding out the experience. Dine-in, pickup, and delivery are all available, and a catering program is in development.
065f83bc7f: Mali Thai is a Thai restaurant on Main Street in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, serving a broad menu of curries, noodles, soups, and appetizers with clearly labelled vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options. The restaurant offers dine-in alongside takeout and delivery through DoorDash, UberEats, Ritual, and Skipthedishes, and also accepts call-in pickup orders. Main Street is one of Vancouver's most bikeable corridors, making this a practical meal stop for cyclists riding through the city.
22f4e0ce1f: Loku Japanese Cuisine is a Japanese restaurant on Commercial Drive in Vancouver serving sushi and traditional Japanese fare. It offers dine-in service in a vibrant neighborhood popular with cyclists and pedestrians. The restaurant provides a convenient place to rest and refuel while exploring Vancouver's urban routes.
a5915dd970: Union Pacific Coffee Co. is a heritage café established in 2006 inside the historic Hart's Block building along Dragon Alley in Victoria's Chinatown. Revitalized by twins Kelley and Lindsay, it serves specialty coffees sourced from JJ Bean in Vancouver alongside freshly baked in-house pastries, breakfast sandwiches, and a full lunch menu. The laid-back Pacific Northwest ambiance and vibrant heritage setting make it a natural stop for cyclists passing through the city centre.
23938d143f: Asian Fiesta is a Chinese fast-food restaurant located in a strip mall in Fort St. John, serving a broad menu of Cantonese-style dishes including chow mein, fried rice, ginger beef, and crispy fried chicken. The restaurant offers both local delivery and pickup ordering through its own website. With over 100 customer reviews and a full online menu, it is a well-established quick-service option for cyclists passing through this northern BC hub.
a726c255d4: Tacos La Cantina is an authentic Mexican taqueria founded by Whistler local Pepe Barajas, with its flagship location in the Village Marketplace. The menu centres on fresh tacos, burritos, quesadillas, and legendary margaritas made daily, with a strong lineup of gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian choices. A lively, casual atmosphere and quick-service format make it a practical and satisfying stop for hungry cyclists passing through the Village.
0115610efc: Ruka Coffee is a community-minded café on East Broadway in Vancouver, operated by a couple since 2022 and built around single-origin beans sourced from local roaster Agro Roasters, which works directly with organic, sustainably farmed crops. The menu spans espresso classics, cold brew, frappes, bubble teas, and house-baked pastries alongside savory wraps. The space also functions as a rentable venue for private events with a full catering program.
4b03edd42d: Hungry Bear is a casual restaurant in Fort St. John serving a mix of Asian dishes and burgers — an eclectic combination that makes it a convenient stop for touring cyclists passing through the Peace River region. It operates out of a single-storey retail building on 100 Avenue, one of the main commercial corridors in town.
4783f5cd71: Taishoken is a Japanese ramen restaurant in Vancouver's downtown core, specializing in tonkotsu, miso, and tsukemen-style noodle bowls. The menu spans a range of broth styles alongside gyoza, rice dishes, and several vegetarian options. Online ordering with pickup is available directly through the restaurant's website.
552c209456: Koh-I-Noor is a long-running North Indian and Nepalese restaurant in downtown Kamloops, known for its tandoor oven cooking, lunch buffet, and one of the city's notable views. The kitchen cooks with traditional clay-oven (tandoor) techniques and sources halal meat, offering a wide menu that spans curries, tikkas, momos, and fresh naan. Touring cyclists will find a full sit-down dining room with banquet capacity and a range of dietary accommodations including gluten-free, vegan, and no-MSG dishes.
cb39794b7f: bb.q Chicken is a Korean fried chicken restaurant located in Poco Place mall in Port Coquitlam, part of the bb.q Chicken international brand. It specializes in various chicken preparations and distinctive sauces, providing a casual dining option at the mall's corner location.
f817d44ca7: Sushi by Yuji is a casual sushi restaurant located on Kingsway in Vancouver. It offers a convenient food stop for touring cyclists exploring the East Vancouver neighbourhood.
8ff92fa6d7: NoodleBox is a BC-based fast-casual Asian noodle franchise serving customizable wok-fired noodle bowls in styles ranging from Pad Thai to Kung Pao and Teriyaki. The Edmonds location in Burnaby is one of several Lower Mainland outlets, offering a quick and filling counter-service meal. Dishes can be modified to be vegan or gluten-friendly, making it an accessible fuel stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.
f193afa932: Old Town Bakery is a scratch bakery in historic downtown Ladysmith operating continuously since 1932 — now run by Kate and Geoff Cram since 2002 — and is famous for nine daily cinnamon bun flavours that earned a 'Island's Best' Reader's Choice award from the Victoria Times Colonist in 2005. Beyond buns, it offers a full range of breads, pastries, custom cakes, sandwiches, soups, and salads. It sits a short walk from Ladysmith Marina and Transfer Beach Park, making it a natural fuel stop on Vancouver Island's east coast.
ef8ca78306: On The Go Gelato is an indoor gelato and ice cream shop in Tsawwassen, BC, tagged as wheelchair accessible in OpenStreetMap. It appears to be a small artisan-style gelato outlet — the kind of sweet stop a touring cyclist might seek out after a ride along the South Delta routes or before or after a BC Ferries sailing from the nearby Tsawwassen terminal.
1bca259dd8: Porker Face is a Korean restaurant situated on Lougheed Highway in Burnaby, offering indoor dining. Its name suggests a pork-forward menu concept, likely featuring Korean barbecue or similar dishes popular with hungry cyclists. The Lougheed corridor is a common route for cyclists travelling east-west through Burnaby.
1daf3596a0: Field House Brewing Co. is a community-rooted craft brewery that opened its Chilliwack tasting room in 2020 at the District 1881 development in downtown Chilliwack. The rotating tap list spans crushable ales, experimental IPAs, and barrel-aged sours, complemented by a farm-to-table canteen program using fresh local ingredients. Cyclists passing through will find a laid-back atmosphere with regular live music nights and community programming.
8d63788c61: Ironworks Café & Crêperie is a Vancouver Island cafe chain open since 2018, built around made-from-scratch Belgian-style crepes and locally roasted Italian coffee. The brand operates confirmed locations in Duncan and Nanaimo and references a Ladysmith presence in customer reviews and footer listings, though that location's current status is uncertain. The menu spans sweet and savoury crepes with broad dietary accommodation, including vegan and gluten-free batter choices.
021a71f0ba: Bai Tong Thai Food is a sit-down Thai restaurant on Bernard Avenue in the heart of downtown Kelowna, offering an extensive menu of curries, noodle dishes, soups, and desserts. With 123 customer reviews highlighting generous portions, fresh ingredients, and notably warm service, it has established itself as a well-regarded local favourite. The restaurant offers both dine-in and takeout, and also provides delivery, giving touring cyclists flexible options for a post-ride meal.
b13e6a3f7c: Lynn's Vietnamese is a Vietnamese restaurant located in Vernon, BC. It represents one of the dining options catering to those craving Southeast Asian cuisine in the Okanagan region. Touring cyclists passing through Vernon may find it a welcome stop for a hot meal after a long day on the road.
f8757183b1: Bandra Cafe is a café located in Richmond, BC. The business maintains an online presence, though website details could not be verified at this time.
926fc9ccae: Wick's Cafe is a community-rooted neighbourhood cafe in Vancouver's Marpole area, built around the idea that great coffee and human connection go hand in hand. The menu features carefully sourced, sustainably harvested coffee alongside fresh-baked goods, handmade panini, sandwiches, and wraps. OSM records outdoor seating, making it a pleasant stop for a cyclist passing through South Vancouver.
658b34e98d: Golden Samosa Bakery is a long-established South Asian bakery in Surrey with over 30 years of history, producing more than a million handcrafted samosas annually. Known for their award-winning samosas in multiple varieties — potato-peas, paneer, chicken, and beef — the bakery also serves pakoras, chana masala, and samosa meals. It is a popular stop for bulk orders and community events, with a loyal following across Metro Vancouver.
a3edd0140f: Thai Taste is a family-owned authentic Thai restaurant located in a commercial plaza on Vedder Road in Chilliwack. It serves dine-in and takeout and is also available through Skip the Dishes. Touring cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley would find it a convenient stop for a sit-down Thai meal or a quick takeout order.
f9885175d6: Pizza Coming Soon is an evening pizzeria tucked into Vancouver's historic Chinatown on East Pender Street, operating under the parent company Laughing Seal Dreams Worldwide Enterprises Inc. It offers dine-in service alongside delivery through DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Skip the Dishes. The restaurant has a no-smoking policy and accepts reservations for larger groups via email.
d36a759cdd: MATCH Eatery & Public House is a casual full-service restaurant and sports pub chain operated under the Gateway Casinos family, with locations across BC, Alberta, and Ontario. The Kamloops outpost serves an extensive menu of pub classics, pastas, burgers, wings, and pizzas alongside a full bar. Touring cyclists will find a welcoming sit-down atmosphere with takeout and delivery also available.
6b421a836d: India Chaat House is an Indian restaurant situated on Marine Drive in White Rock, a scenic waterfront road that is a popular cycling route along Semiahmoo Bay. b235b48b05: Nook Restaurant (Shipyards) is an Italian neighbourhood restaurant in North Vancouver's Shipyards district, serving housemade pasta, pizza, antipasto, and cocktails with locally sourced ingredients and Italian imports. a0e7e13015: East is East is a Silk Road-inspired restaurant drawing on culinary traditions stretching from Mongolia through Tibet, India, Persia, and Istanbul, with all food made from natural whole ingredients, organic and local where possible.
