a63ed99855: The Pink Geranium is a market, café, and e-bike rental hub at the north end of Galiano Island, reopened in 2021 in a historic building that first housed a beloved island restaurant founded in 1972. The café serves espresso drinks, breakfast and lunch sandwiches, baked goods, and pantry items, making it a natural provisioning stop for cyclists on the island. It also operates as the island's designated e-bike rental point and check-in location for the Bodega Ridge resort properties.
23a1ea99f7: Pizza 64 is a Canadian pizza chain founded in 2010 with 20+ locations across British Columbia, known for freshly made dough and sauce prepared at each location. The Abbotsford location offers a broad menu of specialty, signature, and gourmet pizzas alongside wings, pasta, and sides. Online ordering is available, making it a convenient takeout stop for cyclists passing through the area.
2b8f25fcc9: Roll N Bowl is a Japanese-inspired restaurant on Yates Street in the heart of downtown Victoria, serving an extensive menu of sushi rolls, rice bowls, poke, and Asian fusion dishes. Online ordering with pickup from the 788 Yates St location is fully supported through their Square-powered website. Its central location in a dense commercial block makes it an easy refuelling stop for cyclists moving through downtown.
d24ac897f2: Cafe Vosino is a community-owned cooperative café in the heart of Sooke, BC, born when local patrons pooled resources to purchase and reopen the much-loved 'Stick in the Mud' coffee house — its new name a nod to Sooke's historic postal code V0S 1N0. Operated under the Sooke Community Investment Cooperative, it functions as both a neighbourhood gathering place and a small retail hub offering locally baked bread and café merchandise. Touring cyclists passing through Sooke will find a welcoming stop with outdoor seating and a strong community character.
d88ee4ee02: COBS Bread is a Canadian franchise bakery (part of the Australian Bakers Delight family) baking all products fresh from scratch on-site every day — no frozen or refrigerated goods. The Commercial Drive location on one of Vancouver's most vibrant neighbourhood corridors offers a wide range of breads, rolls, scones, cruffins, croissants, and savoury items including pizza-style products. Leftover baked goods are donated to local charities at day's end, a notable community practice.
63d8258e75: Fatburger is a classic burger chain with roots going back to a 1947 Los Angeles hamburger stand, now Canadian-owned and operated since 2005. The Kamloops location at Summit Drive serves build-your-own burgers made with fresh, never-frozen Alberta Angus beef, alongside chicken, plant-based options, and hand-scooped milkshakes. Every order is cooked-to-order, making it a solid stop for a hot, customizable meal mid-ride.
a5405a5b64: Ava Bakery is a family-owned Persian bakery in Port Coquitlam, founded during the COVID-19 pandemic by a couple who pivoted from hospitality and healthcare into traditional Iranian baking. The shop specializes in authentic Persian breads — Taftoon, Barbary, Lavash, Shirmal, and whole wheat Barbari Naan — alongside pastries, sweets, and prepared dishes such as Haleem and Persian Noodle Soup. It offers touring cyclists a rare chance to stock up on freshly baked breads and traditional Iranian snacks in the Tri-Cities area.
aabfcd47e0: Sushi Gio is a Japanese restaurant in Langley offering sushi and Japanese cuisine with dine-in and online ordering for takeout. It provides a convenient meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.
7b4bd71d94: Sabhai Thai is a family-owned authentic Thai restaurant that has operated since 2006, now running two Vancouver Island locations — Sidney and Langford. The Sirimalalak family cooks from scratch using traditional Thai recipes and ingredients, and has earned repeat recognition as the top ethnic restaurant in Sidney. A touring cyclist stopping in Langford will find a full sit-down menu spanning noodles, curries, soups, and appetizers, with vegetarian and vegan options throughout.
a07464892d: This McDonald's on 152 Street in Surrey is a drive-through fast food location serving burgers, breakfast, and McCafé coffee to go. It sits in a busy commercial corridor and is wheelchair accessible, making it a convenient roadside stop for touring cyclists cutting through the Fraser Valley region. The broad menu and takeout-friendly format make it a reliable resupply point for calories on the road.
f161cae14d: Sol Lee's Korean Restaurant is a Korean eatery located in a unit at 329 North Road in Coquitlam, BC. It offers touring cyclists a chance to refuel with Korean cuisine in the heart of the Tri-Cities area. The restaurant was confirmed present as of August 2024 via OSM community verification.
b630cf05ea: Chuan Ku BBQ Restaurant is a Richmond dining destination specializing in Old Beijing cuisine, with a menu spanning grilled whole fish, skewers, copper stove hot pot, spicy crab, and sheep scorpion. The restaurant offers more than 100 dishes rooted in traditional northern Chinese cooking, making it a distinctive stop for cyclists exploring Richmond's diverse food scene. Online ordering for pickup is available.
612b991011: Owl's Nest Bakery Bistro is a cozy all-day breakfast and lunch spot in Chemainus offering house-made baked goods, eggs benedicts on fresh focaccia, and a full espresso bar. The cafe offers both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a comfortable stop for cyclists passing through town. A Saltair location also exists, giving touring cyclists along that corridor another option.
dff0fffddf: A vegetarian-only restaurant located in Crescent Valley. Serves as a plant-based dining destination for local and touring visitors.
7141effc83: Steveston Seafood House is an award-winning fine dining restaurant in the heart of historic Steveston village, celebrated for its creative Pacific seafood menus built around locally sourced BC ingredients including Qualicum Bay scallops, Salt Spring Island mussels, and daily-catch fish. The menu also draws on the Calabrian coastal cooking traditions of the chef's family, weaving West Coast bounty with rustic Italian heritage across dinner, lunch, and weekend brunch services. Steveston sits at the terminus of popular Metro Vancouver cycling routes along the waterfront and dyke trail network.
b0e25d977d: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain known for using fresh dough made from 100% Canadian wheat and organic tomato sauce, with a broad menu of customizable pizzas, salads, sides, and desserts. This North Vancouver location on Hastings Street offers delivery and takeout. The chain emphasizes clean ingredients with no artificial colours or flavours, making it a convenient calorie-replenishment stop for cyclists passing through the area.
953a068fd8: Samurai Bowl is a Japanese-Asian fusion quick-service restaurant in Whistler's Creekside neighbourhood, open 7 days a week and serving ramen, Korean fried chicken, poke bowls, and Thai curry. It is part of a locally owned family of four Samurai restaurants across Whistler and Squamish, established in Creekside in 2006. The restaurant emphasizes eco-friendly practices, using compostable and recyclable takeout containers—an appeal for environmentally conscious cyclists on tour.
d332825441: Caffè W has been serving the West Broadway neighbourhood since 1995, making it one of Vancouver's longer-running independent cafés. The menu ranges from classic espresso drinks and specialty lattes to smoothies, frappes, and a full brunch lineup. The café is known for its exclusive 'Dubai Chocolate' creations — a pistachio-and-chocolate dessert series not found elsewhere — and a rotating display of artisan pastries.
3e6e78a09f: Green Leaf Salad Bar is a Lebanese restaurant and by-weight salad bar in Vancouver's West End, celebrated as a Readers' Choice 'Best of the City 2014' winner by WE Vancouver and a four-time consecutive Yelp People's Choice award recipient (2016–2019). The menu centres on Lebanese staples — chicken shawarma, falafel wraps, daily rotating hot specials such as beef kafta and moussaka — alongside a fresh seasonal salad bar priced by weight. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a compact, fast-casual spot with both indoor and outdoor seating and a full catering operation.
e946cfc844: Pho Japolo is a proudly family-run Vietnamese and Japanese fusion restaurant operating since 1995, with the Kitsilano outpost anchoring a four-location Lower Mainland chain. The menu spans hearty beef noodle soups with a range of traditional pho combinations alongside inventive sushi creations like sushi pizza and sushi burgers. Regulars highlight the generous portions, warm homey atmosphere, and reliably consistent food as reasons to keep coming back.
225cde21c1: Papa John's on Bainbridge Avenue is a pizza chain location in Burnaby offering both delivery and carryout, with a menu featuring pizza, breadsticks, and wings. It is a no-drive-through format, making it a straightforward stop for cyclists looking to grab a hot meal or order ahead for pickup. The location is part of the Papa John's Canadian franchise network.
e0d4a279ec: La Cervecería Astilleros is a Mexican-inspired craft brewery and taproom in the Shipyards district of Lower Lonsdale, bringing Mexican ingredients and brewing traditions to BC craft beer. Their award-winning Salted Lime Lager took first place at the 2023 Canadian Brewing Awards, and a constantly rotating small-batch tap list means there is always something new on pour. Cyclists can refuel with tacos, burritos, and margaritas alongside the house lagers, with both indoor and outdoor seating available.
a4f2dc4f9c: Grounds & Greens Cafe is a family-owned, fully plant-based cafe in downtown White Rock run by chefs Mannel and Ben Kilford, who bring over 35 years of combined culinary experience including time with Four Seasons Hotels. The menu centres on creative power bowls, artisan coffee, and house-made dishes using locally sourced ingredients, with a strong zero-waste ethos that eliminates single-use containers. A second location operates in Fort Langley, and the cafe is noted for being dog-friendly and welcoming to non-vegans.
df6026cda3: Quarterway Pub is a well-established neighbourhood bar on Bowen Road in Nanaimo, offering a full menu of appetizers and mains alongside a busy events calendar including karaoke nights, NHL game-day specials, and a monthly meat draw. It markets itself as Nanaimo's go-to bar, suggesting a lively, community-centred atmosphere that draws regulars throughout the week. A touring cyclist finishing a ride through the mid-island corridor would find a sit-down meal and cold drinks in a classic pub setting.
2924b5a991: Cha Tra Mue is the Vancouver location of a celebrated Thai tea brand with over 80 years of history, bringing premium milk teas, rose teas, and Thai coffee made from handpicked highland leaves grown in Chiang Rai to West Broadway. The shop offers a dedicated Vegan Series alongside its classic menu and Thai tea soft serve, making it a genuine Thai tea house rather than a generic bubble tea chain. Cyclists passing through this busy commercial corridor will find it a refreshing stop for an authentic cold or hot Thai tea drink.
0f599d6901: Caffè Mira is a neighbourhood coffee shop founded in 2017 with three locations across greater Vancouver, including this New Westminster spot at 28 E Royal Ave. The café serves coffee drinks, sandwiches, pastries, and other fresh dishes for dine-in or takeout. Catering is also available, making it a practical stop for both a quick refuel and a longer sit-down break.
d80e93b55b: Montana's is a Canadian BBQ restaurant operating as part of a national chain with a location in Delta. The establishment serves casual barbecue cuisine in a relaxed dining atmosphere. Touring cyclists will find it a straightforward option for a meal break in the area.
91d8fd5c18: Orange Julius is a juice-focused quick-service restaurant in Victoria offering takeout beverages. It provides a convenient refueling option for touring cyclists seeking fresh juice or smoothie refreshment. The takeout-oriented format enables efficient, quick service for cyclists on the road.
f66cbee19b: Umai Sushi & Grill is a Japanese and Asian fusion restaurant in Garibaldi Highlands, Squamish, offering an extensive menu of creative sushi rolls, aburi, teriyaki, and chirashi bowls. The restaurant positions itself as a comfortable dine-in space suitable for casual lunches through larger group dinners, and also offers online ordering for takeout. It sits in the Tantalus Road commercial area of Garibaldi Highlands, a node frequently passed by cyclists riding the Sea-to-Sky corridor.
116cf5478f: The Village Taphouse is a full-service restaurant and taphouse operated by Cactus Restaurants Ltd. at the Park Royal complex, offering an extensive menu of shareable plates, pizzas, burgers, salads, and handhelds alongside a drinks program spanning wines, spirits, and ales. A touring cyclist can fuel up with a proper sit-down meal or grab takeout and delivery, making it a practical stop on a North Shore ride. The restaurant is affiliated with Ocean Wise seafood sourcing and offers several plant-forward dishes alongside the heartier fare.
558e895e3b: Seasons in the Park is a long-established fine-dining restaurant perched atop Queen Elizabeth Park, offering sweeping panoramic views of the Vancouver city skyline, gardens, and North Shore mountains. Part of the Sequoia Company of Restaurants (founded 1978 in Vancouver), it serves regionally inspired cuisine built around a wood-fired grill, Pacific seafood, and locally sourced ingredients. Cyclists who climb the park road to the summit hilltop will find a full-service dining room with an outdoor patio and multiple private event spaces.
a624d0924d: Paul's Omelettery is a beloved South Granville breakfast and brunch institution that has been serving comfort food since 2000, earning a loyal following for its crepe-style omelettes, lumberjack pancakes, and eggs Benedict. Owned and run by Dino Arsens, the restaurant occupies a chic yet relaxed space with bench seating and a wood bar, and is steps from Granville Island — a natural stop on Vancouver's seawall cycling corridor. Menu highlights include B.C. free-run egg omelettes, huevos rancheros, and house corned beef hash.
fc7e040be5: Cactus Club Cafe is a well-established upscale-casual Canadian chain known for chef-driven international cuisine in stylish, energetic dining rooms. The Station Square location in Burnaby is one of several Metro Vancouver outposts offering a broad menu of cocktails, seafood, pasta, and shared plates. Takeout and delivery are available directly through the restaurant, making it a viable stop for a cyclist wanting a sit-down meal or a grab-and-go option.
506c70cde6: Maruhachi Gaiden is a ramen restaurant on Vancouver's Main Street, operating under the broader Maruhachi Ra-men Canada brand. Situated along a well-traveled urban cycling corridor in South Vancouver, it serves Japanese noodle dishes and offers online pickup ordering. The 'Gaiden' name suggests it may be a spin-off or sister location within the Maruhachi family of restaurants.
be4a17a617: Simba's Grill is a family-run East African Fusion restaurant that has been proudly serving since 1999, located in Burnaby at the Boundary Road and Laurel Street corner. Known for generous portions of authentic East African dishes — from grilled mishkaki and kuku choma to coastal coconut curries and biryanis — it promises a feast suited to a hungry touring cyclist. The menu spans appetizers, chef's specials, curries, and a dedicated vegetarian section with eight plant-based entrées.
c1c29d8960: Fresh Tandoori Flavour is a multi-location Indian restaurant chain with its Sidney outpost on Beacon Avenue, the town's main commercial strip. The kitchen turns out traditional tandoori platters, curries, kebabs, and freshly baked naan using time-honoured recipes and locally sourced ingredients. Both dine-in and online ordering are available, making it a flexible meal stop for cyclists touring the Saanich Peninsula.
8cb8fe57aa: Affirmation Coffee is a newly renovated neighborhood café on Bowen Road in Nanaimo, focused on freshly crafted coffee and homemade baked goods made from locally sourced ingredients. Reviewers highlight standout lattes, Biscoff cheesecake, muffins, and classic Nanaimo bars in a clean, uncluttered space. It offers a comfortable spot to sit down and recharge mid-ride in the north end of Nanaimo.
04b6aedea0: Sweet Memory is a restaurant in Richmond, BC offering indoor sit-down dining in a smoke-free environment. No address or cuisine details are publicly confirmed from available sources, making it a somewhat undocumented local spot. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond may find it worth seeking out, though specifics on offerings remain unverified.
1699deb11b: Ginger Sushi is a sushi restaurant on Vancouver's lively Commercial Drive, a cycling-friendly corridor popular with locals and visitors alike. The restaurant offers dine-in and online ordering for takeout, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through East Vancouver.
bed20d5c1f: No Bad Days Cafe is a casual cafe in Vancouver with indoor and outdoor seating offering food and beverages. The business centers on an uplifting theme with the tagline 'one bite closer to a unstoppable you.' It provides a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking a meal or drink break.
1808d0c649: Menbow Ramen Express is a quick-service ramen outlet located inside a Victoria shopping mall, part of the growing Menbow Ramen Group which sources key ingredients directly from Japan. The menu centres on tonkotsu and tori broths across multiple flavour profiles including shio, shoyu, and miso, with non-broth mazemen also available. Touring cyclists stopping for a hot, filling meal will find a range of ramen styles including a vegetarian tomato option, plus pickup and third-party delivery available.
1907d6d589: Great Pizza 2 for 1 is a pizza and Indian-fusion fast-food outlet operating out of a unit in Chilliwack, offering an unusually broad menu that blends classic Canadian pizza with South Asian dishes like tandoori chicken, paneer tikka, and dal makhni. The 2-for-1 specialty pizza lineup and Indian menu make it a distinctive stop for cyclists looking for a substantial, varied meal. Online ordering and pickup are supported.
2eeb3ede17: McDonald's on Commercial Drive sits in one of Vancouver's most lively and cyclist-travelled corridors, offering the standard quick-service menu of burgers, breakfast items, and beverages. The location has indoor seating and takeout, making it a straightforward refuelling stop for riders passing through the Drive. As a national franchise, amenity specifics vary by location and must be confirmed on the ground.
944560ab49: Buddha-Full Northwoods Village is a 100% vegan, organic, and gluten-free cafe, juice bar, and provisions store situated in Northwoods Village on Dollarton Highway in North Vancouver. One of two Buddha-Full locations in the region, it offers cold-pressed juices, smoothies, entrees, and salads alongside a retail shop stocked with provisions. The ethos-driven brand emphasizes community values and clean plant-based eating, making it a distinctive fuel stop for cyclists seeking organic, allergen-conscious food.
fdb0c17b73: Papa John's is a national pizza chain located on 6th Avenue in New Westminster offering delivery and carryout. The menu includes pizza, breadsticks, and wings, with vegetarian and gluten-free options available. A touring cyclist looking for a hot meal or a quick carryout stop in New Westminster would find this a convenient option along the route.
97059c6d99: Red Swan Pizza is a Canadian gourmet pizza chain with a location in north Kamloops, offering fresh handmade pizzas with premium ingredients available for pickup or delivery. The menu extends beyond pizza to include pastas, salads, sides, and desserts, and the chain also offers catering for events. Touring cyclists passing through Kamloops will find this a convenient stop for a hot meal or a takeout order.
9133355bbd: Wings is a Canadian restaurant chain specializing in chicken wings and burgers, located on Fraser Hwy in Langley. A sit-down restaurant with online ordering capability, it sits on a busy arterial route through the Fraser Valley. Touring cyclists passing through Langley would find it a straightforward stop for a hearty meal.
7b256f3b67: Namaste Indian Cuisine is a sit-down Indian restaurant founded in 2010 on Douglas Street in downtown Victoria, drawing on regional cuisines from across India — from fiery northern curries to coastal southern dishes. The menu is broad, spanning tandoor specialties, biryanis, and Indo-Chinese fusion alongside a large vegetarian selection, with many items labeled gluten-free. Carryout is available, making it a practical mid-ride fuel stop in the heart of the city.
3896e975d8: Riviera Cafe & Restaurant is a cafe and restaurant in Vancouver, BC. With minimal public information available, it appears to offer a combined cafe and full-service dining experience. Touring cyclists passing through Vancouver may find it a convenient stop, though details about its offerings remain unverified.
ebf1e2e5ea: Mirch Masala is a family-style Indian restaurant in Delta, BC, serving authentic tandoori dishes, rich curries, and a broad Indo-Chinese appetizer selection. The restaurant pairs its food menu with a full cocktail bar and a daily happy hour program. Touring cyclists looking for a generous, flavour-forward sit-down meal with strong vegetarian options will find plenty of choice here.
81435e2901: Stanley Park Brewing occupies a heritage building constructed in 1930 as a social sports pavilion, revitalized as a craft brewery and full-service restaurant in 2019 within Vancouver's iconic Stanley Park. Two large covered outdoor patios and cozy indoor dining rooms serve a west coast-inspired menu alongside award-winning craft beers brewed on-site each week. Situated just steps from Stanley Park's seawall and recreational trail network, it is a natural mid-ride or post-ride destination.
df9bfa7e1b: Mai Thai is an authentic Thai restaurant in downtown Prince George, owned by Thailand-born Nid Chuthep, who has been serving the community since 2006 with the current downtown location opening in 2017. The menu spans curries, stir-fries, soups, salmon dishes, and seafood, all prepared with fresh ingredients and daily specials, alongside a dedicated vegetarian section and gluten-free options. Cyclists can sit down for a full dine-in meal or place an online order for pickup or delivery.
fa34bfec7a: Indian Burger Joint is a fast-casual 100% vegetarian Indian fusion restaurant founded in 2023 by Navneet Bhadu, serving burgers, grilled naan-wiches, hotdogs, tacos, and Indian street food seasoned with traditional regional spices. The Kingsway location is one of six across BC and runs late into the night, making it a practical refueling stop for cyclists on this busy corridor. The entirely meat-free menu with vegan options throughout is a distinctive offering rarely found at a quick-service restaurant.
b9a221f320: Ay Chihuahua is an authentic Mexican restaurant on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, serving traditional dishes including pozole soup, tacos, enchiladas, and chimichangas prepared with homemade sauces and fresh ingredients. The restaurant operates two Lower Mainland locations and offers both dine-in and takeout. Customer reviews consistently highlight the quality of the homemade recipes and the availability of gluten-free options.
bf9fdf07e7: Batch is an outdoor pub with multiple Vancouver locations, including a year-round Kitsilano outpost and seasonal plazas at Ambleside and the Plaza of Nations. The venue leans heavily on atmosphere — fire pits, food trucks, local brews, hot cider, and live music every day of the week. It is dog-friendly and draws a relaxed neighbourhood crowd, making it a reasonable rest stop for cyclists exploring the Kitsilano or waterfront areas.
443f55a194: Sushi Waa is a sushi restaurant located in a commercial unit on Tenth Street in Nanaimo. It offers takeout alongside dine-in service and provides online ordering through a dedicated menu platform. Cycling visitors passing through Nanaimo's south end will find it a straightforward stop for Japanese cuisine.
ffa705af51: Dosanko is a Japanese yoshoku restaurant in Vancouver's historic Japantown, founded by chef Nathan Lowey and his Hokkaido-born partner Akiyo Lowey, serving Western-influenced Japanese home cooking rooted in seasonal, locally sourced, and housemade ingredients. The kitchen follows a mottainai (no-waste) philosophy, crafting miso, shoyu, and dashi from scratch in-house. The cozy 45-seat dining room sits near Canada's oldest Japanese language school and is also available for private events up to 55 guests.
d6ebd69f49: Perugia Italian Caffè is a UBC Food Services café inside the Life Sciences Centre on the UBC Vancouver campus, serving Italian-inspired meals prepared in-house. Specialties include roast chicken, sundried tomato salmon, classic pastas, flatbreads, soups, and Italian-style wraps and sandwiches. The café serves organic, locally-roasted Milano coffee and Fair Trade Tea, with take-out options suited to cyclists on the move.
1e89148b50: Calico Cat Tea House is a tea-focused cafe in Nanaimo's Haliburton Street neighbourhood, open Wednesday through Sunday. It offers a relaxed, specialty tea experience that would make a pleasant mid-ride stop for cyclists exploring the city. The intimate setting is typical of a neighbourhood tea room.
ce69735478: The Sauce Pasta Cafe is a casual gourmet pasta spot in Vancouver's West End, built around a rotating lineup of more than a dozen housemade Italian sauces prepared fresh daily from local ingredients. It pitches itself as high-end Italian food without the tablecloths or reservations, available as takeout, delivery, or casual dine-in. For a touring cyclist in the West End, it offers a quick, filling, customizable pasta meal close to Stanley Park.
fd5d67e928: Downlow Chicken Shack is a casual fried chicken restaurant on Commercial Drive in Vancouver, part of a multi-location chain. It serves quick meals and offers a convenient food and beverage stop for cycling tourists passing through the neighborhood.
d8c26f74f8: A Japanese sushi restaurant in North Vancouver with indoor seating. A dining option for the local community and visitors to the area.
d91aaebb59: Sushi Kuni is a Japanese-Korean restaurant in Chemainus offering sushi and Korean cuisine. A convenient sit-down dining option for touring cyclists passing through the community.
eff74259bb: Max's Place is a locally owned café, restaurant, and bakery that has been a downtown Cranbrook institution for over 25 years, with a Red Seal chef producing a made-from-scratch rotating daily menu of soups, sandwiches, quiches, and their famous cinnamon buns. Owners Lisa and Graham are deeply embedded in the community and are known for greeting regulars by name, creating a genuinely welcoming atmosphere for visitors passing through. Outdoor patio seating and a broad food menu spanning breakfast through lunch make it a natural refueling stop for cyclists riding through the East Kootenays.
74c08ebea6: Breka Bakery & Café is a local Vancouver family business born in 2006 from a well-established German bakery at Fraser and 49th in the Sunset neighbourhood, now operating 8 locations across the city. Regularly voted among Vancouver's best bakeries and cafés, it built its reputation on quality baked goods, sandwiches, soups, and hot beverages spanning a wide range of dietary preferences. The original Fraser Street flagship remains a neighbourhood institution and a convenient resupply stop for cyclists travelling through the Sunset and Oakridge corridors.
f64575f22f: Palmyra Mediterranean Grill is a family-owned halal restaurant operating since 2013, serving shawarma, kabobs, falafel, and other Middle Eastern dishes made with local and seasonal ingredients. The restaurant offers both dine-in and takeout, as well as delivery through Uber Eats and DoorDash. Touring cyclists will find a full menu of hearty, protein-rich plates and several plant-based options.
0b63a7667d: Empire Garden is a full-service Szechwan and Cantonese restaurant in Langley's Walnut Grove neighbourhood, drawing diners from across the Lower Mainland for dishes like dim sum, live fresh seafood, and made-to-order entrees. The banquet facility seats up to 160 people and the kitchen offers pickup and delivery, giving passing cyclists flexibility on how they order. Vegetarian options are part of the regular menu.
65ec7f365b: Milano's Ristorante is a long-established Italian and Mediterranean restaurant in North Nanaimo, founded by the Mavrikos family whose restaurant roots stretch back to 1974 in Victoria. Specialising in house-made pizza, pasta, and Greek-influenced dishes with fresh daily preparation, it has earned a loyal local following over more than two decades under the Milano's name. A partnership with the nearby Avalon Cinema Complex for 'Dinner and a Movie' packages adds a distinctive local character.
bd04e7300d: L'Isola Bella Bistro is a family-run Sicilian Italian restaurant in Lake Country's Okanagan valley, opened in 2007 by Andrea DiMaggio who brought old family recipes from his native Sicily. The bistro has earned multiple consecutive Kelowna Platinum Awards for best Italian restaurant and is frequently praised for consistent quality and warm service. Touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan can stop for Sicilian-inspired pastas, cacciatore, bruschetta, and paninis, with takeout also available.
278162124b: Yummy Slice Pizza is a Canadian-owned pizza-by-the-slice chain with numerous locations across the Lower Mainland, specializing in takeout and delivery. The Richmond Number 3 Road location sits in a busy commercial corridor and offers an unusually broad menu that spans classic North American pies through South Asian-inspired options like Tandoori Paneer and Yummy Potato. A catering program serving schools and corporate clients signals an established, high-volume operation well-suited to feeding hungry groups.
e060e6215d: Stomping Grounds Cafe & Bistro is a casual cafe in Pitt Meadows offering coffee and light dining. It features outdoor seating.
79e0a1133f: L'aromas Coffee Terra Nova is the Richmond outpost of a locally-founded, independently-owned BC coffee roasting company established in 2015 by three friends who started with a coffee trailer at community markets. The brand has grown to four distinct café locations, each rooted in a neighbourhood identity, with a focus on quality espresso and in-house baked goods. Cyclists passing through Richmond's Terra Nova area will find a sit-down café environment with an online ordering option and a loyalty rewards program.
2da507cf38: Rail and River Bistro (also branded as the Rail and River Steak & Seafood House) is a riverside full-service restaurant in historic Fort Langley, serving AAA premium cuts alongside West Coast seafood including salmon, prawns, and scallops, complemented by BC wines and craft cocktails. The restaurant is part of the Fairhaven Group and can seat up to 60 guests for private events on-site. It runs a monthly 'Voyager Club' themed five-course dinner series, adding a notable special-event dimension to the regular brunch, lunch, and dinner offerings.
bc36584d5c: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain located in Westshore Town Centre (between M&M Meats and Bulk Barn) at Kelly Road and Jacklin Road, serving the Langford, Colwood, and View Royal areas. The menu emphasizes quality ingredients including antibiotic-free chicken and pork, 100% organic tomato sauce, and daily-fresh dough. Vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-smart pizza options are available alongside wings, salads, and sides.
92f18542aa: Pizza Pizza is a national Canadian pizza chain founded in 1967, with this location on Lansdowne Street in central Kamloops. It offers counter service pizza by the slice or whole pie, with takeout and delivery available. The menu includes gluten-free crust and plant-based options alongside the standard lineup, making it a flexible quick-stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.
c28cf272d2: Jackknife Brewing is a punk-metal-inspired craft brewery and pizzeria in Kelowna, BC, celebrated for experimental beers brewed with centuries-old Nordic Kveik farmhouse yeasts and locally foraged ingredients like spruce tips, juniper, and wild berries — earning a World Beer Cup silver in 2024. The space doubles as an intimate live music venue they call 'the dungeon,' hosting regular metal and rock shows. Touring cyclists can refuel on classic New York-style pizza alongside creative, award-winning ales.
3ddbf8965c: The Shepherd's Inn is a family-owned highway stop at Mile 72 of the Alaska Highway, about 42 km northwest of Fort St. John, serving home-cooked western and breakfast meals with bread, soups, and pies made from scratch on-site. It is part of a larger complex that includes a motel, convenience store, and fueling station — functioning as a genuine full-service oasis on a remote stretch of highway. Bus and RV tour groups are welcome with advance notice, and the restaurant takes to-go orders by phone.
7b399e2121: Hatsuki Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in Kamloops. The business maintains an online presence but provides limited information about its facilities and services on the website.
dabe522b66: Harry's Fish & Chips is a British-inspired fish and chip restaurant that opened in 2021 in the Tsawwassen area of Delta, BC. The kitchen hand-cuts fresh local Delta potatoes daily and makes its batter, tartar sauce, and coleslaw in-house. Both dine-in and takeout are offered, with ample seating and straightforward parking according to customer reviews.
8719e98033: Fable Diner & Bar occupies the base of Vancouver's historic Lee Building on Richards Street, growing out of the farm-to-table tradition established by Fable Kitchen in Kitsilano in 2012. The kitchen crafts nearly everything from scratch using locally sourced BC ingredients, offering a menu that spans hearty breakfasts, eggs benedicts, smash burgers, and cocktails. Named among 2025's top brunch and lunch destinations in Vancouver, it provides a full sit-down dining experience in the heart of downtown.
ec82f6b8d0: Willows Galley Fish & Chips has been an Estevan Village institution since 1980, tucked into Oak Bay's neighbourhood shopping strip in Victoria. 6ba5f9c9aa: An Irish pub on East Georgia Street in Vancouver offering indoor seating and casual dining. A convenient food and drink stop for cyclists exploring the downtown area.
36416c28e7: All About Pho is a Vietnamese restaurant in Surrey serving traditional pho, vermicelli bowls, banh mi, bubble tea, and a broad range of Vietnamese favourites prepared with fresh organic ingredients and family recipes. 08e8e41c4a: A family-owned Vietnamese restaurant that has been serving Victoria since 1986, making it one of the city's most enduring independent eateries. 747739a015: La Quercia is a refined northern Italian restaurant on Vancouver's West 4th Avenue, anchored by a seasonally focused menu built on slow-cooking traditions with housemade bread, charcuterie, preserves, and butchery. 1570554165: The Boxcar is a cozy cocktail bar and beer parlour on Vancouver's Main Street corridor, pouring craft cocktails and local beers alongside Roma-style pizza from award-winning Mortadella Pizzeria located next door. 70cf26f299: Liquids + Solids is a scratch-made soup café that has been feeding Vancouverites since 2001, now operating solely from its factory café on Franklin Street at Commercial Drive. 4bd5dbee1d: Famous ROME Ice Cream is a family-run gelato and ice cream shop on Marine Drive in White Rock, opened in October 2021 by a Korean-Canadian family. fb92df9f5b: Carnitas Don Jose is a Mexican food-court stall in downtown Vancouver run by Don José Velázquez, an 8-time Mexican charrería national champion turned chef who brings traditional Carnitas Estilo Michoacán from Zamora, Michoacán to the city. c03192e113: Noodle Island is a Vietnamese restaurant situated in a commercial unit on Fraser Highway in Surrey. It serves noodle-based dishes consistent with Vietnamese cuisine, making it a potential stop for touring cyclists looking for a filling meal along this busy corridor.

608da63e4b: Mogu Fried Chicken is a 34-seat izakaya-style Japanese fried chicken restaurant on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, opened by Yuji and Kumiko Aoki after seven years operating the Mogu food truck at Howe and Dunsmuir. 851f1cc268: Ithaka is a family-owned Greek restaurant open since 2014, serving authentic Mediterranean cuisine from recipes passed down through the family. 8d706ed2ee: BarBurrito is Canada's largest burrito chain, proudly Canadian since 2005 and now operating 385+ locations nationwide. f2189ae927: Bombay Kitchen on Denman is an Indian restaurant in Vancouver's West End, situated on Denman Street — a primary cycling corridor linking the city to Stanley Park. ff95555e56: The Ruddy on Bowen is an independent grocery store and café that has served Bowen Island's Snug Cove since 1997, situated within walking distance of the ferry terminal at Horseshoe Bay. 1097afa630: This Starbucks location sits along Ladner Trunk Road in Tsawwassen, positioning it as a convenient stop for cyclists traveling through the Delta region or connecting to the BC Ferries terminal. 72b8a07e97: Dumpling Drop has been operating in Victoria's historic Chinatown since 2018, serving deep-fried dumplings with housemade chili oil alongside rotating sides like cucumber salad and mango sticky rice. b915ab78a3: New Bhaia Sweet Shop and Restaurant has been a community fixture on Fraser Street since 1997, specializing in East Indian sweets and widely known for their beef, chicken, and veggie samosas. 430d81ff94: OAKBERRY AÇAI is a Brazilian-origin global açaí chain serving organic açaí bowls, smoothies, and snacks with unlimited toppings, located in the food court of the Metropolis at Metrotown mall in Burnaby. 552aac16df: Koerner's Pub is the long-standing campus pub at the University of British Columbia, tucked into the West Mall area of the UBC Endowment Lands. c166f95c1b: Victoria Harbour House is a family-owned steak and seafood restaurant that has been a local favourite since 1980 and has been voted one of the best restaurants in Victoria. 88395772c5: Sushi Heaven is a Japanese restaurant in New Westminster offering a broad menu of maki, nigiri, sashimi, donburi, bento boxes, tempura, and aburi oshi. 1f3a6cfa30: Pendray Tea House is the signature restaurant of the Pendray Inn & Tea House, a heritage Victorian mansion built in 1897 and now operating as an upscale boutique hotel steps from Victoria's Inner Harbour. feb032e8e5: Breka Bakery & Café is a local Vancouver family business that started in 2006 and has grown to eight locations, all operating around the clock every day of the year. 7bbc84f830: Boiling Point is a Taiwanese hot soup specialty restaurant chain serving individual hot pot meals cooked at the table, with a wide range of broth bases from Taiwanese spicy to Korean bean paste to Milk Cream Curry. c1d89aa02f: Camp Café occupies a heritage building in Silverton (constructed between 1903 and 1906) and serves freshly baked grab-and-go food made with local, organic, and farm-fresh ingredients. 2092d6c3e7: Banzai Sushi House is a Japanese sushi restaurant located in a strip mall unit on Westminster Highway in Richmond, operated as a division of Samurai Cambie. f597e60b4a: Catch Kitchen + Bar is an upscale casual waterfront restaurant on the second floor of Bayview Pier at Fisherman's Wharf in historic Steveston Village, featuring a rooftop patio with a 270-degree panoramic view of the harbour and river inlet. fd4167c2ee: Oh! Zzhu Sam Korean Restaurant has been part of the Burnaby community since 2016, offering creative Korean cuisine including stir-fry, octopus with pork belly, and signature Korean fried chicken. 1b84661841: The Black Antler is an independent restaurant and bar in downtown Penticton, run by husband-and-wife team Dan and Lynn, who relocated from elsewhere in the Okanagan to fulfil a lifelong dream. 4e2c17f35e: Akane Japanese Restaurant is a sushi and teriyaki spot in the Walnut Grove neighbourhood of Langley, serving Japanese and Asian cuisine prepared with fresh ingredients. d457c8ccce: The Coda is a live music venue and bar in downtown Victoria hosting jazz, indie rock, folk, swing, and dance music across two stages (Bar Stage and Main Stage). 8e98f19b44: Propaganda Coffee is a specialty multi-roaster café in Vancouver's Chinatown neighbourhood that rotates a curated lineup of Canadian roasters through filter, pour-over, and espresso brewing styles. 6da0d9a3ff: Takara Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Burnaby whose name means 'treasure' — a nod to the freshness of their fish and the care put into their craft. cd1b97b2a4: The Keg Richmond South is a well-known steakhouse and bar situated near the Ironwood Complex at Steveston and No. 5 Road. fe481b5ddd: Amato Gelato & Cafè is a classic Italian gelato shop in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, carrying on over 85 years of family tradition through the Mario's Gelati lineage. 00a559aa17: C-Lovers is a BC-born fish and chips chain founded in 1984, serving hand-battered halibut, haddock, cod, salmon, and prawns alongside hand-cut Kennebec potato chips in a casual, family-friendly dine-in setting. 832f0702f1: Coastal Crust is a family-run pizzeria on Sechelt's Cowrie Street offering handmade-daily-crust pizzas by the slice, artisan deep-dish whole pies, calzones, pastas, and salads. e28ee531a3: Donair Dude is a BC-born fast food chain that opened its first location during the 2010 Winter Olympics, growing from a single shop into a multi-location franchise serving Mediterranean-style donair wraps, platters, and poutine. 0496d1fbf1: A McDonald's fast-food restaurant on Scott Road in the Tsawwassen/Delta area, offering burgers, chicken sandwiches, McCafé coffee drinks, and a drive-through. 79e9a581cf: Habit Coffee is a community-focused coffee shop in Victoria's Chinatown with a strong sustainability ethos, having maintained carbon-neutral operations across both its locations for over 10 years. 4b1171079e: Ton Ton Sushi is a Japanese and Korean sushi restaurant on Cambie Street in Vancouver, serving sushi and a fusion of Japanese and Korean dishes. c093e5ddbd: Khanh Express is a family-founded Vietnamese-Cambodian noodle soup restaurant in downtown Vancouver, built as a tribute to the owner's father and his love of pho. db2d8c260d: BjornBar Bakery is a boutique bakery café founded by Tamera Clark, best known for over 30 handcrafted dessert bars — from classic Nanaimo to adventurous Spumoni — all made in-house by hand. 9656d720de: AnnaLena is a Michelin-starred tasting menu restaurant in Vancouver's Kitsilano neighbourhood, steps from Kitsilano Beach, owned since 2015 by Chef Michael Robbins and General Manager Jeff Parr. 63ad0d917d: Bloo Lounge is a modern shisha and hookah bar on Hastings Street in Burnaby that also serves food and drinks in a lounge setting. e0130d4a91: Five Guys on Robson Street is a well-known American-style burger chain in the heart of downtown Vancouver, offering extensively customizable burgers, hot dogs, fresh-cut fries double-cooked in peanut oil, and over 1,000 milkshake combinations. c82c356607: Shota Sushi & Grill is a Japanese restaurant in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood offering an extensive menu that spans sushi, sashimi, nigiri, tempura, BBQ, hotpot, udon, and rice bowls. ba3cd0ddb2: Dai Jang Kum is a restaurant in Richmond's Saint Edwards Drive commercial area, a district known for its concentration of Asian dining establishments. 0c34193d24: Lao Cai is a Shaanxi-style Chinese restaurant with 15 years of history, rooted in the street-food tradition of Xi'an with signature dishes like liangpi cold noodles, roujiamo stewed-meat sandwiches, and lamb pao-mo soup. f47cd61a46: High Tide Grill is a casual fast-food spot on Bowen Island serving hot dogs and burgers. 8b75c7159c: Mama's Rice Bowl is a small, family-run Korean fast-food spot serving Korean-inspired rice bowls with toppings like bulgogi, japchae, and spicy mayo sauce. ff3b71f775: A Domino's Pizza franchise in the Burnaby neighbourhood of Vancouver offering carryout and delivery pizza. The menu leans Southern-inspired, with crowd favourites like Fried Chicken French Toast, fluffy three-stack pancakes, and the hearty Charlie Bowl, all made with locally sourced ingredients. The cozy, vintage-eclectic interior and signature cocktails (mimosas, bacon Caesars) make it a natural rest stop for cyclists exploring the Kitsilano neighbourhood.
b19c4e526a: Gokudo Shabu Shabu is a Japanese-Taiwanese fusion hot pot restaurant with locations in Richmond and Burnaby, BC. Diners choose from 17 unique soup bases — including sukiyaki, satay, spicy mix, and a vegetarian broth — and cook thinly sliced meats and fresh vegetables at the table in a customizable, interactive format. The restaurant emphasizes sustainable and locally sourced ingredients alongside house-crafted sauces developed by the founder's wife.
c0c8703d5d: The Reach is a community-rooted neighbourhood pub on Dewdney Trunk Road in Maple Ridge, serving no-fuss comfort food alongside a rotating selection of local craft beers. It functions as a genuine local gathering place with weekly themed food specials, live music nights, and Sunday trivia. Touring cyclists passing through Maple Ridge's Fraser Valley corridor would find a welcoming, unpretentious stop with a full pub menu and a strong sense of neighbourhood hospitality.
fec7b55d64: Cosmos Pizza & Pasta is a family-run Italian restaurant that has been serving fresh pizzas and pastas in Victoria since 2007, located inside The Burnside Plaza on Tillicum Road near Tillicum Mall. With a consistent recipe and emphasis on fresh ingredients, it's a well-established neighbourhood spot for a sit-down or pick-up meal. A touring cyclist would find it a convenient dinner stop on the western side of Victoria.
264c938799: Banana Leaf Surrey is the South Surrey outpost of a well-established Malaysian restaurant group with five Lower Mainland locations. The kitchen prepares family-style dishes with freshly made in-house sauces and offers multi-course tasting menus alongside an à la carte menu spanning satay, laksa, seafood curries, and roti canai. Takeout and third-party delivery round out the options for cyclists who want a flavourful meal on the go.
1a287bb8a0: Angus T is a Belgian-style croissant bakery founded in 2016 in Vancouver's Yaletown neighbourhood, built around a family recipe passed down through generations from a small Belgian village. All pastries are handcrafted daily in an open kitchen using locally and European-sourced ingredients, spanning an extensive menu of sweet and savory croissants, cinnamon buns, babka buns, and specialty coffee. A touring cyclist stopping in will find a broad selection of quick, filling baked goods and café drinks in a warm indoor seating environment.
831c375c2d: Pho 24 Express is a Vietnamese restaurant on Kingsway in Burnaby, self-described as the area's top Vietnamese food destination, with a menu built around phở, salad rolls, and a variety of savory starters. The restaurant is open late every day of the week, including statutory holidays, making it a reliable option for cyclists finishing a long day on the road. Catering services and reservations are also available.
0d0932197a: Piggy & Paisley is a boutique cafe nestled in Victoria's James Bay neighbourhood, steps from the oceanside bluffs and cycling paths along Dallas Road. It specialises in premium globally-sourced teas, handcrafted in-house pastries, and locally-roasted coffee from suppliers including Bows and Fantastico. The cafe is also known for its reservation-only Afternoon Tea service, offering tiered trays of scones, sandwiches, and desserts in a deliberately serene setting.
2ccc105f0d: Chucila Restaurant is listed as a restaurant on Number 3 Road in Richmond. No functioning website exists to confirm its cuisine, character, or current status.
e64b438288: Poseidon Restaurant & Bar is an authentic Greek and Mediterranean restaurant in Langley, BC, with a special emphasis on daily-caught seafood and dishes prepared on a charcoal brazier. The 90-seat dining room offers a modern, contemporary setting for experiencing traditional Greek cuisine and hospitality. The restaurant also caters to private functions including group bookings, weddings, and corporate events.
cbd489e9f9: Il Cappello is a full-service Italian enoteca in Burnaby, proudly part of the Dolce Amore family founded by Giancarlo and Daniela Cusano. The kitchen is led by Sicilian-born Head Chef Daniele Navarria—trained at Pétrus and Le Gavroche—with a menu spanning antipasti, house-made pasta, and Neapolitan-style pizza made from 100% organic Canadian flour. The sommelier-curated wine list spotlights Italian estates and indigenous varietals alongside select BC favourites.
bf79d52fa7: Viet Family is a fully vegan Vietnamese restaurant on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most-cycled urban corridors, established in 2022 by the Ho family and relocated to its current spot in 2024. The menu centres on Vietnamese staples — pho, summer rolls, bún bowls, and dry vermicelli platters — all plant-based and crafted with house-made broths and sauces. The restaurant also offers catering and private event hosting, suggesting a comfortable, full-service dining environment well suited for a group rest stop.
eff6faa9ba: Tacofino is the West Coast Mexican food brand that got its start in Tofino, built around a beach-casual menu of tacos and burritos inspired by surf culture. The brand now has two Tofino presences — the original food truck on Pacific Rim Highway and a newer town-centre location on Campbell Street — both offering quick counter-service meals. For cyclists riding the Pacific Rim corridor, either stop provides a well-known, no-fuss refuelling option.
af85017289: Bread Culture is a small-batch artisan bakery in Vancouver's Dunbar neighbourhood, specialising in naturally leavened, hand-crafted sourdough breads and French-style viennoiserie made fresh daily from organic ingredients with no additives. The menu spans an impressive range of organic sourdoughs, croissants, Danish pastries, brioches, choux, and baguette sandwiches, with pre-ordering strongly recommended two days in advance for specialty or large items. It accepts pre-orders via email and processes checkouts securely through Square.
9063d2e00f: A Vancouver Pizza Kitchen branch serving pizza from a storefront in Kelowna's Rutland area. Part of a regional restaurant chain, this location provides a dining option on Rutland Road South in the Okanagan.
bc9bf77a34: Hot House Pizza is a Victoria-based pizza chain with several locations across the city, offering hand-made crusts, fresh-made sauce, and a wide range of specialty and build-your-own pizzas. The Victoria West location caters to takeout and delivery customers, with slices available to-go — a quick refuelling option for cyclists passing through the Vic West neighbourhood. Dietary accommodations include gluten-free, dairy-free, and vegan cheese options.
fa0b0518e9: L'Onore Pizza is a pizza restaurant located on East Royal Avenue in New Westminster. It sits in a mixed-use building (unit 110) in a walkable urban neighbourhood, making it a potential meal stop for cyclists riding through the city. No further details about the restaurant's character or offerings could be retrieved from its online presence.
7e023f3d96: Container Brewing is an award-winning craft brewery taproom in Vancouver's Strathcona neighbourhood, recognized at the Canada Beer Cup, Growlies, and BC Beer Awards for a lineup ranging from hop-forward IPAs to rich stouts, all brewed on-site by head brewer David Dayco. The taproom hosts a rotating roster of visiting food trucks and runs regular events including sports screenings on a big screen. Touring cyclists will find a lively local stop with reservations available for groups.
75a7c88de5: Notch8 Restaurant & Bar is the signature dining room of the Fairmont Hotel Vancouver, one of the city's most storied heritage properties in the heart of downtown. Recognized as one of Canada's Top 50 Hotel Restaurants for 2025, it serves breakfast through late-night dinner and a celebrated Afternoon Tea program. The kitchen blends classic French technique with Pacific Northwest ingredients under Executive Chef Mike Reid.
9b3fb64d61: Pho Spot is a Vietnamese restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver with a broad menu spanning pho, vermicelli bowls, rice plates, Vietnamese subs, and appetizers. It features a dedicated vegetarian section with plant-based versions of its noodle soups and rolls. Online pickup ordering is available, making it a convenient stop for cyclists passing through North Vancouver.
665e1af00a: Himalayan Spice Bistro is a family-owned South Asian restaurant in downtown Fernie, serving dishes crafted with authentic Himalayan spices and ingredients. It offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery, making it a flexible stop for cyclists moving through the Elk Valley. The menu includes vegetarian options alongside a range of traditional South Asian dishes.
3feafe0867: Sidney by the Sea's first brewery, Beacon Brewing is a family-owned microbrewery and tasting room housed in the Oceanna building complex in downtown Sidney. A dog-friendly patio, weekly vinyl nights, and live Friday music make it a lively community hub well worth a stop on a Saanich Peninsula ride.
bc03ef7d0f: A 24/7 McDonald's fast food restaurant in Surrey's 96 Avenue corridor, offering burgers, breakfast, McCafé beverages, and a full takeout menu. The location includes a drive-through and is part of the Canadian McDonald's chain, which operates the MyMcDonald's Rewards app for order-ahead and loyalty points. Touring cyclists will find it a reliable all-hours food stop on a busy suburban arterial.
aee2302cdf: Superflux Cabana is a craft beer bar and restaurant in Victoria, BC, operated by Superflux Beer Company as their 'island outpost.' Located upstairs at 804 Broughton Street, the 110-seat venue features two rooftop patios and an indoor lounge styled after a 1970s Vegas hotel bar, with the latest Superflux beers always on tap and a full late-night kitchen serving burgers and casual fare.
be868cf5a0: Yokidomo Sushi is a Japanese restaurant on West Saanich Road in Victoria offering a broad menu of sushi rolls, sashimi, donburi, noodles, bento boxes, and party trays, with a newer Korean Fried Chicken section. Located in a strip-mall unit, it serves as a practical sit-down meal stop for cyclists exploring the Saanich Peninsula.
4f0517f5fb: Shiro Japanese Restaurant is a sushi and Japanese cuisine spot on Cambie Street in Vancouver, offering a broad menu spanning nigiri, sashimi, maki rolls, tempura, donburi, and noodles. The restaurant supports online ordering with pickup ready in 30–45 minutes, making it a practical stop for cyclists wanting a quick, satisfying Japanese meal on a key Vancouver cycling corridor.
f00dad0469: BjornBar Cafe is a boutique bakery and café located inside the DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel in North Vancouver's Lynnmour neighbourhood, one of three Lower Mainland locations of this local chain. The shop is best known for over 30 flavours of handmade dessert bars — from classic Nanaimo to adventurous Spumoni — alongside fresh pastries, lunch items, and specialty coffee. For cyclists on the North Shore, it offers a quality café stop in a hotel setting.
945fc16f39: Feast & Fallow is a fully plant-based/vegan café in Vancouver's Cambie corridor, serving locally sourced coffee, house-baked pastries and breads, savoury toasts, and a Saturday brunch menu. The café operates with a volunteer crew and is deeply mission-driven, advocating for a just urban food system through community workshops on topics like urban agriculture, composting, and food security. A touring cyclist stopping here will find a welcoming, community-minded space with a full espresso bar and substantial vegan food options.
af72f3d478: Golden Island is a long-running Chinese restaurant that has served Salt Spring Island for over 40 years, operating as a takeout and delivery operation. The menu features house-made BBQ pork, crispy ginger beef, house-made sauces, and a range of combination meals, plus beer, wine, and ciders to go. A local institution with a loyal following, it is a practical meal stop for cyclists touring Salt Spring Island.
6a6afcb016: Indian Curry Corner is a family-owned North Indian restaurant on Victoria Drive with over 25 years of culinary experience behind its kitchen. The menu spans a wide range of curries, tandoori items, biryanis, breads, and appetizers, with a notably deep vegetarian selection including paneer dishes and plant-based options. The restaurant also offers catering and in-store food pickup, making it a practical stop for a sit-down meal or grab-and-go order.
f8190b0bb6: Fudo is a Japanese restaurant and sushi bar that opened in 2017 at Broadmead Village Shopping Centre, specializing in traditional and fusion cuisine under Executive Chef Yang, one of Victoria's only female sushi chefs. The restaurant is known for locally sourced BC seafood — including spot prawns, sockeye salmon, and bluefin tuna — and has been voted best Japanese food in Victoria by Yam Magazine. Raku Ramen is also served on-site, rounding out the menu for cyclists looking for a substantial, varied meal.
fe5741f7c2: River's Reach Pub is a multi-award-winning neighbourhood pub in New Westminster that has been operating since December 2000, collecting six Newsleader A-List and thirteen Record Reader's Choice Best Pub awards. The interior recreates an early 1900s West Coast atmosphere with river rock, old-growth hardwoods, fireplaces, and 19th-century antiques. Cyclists stopping in will find a full kitchen menu, an extensive beer list with domestic, import, and craft options, wines, and cocktails — with a 19+ age restriction throughout.
72dccd801d: Good Kid Coffee is an independent specialty coffee shop in Abbotsford founded by Tim and Lisa Rosebush, who honed their craft in Calgary before bringing their vision for a welcoming community space to the Fraser Valley. The shop features a rotating filter coffee menu, a full espresso bar, teas, pastries, bagels, and breakfast and lunch items. Online ordering with in-store pickup is available, making it a practical stop for cyclists planning their route.
abd9cd8132: Roma Italian Ristorante is a casual Italian restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver, turning out handmade pizza from a wood-fired oven alongside fresh pasta prepared from scratch by a seasoned chef. A touring cyclist will find a sit-down meal with full table service, online ordering for pickup, and delivery partnerships for off-bike days.
9bb163b77a: Thomas Haas Chocolates is a celebrated Vancouver-area patisserie and chocolatier with two café locations, known for handcrafted chocolates, French macarons, cakes, and gourmet sandwiches made by an in-house team of pastry chefs. The North Shore location sits at Harbourside Drive near the North Vancouver waterfront, making it a natural refuelling stop on the popular seaside cycling routes of the area. The shop also carries a 'Powered by Chocolate' cycling jersey line, signalling a deliberate nod to cycling culture.
5cd4e45fa3: Pho Tru is a Vietnamese restaurant in downtown Victoria rooted in the street-side food culture of Vietnam, serving pho noodle soups, vermicelli salad bowls, jasmine rice plates, Saigon subs, and fresh spring rolls made from family recipes passed through generations. The restaurant has two Victoria locations — downtown on Blanshard Street and inside Mayfair Shopping Centre — with dine-in, pick-up, and delivery available. Touring cyclists moving through central Victoria will find generous, affordable bowls well-suited to refuelling on a long ride.
ac89c7656b: Mr Mikes is a Canadian casual steakhouse chain with roots going back to 1960, offering premium steaks, burgers, pastas, salads, and shareable appetizers in a relaxed, come-as-you-are atmosphere. The Kamloops location on Summit Drive serves dine-in, takeout, and delivery, making it a solid option for a sit-down meal or a meal to go after a long day on the road. The brand prides itself on being unstuffy and welcoming to locals and tourists alike.
e0a82eeeac: Caffe W is a Vancouver café that has been operating since 1995, with its original home on West Broadway and a newer downtown outpost on Robson Street. The café serves a broad menu of espresso drinks, iced coffees, smoothies, brunch plates, and a distinctive signature item — the Dubai Chocolate Strawberry Cup with pistachio and kenaf — found nowhere else. Situated on a busy pedestrian strip in the West End, it offers both indoor and outdoor seating.
2776d8a2e2: Pacific Farms Market is a takeaway-only food stand in Richmond (Steveston area) serving pizza and regional cuisine in a cafeteria-style format. With no indoor or outdoor seating on site, it is a grab-and-go stop suited to cyclists passing through the area. The OSM record was last verified in June 2023.
90949558c9: Tamarind Hill is a Singaporean and Malaysian restaurant on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver, serving dishes like Singapore Laksa, Char Kuey Teow, Nasi Goreng, and Beef Rendang. It offers a focused, authentic Southeast Asian menu with both meat and seafood specialties alongside a solid selection of vegetarian dishes. Online ordering with quick pickup is available, making it a practical stop for cyclists riding the Lonsdale corridor.
fcad8b3822: Crema Ice Cream & Desserts is a small-batch artisan scoop shop founded in 2019 by a Taiwanese-Peruvian couple who blend Asian and Latin American flavours into creative, culturally-inspired ice creams made with natural ingredients and seasonal local produce. Beyond classic scoops, the shop offers milkshakes, sundaes, handmade sammies, ice cream cakes, and even dog-friendly pawsicles. The business also runs an ice cream cart and truck catering service for events throughout the Lower Mainland.
59056b9e27: Istanbul Döner Shop is a Turkish street-food spot on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, a neighbourhood popular with cyclists riding the seawall route to and from Stanley Park. The menu centres on kofte platters and wraps served with freshly baked tombik bread and rice, ordered online through a Square storefront. Its location on one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors makes it a convenient quick stop for touring riders.
0d2e36ed50: BarBurrito is Canada's largest burrito chain, operating since 2005 with 385+ locations, and this Colwood outpost serves customizable Mexican-inspired burritos, bowls, tacos, and quesadillas made to order. A touring cyclist stopping in the Colwood/Langford corridor will find a quick, filling meal with a wide range of protein and dietary options.
8e21c25342: La Taquisa is a family-run Mexican restaurant serving scratch-made, home-style tacos and dishes from fresh, local ingredients and hormone- and antibiotic-free local meats. Catering with a fully customizable build-your-own taco bar is also available for events.
84ac443f26: A family-friendly Indian restaurant and sweets shop on Fraser Street in Vancouver, offering authentic curries, freshly baked breads, savory snacks, and a large selection of traditional Indian sweets made fresh daily. The menu includes vegetarian options and daily combo specials, making it a convenient and affordable refuelling stop for cyclists passing through the South Vancouver corridor.
acee72b94e: Memphis Blues is an award-winning Southern BBQ chain with a well-established location on Vancouver's cycling-friendly Commercial Drive, recognized by Georgia Straight, Vancouver Magazine, and Food Network Canada for its applewood-smoked meats cooked low and slow on-site daily. It sits on one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors and offers a hearty, casual meal for riders passing through the East Side.
cf608f4913: A 24/7 McDonald's franchise on Kingsway in Vancouver, offering the full Canadian McDonald's menu including breakfast, burgers, McCafé beverages, and seasonal limited-time items. The location includes a drive-through and indoor seating, making it a convenient all-weather stop for cyclists passing through the Kingsway corridor. Wheelchair accessible.
9569af795b: Andonis is a Mediterranean and Greek supper club on Granville Street in downtown Vancouver, blending elevated cuisine with live music, DJ sets, and curated entertainment into one immersive experience. Self-described as Vancouver's first true supper club, it draws on Greek coastal culinary traditions with a contemporary twist and a private dining room (Cretes Room) that seats up to 14 guests. For touring cyclists, it represents an upscale dinner destination in the heart of Vancouver's entertainment corridor.
5ab24a2c38: Chancho Tortilleria is an authentic Mexican tortilleria on Vancouver's vibrant Commercial Drive, making fresh tortillas daily from ancient, non-GMO corn sourced directly from small Mexican farms. The menu revolves around tacos, tortas, and tragos (cocktails), with an emphasis on high-quality pork and locally sourced ingredients. The walk-in, no-reservations format makes it a relaxed and accessible stop for cyclists passing through the Drive.
fc9b625d45: Two Sparrows Cupcakes & Coffee Bar is a specialty cupcake shop and espresso bar located inside Woodgrove Centre, Nanaimo's large enclosed mall on the Island Highway. The menu spans a full range of espresso-based hot and iced drinks, frappes, dirty sodas, and handmade cupcakes, with gluten-free and vegan options available on request. For a touring cyclist passing through north Nanaimo, it offers a sweet resupply and a quality coffee stop in a covered indoor setting.
83aa106f05: Fu Wah Express is a Chinese takeout restaurant on Goldstream Avenue offering a broad menu of classic Chinese-Canadian dishes spanning chow mein, chop suey, fried rice, Szechuan specialties, soups, and appetizers. The menu includes a dedicated vegetarian section as well as vegan-labelled items.
ce56573a0c: Kung Pao Wok is a quick-service Chinese food franchise founded as a family company in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, now operating roughly 100 locations across North America in regional and super-regional shopping centres. ed28d1757a: Ciclo Espresso The Post is a modern Italian coffee bar situated inside The Post development in downtown Vancouver, serving specialty espresso drinks, 72-hour fermented dough panino baked in an open-flame brick forno, house pastries, Neve gelato from Milan, and cocktails. Touring cyclists will find a quality urban refueling stop with outdoor seating and an Italian-inspired menu that goes well beyond standard cafe fare.
cf353c45f2: Phở Sunrise is a Vietnamese restaurant in South Surrey specializing in pho, located in a strip-mall unit at 15355 24 Avenue. It sits in a suburban commercial area near the 24 Avenue corridor and offers a sit-down dining experience focused on Vietnamese cuisine. A touring cyclist in the South Surrey area would find it a convenient stop for a restorative bowl of noodle soup.
66d4730598: The Narrow Lounge is an intimate, dimly lit bar and lounge at 1898 Main Street in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, part of The Narrow Group's collection of restaurants and art spaces. It serves creative house cocktails and wine alongside Mexican-inspired fast food from its in-house Taco Kat menu, with a covered summer patio offering a livelier outdoor alternative. The venue has a reputation for a lively, unpretentious atmosphere and a devoted local following.
f006f77059: The Ovaltine Cafe is one of Vancouver's oldest continuously operating diners, open since 1942 in the Downtown Eastside and virtually unchanged in decor — retro booths, neon signage, and a classic counter. d7a60d8bcf: A pub part of the Browns Restaurant Group chain. Offers both indoor and outdoor seating with Wi-Fi, providing touring cyclists with a place to eat, rest, and stay connected.
e5a0158da0: Sushi Lovers is a sushi and sashimi restaurant in Richmond's Blundell Road area, offering a menu that includes party trays and more. Cyclists passing through Richmond's flat, bikeable streets will find this a convenient stop for Japanese fare.
176c1f60ca: Neptune Eats is a Cantonese-style restaurant in Vancouver's Kerrisdale neighbourhood, specializing in Hong Kong-style cuisine with a menu spanning breakfast through dinner and seafood feasts. It sits on West 41st Avenue, a quiet residential commercial strip popular with local cyclists.
2798492f7e: Sal y Limón is a Vancouver-born Mexican restaurant founded by four food enthusiasts drawing on family recipes from Manzanillo, Mexico, serving tacos, tortas, burritos, and other street food favourites. Catering, gift cards, and both pick-up and delivery ordering are available.
c63f8d9667: Joe Fortes Seafood & Chop House is a Vancouver institution open for over 35 years, named after Seraphim 'Joe Fortes,' the city's first official lifeguard who became one of its most beloved citizens. It specializes in Pacific Northwest seafood and premium chops, serving more than 50 kinds of fresh fish alongside an award-winning list of over 300 wines.
da35c2553c: Ground Up Cafe & Catering is a community-rooted breakfast and lunch spot in the heart of Gabriola village, run by born-and-raised Gabriolans who source ingredients from local farms and make everything from scratch. The cafe doubles as a catering operation for weddings, luncheons, and conferences, and has built a strong following for its specialty coffee and fresh-baked goods. For a touring cyclist arriving by ferry to Gabriola Island, this is a natural first stop at the village center.
e5fdc60258: Red Tomato Pies is a BC-born pizza chain founded in Williams Lake by Jason and Amber Akeson, now operating 11 locations across Western Canada. 611afc0249: Pho V. Ta is a Vietnamese restaurant in Nanaimo serving authentic pho, vermicelli bowls, rice dishes, and Vietnamese crepes, all made with zero MSG. d0f6f93a5c: Busaba Thai Cafe is a family-owned authentic Thai restaurant in Creston, BC, and one of two locations operated by the same family (the other in Nelson). The kitchen draws on regional Thai cuisines — Northern farmlands, Central floating markets, and Southern fishing villages — using imported Thai spices alongside fresh local ingredients. Touring cyclists will find a stylish dine-in space with takeout available and menu options clearly labelled for dietary needs.
f0976cd465: Monsoon Curry is an Indian restaurant with multiple Vancouver locations in Cambie Village and Dunbar. The Cambie location offers casual Indian dining in a neighborhood setting.
32a2836c18: Chopsticks is a licensed, air-conditioned casual family restaurant in Castlegar that has been serving Chinese, Cantonese, and Japanese cuisine—including fresh-made-while-you-wait sushi—since 2004. Sushi-making classes are also available, making it a locally well-rooted stop for touring cyclists passing through the Kootenay region.
0adf08bdcc: Terra Breads is a Vancouver artisan bakery founded in 1993, known for naturally leavened sourdough loaves, specialty breads, and small-batch granola made with no added preservatives and locally sourced ingredients. The Granville Island location sits inside the iconic Granville Island Public Market, a busy destination accessible by bike paths along False Creek. Touring cyclists can pick up high-quality bread and granola for the road in one of the city's most scenic cycling-accessible spots.
4a5b4cb200: Original Tandoori Kitchen is a full-service Indian restaurant on Main Street in Vancouver's South Vancouver neighbourhood, specialising in tandoori meats, fresh-baked breads, and regional curries prepared by named chefs using traditional techniques. The restaurant presents itself as a fine-dining experience while offering an extensive menu that spans hearty biryanis, seekh kebabs, and a wide range of vegetarian dishes. Touring cyclists will find a sit-down dining room with table reservations available online.
5c087aaa58: Livia is a family-run Italian bakery, café, and wine bar on Vancouver's beloved Commercial Drive, founded by husband-and-wife duo Claire Livia Lassam and Jordan Pires and named after Claire's grandmother. The shop serves handmade sourdough, Italian-leaning brunch and lunch, boutique Italian wines, cocktails, and handmade pasta. Evening pop-up events (including a Friday Lasagna and Lambrusco night) and private buyouts make it a destination as well as a daytime stop.
0c69cea739: Tre Galli Gelato Caffe is a family-run Italian café founded in 2004 by the three Gallo brothers, offering handmade artisan gelato, sorbetto, LaVazza coffee, pizza, and pastries at their New Westminster Quayside Drive location. The café has both indoor and outdoor seating, making it a comfortable mid-ride stop for cyclists exploring the Fraser River waterfront. Their gelato is made in-house to authentic Italian recipes, with a rotating selection of flavours including dairy-free sorbetto.
71cf33fd8c: Menbow Ramen Bar is a BC-based Japanese ramen chain with a mall-format location at Tsawwassen Mills. Cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen area will find a full ramen menu with appetizers, online ordering, and third-party delivery available.
b6c564e166: Merci Beaucoup Cafe is a family-owned authentic Vietnamese restaurant on Commercial Drive with roots from Hai Phong, Vietnam, serving traditional dishes like Pho and Banh Mi alongside Vietnamese coffee. The interior is styled with a Parisian café ambience, and the kitchen sources ingredients locally. It sits on one of Vancouver's liveliest and most cyclist-frequented streets, making it a natural stop on any Commercial Drive ride.
5417e10aff: Cheesecake Etc. is a Vancouver institution on Granville Street, founded in 1979 by jazz musicians Mike and Edith Sims who channelled their love of Parisian and American jazz cafés into a West Coast dessert destination. All cheesecakes — offered in original, chocolate, and matcha varieties — are baked on-site from a secret family recipe, with no crust, making them naturally gluten-free. Live jazz events are hosted periodically, giving cyclists an atmospheric evening stop in the heart of the city.
d6369cfac9: The Loft Pub is a Victoria institution on Gorge Road East offering live music every day of the week, with a strong emphasis on Rock and Blues featuring both cover acts and original artists.
