A sunny patio with views of the surrounding mountains makes it a welcoming stop for cyclists passing through Golden.
bb82a943af: Canadian Classic Pizza Ltd. is a community pizza restaurant that has been serving the Abbotsford area since 2007. The menu is notably diverse, blending classic Canadian toppings with South Asian-inspired options like Paneer, Palak Paneer, and Shahi Paneer pizzas, plus gluten-free crust available on request. Cyclists can dine in or take out, with delivery also available.
d1464856fe: A McDonald's Canada fast-food outlet located in North Vancouver, serving burgers, chicken, breakfast, and McCafé beverages. The location includes a drive-through and offers takeaway. As a large chain presence on a cycling route, it could serve as a calorie stop, though the site is primarily designed around vehicle access.
2a067ea203: Shuck Taylor's is a casual, walk-in oyster bar in downtown Victoria run by the Wandering Mollusk, focusing on freshly shucked Pacific oysters, lobster rolls, and global shellfish including Nova Scotia lobster and Caspian Sea caviar. The restaurant operates on a first-come, first-serve basis with no reservations, and also offers sustainable seafood boil buckets available for online order and in-store pickup. The parent brand, Wandering Mollusk, also runs pop-up oyster bars and catering events across Vancouver Island and the Lower Mainland.
56d835ab2e: Silom Thai Cuisine is a Vancouver restaurant inspired by the lively Silom Road dining district of Bangkok, known for its street food and restaurant culture. The restaurant emphasizes authentic Thai cooking using traditional ingredients and recipes rooted in Thailand's culinary heritage. It operates as a full sit-down dining establishment with reservations available, making it a viable stop for cyclists looking for a proper meal on the Knight Street corridor.
64e18de2e0: Cascadia Bakehouse is a wife-and-husband-run neighbourhood micro bakehouse and caffè in Port Moody, specialising in naturally leavened heritage grain breads, viennoiserie, and house-made pastries using seasonal, local, and organic BC ingredients. The menu rotates around relationships with BC farmers and Italian and Japanese culinary influences from owners Kaitlin and Marco. Cyclists can stop for freshly baked bread, house-made preserves and nut butters, and espresso-based drinks.
90a5509a18: The Wildflower is a family-friendly, full-service restaurant inside the Fairmont Chateau Whistler, one of Whistler's landmark luxury mountain resorts at the base of Blackcomb Mountain. It serves locally inspired breakfast and dinner dishes alongside Whistler's most extensive wine list and a selection of regional craft beers. A touring cyclist finishing a ride in Whistler would find a welcoming, sit-down dining experience with a broad menu and a family-friendly atmosphere.
c4f4c9b6e2: The Basic Eats is a casual all-day breakfast and lunch spot with three Vancouver locations, emphasizing affordable prices, generous portions, and locally sourced ingredients. The Main Street location sits in one of Vancouver's most bicycle-friendly corridors, making it a practical refuelling stop for cyclists. The menu leans heavily on egg dishes, griddle items, and Eggs Benedict variations, with a solid selection of vegetarian options throughout.
c1d49aa4f3: Ono Poké is a Victoria-based Hawaiian poké bar with four shopping-centre locations across the city, founded by a restaurateur who discovered traditional Hawaiian poké on a trip to the islands and set out to recreate that experience on the West Coast. The menu centres on customizable ahi tuna bowls marinated in house shoyu blends, alongside Hawaiian hot plates like Loco Moco and Garlic Shrimp. It's a fast-casual, build-your-own concept with a broad range of dietary accommodations, making it a practical and flavourful refuelling stop for cyclists passing through Victoria's commercial centres.
eae86524c8: Hapag — a Filipino word meaning 'table' — is a neighbourhood Filipino grill on Victoria Drive in East Vancouver, serving classic dishes like Crispy Pata (deep-fried pork hock), Sisig, and a roster of grilled meats straight from the ihaw-ihaw (charcoal grill) tradition. The menu spans street-food staples such as BBQ pork skewers and Isaw, through to baked desserts like Ube Cheesecake and Leche Flan, alongside party trays for larger groups. Dine-in and takeout are both available, making it a solid stop for a hearty, culture-rich meal on a long ride through East Van.
81f085d267: Farm Country Brewing is a Langley craft brewery producing a wide roster of beers from German Pilsners and hazy IPAs to fruit sours and stouts, served in a plaza tasting room with a full food menu built around locally-sourced ingredients. The space hosts regular live music, open-mic nights, and themed trivia evenings, giving it a lively community-hub feel. Cyclists in the Fraser Valley corridor will find a solid sit-down meal and a rotating selection of house-brewed beer within a short detour of the Langley Central transit hub.
c93044b179: Founded in 1978 by the Allen and Green families, Donegal's Irish House is an independently owned, family-operated neighborhood pub in Surrey with nearly five decades of community history. It hosts regular live music events and serves a broad menu of pub classics alongside a creative cocktail list. Cyclists stopping in will find a genuinely welcoming atmosphere shaped by Irish hospitality tradition rather than corporate formula.
d076bc457a: Founded in 2011 by two friends, Timbertrain Coffee Roasters has grown into a well-regarded Vancouver specialty roaster with three café locations, including this Gastown outpost on West Cordova Street. The café emphasizes single-origin and seasonal coffees sourced through direct, transparent relationships with farms across multiple origins. Situated in one of Vancouver's most cycling-accessible and tourist-frequented neighbourhoods, it offers a welcoming community space for a post-ride espresso or bag of freshly roasted beans.
dcb45ebbb6: Pokébar is a fast-casual Hawaiian-style poké bowl restaurant where guests build fully customizable bowls starting from rice, noodles, or greens bases and layered with fresh-daily fish and a wide array of proteins, mix-ins, sauces, and toppings. The chain traces its roots to a family sushi restaurant opened in 1989 and now operates multiple BC locations, with the Davie Street outlet serving Vancouver's busy West End. Touring cyclists will find a quick, filling, and relatively healthy meal option with both counter pickup and major delivery app support.
0f7812ec18: The Indian Oven is a sit-down Indian restaurant on the second floor of a Kitsilano building on West 4th Avenue, a well-travelled cycling corridor. The kitchen emphasizes authenticity, preparing every dish from scratch with hand-picked spices and locally sourced produce, and the menu spans appetizers, tandoori, a wide range of curries, and freshly baked breads. Online ordering and delivery are available, making it a convenient stop or meal-ahead option for cyclists passing through the neighbourhood.
b57352b3af: 49 Below is a small-batch, slow-churned craft ice cream company rooted in Oak Bay, Victoria, making nearly all mix-ins and sauces in-house using a custom dairy base from a local Vancouver Island farm. Founded after a chance encounter with Tuscan gelato, it has grown from a home kitchen subscription business into two neighbourhood scoop shops with seasonal rotating flavours and custom ice cream cakes. The Oak Bay shop on Cadboro Bay Road is a welcoming stop with a community-first ethos and genuine local character.
9d0ac7dcc0: Four Winds Brewing's Tilbury taproom is a craft brewery tasting room paired with a full in-house kitchen, serving handmade tacos, burgers, and seasonal tapas made from locally sourced and organic ingredients. It functions as a community hub where the brewery's freshest beers on tap are poured alongside food made entirely from scratch. Takeout taco kits and beer to-go are available for those who want to grab something on the road.
57e479c7f8: Fezziwig's is a Kelowna institution that has been baking all its bread fresh on-site every morning since 2006, using locally sourced and organic ingredients where possible. Named after the warm-hearted Dickens character, the cafe offers hearty home-style breakfasts and a generous sandwich menu, alongside Cherry Hill Coffee — a local, organic, fair-trade roaster. This Guisachan Village Centre location is one of three around Kelowna, making it a reliable mid-ride stop in the city's south end.
5df5676a62: Pizza Factory has been a neighbourhood pizza staple in Burnaby's Metrotown area since 1996. The menu spans customizable pizzas in multiple sizes alongside pastas, salads, and sides, with vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free crust options available. Situated on the Kingsway corridor, it offers both walk-in pickup and online ordering, making it a practical refuelling option for cyclists passing through the area.
e4062de3ad: This Tim Hortons in Sardis is a full-service outpost of Canada's most ubiquitous coffee chain, located in a retail plaza on Luckakuck Way in Chilliwack. It offers a complete menu spanning freshly brewed coffee, espresso drinks, breakfast wraps with Canadian eggs, baked goods, soups, and chili — enough variety for a proper mid-ride fuel stop. The dine-in setting with drive-through availability makes it a dependable and familiar waypoint on routes through the Fraser Valley.
da4f907d35: Sushi restaurant in North Vancouver with takeout and delivery service. Provides on-site washrooms for customer use.
a84ae36ce2: Sainam is an Isaan-style Thai eatery and bar in Vancouver's West End, helmed by award-winning chef Angus An. The menu centres on the bold, rustic flavours of Thailand's northeastern Isaan region — papaya salads, grilled meats, and fermented dishes meant to be shared with sticky rice. It sits on lively Davie Street, making it a convenient stop for cyclists riding through the West End.
247c2d8fb8: Sushi Royal Tokyo is a Japanese restaurant in downtown Kamloops with a broad menu spanning sushi rolls, sashimi, nigiri, tempura, katsu, teriyaki, and donburi. It offers both dine-in and online ordering, which suits cyclists looking to order ahead or grab a quick meal. Its central Victoria Street location puts it in the heart of Kamloops's downtown core.
f3212403d9: Embers Brewhouse is a craft brewpub that opened in 2025 in downtown Kamloops, serving house-made beers alongside a food menu in a casual sit-down setting. Situated on Victoria Street in the city core, it sits on a natural route through town for cyclists riding the TransCanada or exploring the Kamloops area. Regular programming like Saturday trivia nights points to an active local gathering spot rather than a purely tourist-facing operation.
a4ccd5d939: Pho Ever is a Vietnamese restaurant on Granville Street in South Vancouver offering authentic pho, Vietnamese sandwiches (bánh mì), and bubble teas. It serves both dine-in and takeout customers seven days a week. The Granville Street corridor is a common cycling route, making this a convenient stop for riders exploring the area.
60b3bc8a64: Train Wreck Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom in Port Moody that brews unfiltered, full-flavoured beers on-site using traditional techniques and quality local ingredients. The sprawling event space hosts daily rotating food vendors, bar games, and live music, making it a lively community gathering spot rather than a typical pub. Brewery tours are also on offer for visitors wanting a behind-the-scenes look at the brewing operation.
8a1f8920a9: Lot 1 Pasta Bar is Victoria's original pasta bar, blending family-heritage Italian recipes with international flavours and locally sourced BC ingredients in a warehouse-style space with 17-foot ceilings and an industrial aesthetic. Founded by the team behind Victoria's original burger lounge, it offers handcrafted pasta, creative cocktails featuring local distilleries, and a rotating selection of Vancouver Island draught beers. A touring cyclist looking for a substantial sit-down meal with gluten-free and vegan options in the heart of Victoria would find this a solid choice.
bce6c44737: Hula Poké is a Hawaiian-inspired poke bowl chain expanding across Western Canada, with a location inside Tsawwassen Mills mall. Diners build custom bowls from proteins like ahi tuna, salmon, chicken, or tofu over coconut or sushi rice, picking from a range of globally-influenced signature sauces. The fresh, customizable format makes it a practical and satisfying stop for cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen area.
461051503f: Ocean Park Pizza & Village Pub is a family-owned restaurant and neighbourhood pub that has anchored the Ocean Park community for over 47 years, earning the 2018 South Surrey & White Rock Chamber of Commerce Medium Sized Business of the Year award. The current Craftsman-style building, opened in 2006, combines a full-service pizza and Italian-American restaurant with a pub featuring 20 beers on tap. It is open 364 days a year and well-regarded locally, having been voted best pub and best pizza in South Surrey/White Rock by multiple community readers' choice polls.
fb3afed5c8: Rosalinda's is a family diner in downtown Vernon serving all-day breakfast and lunch with a Filipino-Canadian twist — think Pancit Noodles and Mano Dino Burger alongside classic Eggs Benny and French Toast. Home-baked bread, buns, desserts, and pastries are made in-house. It's a welcoming neighbourhood spot steps from Polson Park and within reach of Kalamalka and Ellison Provincial Park trails.
be06188fbd: Myth Grill & Yakitori Bistro is a modern Japanese charcoal-grill restaurant in Richmond, cooking skewers and grilled meats over traditional binchotan charcoal to highlight seasonal ingredients. Part of the Myth Group restaurant family, it aims for a relaxed urban tavern atmosphere blending yakitori tradition with sake and a cozy wooden interior. Cyclists passing through Richmond's Ackroyd Road commercial corridor could use it as a sit-down or takeout meal stop.
682bde4b39: Delhi Fusion Indian Cuisine is a sit-down Indian restaurant on Vancouver's bustling Commercial Drive, blending traditional tandoor cooking with inventive fusion dishes such as Butter Chicken Pizza and Samosa Chaat Burger. The menu spans a wide range from street chaat and Indo-Chinese momos to biryanis and tandoori specialties, with a full catering service available for events. Commercial Drive is one of Vancouver's main cycling corridors, making this a convenient full-meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the east side.
5b64e71b9b: Taste of Saigon Cafe is a Vietnamese restaurant on Squamish's main commercial strip, Cleveland Avenue, sitting along the Sea to Sky cycling corridor between Vancouver and Whistler. It offers indoor seating in a smoke-free environment, making it a sheltered rest stop for cyclists passing through town. Vietnamese cuisine — pho, banh mi, and similar dishes — tends to be hearty and well-suited to the appetite of a touring cyclist.
06d0c0d8d1: Chilango Modern Mexican is a contemporary sit-down restaurant on Kelowna's main downtown corridor, Bernard Avenue, specializing in Mexican street-food-inspired dishes including tacos, burritos, and craft cocktails spanning brunch through late-night service. It is the sister restaurant to El Taquero, a Kelowna institution next door that has been serving traditional street tacos for over 10 years. Positive guest reviews highlight the food quality, friendly service, and lively atmosphere, making it a viable meal stop for cyclists rolling through downtown Kelowna.
0c9a366e3d: Hermann's Jazz Club is Canada's longest continuously running jazz club, tracing its roots to 1981 and now a civic institution in the heart of downtown Victoria. Operated by the non-profit Arts on View Society with the City of Victoria as building owner since 2024, it offers an intimate 130-seat lounge and restaurant featuring nightly live jazz, blues, and world music alongside a full dinner menu. A touring cyclist finishing a day's ride will find a convivial evening venue with hearty entrées and a rich local music culture steps from the city centre.
093d1e6e69: Naan Club is a modern Indian bistro in a Coquitlam retail plaza bringing authentic Indian cuisine with westernized hospitality — spanning classic butter chicken and naan through to tandoori sliders and masala fries. The restaurant features a full cocktail bar with signature drinks and a heated lounge patio under development. Dishes can be customized by spice level, making it accessible to a wide range of palates.
380e450182: Fraser Park Restaurant is a long-running Burnaby neighbourhood institution founded in 1997 by Anton and Sylvia Heggen, serving hearty homestyle German-Filipino fusion food made from scratch. The restaurant is known for its signature schnitzel burger, German breakfast with housemade potato pancakes and sausages, and daily housemade soups. Described as one of the most notable eateries in BC's lower mainland, it offers substantial, calorie-rich meals well suited to hungry touring cyclists.
29fbc4e6aa: V-Show Karaoke is a karaoke bar in Burnaby offering air-conditioned indoor seating with a no-smoking policy. The venue accepts credit and debit cards and is wheelchair accessible. Touring cyclists may find it a convenient stop for evening entertainment and refreshment.
00c9abb124: Ignite Pizzeria is a Vancouver-born stone-fired pizza restaurant that opened its Mount Pleasant location in 2017, now the flagship of a growing multi-location chain across Metro Vancouver. Pizzas are hand-tossed with low-sodium dough given a three-day rest before firing at 800°F, with a menu that covers both meat-forward and fully vegan options. The Mount Pleasant location is licensed, making it a sit-down dining option for cyclists coming off the Main Street corridor.
900a9841e6: Small Victory is a family-owned artisan bakery and café whose founders trace their roots to a Kenyan immigrant bakery started by their parents on West Broadway. The Yaletown location sits on Marinaside Crescent, steps from the False Creek seawall — one of Vancouver's busiest cycling corridors — making it a natural stop for riders. The menu runs from handcrafted sourdough loaves and laminated pastries to full brunch and lunch offerings including sandwiches, power bowls, and specialty coffee sourced from local roasters.
b8c7f499a9: Legends Bistro is the clubhouse restaurant at Cultus Lake Golf Club, set in a beautiful solarium with views of the fairways and surrounding mountains. It serves the public year-round across breakfast, lunch, and dinner, with a menu spanning American classics, pizza, sandwiches, and salads alongside a full bar. Themed weekly dinner nights and proximity to Cultus Lake's recreational area make it a natural stop for cyclists passing through the Columbia Valley corridor.
b9e512bb6c: Sol Fine Foods is a scratch-kitchen cafe and deli on the Selkirk Waterfront in Victoria, serving locally sourced breakfast and lunch made with Berryman's meats, farm-fresh eggs, and produce from regional suppliers. Coffee is roasted by The Stick in the Mud Roastoreum, and the daily fresh sheet rotates hot specials alongside staple sandwiches, burgers, soups, and baked goods. Indoor dining and a sun-bathed patio are available, along with catering and online ordering for fresh and frozen take-home provisions.
c172010d7f: Good Earth Coffeehouse at Village Walk is a franchise café on Oak Bay Avenue in Victoria's Oak Bay neighbourhood, serving espresso drinks, fresh baked goods, breakfast sandwiches, soups, and seasonal specialty beverages. The menu spans a wide range of dietary needs — vegan, vegetarian, gluten-friendly, and dairy-free items are labelled throughout. Online ordering and catering are available, and the café sits on a well-travelled commercial strip convenient to cyclists exploring the area.
e9ccba6065: A coffee and bakery cafe located on Pender Island's Schooner Way. Serves the local community and provides a convenient rest stop for touring cyclists exploring the Gulf Islands.
020aa30b3d: Heavenly Desserts is a premium dessert restaurant franchise originating in the UK in 2008, now with multiple Canadian locations. The Victoria outpost serves signature dishes including the Croffle (a croissant-waffle hybrid), elaborate American waffles, milk cakes, and crêpes, all with full table service. Each location features unique, elegantly designed interiors described as atmospheric and refined.
0741aa8fe1: Sunrise Pizza & Steak House is a neighbourhood pizzeria on Commercial Drive, one of Vancouver's most celebrated cycling corridors on the East Side. The broad menu spans handmade pizzas with fresh homemade crust, Greek specialties, Italian dishes, seafood, and steaks, making it well-suited for groups with varied tastes. Online ordering with delivery is available, offering a convenient refueling option for cyclists passing through the area.
49ac8db7e7: Park Royal South Food Court is housed within Park Royal, which opened in 1950 as Canada's first enclosed shopping centre, located in West Vancouver on the lands of the Squamish Nation. The food court features more than a dozen counter-service vendors including Tim Hortons, Subway, Booster Juice, Vina Vietnamese, and OPA! of Greece, making it a practical multi-option meal stop. The broader mall complex provides bicycle racks and, at the Park Royal North building, a dedicated Bike Stop with a tire pump and North Shore biking map.
ed94bdf90f: Kokomo is a plant-based cafe and eatery in Kitsilano serving freshly made bowls, salads, acai bowls, and smoothies with an entirely vegan menu. It is one of four Metro Vancouver locations operated by Kokomo Foods Inc., offering both indoor and outdoor seating. The kitchen focuses on whole-food, globally inspired dishes — from lemongrass noodle salad to shawarma macro bowls — making it a solid refuelling stop for cyclists.
7055a3ac14: A Greek-Italian restaurant serving pizza, pasta, and Greek specialties in Kamloops. Syros provides touring cyclists a substantial sit-down meal option with Mediterranean and Italian cuisine, offering a good rest stop along Tranquille Road.
cb6f56b09e: Season's Apple Café is a small Italian-cuisine café in Burnaby, operated by Park Chul Sung and Kim Kyung Hwa. Situated in a unit at 8699 Tenth Avenue, it appears to serve a neighbourhood clientele as a morning-to-afternoon café stop. Its Italian food focus may appeal to cyclists looking for a sit-down coffee or meal break in the area.
8554cb620a: The Modest Butcher is a full-service restaurant and market situated on the grounds of Mt. Boucherie Estate Winery in West Kelowna, offering locally sourced meats, handcrafted cocktails, and an award-winning wine portfolio. The kitchen serves everything from casual burgers to tomahawk steaks dry-aged in-house, with a playful, irreverent personality that has made it a notable Okanagan dining destination since 2020. A touring cyclist looking for a substantial sit-down meal with local wine in the West Kelowna area will find this a solid stop.
69384144be: Grand Forks Station Pub is a pub in the village of Grand Forks. The establishment serves food and drink to locals and travelers in this small community. Outside smoking is permitted on the premises.
f1b66569aa: Silvestre is a family-run Peruvian restaurant on Water Street in Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, opened by Peruvian immigrants to share the authentic flavours of their homeland. The menu centres on traditional Peruvian classics — ceviche, causa rellena, chicharron, and tamales — alongside breakfast plates and housemade gelato. Its location on a popular urban cycling corridor makes it a convenient stop for riders exploring the waterfront.
176247adba: Yama Sushi is a Japanese sushi restaurant in North Vancouver offering dine-in and online ordering. A casual dining spot convenient for cyclists seeking Japanese cuisine during their travels through the area.
63c8cf0729: Rain or Shine is a beloved Vancouver homemade ice cream chain making small-batch flavours with locally sourced BC ingredients, including custom-formula dairy from Birchwood Dairy Farm in Abbotsford. The UBC location sits on University Boulevard at the edge of campus, placing it directly on a popular cycling corridor near Pacific Spirit Regional Park trails. A rotating seasonal menu complements permanent flavours, with dedicated vegan and gluten-free options throughout.
8905300b84: Ms Tiffin is a Vancouver Indian street food restaurant and tiffin subscription service founded in 2017 by Seema Nanda, offering bold dishes from crispy chaats and frankies to butter chicken poutine alongside home-style tiffin meal deliveries and a selection of mithai. Customer reviews praise the spacious, relaxed dining area and the authenticity of the food, which draws comparisons to roadside dhabas. The operation also handles wedding catering and group orders, making it a notable community hub for Indian cuisine in the city.
dc9424e08c: The Peri Peri Shack is a flame-grilled peri peri chicken restaurant drawing on the African and Portuguese culinary tradition of the Peri-Peri pepper, with chicken marinated 24 hours in a secret spice blend before grilling. Cyclists can choose from seven flavour profiles ranging from Plain and Mild through Citrus & Herb, Mango, and Hot up to the signature Peri Nero. The restaurant also offers catering and sharing packs suited for groups.
3780c2e59e: Toto Sushi is a Japanese restaurant in Tsawwassen (Delta, BC) that relocated from Steveston, bringing the same quality-focused approach to its new community. The kitchen emphasizes wild sockeye salmon, premium Japanese Yamabuki sushi vinegar, roasted sea salt, and preservative-free nori. Cyclists passing through the Tsawwassen area will find a full menu spanning nigiri, sashimi, specialty rolls, teriyaki, ramen, and party trays.
08f64ec5ed: Stanley's Bar & Grill is a full-service restaurant housed inside the historic Stanley Park Pavilion, offering what the venue describes as Stanley Park's largest outdoor patio overlooking the park's lush gardens. The menu is built around local ingredients, Ocean Wise seafood, BC craft beers, and local wines, with award-winning dishes like the Royal Huntsman Burger. Situated at the heart of one of Vancouver's premier cycling destinations, it is a natural midride stop for anyone exploring Stanley Park's network of seawall and park paths.
09a82d9fe2: Sixth Street Grill is a sit-down restaurant in North Vancouver's uptown area, offering both indoor and outdoor seating in a no-smoking environment. The OSM record notes it has moved on from its fish-and-chips origins, suggesting a broader current menu. Its outdoor patio and central street address make it a plausible rest stop for cyclists passing through the neighbourhood.
91ec427748: Tim Hortons is a Canadian quick-service chain offering coffee, baked goods, soups, and breakfast wraps. This downtown Vancouver location sits in the West Pender Street business corridor and operates on weekdays only. It is a practical pit stop for cyclists moving through the downtown core who need a quick meal or beverage.
0c0f01c6e8: Belleville's Watering Hole & Diner is a locally owned restaurant and lounge sitting right on the edge of Victoria's Inner Harbour, in continuous operation since 2015. It offers a broad menu running from breakfast through late night, with fresh seafood, comfort food classics, craft cocktails, and local brews alongside an unobstructed harbour view. Large-group and private event bookings are available, and the Inner Harbour location puts it squarely on the path of cyclists touring the Victoria waterfront.
964f317ceb: Chimac is a Korean fried chicken and pub located on Yates Street in downtown Victoria. It offers casual indoor dining with a focus on Korean-style fried chicken and pub fare. As a full-service restaurant in Victoria's downtown core, it provides a convenient dining option for touring cyclists.
2c2d89a497: Guacamole Mexican Grill is a locally operated Mexican restaurant on King George Boulevard in Surrey, serving traditional Mexican specialties prepared with an emphasis on fresh ingredients. Situated on a major arterial road through Surrey, it offers a sit-down dining experience in a neighbourhood setting. Cyclists passing through the King George corridor would find this a convenient stop for a full meal.
144456fff5: Broyé Cafe & Bakery is a Vietnamese-inspired coffee shop and bakery on Fraser Street in Vancouver, specializing in bold Vietnamese coffee made from premium imported beans using traditional methods alongside creative house-exclusive drinks. The menu also spans fresh pastries, desserts, and Banh Mi sandwiches. It is part of a small growing chain with a second Vancouver location on Hornby Street and a Saskatchewan outpost.
09324537ca: Panago is a Canadian pizza chain with a Tsawwassen location offering delivery and takeout of gourmet-inspired pizzas made with organic tomato sauce and antibiotic-free meats. The menu spans classic and specialty pizzas alongside wings, salads, cheesy bread, and desserts, with dedicated vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-smart options. For a touring cyclist passing through Delta, it provides a wide range of filling, customisable meal choices.
41a74ec018: A MICHELIN Guide recommended Italian restaurant inspired by the Friuli region of northern Italy, located inside the Hyatt Vancouver Downtown Alberni. Fresh pasta is made in-house daily and the seasonal menu highlights local BC ingredients, including eggs from the restaurant group's own farm in Abbotsford. Part of a well-known Vancouver restaurant group that also operates Ask For Luigi, Di Beppe, and several other establishments.
3b2fb19a33: The Courtyard Café is a café located within Hotel Grand Pacific, a full-service hotel positioned steps from Victoria's Inner Harbour and the BC Legislature. Sitting at one of Victoria's most-visited tourist corridors, it is a natural stop for cyclists exploring the harbour front. The café operates daily and serves hotel guests and walk-in visitors alike.
3facd7f27a: Samurai is an authentic Japanese sushi restaurant on Davie Street in Vancouver, offering traditional Japanese cuisine in a full-service dining setting. It maintains multiple locations across the city and serves as a comfortable meal stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. The restaurant provides a sit-down dining experience in Vancouver's vibrant Davie Street neighborhood.
4c6f9df812: JoJu Hotpot and Asian Cuisine serves authentic Taiwanese and Cantonese food in the Burnaby Heights neighbourhood, offering a full dine-in menu of hotpot and Asian dishes. The restaurant also offers a catering menu for group celebrations and sells house-made frozen dim sum for takeaway. It is a neighbourhood staple appealing to cyclists looking for a hearty, inexpensive sit-down meal along the Hastings Street corridor.
b07d087c7f: A Subway franchise located inside the Okanagan Lake Shopping Centre on Highway 97 in West Kelowna, offering made-to-order Footlongs, 6" sandwiches, wraps, and salads with fresh-baked bread. The location serves breakfast and supports catering orders in addition to its standard menu. Cycling tourists on the Highway 97 corridor have access to quick pickup or dine-in options at this shopping centre stop.
b9e8d372ab: Messob Ethiopian Cuisine has been serving authentic Ethiopian food in Victoria since 2002, with all meals accompanied by injera, the traditional spongy flatbread that doubles as both plate and utensil. The menu is notably cyclist-friendly, offering a broad range of vegetarian and vegan plates alongside meat options, with catering also available for groups. The restaurant is a compact neighbourhood spot on McKenzie Street that has built a loyal local following over more than two decades.
eaf64497d1: A Subway franchise located on Willingdon Avenue in Burnaby, offering made-to-order subs, wraps, and salads with customizable fresh toppings and fresh-baked bread. Orders can be placed in-store, via app, through delivery, or at curbside pickup. As an independently owned and operated franchise, it provides a widely recognizable and accessible meal stop along a busy urban corridor.
bc047b20f2: Finley's Bar & Grill is a full-service pub and restaurant in downtown Nelson serving breakfast through late night, with a broad menu spanning eggs benny, wings, burgers, poutine, and banquet-style catering. The venue features a patio and hosts regular live music events, karaoke nights, and community fundraisers, making it a notable gathering spot on Nelson's main strip. Online ordering with delivery and takeout is available alongside full dine-in service.
3dc7f7f751: Bacayon's Chibugan is a Filipino takeout restaurant specializing in traditional home-style dishes and large party trays, with an extensive menu covering classic preparations like kare-kare, adobo, dinuguan, and a wide range of Filipino sweets. The business operates primarily as a pickup-order operation with online ordering available. A touring cyclist looking for a substantial, flavour-forward meal in the Surrey area would find a broad selection of rice, noodle, pork, chicken, and vegetable dishes.
9d76e6b8ad: Billy Gruff Creamery is an ice cream and gelato shop that has been a fixture at The Old Country Market in Coombs for decades, part of a beloved Vancouver Island landmark famous for its rooftop goats. The creamery sits within a large, bustling complex of restaurants, groceries, and gift shops that draws travellers heading to and from the west coast of Vancouver Island. The dog-friendly patio and extensive parking area—including a shaded lot suited to large vehicles—make it a natural mid-route stop.
3144f431ef: The Vicious Poodle is a bar and full-service restaurant on Johnson Street in the heart of downtown Victoria, serving both brunch and dinner menus alongside a lively weekly entertainment programme of drag shows and themed nights. The kitchen offers strong vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options alongside pub classics, making it a genuinely inclusive stop for hungry riders finishing a day's ride into the city. OSM confirms wheelchair accessibility at the venue.
90105003b0: Delara is Chef Bardia Ilbeiggi's modern Persian restaurant on Vancouver's West 4th Avenue cycling corridor, named for a Persian word meaning 'beloved — she who brings beauty to hearts.' feac78557d: Meat & Bread is a well-known Vancouver sandwich chain whose Pender Street location sits in the heart of the downtown financial district, celebrated for its signature porchetta sandwich with salsa verde and crackling. ddb3f071e0: Velo Star Cafe is a cycling-themed cafe in Vancouver serving sandwiches and coffee with outdoor seating. The name suggests a strong cycling connection, making it a natural gathering spot for cycling enthusiasts. A convenient stop for food and refreshment on local cycling routes.

f86e89bd8f: Fantacity Karaoke is an Asian restaurant with karaoke on Robson Street in downtown Vancouver, one of the city's busiest pedestrian and cycling corridors. 0e5a0f5278: Sharetea is a Taiwanese bubble tea chain founded in 1992, now operating over 400 stores worldwide, including this Coquitlam location. 9505981976: Indian Burger Joint is a 100% vegetarian and vegan fast-casual chain founded in 2023 by Navneet Bhadu, serving Indian-spiced fusion burgers, grilled sandwiches, naan-wiches, tacos, and Indian street food across five BC locations. 11ccb87a37: Crepe Delicious is a Canadian franchise concept founded in 2004, serving made-to-order sweet and savory crepes alongside handcrafted gelato available in over 100 flavors. 267ef8908d: Zapoteca is an authentic Mexican restaurant on White Rock's Marine Drive waterfront, opened on Valentine's Day 2018 by a trio of founders with roots in Guadalajara, Guanajuato, and Nelson, BC. 1924babca5: Founded in 2014, John 3:16 Malaysian Delights is Richmond's original and most prominent Malaysian restaurant, serving authentic dishes such as Beef Rendang, Nasi Lemak, Hainanese Chicken, and Roti Canai prepared from freshly sourced ingredients. It is a well-known destination on one of Vancouver's main urban cycling corridors.
d2164fbe96: Coasters Coffee is an independent cafe in New Westminster founded by two sisters who designed the space around a West Coast nature aesthetic, bringing the feel of the outdoors inside. The cafe sources its coffee from local roasters committed to organic and ethical growing practices, and its loose-leaf teas from a 100% Canadian-owned supplier. Touring cyclists will find a calm indoor setting with a broad menu of specialty espresso drinks, teas, matcha, and food including salads and pastries.
ee878a0652: Grindstone Cafe is a long-established neighbourhood coffee shop on Herald Street in Victoria, open since 1990 and known for its genuinely welcoming atmosphere. Cyclists can fuel up on locally roasted coffee, made-to-order grilled sandwiches, wraps, salads, house-made Tortilla Soup, and carrot cake. A sunny street-side patio adds an appealing spot to rest on a ride through Victoria.
bc0f4dd34c: Dai Cha Fan is a Chinese fast food establishment located in a Richmond shopping center. It serves as a convenient stop for touring cyclists seeking quick refreshment in the Greater Vancouver area.
9103ebbb65: Donair Addict is Tofino's evening shawarma counter, serving substantial beef and chicken wraps built from top sirloin and free-range marinated chicken — a cut above the typical fast-food donair. The falafel option and gluten-free rice base make it a viable stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions. It bills itself as the high-quality shawarma option in an oceanside surf town not otherwise known for Middle Eastern food.
5153533991: Bobby Sox 50's Diner is a retro 1950s-themed diner on the Lougheed Highway in Maple Ridge, offering a classic American diner experience in a nostalgic setting. Situated on a major arterial corridor through the Fraser Valley, it is a plausible rest stop for cyclists travelling along or crossing this busy route.
b0ab850c6c: Pita Pit is a Canadian fast-casual chain specializing in freshly assembled pita sandwiches, salads, and rice bowls built from a wide selection of proteins and vegetables. This Chilliwack franchise (unit K300) offers takeout and online ordering through Uber Eats, Skip the Dishes, and DoorDash. The build-your-own format and healthy ingredient focus make it a practical refuelling stop for touring cyclists moving through the Fraser Valley.
07c2b43d45: Flipside Burgers is a gourmet burger food truck permanently stationed at Aframe Brewing in Squamish, BC, serving beef, chicken, and vegetarian burgers built from local BC ingredients. Cyclists can order from the outdoor Take Out window without entering the brewery, or opt for patio dine-in by purchasing a beverage inside Aframe first. The pairing of craft beer and scratch-made burgers in an outdoor setting makes it a popular rest stop on Squamish's busy cycling corridor.
8a18bc16db: Elisa is a Michelin Guide-recommended wood-fired grill in Vancouver's Yaletown neighborhood, celebrated for its fine steaks and seafood. Ranked among the 101 Best Steak Restaurants in the World and named Vancouver Magazine's Restaurant of the Year, it features both indoor and outdoor seating with a full bar. The restaurant also operates Luigi & Sons Butcher Shop as a companion venture.
8723df7df8: Vietnamese restaurant serving pho and banh mi, located on Quadra Street in Victoria. A casual dining option for touring cyclists.
a7530d04a9: Barn Nork Aharn Thai is a small, well-loved Thai restaurant in Whistler running a busy made-to-order kitchen with only four dine-in tables and a strong takeout focus. The menu features house-made dishes such as crispy chive cakes, green papaya salad, and a family-recipe grilled chicken, with a clear emphasis on fresh, authentic preparation. Cyclists looking for a flavourful post-ride meal will find genuine Thai cooking with vegan and gluten-free options available.
614b174836: Neptune Palace Seafood is a large-format Chinese seafood restaurant in Vancouver's Marpole neighbourhood, part of a multi-location chain also operating in Surrey and Burnaby. The Vancouver flagship is known for its dim sum service, signature roasted duck preparations, and banquet-style event hosting with space for roughly 200 guests. It is a substantial sit-down destination on the SW Marine Drive corridor, popular for family and group gatherings.
483e36540e: Mister Artisan Ice Cream is a Vancouver artisan ice cream shop that uses liquid nitrogen to create exceptionally rich, dense, made-to-order ice cream from scratch with natural, locally sourced ingredients. The Robson Street location sits on one of Vancouver's busiest pedestrian corridors, making it a convenient sweet stop for cyclists touring the downtown core. Seasonal rotating flavours and vegan options give it broad appeal.
7a60988f93: Phở Hòa is an international Vietnamese noodle-soup chain founded in California in 1983, now operating in over 60 locations across 6 countries including Canada. The brand positions itself around a health-conscious broth made from lean meats rather than traditional bone marrow, alongside a full menu of pho variants, rice plates, vermicelli bowls, and fresh rolls. A touring cyclist stopping here would find a warm sit-down meal with substantial noodle-soup options designed for comfort after a long ride.
e231096924: Woking Dragon is a family-owned Chinese restaurant operating since 2003, offering modern western-style Chinese cuisine across three Lower Mainland locations including Willoughby Town Centre in Langley. The restaurant has earned recognition as a favourite Chinese food destination in the Tri-Cities market. A touring cyclist stopping here can expect a sit-down meal with online ordering and takeout options available.
7cc7bef843: Lunitas is a casual, colourful Mexican eatery perched on the hillside overlooking Gibsons Harbour, serving creative tacos, ceviche, and craft cocktails made with local seasonal ingredients alongside B.C. wines and microbrewed beer. It has been voted Best Cocktail Establishment five years running and Best Tacos four years in a row on the Sunshine Coast. Access to the restaurant involves a staircase or boardwalk route, with the host stand moving down to the SeaWalk Patio in summer.
169ef4b44c: The Barkley Cafe is a family-run cafe in Davison Plaza on Peninsula Road in the heart of Ucluelet, on the west coast of Vancouver Island. It serves fresh-to-order breakfast and lunch — including sandwiches, house-baked goods, and specialty coffees from Victoria-based Caffe Fantastico — with a notable commitment to sustainability including composting coffee grounds in an on-site herb garden. A warm, welcoming stop with both dine-in and grab-and-go options suited to cyclists passing through.
819675862c: Fish With You is a Sichuan-inspired Chinese restaurant in Richmond specializing in fish-centric dishes including Sauerkraut Fish, Spicy Sichuan Fish Fillet, and Tomato Fish Soup. Diners receive unlimited steamed rice alongside customizable add-ins such as tofu, wood ear mushrooms, and vermicelli. The Richmond location on Alexandra Road is part of a two-branch chain also operating in Burnaby, offering both dine-in and online ordering through delivery platforms.
2cc5b31ba1: Onigiri Ya is a Japanese rice ball shop on Robson Street in Vancouver's downtown core, one of three Vancouver locations operated by the Maruhachi Ramen Group. The shop focuses on freshly made onigiri available for pre-order pickup, offering a quick and portable meal well-suited to cyclists on the move. The Robson branch is steps from the seawall and major cycling routes through the city centre.
9153332e4d: A restaurant and confectionery shop specializing in Indian cuisine, located on Lougheed Highway in Chilliwack. The business combines a sit-down restaurant with an attached sweets shop offering both prepared Indian meals and confectionery items.
52f7208e5a: The Galley Patio & Grill is a casual, long-running waterfront restaurant at the Jericho Sailing Centre in Vancouver, serving West Coast comfort food including beer-battered BC rockfish, locally sourced burgers, and seasonal salads on an open patio. It has been operating since at least 2003 — its signature Jamaican Jerk Chicken Burger is noted as a Galley original from that year — and sources humanely raised beef from Semlin Valley Ranch in Cache Creek. The restaurant also provides catering for events at the Jericho Sailing Centre, making it a well-established fixture on Vancouver's western waterfront cycling corridor.
4b2a750758: Rabbit Rabbit is a small wine bar and restaurant on the edge of Victoria's historic Chinatown, helmed by Executive Chef Billy Nguyen and Wine Director Sydney Cooper, with a frequently changing menu of locally sourced, seasonally driven cuisine. The wine program is curiosity-driven and focuses on small, sustainable producers from around the world, with notable representation from Vancouver Island wineries and appellations. The bar earned recognition in Air Canada's Best New Restaurants 2025 and has been nominated for the 2026 Vancouver Magazine Restaurant Awards.
9325e79a3e: The Barley Merchant is a craft-focused taproom and kitchen in Langley, BC, built around a strict 'We Serve BC' philosophy: all 50 taps pour exclusively from independently owned BC breweries, cideries, and distilleries. Since opening, it has rotated through more than 2,100 unique BC craft beers from over 165 breweries across the province. A full food menu sourced from BC ingredients accompanies the drinks program in a relaxed, upbeat setting.
925a800b70: Wild Sushi is a sushi restaurant located on Dunbar Street in Vancouver. As a restaurant, it serves prepared food to customers. Limited website information is available due to access issues.
349df1b1be: Kumare Restaurant & Bakery is a Richmond Filipino restaurant celebrating the regional diversity of Filipino cuisine through an extensive menu of silog breakfasts, soups, mains, and classic pastries. The business also operates a street food truck serving pop-ups and community events across the Lower Mainland, and ships authentic Filipino baked goods throughout BC. A touring cyclist will find a community-oriented dining destination with broad dietary accommodation and dedicated takeout and boxed lunch services.
eb59b190f6: The Bay Gibsons is a New York-style thin-crust pizza restaurant in Gibsons, BC, known for creative named pies made with cold-fermented, fresh-milled flour dough. The menu ranges from classic pepperoni to inventive signatures like the Dirty Little Peach and Mary Had a Little Lamb, with vegetarian options throughout. Notably, the restaurant accepts Bitcoin and Lightning Network payments in addition to conventional methods.
1a068e4221: Run With Soup is a restaurant in Sechelt. The website was inaccessible during verification, limiting available information about the establishment's character and amenities for touring cyclists.
c7f154708c: Pizza Dough Therapy by Ojas Blend is an independent artisan pizza shop on Johnston Road in White Rock, offering an eclectic lineup of globally inspired pies—think jerk chicken and pineapple, palak paneer, and chipotle chorizo alongside classic margherita. The menu is unusually broad for a fast-food format, with a full vegetarian section and vegan cheese available as an add-on. Pickup orders can be placed online, making it a convenient refuelling stop on the White Rock waterfront cycling corridor.
0bdf69b10f: Papa John's is a national pizza chain franchise located in a strip-mall unit in north Nanaimo, offering pizza, breadsticks, and wings for delivery or carryout. It sits along the Rutherford Road corridor, which connects residential areas to the highway, making it a reachable stop for cyclists passing through the north end of the city. The carryout option makes it a practical choice for a hot meal on the road.
9da7ccfc82: West Coast Poké is a Vancouver poke bowl restaurant on West 8th Avenue built around chef-inspired flavours, fresh ingredients, and sustainable sourcing. It offers both signature classic bowls (featuring Ahi tuna, Atlantic salmon, prawn, and albacore tuna) and a fully customizable build-your-own option with a wide range of proteins, toppings, and house sauces. The emphasis on an on-the-go, nourishing meal format makes it a practical and appealing fuel stop for touring cyclists.
c622a0caae: North Garden Cafe is a Hong Kong-style Chinese restaurant in Coquitlam serving an extensive menu of seafood, hot pot, congee, chow mein, and more. The restaurant offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery with online ordering available. It accepts cash or debit only.
cc4647cf3a: Bean Scene Coffee House is a long-established independent coffee shop in the heart of downtown Vernon, BC, with a loyal local following built on good coffee and a relaxed social atmosphere. The business describes itself as a place where 'a cup of coffee is a moment to share,' emphasising community and conversation over quick turnover. For touring cyclists moving through the Okanagan, it offers a welcoming downtown rest stop on 30th Avenue.
2960e85760: Tan's Kitchen is a Chinese restaurant on the West Island Highway in Parksville serving Cantonese and Szechuan dishes including Salt & Pepper Squid, Ginger Beef, and General Tso's Chicken. The restaurant offers all-you-can-eat service and outdoor dining, and advertises no MSG in its food. It sits on a main cycling corridor along eastern Vancouver Island, making it a convenient full-service meal stop.
3ebf599a9c: The Seaside Restaurant is a historic waterfront kitchen in Vesuvius Bay, located steps from the Vesuvius Ferry Terminal on Salt Spring Island — making it a natural stop for cyclists arriving or departing by ferry. The site has been a community landmark since the 1940s, beginning as Vesuvius Marine with a hand-pumped gas station before evolving into the beloved seaside eatery it is today. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available, and the restaurant offers catering and online ordering.
63f0cb13b3: Gong Cha is a globally recognized bubble tea brand operating over 1,650 stores across 20 countries, with more than 50 locations across Canada. This Kelowna location serves handcrafted tea-based drinks in a primarily takeaway format, ideal for a quick stop on a cycling route. A rewards program lets customers accumulate points across all Canadian locations.
c207ced311: Hongdae Korean Restaurant is a Korean eatery in Coquitlam specializing in jokbal (braised pig's trotters), advertised as freshly prepared daily. Located at the intersection of North Road and Lougheed Highway, it offers indoor seating and online ordering. The late closing time makes it a viable stop for cyclists finishing a long evening ride.
260bdf6e3f: Established in 1984, Granville Island Brewing operates this taproom on Granville Island where visitors can sample the full core lineup alongside exclusive small-batch Taproom Series releases brewed on-site — beers unavailable anywhere else. The taproom offers indoor and outdoor patio seating with a food menu, dogs are welcome on the patio and brewery entrance, and the space is wheelchair accessible via a side-door ramp.
5398518200: Noodlebox is a Canadian fast-casual franchise specializing in wok-fired Asian noodle and rice dishes built to order from a customizable menu of sauces and proteins. The chain operates multiple BC locations and emphasizes fresh, made-to-order cooking with broad dietary accommodation. A cyclist stopping in Chilliwack would find a quick, filling meal with vegan and gluten-friendly options available on request.
1b187b8e34: A sushi and poke restaurant with indoor seating in Burnaby. A casual dining option for cyclists passing through the area.
899f9903cd: Little Caesar's is a well-known Canadian pizza chain offering hot-and-ready pizzas for carryout and delivery. This Nanaimo location (unit 3) is part of the globally recognized franchise founded in Michigan in 1959. For a touring cyclist looking for a quick, filling meal, it offers an accessible fast-food option in the Nanaimo area.
64900d068a: A pub and fast food restaurant in Scotch Creek serving the local community and traveling guests. Located on Squilax Anglemont Road, it offers casual dining and refreshment options for cyclists and other travelers.
da995e84e2: The Teahouse has occupied the heritage building at Ferguson Point in Stanley Park since 1978, offering west coast seafood and seasonal menus with unobstructed ocean views from window-lined dining rooms and a waterfront patio. Part of the Sequoia Company of Restaurants, it sits directly along the Stanley Park Seawall—one of the most heavily cycled routes in Vancouver—making it a natural candidate rest stop for touring cyclists. The restaurant operates a full dinner, brunch, and lunch service with dedicated private event spaces including a glass-roofed conservatory and garden lawn.
2f2a7e9d00: The Edge is an award-winning fine dining restaurant perched 1,000 feet above Okanagan Lake at The Rise Resort golf club on the edge of Vernon, named Vernon's Restaurant of the Year 2025. The 30,000-square-foot space features floor-to-ceiling windows and a multi-level patio delivering 360-degree panoramic views of the Okanagan Valley. The kitchen sources almost exclusively from named Okanagan and broader BC producers—farmers, foragers, stone millers, and charcutiers—with a wine program anchored in local Okanagan vintages.
17f1589a37: Victoria's first and largest board game cafe, offering access to over 1,500 games to play in-venue for a flat per-person fee with no time limit. Fully licensed since 2018 and family-friendly, the cafe serves an extensive menu of toasted sandwiches, flatbread pizzas, snacks, coffee drinks, and dozens of housemade milkshake flavours. A touring cyclist looking for a relaxed, social stop in downtown Victoria will find good food, cold drinks, and a genuinely unique atmosphere.
2309846d07: Pür & Simple is a Canadian breakfast and brunch franchise chain with over 65 locations across North America, bringing upscale daytime dining to Kelowna with creative twists on comfort-food classics like Eggs Benedict, pancakes, French toast, and waffles. The restaurant also offers a full Nespresso coffee bar, smoothies, and a kids menu, making it a well-rounded fueling stop for groups of all sizes. Both dine-in and online ordering for delivery or takeout are available.
1ea015f557: Harvest Community Foods is a community-supported, locally sourced grocery store and noodle soup café in Vancouver's Strathcona neighbourhood, owned and operated by local chefs Andrea Carlson and Gabriella Meyer. The shop serves a rotating menu of ramen, udon, and rice bowls with multiple vegan options, alongside a grocery section emphasizing urban produce and small-batch local foods. It also functions as a pickup hub for CSA (Community Supported Agriculture) bags filled with seasonal produce sourced from regional farms.
8f6ed2f999: Maison d'la Poutine House is a Quebec-inspired restaurant in Chilliwack offering classic poutine alongside handmade-dough pizzas with toppings like Montreal smoked meat and pepperoni. The menu leans into hearty, comfort-food staples that make for a satisfying refuel after a long day in the saddle. Orders can be placed online for pickup or delivery.
50c4a3fdc2: Bailey's Pub is a locally owned neighbourhood pub in North Kamloops serving scratch-made Canadian food for breakfast, lunch, and dinner seven days a week. The casual, welcoming atmosphere caters to groups of any size, with walk-ins accepted alongside reservations. Touring cyclists will find a full-service meal stop with takeout available and regular entertainment including karaoke and trivia nights.
c6cbe0c391: Mount Currie Coffee Co. is a locally rooted coffee shop with two locations serving the Sea-to-Sky corridor — Pemberton and Whistler Village — pouring premium espresso drinks from Gradient Coffee roasted just up the road in the Pemberton Industrial Park. Active supporters of both PORCA and WORCA, they co-sponsor annual mountain bike events and describe themselves as 'a place to start your adventure,' making them a natural gathering spot for cyclists in the region. Call-ahead ordering is available for groups heading out on the trails.
7552a600cf: K & H Seafood Restaurant is a Chinese seafood dining destination on Kingsway, one of Vancouver's main east-west arterials and a common cycling corridor. The restaurant sits in a dense commercial strip in East Vancouver that serves a large Chinese-Canadian community. Touring cyclists passing through on Kingsway or nearby routes will find a full-service sit-down option for seafood and Chinese cuisine.
010d3c555e: Hook Cantina is a restaurant on Denman Street in Vancouver's West End, situated near the Stanley Park seawall and popular urban cycling routes. Its cantina-style name suggests a casual dining concept well-suited to the neighbourhood's active, outdoor-oriented clientele. No further details about the menu or interior could be confirmed due to a website access issue.
68d12e4ead: A cafe serving the Vancouver community. Limited wheelchair access is available. No vegan options are offered according to OSM records.
e4d57ccf18: A family-owned Chinese and Japanese restaurant that has anchored downtown Kamloops since 1971, making it one of the longest-running restaurants in the city. The menu spans Cantonese stir-fries, house-recipe Szechuan dishes, an extensive sushi selection, and in-house roasted duck — all prepared by the restaurant's own chefs. A private tatami room accommodating up to 16 guests adds a distinctive dining option that sets it apart from typical downtown restaurants.
f9a5fb6c6a: Frank's Pies & Slices is a New York-inspired pizza restaurant tucked along North Commercial Drive in East Vancouver, operating out of the Resurrection Spirits space. The menu leans into creative, shareable pies with names like 'Notorious P.I.E.' and 'Silk Tracksuit', alongside share plates and late-night pizza slices. A cyclist finishing a ride along the nearby Commercial Drive corridor would find a lively, independently run spot well suited to a post-ride meal.
7cba92fab5: Aroma Eatery is a Chinese restaurant offering takeaway service. It provides a convenient food and refueling stop for touring cyclists. Amenities such as bike parking and water access are unconfirmed.
460353b2e8: Smith's Irish Pub is an Irish-owned bar in the heart of Vancouver's historic Gastown neighbourhood, spread across two adjoining storefronts. The venue offers a cozy main bar, an elegant lounge with private snugs, and The Forge — a hidden cocktail and whiskey bar that can be hired privately. Touring cyclists arriving in Gastown will find a lively house-of-rugby atmosphere with live music and food service from SMASHED!
f1f2748eee: A dual-concept restaurant combining Ricky's breakfast café with Famoso Pizzeria, allowing cyclists to stop for either breakfast or pizza at a single location. Both brands operate together under FDF Restaurant Brandz ownership and management. This location on Sumas Way offers diverse dining options for touring cyclists.
fca1c6a4bb: HellCrust Pizza is a franchise pizza chain with a North Vancouver location operating as a fast-food format. The location offers both indoor air-conditioned seating and outdoor seating, making it a potential mid-ride meal stop. A dedicated app and coupon program suggest it caters to frequent, convenience-oriented customers.
2929799307: Charlotte & the Quail is a farm-to-plate breakfast and lunch restaurant perched on the edge of a 10-acre botanical garden on Quayle Road, serving seasonal menus built around produce from neighbouring farms and Vancouver Island. It is directly accessible via the Galloping Goose and Lochside Trail, making it a natural destination stop on a cycling day. The restaurant has operated at this location since 2010 and dishes are garnished with edible flowers harvested fresh each morning.
a6729fd6ec: Fable Kitchen is a farm-to-table sit-down restaurant in Kitsilano's West 4th corridor, open since 2012 and built around locally sourced, seasonal ingredients that change with the menu. Head chef Michael Broadbent leads a team known for creative cuisine paired with a notable cocktail and wine program. The restaurant has been featured in the Michelin Guide Vancouver coverage and multiple Best Brunch lists, making it a noteworthy destination on a popular cycling corridor.
66e4752106: Rainbow Butterfly is a Chinese restaurant in North Vancouver. Additional details about amenities and facilities were unavailable for verification.
b8b9b222f7: Uprising Breads Bakery Café is a 40-plus-year community institution at the corner of Venables and Commercial Drive in East Vancouver, baking multigrain breads, pastries, and honey-sweetened goods on site every morning. The café serves a full lunch menu of homemade soups, hot savory items, and sandwiches made on fresh-baked bread, alongside espresso drinks. Both indoor and outdoor seating are available in a bright, welcoming space that locals describe as a neighborhood meeting spot.
58c44bf88e: Angels Ice Cream is an artisan gelato and gift shop on White Rock's famous Marine Drive, steps from the beach promenade and pier — a natural stop for cyclists riding the waterfront. The shop offers handcrafted gelato alongside coffee, gifts, jewellery, and seashells, blending a sweet treat with a souvenir experience. Its location on one of BC's most scenic coastal cycling routes makes it a memorable mid-ride destination.
5f6cb689ef: Tacofino is a BC-born taco chain that grew from a Tofino food truck into a multi-location restaurant group serving West Coast-inspired Mexican food. The Kitsilano outpost sits directly on West 4th Avenue, one of Vancouver's busiest protected cycling corridors linking Point Grey to downtown. It is a well-known casual stop with pickup ordering available through multiple platforms.
204d077f25: Hanks is a small, independently operated restaurant on Douglas Street in downtown Victoria, built around an ever-changing menu sourced directly from local farmers and fishers. The kitchen leans into flavour combinations you don't typically encounter, served in a casual, deliberately loud setting. A touring cyclist rolling into the city centre would find a neighbourhood spot with a strong local identity and a rotating selection of ingredient-driven dishes.
f4dabf3d70: Aroma Pizza is a long-established Italian restaurant in Kelowna that claims to have been serving pizza, pasta, subs, and focaccia since 1978. Located in a commercial unit on Kane Road, it offers dine-in, takeout, and delivery. The About page lists free Wi-Fi, parking, and live music as in-house amenities.
b99e78d375: Come Along Seafood Restaurant serves Chinese seafood cuisine in Vancouver. The restaurant's web presence is currently under development, limiting verification of current operations and amenities.
452b277dd8: Tim Hortons is Canada's ubiquitous quick-service coffee and food chain, and this Chilliwack location on Vedder Road offers both dine-in and drive-thru service. The menu spans freshly brewed coffee, soups, wraps, baked goods, and Timbits, making it a practical rest stop for cyclists needing a hot meal or a caffeine fix. The location is wheelchair accessible and includes free Wi-Fi.
b7eda6e396: Sushi Crave is a sushi restaurant located in a unit within a commercial strip at 10880 Number 5 Road in Richmond, BC. The Number 5 Road corridor runs through agricultural and commercial areas of Richmond and is traveled by cyclists exploring the city's flat, bikeable terrain. Touring cyclists in the area may find this spot a convenient stop for Japanese cuisine.
3a555c2bcc: Kokanee Pub is a pub housed in a historic Creston building that once served as the area's first hotel, established in 1898. The menu features burgers, sandwiches, fish and chips, chicken, and other diner-style fare, with selections from various breweries on tap.
3c11782cc8: Brazza Gelato & Coffee is an Italian-style cafe on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver serving authentic European espresso drinks alongside an extensive selection of handcrafted gelato and sorbetto made in-house daily. The menu also includes freshly baked croissants, scones, strudels, and panini and croissant sandwiches, making it a well-rounded stop for cyclists needing a real meal or a sweet treat. The shop sits on a busy pedestrian corridor with public bike racks directly on the Lonsdale Avenue sidewalk out front.
8910f0e325: The Library Lounge is an intimate cocktail lounge and full-service dining room at the heart of Nelson's historic Hume Hotel, a property whose bar and fireplace are restorations of the original 1898 splendour. The room features a monumental brick hearth, original caryatids and mouldings, and a cozy parlour-like atmosphere anchored by live jazz several nights a week. Touring cyclists arriving in Nelson will find a complete food and beverage menu, local craft beer, and craft cocktails in one of the Kootenays' most storied hospitality venues.
e008e4ab74: Devil's Elbow Smoke & Ale House is a BBQ-focused bar and restaurant that opened in 2014, built around slow-smoked meats sourced locally from Jackson's Butcher in Kitsilano and housemade sauces paired with BC craft beer on tap. Located steps from a SkyTrain station in downtown Vancouver, it offers a lively atmosphere with a dedicated Whiskey Room for private events. A touring cyclist rolling into the city will find a full all-day food menu, delivery via DoorDash, and an extensive craft beer and whiskey selection.
93ac68f794: Rhino is a coffee house operating out of a unit in a multi-tenant building on Saanich Road in Victoria. The Instagram handle 'rhinocoffeehouse' suggests a cafe identity distinct from any chain, making it a likely independent neighbourhood spot. Touring cyclists passing through the Saanich corridor may find it a convenient stop.
fd4bb8d0c7: Sweet Cherubim is a long-established organic and natural foods store paired with a fully vegan restaurant on Vancouver's Commercial Drive, one of the city's most cycling-friendly corridors. Cyclists can dine in or grab takeout from a wide plant-based menu spanning samosas, burgers, wraps, salads, soups, and desserts. The attached store carries bulk pantry staples, health supplements, baked goods, and personal care items, making it a practical resupply stop as well as a meal destination.
34d63bd333: Wake Up Jake Restaurant is an independent seasonal eatery operating inside Barkerville Historic Town & Park, the largest living history museum in western North America and a National Historic Site of Canada. Housed in Building #56 in the heart of this authentically restored gold-rush townsite, it serves a full menu of old-style favourites spanning breakfast, lunch, and supper, including children's specials. Touring cyclists riding the Cariboo region will find it one of the most historically atmospheric full-service meal stops in BC.
c2093842eb: The Pie Hole is a beloved BC pie bakery founded by Jenell Parsons in 2011, growing from farmer's markets and food truck festivals to three brick-and-mortar locations, including this Langley outpost on Fraser Highway. The shop offers an extensive rotating menu of both sweet and savoury pies — from Vietnamese Coffee and Fat Elvis to Thai Chicken and Steak & Stout — alongside vegan and gluten-free options. Founder Jenell Parsons is widely celebrated as 'Canada's Pie Queen' and has been featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives.
3e41bbf8da: A Trail landmark since 1896, The Arlington is a family-friendly bar and grill sitting two blocks from the Columbia River at the corner of Spokane St and Bay Ave in downtown Trail. Under its current owners since 2005, it serves a menu of nearly 100 elevated pub-fare items covering breakfast through dinner seven days a week. A sunny patio, a large interior with capacity for over 200 guests, and weekend live music and karaoke make it a lively stop in the heart of the Kootenays.
df5bd5110f: The Magic Cattle Guard Diner is a casual restaurant and bar in the Sun Peaks ski resort village, named after the old cattle guard that once marked the boundary where rain turned to snow and the mountain community began. The kitchen serves house-smoked meats, scratch-made soups, creative burgers, and weekend brunch, with a warm atmosphere designed to feel like meeting old friends. Sun Peaks is Canada's second-largest ski resort, making this diner a natural gathering spot for cyclists riding through the alpine village.
47f41dc946: Fresh Healthy Café is a nutrition-focused eatery in Gibsons on BC's Sunshine Coast, built around superfood smoothies, cold-pressed juices, acai and pitaya power bowls, and grilled paninis. The café leans heavily on whole-food ingredients and offers a wide range of vegan-friendly and gluten-free choices, making it a standout refuelling stop for health-conscious cyclists. Online ordering with in-store pickup is available, convenient for riders who want food ready on arrival.
69a1afd1f2: Bridgeview Cafe is a Kootenays cafe serving coffee, bagels, and wraps with outdoor seating. The Facebook handle 'thebridgeviewcafetrail' suggests a connection to nearby trail infrastructure, hinting that it may already serve an active-travel clientele. It appears to be a compact, weekday-oriented stop in an area with limited services.
ab1f85cb23: Naomi is a Vietnamese restaurant in the Lower Mainland & Fraser Valley region of BC, likely specializing in pho based on the Facebook page title 'Naomi Pho Restaurant'. It operates Tuesday through Saturday and would offer a warm, filling meal option for cyclists passing through the area.
cb85d5c86c: A Bread Affair – Langley is the production heart of this organic artisan bakery chain, where every loaf is hand-shaped using slow fermentation and locally sourced BC ingredients. The Langley location doubles as a full-service café, offering fresh-baked sourdough and pastries alongside quality coffee — a tucked-away stop on the Langley Bypass between Kal-Tire and the Toyota dealership.
