bee02220d7: Austin Fish & Chips is a fish-and-chips restaurant in Maple Ridge, BC, located along the Lougheed Highway in the Fraser Valley. It offers both dine-in and takeout service, making it a practical roadside stop for cyclists passing through the corridor. The menu centres on classic fish-and-chips fare with a range of food and beverage options.
692779c5e5: A McDonald's fast food location on Fraser Highway in the Lower Mainland/Fraser Valley, offering burgers, fries, McCafé beverages, and drive-through service. As a franchise of Canada's largest fast food chain, it provides takeout and drive-through options for travellers on this busy highway corridor. The corporate website offers no location-specific details about amenities relevant to touring cyclists.
0812635204: The Flying Apron is a scratch bakery and café in Comox, BC, where a Red Seal Pastry Chef—three-time Skills Canada Provincial medallist—leads a team that begins baking before sunrise daily. The menu rotates seasonally and spans fresh breads, laminated pastries, artisan cakes, and cookies, all made in-house from locally sourced ingredients. Dedicated gluten-free and vegan options are consistently available, making it a welcoming stop for cyclists with dietary restrictions.
f7a965df36: Anie's Pizza & Bakery is a small owner-operated restaurant in Cache Creek sitting along the Cariboo Highway (also known as the Gold Trail), serving made-from-scratch pizza with hand-tossed dough, home-baked bread, and freshly rolled cinnamon buns. The kitchen locally sources produce and deli meats and makes everything in-house, from custom pizzas to sandwiches built on house-baked loaves. Catering is available, and the location on a major Interior BC highway makes it a natural resupply stop for touring cyclists passing through.
56e1ed77fa: The Elements Restaurant is a Chinese-Canadian restaurant on the Trans-Canada Highway (Highway 16) in Houston, BC, serving a broad menu of chow mein, fried rice, chop suey, sizzling hot pots, and combination dinners. Situated in a small interior BC community along a major touring corridor, it stands out as one of the few full-service dining options for cyclists passing through the region. Online ordering with 15–30 minute pickup is available, and recent reviewers consistently praise generous portion sizes.
6fd6b5d2e4: De l'Île Restaurant is a small dinner-service restaurant on Vancouver Island, operating out of 129 Second Avenue West in the Vancouver Island & Gulf Islands region. The associated website has evolved into a food and travel blog alongside a digital recipe store, suggesting a chef-driven operation with interests spanning Italian cuisine, wine, and amaro. For touring cyclists, it offers a sit-down dining option in a community not saturated with evening restaurant choices.
9316ce5487: The White Tower is a long-established Campbell River institution on Vancouver Island, serving authentic Greek cuisine alongside pizza, steak, lobster, and curry dishes for over 30 years. The restaurant is family-operated by Bill and Surinder Tsangaris and seats more than 120 guests, making it well-suited for larger cycling groups. A full licensed bar with wine, beer, and cocktails rounds out the sit-down dining experience.
4263d64f9d: Projekt Blend is a contemporary specialty café in Langley serving precision espresso drinks, signature lattes, and freshly made food in a workspace-friendly environment. The menu features creative items like smash burgers, Monte Cristo sandwiches, and a rotating roster of seasonal drinks, all made with locally sourced ingredients where possible. The café actively positions itself as a community gathering space — a warm 'third place' well-suited to a mid-ride stop or a longer work session.
b9ad472154: Sushi Wara is a Japanese restaurant in Qualicum Beach specializing in sushi and traditional Japanese cuisine. The restaurant provides online ordering for convenient meal stops. It serves the Qualicum Beach community as a useful dining option for touring cyclists passing through the area.
78f94c15bc: Mazatlán is a Mexican restaurant offering dine-in service with outdoor seating available. A casual spot for cyclists seeking a meal break during their travels through the Lower Mainland.
208c8bea7f: Oliver Street Bar & Grill is a neighbourhood pub and American-cuisine restaurant in Williams Lake, BC, billing itself as a local gathering spot for food, cold drinks, and community. It offers both a dine-in experience and a dedicated to-go menu, giving passing cyclists a convenient option for a sit-down meal or a quick pickup. Williams Lake sits at a key crossroads in BC's Cariboo region, making this a practical stop on longer interior touring routes.
581ddf12ac: Gneiss Wines is a small-lot artisan winery housed in the District Wine Village in Oliver, BC, a curated cluster of South Okanagan wine, beer, and spirits producers a few minutes from downtown. The name references the gneiss rock formations underlying their Naramata Bench vineyard, which runs along more than a kilometre of the Kettle Valley Railway cycling trail. Founded by partners with multi-generational Okanagan roots, the winery crafts small-batch varietals including Tempranillo, Cabernet Franc, Pinot Gris, and Pinot Noir from sustainably managed local vineyards.
199d7002fc: Café Artigiano is a pioneering BC specialty coffee chain with over 25 years of history, known for expertly crafted espresso drinks using in-house roasted 100% Arabica beans from their Burnaby roastery. This Langley location is part of a network of 25 cafes across BC and Alberta, each serving artisanal baked goods made from organic, local ingredients free of artificial additives. Some locations now operate as Cafe-Bars offering cocktails and Italian bites into the evening.
aa07ab4ec1: Red Rock Grill is a locally owned and operated restaurant in 100 Mile House, BC, established in 2009 by a second-generation restaurateur born and raised in the South Cariboo. The kitchen turns out chef-prepared food made fresh daily — spanning creative small plates, burgers, mains, and pasta — alongside what the restaurant bills as the largest selection of BC craft beers on tap in town. It is a community-rooted, full-service stop for cyclists seeking a quality sit-down meal in the Cariboo interior.
fcb93507bb: The Jolly Coachman is a long-standing neighbourhood pub and liquor store nestled in Pitt Meadows, serving the community with daily food specials, craft beer on tap, and a happy hour menu. It has a community-focused identity with Lions Club ties, meat draws, and local fundraisers. A touring cyclist passing through the Pitt Meadows area would find a full sit-down pub menu alongside an attached liquor store.
6051e4042c: MNT Takao Café is a café located at 1265 Ironwood Street on Vancouver Island, in the Campbell River area. The name suggests a Japanese-influenced theme, and the unit address indicates a multi-tenant commercial setting. Touring cyclists passing through the area may find it a useful stop for refreshments.
666aa4a1fd: Chez Joe Poutine is a French-Canadian inspired poutine restaurant in Sun Peaks, BC, opened in 2017 by Suzanne, a Quebec transplant who set out to recreate authentic Quebecois poutine on the west coast. The menu spans classic and specialty poutines, grill items (burgers, smokies, hot dogs, chicken tenders), and ice cream, with an unusually inclusive range of gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian adaptations. For a touring cyclist arriving at Sun Peaks, it offers a calorie-dense, customizable hot meal in a casual counter-service setting.
311f9beae0: Pescadores Bistro is a walk-in-only brunch and lunch restaurant in Port Alberni, perched across from the Alberni Inlet and Marina with a landscaped outdoor patio where wildlife sightings are common. The menu ranges from eggs benedict and omelettes to fish tacos and fresh-ground beef burgers, with vegan and gluten-free options throughout. It sits on the main highway corridor to Tofino, positioning it as a natural midpoint fuel stop for cyclists heading to the Pacific coast.
5ea83efe8a: A café in the Vancouver Island & Gulf Islands region. Details about current operations and amenities could not be verified due to website access issues.
38ca3d2deb: Flying Saucers is a tea and coffee bar on Cowrie Street. It offers hot and cold beverages to the community. Like many cafes, it provides a place for cyclists to stop and refresh.
2f9f046e81: Rusty Iron Coffee Co. is a community-oriented coffee shop in 108 Mile Ranch run by co-owners Ryan and Nathania, built around the philosophy that good coffee brings people together. The café offers a full menu of specialty espresso drinks, iced beverages, breakfast and lunch wraps, and housemade baked goods, sourcing beans from Smoking Gun Coffee Roasters in Abbotsford. Cyclists travelling the Cariboo corridor will find a welcoming, wheelchair-accessible stop for hot or cold drinks, light meals, and branded merchandise including retail coffee beans and insulated mugs.
c7302048c9: J & V Restaurant is a Chinese cuisine kitchen in Castlegar serving an extensive menu of Cantonese and Szechuan classics — from wonton soup and chow mein to Szechuan prawns and dry garlic pork. The business operates exclusively as drive-through pickup with no dine-in or delivery, making it a quick stop for touring cyclists passing through the Castlegar area. Catering is also available on request.
8d2411c6d2: Juice Five O is a Vietnamese food restaurant located inside the Kruk Centre for Performing Arts in Dawson Creek, in BC's Peace Region. The menu centres on traditional Vietnamese dishes such as pho, vermicelli noodles (bun), and curry chicken, with an emphasis on fresh ingredients and house-made preparations. Takeout and delivery are available alongside a drink menu that includes bubble tea, smoothies, and coffee.
89c6163cf4: Pho Galaxy is a Vietnamese restaurant in Langley, BC, specializing in traditional pho, rice dishes, vermicelli bowls, and fresh appetizers made with premium ingredients. The warm, family-friendly dining room and a dedicated vegetarian pho menu make it a welcoming stop for cyclists with varied dietary needs. Online ordering and pickup are available for those who prefer a quick grab-and-go meal.
9ee632c9ec: Kershaw's Cafe is a small cafe situated in Atlin, one of British Columbia's most remote communities near the Yukon border, accessible primarily via a long gravel road. The cafe operates on a limited weekly schedule with outdoor seating, making it a rare sit-down stop for cyclists undertaking the demanding Atlin region routes. For touring cyclists venturing this far north, it likely represents one of very few food service options in this off-the-grid destination.
3249d2a5a3: Tod Mountain Cafe is a mountain-inspired café in Sun Peaks village serving ethically sourced, small-batch roasted coffee alongside an all-day breakfast menu of crêpes, bagel sandwiches, burritos, and avocado toast. The café emphasizes locally sourced seasonal ingredients and describes a warm, comfortable atmosphere suited to refueling after outdoor adventure. It is a natural stop for cyclists passing through or based at Sun Peaks Resort.
e8da49dfc1: The Beach Hut is a fast-food kiosk or counter-service eatery located on Marine Avenue in Powell River, BC, with its Facebook identity tied to Willingdon Beach — a popular stop along the Sunshine Coast. Its beachside setting makes it a natural rest point for cyclists riding the Powell River stretch of the Sunshine Coast route.
6693aaf011: Lost Boys Café is a mountaintop restaurant perched at 5662ft (1726m) at Fernie Alpine Resort, accessible via the Timber Express Chairlift. It offers full meals, snacks, and Starbucks coffee alongside panoramic views of the Elk Valley. The café is fully licensed and operates as part of the resort's ski and bike park seasons.
5a75ebcb56: The Bull Wheel is a restaurant operating within Big White Ski Resort, a large mountain resort located east of Kelowna in BC's Okanagan Highlands. The resort offers both winter ski and summer seasons, including guided eBike tours, making the restaurant a potential stop for cyclists accessing the mountain. Sitting at elevation in the resort village, it is part of a full-service dining lineup for resort guests.
1c2ed44c0f: Q's Restaurant is a Korean and Japanese fusion dining room in Golden, BC, established in 2017 and situated along the Trans-Canada corridor. The menu spans Korean BBQ, sushi rolls, ramen, udon, and Pad Thai, with an emphasis on locally sourced vegetables and seafood and house-made sauces. For touring cyclists riding the Kootenay or Columbia Valley routes, it offers a full sit-down meal with vegetarian and tofu options in a warm indoor setting.
a9a1c1f79e: Stikine River Song Cafe & Lodge occupies the historic Hudson's Bay Trading Post in Telegraph Creek, one of BC's most remote communities deep in Tāłtān Territory, accessible via a long gravel road from Dease Lake. The café is celebrated locally and by travellers for hearty homemade meals and freshly baked pies, and doubles as the community gathering place. The same building holds nine renovated lodge rooms — some with kitchenettes — making it a rare full-service stop for cyclists undertaking wilderness expeditions in the upper Stikine River corridor.
bda2ae2ff9: Pizzarama Pizza is a pizza takeout and delivery shop in the Nechako Centre mall in Kitimat, BC, currently transitioning its brand to Canadian2for1Pizza. For cyclists on the north coast route, Kitimat sits at the head of the Douglas Channel and this shop offers a convenient hot meal stop in the town centre. Online ordering is available alongside in-person service.
24b278628d: Costa del Sol is a Mexican and Latin restaurant occupying a beautifully converted early 1900s Powell River police station, featuring authentic talavera tile work, original stained glass art, and a vibrant Mexican colour palette with local art on display. Part of the Point Group Hospitality group, it serves fresh, locally-sourced Mexican and Latin dishes along Powell River's downtown marine mile — a natural landmark stop on BC's Sunshine Coast cycling corridor.
7333e07bc8: Ice cream shop in Coombs, BC. A casual refreshment stop for touring cyclists passing through Vancouver Island.
7c5cf8ba6c: Hungry Herbie's is a Cache Creek institution that has been serving made-to-order burgers, hand-cut fries, and fried chicken on the Cariboo Highway since 1957. Home of the famous MONSTERBURGER™, the restaurant built its reputation by resisting the shortcuts of chain fast food — buns are baked fresh and fries are cut in-house daily. Sitting directly on the main highway through town, it is a well-regarded and long-standing refueling stop for travellers along this busy cycling corridor.
d3794edcce: Roots Rising Bakery is a 100% gluten-free bakehouse on the North Island Highway in Courtenay, founded by a chef whose personal health journey led her to specialize in food as medicine. The bakery produces artisan breads, pastries, and cakes across three distinct lines — Rising Roots, Primal Roots (keto/paleo/diabetic-friendly), and Wild Roots (vegan sourdough) — making it a rare stop catering to cyclists with celiac disease, dairy intolerances, and other dietary restrictions. Products are also stocked at a number of local Courtenay-area cafes and restaurants.
82b9219a7a: Blacksmith Bakery is an artisan bakery and licensed café-bistro chain founded in 2014 by Chef Stephan Schigas, whose career included heading the pastry kitchen at London's Michelin-starred Zafferano. The original Fort Langley location occupies the historic site of Reid's Blacksmith Shop (circa 1910), giving the brand its name and a strong sense of local character. With four locations across Fort Langley, Langley, and Maple Ridge, it offers European-style pastries, brunch, and bistro fare — a solid food stop for cyclists moving through the Fraser Valley.
b044906b45: Pot Stickers 'n' Curry is a family-run Indo-Tibetan takeout restaurant in Campbell River, helmed by Chef Narayan, who brings 30 years of Asian cooking experience from across the world, and his wife Sama, who hand-rolls every potsticker and samosa from scratch. The menu spans Himalayan dumplings (momos and potstickers), chow mein, curries, noodle soups with house-made broth, and sides like garlic naan and samosas. It is a distinctive and affordable stop offering multiple vegan dishes alongside meat options.
b99e57e0a9: Gateway Grill is a casual, relaxed dining restaurant established in 2011 and located within the Quality Inn & Suites in Clearwater, BC. The restaurant actively courts tour groups, offering catering packages for breakfast, lunch, dinner, and meals to go, plus two private rooms seating up to 50 guests. Its position inside a hotel property makes it a convenient and group-ready dining stop for cyclists moving through the Clearwater corridor.

bf2a8b9296: Sacred Mountain Lavender is a boutique lavender farm established in 2001 on the southern slopes of Mount Tuam near Fulford Harbour, Salt Spring Island, growing over 60 varieties of lavender organically across 2.5 acres. The farm distills its own essential oils on-site and produces a range of handcrafted culinary and spa products. Visiting cyclists can take a self-guided tour of the lavender fields, drying room, and distillation equipment, and browse the seasonal farm shop for locally made lavender goods.
b3027208a7: Nutritionally Organics & Wellness Market is a health food and supplement store carrying organic groceries, sports nutrition, electrolytes, herbal products, and wellness supplements. The shop stocks cyclist-relevant products such as Nuun electrolyte tablets and a wide range of amino acids, proteins, and recovery aids. A 'Locations' page suggests at least one physical retail presence, though the specific address was not captured in the fetched content.
91864746e8: Seasons Farm Market is a barn-based farm market in Abbotsford's agricultural corridor, stocking local free-range eggs, fresh dairy, garden produce, baked goods, and quality cuts of meat. The market emphasizes ethically raised, sustainable, and locally sourced food, and positions itself as a community gathering spot as much as a grocery stop. For a touring cyclist passing through the Fraser Valley farmland, it offers a genuine farm-fresh resupply point.
002ea6c865: G & R Ginseng Trading Ltd (養生堂 — 'Health Preservation Hall') is a Richmond-based specialty retailer focused on premium ginseng varieties, dried seafood (abalone, sea cucumber, fish maw, scallop), bird's nest, Korean red ginseng, and a broad range of Traditional Chinese Medicine products. The store offers both in-person and online shopping with delivery, serving Metro Vancouver's Chinese-Canadian community. A touring cyclist passing through Richmond's Capstan Way shopping area could find specialty health supplements and some dry-goods groceries, though the product range skews toward high-value culinary and medicinal items rather than everyday cycling supplies.
35a3840974: Red Cliff Farm is a small organic farm on the outskirts of Kamloops selling farm-fresh eggs and organically grown vegetables, including garlic varieties such as Red Russian and Music. The farm is home to free-ranging chickens and operates as a direct-to-consumer farm stand. Notably, it accepts Bitcoin payments via Lightning and on-chain, making it an unusual and locally distinctive stop for cyclists seeking fresh, organic food.
a91a9d7078: Buckerfield's is BC's original country store, founded in 1919 and now operating ten locations across the province, with the Duncan store also serving as the company's head office. The large-format store carries farm and livestock supplies, pet products, garden centre items, wild bird feed, and outdoor clothing — a useful one-stop rural retailer on the Trans-Canada Highway corridor. The store is wheelchair-friendly, pet-friendly, and publicly accessible with free parking.
1c6ba225a1: Brightside Blueberries & Such is a small veganic farm stand in the Cowichan Valley near Duncan, selling blueberries, produce, seeds, fruits, and nuts directly from the farm. The operation proudly bypasses retail middlemen entirely, with customers buying straight from the roadside stand. A cyclist passing through the valley in summer can expect seasonal BC-grown blueberries and other veganic farm goods.
cc407ff3fb: Play is Kelowna's premium athletic footwear and apparel specialty store, focused on running, training, hiking, and lifestyle products from top brands including Salomon, HOKA, On, Brooks, Patagonia, and Arc'teryx. Located at Harvey Avenue and Spall Road, the shop stocks a wide range of performance gear including nutrition products (Tailwind, Skratch Labs, Maurten), hydration vests, and accessories relevant to endurance athletes. They also host a Play Run Club, making them a community hub for active locals and visiting athletes.
4d2adb93a8: Monster Vineyards is a boutique winery in Penticton that playfully debunks the Ogopogo legend of Lake Okanagan, celebrating the imaginative contraptions people might have built to fake the mythical creature. Winemaker Stefan Arnason sources grapes from select Okanagan vineyards to produce bold, fruit-forward wines available through an on-site tasting room and wine shop. A patio is referenced in the photo gallery, making it a potential rest stop for cyclists exploring the South Okanagan wine route.
1ec09d89d5: Sunset Farm is a 45-year-old working sheep farm run by Sandy Robley on Salt Spring Island's Sunset Drive, spanning over 300 acres of owned and leased Gulf Islands pasture. The farm shop offers farm-fresh eggs, island lamb, and chicken alongside a wide selection of wool goods including yarns, blankets, sheepskins, and handmade crafts. The farm has a notable history of supplying lamb for Queen Elizabeth's visit to Victoria in the 1980s.
bf082cc4a3: Dickinson Family Farm is an RV campground set within a cherry orchard in Summerland, offering U-pick cherries across six varieties each July. The sites sit among the trees in a quiet, green setting with no concrete — a contrast to typical campgrounds. Touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan during cherry season can pick fruit directly from the trees alongside RV guests.
4fbd483e1a: Charlie Brown's Health Foods is a family-owned local institution in Nanaimo, operating since 1971 and voted Best Health Food Store in the area. Located in a unit at 1533 Estevan Rd, it offers alternative and holistic health products and groceries. Touring cyclists looking to stock up on natural foods or specialty health items in Nanaimo will find this a long-established community staple.
ff862c299d: Granny's is an iconic fruit stand and bakery just off Highway 97 in Summerland, celebrating the Okanagan with locally sourced ingredients and homemade baked goods. The shop leans into a nostalgic 1950s–60s atmosphere, complete with antiques and a working 1961 Nordemende radio playing golden oldies. Cyclists on the Okanagan highway corridor will find fresh espresso, sandwiches, waffles, and locally roasted coffee waiting for them.
c2e57116a9: Docksteader Source for Sports is an independently owned member of the national Source for Sports buying group, with over 150 affiliated stores across Canada. Located in Surrey on King George Boulevard, it specializes in hockey, baseball, softball, lacrosse, racquet sports, inline skating, and team merchandise, along with equipment services like skate sharpening, racquet stringing, and glove repair. Touring cyclists may find athletic apparel, footwear, and hydration products here, but the store does not appear to stock cycling-specific equipment or offer bike repair services.
ad569a0f95: Sport Chek is a major Canadian sports retail chain with a Penticton location on Skaha Lake Road, stocking a broad range of sporting goods including cycling gear, apparel, and footwear. As one of the larger sports retailers in the region, it may carry bike accessories and parts that a touring cyclist could source in a pinch. The chain's website references a 'Sports Equipment Servicing' section, suggesting some in-store service capability beyond pure retail.
1d2488027f: Now operating as Pomme Natural Market Duncan after joining the Pomme chain, this natural and organic grocery store sits on the Trans-Canada Highway in Duncan, making it a convenient stop for cyclists travelling the Cowichan Valley corridor. The store emphasizes local and organic products, weekly produce specials, and a community-oriented ethos with long-standing staff continuity through the rebrand.
a19cdf45a2: Adidas is a global sportswear brand with a retail location on Burrard Street in downtown Vancouver. The store carries Adidas apparel, footwear, and accessories across a range of sports. A touring cyclist passing through might find running shoes, base layers, or casual athletic wear here, but should not expect dedicated cycling or bike-service offerings.
2f3a239e8d: Don-O-Ray Farms is a family-owned farm market in Kelowna's Lower Mission with over 20 years of operation, growing and selling fresh-picked fruit, vegetables, and herbs including standout items like giant peaches, sweet corn, and purple cauliflower. Alongside fresh produce, the farm offers its Nature's Kitchen line of prepared products — jams, hot sauces, spice blends, and homemade pies — available for online order with farm pickup year-round. The full in-person market is open through the core of the cycling season, making it a practical fresh-food stop for riders touring the Okanagan.
5438567ef3: Gulraj Farm is a family-operated blueberry farm in Tsawwassen run by Bainsdavinder and Nirlep. As a direct-sales farm shop, it offers cyclists on the South Delta route a chance to pick up fresh local blueberries close to the Tsawwassen ferry terminal area. Farm stands like this are classic touring stops for fresh, locally grown produce.
3c8a3214fc: Duck Creek Farm is a 13-acre family farm on Salt Spring Island that has operated since 1990, growing over 30 varieties of fruits and vegetables using organic, no-till, and non-chemical permaculture practices. The farm sells directly to cyclists and visitors via an on-farm farmstand, a seasonal on-farm Friday market, and the Tuesday market at Centennial Park in town. The property also stewards a salmon enhancement creek, and on any given visit you may encounter eagles, turtles, or beavers alongside the market garden.
cd0280c228: Urban Farm Market is a fruit and vegetable store located on Westminster Highway in Richmond, BC. It operates as a small farm-market format shop, the kind of stop a touring cyclist might seek out for fresh produce along a route. Its social media presence is minimal and has seen little activity since 2022.
c2c6bdd432: Mountain Warehouse is a UK-based outdoor gear chain that designs and sells its own exclusive branded products, positioning itself as a lower-cost alternative to multi-brand outdoor retailers. The Kelowna location sits inside Orchard Park Shopping Centre, a large regional mall on Harvey Avenue. Touring cyclists may find general outdoor clothing, footwear, and camping accessories here, though it is not a dedicated cycling or bike service shop.
fe27933e24: Maan Farms is a multi-generational family farm in Abbotsford's Fraser Valley offering U-pick and pre-picked strawberries, raspberries, and blueberries alongside an award-winning estate winery that produces berry wines entirely from fruit grown on the property. Founded in 1977, the farm has grown from a roadside stand into a full agritourism destination featuring a Country Market, barnyard animals, a corn maze, goat yoga, and a restored heritage barn. For touring cyclists, it is a distinctive Fraser Valley stop to stock up on fresh local berries in season.
33ed49daf1: Sport Chek is one of Canada's largest sporting goods retail chains, operated by Canadian Tire, carrying a broad range of athletic clothing, footwear, and equipment. This Vancouver Broadway location sits at Broadway and Ontario Street in a well-trafficked urban area. Touring cyclists may find helmets, cycling apparel, hydration gear, and basic accessories, though it is not a dedicated bike shop.
4c4c4e29e7: Sport Chek is Canada's largest national sporting goods chain, with this location inside the Sevenoaks Shopping Centre in Chilliwack. The store carries a broad range of outdoor and athletic gear, and OSM notes bicycle sales on-site. Touring cyclists passing through Chilliwack may find it useful for basic supplies, cycling apparel, and potentially bike-related accessories.
9bb897f491: JoieFarm is an estate winery perched on the Naramata Bench with vineyards spread across the South Okanagan, one of BC's most celebrated cycling wine routes. The property features a tasting room and The Hot Dog Lounge, offering visiting cyclists a place to sample wines and grab a bite alongside the vines. The winery positions itself as a pursuer of 'West Coast wonder and beauty,' crafting small-lot, terroir-driven wines from its estate vineyards.
95a0077451: A family-run, year-round farm market on Clayburn Road in Abbotsford featuring a full-service butcher shop, in-season local produce, and farm-to-table products. They have an on-site cafe and a culinary team preparing ready-made meals — ideal for a touring cyclist looking to restock with quality local food. Part of the Fraser Valley Circle Farm Tour self-guided route.
523a565d02: Best Choice Blueberry Farm is a family-run u-pick and pre-picked blueberry farm on the Tsawwassen/Delta agricultural flats, open seasonally from July through early September. Cyclists can hand-pick fresh blueberries straight from the field or buy pre-packed boxes and organic garlic on-site, with no reservations or entry fee required. The farm is cash-only and is well-regarded by repeat local visitors for its large, sweet berries.
36e0e26dcf: Mt. Waddington's Outdoors is a backcountry equipment retailer with stores in Chilliwack and Whistler, carrying premium outdoor gear across camping, hiking, climbing, paddling, and snow sports. The shop stocks high-end brands such as Arc'teryx, Blue Ice, Alpacka, and NRS, and offers gear-fitting, repair, and consultation services. A touring cyclist passing through Chilliwack may find useful camp and hiking consumables here, though no dedicated cycling section is evident.
5662bd9e61: Mi Tierra Latina (listed in OSM as My Latin American Grocery Store) is a specialty Latin American grocery stocking authentic products from nine countries — Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, El Salvador, Guatemala, Mexico, Peru, and Venezuela. The store carries a broad range of packaged goods including beverages, sauces, corn and bean products, frozen food, snacks, and spices. A touring cyclist passing through North Vancouver could use it as a food resupply point for specialty and everyday pantry staples.
11bdfdc6bf: Natural Focus is a natural health products retailer that has been operating for 30 years, starting on Hastings Street in Burnaby and now based in Surrey. The store carries a broad selection of vitamins, supplements, protein, herbal products, and natural grocery items, available both in-store and online. A touring cyclist passing through could pick up natural snacks, protein supplements, and wellness staples from a well-stocked specialty health shop.
505a9e8d4c: Time Out Source for Sports is a North Vancouver sporting goods store specializing in hockey equipment — sticks, skates, protective gear, and goalie equipment from Bauer, CCM, True, and Warrior — alongside baseball, soccer, football, and inline hockey gear. The store also serves a number of local teams and associations on the North Shore. No cycling products, bike repairs, or cycling-related services are mentioned anywhere on the website.
56cb2aaeff: North End Farm is a small organic farm stand on Salt Spring Island offering fresh vegetables, fruits, meats, bread, pies, and treats, alongside products from other local island producers. It operates on a self-serve honour system — customers pay via cash box or e-transfer — making it a relaxed and characterful stop. For touring cyclists, it's a genuine source of fresh, local food in a community known for its agricultural identity.
580f95ddd5: Strathcona Beer Company is a craft brewery and taproom anchored in Vancouver's oldest residential neighbourhood, housed in a purpose-built 12,000 square foot facility that includes a 25-hectolitre brewhouse with five fermenters and five brite tanks — every pint poured is brewed on site. The 67-seat tasting room serves a rotating lineup spanning classic international styles like Premium Pilsner, Belgian Golden Ale, and British IPA alongside seasonal specialties and cask brews. A gourmet pizza kitchen and retail area selling exclusive apparel make it a natural stop for cyclists exploring the Strathcona area of East Vancouver.
6780b20976: Coastal Olive Oils Co. is a family-owned specialty tasting room in Tsawwassen that stocks around 40 extra virgin, fused, and infused olive oils alongside balsamic vinegars sourced from Modena, Italy. Customers are invited to sample before buying, giving it the feel of a curated food-experience shop rather than a grocery. The shop also carries artisanal Pappardelle's pasta and offers home delivery to Tsawwassen and Ladner.
94f1ced61f: Bench 1775 is an award-winning winery on a 30-acre waterfront estate along Naramata Road — one of BC's most celebrated cycling routes — with sweeping 180-degree views over Okanagan Lake. The winery produces whites, reds, rosés, and icewines across multiple Okanagan and Similkameen Valley vineyards, and operates the Bench Patio Bistro, described by prominent critic Anthony Gismondi as 'the best patio in the world.' Cyclists riding the Naramata Bench pass directly by this destination winery, which offers tastings, retail wine purchases, and full patio dining.
8bfcb4a2b7: JM Fruit And Veg. Market is a farm-stand style produce market on Douglas Road in West Kelowna, selling fresh local fruit and vegetables including BC cherries in season. It operates as a small independent roadside market typical of the Okanagan region, where farm-direct produce stops are a staple of cycling routes through the valley. Touring cyclists passing through West Kelowna can expect fresh local produce but should not count on other services.
eb83761681: Hofstede's Country Barn is a well-established farm market in Chilliwack offering locally sourced produce from Okanagan growers, a full deli with nitrate-free meats and cheeses, and an in-house bakery turning out fresh buns, breads, and pastries daily. The on-site cafe serves hot sandwiches, salads, and rotating homemade soups, making it a genuine resupply destination in the Fraser Valley rather than a convenience stop. The store also stocks a broad selection of European specialty groceries, organic items, and gluten-free products.
6264ee9582: Sport Chek is Canada's largest sporting goods chain, stocking a wide range of athletic clothing, footwear, and outdoor equipment. This North Vancouver location is part of an indoor retail complex and would carry cycling accessories, apparel, and potentially bikes as part of its broad sporting goods inventory. Touring cyclists passing through may find helmets, tubes, and gear essentials here even without a dedicated bike service department.
e65bf3da4c: The Hatch is a quirky, art-infused winery tasting room in West Kelowna, part of the Jason Parkes Customs collective of Okanagan wine venues. It leans into irreverence — eccentric label art, eclectic wine series, and a deliberately offbeat atmosphere that blends a working cellar with a creative hangout. Touring cyclists on Boucherie Road can book a flight of five wines in advance or walk in when space allows.
2bd6064ccd: Bates Beach Farm is a small family-run farm market in the Comox Valley, situated beside Seal Bay Regional Park on Vancouver Island's east coast. It exploits an ocean-influenced microclimate to grow standout berries, tomatoes, garlic, and peppers, with a declared focus on Mediterranean-style produce. In addition to fresh seasonal fruit and vegetables, the market carries house-made frozen soups and fresh salsas, and also hosts a booth at the Comox Valley Farmers Market.
14dd4d1f33: Sport Chek at Metropolis @ Metrotown is a large-format Canadian sporting goods chain located inside one of BC's busiest shopping malls in Burnaby. The store carries bikes, cycling apparel, and accessories across multiple sport categories, and the chain operates an equipment servicing program at many locations. For a touring cyclist, it is a useful stop for gear, clothing, and possibly basic parts in an otherwise commercially dense area.
97ae1c8be4: Great Mountain Ginseng is a specialty Chinese health food retailer focused on Canadian (American) ginseng, bird's nest, sea cucumber, and traditional Chinese herbal medicines, operating both an e-commerce store and a physical retail location in Richmond. The store is housed inside a shopping complex and offers in-store pickup alongside online orders. Touring cyclists could find dried goods, snack foods, specialty hot drink powders, and a range of health-focused food items here.
370b4bd054: A certified organic vegetable farm in South Delta growing more than forty varieties of produce. They operate a farm stand for most of the year and also sell bedding plants and organic seedlings. A good stop for touring cyclists looking for fresh, locally grown food near the Tsawwassen ferry terminal area.
cf6894f0e7: The Egg Store is a family-owned farm retail shop selling farm-fresh eggs picked daily and brought directly from local farms. It carries multiple varieties including freerange, organic, double yolkers, and enriched white eggs in bulk and by the dozen. A standout feature for passing cyclists is the on-site 'Eggspress' egg vending machine, stocked daily with fresh eggs for after-hours purchases.
6de8c57397: Surrey Farms is a family-operated farm market established in 1989, now farming over 400 acres and operating two retail locations in Surrey. The business is best known for its exceptional fresh berries—strawberries, blueberries, raspberries, and blackberries—alongside seasonal Okanagan fruit and local vegetables. The popular U-Pick fields draw visitors from across the Lower Mainland, making this a distinctive stop for cyclists seeking fresh, locally grown produce.
6bf52b6585: Brightside Eggs is a third-generation family farm in Chilliwack producing certified-organic, cage-free, free-range eggs audited annually by ECO-CERT Canada. The farm operates 'The Egg Shack,' a self-serve on-site vending machine where visitors can purchase hand-sorted, ungraded eggs in recyclable cartons at any time without needing cash. A stop here offers touring cyclists a direct connection to Fraser Valley agricultural heritage and a genuinely local food purchase.
18b46fb9da: Red Roof Family Farm is a farm-direct shop in Lake Country, situated in the Okanagan fruit-belt corridor popular with touring cyclists. OSM tags it as a farm shop, suggesting seasonal produce and farm goods. Its roadside location on Okanagan Centre Road would make it a natural stop on regional cycling routes, but current operating status is uncertain.
5e1c7015cb: Seek & Surf is a husband-and-wife-run surf and skate shop on Sooke Road, anchoring the Juan de Fuca Strait surf community with surfboards, wetsuits, fins, and a curated selection of outdoor lifestyle goods. Founded by Mike and Cas, the shop positions itself as an inclusive gathering place for outdoor enthusiasts rather than a purely transactional retailer. Touring cyclists passing through Sooke may find it worth a stop for dry bags, sun care products, footwear, or simply a welcoming local vibe.
e1db17c20d: MEC (Mountain Equipment Company) is one of Canada's largest outdoor retailers, operating a location in Kelowna. As a full-service outdoor shop, it typically carries a broad range of cycling gear, apparel, and accessories suited to touring and adventure cyclists. The Kelowna store serves the broader Okanagan cycling community in a region known for its extensive trail networks and long-distance touring routes.
bbec830e38: Meridian Farm Market is a Lower Mainland farm market chain emphasizing locally sourced, farm-fresh products including grass-fed and free-range meats, seasonal produce, artisan baked goods, deli items, and a full range of pantry staples. The market positions itself on BC-local sourcing and craft quality, making it a well-stocked resupply stop beyond a typical convenience store. Multiple physical locations operate across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver region.
d45f20fc59: 12 Baskets Nutrition & Health Co is a natural health and supplement retailer in Richmond, BC, stocking an extensive lineup of vitamins, herbs, probiotics, homeopathic remedies, and natural beauty products from dozens of Canadian and international brands. The store also carries a food section with superfoods, dried fruits, nuts, seeds, natural condiments, and manuka honey — useful resupply items for a touring cyclist. It operates both a physical retail location and an active online store with Canada-wide shipping.
15f611aacc: Sea Dog Farm is a 5-acre certified organic operation in Sidney, BC growing a wide variety of fruits, vegetables, berries, herbs, cut flowers, and free-range eggs. The Centennial Park Farmstand sits at the south end of the property beside a trail in Centennial Park, offering direct farm-to-consumer sales. A live stand cam on the website lets visitors check what is currently stocked before making the trip.
4c3f1cc99f: Rockweld Farm is a family-owned ethical chicken and egg operation run by Tim and Flo Rempel, featuring an on-farm store in Abbotsford's agricultural heartland. The store sells free-roam, non-medicated chicken in a remarkable range of forms — whole birds, cuts, sausages, pot pies, smoked meats, and bone stock — alongside organic beef, cheese, assorted fish, and locally grown frozen berries. Cyclists passing through the Fraser Valley farm country will find a genuine farm-direct stop with an unusually broad selection of locally sourced foods.
fa3226ce08: Fruition Farm Stand is a family-run roadside farm stand on the south end of Quadra Island, operated by the Greenland family since 2021, offering sustainably grown vegetables, small fruits (blueberries, raspberries, blackberries, cherries), garlic, and free-range eggs. The farm uses low- to no-till practices with no synthetic fertilizers or pesticides and has a completed Environmental Farm Plan. Cyclists exploring Quadra Island can stop at this working farm for a genuine local produce pickup just steps from the fields.
a20659378b: JX Campground and Surf Shop is a campground, surf rental, and e-bike rental hub sitting on the Tofino-Ucluelet Highway on Vancouver Island's rugged west coast. The property hosts T-Bird E-bike Rentals for exploring the surrounding Yuułuʔiłʔatḥ First Nation territory, alongside tent and RV campsites and multiple on-site food trucks. It offers a convenient overnight and resupply stop for touring cyclists riding the Pacific Rim corridor.
ff2b0b1a6c: Mountain Equipment Company (MEC) is a major Canadian outdoor retailer operating from a four-storey retail building in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood at 111 East 2nd Avenue. The brand — widely known by its short name MEC — has long been a destination for cyclists and outdoor enthusiasts seeking gear, apparel, and equipment. Its central Vancouver location places it within reach of cyclists arriving in or transiting through the city.
3c41f5e763: Valhalla Pure Outfitters Nelson has been serving the outdoor community since 1996 and is part of a BC-wide chain billing itself as 'Canada's Mountain Sports Specialists.' The Nelson location carries gear for backcountry skiing, avalanche safety, split boards, snowshoeing, hiking, and camping, with a focus on tested, quality brands. Touring cyclists passing through Nelson may find general outdoor apparel and gear, though bike-specific services are not confirmed at this location.
93e20d61fe: Body Energy Club is a Vancouver-born health food chain founded in 2002, offering sports supplements, vitamins, energy gels, electrolytes, protein bars, and a smoothie and cold-pressed juice bar. The Waterfront Station location is tucked inside one of Vancouver's busiest transit hubs at the edge of the seawall cycling network. Cyclists can stock up on ride nutrition — gels, electrolytes, and snacks — or grab a smoothie or healthy to-go meal before or after a ride.
d235738a5b: See Ya Later Ranch is a historic winery and bistro perched high atop Hawthorne Mountain above Okanagan Falls, with roots going back to 1920 when founder Major Hugh Fraser planted the first vines. It is one of the highest-elevation vineyards in the Okanagan Valley and holds the largest planting of Gewürztraminer in North America across 65 acres. Touring cyclists who make the climb are rewarded with award-winning tastings, a valley-view bistro, and a lively events calendar including a Pride celebration.
6c03b0ba7c: A family-run farm market operating since 1980 on King Road in Abbotsford, the Berry Barn is the produce and berry arm of Neufeld Farm Market. They grow their own strawberries, raspberries, blackberries, and blueberries on-site, hand-picked daily in season, and also stock Okanagan fruit, everyday produce, meats, seafood, and soft ice cream. A touring cyclist passing through the Fraser Valley can load up on fresh local fruit and staple groceries here.
bb03be6629: Nature's Essence is a health food and natural products shop located inside a Richmond shopping centre, stocking a broad range of vitamins, supplements, and wellness brands alongside a modest food section (honey, proteins, teas, maple products). The store carries hundreds of brands spanning organic, vegan, and whole-food lines, making it a useful stop for cyclists seeking sports nutrition, electrolyte products, or natural snacks. It also offers beauty and body care, essential oils, and cleaning products.
c82b3c8e65: The Health Food Centre is a family-owned and operated health store that has served Dawson Creek for 49 years, making it a long-standing institution in this northern BC community. The store stocks a broad range of wellness products including supplements, bulk herbs, GF and vegan food options, aromatherapy, natural beauty care, and an in-store refillery station for eco-friendly household products. For touring cyclists passing through Dawson Creek, it offers a useful stop for specialty dietary staples and natural health supplies.
d70254ac14: Surrey Farms is a family-run operation founded in 1989 that has grown from a small roadside stand to over 400 acres, with two farm market locations in Surrey. The red Surrey Farms market on 152 Street is a longtime community landmark, known for exceptional fresh strawberries, blueberries, raspberries, and blackberries, as well as a broad selection of local fruits and vegetables. U-Pick berry fields are open to the public during the seasonal harvest and draw visitors from across the Lower Mainland.
abceefd619: Madrona Farm is a long-running organic farm at the foot of Mt. Doug, just minutes from downtown Victoria, operating under The Land Conservancy and selling freshly harvested produce at a roadside veggie stand. The farm grows over 105 varieties of vegetables and 35 varieties of fruit across all four seasons, with staff picking the morning of each market day and washing produce on-site. A touring cyclist would find an exceptional selection of fresh local vegetables and fruit in a working farm setting.
b70d8ffe94: Nature's Fare Markets is a BC-based health food grocery chain with a well-established Kelowna location staffed by more than 75 employees, some with over 20 years tenure. The store carries certified organic produce, zero-waste bulk goods, vitamins, supplements, and clean beauty products alongside ethically sourced meat and dairy. An on-site Bistro serves local, organic, and sustainable foods, and grab-and-go salads, smoothies, and kombucha on tap make it a practical resupply stop for touring cyclists.
c852e29ead: West Coast Natural Foods is a long-established health food store in Sooke serving the community since 1980. It carries organic and natural groceries including quality meat and fish alongside a broad range of vitamins, minerals, herbal remedies, and nutritional supplements from brands such as Natural Factors, Sisu, and Flora. For a touring cyclist passing through Sooke, it offers a compact resupply stop for whole foods and wellness products.
29696bbc27: New Generation Foods is a multicultural natural foods grocery store specializing in staple pantry items — flours, grains, beans, lentils, rice, spices, dried fruit, and nuts — sourced for Latin American, African, Middle Eastern, South Asian, and European communities. The store produces its own Kismet brand of bulk-style dry goods, with a strong emphasis on dietary-restriction-friendly flours (corn, rice, quinoa, sorghum, amaranth, oat, barley, teff). For a touring cyclist, it offers a practical resupply point for high-calorie, lightweight staples at what the store describes as competitive prices.
2e658f131a: Schoolhouse Farm is a small, woman-owned, family-run diversified farm in Ladner operating with no-spray, no-till, regenerative practices. Its farm store carries seasonally harvested vegetables, culinary and medicinal herbs, and cut flowers, plus a curated selection of third-party goods, accepting cash, card, and e-transfer. When fields are blooming, the farm also offers u-pick flower sessions in a working farm setting framed by willow trees and public seating.
2cfbdab411: Sparkes Corn Barn is a family-owned farm stand that has grown and sold fresh sweet corn in the Chilliwack area since 1998, operating a network of distinctive green-and-yellow drive-thru roadside barns across the Fraser Valley. All corn is non-GMO, picked fresh daily, and sold the same day directly from their own fields. During the summer harvest season, cyclists will also find locally grown strawberries, raspberries, and blueberries at the stands.
c84e89e99e: Dolson's Source For Sports is the Kamloops location of Canada's largest sports equipment buying group, Source For Sports. The store specializes in hockey, skiing, lacrosse, racquet sports, and outdoor recreation gear, offering a wide range of equipment services from skate sharpening to ski stone grinding. A touring cyclist might find athletic apparel, water bottles, hydration gear, and trail/hiking accessories here, but the store shows no dedicated cycling focus.
609b23776a: Sport Chek is a major Canadian sporting goods chain located inside Hillside Mall in Victoria. It operates an in-store Service Shop staffed by technicians who perform bike tune-ups and repairs, bookable online, by phone, or as walk-ins. As part of the Canadian Tire family of brands, it also stocks a broad range of cycling apparel, footwear, and accessories.
13481f6e94: Sunshine Coast Olive Oil Co. is an independent, family-owned gourmet food store in Gibsons specializing in award-winning single-estate and infused extra virgin olive oils and balsamic vinegars sourced with full farm-to-table traceability through direct farmer relationships. The shop carries oils certified to the Ultra Premium (UP) standard—the highest tier within the extra virgin category—alongside specialty groceries including crackers, olives, spreads, gourmet pasta, and condiments from BC, Greece, Italy, and Spain. It also operates an online store with in-store pickup, making it a distinctive artisan provisions stop on the Sunshine Coast.
97ee0ea998: Crooked Horn Farm is a certified organic vegetable farm in the Slocan Valley near Winlaw, BC, run by Gord and Ange. The farm offers seasonal CSA shares with weekly pickup options in the Slocan Valley and Nelson, providing fresh locally grown produce from late spring through fall. A touring cyclist riding through the rural Slocan corridor could find fresh organic vegetables here during the growing season.
1c333773d5: Sportstop Source for Sports is a member of Canada's largest sporting goods buying group (Source for Sports), located in the Crystal Lodge North Wing in Whistler Village. The shop carries sporting goods and sportswear serving the outdoor enthusiast community in one of BC's premier mountain resort destinations. A touring cyclist passing through may find outdoor apparel, accessories, and general sports gear here.
d53ba7c70a: Vitasave is an independently owned Canadian health supplement and natural wellness retailer that has been operating since 2010, now serving over a million customers across two Vancouver storefronts. The Robson Street location stocks 3,000+ vitamins, supplements, protein products, and grocery superfoods — all NPN-certified and third-party tested — and also offers a smoothie menu. For cyclists seeking to restock on nutritional or health-focused supplies mid-tour, it is one of the more comprehensive natural health shops on central Vancouver's main retail corridor.
c32c8d578a: A family-run farm market operating since the early 1980s on King Road in Abbotsford, rooted in a raspberry and chicken farm started by the Neufeld family in 1966. The market specializes in free-run, hormone-free chicken along with turkey, beef, pork, seafood, produce, berries, and local specialty items. They also operate The Berry Barn for seasonal produce and soft ice cream, and run a well-known community fundraising program.
0d8eb85127: Climb On Equipment is a specialty outdoor and technical climbing gear retailer in Vancouver, stocking a broad range of products for rock climbing, alpine climbing, ice climbing, work and rescue applications, and backcountry camping. The store carries harnesses, ropes, protection hardware, helmets, footwear, tents, sleep systems, and technical apparel from leading brands. Cycle tourists may find it useful for camping supplies and outdoor apparel, but it is not a bike shop.
0316e1cf4e: Haslam Creek Berry Farm is a certified organic U-pick blueberry operation on Rugby Road outside Nanaimo, offering two varieties of blueberries — Chandler and Draper — during the summer and early fall picking season. The farm operates on a seasonal schedule with weekend picking days during harvest, making it a potential detour for cyclists passing through the Nanaimo area seeking fresh local produce. Cash and e-transfer are the only accepted payment methods.
556d8dc380: Southlands Grange is a community-based farm and market district on the Tsawwassen peninsula anchored by a working community farm, a flower farm, and the Southlands Tsawwassen Farmers Market featuring fresh local produce, baked goods, and handmade goods from local growers. The campus surrounds an open-air Market Square beside an orchard, with a restored historic Red Barn, commissary kitchen, and nearby cafés and local shops. A touring cyclist arriving here encounters authentic Metro Vancouver working farmland alongside a lively, food-focused community hub.
af595573a7: Vancouver Island Refillery is a health food and refill shop on Wesley Street in Nanaimo, operating under a zero-waste, bring-your-own-container retail concept. The store has a membership program and an online shop, suggesting a community-oriented operation appealing to sustainability-minded shoppers. For touring cyclists, it represents a stop for health-oriented supplies in central Nanaimo.
095267b5c0: Evo Village Sports is a Whistler outpost of Evo, an outdoor and action-sports retailer known for cycling, snow sports, and related gear. Located in Whistler Village, it serves the resort's active clientele with equipment and apparel. Touring cyclists passing through Whistler may find it a useful stop for gear and supplies.
f8f28b5e9f: Running Room is a Canadian running-specialty chain carrying running footwear, performance apparel, and training accessories for men and women. The North Vancouver location is part of a national network founded on the philosophy of helping everyday runners improve. A touring cyclist might find nutrition products, socks, or moisture-wicking apparel here, but no cycling-specific services are offered.
73c50f814c: E.P. Orchards is a certified-organic farm shop on Bentley Road in Naramata, situated in the heart of the Okanagan's fruit-growing country. The operation offers self-harvesting (U-pick), making it a hands-on stop for cyclists exploring the Naramata Bench. It sells exclusively organic produce, a rarity along the route.
e5690dc5a5: 50th Parallel Estate is an award-winning Okanagan estate winery specializing in Pinot Noir and aromatic white wines, set in Lake Country along a popular cycling corridor between Kelowna and Vernon. The property includes the Block One fine-dining restaurant focused on regional-seasonal ingredients, wine caves open for exploration, and a tasting room with appointment and walk-in options. Event and wedding venues accommodate groups from 10 to 350 people, making it a notable destination stop on a multi-day Okanagan cycling tour.
15f55e8113: A long-running specialty food store (formerly Galloway's, dating back to the 1930s on Robson Street) now located in New Westminster. Stocks a large selection of spices, grains, coffee, ethnic foods, organic items, and gluten-free products not found in conventional grocery stores. Small and cozy with knowledgeable staff and a reputation as a destination shop for customers across the Lower Mainland.
f127849f51: BCB Honey Farm is a South Surrey farm store founded in 2003 by Dr. Tabari, who runs thousands of honeybee hives across the Lower Mainland and Peace River to support BC's pollination independence. The farm produces internationally award-winning raw honey — taking First Place at the 2019 International Honey Commission and a Quality Gold Award at the London Honey Quality Competition. Cyclists can stop in at the farm store or pull up to the drive-thru window to pick up locally produced honey and honey infusions.
d5ee2b99a4: A multi-generational family farm in Abbotsford operating since 1990, known for seasonal ticketed experiences including tulip gardens, pumpkin patches, and sunflower fields. They also run Taves Estate Cidery on-site and have a country store with farm products and u-pick apple fields. The farm sits on Gladwin Road in the Fraser Valley's agricultural lowlands.
a31dc7cdef: Purcell Outdoors is a compact 950-square-foot outdoor gear shop in downtown Kimberley's Platzl, stocking a wide range of brands for trail running, hiking, backpacking, and ski touring. Kimberley sits at the centre of extensive trail networks and is a stop on the Powder Highway, making this a natural resupply point for adventure travellers passing through. Staff are active endurance athletes with deep local knowledge of the surrounding Purcell Mountains terrain.
f4fc66ca9a: Gatzke Orchard is a four-generation family farm and fruit stand situated on the isthmus between Kalamalka and Wood Lakes in Oyama, operating each season with fresh cherries, raspberries, berries, house-made pies baked from a 1941 Grandma Gatzke recipe, and a range of locally-made value-added products. The farm also hosts Pedego Electric Bikes as a partner operation, positioning it as a natural hub for cyclists riding the Okanagan Valley Rail Trail. A wood-fired pizzeria (Pane Vino) operates on the property, making it a well-rounded stop for touring cyclists seeking fresh local food.
d4cb987580: Rewilding Roses is a small Roberts Creek operation combining a farm stand with a line of grass-fed tallow skincare products, organic meat, and handcrafted goods. The producer appears at the Sechelt Farmers Market and operates a roadside farm stand at their Joe Road property. 562914700c: H Mart (Hanahreum Mart) is a Canadian branch of a large Korean-founded supermarket chain specializing in Asian groceries, fresh produce, seafood, and specialty food items. The Richmond location sits within a shopping centre on Hazelbridge Way and serves the city's substantial Asian-Canadian community. Touring cyclists will find an extensive selection of packaged foods, fresh fruit, and pantry staples well suited for resupply.
fca5e1612b: A BC Liquor Store in West Vancouver.
4f9500e306: The Penticton Community Centre is a City of Penticton–operated public facility offering a pool and fitness room to residents and visitors in the South Okanagan. As a full-service municipal rec centre, it has the potential to serve touring cyclists needing showers or a place to freshen up mid-route. Penticton sits at the heart of several major cycling corridors including the Kettle Valley Rail Trail.
c9601903d1: The Goldstream Suspension Bridge is a striking pedestrian and cycling feature spanning a forested river gorge in the greater Goldstream/Sooke Hills wilderness area west of Victoria. It sits along a popular trail network managed by the Capital Regional District and serves as a scenic highlight on the Vancouver Crossing Loop route. Touring cyclists passing through the region frequently use it as a landmark waypoint amid old-growth Douglas fir and western red cedar.
30c356ea98: Chown Adult Centre is a community centre in Vancouver's east side serving adult residents with programming and shared facilities. As a publicly accessible community hub, it may offer basic amenities useful to touring cyclists passing through the neighbourhood. The centre is located near East 15th Avenue in a residential area of Vancouver.
360f063f38: Heritage Park Museum is a living history museum set on nearly 2 acres overlooking the City of Terrace, featuring several historical log buildings and artifacts drawn from across the region. Exhibits weave together themes of mining, telegraph lines, logging, pioneer life, and farming, representing the area's history up to 1950. The museum offers guided public tours, audio tours in English and French, and a full range of accessibility-focused options including wheelchair-accessible and sensory-friendly tours.
e2e2852944: Planet Bee is a working honey farm and meadery on the outskirts of Vernon, BC, where visitors can observe on-site beehives, stroll bee-friendly gardens, and sample honey and mead at the daily tasting bar — all free of charge. The farm produces Western Canada's largest curated selection of raw honey, bottled by hand on-site in the Okanagan Valley. Educational group presentations are offered seasonally, making it a genuinely engaging stop for curious travellers.
cac61faecc: West Richmond Community Centre is a City of Richmond–operated public recreation facility serving the western part of Richmond, BC. It is part of the city's municipal network of community centres delivering programs and activities for residents of all ages. Touring cyclists in the Richmond area may find it a useful urban waypoint, though specific cyclist-facing services are unconfirmed.
f36aa0974c: Historic Downtown Abbotsford is a walkable heritage neighbourhood established in 1891, sitting on the unceded territory of the Semá:th and Mathxwí First Nations and home to over 225 businesses including boutique retailers, award-winning restaurants, galleries, and murals. The Abbotsford Downtown Business Association manages a dedicated outdoor events space called Open Space and hosts seasonal festivals such as Berry Fest and Winter Jubilee. Touring cyclists will find a dense cluster of dining and shopping options within a compact, strollable footprint in the Fraser Valley.
dd223c7a15: The Fernie Aquatic Centre is a City of Fernie-operated indoor aquatic facility featuring a six-lane 25-metre competitive pool, a warm leisure pool for young children, a 25-person hot tub, and a steam room. The centre includes a full-service retail swimming boutique and a comprehensive suite of accessibility features including a pool lift and ramp access. A shower-only access option makes it a practical stop for touring cyclists wanting to freshen up mid-route.
58d35e9625: The Cowichan Lake branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library has served its community since informal services began in 1936, moving into a purpose-built facility in 2013. It holds a collection of more than 14,500 items and offers six public-access computers alongside free Wi-Fi. For touring cyclists passing through Lake Cowichan, it provides a welcoming public space to get online, rest, and access local resources.
f2fc23bd15: Bert Flinn Park is a nature reserve in Port Moody, BC, offering natural green space within an urban area. It is managed by the City of Port Moody and provides trail access through forested terrain. Touring cyclists passing through the Tri-Cities area may find it a worthwhile stop for a natural respite.
dd90af28b4: The Collingwood Branch is one of the Vancouver Public Library's neighbourhood locations, situated on the busy Kingsway corridor in East Vancouver. It occupies a two-storey retail building and serves the surrounding Collingwood and Renfrew communities with free public library services. For a touring cyclist, it offers a publicly accessible urban rest stop with the resources of a full library branch.
d3f325d0eb: The SS Naramata is a historic tugboat preserved at the S.S. Sicamous Marine Heritage Park on the Penticton waterfront, alongside the famous SS Sicamous sternwheeler and other Okanagan lake vessels. The park interprets over a century of inland marine transportation history in the Okanagan Valley, with connections to the Kettle Valley Railway era that cycling tourists on the KVR trail will find compelling. It is run by the S.S. Sicamous Marine Heritage Society, a volunteer-driven nonprofit dedicated to education and community outreach.
49c3149928: The Museum of the Cariboo-Chilcotin is a regional history museum in Williams Lake and the home of the BC Cowboy Hall of Fame, with exhibits spanning First Nations peoples, ranching and rodeo culture, railway history, mining, and forestry. The museum features rotating exhibitions including a powerful collection documenting the 2017 Cariboo Chilcotin wildfires. Located directly off Highway 97, it offers touring cyclists a rich cultural detour into the deep heritage of British Columbia's interior.
7236c6c916: Koksilah River Park is an undeveloped provincial park on southern Vancouver Island, tucked along the Koksilah River and Canyon about 7 km west of Shawnigan Lake within the Vancouver Island Forest Reserve. Visitors come for rustic hiking routes, river swimming, and canoeing or kayaking in a quiet forested setting with no crowds or developed infrastructure. Access is via Renfrew Road, a logging road off Shawnigan Lake Road, making it a scenic detour for touring cyclists exploring the Cowichan Valley.
591ab80704: Opened in 2023, the Aberdeen Tiny Library is only 352 square feet — the smallest branch in the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system — and is located inside a mall on the Trans-Canada Highway in southwest Kamloops. It is the first new library location in Kamloops since 1974, serving a rapidly growing part of the city. A touring cyclist passing through can access free Wi-Fi and library resources in a wheelchair-accessible, climate-controlled space.
30cbe6eba8: Kelowna Community Theatre is a municipally operated performing arts venue on the downtown Kelowna waterfront, hosting live theatre, concerts, and community events. It has its own Wikipedia entry (Wikidata Q14874642), reflecting its standing as a significant cultural landmark in the Okanagan. A touring cyclist exploring Kelowna's vibrant downtown would find it situated near the lakefront promenade.
074ffb83f6: Sunnyside Acres Urban Forest Park is a 140-hectare second-growth forest park in South Surrey, operated by the City of Surrey. The forest regenerated after logging in the early 1900s and is home to birds, coyotes, and black-tailed deer. Touring cyclists can explore a network of nature trails through this urban wilderness.
46683494cd: The Central Branch is the flagship location of the Greater Victoria Public Library system, situated in downtown Victoria. It houses the Heritage Room, a broad physical and digital collection, and public computer access, making it a genuine community hub. Touring cyclists passing through the city core may find it a convenient stop for connectivity and rest.
3a0f3c0a11: A branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library system located in Langley's Walnut Grove neighbourhood. The library offers public computers, free Wi-Fi, and a fully accessible ground-level facility with outdoor bike racks — a handy stop for touring cyclists needing a rest, a charge, or a read.
36a67b00e8: Port Kells Branch is a compact (1,200 sq ft) neighbourhood public library in Surrey's Port Kells area, operated by Surrey Libraries. It offers free computers, free Wi-Fi (including Eduroam for university students), self-checkout, and a 24-hour book return drop. The branch is notably car-dependent — the nearest bus stop is 1.8 km away — which is worth noting for cyclists navigating to or from the site.
b3a78b364f: The Cheakamus River Suspension Bridge spans the Cheakamus River near Whistler's Cheakamus Crossing/Function Junction area, providing the primary legal access to the celebrated Train Wreck site—a forest clearing where boxcars from a 1956 railway derailment remain among towering old-growth cedar and fir. The suspension footbridge has a locomotive-inspired design and connects directly to the Sea to Sky Trail, making it accessible to trail cyclists and hikers alike. The surrounding site has evolved into a free, open-air graffiti art gallery that local photographers, trail runners, and mountain bikers have long frequented.
abd1d57843: Spirit Garden is a free-access community garden in Victoria managed by the City. Located on Kings Road, it offers a peaceful green-space stop for touring cyclists passing through the neighbourhood.
af00b52c00: Parkview Activity Centre is a City of Kamloops-operated community centre located in the North Shore neighbourhood of Kamloops. It is part of the city's broader recreation and culture network, offering programming for residents. As a neighbourhood activity hub, it may serve as a convenient rest point for cyclists moving through the area, though specific cycling amenities are unconfirmed.
915507a704: The White Rock Community Centre is a City of White Rock-operated multipurpose facility housing a fitness gym, dance studio, arts room, gallery, presentation hall, and several rentable meeting spaces. Situated on Russell Avenue in the coastal city of White Rock, it serves as the primary hub for community programs, cultural events, and recreational activities for residents and visitors. Touring cyclists passing through White Rock may find it a convenient central facility, though no cycling-specific amenities are advertised on the website.
ca42b61913: Stephens Coyote Ridge Regional Park is a regional nature reserve near Kelowna managed by the Regional District of Central Okanagan. It is part of a network of 30 regional parks encompassing over 2,100 hectares, with designated trails winding through Central Okanagan landscapes. The park is day-use only, offering a natural rest stop or side trip for touring cyclists exploring the Kelowna area.
7fba740f9e: Fraser Library is the Surrey branch of Simon Fraser University Library, located inside SFU's Central City campus in the heart of Surrey's city centre. It serves the SFU Surrey community with research resources, study spaces, and technology access, and is open to the public per OSM access tags. A touring cyclist could stop here for Wi-Fi, a quiet indoor rest, and proximity to the Central City transit hub.
0cfd1cc949: A community hub operated by the Ukrainian-Canadian Cultural Society of Vancouver Island, dedicated to preserving and celebrating Ukrainian-Canadian heritage on Vancouver Island. The centre hosts cultural events, Ukrainian supper nights with homemade perogies and cabbage rolls, a Ukrainian library, gift shop, dance programs, and choirs. Located on Douglas Street in Victoria, it doubles as a licensed event venue with a spacious hall, stage, and kitchen facilities.
08f6a80f74: Howard Horel Nature Reserve is a 25-hectare protected area on Salt Spring Island within the globally rare Coastal Douglas-fir zone, featuring forested terrain, rocky bluffs, Garry oak, small wetlands, and streams flowing into upper Fulford Creek. The reserve harbours seven Species at Risk and was acquired in 2018 through an anonymous donation honouring a long-time Salt Spring family. Touring cyclists can access the reserve's easy trail network via Bryant Hill Park, reached from the end of Mereside Road or Sarah Way.
203e18d8fb: Abkhazi Garden is a historic show garden in Victoria's Fairfield neighbourhood, operated by The Land Conservancy of British Columbia as one of its featured conservation projects. The garden is publicly accessible with donations requested, set on a heritage property preserved as a naturalistic landscape. It sits within easy cycling distance of downtown Victoria and offers a quiet green respite for touring cyclists passing through the city.
9611699fd7: Hill's Native Art is a long-established BC chain specializing in Indigenous Canadian art, jewelry, and cultural items. The Vancouver Broadway location brings authentic First Nations artwork to a neighbourhood commercial strip in Vancouver. Touring cyclists passing through would encounter a curated gallery focused on West Coast Indigenous traditions.
d507fe68e0: The Tennis Centre is a multi-location indoor and outdoor tennis facility founded by coach Larry Jurovich, who has coached players to Grand Slam appearances and served as Head of Coach Education for the UK's Lawn Tennis Association. The Coquitlam location opened in 2017 as the network's second site, part of a vision to make tennis accessible beyond the traditional country-club model. A touring cyclist arriving here would find a dedicated sports facility, though current operational status of this specific location is uncertain.
7ecd8bd229: The Whistler Visitor Centre is Whistler's official in-resort information hub, staffed by knowledgeable Tourism Whistler employees who can assist with accommodation, activity bookings, transit schedules, and broader BC travel planning. Located adjacent to the bus and taxi loop at 4230 Gateway Drive, it is a natural stopping point for anyone arriving by public transit or exploring the valley. Touring cyclists would find it particularly useful for local maps, event listings, and regional destination information.
11acf15c5a: Willingdon Community Centre is a City of Burnaby-operated civic recreation facility set within Willingdon Heights Park in northwest Burnaby. It offers weight and cardio rooms, fitness and yoga classes, and gym and racquet sports alongside children's and preschool programs. As a publicly accessible facility in a park setting, it could serve as an urban rest point for cyclists riding through the area, though no dedicated cycling services are advertised.
b2422fff99: The Mary Winspear Centre is a 30,000 sq ft non-profit community and performing arts venue in Sidney, BC, hosting theatre productions, concerts, art exhibitions, conferences, and community celebrations. Operated by the Saanich Peninsula Memorial Park Society, the wheelchair-accessible facility includes the Charlie White Theatre, Bodine Family Hall, an art gallery, and meeting rooms. Situated close to the BC Ferries Swartz Bay terminal and with a seaside setting, it is a cultural hub for visitors arriving on the Saanich Peninsula by bike or ferry.
1e2c1153b1: Established in 1998, Vancouver Whale Watch is the original whale watching company in Vancouver, departing from the historic fishing village of Steveston in Richmond. Tours run 3 to 5 hours through the Gulf Islands and Strait of Georgia aboard a fleet of zodiacs, with professional wildlife guides focused on Orcas, Humpback Whales, and other marine life. The company boasts a 98% whale sighting rate and offers a lifetime free return guarantee if no whale is spotted.
e714aedf1e: West Vancouver Recreation Centre is a public recreation facility serving the District of West Vancouver on BC's North Shore. It is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a tourist attraction and represents a significant community hub situated near popular North Shore and Sea-to-Sky cycling routes.
f511f049bc: The Cultch is a landmark community arts hub in East Vancouver, presenting over 20 productions per year across three theatre spaces — the Historic Theatre, Vancity Culture Lab, and York Theatre — as well as a gallery and multi-use spaces. Operating since 1973, it programs contemporary work in theatre, dance, music, circus, and visual arts from local, national, and international artists, and underwent a $30 million refurbishment under its current Executive Director. A touring cyclist arriving in East Van will find a vibrant cultural destination known for diverse, risk-taking programming and strong community ties.
23f41ee639: Steveston Outdoor Pool is a City of Richmond–operated seasonal outdoor swimming facility located in the historic Steveston fishing village neighbourhood. Sitting near the Steveston waterfront, it is a classic community pool well-positioned for cyclists riding the popular Richmond dyke trail network. The pool operates as a summer destination, making it a natural cooling-off stop on a warm-weather tour of the Fraser River delta.
8467d98be6: The ORL UBCO Branch is a public library branch of the Okanagan Regional Library system located on the University of British Columbia Okanagan campus in Kelowna. It functions primarily as a holds pick-up location with a small selection of popular materials, and is staffed only on Tuesday mornings and during occasional special events. Multiple bus routes serve the campus, and the building's book drop is always accessible.
1d02fc7d9e: Centennial Outdoor Pool is a City of Port Coquitlam-operated outdoor swimming facility located on Chester Street in the Tri-Cities area. Run by the municipality as part of its aquatics programming alongside spray parks and indoor pools, it offers a seasonal aquatic destination for residents and visitors. The facility is wheelchair accessible and charges an admission fee, making it a potential summer refreshment stop for touring cyclists passing through Port Coquitlam.
a7132d4c7c: The Capilano Branch of the North Vancouver District Public Library is a community cornerstone located in the heart of Edgemont Village, offering a reading area, children's and teen sections, a quiet study room, and public computer workstations. Uniquely, the NVDPL system lists E-Cargo Bikes among its borrowable items, making this library system of direct interest to cycling-curious visitors. Free Wi-Fi and an accessible central location make it a practical stop for touring cyclists passing through North Vancouver's residential hillside neighbourhoods.
2d088def75: The CPR Station Museum occupies a beautifully preserved 100+ year old Canadian Pacific Railway station in Castlegar, considered one of the finest remaining examples of its kind in British Columbia. The museum explores the railway and pioneer heritage of the Columbia River Valley through exhibits, newspaper archives, and a restored station agent's residence on the upper floor. The same society also manages nearby Zuckerberg Island Heritage Park, featuring a Russian Orthodox-influenced chapel house, a 473-foot military-built suspension bridge, and over 8 hectares of river woodland trails.
b83bd22ab2: VanDusen Botanical Garden is a 55-acre urban oasis in Vancouver's Shaughnessy neighbourhood, home to over 7,500 plant species from around the world.
