Located on Carmi Avenue in Penticton, it is a family-oriented motorsport venue in the heart of the Okanagan.
6beabe3d00: The Firehall Branch is one of the Vancouver Public Library system's neighbourhood locations, serving the Fairview and South Granville area of Vancouver. As a free, publicly accessible institution, it offers a useful midpoint stop for touring cyclists moving through the city's west side. The VPL system is a well-established public resource with multiple branches across Vancouver.
d412514bd9: Historic Hat Creek Ranch is a BC heritage site designated since 1981, encompassing roughly 130 hectares of farmyards, fields, and rangeland along with approximately twenty historic wooden buildings dating from 1861 into the early 20th century. Located near Cache Creek on the Gold Rush Trail, it offers a rare glimpse into the era of roadhouse travel and early BC ranching. Touring cyclists passing through the Interior could find it a compelling cultural stop along a route that follows historic wagon roads.
da171ecfa9: The Chilliwack Track Complex is an 8.46-hectare public athletic facility constructed as a joint venture between School District No. 33 and the City of Chilliwack for the 1993 BC Summer Games. It features a 400-metre synthetic running track built to international standards, set behind Sardis Senior Secondary School. A fieldhouse on site includes washrooms and a concession stand, making it a functional rest stop for cyclists passing through Sardis.
dd37738ccf: The Canadian Museum of Flight, established in 1996 at Langley Airport, preserves and displays a collection of historic Canadian aircraft and aviation artifacts. It is one of British Columbia's dedicated aviation heritage museums and a notable destination for those cycling the Fraser Valley region. Touring cyclists will find it a distinctive stop offering a look at Canada's aviation history in an airport setting.
481eea8c1f: The Port Alberni Branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the community since 1936, with origins in the back of McVicar's Drug Store where shop employees acted as library attendants. The branch moved to the Echo Centre in 1972 and underwent a major refurbishment and expansion in 2007, now holding a collection of over 35,000 items. Touring cyclists can drop in for free public WiFi, sit-down service, and public access computers in a fully wheelchair-accessible space.
359bc61ba4: Remote Passages Marine Excursions has run eco-tours out of Tofino's Wharf Street since 1986, pioneering zodiac-based whale watching on BC's west coast and expanding to sea kayaking, black bear watching, Meares Island old-growth rainforest tours, and the boat-and-hike journey to Hot Springs Cove. Operating in the Clayoquot Sound UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, the company offers one of the longest wildlife viewing seasons on BC's west coast, from February to November. Touring cyclists who have ridden to Tofino can extend their adventure onto the water, encountering gray whales, humpbacks, orcas, sea otters, and coastal bears in their natural habitat.
c922d51081: The Museum of Northern British Columbia is a century-old regional institution in Prince Rupert dedicated to preserving and interpreting the natural and cultural heritage of the Northwest Coast, with a particular focus on Tsimshian First Nations history and art. It administers several related sites including the 'Wiwaabm Ts'msyeen Tsimshian Performance Longhouse and the Kwinitsa Station Railway Museum, and offers immersive guided tours combining gallery visits with live feast experiences and traditional dance. For a touring cyclist arriving in Prince Rupert, it represents a compelling cultural anchor in a remote northern port city steeped in Indigenous and maritime history.
4e15130e92: Tom Hopkins Ravine Park protects over 6.5 hectares of sensitive second-growth forest ravine ecosystem in Surrey, with more than 1 km of Delta Creek running through it. Natural area trails in the west section of the park offer a quiet forest walk, with a pedestrian bridge crossing Delta Creek. Access is from 98A or 99 Avenue, and most of the ravine interior is inaccessible to protect the sensitive habitat.
f6866f7a4b: The Cumberland Museum and Archives is a community history museum on Vancouver Island that chronicles the diverse stories of Cumberland's coal mining heritage, its multicultural workforce, and the social and political struggles that shaped the region. Founded in 1969 and operated by a non-profit historical society, it houses permanent and rotating exhibitions alongside a community research library and digital photograph archive. Cumberland is a celebrated cycling destination — particularly for mountain biking — making this a natural cultural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Comox Valley.
90f53f5228: The S.S. Moyie is the oldest known intact passenger-carrying sternwheel steamer in the world, built in 1898 for the Canadian Pacific Railway and now permanently ashore in Kaslo on Kootenay Lake. Designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 1958, it offers tours of the original vessel—including the freight deck, saloon, pilot house, and paddlewheel—alongside a Visitor Centre, Gift Shop, Caboose, and the Kootenay Lake Archives. For a touring cyclist completing the Kootenay Lake loop, this waterfront site is a genuinely remarkable piece of BC and CPR history.
be67fd3c46: The YMCA-YWCA Downtown Victoria is a full-service community fitness and recreation centre operated by the YMCA-YWCA of Vancouver Island, offering pool and aquatics, fitness programs, and community health services in the heart of downtown. It is one of two YMCA facilities on Vancouver Island and offers a 'Member for a Day' option that allows drop-in visitors to access facilities without a full membership. As a non-profit with financial assistance programs, it functions as an accessible community hub for both residents and visitors.
5287fb4a39: Queensborough Community Centre is a civic, two-storey recreation facility operated by New Westminster Parks and Recreation Department, situated in the Queensborough neighbourhood—a relatively isolated community on the south arm of the Fraser River. As the primary public recreation hub for this island neighbourhood, it serves residents with a range of programming and facilities. Touring cyclists crossing through Queensborough may find it a useful waypoint, though specific cyclist-oriented amenities are not confirmed.
829e4b09dc: Parkgate Community Centre is a publicly operated recreation facility run by the North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission (NVRC) in the eastern reaches of North Vancouver, near the Deep Cove area and popular North Shore cycling routes. The centre houses a large gymnasium with badminton, pickleball, basketball, and volleyball courts, a climbing wall, a fitness centre, a pottery studio, and several bookable meeting and multi-purpose rooms. As a community hub near trailheads and scenic coastal roads, it could serve as a practical rest or regrouping point for touring cyclists passing through the area.
6bfcc597d8: Scotia Barn (formerly Burnaby 8 Rinks) is one of Canada's largest multi-rink indoor ice facilities, operated by Canlan Sports and featuring six NHL-sized ice rinks, a dedicated figure skating rink, and an indoor soccer field. It hosts competitive leagues, drop-in programs, camps, and tournaments year-round for youth and adults across Metro Vancouver. As a large commercial sports complex, it caters primarily to ice hockey and skating participants rather than touring cyclists.
ca484aa9db: Juan de Fuca Recreation Centre is a publicly operated civic sports and recreation facility run by Westshore Parks and Recreation in the Westshore area near Victoria. It serves the broader Capital Regional District community and is typical of large multi-purpose Canadian recreation centres that anchor neighbourhood activity. Touring cyclists in the Victoria area may find it a useful stop given its public mandate and likely range of facilities.
f468aeb6b6: Fleetwood Branch is one of ten Surrey Libraries locations serving the Fleetwood neighbourhood of Surrey, BC. As a public library, it offers free access to books, digital resources, computer terminals, and community programming. Touring cyclists may find it a useful urban rest stop with Wi-Fi and public-use computers available without admission.
cb870902bd: The Large Quarry Garden is a sunken ornamental garden carved into a former basalt quarry within Queen Elizabeth Park in Vancouver, featuring tiered flowerbeds and reflecting pools set against the quarry walls. Situated at one of the highest points in Vancouver, the surrounding park offers panoramic views of the city and North Shore mountains. It is a popular stop on cycling routes through the area and is freely accessible to the public.
26fdb47a8e: The Irving K. Barber Learning Centre is a landmark four-storey building on UBC's Vancouver campus, publicly accessible to all British Columbians as a hub for research, lifelong learning, and community engagement. It houses multiple library services including the Music, Art & Architecture Library and Chapman Learning Commons, alongside rotating art exhibits, event spaces, and community programs. Named after BC philanthropist Irving K. Barber, it is a notable cultural and educational destination for anyone exploring UBC's campus by bike.
2e7f524245: The Queensborough Library is a branch of the New Westminster Public Library, situated inside the Queensborough Community Centre on Ewen Avenue. It offers free public Wi-Fi, public computers, borrowing services, and regular community programming including employment services drop-ins. For a touring cyclist, it represents a welcoming public indoor stop with digital access in the Queensborough neighbourhood of New Westminster.
49ae924fa2: The Hive is a bouldering-focused climbing gym occupying a two-storey building in Vancouver's Industrial Avenue corridor. It is part of a multi-location BC and Manitoba chain and is notable as one of two Hive branches within walking distance of each other on the same street. For touring cyclists looking for an active rest day, it offers a drop-in climbing experience in an urban industrial setting.
a7dc68cf4a: The Art Gallery of Greater Victoria is anchored by a striking 1889 Victorian mansion alongside seven modern galleries, holding the largest public art collection in British Columbia — over 22,000 works — including the most significant collection of Asian art in Western Canada. Founded in 1951 when the Spencer Mansion was donated to the city, the AGGV is a genuine landmark in Victoria's Rockland neighbourhood and a draw for visitors from across the island and beyond. Cyclists will find it a culturally rich stop, with free admission days and a coat-room locker area where large bags can be safely stored.
80a7de4809: The CPL Poirier Branch is a single-storey civic library operated by Coquitlam Public Library, providing free access to books, digital resources, computers, and community programming. As a no-admission-required public facility in the Tri-Cities area, it offers a welcoming rest environment for touring cyclists passing through Coquitlam. The branch is fully wheelchair accessible and runs a broad range of programs for adults, teens, and children.
852f14fb7c: The Grouse Grind is one of Metro Vancouver's most iconic challenges, a steep trail climbing nearly 900 metres up the face of Grouse Mountain in North Vancouver. Touring cyclists can ride to the base at 6400 Nancy Greene Way and experience the mountain complex, which also hosts the Grouse Bike Park with lift access, bike rentals, and mountain bike camps — making it relevant beyond just the hiking trail. The summit is home to grizzly bear habitat, wildlife demonstrations, scenic lookouts, and multiple dining venues with panoramic views of Vancouver.
2e4c8b3b2b: Other Guise is a community-motivated theatre company founded in 2001 and based at 716 Johnson Street in downtown Victoria, dedicated to original theatrical presentations that reflect Vancouver Island's history and culture while supporting local professional and emerging artists. The fully ground-level, step-free venue features automated entry doors, a main performance and lounge space, and a bar, making it a welcoming stop in the heart of Victoria. The company holds charitable status and takes a zero-waste approach to its operations.
605b0d6bbd: Founded in 1999 with a mission to create a more inclusive surf community, Surf Sister is Tofino's well-known surf school and shop offering lessons, camps, and rentals for all ages and abilities. The main 'Shred Quarters' location sits in downtown Tofino, with a second outpost at Pacific Sands Beach Resort. A repeat Tripadvisor Traveller's Choice Award winner, it draws visitors from around the world to BC's rugged west coast surf scene.
c0e44d915d: The BC Golf Museum and Hall of Fame chronicles the history of golf in British Columbia, honouring the province's notable players, courses, and contributors to the sport. Located in Point Grey near UBC, it sits along routes popular with Vancouver-area cyclists. A touring cyclist passing through the area would find it a compact cultural stop in a quiet residential neighbourhood.
621013e8ad: New Brighton Pool is a seasonal outdoor public swimming pool operated by the City of Vancouver, situated near the waterfront in the Hastings-Sunrise neighbourhood of East Vancouver. It is open during summer months and is one of several outdoor pools the city operates for public recreation. Touring cyclists riding the nearby Central Valley Greenway or exploring the East Vancouver waterfront will find it a convenient stop on a warm summer day.
168a013c40: Mossom Creek Hatchery and Education Centre is one of the longest-running community hatcheries in British Columbia, established in 1976 by high school volunteers and now managed by the Burrard Inlet Marine Enhancement Society within Mossom Creek Park in Port Moody. The facility sits in a pristine watershed setting with forest and creek views, wildlife cameras, and hands-on salmon enhancement and education programs. In 2023 it received the Gold Accessibility Certification from the Rick Hansen Foundation.
ca07e210fb: The HUB at Cowichan Station is a volunteer-run community centre housed in a restored 100-year-old elementary school building in the rural Cowichan Valley, operated by the Cowichan Station Area Association. It offers fitness classes, a film club, disc golf, and an on-site café, making it a lively gathering place for locals and visitors alike. Cyclists touring the Cowichan Valley's back roads will find it a welcoming stop in a small agricultural settlement between Duncan and the Saanich Peninsula.
2de6e4a6c9: The Chinese Cultural Centre Museum and Archives is a free-admission cultural institution in Vancouver's historic Chinatown, preserving and presenting the history of Chinese Canadians in British Columbia. It is part of the larger Chinese Cultural Centre of Greater Vancouver, which has operated since 1981 and offers community events, Cantonese opera performances, and organized walking tours of Chinatown. A cyclist passing through Chinatown will find this a meaningful stop for understanding the neighbourhood's deep cultural heritage.
c4483c2c17: Ayum Creek Regional Park Reserve is a nature reserve in the Sooke area, managed by the Capital Regional District. It sits along Ayum Creek and offers a natural setting for visitors exploring Vancouver Island's southern coast by bike.
92768d1cad: The Wasa Hotel Museum is a historic two-storey hipped-roof building within Fort Steele Heritage Town, a sweeping outdoor heritage complex of more than 60 historic and reconstructed structures operated by the Cranbrook Archives, Museum, and Landmark Society. The site interprets BC's late-19th-century Gold Rush and ranching era on the ancestral territory of the Ktunaxa and Secwépemc peoples, now under renewed stewardship since April 2025. Touring cyclists will find the Wasa Hotel listed as one of the site's designated cooling stations, making it a useful mid-ride refuge on hot Kootenay days.
62b7009518: A year-round public aquatic centre in Grand Forks, originally opened in 1987 and operated by the Regional District of Kootenay Boundary. The facility features four 25-metre lanes, a large shallow-water leisure area, sauna, whirlpool, and a fitness and wellness centre. For touring cyclists passing through the Boundary region, it offers a welcome chance to swim, soak in the hot tub, and clean up.
7bd41807a3: Nanaimo Art Gallery is an ambitious public contemporary art gallery founded in 1976 and now situated in the heart of downtown Nanaimo on Commercial Street, on the traditional territory of the Snuneymuxw First Nations. The gallery presents rotating exhibitions of contemporary art alongside robust programs for all ages, and operates on an admission-by-donation model that makes it genuinely accessible to all visitors. A touring cyclist exploring downtown Nanaimo will find it a short walk from the waterfront, neighboured by cafes and shops along a lively commercial strip.
b26634c47f: The Qualicum Beach branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the community since 1937 and has been housed in the Town Hall building since 1997. Part of the Vancouver Island Regional Library system — one of the largest public library networks in BC — it provides free public services to residents and visitors across a wide stretch of Vancouver Island. Its central Qualicum Beach location makes it a natural waypoint for cyclists passing through town.
1d948bc4e7: The Shaw Centre for the Salish Sea is BC's only not-for-profit aquarium in Greater Victoria, situated on the Sidney waterfront on the traditional territory of the W̱SÁNEĆ (Saanich) people. The centre offers interactive self-guided exhibits, daily animal ambassador programs, and behind-the-scenes aquarist tours focused on the ecology of the 110,000 sq km Salish Sea bioregion. Touring cyclists riding the Saanich Peninsula or catching ferries from Sidney will find it a compelling cultural stop, recognized among the top attractions on Vancouver Island.
ac928d95a7: Rosemary Brown Recreation Centre is a year-round City of Burnaby multi-sport facility anchored by two NHL-sized ice rinks seating 263 and 148 spectators respectively. The centre hosts public skating, hockey leagues, figure skating, ringette, and in the off-season converts to dry-floor sports including pickleball and lacrosse. Named after a pioneering BC politician and social activist, it functions as a busy community hub on Burnaby's south slope.
72dc2abe21: The Mission Branch is part of the Okanagan Regional Library (ORL), a regional system of 30 branches serving over 399,000 people across the Okanagan and surrounding areas, established in 1936. Located in the Mission neighbourhood of Kelowna on Gordon Drive, it offers typical public library services including books, digital resources, and programs. As a free public institution, it can be a useful rest and resource stop for touring cyclists passing through the area.
56c0626847: Gallery 1710 is the home of the South Delta Artists Guild in Tsawwassen, showcasing rotating monthly exhibitions of original works by local artists spanning realism to abstract, watercolour to mixed media and 3D art. Located just minutes from the Tsawwassen ferry terminal and close to the Delta dike cycling network, it makes a natural cultural stop for cyclists passing through the area. The guild, incorporated in 1975, also runs workshops and Saturday artist demonstrations open to the public.
4b24edb7bd: A Canadian art gallery in East Vancouver's light-industrial Venables corridor, operating since 1986. Represents BC and North American artists across painting, photography, and digital art with rotating exhibitions. Free admission and no appointment needed on weekdays, making it an easy cultural stop.
05e0b1e511: The Stó:lō Gift Shop is a 100% Indigenous-owned retail store located on the historic Coqualeetza grounds at Stó:lō Nation in Chilliwack. It carries an extensive selection of authentic Aboriginal arts, crafts, and giftware from local artists and suppliers across British Columbia, including hand-carved silver jewellery, traditional medicines, drums, and Coast Salish-designed apparel. A stop here offers touring cyclists a meaningful cultural experience and the chance to support Indigenous artisans directly.
1fdd075d7e: Christine Sinclair Community Centre is a City of Burnaby recreation facility named after Canadian soccer icon Christine Sinclair, situated in the Burnaby Lake 'sports central' hub alongside sports fields and ice arenas. Formerly known as Fortius Sport & Health, it was rebranded as part of Burnaby's community recreation network and offers state-of-the-art fitness amenities including cardio and weight rooms, a gymnasium, and a steam room. Its central location near Bill Copeland Sports Centre makes it a substantial recreation node for the eastern Burnaby area.
20ecd6cb28: The Pemberton & District Public Library is a modern community library serving the Pemberton valley, a popular hub for cycling in the Sea-to-Sky corridor. Beyond books, it offers a 'Library of Things' collection, free digital resources, and a bookable 2-person meeting pod. Touring cyclists would find free Wi-Fi and public computers available during open hours.
b18dc325fe: The Chemainus Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library is a modern civic library that opened in January 2020, the community's third location since the original library debuted in the local Masonic Hall in 1949. It offers free public WiFi, computers, printing, scanning, and research assistance as part of the broader VIRL network spanning Vancouver Island. Wheelchair accessible and centrally located, it makes a practical indoor rest stop for touring cyclists seeking connectivity while passing through Chemainus.
c9fd074e8f: Gallery Gachet is an artist-run centre in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside with a mandate to support artists addressing mental health and socio-political marginalization. The gallery hosts rotating exhibitions, curator talks, and workshops in a single-level accessible space. Located near Pigeon Park between Carrall and Columbia Streets, it's easily reached by transit or bike.
bc7ba686bb: The Nelson Public Library is a well-established community library in the heart of Nelson, serving residents and visitors with an extensive physical and digital collection including books, audiobooks, DVDs, and online databases. Open to anyone for on-site use, it offers a welcoming space to learn, study, and relax, with free access to computers and wireless internet. The library sits on the traditional territory of the Sinixt, Ktunaxa, and Syilx peoples and has been a pillar of the community for over 125 years.
94dc191c84: A City of Surrey municipal recreation centre in the Guildford neighbourhood offering swimming, sports, and fitness programs. The facility includes a pool and hosts a wide variety of drop-in and registered programs. Wheelchair accessible.
aa00607bc9: The Ranger Station Art Gallery occupies the original 1951 Forestry Ranger Station building on the shore of Harrison Lake, operated by the not-for-profit Kent Harrison Arts Council since 1972. It is the only public art gallery in the area, hosting monthly exhibitions by visual artists and running a year-long national artist-in-residence program with on-site living and studio space. Cyclists passing through Harrison Hot Springs can step into this historic building to catch rotating shows featuring a wide range of visual art media.
754be4ab94: A small community library on Mayne Island, part of the Southern Gulf Islands Community Libraries network. It offers free Wi-Fi, printing services, and a quiet place to rest for cyclists exploring the Gulf Islands by ferry. The library also connects visitors to community resources including the Mayne Island Museum and Chamber of Commerce.
aba5a9a9ca: Westholme Tea Company is a working organic tea farm and artisanal teashop in the Cowichan Valley near Chemainus, one of only a handful of places in Canada growing true Camellia sinensis tea plants. The farm imports and hand-blends organic loose-leaf teas from estates around the world alongside their own rare Canadian-terroir harvest. Cyclists touring the Cowichan Valley have specifically noted stopping in here for tea samples and welcoming service from staff.
7eb3b12838: The Creativity Commons (Nanaimo Harbourfront) is a public library branch operated by Vancouver Island Regional Library, situated on Nanaimo's waterfront with a history of library services in the community dating to the 1860s. The branch occupies floors 2 and 3 of its building and offers meeting room bookings, digital learning resources, and a broad range of collections. Its central harbourfront location makes it a natural stopping point for touring cyclists passing through downtown Nanaimo.
53ccb48007: The Patricia Bay Visitor Centre is operated by the Saanich Peninsula Chamber of Commerce and serves as a tourism information office on the Patricia Bay Highway corridor between Victoria and the Swartz Bay ferry terminal. It is a practical first or last stop for cyclists arriving or departing via the BC Ferries route, offering regional orientation for Sidney, North Saanich, and Central Saanich. The Chamber has served the peninsula since 1912 and represents over 250 local businesses.
6e388e7812: VPL Oakridge Branch is a public library in Vancouver's Oakridge neighbourhood operated by the Vancouver Public Library system. It is freely accessible to the public and offers Wi-Fi, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists needing internet access or a quiet place to rest. As part of a major urban library network, it is a well-established civic resource.
e8811374fc: Dunbar Community Centre has served the Dunbar neighbourhood of Vancouver since 1958, jointly operated by the Vancouver Parks Board and the volunteer-run Dunbar Community Centre Association. The facility houses a fitness centre, squash courts, pottery room, and a preschool, offering a wide range of recreational and social programs. Touring cyclists passing through southwest Vancouver may find it a convenient neighbourhood stop, though it is primarily a local community resource rather than a destination attraction.
919b433656: The Creston Museum is a community history museum operated by The Creston & District Historical & Museum Society, dedicated to the unique pioneer, Indigenous, agricultural, and industrial heritage of the Creston Valley at the heart of the Kootenays. It features rotating exhibits on subjects ranging from WWI soldiers to a model railway, alongside archives, photo galleries, and children's programs. For a touring cyclist rolling through the valley between the Purcell and Selkirk ranges, it offers rich local context on the landscape and communities they are riding through.
e133d726aa: The Port Hardy branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served this northernmost Vancouver Island community since 1972, situated on the unceded traditional territory of the Kwakwaka'wakw peoples. As a full-service public library, it offers books, digital resources, computers, and meeting room facilities to the public at no charge. For touring cyclists reaching the end of the Island Highway, it provides a welcoming indoor rest stop with community resources in a remote location.
eb32dea24b: Steveston Village is a heritage fishing village at the mouth of the Fraser River in Richmond, voted #1 Metro Vancouver neighbourhood out of 192 in 2020 and declared a heritage zone in 1960. It remains a working fishing village where cyclists can buy fresh seafood off the dock, explore national historic sites like the Gulf of Georgia Cannery and Britannia Shipyards, and stroll the waterfront along Fishers Walk. The village's Moncton Street streetscape—lined with cafés, bookshops, and film locations—makes it a compelling stop on any cycling tour of the Lower Mainland.
4ffb0c6423: Bald Mountain Park is a nature reserve managed by the Cowichan Valley Regional District, situated near Lake Cowichan on Vancouver Island. As a CVRD-administered park, it likely offers natural trail experiences through the region's characteristic coastal forest and mountain terrain. Touring cyclists in the Lake Cowichan area may find it a worthwhile side trip for scenery and a break from the road.
0d2f79ca79: The International Friendship Garden & Cultural Gateway is a public garden in Abbotsford operated by the City of Abbotsford Parks, Recreation & Culture, celebrating cultural diversity through landscape design. Tagged in OSM with a fence barrier, it is a defined, enclosed attraction along George Ferguson Way. Touring cyclists riding through Abbotsford may find it a worthwhile rest or sightseeing stop in an urban park setting.
8fbe905740: Vallea Lumina is an immersive multimedia night walk through the forest on Cougar Mountain, blending lighting installations, soundscapes, and interactive storytelling along a designated trail. Operated by The Adventure Group, the experience runs year-round after sunset and follows either a 1 km winter course or a 1.5 km summer course through the forest. A free bookable shuttle connects Whistler Village Gateway Bus Loop to the Cougar Mountain basecamp, making it accessible without a vehicle.
a25831431b: The Granville Island Public Market is a large indoor market on the waterfront in Vancouver, featuring fresh produce, seafood, baked goods, farmers stalls, and locally handcrafted artisan products. Managed by Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation on behalf of the Government of Canada, it has operated since Granville Island's transformation from an industrial site in the 1970s and attracts millions of visitors annually. The market is open on all statutory holidays except December 25, 26, and January 1.
e8e7faaa70: Bau-Xi Gallery is one of Canada's oldest and most respected contemporary art galleries, founded in 1965 and situated on Vancouver's South Granville gallery strip. It shows a rotating programme of painting, sculpture, photography, and mixed media by Canadian and international artists, with free admission. The Granville Street corridor is a natural waypoint for cyclists exploring the city's west side.
981f22f127: Kiyo Park is a small urban nature park in Surrey's Whalley neighbourhood, threaded by King Creek and connected by a pedestrian pathway and bridge that doubles as a wildlife viewing platform. The park is notably good for spotting spawning salmon in autumn, along with resident bird life along the creek corridor. The western portion offers open meadows and shade trees, making it a quiet spot for a short break on a local ride.
ef66d07123: Guildford Recreation Centre is a municipal sports and recreation facility operated by the City of Surrey in the Guildford neighbourhood. As a full-service recreation centre, it offers programs and activities typical of a large municipal complex. It sits along 152 Street, a major corridor in Surrey's suburban east side.
69f326a54e: The Hope Library is Fraser Valley Regional Library's branch serving the town of Hope, BC, housed in a civic building on 6th Avenue. It offers digital library services, computers, printing, and a range of community programs as part of FVRL's extensive regional network. For touring cyclists moving through the Fraser Canyon gateway, it represents a quiet rest point in the heart of the downtown core.
c4c71a6e2d: Oliver Woods Community Centre is a City of Nanaimo public recreation facility on Oliver Road. It is part of the city's network of community and activity centres offering recreation programs and drop-in activities. Touring cyclists passing through south Nanaimo may find it a convenient municipal stop.
6662799dba: The Millennium Sport Centre is a civic sports facility in Vancouver's Hillcrest neighbourhood, built as part of the 2010 Winter Olympics legacy infrastructure. It sits adjacent to Nat Bailey Stadium and Hillcrest Park, making it a notable landmark on the southeast side of the city. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find it a recognizable civic anchor in a well-connected recreational corridor.
09575f8d0d: A museum dedicated to the history and culture of Chinese Canadians, housed in the Hoy Sun Ning Yung Benevolent Association building on Fan Tan Alley — North America's narrowest commercial street. Located in Canada's oldest surviving Chinatown (est. 1858), it features rotating exhibits, artifacts, and community programming. Free admission makes it an easy stop for touring cyclists passing through downtown Victoria.
cef32fe392: The Amphitrite House Interpretive Centre is a single-storey, wheelchair-accessible tourism information office situated on Coast Guard Road at the western edge of Ucluelet, near the tip of the peninsula. It provides interpretive information for visitors to this dramatic stretch of Vancouver Island's outer coast. The building's location in the Coast Guard Road area places it close to the Amphitrite Point Lighthouse and the rugged Pacific shoreline.
8a611a77e5: A municipal recreation centre in Oak Bay operated by Recreation Oak Bay, part of the District of Oak Bay's parks and recreation system. The facility offers registered programs, drop-in activities, and community services in a residential neighbourhood near the Victoria waterfront.
b76e003283: Mark Hobson Gallery is the dedicated showroom for Canadian wildlife and landscape artist Mark Hobson, who has painted professionally from Tofino since 1984. His work — executed in watercolour, acrylic, and oil — captures the West Coast's pounding surf, rain forests, and coastal wildlife, with many pieces begun outdoors on location. Touring cyclists rolling into Tofino can browse original paintings, limited-edition giclée prints, and commission custom artwork directly from the artist.
e9b2780ff3: Upper Canyon Open Space is a nature reserve managed by the City of Kelowna, situated in the upper canyon area of the city. As a publicly accessible open space, it offers natural terrain that may appeal to cyclists looking to explore Kelowna's canyon landscapes on foot or by trail. The area is part of Kelowna's parks and beaches network.
c30d8b7657: A 42-hectare nature reserve on Galiano Island protecting one of the last intact tracts of mature and old-growth Coastal Douglas-fir forest in the Southern Gulf Islands. The reserve stretches from Trincomali Channel to the island's central ridgeline, encompassing rare Garry Oak woodlands, creek and wetland habitats, and 600 metres of undeveloped coastline. Established in 2024 by the Galiano Conservancy Association through Canada's Old Growth Nature Fund.
4c969c2817: Bowen Creek Corridor is a nature reserve within the City of Kelowna, offering a natural greenway along Bowen Creek. As a linear corridor, it likely provides a route through natural habitat that touring cyclists in the Kelowna area could use for recreation or as a connector. The site is managed by the City of Kelowna as part of its parks and beaches network.
d55565eb1b: The Railway Museum of British Columbia, operated by the non-profit West Coast Railway Association, preserves 95 heritage locomotives and railway cars in the spectacular mountain setting of Squamish on the Sea to Sky corridor. Visitors can climb into the cab of the Royal Hudson 2860 steam locomotive, ride the BC-21 Budd Rail Diesel Car, and explore restored luxury passenger cars inside the CN Roundhouse. It is a hands-on, immersive destination telling the story of the railways that shaped British Columbia and Western Canada.
526f581fa2: Thornton Creek Enhancement Society is a non-profit salmon hatchery near Ucluelet dedicated to sustaining Chinook, Coho, and Chum salmon populations in Barkley and Clayoquot Sounds, operating since 1981 within the traditional territories of the Toquaht, Ucluth Aht, and Tla-o-qui-aht Nations. During the fall salmon run the hatchery becomes a popular destination, offering educational tours by donation where visitors can observe the salmon lifecycle up close. It also runs school programs and snorkel surveys, making it one of the more ecologically engaged visitor experiences on the west coast of Vancouver Island.
7fa134f030: Gleneagles Community Centre is a municipally operated recreation facility in the Gleneagles neighbourhood of West Vancouver, situated along Marine Drive near Howe Sound. Run by West Vancouver Municipality, it serves as a hub for local recreation programs and community gatherings. Its location on the scenic Marine Drive cycling corridor makes it a natural waypoint for touring cyclists passing through the area.
163fdd1581: Rossland Arena is a municipal ice facility operated by the City of Rossland, offering ice skating, ice hockey, and curling. It is a seasonal venue serving the local community and is situated in Rossland, a small city in the West Kootenay region of BC known primarily for its mountain terrain.
2c125d7497: Extreme Air Park Richmond bills itself as Canada's largest indoor trampoline park, spanning 42,000 sq ft of interlocking trampolines across activities including dodgeball courts, rock climbing, a foam pit, and slam-dunk basketball. The facility can accommodate up to 440 jumpers simultaneously and is part of a three-location Lower Mainland chain. It is a high-energy indoor attraction with no evident connection to cycling tourism.
f4ca329ace: The YMCA of Northern BC is a community sports and recreation centre in Prince George offering fitness, aquatics, child care, youth support, and outdoor education programs. As the regional hub for YMCA services in northern BC, it anchors a wide range of health and wellness programming for residents and visitors. Touring cyclists passing through Prince George may find it a useful urban stop given its full-service nature, though specific cycling amenities are not confirmed.
82028fe3a4: The Qualicum Beach Chamber of Commerce has served as the voice of local business since at least the 1920s, acting as the town's primary visitor information hub on the east coast of Vancouver Island. Cycling tourists passing through can use it as a starting point to discover local restaurants, accommodations, shops, and community events. The organization also promotes Qualicum Beach as a tourism destination and maintains an active local business directory.
b8fd2cd7d6: WildPlay Element Park is an outdoor adventure park near the Nanaimo River offering aerial obstacle courses through the forest canopy, ziplines, a bungy jump, a giant primal swing, and axe throwing. The park features multiple course difficulty levels—including a kids' course and an extreme course reaching 60 feet high—and is part of a multi-location BC chain. It makes for a memorable active detour for touring cyclists seeking an adrenaline break mid-route.
1a467a9986: The Cowichan Community Centre is a regional-district-operated community facility in Duncan, BC, formerly known as the Island Savings Centre. It serves the broader Cowichan Valley area as a multi-use civic venue. A touring cyclist passing through Duncan might consider it a potential rest stop, though specific cycling-oriented amenities are not confirmed.
66b26a9a0f: Thompson Community Centre is a City of Richmond civic recreation facility serving the south Richmond neighbourhood near Granville Avenue. As part of Richmond's network of publicly operated community centres, it offers recreational programming to local residents and visitors. Touring cyclists passing through Richmond's flat, cycling-friendly terrain may find it a convenient rest point, though specific cyclist-oriented amenities are unconfirmed.
f2ac81b27d: St. Joseph's Catholic Church is the oldest church in Kamloops, built jointly by Catholic missionaries and the Tk'emlups te Secwepemc in the late 19th century on Tk'emlups band lands near the industrial park. Designated a Canadian heritage site, it has been fully renovated with artifacts restored, including a striking gold-gilded altar. For a touring cyclist with an interest in Indigenous and colonial history, it represents a rare surviving piece of early Kamloops cultural heritage.
082c227c48: Beban Park Pool is an indoor public swimming pool operated by the City of Nanaimo within the Beban Park recreational complex. It offers drop-in swim sessions alongside programmed aquatic activities for residents and visitors. For touring cyclists, it represents a chance to relax and recover in a heated indoor pool mid-route through Nanaimo.
332f63c0b7: The Westside Learning Lab is a community branch of the Okanagan Regional Library, a 30-branch regional system established in 1936 that serves over 399,000 people across south-central British Columbia. Located on the Okanagan Highway on Kelowna's west side, it gives the public free access to ORL's digital collections, e-learning resources, and system-wide programs including Makerspaces and a Library of Things technology-lending service. As a publicly accessible library branch it provides a useful rest stop for touring cyclists passing through the Westside corridor.
9b9c341e2a: False Creek is an urban inlet cutting through the heart of Vancouver, best known to cyclists as the body of water encircled by Vancouver's world-famous seawall multi-use path. The waterway separates downtown Vancouver from the False Creek South and Olympic Village neighbourhoods, and the surrounding shoreline offers continuous, car-free cycling along parks, marinas, and public plazas. It is a central landmark on any cycling tour of Vancouver's waterfront.
dfb235a5a6: Admiralty Point Lands is a nature reserve on Indian Arm in the Belcarra area of North Vancouver, part of the broader Belcarra Regional Park managed by Metro Vancouver. The waterfront lands offer coastal forest and shoreline habitat. Despite the OSM name crediting Parks Canada, the area appears to fall under Metro Vancouver Regional Parks stewardship.
73bec51dd9: Alliance Française Vancouver is a Francophone cultural centre serving the city since 1904, now housed in a new three-storey building in the Oakridge neighbourhood that opened in 2024. It hosts public cultural events including film screenings, theatre, concerts, art exhibitions, and book clubs, alongside a French-language library and a VR library. Conveniently accessible via the Canada Line (Oakridge–41st or Langara–49th stations), it offers a welcoming cultural stop for curious visitors.
c85d32651a: Pearkes Recreation Centre is a municipally operated multi-sport facility run by Saanich Parks & Recreation in the Tillicum neighbourhood of Victoria. As a full-service community recreation centre, it serves as a practical stop for touring cyclists passing through the western side of the city. The centre is publicly accessible and part of the broader Saanich Parks & Recreation network.
4047d36182: Ground Up Climbing Centre is Squamish's anchor indoor climbing gym, offering both roped climbing and bouldering in a town world-famous for its outdoor granite walls and deep adventure culture. The gym caters to everyone from first-timers to competitive youth teams, and visiting climbers stopping in for a session are explicitly welcomed. For touring cyclists rolling through Squamish, it offers a direct connection to the region's iconic climbing scene right in the heart of town.
ce3b86998a: The Chilliwack Visitor Centre is operated by Tourism Chilliwack and serves as the official gateway for trip planning in the Fraser Valley region. It offers downloadable guides, local event listings, and connections to outdoor adventure, farm experiences, and arts and culture. For a touring cyclist passing through Chilliwack, it is a practical first stop for maps, local knowledge, and regional cycling routes.
732ce84ad0: The Penticton Public Library is a full-service community library on Main Street in the heart of Penticton, offering free public Wi-Fi, computers, printing, scanning, and a makerspace. It runs a 'Library of Things' lending program that includes outdoor exploration gear alongside tech items like Nintendo Switch consoles. For touring cyclists, it serves as a practical downtown hub for connectivity, rest, and trip planning.
8b52e913fb: The Daajing Giids branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served this remote Haida Gwaii community since 1983 and is housed in the refurbished Community Hall. Situated on the traditional territory of the Haida Nation, it is one of the few public indoor spaces available to touring cyclists exploring the archipelago. The branch offers free public Wi-Fi and public computer access, making it a practical waypoint in an area with limited connectivity.
93e3455003: Dog Mermaid Eco & Indigenous Excursions is an Indigenous-led outdoor adventure company operating since 2010 from two Southern Gulf Island resort bases — Poets Cove Resort on Pender Island and Mayne Island Resort on Mayne Island. The company offers guided kayak tours, paddleboard rentals, hiking, yoga, kids camps, and multi-day island excursions with a strong emphasis on Indigenous ecological knowledge and marine education. A touring cyclist exploring the Gulf Islands could easily incorporate a half-day or full-day water excursion into their trip.
7c7a594e3d: A volunteer-operated, admit-by-donation nature interpretive centre perched at the edge of the Cowichan Estuary — a 400-hectare ecosystem and internationally designated Important Bird Area — in Hecate Park, Cowichan Bay. Visitors can explore interactive exhibits about the estuary, marine and bird life, and the Cowichan and Koksilah watersheds, including a live heron-rookery webcam. For touring cyclists passing through Cowichan Bay, it doubles as a tourist information hub and a quiet stop to learn about one of Vancouver Island's most ecologically significant coastal habitats.
694729d861: Newton Recreation Centre is a City of Surrey municipal facility featuring a wave pool, wading pool, hot tub, and steam room. It offers drop-in fitness, sport, and swimming activities and is conveniently located next to a bus route. Touring cyclists passing through Surrey's Newton neighbourhood could stop in for a refreshing swim.
face957118: A nature reserve protected by Islands Trust Conservancy, also known by its Hul'qumi'num name S'ul-hween X'pey. Located in the Nanaimo area within the Islands Trust region, it is part of a network of conservation lands preserved over 31 years of partnership between the Conservancy, local organizations, and landowners.
11724e87bb: Founded in 1958 and operated by the Princeton and District Museum and Archives Society, this community museum houses an impressive range of collections including over 40,000 fossil and mineral specimens, a First Peoples basket display, approximately 10,000 historic photographs, and an original 1880s cabin. It has grown from a small log cabin to a multi-wing facility and is widely praised as one of the best small-town museums in BC. Touring cyclists interested in the natural and human history of the Similkameen Valley will find it a rewarding stop.
603fee4a91: Trethewey House is a 1920s heritage home built for B.C. timber baron J.O. Trethewey, restored to its circa-1925 appearance and operated as a history museum by the non-profit MSA Museum Society in Abbotsford. The Arts and Crafts-style house was constructed of first-growth fir milled at the family's own Abbotsford Lumber Company and features bricks made from locally mined clay. It serves as a living record of the Fraser Valley's early industrial and domestic history.
c9bccfc1a6: Nakusp Hot Springs is a community-owned natural mineral hot springs facility nestled in the Kuskanax Valley in the foothills of the Selkirk Mountains, accessible via a 14 km paved road northeast of the village of Nakusp. The site features two soaking pools continuously fed by natural mineral springs, set within over 200 acres of year-round outdoor recreation including hiking and biking trails. As of 2025, 70 hectares surrounding the springs have been formally designated as a protected natural area under the Municipal Protected Areas Project.
98c5ac660f: The Chinese Cultural Centre of Greater Vancouver is a long-established community institution at the heart of Vancouver's historic Chinatown, operating the largest Chinese language school in British Columbia with over 300 classes in Cantonese and Mandarin. Beyond education, it hosts Cantonese opera performances, calligraphy competitions, and organized walking tours of Chinatown, making it a genuine cultural landmark for visitors. A separate museum and archives facility preserving Chinese-Canadian heritage operates at 555 Columbia Street nearby.
aa605756d9: Roy Henry Vickers Gallery is a world-renowned First Nations art gallery in Tofino built in 1986 by artist Roy Henry Vickers himself alongside close friends and family. The building is modelled after a traditional Northwest Coast longhouse with cedar-planked walls, and showcases limited edition prints, original paintings, and carvings that draw visitors from around the world. It is considered a cultural landmark in Tofino and a distinctive stop on BC's west coast.
a0e32727ce: Science World is Vancouver's iconic science museum housed in a striking geodesic dome on the False Creek waterfront, operated as a charitable non-profit focused on STEAM education. Visitors explore interactive, hands-on exhibits and galleries designed to spark curiosity across all ages. The museum actively engages with the cycling community, hosting Go By Bike Week events and situated along one of Vancouver's most popular waterfront cycling corridors.
dd40c868b3: Historic Greenaway Outdoor Pool is a free seasonal outdoor swimming pool operated by the City of Surrey, located in Greenaway Park on 60th Avenue just east of Fraser Downs Racetrack. It offers free public swims and swimming lessons during summer months, making it a welcome refreshment stop for touring cyclists passing through Surrey's south side.
459ca02985: The BC Forest Discovery Centre is a 100-acre open-air museum in Duncan, BC, featuring an operational narrow-gauge railway, forest and marsh trails, heritage logging camp buildings, and exhibits chronicling the history of BC's coastal forest industry. Visitors can walk through an 1930s logging camp, board a steam or gas-powered train, and explore over a century of forestry artifacts and heritage structures. The museum is operated by the BC Forest Museum Society, a registered charitable non-profit, and hosts seasonal special events throughout the year.
13f569d8b1: The Juan de Fuca Branch is part of the Greater Victoria Public Library system, serving the western communities of the Capital Regional District along the Island Highway corridor. As a public library it offers a welcoming, climate-controlled indoor space with public computers and digital collections. It is operated by the Greater Victoria Public Library, which maintains a network of branches across the greater Victoria area.
a33ddb27f2: Buhlman Road Park Reserve is a nature reserve near Sidney, BC, managed by the Capital Regional District. It appears to correspond to the CRD's Bulman Trail, a natural-surface trail in the Greater Victoria region. Touring cyclists exploring the Saanich Peninsula may use it as a short off-road detour through protected green space.
c251c29e14: Sea to Sea Regional Park is a wilderness nature reserve managed by the Capital Regional District in the hills above Sooke on southern Vancouver Island. It forms part of a green corridor linking regional parks and wilderness areas accessible from the Greater Victoria region. The park is listed in the CRD's regional parks and trails network, making it a potential destination or waypoint for touring cyclists exploring the Sooke area.
9ffe726c93: The Hedley Heritage Museum is a volunteer-run heritage museum celebrating the gold-rush mining history of Hedley and the Similkameen Valley, featuring a replica miner's cottage, a hospital and school exhibit, vintage mining machinery displayed across the street, and a Miners' Lounge with historical photographs and a family history centre. It doubles as the village's tourist information booth, making it a natural stop for cyclists passing through on Highway 3 (the Crowsnest). The on-site tea room with a shaded veranda and gift shop selling ore samples and local crafts add a pleasant rest-stop dimension.
551ac717f1: This information node sits at the entrance to The Butchart Gardens, a 122-year-old, 55-acre world-famous display garden in Brentwood Bay designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 2004. Still privately owned by the founding Butchart family, the gardens feature distinct themed sections—Sunken, Rose, Japanese, Italian, and Mediterranean—along with summer evening illuminations and fireworks. A touring cyclist arriving from Victoria (approximately 22 km via Highway 17 and Tanner Road) would find multiple dining venues and a gift store on site.
62a69aae83: Purgatory Lookout is a scenic viewpoint in the Bella Coola backcountry reachable via the West Nusatsum FSR, offering views of the Noeick River valley, Styx Mountain, and Purgatory Glacier. The 7.8 km route from Odegaard Falls is open to foot, bike, and motorized travel, and is described as an ideal mountain bike excursion through meadows, ponds, and talus slopes. The Noeick River valley below was repeatedly scoured by jökulhlaups — glacial outburst floods from Ape Lake — giving the landscape its dramatic character.
f9ad5f0e53: Forests for the World is a City of Prince George-managed park and trail destination, listed prominently in the city's parks-and-trails portfolio. Situated near Prince George, it is tagged in OpenStreetMap as a tourism attraction, suggesting it draws visitors as a destination in its own right. Touring cyclists passing through Prince George may find it a worthwhile stop, though specific on-site facilities could not be confirmed from available evidence.
64aefb62b7: Port Moody Public Library is the public library serving Port Moody and the broader Tri-Cities region, located in the Newport Village neighbourhood. Beyond books, the library lends unusual items like ukulele kits, coding kits, and 'Bat Packs,' and offers accessible-format materials for patrons with visual or physical disabilities. Free public Wi-Fi makes it a practical rest stop for touring cyclists looking to plan routes, check in, or simply decompress.
80b2546287: The Port Alice Branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library has served this remote North Vancouver Island community since 1972, on the unceded traditional territory of the Quatsino nation. As one of the few public indoor spaces in Port Alice, it offers free WiFi, public computers, printing, and photocopying in a wheelchair-accessible building. For touring cyclists riding the isolated north island routes, it provides a rare opportunity to rest indoors and get connected.
2045004dcf: Saanich Commonwealth Place is a large municipal aquatic and fitness centre operated by the District of Saanich, anchored by a 50-metre competition pool alongside a wave pool, tots pool, dive tank, and water slide — one of the most comprehensive aquatic complexes on Vancouver Island. The facility also offers a steam room, sauna, hot tub, weight room, gymnasium, and functional fitness studio, giving touring cyclists a rare opportunity to recover thoroughly after a long day on the road. It sits near Elk Lake, a popular cycling destination in its own right, making it a natural stop on routes through the Saanich Peninsula.
e479a98f20: The Wild Coast Nature Refuge is a 32-acre waterfront conservation area on Bowen Island at Cape Roger Curtis, acquired by the Bowen Island Conservancy in December 2020. It protects a rare coast bluff ecosystem where whales can be spotted just offshore from lichen-covered cliffs, and a Conservation Covenant ensures permanent protection of its biological diversity. Public access is limited to a loop walking trail connecting viewpoints on the coastal bluffs.
9a602a6e68: Bard on the Beach is Western Canada's largest not-for-profit professional Shakespeare Festival, staging plays and special events in two modern performance tents set against a backdrop of mountains, sea, and sky in Vancouver's Sen̓áḵw/Vanier Park. Now in its 37th season, the festival presents multiple Shakespeare productions alongside related dramas and special events such as improv nights. The Vanier Park site sits directly along Vancouver's waterfront seawall cycling corridor, making it a natural cultural stop for touring cyclists exploring the city's coastline.
c3ac7e1bbe: The Kilby Historic Site is BC's only reminder of the once-thriving community of Harrison Mills, centred on an original 1906 general store now filled with artifacts, hands-on activities, and costumed interpreters. The site encompasses heritage farm buildings, friendly farm animals, a café, and a 41-site campground — making it a rare attraction where touring cyclists can arrive, explore, eat, and camp all in one place. Celebrating its 120th anniversary, it sits in a scenic corner of the Fraser Valley within easy riding distance of Mission, Chilliwack, and Harrison Hot Springs.
506fdafec4: The Surrey Nature Centre is a publicly operated interpretive facility nestled alongside Green Timbers Urban Forest, one of Surrey's largest tracts of second-growth forest. Visitors can borrow activity backpacks or fishing rods from the front desk, explore the Birds of Green Timbers exhibit, and browse a library of field guides and nature books. The centre serves as a natural trailhead destination for cyclists exploring the Green Timbers Urban Forest trail network.
ce6e316d96: Britannia Branch is a public branch of the Vancouver Public Library serving the Grandview-Woodland neighbourhood. As a publicly operated library, it offers free access to books, digital resources, and community programming. For touring cyclists passing through East Vancouver, it represents a free, welcoming rest stop in a well-serviced urban neighbourhood.
cb5af72e36: Malkin Bowl is an outdoor amphitheatre nestled in Stanley Park, hosting live music concerts and the long-running Theatre Under the Stars productions. The venue is accessed directly from Stanley Park's main cycling and walking paths, making it an easy stop or evening destination for touring cyclists exploring the seawall. General admission standing with a hillside viewing area gives it a relaxed, festival-like atmosphere.
3dee14d47e: The Japanese Garden is a tranquil ornamental garden located within Polson Park in Vernon, BC. Polson Park is a large municipal park in the heart of the city and is a popular stop for visitors passing through the Okanagan. The Japanese Garden forms a scenic centrepiece within the park grounds.
ba2d864844: The Seymour River Fish Hatchery & Education Centre is operated by the non-profit Seymour Salmonid Society and raises hundreds of thousands of coho, steelhead, chum, and pink salmon annually to supplement fish stocks cut off from spawning grounds by Seymour Falls Dam. The society runs a well-regarded 'Gently Down the Seymour' education program serving 1,200–1,500 school children per year and hosts public events such as Family Fishing Day. Access to the hatchery site is gate-controlled and the road is explicitly stated to be not open to the general public.
89df13103b: North Delta Centre for the Arts is a municipal arts facility operated by the City of Delta, located in the North Delta neighbourhood. It serves the local community as a venue for arts and cultural programming. Touring cyclists exploring the Fraser Delta region may find it a worthwhile cultural stop.
05c0092256: Panorama Recreation Centre is a large community recreation facility operated by the Peninsula Recreation Commission, serving the communities of North Saanich, Central Saanich, and Sidney on the Saanich Peninsula. The centre includes a full aquatic complex with pools, a waterslide, lazy river, and hot tub, alongside arenas, a weight room, fitness studio, and racquet courts. Touring cyclists passing through the area will find accessible changerooms with showers and a notably comprehensive accessibility infrastructure.
10f568d48d: The Dunbar Branch is a neighborhood outpost of the Vancouver Public Library system, serving the quiet residential Dunbar-Southlands area of Vancouver's west side. As a free, publicly accessible municipal building, it offers a welcoming rest stop for touring cyclists moving through this part of the city. The branch sits on a low-traffic stretch of Dunbar Street, making it an easy detour off the north-south corridor.
1f529097eb: 8EAST is a social space for new culture operated by the New Orchestra Workshop (NOW) Society in the heart of Vancouver's Historic Chinatown. It functions as a meeting place and performance venue for musicians and community members, hosting regular improvised music events, installations, and artist talks. A touring cyclist interested in Vancouver's contemporary arts scene might stop in for a performance, but the space offers no confirmed cyclist-specific services.
4ae600fbf7: Rocky Point Swimming Pool is a seasonal outdoor public pool operated by the City of Port Moody, located within Rocky Point Park. The facility offers public swims, swim lessons, and Aquafit classes during the summer season. Rocky Point Park sits along the Burrard Inlet shoreline, making it a scenic stop for cyclists exploring the Tri-Cities area.
f5417b38b2: Centre 64 is Kimberley's community arts hub, operated by the Kimberley Arts Council in partnership with the City of Kimberley. It hosts a 126-seat theatre, a 1,050 sq ft gallery with two-storey ceilings, a pottery studio, and regular programming spanning film screenings, live theatre, live music, and art workshops. A touring cyclist looking to engage with local culture would find a lively, year-round venue at the heart of this Bavarian-themed mountain town.
cd3fa70932: The Nisg̱aʼa Museum in Lax̱g̱altsʼap (Greenville) is the official cultural institution of the Nisg̱aʼa Nation, housing ancestral regalia, art, and historical artifacts returned to the community. Designed by Hillel Architecture, the building itself is architecturally significant and sits within Nisg̱aʼa Lands in the remote Nass Valley of northwestern BC. For touring cyclists venturing into this rarely visited region, it offers a compelling cultural destination at the end of a long ride.
d167f847f6: The Studio & Stage Door is a city-owned heritage building dating to 1909, originally built by the local Masons as their Temple, and home to Cranbrook Community Theatre for over 50 years. dcb786fee2: Established in 1991, Spirit Gallery is an Aboriginal-owned West Coast Native Art gallery located in Horseshoe Bay, steps from the waterfront of Howe Sound. It carries an extensive collection of carvings, jewellery, prints, and gifts from both renowned and emerging Indigenous artists. For cyclists riding the Sea to Sky corridor or catching the Horseshoe Bay ferry, the gallery is a distinctive cultural stop in a walkable village setting.
079ba0b0e9: The Public Mineral Pool in Harrison Hot Springs is an indoor facility fed by the area's famous natural mineral hot springs, one of the most celebrated hot spring destinations in British Columbia. Operated as a public pool on Hot Springs Road, it offers access to geothermally heated mineral water in a setting long prized for its restorative qualities. For a touring cyclist arriving after a long day in the saddle, a soak here would be a memorable highlight of the Harrison River Valley.
4d5b2c2a75: The Centre of the Universe is the visitor centre of the Dominion Astrophysical Observatory, a National Historic Site perched on a hill about 20 minutes from downtown Victoria. 1041574074: The Sid Williams Theatre is a 500-seat performing arts centre in downtown Courtenay, BC, operated by the Sid Williams Theatre Society as a registered charitable organization. c936d5ee0b: Western Financial Place (locally known as Rex Plex) is Cranbrook's primary arena and multi-use recreation complex, home to the Junior A Cranbrook Bucks hockey team and a wide range of live events. e4fa352a58: A single-storey municipal community centre in the Albion neighbourhood of Maple Ridge, operated by the City. 1bf7b56446: George Derby Conservation Area is a nature reserve located in Burnaby, BC, offering natural green space within the Metro Vancouver region. 3843ad1791: A collaborative community food garden in Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, situated between Main Street and Scotia Street. c7059d30bc: The Little Campbell River Hatchery is a fish hatchery operated by the Semiahmoo Fish & Game Club, a community-based conservation organization in Surrey, BC. 975dcaff5e: A volunteer-run community centre on Quadra Island, situated in Blenkin Memorial Park in Quathiaski Cove. eaa33014c1: The Chilliwack Cultural Centre is the Fraser Valley's primary performing arts and creative hub, featuring two performance theatres, an art gallery, 21 music studios, and four arts and crafts studios on the traditional territory of the Stó:lō Coast Salish People. 55a1607f34: Queen Elizabeth Park sits at 125 metres above sea level — Vancouver's highest point — and spans 52 hectares of gardens, arboretum, and public art, including Henry Moore's 'Knife Edge-Two Piece.' Fine dining is available at Seasons in the Park, and a designated picnic area with BBQ pits sits among the arboretum trees on the north side.
5b5ba20d76: Robert's Lake Regional Park is a nature reserve and regional park situated near Kelowna in British Columbia's Okanagan region. 84f17140ac: The Pomeroy Sport Centre is a large municipal recreation facility in Fort St. John operated by the City. 3710ef0baa: Harper Mountain is a family-owned ski hill that has operated since 1973, sitting just 20 minutes from Kamloops with 1,400 vertical feet of terrain across more than 400 acres. b3c4946648: Yellow Bird Arts Gallery is a locally-owned art gallery and custom framing studio located inside Country Club Centre mall in Nanaimo, with over 30 years serving Central Vancouver Island. 80608b58ba: The Rotary Interpretive Centre is a volunteer-run nature education facility within the Great Blue Heron Nature Reserve, built and donated by the Chilliwack Rotary Club in the early 2000s and now welcoming over 20,000 visitors annually. Touring cyclists passing through the Sumas Prairie area will find a genuinely welcoming community stop open nearly every day of the year.
1fc69bfb09: Templeton Park Pool is a City of Vancouver-operated indoor aquatic facility in the Grandview-Woodland neighbourhood, featuring an inground pool and sauna. bde28119bb: Glenora Trails Head Park is a Cowichan Valley Regional District park near Duncan on Vancouver Island, providing trailhead access to the Glenora trail network. 79e71334f3: The Chemainus Theatre Festival is a fully professional, non-profit theatre in the seaside community of Chemainus on Vancouver Island, presenting Canadian performers in a 274-seat wheelchair-accessible auditorium with a raked floor for clear sightlines from every seat. 17673b1577: Osoyoos Desert Centre is a 67-acre nature interpretive facility operated by the Osoyoos Desert Society, showcasing one of Canada's rarest antelope-brush desert ecosystems in the South Okanagan. 2e903cc579: The Samuel and Frances Belzberg Library is the downtown Vancouver branch of Simon Fraser University Library, situated in the Harbour Centre building at the heart of the city's core. fe379a21de: Brennan Park Recreation Centre is Squamish's municipal multi-sport facility, hosting a swimming pool, ice hockey rink, and skating arena in the heart of one of BC's premier outdoor adventure towns. Touring cyclists passing through Squamish would find it a practical stop for public amenities in a well-maintained civic building.
f15a0ce92a: Chali-Rosso Art Gallery is a fine art gallery operating since 2005, specializing in original works on paper by Modern Masters including Picasso, Dalí, Chagall, Miró, and Matisse, alongside Inuit art and contemporary Canadian artists. 2c8bacc838: The FINA Gallery is a public art gallery space located in the foyer of the Creative and Critical Studies Building on the UBC Okanagan campus, programmed by the UBC Okanagan Gallery. 215aea7f76: The Cumberland Branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the community since 1947, now operating from a purpose-built ~3,200 sq. ft. civic building on Dunsmuir Avenue that opened in 2013. f0bf745c0e: The Vogue Theatre is a 1,161-capacity Art Deco concert hall built in 1941 on Vancouver's historic Granville Street entertainment strip, one of the last surviving venues from the city's famed Theatre Row. 4a3c22eb1f: The Rose Garden is a public park in Sidney, BC, maintained by the Town of Sidney and listed among its official parks. 616954d821: Munson Mountain Park is a municipal nature reserve and prominent hilltop landmark in Penticton, BC, managed by the City of Penticton. c4c88c3c9d: The Jim Ciccone Civic Center is Prince Rupert's main municipal sports and recreation complex, operated by the City of Prince Rupert's Recreation Department. 59de4f43ed: Cliff McNabb Arena is a City of Nanaimo municipal ice arena located in Nanaimo on Vancouver Island. It is part of the city's parks and recreation network, offering skating programs and arena activities. It functions primarily as a local sports facility rather than a visitor attraction.
d2076aa590: The Cowichan Aquatic Centre is a public swimming facility operated by the Municipality of North Cowichan, located in Duncan on southern Vancouver Island. e80141ff80: The Nanaimo Wellington branch of Vancouver Island Regional Library is a public library situated inside Country Club Centre, halfway between downtown Nanaimo and the north end of the city. c66f7337f5: The Cowichan Community Centre Sports Complex is a major public recreation facility in Duncan operated by the Cowichan Valley Regional District. d089fb3ea7: Landmark Cinemas is a major Canadian cinema chain with a Fort St. John location in a commercial area on 93 Avenue. d17ce4694c: The Agassiz-Harrison Museum & Visitor Centre occupies one of Canada's oldest surviving wood-built Canadian Pacific Railway stations, constructed in 1893 and located in the heart of downtown Agassiz. 19f2fb0ccd: Brocklehurst Pool is a municipal outdoor swimming pool operated by the City of Kamloops, located in the Brocklehurst neighbourhood. f8166aa48d: BC Wildlife Park is a non-profit wildlife park and rehabilitation centre in Kamloops, BC, operating since 1965 and home to nearly 200 animals representing 65 species native to British Columbia, including cougars, wolves, bears, and the only Kermode bear in human care in the world. eed808bd1c: The Ferry Building Gallery is a public community art gallery housed in a heritage building over 100 years old at Ambleside Landing in West Vancouver, operated by the District of West Vancouver. bc7d214af5: The Archie Browning Sports Centre is a municipally operated recreation facility in Esquimalt, run by the Township of Esquimalt. 7ef0ab3260: Blackburn Lake Nature Reserve is an 18.4-hectare protected area managed by the Salt Spring Island Conservancy, surrounding about two-thirds of Blackburn Lake at the geographic centre of Salt Spring Island. Cyclists exploring Salt Spring Island can lock up and walk the trails, though dogs are strictly prohibited to protect the sensitive wildlife habitat.
170d6ac1dc: The Mount Pleasant Branch of the Vancouver Public Library is a public branch library serving the Mount Pleasant neighbourhood at the corner of Kingsway. d4fb042974: The Inverholme Schoolhouse is a preserved one-room schoolhouse originally built in 1909 in East Ladner and physically relocated to Deas Island Regional Park in 1981, where it stands as a heritage museum within the park grounds. 7e8eef4bd8: A municipal recreation centre operated by the City of Delta in the North Delta area. As a sports centre it likely offers fitness and recreation programs for the surrounding community. cc26cfa32e: The Karen Magnussen Community Recreation Centre is a public facility operated by North Vancouver Recreation and Culture (NVRC), offering an aquatic centre, arena, fitness centre, and multipurpose gymnasiums. 8ea5ec5d42: Kariton Art Gallery + Boutique is a community art gallery operated by the Abbotsford Arts Council, housed in a detached heritage building on Ware Street in Abbotsford. e906e8948a: La Boussole (French for 'the compass') is a Francophone community centre and NGO serving Vancouver's French-speaking community at 312 Main Street in the Downtown Eastside. 99d2ead30a: Sir Landon James Charters is an Indigenous-owned and operated boat charter company in Tofino, led by Captain Bert Tom, a proud member of the Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation whose ancestors have called these waters home for over 10,000 years. f3ee16e085: The Oliver & District Heritage Society Museum is a not-for-profit community museum preserving the history of Oliver and the surrounding Okanagan region, encompassing mining heritage, First Nations culture, and the agricultural story of Canada's Wine Capital. 5ea5d2bed9: O'Keefe Ranch is a historic living museum near Vernon, BC, preserving one of British Columbia's oldest cattle ranches across a sprawling multi-building property with year-round resident farm animals. b5dc236fb1: Helmcken House is one of the oldest surviving residential buildings in British Columbia, constructed in 1852 for Dr. John Sebastian Helmcken, a physician and influential figure in early colonial BC politics. ddb6123eee: Ian Tan Gallery is a long-established (1999) contemporary Canadian art gallery occupying a striking storefront on Vancouver's South Granville arts corridor, known for its floor-to-ceiling windows and soaring ceilings filled with rotating exhibitions of paintings, drawings, glass works, and sculpture. b71cca53fa: Clayton Community Centre is Surrey's newest municipal recreation facility, operated by the City of Surrey and combining fitness and recreation programs, a branch library, and childminding services under one roof. c5ae10f818: Browne Creek Wetlands is a nature reserve situated within the Vedder Greenway along the south bank of the Vedder River in Chilliwack. ed4c14224c: Fort Langley Library is a public branch of the Fraser Valley Regional Library (FVRL) system, nestled in the heritage village of Fort Langley. 0a0fdbcd06: Britannia Shipyards National Historic Site is a free, eight-acre outdoor heritage site on the banks of the Fraser River in Steveston, showcasing the oldest shipyard community in British Columbia through preserved heritage buildings arranged along a wooden boardwalk. 0eb046bb98: A 58-acre nonprofit organic teaching farm and garden nestled between Harrison Hot Springs and Agassiz, featuring restored wetlands, old-growth forest groves, heritage farmhouse and barn circa 1910, and a trail system with interpretive signs along the Miami River. 00fae03bd5: The Sooke branch of the Vancouver Island Regional Library has served the community since 1963, sitting on the unceded traditional territory of the T'sou-ke First Nation. c0c0cebbe5: Ucluelet Community Centre is a municipal recreation facility run by the District of Ucluelet, offering seasonal programs in fitness, arts, and youth activities. 50505ad47e: False Creek Community Centre is a publicly operated civic facility on Granville Island, jointly managed by the Vancouver Park Board and the non-profit False Creek Community Association since 1980. 2ff8f1c561: The Marianne and Edward Gibson Art Museum is a new purpose-built public art museum on SFU's Burnaby Mountain campus that opened in Fall 2025, consolidating SFU Galleries' collections into a single, more accessible facility. 3aa938a8bf: Climb Base5 is a premier indoor rock climbing facility in Coquitlam offering bouldering, auto-belay, top rope, and lead climbing for all skill levels. 9e12422efd: Seabreeze Gallery is a cooperative art gallery nestled in the heart of Snug Cove on Bowen Island, dedicated exclusively to handmade works by local artists spanning jewellery, glassblowing, sculpture, painting, fibre arts, ceramics, leatherwork, and more. 4e653a47a0: The Centennial Activity Centre is a City of Coquitlam recreation facility built around a large gymnasium operated jointly with School District 43. de03e34b70: The Recreation Centre sits within the Royal Roads University campus at Hatley Park, a 260-hectare National Historic Site roughly 25 minutes west of downtown Victoria. 9d88a80594: River Wrangler Sportfishing is a fully licensed and insured Fraser Valley outfitter specializing in White Sturgeon and Salmon fishing on the Fraser and Harrison rivers. 9507a54f15: Ladner Leisure Centre is a City of Delta-operated municipal recreation facility in the Ladner neighbourhood, with swimming as its primary programmed sport. eb46ec1a6d: Romper Room is a long-established indoor rock climbing centre that has served the mid Vancouver Island climbing community since 1996, offering 7,500 sq ft of climbing surface including top rope, lead walls, a bouldering cave, auto-belays, and two MoonBoards. 1fef9574a5: Champlain Heights Community Centre is a neighbourhood recreation hub in southeast Vancouver featuring a fitness centre with sauna, squash and racquetball courts, a dance studio, and indoor cycling programs. c9cfabe3fc: The Castlegar and District Community Complex is a publicly operated recreation facility run by the Regional District of Central Kootenay, serving residents and visitors in the Castlegar area. ea4cda576f: Forbes Hall Community Centre is the civic heart of Thetis Island, a quiet Gulf Island in the Salish Sea reachable by ferry from Chemainus.
