It offers public computers, Wi-Fi, printing, and wheelchair-accessible premises. A notable feature is the adjacent StoryWalk® in Fadear Park next door, where pages of a rotating children's picture book are installed outdoors for a combined walking-and-reading experience.
d96cb12be3: The Clearwater Wells Gray Park Visitors Centre is operated by Information Wells Gray, a non-profit organization serving as the primary information hub for Wells Gray Provincial Park — one of BC's largest wilderness parks at over 5,000 km². Touring cyclists passing through Clearwater can access up-to-date trail reports, road conditions, and park regulations, as well as guidance on camping, canoeing, hiking, and wildlife. The centre is the logical first stop for anyone planning to explore the park's iconic waterfalls, backcountry routes, or hut-to-hut trail system.
6e20f1e755: Jamieson Woods Nature Preserve is a public nature reserve near Hudson's Hope in northern BC, notable for its ancient sand dunes and likely old-growth aspen forest. Listed among the district's trail network, it sits in a remote and scenic part of the Peace River region that touring cyclists on northern BC routes may pass through.
5662249b2e: Beaver Lodge Forest Lands is a 520-hectare public forest within the city of Campbell River, featuring diverse habitats including stands with old-growth characteristics such as Douglas-fir, western redcedar, and Sitka spruce. Originally donated in 1931 as one of BC's first operational forest plantations, it is now protected under its own provincial legislation and offers a network of trails for walking, running, and cycling. The Greenways Loop trail connects through the forest lands, making it an accessible natural stop for touring cyclists passing through Campbell River.
781d3a2e73: McMillan Creek Regional Park is a free public natural area in Prince George where McMillan Creek flows through a forested ravine of Douglas fir on its way to the Nechako River cutbanks. Visitors can choose between a 2.5 km trail or a shorter 1 km route leading to a scenic overlook of the river and the city beyond. The creek is a protected rainbow trout spawning habitat with special provincial fishing regulations, and interpretive signage explains the ecology along the way.
6d7b06a3f3: The Aldergrove Community Centre is a large Township of Langley recreation facility featuring an aquatic complex with a wave pool, waterslides, diving boards, hot tub, and sauna, alongside an ice arena and fitness centre. Extensive accessibility infrastructure includes a portable aquatic lift and water wheelchair ramp into the social pool. A touring cyclist would find showers, change rooms, washrooms, and multiple food options within a single facility.
71ad7b4e8f: Strike Zone is a long-running Prince George institution founded in 1994, offering 16 lanes of 10-pin bowling alongside an 18-hole themed indoor glow-in-the-dark mini golf course and an arcade — all under one roof with no reservations required. It is one of the few combined bowling-and-mini-golf venues in BC's central interior, making it a distinctive stop for touring cyclists seeking an off-bike activity in Prince George.
15230c22ae: The Houston Public Library is a community public library serving the small town of Houston in BC's Central Interior, offering books, digital resources, computer and internet access, meeting room rentals, and office services including printing, copying, faxing, and scanning. For touring cyclists passing through this remote stretch of highway, it provides a sheltered stop with free internet access and a range of community resources. The library also curates local community information links, making it a useful orientation point for visitors unfamiliar with the region.
70ae167c08: Little Hell's Gate Regional Park is a TNRD-managed regional park in the North Thompson corridor, named for its dramatic canyon scenery reminiscent of the famous Hell's Gate on the Fraser River. Sitting at roughly 51.9°N near the confluence of rugged interior BC geography, it is tagged as a viewpoint in OpenStreetMap, suggesting a scenic overlook experience. Touring cyclists riding through the Cariboo, Chilcotin and Central Interior region may find it a worthwhile detour for the views.
33b8caeaa9: Houston Leisure Centre is a municipal recreation facility operated by the District of Houston in northern BC's Bulkley Valley. It features a swimming pool and offers programs for both residents and visitors. For touring cyclists on Highway 16, it may provide a welcome stop for recreation and refreshment in this small community.
c4d05fcadb: Kʷuḥaa Conservancy is a BC Parks-managed nature conservancy on Vancouver Island, protecting significant natural and cultural values in the coastal wilderness near latitude 49.4°N. Conservancies in BC permit compatible low-impact recreation alongside conservation objectives, making them potential waypoints for adventure-touring cyclists exploring the island's remote western reaches. The Indigenous name reflects the area's connection to First Nations whose territories encompass this land.
36bea1539b: The Golden & District Library is a branch of the Okanagan Regional Library, serving the Golden community in BC's Columbia Valley as part of one of Canada's larger regional library networks. It houses an ORL Makerspace equipped with an Audio Recording Studio, Creation Station, Digitization Stations, Video Recording Equipment, and a Cricut cutting machine. Free car parking is available both in front and behind the building, and a book drop bin is accessible on the exterior when the library is closed.
13a2c0b947: Gibsons Beach is a public ocean beach on the northern edge of Powell River near the Wildwood neighbourhood, offering a mix of sand and rocky shoreline along the Salish Sea. It is less busy than the city's main Willingdon Beach and is popular for beachcombing, family picnics, and exploring the tideline. A small boat launch is also present, making it a quiet, multi-use foreshore stop.
c9407b560c: Prince Rupert Visitor Information Centre is the official tourism information hub for Prince Rupert, BC — a coastal city on British Columbia's wild North Coast that serves as a gateway to the Great Bear Rainforest, world-class fishing, and rich Ts'msyen cultural heritage. The centre provides maps, brochures, and downloadable guides covering hiking trails, wildlife viewing, outdoor adventure, and local dining, and also offers phone and email visitor services. For a touring cyclist arriving by BC Ferries or venturing through this remote northern destination, it is a practical first stop for trip planning and local orientation.
b406010caf: The Terrace Public Library has served the community since 1929 and has been at its Park Avenue location since 1967, sitting on traditional Tsimshian territories. Beyond standard lending, it offers a notable 'Library of Things' program, a publicly accessible 3D printer, remote printing, and an extensive e-library with dozens of digital databases and streaming resources. It functions as a genuine community hub in a northern BC city that touring cyclists use as a resupply stop on the Yellowhead corridor.
167f7c109b: Bear Creek Regional Nature Park is a nature reserve in the Comox Valley on Vancouver Island, managed by the Comox Valley Regional District. It offers a natural green space for outdoor recreation in a region popular with touring cyclists exploring Vancouver Island's trails and coastlines. The park's setting along the Comox Valley makes it a potential rest or exploration stop on cycling routes through the area.
398db1ec49: The Fort Nelson Public Library serves this remote northern BC community at the heart of Municipal Square, offering a broad range of programs and digital services well beyond a typical small-town library. Located along the Alaska Highway corridor, it is a notable waypoint for long-distance cycle tourists in one of the most isolated stretches of the province. The library provides free public internet access, a seed library, meeting rooms, and an unusually rich roster of community programming.
86fba4ff94: Ronning's Garden is a heritage garden carved from BC's northern rainforest by Norwegian homesteader Bernt Ronning, who established his homestead here in 1910 near the terminus of the old San Josef Wagon Road and filled it with exotic plants ordered from around the world. The garden is renowned for hosting one of the oldest and largest Monkey Puzzle trees in British Columbia. Maintained today by a small group of volunteers and free to enter, it is a remarkable off-the-beaten-path destination for cyclists exploring the Cape Scott region of Vancouver Island North, reached by a ten-minute walk along a restored section of the historic wagon road.
db51302918: The Clearwater Library is a branch of the Thompson-Nicola Regional Library system with roots in the community dating to 1946, now housed in a recently renovated building featuring new siding, a covered entrance canopy, and an expanded children's area completed in 2025. It offers free public Wi-Fi, public computers, printing, and a wheelchair-accessible meeting room bookable by the public and non-profit groups. Located in Clearwater, a gateway town to Wells Gray Provincial Park, it sits along a popular cycling corridor in the Thompson-Nicola region.
af60f6bc90: The Forslund-Watson Conservation Land Complex is an 80-acre nature reserve in south Langley, BC, managed by the Langley Field Naturalists. The reserve is an active habitat restoration site where volunteers plant native trees and shrubs, remove invasive species, and maintain old-field habitat for raptors and other wildlife. Whether the reserve is open for general public visitation — and what access or facilities may exist — is not described anywhere on the organization's website.
5b63e2465f: The Trail Memorial Centre is a large multi-purpose recreation facility in Trail, BC, housing two hockey arenas, a curling club, a full gymnasium, racquetball and squash courts, meeting rooms, and a commercial kitchen. The TMC marked its 75th year of operation in 2024 and serves as a major community hub in the Kootenays. Touring cyclists passing through Trail may find it a useful landmark stop, with EV charging stations listed among its on-site amenities.
fb5fb56a8a: The Haylmore Heritage Site commemorates Will Haylmore, the original gold claim mine recorder in the Bridge River Valley, on the property where he lived and operated near Gold Bridge. The Bridge River Valley Community Association has restored one of the buildings and a stage on the grounds, and the site now serves as both a tourism information booth and a place to purchase locally produced artisan goods. A community-owned 4 kW solar array was installed at the site in 2015 as part of a regional renewable energy initiative.
ffb7862218: RavenSong Soap & Candle is an Indigenous-owned artisan shop on Vancouver Island specializing in handcrafted soaps, candles, bath products, and essential oils rooted in Northwest Coast storytelling and ceremony. The brand weaves cultural narrative into every product line, from Full Moon Ritual soaps to Northwest Coast Art Bars, and features work by Indigenous artists. A second retail location is opening in Downtown Campbell River, with the existing Willow Point store remaining open.
8b0435afea: Midway Public Library is a small but far-reaching community library serving the West Boundary of British Columbia, drawing patrons from Midway, Bridesville, Rock Creek, Westbridge, and Beaverdell. It offers physical collections alongside digital resources including ebooks and audiobooks via Libby, office services, and accessible programming. For touring cyclists passing through this remote stretch of Boundary Country, it is one of the few public institutions in the region offering community resources.
e2df75f1cb: The Mount Robson Visitor Centre is the official BC Parks Welcome Centre at the western entrance to Mount Robson Provincial Park, home to the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies at 3,954 m. Positioned along the Yellowhead Highway (Highway 16), it anchors the 63 km Mount Robson Corridor and serves as the primary information gateway for the world-renowned Berg Lake Trail. Touring cyclists on the transcontinental Yellowhead route will find it a natural stop amid some of the most dramatic mountain scenery in British Columbia.
18dbe89343: The Greenwood Museum Archives & Visitor Centre sits in Greenwood, BC, recognized as the smallest city in Canada, making it a singular cultural stop along a cycling route through the Boundary Country. The museum covers local mining, forestry, and Japanese-Canadian history, and offers a self-guided Heritage Walking Tour with maps available at the front desk. It also serves as the regional visitor centre, stocking provincial and local publications useful for cyclists planning onward routes.
8b890304ad: Cariboo Bowl is a 5-pin bowling alley serving the Williams Lake area of BC's Cariboo interior, offering public open bowling, a full slate of adult and youth leagues, and Friday-night Cosmic Bowl. The facility accommodates up to six bowlers per lane and accepts group and birthday-party bookings by reservation. For touring cyclists passing through the region, it provides a social indoor activity option, particularly useful during inclement weather.
9d189a3e7d: Confluence Climbing is Golden's indoor bouldering gym, offering roughly 1,200 sq ft of climbing surface across walls ranging from a 3-degree slab to a 45-degree overhang, plus Canada's first 12′×12′ adjustable Grasshopper board with a lit-hold, app-connected problem database. The facility also houses a fitness area with free weights, a rowing machine, a stationary bike, hangboards, and a mezzanine lounge. For touring cyclists passing through Golden, it's a standout rainy-day or rest-day option in a mountain town surrounded by the Purcells, Selkirks, and Rockies.
0bb2d61287: Saahlinda Naay (Saving Things House) is the Haida Gwaii Museum in Skidegate, a landmark cultural institution dedicated to Haida knowledge, language, art, and the islands' natural and supernatural heritage. It offers rotating temporary exhibitions alongside permanent galleries exploring the deep connections between the land, sea, and Haida peoples. For a touring cyclist passing through Haida Gwaii, it is one of the most compelling stops on the archipelago — a genuinely remote and rare cultural experience at the edge of the Pacific.
629dea5386: The Pesuta is the partially intact wooden hull of a Japanese log barge that ran aground on the north beach of Haida Gwaii on December 11, 1928, and has been weathering on the sand ever since. It sits within Naikoon Provincial Park, a vast wilderness of beach, bog, and old-growth forest on the traditional territory of the Haida Nation. Touring cyclists on Haida Gwaii typically reach it via a beach hike from the Tlell River trailhead, making it one of the most dramatic and remote landmarks on any BC cycling itinerary.
173dc439d8: Glover Community Nature Park is a forested nature reserve operated by the Comox Valley Regional District on Vancouver Island. It offers a natural woodland setting for quiet recreation and wildlife observation close to the Comox Valley communities. Touring cyclists looking for a green break or a short trail walk would find it a low-key stop between destinations.
c7c05d8931: YuWala Marine Charters operates out of Bella Bella, the gateway to the Great Bear Rainforest, offering Indigenous heritage and eco-tours led by knowledgeable Heiltsuk guides across the channels, fiords, and outer islands of BC's Central Coast. Tours include wildlife viewing of bears, wolves, whales, and eagles, as well as cultural storytelling, traditional salmon BBQs, and exploration of ancient clam gardens and rock carvings. The company also runs practical marine transportation — water taxis, dive charters, and crew shuttles — making it a key logistics hub for the remote Central Coast.
3dce431d90: The Mackenzie Rec Centre is a publicly operated community recreation facility run by the District of Mackenzie in northern BC. It appears within the district's broader Recreation, Arts & Culture portfolio alongside parks, trails, and program offerings. For a touring cyclist arriving in this remote northern community, it is likely one of the few public facilities offering indoor amenities.
7eb1199c01: A small-town public library housed in the historic Library and Pioneer Museum Building in Hazelton, in the Upper Skeena region. Beyond books, it features a Pioneer Museum, an art collection, and a local history reference collection that document the area's heritage. Touring cyclists will find free Wi-Fi, computer access, and a welcoming rest stop in a remote stretch of northern BC.
fa9a2436b4: A publicly operated single-sheet NHL regulation-sized ice arena and fitness centre in Sicamous, surrounded by the Shuswap region's mountain scenery. The facility also houses a recently renovated fitness centre with cardio and strength equipment, a concession stand, and a banquet hall used for tournaments and community events.
fb09e12f5c: Housed in the historic 1916 brick 'Dominion' building — originally Ashcroft's post office — this local history museum is considered one of the best in any BC village. Its collection spans Ashcroft's early 1900s 'Glory Days,' with exhibits honouring Indigenous Peoples, the Chinese community, ranching, fossils, and a popular coal mine reproduction. The museum also maintains extensive genealogical and historical archives available to visiting researchers.
8094ea0210: The Steward Visitor Centre is a two-storey tourist information office in Stewart, BC, at the head of the Portland Canal near the Alaska border — a remote but iconic stop for cyclists riding the Cassiar Highway. Stewart sits at one of Canada's most northerly ice-free ports, surrounded by glaciers, fjords, and wildlife, and the visitor centre serves as the gateway orientation point for the area. Mobile reception is confirmed on site.
9456de1da4: Willow Point Greenway is a linear nature reserve corridor in the Willow Point neighbourhood of Campbell River on Vancouver Island, providing a traffic-free green passage for cyclists and pedestrians. It forms part of the City of Campbell River's municipal parkland network and sits within easy reach of the Discovery Passage coastline. Touring cyclists passing through Campbell River can use it as a quieter off-road route through the southern part of the city.
babe43b311: SkyTrek Adventure Park is a family-oriented outdoor adventure park situated directly on the Trans-Canada Highway (Highway 1), roughly 32 km west of Revelstoke and 35 km east of Sicamous — a busy touring corridor. The park features a treetop Sky Course with over 30 aerial elements, zip lines, an adventure tower, and kids' zones, and shares its site with the well-known Enchanted Forest attraction. Its highway-accessible location makes it a natural mid-route stop for cyclists riding between Sicamous and Revelstoke.
dfb27cd651: Cliff Gilker Park is a nature reserve managed by the Sunshine Coast Regional District (SCRD) located near Roberts Creek on BC's Sunshine Coast. It is a publicly accessible park listed under the SCRD's parks portfolio. Touring cyclists passing through the Sunshine Coast area may find it a worthwhile natural stop, though specific on-site cycling facilities are unconfirmed from available sources.
40c603e969: The Fort St. John North Peace Museum, operated by the North Peace Historical Society, chronicles the North Peace region from ancient dinosaur footprints and Indigenous Dane-Zaa history through the fur trade, agricultural settlement, and the 1942 construction of the Alaska Highway. Visitors explore a rich collection of replica buildings — trapper's cabin, general store, schoolhouse, jail, and more — alongside hands-on interactive exhibits and over 13,000 archival photographs. For a touring cyclist passing through northeastern BC, it offers a compelling half-day stop to understand the dramatic transformation of the landscape they are riding through.
5daa764b48: The Paint Pots are a series of vivid ochre-coloured mineral springs in Kootenay National Park, reached by a short trail off Highway 93. The iron-rich deposits hold deep cultural significance for Indigenous peoples and have been a gathering place for thousands of years. Touring cyclists riding the Kootenay Parkway pass close by and can make a quick detour to see one of the most distinctive geological features in the Canadian Rockies.
c7d3bc3c63: The Kitimat Chamber of Commerce & Visitor Centre has been connecting local businesses and welcoming visitors since 1955. Housed within is the Coastline Collective Gift Store, featuring handmade goods and souvenirs from over 20 local artisans alongside maps, brochures, and community information. It is a natural first stop for touring cyclists arriving in Kitimat who want local knowledge, regional brochures, and a taste of the community's creative economy.
38ed51492b: The Prince Rupert Fire Museum is a heritage attraction in Prince Rupert, BC, dedicated to preserving the history of firefighting in the region. It was previously associated with the Prince Rupert Public Library's web presence, suggesting a community-operated or volunteer-run institution. Touring cyclists passing through Prince Rupert's compact downtown may find it a worthwhile cultural stop, though current access details are unconfirmed.
1fea725972: Copper Sun Journeys is an Indigenous-owned and -operated guided adventure company based in Bella Coola (Q'umk'uts, Nuxalkulmc), offering sacred petroglyph experiences, totem story tours, ancient cedar forest walks, and river rafting in the Great Bear Rainforest. Endorsed by Indigenous Tourism BC as a must-see attraction, it is led by local Nuxalk guides and operates June through October. Touring cyclists passing through the remote Bella Coola Valley would find this a rare opportunity to experience living Indigenous culture and dramatic coastal mountain wilderness.
3a88c5abc3: Exhale (operating as 'Exhale Art & Crystal') is an art gallery and crystal shop located in the Okanagan & Thompson region of British Columbia. It sits at the intersection of fine art and mineral/crystal retail, likely appealing to cyclists looking for a cultural or curiosity stop on a touring route. The minimal web presence makes it something of a hidden gem worth discovering in person.
9de76a0869: Destination Osoyoos is the Destination Marketing Organization (DMO) for Osoyoos and operates the Osoyoos Visitor Centre on Main Street. The town bills itself as 'Canada's Warmest Welcome,' sitting beside the warmest lake in Canada in the semi-arid South Okanagan. Cycling tourists will find the centre a useful planning hub for regional biking routes, wine tours, and hiking in the surrounding grasslands and highlands.
bbe6555fb7: Praised by Lonely Planet as one of Vancouver Island's best community museums, the Alberni Valley Museum documents the richly diverse history of the Alberni Valley through collections spanning First Nations culture, industrial history, and folk art. Its distinctive Visible Storage system makes the entire collection accessible to visitors at all times, accompanied by easy-to-use catalogue books. The museum also presents a rotating program of temporary exhibits and operates a museum shop.
a1e7985b3f: The Golden & District Centennial Arena is a municipally-operated indoor ice facility run by the Town of Golden's Recreation Services department, serving as the primary hockey and skating venue for the Columbia Valley community. Located in Golden, a mountain town at the junction of Highway 1 and Highway 95, the arena functions as a community gathering hub year-round. A dedicated Arena Lounge operates within the facility, suggesting on-site food and beverage service beyond the ice surface itself.
50c1b26256: A cultural interpretive centre in Gitlaxt'aamiks (New Aiyansh), the capital of the Nisg̱a'a Nation, located 100 km northwest of Terrace on Highway 113. The centre showcases traditional artwork of the Gitmidiik (Grizzly Bear) clan, artifacts, displays, and audio-visual presentations on the history of the village, including a replica traditional smokehouse. It also features a restaurant with traditional and western cuisine, a gift shop, and a theatre.
d9dba679d9: Gibsons Public Art Gallery (GPAG) is a free non-profit public gallery housed in the historic former Bank of Montreal building at the centre of Gibsons' Landing on BC's Sunshine Coast. Founded in 2003, it anchors a creative district that includes five commercial galleries, artists' studios, and a heritage museum. Gibsons is a 40-minute ferry ride from Vancouver, making GPAG a natural cultural pause for cyclists touring the Sunshine Coast.
c4285a2f2d: Laughing Falls is a natural waterfall situated within Yoho National Park on the western slopes of the Great Divide in British Columbia, part of the Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks UNESCO World Heritage Site. The park is celebrated for its glaciers, dramatic peaks, and cascading waterfalls, and lies along the Trans-Canada Highway corridor — a heavily travelled touring route for cyclists. Visiting the falls requires leaving the road and hiking a trail into the Yoho Valley.
41672b7c7b: The Comox Community Centre is a civic facility operated by the Town of Comox, offering fitness programs, racquet courts, and rentable spaces to residents and visitors on Vancouver Island. It sits in the heart of the Comox Valley, a region popular with touring cyclists exploring coastal routes. The centre lists 'Accessible Recreation' as a program area, suggesting a commitment to welcoming a broad range of visitors.
08cd32469f: The Sandon Historical Society Museum preserves and interprets the history of Sandon, a former silver-mining boomtown in the Kootenays that is now effectively a ghost town. The museum recently added a permanent exhibit, 'Window to the Past – Japanese Canadians in Sandon,' documenting the internment of Nikkei residents during 1942–1944. Located at the end of Slocan Star Street along a route signposted from Three Forks, it is a remote but rewarding destination for cyclists exploring the Slocan Valley.
880b5e7833: Coast Gravity Park is a dedicated mountain bike park in Sechelt, BC, on BC's Sunshine Coast, purpose-built for gravity-oriented trail riding. The park offers bike rentals, enabling visitors who arrive without their own equipment to participate, and runs private bookings and organized events in addition to regular day passes. It is one of the few ticketed MTB bike parks on the Sunshine Coast, making it a notable destination for cycling tourists in the region.
1d47072dc3: The South Shuswap Branch is part of the Okanagan Regional Library, a 30-branch regional system established in 1936 serving over 399,000 people across 59,600 square kilometres. Located on Golf Course Drive, the branch hosts regular community programs including events like laughter yoga and knitting circles, and maintains a book drop bin outside the main entrance. Free on-site parking is available, making it a practical stop along a cycling route through the South Shuswap area.
e54a582de7: Mount Robson Park protects the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies (3,954 m) and is one of British Columbia's most celebrated provincial parks. The 63 km Mount Robson Corridor follows Highway 16 (Yellowhead), giving touring cyclists dramatic views of mountains, creeks, and wetlands as they pass through. A Welcome Centre at the park's western entrance serves as an orientation point, and the world-renowned Berg Lake Trail draws backcountry adventurers from around the globe.
f749452c17: Friendship Community Garden is a community garden in the Comox Valley, operated under the Healthy Families Program of Comox Valley Family Services Association. Community gardens like this one offer a pleasant, low-key stop for touring cyclists passing through the area. The garden's connection to a social services organization suggests a community-oriented, welcoming space.
373573031d: A community outdoor swimming pool in Hagensborg in the Bella Coola Valley, originally built in 1967 as a federal Centennial project. Operated by the Central Coast Regional District during summer months only, it offers public swims, lap swims, and Red Cross swimming lessons. For touring cyclists passing through one of BC's most remote valleys, it's a rare chance to cool off after a long ride through the Coast Mountains.
91f487347a: Alert Bay Public Library & Museum is a combined public library and museum serving the community of Alert Bay on Cormorant Island, situated on the traditional lands of the Kwakwaka'wakw Peoples. The institution holds a library collection alongside museum resources and offers public computer and internet access. For touring cyclists arriving by ferry to this remote island destination, it provides a cultural stop with connectivity.
65902a159f: Baldy Mountain Resort is a four-season mountain destination perched above the South Okanagan near Oliver, with a summit of 2,310 m and over 600 acres of skiable and gladed terrain receiving 25–35 feet of dry desert powder annually. In summer the mountain hosts artisan markets, disc golf, and a hilltop coffee bar with panoramic views over Canada's only natural desert and the surrounding wine country. The access road is partly unpaved, making it a realistic destination for gravel or mountain bikers exploring the Oliver–Osoyoos corridor.
13ba8883c2: McBride & District Public Library is a community hub in the small Robson Valley town of McBride, situated along the Yellowhead Highway in BC's Central Interior. The library offers computer and internet access, a Library of Things, a seed library, and meeting room rentals — practical resources for touring cyclists passing through this remote region. It also maintains a satellite reading room in the hamlet of Dome Creek further up the valley, and hosts local history and oral history projects rooted in the area's railway and ranching heritage.
2dc327d41b: Rogers Pass National Historic Site marks the summit where the Canadian Pacific Railway crossed the Selkirk Mountains in 1885, a pivotal moment in Canada's confederation story. Located within Glacier National Park along the Trans-Canada Highway, the site encompasses ruins of the original CPR right-of-way, ancient cedar groves, and the Rogers Pass Discovery Centre. For touring cyclists, it is one of the most historically resonant high-elevation waypoints on any cross-Canada journey through the Selkirks.
5f8415fd14: The Kunze Art Gallery is housed in Creston's historic red grain elevator, giving it a striking industrial character that sets it apart from typical gallery spaces. It showcases a rotating roster of emerging and accomplished regional artists working in large-scale acrylic painting, sculpture, functional pottery, graphite, and clay, complemented by a gift shop called The Elevator featuring handmade local goods. The gallery received the 'Best of the Best Readers Choice Award 2025' and maintains an active presence on the online platform Artsy, making it a recognized cultural stop in the Kootenays.
5f9b6fe650: The West Coast Trail Information & Orientation Centre is the Parks Canada gateway facility for registering and orienting hikers tackling the legendary 75-km West Coast Trail, one of Canada's most demanding multi-day backcountry routes along the remote west shore of Vancouver Island. The centre sits within Pacific Rim National Park Reserve in the traditional territories of the Huu-ay-aht, Ditidaht, and Pacheedaht First Nations, whose Guardians help maintain the trail. Touring cyclists riding the Vancouver Island coast pass through this isolated region and may find the facility a useful reference point, though it is primarily oriented toward backcountry hikers.
777f748491: Brian Scott Art Gallery is a fine art gallery located on the Island Highway North on Vancouver Island, showcasing the work of artist Brian Scott. Situated along the main touring corridor between Courtenay and Campbell River, it offers cyclists a cultural stop mid-route. The gallery's original web presence has been compromised, so current programming and hours should be confirmed by phone.
5887ff5b38: The largest living history museum in western North America, Barkerville preserves more than 125 heritage buildings along the original Gold Rush streetscape on Williams Creek in the Cariboo. Designated a National Historic Site in 1924, visitors explore working displays, costumed interpreters, and 19th-century shops set amid mountain forests. Cyclists can ride surrounding roads and trails but must push bikes through the Heritage Zone at walking pace.
b7bb7351df: The Assiniboine Creek Trail is a backcountry trail within Mount Assiniboine Provincial Park, part of the Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks UNESCO World Heritage Site. The park is celebrated for its alpine lakes, glaciers, and dramatic peaks, with no road access — trails provide the only way in. It is a remote wilderness destination requiring full self-sufficiency, suited to experienced backcountry travellers.
9d68240a8a: The Kitimat Ice Rink is a municipally operated indoor ice facility in Kitimat, BC, serving the Haisla Nation's unceded territory on British Columbia's North Coast. Tagged in OSM as an ice hockey venue, it sits within the District of Kitimat's broader network of recreation centres that includes Tamitik Arena and the Riverlodge Recreation and Fitness Centre. For touring cyclists, it represents a public recreation anchor in an otherwise remote northern community.
b2847d2283: The Fernie Chamber of Commerce supports local businesses, workforce development, and community events in this small mountain town in the East Kootenays. Known for hosting signature celebrations like Griz Days and the Holiday Kick-Off, the Chamber helps sustain Fernie's year-round economy. A touring cyclist passing through may find it useful as a point of contact for local business information, though its primary function is business support rather than visitor services.
a39bfb443f: The Tatla Lake Branch is a small community library operated by the Cariboo Regional District Library system, situated on BC-20 (the Chilcotin Highway) in the remote Tatla Lake settlement of the Central Interior. Staffed by a community librarian, it is one of the few public facilities along this long, sparsely serviced highway corridor popular with cycle tourists. As a publicly accessible institution, it represents a rare community hub in a stretch of BC where services are few and far between.
8db071f038: The Radium Public Library is a small community library serving Radium Hot Springs and the surrounding Columbia Valley, located on Stanley Street in the heart of the village. It offers public computer and internet access, a Library of Things, digital lending, and a variety of community programs. For touring cyclists passing through the Kootenay Rockies, it provides a welcoming indoor stop with Wi-Fi and a range of local community resources and links.
a1b5b6a7e7: A Emily Carr Statue in Victoria.
9599cabe7a: Cycle City is a downtown Vancouver cycling institution operating two adjacent storefronts on Hornby Street — one for guided tours and one for rentals, repairs, and bike sales — rated #1 on TripAdvisor for Vancouver sightseeing with over 7,125 reviews. The shop carries top bicycle brands including Specialized and provides professional tune-ups and repairs with quick turn-around times, making it a practical stop for touring cyclists needing mechanical support. Beyond repairs, the operation offers a large rental fleet spanning city cruisers, e-bikes, performance road and gravel bikes, multiple guided tour formats, self-guided route maps, and luggage storage.
b8f13834df: Cycle Logic is a well-established multi-location BC bicycle shop — with branches in Kamloops, Prince George, Quesnel, Revelstoke, and Williams Lake — operating a full repair department out of its downtown Kamloops location. As a certified Shimano Service Center staffed by professionally trained mechanics, the shop handles everything from minor adjustments to complete overhauls, with bike fitting services also available. The retail floor covers a wide range of bicycles including e-bikes, a comprehensive parts selection, clothing, and accessories.
56725d1451: A family-owned bike shop in Mission's historic Railway Avenue district, operating continuously since 1978 when the Wenting family purchased the original Planet Earth Cycles. Now occupying 5,200 square feet with 10 staff, the shop carries road, mountain, hybrid, e-bikes, and kids' bikes alongside accessories, GPS computers, clothing, and bike racks. Jerseys from Canadian cycling champions hang on the walls, reflecting deep roots in the local cycling community.
9630931d00: Corsa Cycles is a full-service bicycle shop in Squamish, BC, now operating under the Dunbar Cycles & Corsa Cycles banner following its 2018 acquisition. The shop covers mountain, road, gravel, city, and electric bikes alongside a dedicated service centre, making it a comprehensive stop in the Sea-to-Sky corridor. Its broad parts and accessories inventory—including touring-specific luggage and racks—makes it particularly useful for loaded cycle tourers passing through Squamish.
eef0fce0a6: More Bikes is a full-service independent bike shop with multiple Vancouver locations — Kitsilano (recently relocated to 1828 W. 4th Ave.), UBC, and West Vancouver. The shop carries a broad range of bikes from Giant, Liv, Kona, Rocky Mountain, Brodie, and Cannondale, including e-bikes across several brands, plus a comprehensive parts and accessories floor. A dedicated repair and maintenance department makes it a practical stop for touring cyclists needing mechanical help on the road.
851393aaa8: Bicycleitis is a small, independent bicycle shop located on Shawnigan Lake Road near Duncan on Vancouver Island. It describes itself on Facebook as 'the Small Shop,' suggesting a boutique or owner-operated character. Touring cyclists passing through the Cowichan Valley area may find it a useful stop for bike-related needs.
aa56368fc6: EbikeBC is Canada's premier electric mobility retailer, founded in 2015 by engineers seeking sustainable transportation solutions, specializing in e-bikes, e-trikes, e-scooters, conversion kits, and accessories. The shop operates a dedicated service center handling e-bike repair, diagnostics, battery refurbishment, and component installation. For touring cyclists on e-bikes, it is a specialist resource for parts and servicing in the Vancouver area.
a926fd127e: Half Time Sports is a sports retailer located on Granville Island in Vancouver, a popular destination for cyclists and visitors alike. The shop is tagged as a general sports shop (shop=sports) rather than a dedicated bike shop, so the range and depth of cycling-specific services is unknown. Its Granville Island location puts it within a well-trafficked recreational cycling corridor.
ec7f768f10: The Bike Barn is a full-service bicycle shop in Penticton, BC, sitting at the heart of a region the shop itself describes as home to outstanding mountain, gravel, and road riding. They sell new and used bikes, run tiered professional service packages from basic tune-ups to complete frame-level overhauls, and carry e-bikes — making them a well-rounded stop for touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan.
c17382cbc3: Dunbar Cycles, also branded as Corsa Cycles, is a full-service bicycle retailer and repair shop on East Broadway in Vancouver carrying road, mountain, electric, city, and kids' bikes alongside an extensive parts and accessories catalogue. The shop operates a dedicated service centre for mechanical work. Its inventory spans a wide range of drivetrain, suspension, and touring-adjacent accessories including panniers, handlebar bags, and saddle bags from a large selection of brands.
2ba9ccd862: Kickstand is a volunteer-run, non-profit community bike shop in East Vancouver operating as a low-barrier DIY and Do-It-Together repair workspace where visitors use shop tools and workstands with on-site volunteer guidance. The shop sells new and used parts and refurbished bikes, and runs community programs including bike donation, refurbishment, and partnerships that provide bicycles to refugees and Indigenous families. It is a genuine grassroots resource for cyclists needing affordable, hands-on support with common mechanical tasks.
37125d4bc9: Summit Sport Whistler bills itself as Whistler's largest bike, ski, and board shop, operating year-round with a seasonal swing between snow sports and mountain biking. The shop offers both sales and full bike service, positioning itself as a one-stop destination in a world-class ride destination. A touring cyclist arriving in Whistler needing a tune-up or repair would find a dedicated service operation here.
4d03c62b25: Hub City Cycles is a non-profit community co-operative bicycle shop established in 2012 and tucked into Nanaimo's China Steps neighbourhood, built around a mission of affordable cycling access, bike recycling, and advocacy for cycling as everyday transport. The shop was among the earliest in the region to embrace e-bikes and recently acquired dedicated electric bike repair stands to keep pace with growing demand. Its co-op structure means visiting cyclists encounter experienced mechanics, a genuine community ethos, and an unusually broad range of services under one small but efficiently packed roof.
d3c0e567a1: Non-profit community bike shop on Main Street, run by PEDAL Society. Full-service repairs and tune-ups, refurbished bikes, and new and used parts. DIY workspace for cyclists who want to fix their own bikes or learn how, plus mechanics workshops and clinics.
269c3dd9c0: Bowen eBikes is an eBike rental and full-service maintenance shop located steps from the Snug Cove ferry terminal, making it the natural first stop for cyclists arriving from Horseshoe Bay on a day trip or island stay. As the island's sole bike repair facility, it stocks a broad range of parts and handles everything from tubeless flat repairs and spoke replacements to full drivetrain tuneups. The shop also offers the island's only Low Speed Vehicle rental — a 40 km/h golf cart — for groups or riders who need an accessible alternative.
8c39c14e27: Straight Up Cycles is a full-service bike shop in Victoria operating since 2000, grown from a repair-focused origin into a shop offering new and used road, cyclocross, and mountain bikes alongside bespoke custom builds using brands such as Bassi Frames. Every bike sold leaves the shop fitted to its new owner, and experienced mechanics handle everything from flat fixes to complete strip-and-rebuild overhauls. A rotating consignment section adds used inventory for cyclists looking for a pre-owned ride.
7b3395b9bf: Marty's Mountain Cycle is a boutique mountain bike shop that has operated in Esquimalt — just across the bridge from downtown Victoria — since 1989, making it the original mountain bike shop in the Victoria area. Specializing in high-end mountain bikes from brands like Forbidden and Rocky Mountain, the shop has grown into a community hub known for its mechanical expertise and deep involvement in the South Vancouver Island riding scene. A rental fleet that includes e-bikes rounds out the shop's offerings for visiting riders.
e4107cd317: Kelowna Cycle, also branded as 'The Hub', is a full-service bicycle retailer in Kelowna carrying road, mountain, gravel, commuter, and electric bikes from brands including Cannondale, Rocky Mountain, Norco, Moustache, and Bianchi. Their in-house service department (Hub Bike Service) handles everything from basic tune-ups to complex repairs. Touring cyclists will find a broad inventory of replacement parts — chains, cables, tires, tubes, derailleurs, and more — alongside a complete accessories selection.
3bb8c1db30: Simon's Bike Shop is an independent bicycle retailer situated in Library Square in downtown Vancouver, carrying a broad range of bikes from road and gravel to mountain and e-bikes, with a particularly strong Specialized lineup. Professionally trained technicians handle everything from quick adjustments to full drivetrain overhauls, making it a dependable stop for touring cyclists needing mechanical support before or during a trip. A rentals program and comprehensive parts and accessories inventory — including e-bike batteries and components — add further utility for visitors.
b0a2b1d521: Reckless The Bike Store is a full-service bicycle retailer on Davie Street in Vancouver's Yaletown area, part of the Reckless Bike Stores chain. The shop covers the full spectrum from sales and accessories to mechanical service, with a dedicated Rad Power Bikes eBike service program. Touring cyclists will find rental bikes, pannier bags, and professional mechanical staff under one roof.
8b3e5b918c: Gerick Cycle & Ski is a full-service bike and ski shop located on Nelson's main commercial strip, Baker Street, in the heart of one of BC's most celebrated mountain biking communities. The shop carries an extensive range of bikes and accessories — including Specialized, Giant, Norco, and Liv — and runs a structured service department with a dedicated mechanic team. Beyond sales and repairs, Gerick's is embedded in local riding culture through its group rides program and the 10 Spot Enduro Series.
d6f09a8b95: GearHub Sports is a full-service outdoor and cycling retailer that has served Fernie's Elk Valley community since 2010, stocking over 25,000 products across mountain bikes, components, apparel, ski gear, and trail-running equipment. The shop carries bikes from Devinci and Rocky Mountain — including e-MTBs such as the Altitude Powerplay — reflecting its investment in keeping pace with Fernie's evolving trail scene. Situated on 1st Avenue in the centre of one of BC's premier mountain biking destinations, it operates a second consignment location in town.
a6655cafd7: Cit-E Cycles is BC's largest e-bike retailer, founded in 2011 from a single Langley shop and now operating six locations across the province. Their North Vancouver store carries 300+ models from 20+ premium brands spanning urban, cargo, mountain, and touring styles. Touring cyclists will find one of the broadest e-bike selections in Canada, with in-store test rides and dedicated service support.
cbbc449c21: R.A.D. Cycles is an East Vancouver bike shop established in 2016 in the Mount Pleasant neighbourhood, built around a mission of being the friendliest shop in the city for cyclists of all levels. They offer repair services ranging from flat fixes and tune-ups to accident repair, along with personal bike fitting for new and used bicycles. Touring cyclists will appreciate the standing free-air-and-oil policy and the no-charge repair estimates.
5633556d0a: West Point Cycles is a full-service bicycle retailer and repair shop with multiple Vancouver locations and a Langley presence, serving road, mountain, commuter, and e-bike riders. The shop is an authorized Trek dealer and carries Brompton folding bikes alongside a deep parts and accessories inventory. Touring cyclists will find professional repair packages, a comprehensive parts selection including Schwalbe Marathon Plus tires, and knowledgeable staff.
75237c094b: On Top Bike Shop has been serving North Shore cyclists since 1996 from its location on Lonsdale Avenue in North Vancouver. The shop offers a comprehensive range of bicycle repair services from basic tunes to complete overhauls and suspension rebuilds, and also services skis and snowboards in winter. It is a well-rooted presence in the North Shore riding community, experienced with all bicycle types including e-bikes.
18a70827d7: Richmond eBike is a Metro Vancouver e-bike specialist that has been selling and servicing electric bikes, trikes, scooters, and mobility solutions since 2014. The shop carries a broad inventory of parts and accessories — from motors and controllers to tires, chains, and drivetrain components — and runs a dedicated repair workshop servicing all brands including ICBC inspections. Touring cyclists riding e-bikes will find one of the more complete electric-bike service and parts resources in the region here.
3e2bf2e357: A family-oriented bicycle shop operating since 1959, Russ Hay's is a full-service Specialized dealer in Sidney's downtown core with locations also in Victoria. They offer professional bike fitting by certified specialists alongside a full repair shop, making them a reliable stop for touring cyclists passing through the Saanich Peninsula. The shop stocks a broad range of parts, accessories, and cycling clothing.
cea89f2da0: West Point Cycles is a long-running full-service bicycle retailer with multiple Vancouver locations, carrying a wide range of road, mountain, commuter, folding, and electric bikes from brands including Trek and Brompton. The West 10th Avenue store offers comprehensive mechanical services alongside a deep inventory of parts and accessories relevant to loaded touring, including Ortlieb bags and Schwalbe Marathon Plus tires. A staffed workshop and walk-in estimate policy make it a practical stop for touring cyclists needing mechanical support in Vancouver's west side.
bd9b2344b9: Pedal Bros. is BC's only specialty recumbent trike sales and service shop, re-opened in downtown Kamloops in 2023 after earlier roots in Chase, BC. The shop deals in TerraTrike and Trident Trike recumbent trikes, including e-trike models, alongside accessories from Bivo, Sena, and Portland Design Works. A touring cyclist will find a knowledgeable, cycling-passionate team in a central Kamloops location, though the shop's expertise and service are focused on three-wheeled recumbent cycles rather than standard touring bikes.
9372a9ac44: Revolution Cycles is Rossland's dedicated full-service bike shop, operating for 21 years with an open-concept workshop staffed by certified mechanics and stocked by major brands including Giant, Santa Cruz, Yeti, Devinci, and Rocky Mountain. As a certified Shimano Service Center, the shop covers everything from wheel builds to custom suspension setups. They also offer mountain bike and e-MTB rentals and coaching and guiding services, making them a comprehensive resource for cyclists exploring this renowned mountain biking destination.
81dc24f4a1: Russ Hay's is a long-established full-service bicycle shop in Victoria with two locations (Victoria and Sidney), carrying a wide selection of road, mountain, gravel, commuter, and electric bikes from Specialized, Giant, and Liv. The shop runs a comprehensive service department staffed by mechanics who offer free estimates and welcome walk-ins for everything from minor adjustments to complete overhauls. Certified bike-fit specialists are also on staff, making this a practical stop for touring cyclists needing mechanical help, parts, or a proper saddle position.
0bd2e3e360: A Victoria institution since 1963, Mac's Cycle Centre is a full-service bicycle shop on Shelbourne Street known for its friendly, knowledgeable staff. 11ac95a5b5: Cit-E Cycles is an e-bike specialty retailer claiming Canada's largest selection, with six BC locations including this Lower Lonsdale shop steps from the Spirit Trail waterfront path and the Lonsdale Quay SeaBus terminal. 4f0c4b4425: The Candy Jar is a locally owned Tofino shop operating since 2010 that blends a retro candy store and Island Farms ice cream parlour with a bike and scooter rental service. 00ad12c8df: Velofix is a mobile bike shop franchise that dispatches certified technicians directly to wherever a cyclist needs them — home, trailhead, or accommodation. For touring cyclists in BC, it offers a practical alternative to hauling a bike to a shop, bookable online or by phone.
5edaa18e7b: Forever Bikes, also trading as Jack's Cycle, has served Chilliwack cyclists since 1963, making it one of the longest-running bike shops in the Fraser Valley. 20775579cc: Trek Bicycle Port Coquitlam is the largest Trek retailer in the region, offering full sales and service for bikes and e-bikes of all brands from their Westwood Street location. Touring cyclists will find knowledgeable staff, free multi-point inspections, and local ride recommendations.
866d172fa1: Brentwood Cycle is a locally owned and operated bike shop that has served the Greater Victoria area for over 40 years, situated in Brentwood Bay just minutes from the Lochside Trail to Swartz Bay and the Mount Work trail network. Its location near a major multi-use trail corridor and ferry terminus makes it a natural stop for touring cyclists passing through the Saanich Peninsula.
dc58a4ed5a: Kelowna Cycle, also known as 'The Hub,' is a full-service bicycle shop in Kelowna carrying road, mountain, gravel, commuter, and electric bikes from brands including Cannondale, Rocky Mountain, Norco, and Moustache. The shop also stocks a comprehensive inventory of parts, accessories, and cycling apparel, making it a well-equipped resource for touring cyclists passing through the Okanagan.
0d9bb2a064: Swicked Cycles is Campbell River's largest bike shop, founded in 2010 by a lifelong cyclist with a background in professional mountain bike racing and the Canadian cycling industry. A co-owner's background in tourism and event management gives the shop a notably welcoming orientation toward visiting and touring cyclists.
8ecf03032a: McBike and Sport is a community-oriented multi-sport shop in Smithers, BC, run by enthusiast owner-operators who only sell products in sports they actively participate in — cycling, fishing, running, and cross-country skiing. Smithers sits at the gateway to extensive trail networks and wilderness in the Bulkley Valley, and McBike serves as the local outdoor recreation hub.
d357537bd5: Big Grin Bikes is a full-service bicycle shop in Qualicum Beach on Vancouver Island, specializing in Scott bikes across all disciplines — road, gravel, mountain, and e-bikes — plus Benno eBikes and a wide range of apparel and accessories. The shop's mechanic, Lazarus, is described as focused on getting riders back on the road as quickly as possible.
3b70d805b2: Founded by the English family in 1971, Taw's Cycle & Sports is a long-established Powell River institution combining a full-service bicycle shop with hockey retail under one roof. 0fc7194160: Beaufort Cycles is a full-service bike shop and rental destination located in Cumberland, BC, steps from the celebrated Cumberland Mountain Bike Trail Network. Touring cyclists will find a capable mechanical team and a premium rental fleet in one of Vancouver Island's premier trail towns.
c97709e071: Cap's Bicycles is a full-service bike shop in Langley carrying Norco, Kona, Opus, and Devinci across mountain, gravel, city, e-bike, and kids categories. Their service department employs professionally trained technicians offering everything from basic tune-ups to complete frame-up rebuilds, including dedicated e-bike service packages. A large in-store parts inventory spanning drivetrains, brakes, cables, and components makes it a practical stop for cyclists in the Fraser Valley.
63958df41b: Pemberton Bike Co. is Whistler's original independent, locally owned bike and ski shop, operating since 1994 under the legal name Whistler Bike Co. Inc. DBA Pemberton Bike Co. Touring cyclists will find this a solid stop in the Sea-to-Sky corridor for repairs, rentals, and consumables.
c2800a7b76: Mountain City Cycle has been the Comox Valley's full-service bicycle shop since 1998, stocking a broad range of bikes from Giant, Liv, Devinci, and Surly — including the Surly Bridge Club, purpose-built for loaded touring on and off pavement. The repair workshop handles everything from basic tune-ups to suspension overhauls and offers free walk-in estimates on any work. Touring-relevant accessories including racks, fenders, packs, panniers, and hydration gear are stocked in-store and available for local delivery.
9f1daff706: Bike Chameleon is a small bicycle shop in Campbell River run by operator Rob Stables, carrying Kona brand bikes and offering sales and service for all cycling needs. The shop specializes in wheel and rim repair alongside general bicycle repair, parts, and retail. A recent post noted Rob working overtime during the busy season, suggesting genuine local demand and hands-on service.
394e2dcc62: District Bicycle Co. operates a satellite location at the top of Sun Peaks Resort village, serving mountain bikers and resort visitors with bike rentals, parts, accessories, and on-site repair support. It is part of a three-location company spanning Kamloops, Sun Peaks, and Valemount, with organized group rides as part of their community offering.
de8e4fb284: Pedal Your World is a long-established full-service bike shop in Campbell River, in operation since 1976, offering sales, repairs, and bike rentals including hardtail, city, and full-suspension options. 6212c28a98: Jumping Slug Community Cyclery is a full-service bike shop on the route into Port Alberni on Vancouver Island, offering sales, professional servicing for all bike types, and rentals including mountain, electric, gravel, and adventure bikes. The shop is deeply rooted in the Alberni Valley cycling community, hosting events and weekly group rides. Staff bring strong local knowledge of island backroads and trails, making it a useful stop for cyclists planning routes beyond the town.
6743862b6f: Established in 1981, Black's Cycle is a long-running full-service bicycle shop in the Comox Valley on Vancouver Island, widely regarded as the area's go-to cycling resource. Touring cyclists will find it a well-equipped stop for repairs and supplies, including panniers and e-bike-specific components.
3b83911930: Giant Langley is an authorized Giant brand bicycle dealership in Langley, BC, stocking a full range of road, mountain, gravel, and electric bikes alongside an extensive accessories selection. 1b7072b51f: Double O Bikes & Sports is a social enterprise in Osoyoos operated by the Southern Okanagan Association for Integrated Community Living, with 100% of proceeds donated to support community members with special needs. a26951acbf: Skookum Gear is a full-service bike and ski shop with locations in Revelstoke and Salmon Arm, stocking a broad range of mountain, road, gravel, and e-bikes from brands including Giant, Specialized, Liv, and Rocky Mountain Bicycles. Touring cyclists will find accessories ranging from panniers and hydration packs to lights, pumps, and tools alongside the full workshop.
35d96b02d5: Cumberland's Original Bike Shop since 2000, Dodge City Cycles sits at 535 feet elevation — the highest bike shop on Vancouver Island — and is located at the base of Cumberland's celebrated mountain bike trail network in the Comox Valley. 43c37cebce: Head Over Wheels is a brick-and-mortar bicycle shop established in Qualicum Beach in 1999, carrying Trek, Specialized, and Electra bikes. Services range from repairs and tune-ups to professional bike fittings, consignment, and special orders from supplier catalogues.
cf0678e17f: Suncoast Cycles is a bicycle shop in Powell River, BC, carrying brands including Giant and Trek with floor stock and order-for-pickup options. The shop regularly runs clearance sales on bikes and stocks cycling accessories and gear from brands like DHaRCO. It serves as a local hub for cyclists on the northern Sunshine Coast.
0b3839a9a8: Bubby's Bicycle Service Ltd. is a full-service independent bike shop in Errington on central Vancouver Island, run by mechanic Chris. The shop offers a comprehensive repair menu from basic tune-ups to full overhauls, stocks parts from an extensive brand catalogue, and sells used and consignment bikes. A pickup-and-delivery service means cyclists who can't transport their bike can still get it serviced.
54e6e3920a: Cit-E Cycles is BC's largest e-bike retailer, founded in Langley in 2011 and now operating six locations across the province, with this Langley address serving as its headquarters. The shop carries 300+ e-bike models from 20+ premium brands spanning urban, mountain, touring, cargo, folding, and trike categories. Touring cyclists will find one of the widest e-bike selections in Canada along with in-store service and repair.
9062bdbd8d: Comox Bike Company has been the Comox Valley's local bike shop since 1988, serving island riders across every trail network for over 35 years. 20bcebbe3c: Western Bike Company is a premium cycling component dealer and specialist service shop located in Cumberland, BC — Vancouver Island's legendary mountain biking hub. Touring cyclists passing through Cumberland for its hundreds of kilometres of single-track, road, and gravel routes will find a knowledgeable team oriented toward quality builds and bike protection rather than general repair.
1534ee9581: Trail Bicycles is a full-service bike shop in Courtenay serving the Comox Valley, carrying premium brands including Trek, Norco, Mondraker, Ibis, Pivot, and Salsa. Visiting cyclists can also rent full-suspension mountain bikes with helmets and get insider knowledge on local trails including the renowned Cumberland network.
3de9c30f78: Co-operative car share with hundreds of home locations across the Lower Mainland (Vancouver, Burnaby, Surrey, Richmond, Coquitlam and more), Victoria area (including Esquimalt, Oak Bay, Saanich, Sidney), Nanaimo, Squamish, and Kelowna. Also at major BC Ferries terminals. Open to non-BC residents — N licence or equivalent from any jurisdiction required. Some vehicles have exterior bike racks; SUVs and minivans available for carrying bikes inside.
b06e4282f9: Vehicle and passenger ferry operator serving coastal BC. Key routes for cyclists: Horseshoe Bay to Nanaimo (Departure Bay and Duke Point), Tsawwassen to Swartz Bay and Duke Point, and routes to the Sunshine Coast, Gulf Islands, and Vancouver Island.
b5f48a88ff: Canadian airline serving Kelowna (YLW), Kamloops (YKA), and other BC cities. Bikes must be boxed or bagged; e-bikes not accepted. Bike fee applies.
aeb80395be: National airline serving Vancouver (YVR), Victoria (YYJ), Kelowna (YLW), Kamloops (YKA), Cranbrook (YXC), and other BC cities. Bikes must be pre-registered; boxed or bagged only; e-bikes not accepted. Fee approximately $50 CAD per direction.
37d712c454: Regional airline connecting Vancouver with smaller BC communities including Cranbrook (YXC), Castlegar (YCG), Trail (YZZ), Campbell River, Port Hardy, and others. Advance booking required; e-bikes explicitly prohibited. Fee approximately $105 CAD per direction. Small aircraft with limited space.
f6d9ce9479: Floatplane service connecting Vancouver, Victoria, Nanaimo, Salt Spring Island, and other coastal BC destinations. Bike transport on space-available basis only; advance booking required; 50 lb weight limit; no trailers. Contact before booking.
af77874ba6: Intercity bus service connecting Chilliwack, Abbotsford, Kelowna, Kamloops, and other BC communities. Bikes accepted in the under-bus luggage hold; must be boxed or wrapped in cloth (plastic wrap not accepted). Fee: $30 per bike. E-bike and trailer policy unconfirmed — call before travelling: 1-877-769-3287.
85f8ab1d65: Intercity bus service connecting Chilliwack, Kelowna, Kamloops, Cranbrook, and other BC communities. Bikes accepted; must be wrapped or boxed. Fee: $50 per bike, non-refundable even if bike not brought. E-bike and trailer policy unconfirmed — contact before travelling: 1-833-583-3636.
4cb8d28c4b: National passenger rail. The Canadian runs Vancouver–Kamloops North–Jasper–Toronto; the Skeena runs Jasper–Prince George–Prince Rupert. Bikes travel as checked baggage for $25 per direction (all bike types, including e-bikes, folding, tandem, and recumbent), carried on the baggage-car rack where available, otherwise boxed ($20) or bagged ($5). Checked-baggage service is only offered at staffed stations: on The Canadian's BC segment that means Vancouver and Jasper, not Kamloops North. On the Skeena, confirm which stations can check a bike before you travel, as most stops are unstaffed flag stops. E-bike batteries must be disconnected on check-in. Call VIA (1-888-842-7245) to confirm baggage-car availability before planning a bike trip.
7b48ef5870: Island Link (Tofino Express Bus) intercity bus connecting Nanaimo, Port Alberni, Ucluelet, and Tofino. Bicycles are not accepted on any Island Link vehicle — the operator's baggage policy explicitly restricts bicycles due to vehicle space limitations, with no boxed or bagged exception. Confirm current schedule at islandlinkbus.com before travel.
d6aab2f3c2: Island Link (Island Express Bus) intercity bus connecting Nanaimo, Courtenay, and Campbell River. Bicycles are not accepted on any Island Link vehicle — the operator's baggage policy explicitly restricts bicycles due to vehicle space limitations, with no boxed or bagged exception. Confirm current schedule at islandlinkbus.com before travel.
42fea27c49: Island Link (Victoria Express Bus) intercity bus connecting Nanaimo and Victoria. Bicycles are not accepted on any Island Link vehicle — the operator's baggage policy explicitly restricts bicycles due to vehicle space limitations, with no boxed or bagged exception. Confirm current schedule at islandlinkbus.com before travel.
e73d52aff2: Intercity passenger rail connecting Vancouver (Pacific Central Station) south to Seattle, Portland, and Eugene. Some trains have a dedicated bike car allowing unboxed or bagged bikes; other services require boxing. Bike space must be reserved in advance; fee applies.
614c663cf8: Car and passenger ferry between Victoria (Inner Harbour) and Port Angeles, Washington. Key international crossing for cyclists on the Pacific Coast route. Walk-on cyclists welcome; bikes travel unboxed on vehicle deck. Bike fee applies. Reservations recommended.
f217a1bbde: High-speed passenger-only catamaran ferry between Victoria (Inner Harbour) and Seattle, Washington. Bikes travel unboxed on the outer deck, exposed to weather. Advance booking required — call or submit a Contact Us form; cannot show up with a bike unannounced. Bike fee: $30/direction (confirm currency — may be USD). Space very limited; first-booked, first-served. E-bike policy unconfirmed.
e8324765f2: Passenger ferry between Nanaimo and Vancouver (Waterfront Station). Max 2 bike spots per sailing; walk-on, fully assembled, must roll on/off. Fee: $30 one way, $50 return. No e-bikes; no trailers; max 50 lbs and 80 inches. Book ahead — spots are very limited.
ff1ef2b433: Enterprise and National Car Rental (same company) have locations in Squamish, North Vancouver, Vancouver, Chilliwack, Nanaimo, Victoria, Kelowna, Vernon, Kamloops, and Cranbrook. Call to confirm vehicle type and one-way availability before booking. On Vancouver Island most National branches are run by an independent licensee (National Car & Truck Rental, drivenational.ca) — see its own listing.
77b9f3315a: Independent Vancouver Island licensee of National, with branches at Victoria (airport, downtown, Colwood, Sidney), Duncan, Nanaimo (airport and downtown), Comox airport and Courtenay, Campbell River airport, Port Hardy airport, and North Vancouver. Offers one-way rentals between its Island branches with no drop charge — the best one-way option for the North Island. No bike racks for rent; a bike travels inside an SUV or minivan with the seats folded. Confirm one-way availability and vehicle type when booking.
a60b8f9cd0: Avis and Budget (same company) have the widest BC coverage of the major chains, including Whistler (Avis) and Tofino (Budget — seasonal, airport only, round-trip rentals only). SUVs and minivans available. No bike racks for rent; a bike travels inside an SUV or minivan with the seats folded. Confirm vehicle type and the one-way pair when booking.
bb28ccd0a8: Hertz has locations in Squamish, North Vancouver, Vancouver, Chilliwack, Nanaimo, Victoria, Kelowna, Kamloops (airport only, limited hours), and Cranbrook. Call to confirm vehicle type, bike rack availability, and one-way options before booking.
3a901eb91d: One-way car share operated by BCAA. Every Evo vehicle is fitted with two Thule roof-mounted bike racks. Free-floating service in Metro Vancouver and Victoria — pick up any available car and drop it off anywhere within the zone. Membership required before your trip.
0dcc21bd4f: Ride-hailing available in Vancouver, North Vancouver, Squamish, Whistler, Chilliwack, Kelowna, Penticton, Kamloops, Cranbrook, Nelson, Nanaimo, Victoria, Duncan, and Sidney following BC's province-wide expansion in 2025. Uber XL can typically fit an unboxed bike — contact your driver after matching to confirm before they arrive. No official bike policy; transport is at the driver's discretion.
a9a07b2fab: App-based ride-hailing from Black Top & Checker Cabs (iOS/Android), using licensed taxi vehicles and professional Class 4 drivers. Fixed fares locked at booking with no surge pricing. Holds Passenger Transportation Board TNS authorization for Region 1 (Metro Vancouver, Fraser Valley, and the Sea-to-Sky corridor to Squamish, Whistler, and Pemberton). A four-seat or six-seat van option carries oversized items such as a bike; an extra $15 charge applies to the four-seat van if the trip's purpose is to move cargo. Rides can be pre-booked up to three weeks in advance. Wheelchair-accessible vehicles available.
57af3e5742: BC-based ride-hailing app covering communities where Uber doesn't operate, including Squamish, Whistler, Tofino, Ucluelet, and Nanaimo. Some drivers have bike racks — use the filter in the app to add the number of bikes to your request. For drivers without a rack, whether a bike fits depends on the vehicle; you may need to remove a wheel or partially disassemble. See coastalrides.ca/blog/sunshine-coast-bike-road-trip for an example of the service in action.
49b1ded455: Scheduled motor coach between YVR/Downtown Vancouver, Squamish (reservation-only stop), and Whistler Village. Summer service April 18 – November 21. Bikes must be boxed or bagged — no bare bikes. First bike included in fare; additional bikes $10 each. E-bike and trailer policy not published; contact operator before travelling.
a3a6b94ea1: Scheduled bus between Squamish and Vancouver (Waterfront Station and Hyatt Hotel, Melville St), with stops at West Van, Horseshoe Bay, Lions Bay, and Britannia Beach. Summer service May–September. Bikes carried on external rack (max 2 per bus; call ahead to reserve — not all buses have a rack). Fee $15/bike each way per policy pages (homepage states free — confirm by phone). E-bikes generally not permitted. Unboxed bikes OK on rack; bagged or boxed OK in luggage hold.
6ee82dcb4e: Greater Vancouver regional transit. Bikes accepted on all modes: buses (exterior front rack, 2-bike max), SeaBus (up to 6 bikes at peak), SkyTrain Canada Line (1 bike/car, all times), Expo and Millennium lines (2 bikes/car), and West Coast Express (2 bikes/car). No bike fee on any mode. On the Expo and Millennium lines, bikes aren't allowed on westbound trains 7–9 am or eastbound trains 4–6 pm on weekdays. Canada Line has no time restrictions.
da412616ad: Regional bus systems throughout BC outside Metro Vancouver. Most buses are equipped with exterior front-mounted 2-bike racks; bikes ride unboxed. No bike fee. Trailers not permitted. E-bike policy varies by system — check with your local system before travelling. Regional systems include: Squamish and Whistler (WAVE), Chilliwack, Kelowna Regional, Vernon Regional, Kamloops, Cranbrook/East Kootenay, Nelson, South Okanagan (Penticton), Cowichan Valley, Victoria Regional, and Pacific Rim (Tofino/Ucluelet). Bike racks on community buses can only be used during daylight hours, as bikes block the headlights; all other BC Transit buses have no time-of-day restrictions.
6cb10573d4: Local taxi service in Kamloops. Hatchback cabs can carry bikes — phone ahead to arrange.
4e42f94f53: Local taxi service operating in Duncan and the Cowichan Valley. Ability to transport a bicycle depends on vehicle type and driver discretion.
60eab20168: Passenger-only catamaran ferry service operated by TransLink connecting Waterfront Station in downtown Vancouver to Lonsdale Quay in North Vancouver. This is the primary transit link from Vancouver to the start of the route. Accommodates bicycles: bikes are permitted on board and taken inside the vessel as-is, no extra fare required beyond standard transit fare. Passenger + bike: riders board with their bicycles directly. Walk-on bikes: cyclists walk their bikes on board. Interior transport: bikes are brought into the enclosed cabin area of the vessel
96591f20f2: Free inland vehicle and passenger ferry operated by BC Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure, connecting Balfour to Kootenay Bay across Kootenay Lake. Approximately 35-minute crossing. Year-round service. Accommodates bicycles: cyclists walk or roll bikes aboard as foot passengers at no charge. No reservations; service is first-come, first-served. Passenger + bike: cyclists board as foot passengers with their bike. Walk-on bikes: roll your bike directly onto the vehicle deck. Unboxed bikes OK: no packaging required, bikes roll on as-is
5117c40285: Provides shuttle services to the West Coast Trail and other destinations, but does not accept bikes as luggage.
49b6ad455a: MV Frances Barkley passenger and cargo ferry between Port Alberni and Ucluelet; carries bicycles with advanced reservation. Shuttle / trip support: ferry transport for cyclists and bikes.
a0ea5ddf73: Local taxi service in Penticton. Larger vehicle requests may be able to accommodate bicycles; confirm capacity and availability when booking
af3d5bbd19: FlixBus runs a cross-border coach route between Vancouver and Seattle, with stops in Bellingham and Everett, Washington, operated for FlixBus by local partner MTRWestern. Bikes travel on an exterior rack when space allows, or as boxed/bagged baggage for folding bikes only, for roughly CAD 18.50-37 depending on the fare. E-bikes, tandems, and trailers are not accepted, and space is not guaranteed, so book the bike as an add-on in advance rather than showing up at the curb. Because this route runs on a partner operator's buses rather than FlixBus's own fleet, call ahead to confirm the bike policy applies as described.
0dfb743b40: Small passenger ferry service on False Creek with stops at Granville Island, Hornby Street (downtown), Yaletown, David Lam Park, and Stamp's Landing. Passenger + bike: bikes may be accommodated on the small open deck vessels subject to available space; capacity is very limited
ff02318a56: Epic Rides runs a direct, non-stop shuttle between Vancouver and Whistler for cyclists. Bikes ride free of charge, either boxed or unboxed: a box guards against chips and scratches, while unboxed bikes travel on an exposed exterior rack. Spots per bus are limited, so book ahead. Bikes are not carried from November through April.
c7e12671ea: Whistler Shuttle provides transportation services to and from Whistler, accommodating bicycles on their shuttles. Accommodates bicycles: bikes can be transported on shuttles with advance notice. Passenger + bike: shuttles can carry both passengers and their bikes
dfe0b317b7: Multi-day luxury scenic rail through the BC interior and Canadian Rockies, daytime travel only with overnight hotel stops. Routes run Vancouver to Banff, Lake Louise, and Jasper via Kamloops, plus a Vancouver to Seattle Coastal Passage. Bikes are not carried in the coaches; a bicycle travels as oversized checked luggage moved separately by road and meets you at your hotel, likely for a surcharge. Confirm bicycle handling with the operator in advance.
72459d0fa0: Cantrail Coach Lines operates the Amtrak Thruway motorcoach connection between Vancouver and Seattle (feeding Amtrak Cascades). The operator's own website is currently broken/unreachable, so book through Amtrak. No bicycle policy is confirmed — phone before relying on it for a bike.
6479051fe9: Cross-border intercity coach between Vancouver's Pacific Central Station and Seattle, WA, several times daily. Operated by Greyhound (owned by FlixBus / Flix North America since 2021); no domestic BC route network has resumed since Greyhound exited Canada in 2021.

Confirm current fees and space before travelling, since low-cost-carrier ancillary pricing changes often.
251538fa02: Poparide is a peer-to-peer carpool marketplace (not a scheduled operator) with 112 BC locations listed (densest corridors include Vancouver-Whistler, the Island Highway, and Highway 4 to Tofino/Ucluelet). Listings that take bikes show a bicycle icon in search results. Booking fee is roughly 20% of the trip price on top of the driver's posted seat cost. Because trips are driver-posted rather than scheduled, availability on any given day is not guaranteed.
9b9a58b9bb: Free vehicle and passenger ferry operated by WaterBridge Ferries Inc. under contract to the BC Ministry of Transportation and Transit, connecting Shelter Bay and Galena Bay across Upper Arrow Lake on Highway 23 between Revelstoke and Nakusp.
